# airs-cli-rs design contract (0.1 = milestones 1–3, 0.2 = M3.5, 0.3 = M4t, 0.4 = M4, 0.5 = M5, 0.6 = M6a, 0.7 = M6b, 0.8 = M6c, 0.9 = M6d, 0.9.1 = scm-sdk 0.2.2, 0.10 = M6e, 0.11 = M6f, 1.0 = rename and distribution on scm-sdk 0.2.3, 8.0 = the move into `cdot/prisma-airs-cli` and the TypeScript 7.3.0 port on scm-sdk 0.2.4)

This document is the implementation contract for `airs-cli-rs` (the name of this Rust
implementation and its repository; from 1.0 its executable is `airs`, with `airs-cli-rs` kept as
a compatibility name, §21), a native Rust
reimplementation of a subset of the TypeScript `airs-cli`
(`/Users/cdot/development/redtail/prisma-airs-cli`, package 7.2.1-forgejo.0, commit
`5711012`) on top of the published `scm-sdk` crate (`=0.1.1`, crates.io checksum
`8339891e…d154`, built from scm-sdk-rs commit `7efd137`; `=0.1.0` until 0.7, see G10 in
§15). From 0.9.1 the pin is `=0.2.2` (crates.io checksum `c908cad8…db7c`, the same features;
G25 closed, §15.23); 0.10 keeps `=0.2.2` and adds the `gateway` feature (§19); 0.11 keeps it and adds the `agentguard` feature (§20); 1.0 moves the pin to `=0.2.3` (crates.io checksum `80a58b7b…e809`, the same features; the red team management 0.86.0 update, §15.24). 8.0 moves the TypeScript reference to the final TypeScript release, 7.3.0 (tag `v7.3.0`, commit `7a54e46`, TS SDK 0.35.0, this repository's own history; docs/TESTING.md §3.4), ports its directional security profiles (§13.17) and the rest of 7.3.0, and adopts scm-sdk 0.2.4, the TypeScript 0.35.0 overlay (§15.25; until 0.2.4 is on crates.io, the exact Forgejo commit `4825616` as a temporary git dependency). From 0.3 the Rust CLI keeps its own tenant store (§3) and reads the TypeScript
CLI's files only in `tenant import`, which never modifies them.

The behavioural research this contract is derived from lives in `docs/research/`
(one file per subsystem, with file:line citations into both code bases). When this
document and the research disagree, this document wins: every intentional
difference from the TypeScript CLI is listed in §12 with its reason.

---

## 1. Scope

Release 1 (first deliverable: a native Apple Silicon executable):

| Milestone | Commands |
|---|---|
| M1 tenant loading + diagnostics | `tenant list|ls`, `tenant path [name]`, `tenant read [name]`, `tenant get <name> <key>`, `doctor` |
| M2 read-only management | `runtime profiles list|ls`, `runtime profiles get <nameOrId>`, `runtime topics list|ls`, `runtime topics get <nameOrId>` |
| M3 scanning | `runtime scan --profile <name> [--response <text>] <prompt>` |
| M4t tenant writes (0.3) | `tenant create <name>`, `tenant set <name> <key> [value]`, `tenant unset <name> <key>`, `tenant switch <name>`, `tenant delete|rm <name>`, `tenant import` (Rust-only); every tenant command reads the TOML store (§3) |
| M4 runtime writes (0.4) | `runtime topics create`, `update <topicId>`, `delete|rm <topicId>`, `apply`, `revert`, `eval`, `sample`; `runtime profiles create`, `update <nameOrId>`, `delete|rm <nameOrId>`, `cleanup` (§13) |
| M5 bulk scanning (0.5) | `runtime bulk-scan`, `runtime resume-poll <stateFile>` (§14) |
| M6a Red Team (0.6) | every `redteam` command except `judge`: `list|ls`, `status`, `abort`, `categories`, `languages`, `eula`, `scan`, `report|dashboard [jobId]`, `registry-credentials`, `instances`, `devices`, `prompt-sets`, `prompts`, `properties`, `targets` (backup and restore included), `adapter`, `network-broker` (§15) |
| M6b DLP (0.7) | every `runtime dlp` command except `generate`: `filtering-profiles list\|ls\|get\|replace`, `patterns`, `profiles` and `dictionaries` `list\|ls\|create\|get\|replace\|patch\|delete\|rm` (`profiles delete` is a refusal that sends nothing), `backup`, `restore <file>` (§16) |
| M6c Model Security (0.8) | every `model-security` command: `groups list\|ls\|get\|create\|update\|delete\|rm`, `rules list\|ls\|get`, `rule-instances list\|ls\|get\|update`, `scans list\|ls\|get\|create\|evaluations\|evaluation\|violations\|violation\|files`, `models list\|ls\|get\|versions\|version\|files`, `labels add\|set\|delete\|rm\|keys\|values`, `pypi-auth`, `install` (uv only, with `--fetch-uv`) (§17) |
| M6d Runtime extras (0.9) | `runtime api-keys list\|ls\|create\|regenerate\|delete\|rm`, `runtime customer-apps list\|ls\|get\|update\|delete\|rm\|consumption`, `runtime deployment-profiles list\|ls`, `runtime scan-logs query` (the TS stub), `runtime dashboard applications\|application\|application-violations\|top-applications\|violations-trend\|apps-list`, `runtime sessions chart\|list\|ls\|get\|transaction\|scan-content`, `runtime report`, `runtime profiles backup [profile]`, `runtime profiles restore <file>` (§18) |
| M6e Gateway (0.10) | every TypeScript `aigateway` command, renamed `gateway` (no alias): `workspaces\|workspace list\|ls\|get\|create\|update\|archive` (and the hidden `delete`), `scopes list\|ls\|get\|create\|bind\|delete\|rm`, every `telemetry` read (`cost`, the 17 charts, `filter-boundaries`, `group-by`, `logs list\|ls`), `api-keys service\|user`, `audit-logs`, `configs`, `deployments`, `guardrails`, `integrations`, `mcp integrations`, `organisations`, `plugins`, `providers` (reads and writes), `admin-guardrails`, `inference chat\|responses\|embeddings`, `report\|dashboard`; the doctor's `Gateway API` check (§19) |
| M6f Supplychain (0.11) | every TypeScript `agentguard` command, renamed `supplychain` (no alias): `scans list\|ls`, `scans vulnerabilities <scanUuid> [--include-content]`, `stats`, `rules list\|ls`, `report` (§20) |

0.2 (M3.5 Foundations) adds no command. It gives every command above the `pretty` and
`table` renderings (§2.4, §2.7, §3.6, §7.6, §8.6, §9), TypeScript colours (§2.8) and
the `--debug` API log (§2.9). The specs it is derived from are
`docs/research/ts-renderer.md` (cited as **R§n**) and `docs/research/ts-debug-log.md`
(cited as **L§n**); this document overrides them where they differ.

0.3 (M4t Tenant writes) moves tenants to the TOML store of §3 and adds `tenant create`,
`set`, `unset`, `switch`, `delete|rm` and the Rust-only `tenant import` (§3.11, §3.12).
From 0.3 no command reads the TypeScript registry except `tenant import`. The specs it
is derived from are `docs/research/ts-tenant-config.md` and
`docs/research/ts-tenant-write.md` (cited as **W§n**).

0.4 (M4 Runtime writes) adds the topic and profile writes, `topics apply`, `revert`,
`eval` and `sample`, and `profiles cleanup` (§13; D93–D117). The specs it is derived from
are `docs/research/ts-runtime-writes.md` (cited as **T§n**) and
`docs/research/rs-sdk-writes.md` (cited as **S§n**).

0.5 (M5 Bulk scanning) adds `runtime bulk-scan` and `runtime resume-poll`: async
submissions with durable checkpoints, a per-job `flock` lock, bounded polling, the CSV
output and recovery that never resubmits an ambiguous submission (§14; D118–D131). The
specs it is derived from are `docs/research/ts-bulk-scan.md` (cited as **B§n**) and
`docs/research/rs-sdk-async-scan.md` (cited as **A§n**).

0.6 (M6a Red Team) adds every `redteam` command except `judge`: scans and their bounded wait,
the catalogue, EULA, instances, devices, prompt sets, prompts, properties, targets, adapters,
the network broker, the per-job and environment reports, and the targets backup and restore,
with one attempt per write, credentials redacted in every output and no-clobber files (§15;
D133–D159). It is built in three steps (§15.1). The specs it is derived from are
`docs/research/ts-redteam-scans.md` (**RS§n**), `docs/research/ts-redteam-targets.md`
(**RG§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-redteam.md` (**RK§n**).

0.7 (M6b DLP) adds every `runtime dlp` command except `generate`: the reads of the four DLP
resources, their writes (the dictionary multipart upload included) with one attempt per write,
a read-first guard that never touches predefined or parent-managed resources, confirmations for
deletes, replaces and restores, and the DLP backup and restore in a Rust-only format that never
overwrites a file and never duplicates a resource (§16; D160–D178). It is built in three steps
(§16.1). The specs it is derived from are `docs/research/ts-dlp.md` (**TD§n**),
`docs/research/ts-dlp-backup.md` (**TB§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-dlp.md` (**DK§n**).

0.8 (M6c Model Security) adds every `model-security` command: the reads of groups, rules, rule
instances, scans (with their evaluations, violations and files), models and labels, their writes with
one attempt per write and confirmations for the destructive ones, `pypi-auth`, which never prints the
credential-bearing index URL (a new private `--url-file` is its only channel), and `install`, uv only,
which passes the credential to uv through the environment and can fetch a pinned, checksum-verified uv
with `--fetch-uv` (§17; D179–D203). It is built in three steps (§17.1). The specs it is derived from
are `docs/research/ts-model-security.md` (**MS§n**), `docs/research/ts-model-security-install.md`
(**MI§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-model-security.md` (**MK§n**).

0.9 (M6d Runtime extras) adds the API key, customer-app, deployment-profile, dashboard and session commands, the
original `scan-logs query` stub (replaced by D338–D339), the runtime report (now Signal Brief, D340) and the security-profile backup and restore: every write is one
attempt with confirmations for the destructive ones, an API key value is never printed (a new private `--key-file` is its
only channel), no command shows a value the server did not send, and the backup is a Rust-only format that never
overwrites a file and whose restore never duplicates a profile (§18; D204–D226). It is built in three steps (§18.1). The
specs it is derived from are `docs/research/ts-runtime-extras.md` (**TX§n**), `docs/research/ts-runtime-dashboard-report.md`
(**TR§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-runtime-extras.md` (**RX§n**).

0.10 (M6e Gateway) adds every TypeScript `aigateway` command under the new name `gateway`: the workspace, IAM scope,
telemetry, inventory, admin-guardrail and inference commands, the HTML gateway environment report and the doctor's
`Gateway API` check. Every write is one attempt with confirmations for the destructive, replacing, rotating and
tenant-wide ones; one withholding policy keeps every credential the gateway returns that its rules recognise (credential
names in any form, header and environment lists, credential members, JSON texts, private keys, URLs; §19.3) out of every
output (a one-time
credential goes only to a new private `--secret-output` file); workspace references never pass through unresolved;
telemetry windows are UTC; inference reads its key only from the tenant (§19; D227–D254). It is built in four chunks
(§19.1). The specs it is derived from are `docs/research/ts-gateway.md` (**GW§n**), `docs/research/ts-gateway-report.md`
(**GR§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-gateway.md` (**GK§n**).

0.11 (M6f Supplychain) adds every TypeScript `agentguard` command under the new name `supplychain`: the scan, finding,
statistics and rule-catalog reads and the HTML supplychain environment report. Every request is a read, sent once plus
one re-read after a 401 or 403; every argument check comes before the tenant; walks are complete and checked or fail;
scan names, git URLs, fingerprints and device metadata are never printed, finding content only with
`--include-content` and only on stdout, and an incomplete finding list fails closed (§20; D308–D325). It is built in two
chunks (§20.1); both have landed (chunk 1, the clients and the four reads; chunk 2, the report, the doctor wording
and the live flow). The first live run found that the service sends `null` where both SDK contracts require a scan
member (G71): the scan list is read raw and through a CLI-side tolerant projection, so the rows print where TypeScript
refuses the page (§20.16; D324, D325). The specs it is derived from are `docs/research/ts-supplychain.md` (**SC§n**) and
`docs/research/rs-sdk-supplychain.md` (**SK§n**).

1.0 (Rename and distribution) adds no command and changes no behaviour other than the program name: the executable
is invoked as `airs` (the product, crate and repository keep the name airs-cli), `airs-cli-rs` stays through 1.x as a
compatibility name that prints the same bytes, and every usage line, help example, hint, remedy and Rust-only text that
names the program says `airs`. Directories, environment variables, store and file formats and tenant keys do not
change. Releases ship `airs-cli-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` tarballs (with the compatibility link) and a Homebrew
formula built from the public crates.io crate (§21; D326). It is built in two chunks (§21.1).

Every TypeScript command group is now ported or dropped. Dropped for good: the
`markdown`, `csv` and `yaml` output formats (D50), `tenant create --config` (D84), `redteam judge`
and `runtime dlp generate` (MILESTONES).

## 2. Process conventions

### 2.1 Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success (including scans whose verdict is `block`), a declined confirmation, an M4 command with nothing to change (§13.3) |
| 1 | operational failure: store, lock, tenant and config errors, missing credentials, HTTP/network/timeout/decode errors, not-found, failed/timed-out scans, a debug log that cannot be set up (§2.9), a tenant that cannot be imported (§3.12), an unreadable or invalid input file, a write whose outcome is unknown, a multi-step write that stopped part-way, an eval scan that did not complete, a cleanup deletion that did not succeed (§13.3), a bulk-scan job lock held by another process, a bulk submission that was rejected or whose outcome is unknown, a bulk-scan row that failed, an ambiguous job `resume-poll` cannot continue (§14.15), a red team scan that failed, was aborted or was not seen to finish, an adapter validation that failed, a targets backup or restore with failed rows, an environment report with unknown health or incomplete under `--strict` (§15.3) |
| 2 | usage error: every argument-parse error (clap), flag validation, an invalid output format, local request-input validation (empty scan content, profile name too long, prompt too large; the M4 argument checks, §13), every input error of a tenant write command, stdin values included (§3.10, §3.11, D75), a confirmation refused for want of a terminal (§3.10, §13.2), the bulk-scan argument checks and an input file with no prompts (§14.2), the red team argument checks and confirmation refusals (§15.3) |
| 130 | interrupted by SIGINT (after cancelling in-flight requests), or a prompt cancelled by Ctrl-C or EOF (§3.10) |
| 143 | terminated by SIGTERM (after cancelling in-flight requests) |

**Usage validation always happens before the tenant store is read**, so a usage
error never needs a selected tenant, never causes an HTTP request and never writes.

### 2.2 Streams

- stdout carries data only. stderr carries status lines, the outcome lines of the
  tenant write commands (§3.11, D74) and of the runtime write commands (§13.2, D106),
  prompts (§3.10, §13.2) and errors.
- ANSI colour follows §2.8: TypeScript's escape codes, decided per stream. JSON output
  and tables are never coloured. clap colours its own help and parse errors by the same
  environment rule (it is clap's rendering; §2.8 adopts its decision so the two agree).
- No control character from a server or a file reaches the terminal: every error
  message and detail line, every pretty layout and every table cell replace C0 controls
  (including newline and tab), DEL and C1 controls with U+FFFD (D47, D52). JSON output
  is unaffected (serde escapes control characters). The one exception is the red team
  multi-line server text of §15.3 in pretty layouts, which keeps its line feeds, CR LF
  pairs and tabs (`output::terminal_safe_lines`); every other control character there,
  a lone CR included, is still replaced.
- Status line: `"  <message>\n"` on stderr, suppressed by `--quiet`.
- Operational error (exit 1), stderr, never suppressed:
  ```
  \n  ✗ Error: <message>\n
  [    HTTP <status>\n]
  [    Re-run with --debug to capture redacted API diagnostics.\n]
  [    <extra detail line>\n ...]
  \n
  ```
  The `Re-run with --debug …` hint (TS text, `src/cli/renderer/common.ts:19-23`) follows
  the `HTTP <status>` line, and only that line: it appears exactly when the block has an
  `HTTP <status>` line and `--debug` is off. Under `--debug` it is omitted, because the
  notice already named the log (D69). The Rust-only detail lines (`Request ID: …`,
  `Outcome unknown: …`) come after it.
- Usage error (exit 2) found by our own validation: `"\n  ✗ <message>\n\n"` on stderr.
- clap parse errors and help: clap's standard rendering (help → stdout exit 0;
  errors → stderr exit 2). Running a command group with no subcommand prints that
  group's help to stderr and exits 2. One exception (D91): a parse error of
  `tenant create`, `tenant set` or `tenant unset` never quotes an argument, because a
  value there is often a secret typed in the wrong place. Its `error: ` line is
  replaced, and clap's usage line and `For more information, try '--help'.` follow:
  - an excess positional:
    `too many arguments for '<leaf>'. Expected <n> argument[s] but got <m>.` (the
    TypeScript text; `<n>` is 1 for `create`, 3 for `set`, 2 for `unset`);
  - `--stdin=<value>` or `--client-secret-stdin=<value>`:
    `option '<flag>' does not take a value`;
  - any other unknown argument that is not an option name of some command (`--FAKE`,
    `-x`):
    `unknown option for '<leaf>' (not shown, as it may be a secret); to pass a value that starts with '-', put '--' before it`;
  - an option name (`--config`, D84; `--tsg-id=…` on `set`): clap's own message,
    which quotes only the name (`unexpected argument '--config' found`).
  Every other command and error kind (missing arguments, invalid UTF-8) keeps clap's
  rendering.
- JSON data: the `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` layout (2-space indent) + one `"\n"`.
  Every number is written as ECMAScript `Number::toString` writes it (`js_number`, §2.7):
  integers with `|n| <= 2^53` exactly, every other value as the nearest `f64` (`2.0` →
  `2`, `2.5`, `1e+21`, `100000000000000000000`, `1e-7`, `0.000001`). This replaces the
  0.1 rule (integral floats up to 2^53 as integers, others through serde_json's float
  formatting), which differed from TypeScript for integral values in (2^53, 1e21), for
  exponents and for magnitudes below 1e-5; it is a parity fix, not a §12 row. Empty
  list → `[]\n`.
- A `BrokenPipe` while writing stdout ends the process silently with exit 0 (parity with
  Node's console, which ignores EPIPE). Never panic on a closed pipe. Any other stdout
  write failure (`ENOSPC`, `EIO`, `EDQUOT`, …, also for `--version`) prints
  `\n  ✗ Error: AISEC_SDK_ERROR:Output could not be written to stdout\n\n` (fixed text, the
  OS error is never echoed) and exits 1.
- Data is buffered and written once per command after success, so failing runs leave
  stdout empty. Two commands print their result and then exit 1: `doctor` when a check
  fails (§9), and `runtime scan` when the verdict is `failed` (§8.3, D6). `runtime
  profiles cleanup` writes its pretty preview before it asks and deletes, and exits 1
  when a deletion did not succeed (§13.15). `runtime bulk-scan` and `runtime resume-poll`
  print their summary and then exit 1 when a row failed (§14.14). `redteam adapter validate`
  prints its result and exits 1 when the script did not validate, `redteam targets backup` and
  `restore` print their summary and exit 1 when a row failed, and the environment report writes
  its file and exits 1 for unknown health or under `--strict` (§15). `runtime customer-apps consumption`
  without an app name prints the apps that succeeded and exits 1 when one failed, `runtime sessions list --all`
  prints its first items and exits 1 at its item or page cap, `runtime report` follows the environment
  report's rule, and `runtime profiles restore` prints its result and exits 1 when it did not complete (§18).

### 2.3 Global flags

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `--output <format>` | global (`global = true`), accepted before or after the subcommand; **last occurrence wins** (`args_override_self`) |
| `--quiet` | global; suppresses status lines and decorative headings only (the data/decoration split of §2.7); never suppresses data, errors or the debug write warning |
| `--debug` | global, accepted before or after the subcommand; help text `Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file` (TS). Writes the API log of §2.9 for commands that can send requests; accepted and ignored by `tenant *` |
| `--tenant <name>` | **Rust-only**, global, read-only per-invocation selection of a registered tenant (§3.4); a usage error with `tenant create|set|unset|switch|delete|import` |
| `-V`, `--version` | prints the bare version (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, `1.0.0\n` from 1.0) to stdout and exits 0 when it appears anywhere before a literal `--`, including as an option value. Implemented as an argv pre-scan before clap. TS parity for leaf-command option values (`runtime scan --profile -V hi`: commander fires it during parse); a value of the root `--output` differs (D41). The output is the same under `airs` and the compatibility name `airs-cli-rs` (§21.2). |
| `-h`, `--help` | clap help on stdout, exit 0, zero requests |

Option values may begin with `-` (`--response -x` is a value). A positional prompt that
starts with `-` needs `--` (as in the TypeScript CLI).

### 2.4 Output formats

Valid names, exactly and case-sensitively: `pretty`, `table`, `json`. `markdown`, `csv`
and `yaml` are dropped for good (D50); `Format` has three variants and no others. Each
leaf command's `--help` shows `--output` as `Output format: pretty, table, json`
(`tenant path` says the option is ignored); the root and group help list the same
names. The help text is generated from the per-command policy table below, which
planning also uses.

Resolution (R§1; the TS rule apart from D5, D42, D50, D51 and D59):
1. **Explicit.** The global `--output` (any position before a literal `--`, last
   occurrence wins, §2.3). A value other than the three names is the usage error
   `Invalid output format '<x>'. Expected: pretty, table, json` (exit 2, before the
   tenant is read, D2) on **every** command, `tenant path` and `runtime scan` included,
   which TS lets ignore any value (D59, D5). `--output ""` is invalid too. The 0.1
   message `Output format '<x>' is not supported here. Expected: …` no longer exists:
   every command that renders data accepts all three.
2. **Tenant default.** When `--output` is absent, the management reads (`runtime
   profiles|topics list|get`) use the selected tenant's `defaultOutput` when the
   effective config has it. It is always one of the three names, because any other value
   makes the config invalid (§3.3, D51), so there is no fallback and no status line. The
   format is therefore known only after the tenant is loaded; every other check is done
   before (D2).
3. **Otherwise** `pretty`.

`tenant get` validates its key before `--output` (D34 order, both usage errors).
`runtime topics sample`'s help says the option is ignored because it prints a CSV file.

| Command | `pretty` | `table` | `json` | Default | Tenant `defaultOutput` |

| `tenant list` | the table (pretty = table) | §3.6 | §3.6 | `pretty` | ignored |
| `tenant read` | the table (pretty = table) | §3.6 | §3.6 | `pretty` | ignored |
| `tenant get` | the bare value | one-row `Key │ Value` table | §3.6 | `pretty` | ignored |
| `tenant path` | — | — | — | the path in every format | — (validated, then ignored) |
| `tenant create|set|unset|switch|delete` | — | — | — | nothing on stdout (§3.11) | — (validated, then ignored, D59) |
| `tenant import` | the table (pretty = table) | §3.12 | §3.12 | `pretty` | ignored |
| `doctor` | §9 | §9 table | §9 | `pretty` | ignored |
| `runtime scan` | §8.4 | §8.6 (Rust-only, D5) | §8.5 (Rust-only, D5) | `pretty` | ignored |
| `runtime topics create|update|apply|revert|eval`, `runtime profiles create|update|cleanup` | §13 | §13 (Rust-only, D94) | §13 (TS only through the hidden `--format`, D94) | `pretty` (or the hidden `--format`, §13.1) | ignored |

| `model-security groups delete`, `labels add\|set\|delete` | — | — | — | nothing on stdout (§17.3) | — (validated, then ignored) |
| `model-security install` | — | — | — | nothing on stdout; `--dry-run` prints its plan as shell text in every format (§17.13) | — (validated, then ignored) |
| `runtime api-keys list`, `customer-apps list\|get\|consumption`, `deployment-profiles list` | the TS layouts (§18.4–§18.10) | TS columns, else `Key │ Value` (§18.3) | the TS projections (§18.3, D207, D209) | `defaultOutput`, else `pretty` | honoured |
| `runtime dashboard *`, `runtime sessions *` | the JSON text of the response (§18.12, §18.13) | row tables, else `Key │ Value` (Rust-only, D212) | the same JSON document | `defaultOutput`, else `pretty` | honoured |
| `runtime api-keys create\|regenerate`, `customer-apps update` | the detail layout of the record (§18.5, §18.8) | `Key │ Value` (Rust-only, D223) | the record (Rust-only, D223) | `pretty` | ignored |
| `runtime api-keys delete`, `customer-apps delete`, `scan-logs query` | — | — | — | nothing on stdout | — (validated, then ignored) |
| `runtime report` | — | — | — | the HTML file (or stdout with `--output-file -`); any explicit `--output` is a usage error (§18.14, D155) | ignored |
| `runtime profiles backup\|restore` | the TS summary table and restore blocks (§18.15, §18.16) | the same | TS's one-element array | `defaultOutput`, else `pretty` | honoured |
| `gateway` reads and the writes that print a record (§19.3) | the TS layouts (§19.5–§19.8), else the generic list and `Field │ Value` detail | TS columns, else `Field │ Value` (§19.3; Rust-only for the writes, D50) | the TS projections, else the withheld record (§19.3) | `defaultOutput`, else `pretty` | honoured |
| `gateway` deletes, archives and revocations | — | — | — | nothing on stdout (§19.3, D244) | — (validated, then ignored) |
| `gateway inference *` | the model text (§19.14) | `Key │ Value` of a non-streamed answer (Rust-only); refused with `--stream` | the answer, or JSONL when streaming | `defaultOutput`, else `pretty` | honoured (`table` cannot stream) |
| `gateway report` (the environment report) | — | — | — | the HTML file (or stdout with `--output-file -`); any explicit `--output` is a usage error (§19.15, D155) | ignored |

Status lines (§7.3, §3.6, §8.2) are the same in every format, on stderr. Only
`pretty` prints banners, sections and other decoration.

### 2.5 Cancellation

A dedicated signal thread (its own small Tokio runtime, alive for the whole process)
waits for SIGINT/SIGTERM and calls `Session::cancel()` on the session shared by every
SDK client of the invocation. Because the thread does not depend on the command
runtime, signals are acted on while a synchronous command runs, while stdout blocks
and while the command runtime shuts down. The command then fails with
`ErrorKind::Cancelled` (or, for a command that never yields, finishes and is then
reported as interrupted) and the CLI prints
`\n  ✗ Error: Interrupted; <context>\n\n` and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM).
`<context>` is `no data was written` for reads and
`the scan request may already have reached AIRS (outcome unknown)` for a scan whose
SDK remote outcome is `Unknown` (`no scan was submitted` when `NotSent`). A second
signal exits immediately with the first signal's code. No partial data is written to
stdout, with one exception: a signal that arrives while stdout is being written (a
stalled reader can block that write forever) ends the process at once with
`the output was not completely written` as the context (the message gets 200 ms, since
stderr may be the same stalled pipe). The command runtime is shut down without waiting
for leftover blocking tasks (a slow `getaddrinfo` after a cancel or deadline), so exit
is never delayed by them.

Test synchronisation: when `AIRS_CLI_TEST_SIGNAL_MARKER` names an absolute path, the signal thread creates that file
(empty, 0600, never replacing one; a failure is ignored) right after it has recorded a signal and before it acts on
it. Debug builds only (`cfg(debug_assertions)`, as the `--fetch-uv` hook of §17.14): a release build contains neither
the variable name nor the lookup. The harness's `Running::send_signal_recorded` waits for it, so a test that signals a run blocked on a stalled
stream continues only once the signal is recorded, never after a fixed sleep (§19.20 choice 129). The variable carries no
configuration, credential or endpoint and changes nothing else.

Tenant write commands (§3.9, §3.10) add three cases. A signal while a prompt or the
delete confirmation waits restores the terminal mode and ends the process at once with
the TypeScript status `  Cancelled; no configuration saved.` (no error block). A signal
while piped stdin is read, or while the lock is awaited, ends the process at once with
the context `no configuration was changed`. A signal that arrives outside a prompt but
before the lock is requested (between two prompts, or after the last one was answered)
stops the command before its next step, with the same context and nothing created. A signal during the locked transaction is
acted on when it ends, with the context `the change was saved` once the commit point
was passed and `no configuration was changed` before it. `tenant import` (§3.12) has no
prompt and reads no stdin: a signal while it reads the TypeScript files or plans is
acted on when that step ends (`no configuration was changed`, nothing created), and
its transaction follows the rules above.

Runtime write commands (§13) add their own contexts: `nothing was changed` for a write
that was not sent, `the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` for one
that was, the completed step first in a multi-step command, `<s> of <n> scans were sent;
no metrics were computed` for `topics eval` and `<d> deleted, <k> not attempted` for
`profiles cleanup` (§13.2). A signal at an M4 confirmation prints the status
`  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` and exits 130 / 143.

`runtime bulk-scan` and `runtime resume-poll` (§14.16) checkpoint the job before the signal
is acted on and name it: `no prompt was submitted` during setup, `<s> of <n> prompts were
submitted; the job was saved: resume it with 'airs runtime resume-poll <state>'`
when nothing is in doubt, and `prompts <ranges> may already have been submitted (outcome
unknown); the job was saved in <state>` for a cancelled submission whose outcome is
`Unknown`.

### 2.6 Runtime

`tokio` current-thread runtime built with `enable_all()`. One `scm::Session` per
invocation. No SDK environment capture (`EnvironmentSnapshot::capture` /
`init_from_environment` / `resolve_oauth_config` with a captured snapshot are never
called). The CLI reads exactly these environment variables: `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`,
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HOME` (the store directory, §3.1; `HOME` also for the debug log
directory, §2.9, the bulk-scan state directory, §14.9, and the TypeScript registry path,
§3.13), `XDG_STATE_HOME` (the debug log directory, the bulk-scan state directory and the
TypeScript registry path), `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` (the
TypeScript registry path only: `tenant import`'s default source and the existence check
behind the import hints, §3.4, §9), `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `CLICOLOR`, `TERM`
(colour only, §2.8), and (doctor only, names only) the full environment listing for the
ignored-variable report. None of them supplies a setting's value. From 0.8,
`model-security install` also reads `PATH` (to find uv), and `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `HOME` (the uv tools
directory, §17.13, §17.14); debug builds only read the two loopback test-hook variables of §17.14, which a
release build does not contain; the uv child processes inherit the environment (§17.13). `FORCE_COLOR`
is not read (D58). For https endpoints reqwest additionally honours proxy
variables (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`) and macOS system proxies
(that direction relies on reqwest and is not covered by the loopback tests). A client
with a plain-http (loopback) endpoint never uses a proxy: it gets a transport with the
SDK's hardening (no redirects, no retries, bounded headers, gzip only, the SDK user
agent) and `no_proxy()`, because http is admitted only for traffic that stays on the
host and a proxy would carry the cleartext Basic pair, bearer or `x-pan-token` off it
(D36). Either base transport is wrapped by the debug transport of §2.9 (a pass-through
when `--debug` is off, so a debug run uses the same HTTP stack), and `ObservedTransport`
keeps wrapping that.

### 2.7 Rendering primitives (`pretty` and `table`)

Every renderer writes into `Output`. stdout is buffered and written once after success,
so a failing command leaves stdout empty in every format (D57). Each stdout piece is
either **data** (printed under `--quiet`) or **decoration** (suppressed by `--quiet`);
status lines go to stderr and are suppressed by `--quiet`. No output depends on the
terminal width: nothing wraps, and nothing is truncated except the topic-list
description (§7.6) and the scan prompt preview (§8.2) (R§2.7).

**Table** (TS `formatOutput(rows, columns, 'table')`, R§2.3; `render::table`):
- Input: the column labels and the rows of cell texts (converted as below).
- No rows → the empty string. Whether the caller still prints `"\n"` is per command
  (empty lists, below).
- Column width `w` = the largest display width among the label and that column's cells.
  Display width is `unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width` (UAX #11, ambiguous
  characters narrow). It equals the TS UTF-16 count for ASCII, Latin and emoji text
  and differs for wide, zero-width and other astral text (D53).
- Header line: per column `" " + label + spaces to w + " "`, joined by `│` (U+2502).
  Rule line: per column `─` (U+2500) repeated `w + 2` times, joined by `┼` (U+253C).
  Body lines: as the header, with the cell texts.
- Lines are joined by `"\n"` and the caller adds one final `"\n"`. Every header and body
  line therefore starts and **ends with one space**; the rule line has neither. No outer
  border, no indent, no truncation, never colour.

**Cell text** (`render::cell_text`, R§2.8):
- absent or `null` → empty;
- string → `terminal_safe(s)` (D52; U+FFFD has width 1, so other rows keep their
  widths);
- number → `js_number`;
- boolean → `true` / `false`;
- object or array → compact JSON in the `JSON.stringify(v)` layout (no spaces; model
  key order with unknown keys sorted, D35/D60; non-ASCII unescaped; `"`, `\` and C0
  controls escaped; numbers through `js_number`), then `terminal_safe`, which there
  changes only DEL and C1 controls (JSON leaves them raw).

**`js_number`** is ECMAScript `Number::toString` (the `ryu-js` crate, already in the lock
file through scm-sdk, or an equivalent port): `2`, `2.5`, `1e+21`,
`100000000000000000000`, `0.000001`, `1e-7`, `-0` → `0`. Integers with `|n| <= 2^53` are
written exactly; every other number is first taken as the nearest `f64`. It is the only
number formatter: pretty values, table cells, the JSON in cells and in the Policy block,
and `--output json` (§2.2).

**Pretty primitives** (TS `ui.ts`, R§2.2; `render::pretty`):

| Primitive | Bytes | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| banner(t, s) | `\n  <t>\n` + (`  <s>\n` when `s` is given) + `\n` | decoration |
| section(l) | `\n  <l>\n\n` | decoration |
| key/value block | per pair `"  " + key + spaces to W + "  " + value + "\n"`; `W` = the longest key of **this** block (keys are fixed ASCII labels) | data |
| bullet(text, kind) | `"  " + glyph + " " + text + "\n"`; glyphs `•` U+2022 neutral, `✓` U+2713 pass, `✗` U+2717 fail, `⚠` U+26A0 warn, `○` U+25CB skip, `●` U+25CF flag | data |
| empty list | `  No <resource> found\n` | data |

Values in pretty layouts are `terminal_safe`d (server and file text) and numbers use
`js_number`. A detail line marked "when present" is omitted for an absent value; a
line marked "always" prints an empty value. `active` renders as `active` / `inactive`
in pretty (absent → `inactive`, TS truthiness) and as `true` / `false` / empty in
tables. Timestamps are printed as received.

**Empty lists** (copied from TS, including the asymmetry):
- management lists: pretty → banner + `  No profiles found\n` / `  No topics found\n`
  (no section, no trailing blank line); table → nothing on stdout; json → `[]\n`. The
  status line `  Showing 0` is printed in every format.
- `tenant list` with no registered tenant: pretty → `  No tenants found\n` plus the status
  `  Run 'airs tenant create <name>' to register one.` (D73; the import suffix of
  §3.4 when it applies); table → `\n` (the empty table is still printed, no status);
  json → `[]\n` (no status). `tenant import` with no rows follows the same rule without
  that status line; its own §3.12 status lines are still printed.
- Detail tables always have rows.

**`--quiet`** suppresses: banners, sections, the doctor header and hints, the scan
headings, and every status line. Everything else on stdout is data and stays,
including the ID lines of the pretty profile and topic lists (D55). `--quiet` never
changes a table or JSON.

### 2.8 Colour

**Decision**, made once per process for stdout and, independently, for stderr (the same
rule as clap's own `anstream` auto choice, so help and output agree):
1. `NO_COLOR` set and non-empty → no colour.
2. Else `CLICOLOR_FORCE` set and non-empty (any value, including `0`, as `anstyle-query`
   reads it) → colour, even on a pipe or a file.
3. Else `CLICOLOR` set to `0` → no colour.
4. Else colour iff the stream is a terminal (`std::io::IsTerminal`) and at least one of:
   `TERM` is set and is not `dumb`; `CLICOLOR` is set (not `0`); `CI` is set.

`FORCE_COLOR`, `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TF_BUILD` and the TS `TERM`-name heuristics
are not read, and the stdout decision never colours stderr (D58). Under the test harness
(pipes, `NO_COLOR=1`) there is never colour.

**Escape codes** are chalk's basic styles (R§2.6): bold `\e[1m…\e[22m`, dim
`\e[2m…\e[22m`, red `\e[31m…\e[39m`, green `\e[32m…\e[39m`, yellow `\e[33m…\e[39m`,
cyan `\e[36m…\e[39m`; from 0.6 also blue `\e[34m…\e[39m`, magenta `\e[35m…\e[39m` and white
`\e[37m…\e[39m` (the red team colours, §15.3).
Styling an empty string adds no codes. A styled string that contains `"\n"` is closed
before every `"\n"` and reopened after it (chalk `applyStyle`), so a leading newline
yields `open close "\n" open …`. Printed values never contain ESC (they are
`terminal_safe`), so chalk's nested-close replacement never arises.

**What is coloured** (exactly where TS colours; all else is plain):

| Element | Style | Span |
|---|---|---|
| banner title / subtitle | bold / dim | the text; the indent is outside |
| section label | bold | the label |
| key of a key/value line | dim | the padded key (padding inside); the two separator spaces outside |
| ID line of a pretty list | dim | the ID |
| `active` / `inactive` (list line, `Status` value) | green / yellow | the word |
| ` rev:<n>` in list lines | dim | including the leading space |
| ` — <description>` in topic list lines | dim | including the leading space |
| bullet glyph | neutral dim; `✓` green; `✗` red; `⚠`, `○`, `●` yellow | the glyph only |
| empty-list text | dim | `No … found` |
| status line (stderr, the debug notice included) | dim | the message; the indent is outside |
| scan `Action` value | `BLOCK` red, `ALLOW` green, `FAILED` red (Rust-only) | the value |
| scan `Triggered` value | `yes` red, `no` green | the value |
| scan `Scan ID` / `Report ID` values | dim | the value |
| doctor hint | dim | `    <hint>` (the inner 4 spaces inside, the 2-space indent outside) |
| doctor summary | green (stdout) / red (stderr) | glyph and text as one span |
| debug write warning (§2.9), the directory-sync warning (§3.9) | yellow | glyph and text as one span (TS `ui.warning`) |
| tenant write success line (§3.11, stderr) | green | `✓ <message>` as one span; the indent outside (TS `ui.success`, `  \e[32m✓ <msg>\e[39m`) |
| tenant write info line (§3.11, stderr) | cyan | `ℹ <message>` as one span (TS `ui.info`) |
| bulk-scan summary values (§14.14) | `Blocked` and `Failed` red, `Allowed` green, `Output` cyan | the value (also `0`); `Total` plain |
| bulk-scan failed-rows line (§14.14, stderr) | red | `✗ <message>` as one span (TS `ui.error`) |
| operational error block (§2.2, §2.5) | `chalk.red("\n  ✗ Error: <message>")` = `\e[31m\e[39m\n\e[31m  ✗ Error: <message>\e[39m\n`; the `HTTP` line and the Rust detail lines red; the `Re-run` hint dim; the final `\n` plain | per line |
| usage error | `chalk.red("\n  ✗ <message>\n")` + `\n` = `\e[31m\e[39m\n\e[31m  ✗ <message>\e[39m\n\e[31m\e[39m\n` | as shown |

Never coloured: tables, JSON, the bare `tenant get` value, `tenant path`, prompts and
their `>` re-ask lines (§3.10), `--version`,
values not listed above (Category, Error, detection names, topic examples, key/value
values), and clap output (clap decides its own).

### 2.9 Debug API log (`--debug`)

The log records status and headers only (L§3 adapted by the settled 0.2 decisions):
never a request or response body, never a URL query. It is therefore no exception to
the secret-safety rules of §6 and AGENTS.md.

**Which runs open a log** (D63). The planning table carries a per-command debug policy:
`log` for `doctor`, `runtime profiles|topics list|get`, `runtime scan`, every M4
command except `runtime topics sample`, and `runtime bulk-scan` and `runtime resume-poll`
(the commands that can send requests; bulk-scan reads its input file during planning, so
its input errors create no log, §14.2); `none` for
`tenant *` (the write commands and `tenant import` included) and `runtime topics sample`,
which accept `--debug` and create no directory, no file and no notice. From 0.6 every
`redteam` command has `log`, except the environment report (`redteam report` without a job
id), which has `refused`: `--debug` there is the usage error
`Disable --debug for environment reports to avoid persisting sensitive traffic content`
(exit 2, nothing created, §15.17, D156). From 0.7 every `runtime dlp` command has `log`
(`profiles delete` always fails in planning, so it opens none; §16.3). `refused` stays reserved for the other commands TS
refuses (profile backup/restore, the other environment reports) when they are ported.
`--help`, `--version`, parse errors and usage errors create nothing. The log is opened
after planning succeeds (all usage validation done) and **before the tenant store is
read**, so a store, config or credential error still leaves a (record-free) log. For
`runtime scan` the order of §8.2 becomes: input validation → debug log → tenant → ….

**Location** (D61).
- `$XDG_STATE_HOME/airs-cli/debug/` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is set and non-empty; it must
  be absolute, otherwise the error is `XDG_STATE_HOME must be an absolute path`
  (exit 1, the §3.13 text).
- Otherwise `<home>/.local/state/airs-cli/debug/`, with `<home>` resolved as in §3.13
  (`HOME` as set; unset → the password database). It must be absolute; an empty or
  relative home is a setup failure (no relative fallback, unlike the registry).
- `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH`, `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` do not affect
  it. Nothing in this directory is a tenant file; pruning only ever removes names of the
  debug pattern.
- The directory is created with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)` (every
  component it creates is 0700, subject to the umask). An existing directory is never
  chmod'ed. The leaf is then checked with `symlink_metadata`: a symlink, a non-directory
  or a directory with `mode & 0o022 != 0` is refused.
- File name: `debug-api-<epoch milliseconds, 13 digits>-<8 lowercase hex>.jsonl`, the hex
  being the first 8 characters of a v4 UUID (the TS pattern). The file is created with
  `OpenOptions::new().append(true).create_new(true).mode(0o600)` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL: an
  existing name or a symlink at the path fails). Its uid must then equal the
  directory's uid; otherwise it is removed and setup fails.

**Retention.** Right after the file is created: list the directory, take the regular
files (by `symlink_metadata`) whose names match `^debug-api-[0-9]{13}-[0-9a-f]{8}\.jsonl$`,
order them newest first by the numeric timestamp in the name, then by name (also
descending, so the order is total; never by mtime), keep this run's file plus the 19
newest others, and `remove_file` the rest.
Every error (listing, stat, unlink, `NotFound` from a concurrent prune) is ignored
silently. Non-matching names, symlinks and directories are never touched or counted.
Two runs pruning at once converge on the same names; no lock is taken.

**Setup failure** (the directory cannot be resolved, created or accepted; the file cannot
be created or fails the owner check): an operational error, exit 1, before the
store is read, zero requests, stdout empty:
`\n  ✗ Error: Cannot create the debug log in <dir>; fix that directory or omit --debug\n\n`
(`<dir>` through `terminal_safe`; the OS error is never echoed). Without an absolute
directory to name (an empty or relative `HOME`, or an unset `HOME` without a
password-database home): `Cannot create the debug log: HOME is not an absolute path; set XDG_STATE_HOME or omit --debug`.
TS also exits 1 here, with other text (D68).

**Notice.** As soon as the file exists: the status line `  Debug: API log → <path>`
(TS text, `→` U+2192, the absolute path through `terminal_safe`) on stderr, before any
other status line. `--quiet` suppresses it; the log is still written.

**What is recorded** (D62). A `DebugTransport` wraps the base transport of every client
(§2.6): the management client and its OAuth provider share one, the scanner has its
own, and all of them write to the invocation's one `DebugLog`. Each `Transport::send`
is one attempt and one record, whatever the host: every retry, token request, 401/403
refresh-and-replay, page of a walk and doctor probe. A request the SDK rejects before
dispatch (destination policy, limits, a deadline or cancel before sending) reaches no
transport and has no record. Records appear in completion order.

**Record** (D64, D66): one compact JSON object per line, `"\n"`-terminated, fields in
this order, TS names where TS has the field:

```json
{"timestamp":"2026-10-17T11:03:44.500Z","durationMs":6,"operation":"airs.management.profiles.list","request":{"method":"GET","url":"https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/aisec/v1/mgmt/profiles/tsg/100","headers":{"authorization":"***","service-name":"api","user-agent":"PAN-AIRS/0.2.4-rust-sdk"}},"response":{"status":200,"statusText":"OK","headers":{"content-length":"722","content-type":"application/json","date":"Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:03:44 GMT"}}}
```

- `timestamp`: UTC at entry to `send`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ` (formatted in-crate
  from `SystemTime`).
- `durationMs`: whole milliseconds (truncated) from entry until `send` resolved
  (response headers received, or the error).
- `operation`: `TransportRequest::operation()`, the SDK's fixed name (`oauth.token`,
  `airs.management.profiles.list`, `airs.management.topics.list`, `airs.scan.sync`,
  `airs.scan.results`, …).
- `request.method`; `request.url`: scheme, host, port when present, and path. The query
  and the fragment are dropped (no `?` or `#`), and userinfo, which admission already
  forbids (§5), would become `[REDACTED]@`.
- `request.headers`, `response.headers`: every header the wrapper sees (reqwest adds
  `host`, `accept-encoding` and similar after it, so they never appear), names
  lowercase, sorted by byte order, each name once with repeated values joined by `, `,
  values per the allow-list below.
- `response.status` (a number) and `response.statusText`
  (`StatusCode::canonical_reason()`, `""` when there is none; never the server's phrase).
- `error`, only when there is no response, and then no `response` key:
  `"Request failed"` (`send` returned an error) or `"Request cancelled before a response"`
  (the `send` future was dropped first: a deadline, a cancel or a signal). The error's
  own text is never logged.
- Never present: a `body` key, a URL query, a body size.

**Header allow-list** (D65). A header's value is written only when its name is in the
list; every other value is `***`. That masks `authorization` (Basic and Bearer),
`x-pan-token`, `x-payload-hash`, `cookie`, `set-cookie`, `proxy-authorization` and
every unknown header.
- Request: `accept`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `service-name`, `user-agent`,
  `x-tsg-id`.
- Response: `cache-control`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `date`, `request-id`,
  `retry-after`, `server`, `vary`, `x-correlation-id`, `x-request-id`, and `location`,
  sanitised like `request.url` (a relative reference keeps only its path; one that does
  not parse is `***`).
- An allow-listed value that is not valid UTF-8, or that `SecretSet::taints` (§6: every
  configured secret form, the Basic pair, every OAuth lease), is `***` as well.
- **Token records wait for their lease.** The lease an `oauth.token` response issues is
  only known once the SDK has parsed that response's body, after the transport saw its
  headers. So while the OAuth provider wrapper (`RecordingProvider`, §6) is fetching a
  lease it holds a `TokenHold`: a finished `oauth.token` attempt is kept, its response
  headers raw, and filtered and line-checked only when the hold is released, after the
  lease was added to the `SecretSet`. A token the server echoes in a header of its own
  response is therefore `***` like any other lease, for the first token and for every
  refresh. A hold dropped unreleased (the token future was cancelled by a deadline, a
  cancel or a signal) writes the held records as the fallback record below (no URL, no
  headers). Nested holds flush when the last one ends. Records are still written in
  completion order of their flush.

**Line check** (defence in depth). Before each write the serialised line, and the
sanitised URL before JSON escaping, are checked against the invocation's `SecretSet`
(`SecretSet::appears_in_ignoring_case`: contains any form, ignoring ASCII case; no
fragment rule). Case is ignored because header names are server text written
lowercased: a secret echoed as a header name would otherwise reach the file
case-folded. If it matches, the record is
written instead as `timestamp`, `durationMs`, `operation`, `request.method`,
`response.status`/`statusText` or `error`, and `"redactionFallback": true` (no URL and
no headers); if even that matched, the record is skipped.

**Writing.** A record is serialised outside the lock and written with one `write_all`
of the whole line under a mutex on the O_APPEND file (no buffering), so a crash or a
second signal (§2.5) can lose an in-flight record but never leaves a partial line. On
cancellation the in-flight futures are dropped before the process exits, so their
cancelled records are written.

**Write failure** (D67). The first failed write (any error) closes the log for the
rest of the run and prints once on stderr, never quiet-suppressed:
`  ⚠ Debug: the API log could not be written; it is incomplete`. The warning is written
by the log itself, straight to the process stderr at the moment of the failure (the
transport has no `Output`), coloured by the stderr decision of §2.8. It never changes the
requests, stdout, the exit code or the error text, and no write is retried.

## 3. Tenant store (TOML, owned by airs-cli-rs)

From 0.3 (M4t) airs-cli-rs keeps its own tenant store. Every command that needs a
tenant (`tenant *`, `doctor`, `runtime *`, `--tenant`) reads this store and nothing
else. The TypeScript registry and its JSON configs are read only by `tenant import`
(§3.12, §3.13), which never writes, creates, locks, renames or chmods them and never
opens their `*.lock` files. Credentials and endpoints still come only from tenant
files, never from the environment (§4).

Messages that TypeScript also prints keep the TypeScript text, with the Rust paths and
program name (D70, D73). Every path in a message is absolute, lexically normalised and
passed through `terminal_safe`. No message, status line or report ever contains a
setting's value, apart from `mgmtTsgId` in the lines that TypeScript also prints it in.

### 3.1 Store location

The store directory `D`:

1. `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` set and non-empty: it must be absolute (start with `/`),
   otherwise fail with `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR must be an absolute path`. `D` is the value,
   lexically normalised (`.`, `..`, duplicate and trailing `/`). `~` is not expanded.
2. Else `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set and non-empty: it must be absolute, otherwise fail with
   `XDG_CONFIG_HOME must be an absolute path`. `D` is `<XDG_CONFIG_HOME>/airs-cli`.
3. Else `<home>/.config/airs-cli`. `<home>` is `HOME` as set, or the password database
   when `HOME` is unset. It must be absolute; otherwise fail with
   `HOME is not an absolute path; set AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR or XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. There is no
   relative fallback (unlike the TypeScript registry, §3.13).

Every failure here is an operational error (exit 1), raised after usage validation
(D2) and after the debug log is opened (§2.9).

Files in `D`:

| Path | Content | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `D/config.toml` | the tenant index: version, selection and each tenant's pinned TSG (§3.2) | create, switch, set `mgmtTsgId`, delete, import |
| `D/tenants/<name>.toml` | one tenant's settings, secrets included (§3.3) | create, set, unset, import |
| `D/config.lock` | the write lock and its holder record (§3.9) | every write command |
| `D/.config.toml.<pid>.<16 hex>.tmp`, `D/tenants/.<name>.toml.<pid>.<16 hex>.tmp` | in-flight atomic writes (§3.9) | every write command |

`config.toml` is the commit point: a tenant exists exactly when `config.toml` lists it.
A `tenants/<name>.toml` that `config.toml` does not list is an orphan. Readers ignore
it; `create` and `import` of that name replace it.

### 3.2 `config.toml`

**Reading.** `config.toml` is read by every command that needs a tenant, with the file
checks of §3.8.
- A missing `D`, or a missing `config.toml` (`NotFound`), is an empty store: no tenants
  and no selection. Reading never creates anything.
- The file must be UTF-8 TOML of at most 1,048,576 bytes. It is parsed with the `toml`
  crate; a duplicate key is a TOML error (the crate skips a leading UTF-8 BOM, so one
  is accepted).
- Schema (strict: no other key at any level):
  - `version`: the integer `1`. Required.
  - `active`: a string naming a key of `tenants`. Optional; absent means no tenant is
    selected.
  - `tenants`: a table. Optional; absent means no tenants. Each key is a tenant name
    matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}$`, and each value is a table with exactly
    one key, `tsg_id`, a string of at least one character. At most 1000 tenants. No two
    names may be equal ignoring ASCII case (D85).
- There are no global settings in 0.3. A later milestone that adds one adds a top-level
  key; until then any other key makes the file invalid.
- A safety refusal (§3.8) has its own message. Every other failure, including
  permission errors, gives the TypeScript registry text with this path:
  `Cannot read tenant registry at <D>/config.toml; restore a valid registry before proceeding`
  (exit 1). Nothing from the file is echoed; the `toml` crate's error text, which
  quotes the input, is never printed.

**Canonical bytes.** Every write produces exactly:

```
version = 1\n
active = "<name>"\n                     (only when a tenant is selected)
\n
[tenants.<name>]\n                      (per tenant, names in byte order, D86)
tsg_id = <TOML string>\n
```

A blank line precedes each `[tenants.<name>]` header. A store with no tenants is the
single line `version = 1\n`. Names are written as bare keys (the name
pattern is a subset of TOML bare keys). A TOML string is a basic string: `"`, `\`
escaped as `\"` and `\\`, U+0008, U+0009, U+000A, U+000C and U+000D as `\b`, `\t`, `\n`,
`\f`, `\r`, every other C0 control, DEL and C1 control as `\uXXXX` (uppercase hex),
everything else as raw UTF-8. Writers never produce control characters, but `import`
carries a TypeScript `tsgId` as it is (§3.12).

Before a write, the new bytes are checked: more than 1000 tenants is
`Cannot create tenant <name>: at most 1000 tenants can be registered`; more than
1,048,576 bytes is `Cannot save <path>: it would exceed 1 MiB` (both exit 1, nothing
written, D87).

### 3.3 Tenant files (`tenants/<name>.toml`)

**Reading** (every command that loads a tenant, `tenant read|get`, `doctor`, and
`switch`, `set` and `unset` under the lock), in this order:
1. The directory checks of §3.8 for `D/tenants`, then the file checks for the file. A
   missing directory or file gives `Cannot read a valid tenant config at <path>`; a
   safety refusal gives its own message (§3.8).
2. The file must be UTF-8 TOML of at most 1,048,576 bytes. Each scalar key must be
   one of the 27 keys below with its listed type/read rule. From 8.1, the optional
   strict scanners table follows §3.15; it is not a scalar setting.
   Unknown keys, the TypeScript names (`aiGw*`, `agentGuard*`, `typesafe*`, `dataDir`,
   the retired `*TokenEndpoint` keys) included, make the file invalid (D71, D72).
3. Any failure in 1–2 except a safety refusal: `Cannot read a valid tenant config at <path>`
   (TypeScript text, exit 1), where `<path>` is `D/tenants/<name>.toml`. Nothing from
   the file is echoed.
4. The TSG pin (§3.7).
5. The effective config is the file's values plus the one default, `scanConcurrency`
   = 5. There are no empty values to strip (they are invalid).

**Schema.** 27 scalar keys in **this order**, plus the optional §3.15 namespace. The order is used by `tenant read`, by the
canonical bytes and by the unknown-key message (D71). "Read rule" applies to every
file read; "write rule" applies in addition to every value `create` and `set` accept
from argv, stdin or a prompt (§3.10, §3.11). `import` applies the read rules only
(§3.12), so a hand-edited or imported file can hold a value that `set` would refuse;
such a value fails when it is used (D28, D48), as before.

| # | Key | TOML type | Read rule | Write rule | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `airsApiKey` | string | non-empty | text value | secret |
| 2 | `airsApiToken` | string | non-empty | text value | secret |
| 3 | `airsApiEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 4 | `airsNumRetries` | integer | 0..=5 | decimal integer 0..=5 | |
| 5 | `mgmtClientId` | string | non-empty | text value | credential |
| 6 | `mgmtClientSecret` | string | non-empty | text value | credential, secret |
| 7 | `mgmtTsgId` | string | non-empty; pinned (§3.7) | `^[0-9]{1,32}$` | credential |
| 8 | `mgmtEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 9 | `mgmtDashboardEndpoint` | string | parses as a WHATWG URL (`url::Url::parse`) | endpoint | |
| 10 | `mgmtTokenEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 11 | `dlpEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 12 | `redTeamDataEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 13 | `redTeamMgmtEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 14 | `redTeamNetworkBrokerEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 15 | `modelSecDataEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 16 | `modelSecMgmtEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 17 | `supplychainDataEndpoint` | string | WHATWG URL | endpoint | |
| 18 | `supplychainMgmtEndpoint` | string | WHATWG URL | endpoint | |
| 19 | `gatewayDataEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 20 | `gatewayAdminEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 21 | `iamEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 22 | `gatewayInferenceEndpoint` | string | non-empty | endpoint | |
| 23 | `gatewayInferenceApiKey` | string | non-empty | text value | secret |
| 24 | `gatewayInferenceModel` | string | non-empty | text value | |
| 25 | `gatewayEmbeddingModel` | string | non-empty | text value | |
| 26 | `scanConcurrency` | integer | 1..=20; default 5 | decimal integer 1..=20 | |
| 27 | `defaultOutput` | string | one of `pretty`, `table`, `json` (D51) | the same | |

- Renames from TypeScript (no aliases; the old names are unknown keys):
  `aiGwDataEndpoint` → `gatewayDataEndpoint`, `aiGwAdminEndpoint` →
  `gatewayAdminEndpoint`, `aiGwInferenceEndpoint` → `gatewayInferenceEndpoint`,
  `aiGwInferenceApiKey` → `gatewayInferenceApiKey`, `aiGwInferenceModel` →
  `gatewayInferenceModel`, `aiGwEmbeddingModel` → `gatewayEmbeddingModel`,
  `agentGuardDataEndpoint` → `supplychainDataEndpoint`, `agentGuardMgmtEndpoint` →
  `supplychainMgmtEndpoint`.
- Dropped TypeScript keys: `dataDir` (bulk-scan state lives under
  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/airs-cli/bulk-scans/`, MILESTONES), `typesafeApiKey`,
  `typesafeBaseUrl` and `typesafeModel` (TypeSafe and `redteam judge` are dropped).
- Types are TOML types, not JavaScript coercion: `scanConcurrency = "5"`, `5.0`,
  `true` or `[5]` is invalid, and so is a string key holding a number. A string read
  rule of "non-empty" means at least one character; `""` is invalid (D72).
- Secret keys are those whose name matches `/(?:key|secret|token|password)$/i`:
  `airsApiKey`, `airsApiToken`, `mgmtClientSecret`, `gatewayInferenceApiKey`.
  Credential keys are `mgmtTsgId`, `mgmtClientId`, `mgmtClientSecret`.
- Endpoint keys are the keys whose name ends in `Endpoint` (16 keys).

**Write rules.** Checked in this order; the first failure is the message, a usage error
(exit 2) for argv and stdin values (D75) and an inline re-ask for a prompt (§3.10):
1. Blank (empty, or only JavaScript whitespace): for a credential key
   `Tenant config requires nonempty mgmtTsgId, mgmtClientId and mgmtClientSecret`
   (TypeScript text); for any other key
   `Empty values are not stored; use 'airs tenant unset <name> <key>' to remove a setting`
   (D76), with the command's tenant name and key in place of `<name>` and `<key>` (the
   name as typed: `set` does not check the name's format).
2. A C0 control character, DEL or a C1 control anywhere: `Invalid value for configuration setting`.
3. Per class:
   - text value: nothing more. The value is stored untrimmed (TypeScript parity).
   - `mgmtTsgId`: `^[0-9]{1,32}$`, otherwise `Invalid mgmtTsgId: the Rust SDK requires 1-32 ASCII digits`
     (the D28 text). So ` 100` is refused.
   - endpoint: `scm::Endpoint::loopback(value)` must accept it (§5), and for the three
     URL-rule keys `url::Url::parse` too; otherwise
     `Invalid <key>: endpoints must use https (http is allowed only for loopback hosts) and must not contain credentials, a query or a fragment`
     (the D48 text).
   - decimal integer: `^[0-9]+$` (no sign, no whitespace, no `0x`, exponent or
     fraction; leading zeros allowed), parsed without overflow, then the range;
     otherwise `Invalid value for configuration setting` (D76).
   - `defaultOutput`: exactly `pretty`, `table` or `json`; otherwise
     `Invalid value for configuration setting`.

**Canonical bytes.** One `<key> = <value>\n` line per present key, in schema order, no
blank lines, no comments for scalar-only files: strings as TOML basic strings (§3.2), integers in decimal. The optional named namespace appends the §3.15 tables. A
`create` writes, for example:

```
mgmtClientId = "client-100"\n
mgmtClientSecret = "FAKE-SECRET"\n
mgmtTsgId = "100"\n
```

### 3.4 Selecting the tenant

- Default: `config.toml`'s `active`.
- `--tenant <name>` (Rust-only, D33): first a usage check of the name format
  (`Tenant name must be 1–64 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores and start with a letter/digit`,
  exit 2), then select that tenant without changing the store. Unknown →
  `Tenant not found: <name> (registered: <a, b>)` (exit 1; `(no tenants registered)`
  when empty). The TSG pin still applies. `--tenant` with `tenant create`, `set`,
  `unset`, `switch`, `delete` or `import` is the usage error
  `--tenant cannot be used with 'tenant <subcommand>'; name the tenant as an argument`
  (exit 2), because those commands name their tenant positionally.
- No selection (API commands and doctor):
  - names registered: `No tenant selected. Run 'airs tenant switch <name>' (registered: <a, b>)`
  - none: `No tenant selected. Run 'airs tenant create <name>' and then 'airs tenant switch <name>'`
- Name lists (`registered: …`) are in byte order of the names (D86).
- **Import suffix** (D90). When `config.toml` does not exist (`NotFound`, including a
  missing `D`) and the TypeScript registry path of §3.13 resolves and exists
  (`symlink_metadata` succeeds; the file is not opened; a resolution error counts as
  absent), every "nothing registered" message and status line gets the suffix
  `; a TypeScript tenant registry exists at <path>: run 'airs tenant import' to copy it`.
  It applies to the no-selection message above (the "none" form), the `tenant read`
  / `tenant path` form `No tenant selected; run 'airs tenant create <name>' first`,
  and the empty `tenant list` status (§3.6). The suffix goes before a trailing period
  (`… to register one; a TypeScript … to copy it.`).
- Every hint, remedy and success line that names a command names **`airs`** from 1.0
  (`airs-cli-rs` in 0.3–0.11; D73, §21.4). This replaces the 0.1 rule that hints named
  `airs-cli` because only the TypeScript CLI could change tenants: from 0.3 `airs-cli`
  would change a different store. The program name is one constant (`store::PROGRAM`), and
  it is the name the help shows whatever name the binary was started under (§21.2).

### 3.5 Credential checks (before any client is built, zero requests)

- Present = string with non-whitespace content (a value can no longer be empty, but a
  hand-edited or imported value can be whitespace).
- Management set, checked in order `mgmtClientId, mgmtClientSecret, mgmtTsgId`:
  `Management credentials are not configured (missing <k1, k2>). <remedy>`
- Scanner: either `airsApiKey` or `airsApiToken`:
  `Scanner credentials are not configured (airsApiKey or airsApiToken). <remedy for airsApiKey>`
- Remedy with a selected tenant:
  `Run 'airs tenant set <name> <key>' for <k1, k2> (secrets prompt hidden, or use --stdin)`;
  without one: `Run 'airs tenant create <name>' (prompts for the OAuth credentials), then 'airs tenant switch <name>'`.
- Management commands never require scanner keys; scanning never requires management
  credentials (the TSG pin still applies to every command that reads the tenant file).

### 3.6 Read commands

- `tenant list|ls [--output pretty|table|json]`: reads only `config.toml`. Rows
  `{name, configPath, tsgId, active: bool}` in byte order of `name` (D86), where
  `configPath` is `D/tenants/<name>.toml` (absolute, whether or not the file exists)
  and `tsgId` is `tsg_id`. Empty → `[]`. When tenants exist but none is selected, the
  status `  No tenant selected; run 'airs tenant switch <name>'.` (every
  format). `pretty` and `table` are byte-identical (R§3.7): columns
  `Tenant │ Selected │ TSG ID │ Config file` from `name`, `active` (`true`/`false`),
  `tsgId`, `configPath`. An empty store follows §2.7 (pretty: `  No tenants found` and
  the status `  Run 'airs tenant create <name>' to register one.`, with the
  import suffix of §3.4 when it applies; table: `\n`; json: `[]\n`).
- `tenant path [name]`: prints `D/tenants/<name>.toml` (through `terminal_safe`, D52) +
  `\n`; never opens the tenant file. A valid `--output` is ignored; an invalid one is a usage error (§2.4, D59).
- `tenant read [name] [--output pretty|table|json]`: rows `{key, value}` for the
  effective config in schema order: the keys present in the file plus `scanConcurrency`
  (default 5). Strings as stored, integers as JSON numbers. Secret keys show
  `[REDACTED]` (they are never empty). Endpoint keys are shown with any userinfo,
  query and fragment replaced: `https://[REDACTED]@host/path?[REDACTED]#[REDACTED]` (a
  value that does not parse as a URL but contains `@`, `?` or `#` shows `[REDACTED]`);
  a URL without them is shown byte for byte (D45). Status
  `  Tenant <name> (TSG <tsg>): <path>` (every format; `tsg_id` and the path through
  `terminal_safe`, D52). `pretty` and `table` are byte-identical: the `Key │ Value`
  table of those rows (cells per §2.7; R§3.6 has the capture).
- `tenant get <name> <key> [--output pretty|table|json]`: unknown key → usage error
  `Unknown configuration key. Supported keys: <27 keys, schema order, ', '>` (exit 2,
  D34, D71). pretty prints the effective value alone (`[REDACTED]` for secrets,
  endpoints redacted as for `tenant read`, empty line when unset; never coloured);
  table prints the one-row `Key │ Value` table of the same value (an empty cell when
  unset, R§3.8); json prints `[{"key": "<key>", "value": <value>}]`. No status lines.
- Name resolution for `read`/`path` (positional name, else `--tenant`, else `active`)
  and `get` (its positional name only), exit 1:
  `No tenant selected; pass a name or run 'airs tenant switch <name>' (registered: <a, b>)`,
  `No tenant selected; run 'airs tenant create <name>' first` (plus the import
  suffix of §3.4), `Tenant not found` (an unknown positional name, TS parity; lookups
  are exact, not case-insensitive). An empty positional name (`tenant path ""`)
  selects nothing, like the TS falsy check: it gets the no-selection message, and
  neither `--tenant` nor `active` stands in. An unknown `--tenant` name uses the §3.4
  message `Tenant not found: <name> (registered: <a, b>)`.

### 3.7 TSG pin

- The pinned identity is `config.toml`'s `tenants.<name>.tsg_id`. The tenant file's
  `mgmtTsgId` must be exactly equal to it (byte equality, no trimming); a file without
  `mgmtTsgId` also mismatches. Otherwise:
  `Tenant config TSG differs from its registered identity; register it under a new name`
  (TypeScript text, exit 1; neither value is printed).
- It is checked by every reader of the tenant file: API commands, `tenant read|get`,
  doctor's Config file check, `switch`, `unset`, and `set` of every key except
  `mgmtTsgId`. It is not checked by `tenant list`, `tenant path` or `delete`, which
  never open the tenant file.
- `tenant set <name> mgmtTsgId <tsg>` changes the identity: under the lock it writes the
  tenant file's `mgmtTsgId` and `config.toml`'s `tsg_id` to the new value. It works on
  a mismatched tenant too, which makes it the repair for a mismatch (D83). Nothing
  else changes the pin, apart from `import --replace`.

### 3.8 Safety checks for store directories and files

Every read and write applies these checks; TypeScript applies none of them to its
registry (D79).

**Directories** `D` and `D/tenants`, when they exist, by `symlink_metadata` (not
followed): a directory, not a symlink; owned by the effective uid; `mode & 0o022 == 0`.
Otherwise:
`Refusing to use <dir>: it must be a directory (not a symlink) owned by the current user and not writable by group or others`
(exit 1). Every write transaction checks an existing `D/tenants`, also one that writes
no tenant file (`switch`, `delete`), before it takes the lock (§3.9 step 2), so the
refusal changes nothing. The stale-file sweep and `delete`'s unlink do not use paths
under the directory: they open it with `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`, apply this rule to
the descriptor (`fstat`), and look up and unlink entries relative to it
(`statat`/`unlinkat`), so a directory swapped for a symlink in between is never
followed. The parents of `D` are not checked. A user whose `~/.config/airs-cli` is a
symlink sets `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` to the real directory.

**Files** `config.toml`, each `tenants/<name>.toml` and `config.lock`: `symlink_metadata`
(not followed), then open with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, then `fstat` the descriptor and
require the same device and inode (no swap between the two). The file must be a
regular file, owned by the effective uid, with `mode & 0o077 == 0`. Otherwise:
`Refusing to use <path>: it must be a regular file (not a symlink) owned by the current user with no group or other permissions (chmod 600)`
(exit 1). The size limit and parse failures use the file's invalid message (§3.2,
§3.3), not this one. A different inode at the `fstat`, on a file that is itself regular,
owned and private, means a concurrent writer replaced the file atomically (rename over
the path) between the two checks; that is not an unsafe file. The checks are then
repeated on the new file, up to 16 times, before the file is refused. Any file that
fails the type, owner or mode check is refused at once.

**Read-only files** (writers only). A `config.toml` or tenant file that the writer would
replace and whose mode lacks owner write (`mode & 0o200 == 0`) is refused:
`<path> is read-only; restore write permission (chmod 600) to change it` (exit 1,
nothing written). This keeps the TypeScript rule for configs and applies it to the
index too.

**Creation.** Only a write transaction creates anything (§3.9), and only after all
input was collected and validated (D87). `D`, with any missing parents, is created
with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)`; `D/tenants` with mode 0700. An
existing directory is never chmod'ed. Files are created 0600 (§3.9). A failure is
`Cannot create <dir>; check the permissions of its parent directory` (exit 1; the OS
error is never echoed).

### 3.9 Locking and atomic writes

**One lock for every write** (D77). Every write command takes the same lock, which
covers `config.toml` and every tenant file. Readers never lock: atomic renames mean a
reader sees each file whole, old or new (a reader running during a two-file change can
see one file changed and not yet the other; §3.11 orders the files so that this is
never a corrupt tenant, only a transient pin mismatch during `set mgmtTsgId`).

**Acquiring.**
1. `D` exists and passes §3.8 (it is created first if missing).
2. Open `D/config.lock` with `O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, mode 0600,
   and check it as a §3.8 file (a fresh file is 0600 by `fchmod`).
3. `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` (`rustix::fs::flock`). On `EWOULDBLOCK` the command waits:
   it retries every 100 ms for at most 5 s from the first attempt. After the first
   failed attempt it prints, once, the status line
   `  Waiting for another airs change to finish (<holder>)` (quiet-suppressed).
   When the 5 s pass:
   `Another change is in progress: <D>/config.lock is held by <holder>; try again when it finishes`
   (exit 1, nothing written).
   - `<holder>` is `pid <pid> on <host> since <since>` from the holder record (read
     with `pread` from offset 0, at most 512 bytes, at each failed attempt), or
     `another process` when the record is empty or malformed.
   - Any other `flock` error (`ENOLCK`, `EINVAL`, `EOPNOTSUPP`), and a failure to open
     or create the lock file other than a §3.8 refusal:
     `Cannot lock <D>/config.lock; the file system may not support file locks` (exit 1).
   - SIGINT or SIGTERM while waiting stops the wait: `Interrupted; no configuration was changed`
     (§2.5, exit 130/143).
   - Once the `flock` succeeds, the descriptor (`fstat`) must still be the file at
     `D/config.lock` (`lstat`): a lock file removed or replaced between the open and the
     lock is opened again (step 2; at most 3 times, then the `Cannot lock` message), so
     two writers can never hold locks on two different files.
4. Once held: `ftruncate(0)`, then write the holder record at offset 0:
   `pid=<decimal pid>\nhost=<nodename>\nsince=<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>\n` (UTC; the
   nodename from `rustix::system::uname`, cut to 255 bytes). It is not fsynced.
   - A record is well formed when it has exactly these three lines, `pid` is 1–10 ASCII
     digits, `host` is 1–255 bytes without control characters, and `since` has that
     shape. The holder text is printed through `terminal_safe`.
5. **Releasing**: `ftruncate(0)`, then close the descriptor (`flock` is released on
   close). The lock file is never deleted, because unlinking a `flock` file races with
   a waiter that already opened it.
6. **Crashes.** The kernel releases a `flock` when its process dies, so a crash, a
   SIGKILL or a power loss never leaves the store locked. A dead holder's record stays
   in the file until the next holder overwrites it; while nobody holds the lock it is
   never shown, because only a failed `flock` reads it.

**Transaction.** Every write command runs:
1. Collect and validate all input (argv, stdin, prompts, the confirmation). **No lock is
   held while waiting for the user or for stdin.**
2. Create `D` (and `D/tenants` when a tenant file will be written) if missing (§3.8).
   An existing `D/tenants` is checked (§3.8) whether or not a tenant file will be
   written; an unsafe one is refused here, before the lock.
3. Acquire the lock.
4. Remove stale temporary files: entries of `D` matching
   `^\.config\.toml\.[0-9]{1,10}\.[0-9a-f]{16}\.tmp$` and entries of `D/tenants`
   matching `^\.[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}\.toml\.[0-9]{1,10}\.[0-9a-f]{16}\.tmp$`
   that are regular files (`statat` without following symlinks) owned by the effective
   uid, each directory opened and checked as a descriptor (§3.8; an unsafe or missing
   one is skipped). Only the lock holder writes temporary files, so every match is a
   leftover of a crashed writer. Errors are ignored. Nothing else is removed.
5. Re-read `config.toml` and every tenant file the command needs, and re-run the
   command's state checks: the state may have changed since the unlocked read.
6. Write the files in the command's order (§3.11, §3.12) with the atomic write below.
7. Release the lock.
8. Print the outcome.

**Atomic write** of `bytes` to `path` in directory `dir`:
1. If `path` exists, it must pass the §3.8 file checks and the read-only check.
2. Temporary name `.<file name>.<pid>.<16 lowercase hex>.tmp` in `dir` (the hex from 8
   random bytes, the v4 UUID generator's source). Open with
   `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, mode 0600, then `fchmod`
   0600 so the umask cannot change it.
3. `write_all(bytes)`, `fsync` (`File::sync_all`), close.
4. `rename(temp, path)`.
5. `fsync` `dir` (open it read-only and `sync_all`); when the transaction created
   `D/tenants`, also `fsync` `D`.
6. A failure in 2–4: unlink the temporary file (best effort), and fail with
   `Cannot save <path>; it was not changed` (exit 1; the OS error is never echoed).
   A failure in 5: the rename already happened, so the command does not fail; it
   prints, once and never quiet-suppressed, the warning
   `  ⚠ <path> was saved, but its directory could not be synced; the change may not survive a system crash`
   (yellow, like §2.9's write warning).

Readers therefore never see a partial file. Every file is 0600 when written and every
directory 0700 when created (D78).

**Interruption.** A signal during steps 3–7 does not stop the transaction (§2.5:
a command that does not yield finishes and is then reported). The outcome line is not
printed; the error is `Interrupted; the change was saved` when the commit point was
passed and `Interrupted; no configuration was changed` otherwise. A second signal ends
the process at once (§2.5); the atomic writes leave every file whole, and the
two-file orders of §3.11 make the worst case an orphan tenant file (create, import) or
a pin mismatch that `set mgmtTsgId` repairs.

### 3.10 Input channels

**Argument values** reach validation as clap delivers them. A positional `value` that
starts with `-` is an option to clap unless it is a negative number or follows `--`
(TypeScript parity: `set dev scanConcurrency -1` reaches validation, `set dev
mgmtEndpoint -x` is a parse error, exit 2 per D1). Argv values that are not UTF-8 are a
clap error (exit 2).

**Piped stdin** (`create --client-secret-stdin`, `set --stdin`), TypeScript rules apart
