### 3.15 Application-bound scanner credentials (8.1, D342–D343)

The exact schema, command grammar, error catalog, snapshot ordering and SDK identity
basis are specified in [RUNTIME_CREDENTIAL_CONTRACT.md](RUNTIME_CREDENTIAL_CONTRACT.md).
That contract is part of this section. Existing scalar-only files retain their
canonical bytes, 27 scalar rules and read-only behavior. The optional scanners
namespace is a strict table of at most100 case-unambiguous valid names, each with
one applicationId, admitted scanner endpoint, integer numRetries0–5, non-secret
UUID revision and exactly apiKey or apiToken. Unknown nested fields invalidate
scanners without echoing values. Each app ID has at most one active binding.

Named secrets are included in SecretSet, including unused bindings. Presence of
the namespace (including empty) or a scanner-management invocation enables the
§6 final local-error filter; scanner management enables it before consuming input.
The flag is invocation-local and shared by SecretSet clones. Pure legacy
invocations retain their existing final-error behavior. Public
read/get/list/doctor views expose metadata and hasApiKey/hasApiToken booleans only;
credential coincidences and controls are withheld, and projected-key collisions
refuse output. No raw named credential Serialize/Debug output is provided.
Generic tenant set/unset scanners refuses before store access. New local leaves:
scanners list, set, bind-default, remove, snapshots, restore and delete-snapshot.
Mutations require explicit positional tenant; global --tenant is refused. set
reads bounded private TOML or piped stdin before store access; no new secret argv
option. Destructive leaves require --force. Readers do not create or lock files.

Writes use Transaction. Before first named-table publication, a private no-clobber
snapshot of the previous exact bytes is fsynced under config.lock; snapshot
failure leaves the live file unchanged. Snapshot names are .TENANT.pre-scanners.
UUID.toml or .TENANT.pre-restore.UUID.toml inside D/tenants (no whitespace in the
actual filename). They are not indexed tenant entries. Restore requires matching
store/prefix/TSG and --expect-tsg/--force, rechecks under lock and preserves the
current config before replacement. Listing reveals metadata only; deletion is
explicit. Snapshot failures/rollback never unlink a raced replacement. Older
strict-schema binaries refuse named tables; the first opt-in write explains the
format upgrade. There is no automatic upgrade on read or automatic downgrade.
Keep old Homebrew/npm/RC testing in isolated config roots. Snapshot files never
enter evidence, exports, debug attachments or build archives.

bind-default copies a flat credential and the effective scanner endpoint/retries
into one explicit app association; it does not maintain a live link. With both
flat secrets configured, --use key|token is required: the pinned SDK sends both
headers and provides no client-side precedence. A configured retry value is
copied; its missing effective value is5. New set input defaults retries to0.
Bounded lookups retain zero retries. Changing flat credentials does not rotate a
named copy; doctor explains this. A named-only tenant has configured credentials,
but doctor skips the default scanner probe instead of guessing a named key.

scan/bulk-scan/scan-logs results/reports accept --scanner NAME. Default direct
operations preserve flat behavior; named-only configurations require selection.
Selection cannot try alternate credentials. Management discovery/report lookups
require an exact explicit applicationId binding. Customer-app IDs, display names,
API key labels, auth_code and api_key_last8 do not establish dashboard ownership.
Unbound apps retain management observations with a binding remedy and required
scan-results coverage gap; strict report exits1 after producing artifacts. This
is an intentional migration from the previous automatic flat-key lookup (D343).

Per-app scanner clients admit only their own endpoint and selected secret; all
clients share the invocation's request/deadline/concurrency/report budget. Result
batches never cross configured apps; exact app-name/session buckets remain
separate. Ambiguous same-scan/subrequest attribution without an identifying
session stays unresolved. Report selection is global: default5 IDs, hard10,
at most2 serial actual sends, immediate invocation-wide stop on429. Separate
credential groups can reduce examples; missing examples alone do not fail strict.
No management OAuth credential is sent to the scanner plane.

Named bulk jobs use §14.9 version2 with a non-secret scannerReference. Legacy
jobs retain version1. resume-poll selects the saved name and refuses missing or
rebound app/endpoint before a request; there is no selector override. Same-app/
endpoint revision changes warn about unqualified historic access, checkpoint the
current reference and poll with exactly that active secret. This neither proves
post-rotation service access nor authorizes scan resubmission. Real-service
qualification remains user-run and separate from loopback compatibility evidence.

## 4. Environment handling

- Credentials and endpoints come only from the tenant file. Credential environment
  variables (`PANW_*`, `PRISMA_AIRS_CONFIG_PATH`, …) never change any request.
- Ignored-variable report (doctor): every non-empty variable whose name starts with
  `PANW_` (all of them, including `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG`, `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG_BODY` and
  `PANW_AI_SEC_TIMEOUT_MS`, which the Rust SDK does not read) plus the retired names
  `PRISMA_AIRS_CONFIG_PATH, TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL,
  SCAN_CONCURRENCY, DATA_DIR, MEMORY_ENABLED, MEMORY_DIR, MAX_MEMORY_CHARS,
  ACCUMULATE_TESTS, MAX_ACCUMULATED_TESTS`; sorted by byte order; names only.
- The location variables `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`,
  `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` choose where files are, never what
  they contain, and are never reported.

## 5. Endpoints and SDK clients

- Every configured URL goes through `scm::Endpoint::loopback(value)`: https for any
  host, http only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` and `::1`. Failure →
  `Invalid <key>: endpoints must use https (http is allowed only for loopback hosts) and must not contain credentials, a query or a fragment`
  (exit 1, zero requests, value never echoed; D48).
- Defaults: token `https://auth.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/oauth2/access_token`,
  management `https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/aisec`, scanner
  `https://service.api.aisecurity.paloaltonetworks.com`.
- **Management client** (application-owned OAuth provider, so OAuth failures are
  distinguishable from API failures):
  `ReqwestTransport::new()` (or the direct transport of §2.6 when the API or token
  endpoint is plain http) → `OriginPolicy::new([api, issuer])` →
  `AuthContext::new(issuer, mgmtClientId (raw), 0, mgmtTsgId)` (a non-digit TSG fails
  locally: `Invalid mgmtTsgId: the Rust SDK requires 1-32 ASCII digits`, exit 1) →
  `OAuthProvider::new(ctx, Secret::new(mgmtClientSecret raw), transport, policy, session)`
  wrapped in a provider that registers every lease it hands out in the invocation's
  secret set (§6) → `Client::builder(api).transport(..).destination_policy(..)
  .authentication(Authentication::oauth(provider, false)).session(..).limits(..)` with
  `max_retries = 5` (TS SDK default attempt count for 502/503/504) →
  `ManagementClient::new`. Each command first awaits `provider.get_token(..)`. A `401`
  or `403` answer to a **read** makes the SDK refresh the token once and replay the
  request once (token, request, token, request) before the error is reported; the
  TypeScript CLI sends the same sequence (observed). The SDK never replays a **write**
  (POST, PUT, DELETE: `replay_safe` is false, S§1.2): it invalidates the token on a
  401/403 and reports the error, and the CLI replays a write once after a 401 only
  (§13.2, D95). The doctor probes are the exception: they make
  one attempt (D49), so they neither retry nor refresh and replay.
  No `x-tsg-id` header on profile/topic routes.
- **Scanner client**: `scm::configuration::init(InitOptions{api_key, api_token,
  api_endpoint, num_retries = airsNumRetries})` (trims credentials like the TS SDK,
  caps 2048 UTF-16 units, admits loopback http) → `client_builder()` → `.transport(..)`
  (§2.6) → `.session(..)` → `build()` → `Scanner::new`. `airsNumRetries` therefore only affects safe-read GETs, and the
  doctor probe overrides it with one attempt (D49); the sync scan POST is never
  replayed by the SDK.
- **Red team client** (0.6): `RedTeamClients::build`, the management OAuth identity with the
  three red team planes and the issuer admitted into one destination policy (§15.3).
- Timeouts: single requests use the SDK default 60 s operation budget; full walks
  (`--all`, lookups, latest-topic listing) pass `RequestOptions::with_timeout(300 s)`;
  doctor probes pass `RequestOptions::with_timeout(5 s)` for the whole probe (token +
  request), which really cancels the request.

## 6. SDK error → CLI message (secret-safe, deterministic)

From 8.1 named-credential integration (§3.15), an invocation that reads a named
namespace or runs a local scanner-management command filters every final failure
message, detail and dynamic interruption context through the completed SecretSet
before rendering. This covers local paths that coincide with credentials, including
unused named sets, without changing exit codes or safe messages. Tenant writer
wait notices and durability warnings receive the same filtering.

The SDK never retains server text; the CLI never echoes response bodies, URLs with
queries, tokens or keys. Messages use the TS SDK shape `<ERROR_TYPE>:<text>` with
`ERROR_TYPE = err.error_type()` so they coincide with TypeScript output whenever the
TypeScript text is not server-provided free text.

| SDK error | `✗ Error:` message | extra lines |
|---|---|---|
| `Http` | `<type>:API error <status>` + (`problem()` present: `; <title>; <detail>; <prop>: <reason>…` using the SDK's allowlisted values, duplicates printed once, like the TS SDK `problemMessage`) + (service code present: ` (errorCode: <code>)`) | `HTTP <status>`; `Request ID: <id>` when present. Request ID and error code are omitted when they contain any configured secret or any OAuth token in raw, form-encoded or base64 form, or the HTTP Basic client pair (`mgmtClientId:mgmtClientSecret`, raw or with form-encoded halves, as text or base64). "Any OAuth token" means every lease the provider handed out during the invocation, including the token of a silent 401/403 refresh-and-replay and of a refresh during a walk. Commands and doctor register the same set (every secret-named config value plus the Basic pair). |
| token endpoint non-2xx (`Authentication` from `get_token`) | `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:Token request failed with status <status>` | `HTTP <status>` |
| token endpoint transport failure | `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:Token request failed: network error` | — |
| token decode failure | `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:Token response did not match the OAuth schema` | — |
| `Transport` | `AISEC_CLIENT_SIDE_ERROR:Network request failed (connection refused, reset or unreachable)` | — |
| `Deadline` | `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:Request timed out after <n>s` | — |
| `Decode` | `AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION:Response did not match the expected schema` | — |
| `Limit` with an HTTP error status | treat as `Http` with that status | as `Http` |
| `Limit` on a scan submission with no status and outcome `NotSent` (a body the SDK refused to send for its size) | `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request exceeded a client safety limit` | as for a submission |
| `Limit` otherwise | `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:Response exceeded a client safety limit` | — |
| `Pagination` | `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:Pagination stopped: the service returned a repeated cursor or an empty intermediate page` | — |
| `Destination` (3xx) | `AISEC_CLIENT_SIDE_ERROR:Redirect responses are not followed` | `HTTP <status>` |
| `Cancelled` | §2.5 | — |
| other kinds | `<type>:<kind> error` | — |

For a management write (§13.2) the extra line is
`Outcome unknown: the <thing> may have been <done>.` when the outcome is `Unknown`, and
`Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but the response could not be read.` for a `Decode`
error with a 2xx status, which means the write was applied.

For a scan POST whose SDK remote outcome is `Unknown`, add the extra line
`Outcome unknown: the scan may have been received and processed by AIRS.` The SDK
reports `Unknown` for 5xx answers, transport failures (including a refused connection,
which the SDK does not distinguish from a reset after sending) and decode failures
after a 2xx; it reports `Rejected` for 3xx and 4xx answers, which get no such line.

## 7. M2 read-only management

### 7.1 Flags (lists)

`--limit <n>` (default 100), `--offset <n>` (default 0), `--all`, `--max <n>` (default
10000; `0` = no item cap), `--all-versions`, `--output`. Values are parsed by our code
(decimal digits only) to produce the TS messages (usage errors, exit 2):
`--limit must be a positive integer`, `--offset must be a non-negative integer`,
`--max must be a non-negative integer`, `--all cannot be combined with --offset`
(whenever `--offset` was given explicitly, even `0`). `--max` is validated even
without `--all`.

Gets: `<nameOrId>`, `--revision <n>` (`--revision must be a non-negative integer`,
exit 2), `--all-versions`, `--output`. A value is an id when it matches
`^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` case-insensitively
(compared exactly afterwards).

### 7.2 Requests and semantics

| Invocation | Requests | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles list` | `GET {mgmt}/v1/mgmt/profiles/tsg/{tsg}?offset=O&limit=L&latest=true` (`latest=false` with `--all-versions`) | page rows |
| `profiles list --all` | walk from offset 0 following `next_offset` (absent/0 ends), same `limit` and `latest` | rows up to `--max` |
| `profiles get <id>` | walk `?offset=0&limit=100` (no `latest`) | first row with `profile_id == id` |
| `profiles get <name>` | same walk | highest `revision` (unset = 0), first wins ties |
| `profiles get X --revision N` / `--all-versions` | walk `?offset=0&limit=100&latest=false` | rows matching id/name (and revision); `--all-versions` prints the JSON array, otherwise the first match |
| `topics list` | walk `GET {mgmt}/v1/mgmt/topics/tsg/{tsg}?offset=0&limit=200` (never `latest`) | highest revision per `topic_name` in first-seen order, then local slice `[offset, offset+limit)` (the semantics of `TopicsClient::list` with `latest_only = true`, under the `--all` walk bounds) |
| `topics list --all` | same walk | slice `[0, max)` (`max 0` → everything) |
| `topics list --all-versions` | walk `?offset=0&limit=100` | every row, local slice (`--all`: everything up to `--max`) |
| `topics get <id|name>` (+ flags) | walk `?offset=0&limit=100` | id: first match; name: highest revision; flags: filter like profiles |

Walk limits: `CollectOptions` with `max_items = --max` (`0` → 1,000,000),
`max_pages = 100,000`, `max_bytes = 512 MiB`. Topic page listings (latest and
`--all-versions`) walk under the same bounds with no item cap below the 1,000,000
ceiling, so a page works on every tenant the `--all` listing works on (the latest page
reproduces `TopicsClient::list` with `latest_only`: the same 200-row walk, first-seen
order, first-wins ties, `(more available)` when rows follow the slice). Lookups use
the SDK defaults (10,000 rows, D15). An incomplete walk is an error, never a false
not-found or a partial list. A page with no rows but a fresh non-zero `next_offset`
stops the walk with the SDK pagination error (D46).

### 7.3 Status lines (stderr, quiet-suppressed, every format)

- single page: `  Showing <n> (more available)` when the response carries
  `next_offset > 0`, else `  Showing <n>`.
- `--all`, complete: `  Showing all <n>`.
- `--all` stopped by `--max`: `  Showing first <n> (stopped at --max <m>; more available)`.
- topics latest page: `  Showing <n> (more available)` when the synthesised
  `next_offset` exists, else `  Showing <n>`.
- topics `--all-versions` page: `  Showing <r> of <t> (next --offset <o+l>)` when
  `o+l < t`, else `  Showing <r> of <t>`.
- gets (including `--all-versions`, which prints the list layout): no status line.

### 7.4 Not-found (exit 1)

- profiles get, no flags: `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Profile not found: <x>`
- profiles get with `--revision`/`--all-versions`: `Profile <x> not found`
- topics get id: `Topic <x> not found`; name: `Topic "<x>" not found`; with flags:
  `Topic <x> not found`

stdout stays empty in every format, for these and every other failure (TS pretty has
already printed the banner, D57).

### 7.5 JSON shapes (bare array for lists, bare object for gets)

Profile: `{profileId, profileName, revision, active, createdBy, updatedBy,
lastModifiedTs, policy, dlpTenantId}` in that order (`dlpTenantId` from 8.0, only when the
record carries `dlp_tenant_id`, §13.17), unset fields omitted, `csp_id`, `tsg_id` and
unknown top-level fields dropped; `policy` is the SDK `Policy` model serialised
(schema-ordered known keys, then unknown keys sorted; extensions included). Every profile
read is validated without the SDK's response defaults (§15.25 point 4).

Topic: `{topicId, topicName, revision, active, description, examples, createdBy,
updatedBy, lastModifiedTs, createdTs}`; `examples` is always present (`[]` when
absent on the wire); unknown fields dropped.

### 7.6 Pretty and table layouts (R§3.1–R§3.4 hold the byte captures)

The primitives, cell rules, colours and empty-list rules are §2.7 and §2.8. Every pretty
layout starts with the **banner** `banner("Prisma AIRS — Runtime Configuration",
"Security profile and topic management")` (em dash U+2014; decoration), buffered like
all stdout. Rows are printed in the order §7.2 produces.

**Profile list** (`profiles list`, and `profiles get --all-versions` without its status
line):
- pretty: banner; when empty, `  No profiles found\n` and nothing else. Otherwise
  section `Security Profiles:`, then per profile the ID line `  <profileId>\n` (data,
  D55; omitted when the profile has no `profile_id`, D56) and the name line
  `    <profileName>  <active|inactive>[ rev:<revision>]\n` (data; the ` rev:` part only
  when `revision` is present, `0` included); finally `\n` (data).
- table: columns `ID │ Name │ Active │ Revision` from `profileId`, `profileName`,
  `active`, `revision` (absent → empty cell). Empty list → nothing on stdout.

**Profile detail** (`profiles get`, with or without `--revision`):
- pretty: banner, section `Profile Detail:`, one key/value block, then `\n`. Pairs in
  this order: `ID` (always; empty when absent), `Name` (always), `Status` (always,
  `active`/`inactive`), `Revision` (when present, `0` included), `Created` /
  `Updated` / `Modified` (when `createdBy` / `updatedBy` / `lastModifiedTs` is
  non-empty), `Policy` (when present, `{}` included). The key width is the longest
  included key (8 with `Revision` or `Modified`). The `Policy` value is the §7.5
  `policy` in the `JSON.stringify(policy, null, 2)` layout (`json::to_pretty`, unknown
  keys sorted, D60) with every `"\n"` replaced by `"\n  "`, then `terminal_safe`d
  (which there changes only DEL and C1 controls); its continuation lines therefore start
  at column 2 plus the JSON indent, not under the value column (TS). Everything but the
  banner and the section is printed under `--quiet`.
- table: `Key │ Value` with **all eight** keys in the §7.5 order `profileId,
  profileName, revision, active, createdBy, updatedBy, lastModifiedTs, policy`; an unset
  key is a row with an empty value (the JSON omits it); `policy` is compact JSON on one
  line, however long.

**Topic list** (`topics list`, and `topics get --all-versions` without its status line):
- pretty: banner; when empty, `  No topics found\n` and nothing else. Otherwise section
  `Custom Topics:`, then per topic the ID line `  <topicId>\n` (data, D55; omitted
  without `topic_id`, D56) and the name line
  `    <topicName> rev:<revision>[ — <description preview>]\n`; finally `\n`. The
  ` — …` part (em dash) appears only for a non-empty description. The preview is the
  longest prefix of at most 80 UTF-16 code units that does not split a character, with
  **no** ellipsis (the D43 helper without `...`, D54), then `terminal_safe`.
- table: columns `ID │ Name │ Revision │ Description` from `topicId`, `topicName`,
  `revision`, `description`; the description is **not** truncated. Empty list → nothing
  on stdout.

**Topic detail** (`topics get`):
- pretty: banner, section `Topic Detail:`, then
  1. a key/value block: `ID` (always; empty when absent), `Name` (always), `Revision`,
     `Description` (when non-empty), with its own width (11 with `Description`, else 8);
  2. when `examples` is non-empty: `  Examples:\n` (plain data), then per example a
     neutral bullet `  • <example>\n`;
  3. a second key/value block, only when it has a pair, with its **own** width:
     `Created`, `Updated`, `Modified` (when `createdBy` / `updatedBy` /
     `lastModifiedTs` is non-empty);
  4. `\n`.

  `active` and `createdTs` are not shown in pretty.
- table: `Key │ Value` with **all ten** keys in the §7.5 order `topicId, topicName,
  revision, active, description, examples, createdBy, updatedBy, lastModifiedTs,
  createdTs`; unset keys are empty rows; `examples` is compact JSON (`[]` when absent).

## 8. M3 scanning

### 8.1 Input validation (usage errors, exit 2, before the tenant is read)

- Empty content (prompt `""` and no non-empty `--response`):
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:At least one of prompt, response, codePrompt, codeResponse, or toolEvent must be provided`
- `--profile ""`: `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for POST /v1/scan/sync/request did not match schema: ai_profile: custom`
- profile name longer than 100 UTF-16 code units:
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for POST /v1/scan/sync/request did not match schema: ai_profile.profile_name: too_big`
- prompt / response over 2,097,152 UTF-8 bytes:
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:prompt exceeds max length of 2097152 bytes`
  (`response …` likewise)

### 8.2 Request

From 8.1, optional `--scanner NAME` selects the exact named scanner (§3.15, D342).
Validate its syntax before tenant access. Without it, preserve flat credentials;
a named-only tenant requires explicit selection. The selected endpoint and single
credential replace the flat scanner configuration only in the invocation.

`POST {airsApiEndpoint}/v1/scan/sync/request`, body
`{"ai_profile":{"profile_name":"<P>"},"contents":[{"prompt":"<X>"[,"response":"<R>"]}]}`.
An empty `--response ""` is omitted. Headers from the SDK: `x-pan-token` +
`x-payload-hash` (key), `Authorization: Bearer` (token), both when both configured.
Exactly one POST; never replayed.

Order: input validation → debug log (with `--debug`, §2.9) → tenant → scanner
credentials → client → status lines → request. The status lines are the same in every
format. Status lines (stderr, quiet-suppressed):
```
  Prisma AIRS Runtime Scan
  Profile: <profile>
  Prompt:  "<first 80 characters>[...]"
```
"First 80 characters" means the longest prefix of at most 80 UTF-16 code units that
does not split a character: a character straddling the boundary is dropped, and `...`
follows whenever the prompt is longer (D43).

### 8.3 Result normalisation

- `prompt detections`: for keys `topic_violation, injection, toxic_content, dlp,
  url_cats, malicious_code, source_code, agent` (this order) whose `prompt_detected`
  value is a boolean.
- `response detections`: for keys `topic_violation, toxic_content, dlp, url_cats,
  malicious_code, agent, db_security, ungrounded` whose `response_detected` value is a
  boolean.
- `triggered` = any prompt **or response** detection is true.
- `action`: lower-cased server action; `allow` and `block` pass through.
  **Fail closed**: `error == true`, `timeout == true` or any other action → `failed`
  with `category = "error"` and an error reason: the `errors[]` entries joined as
  `<feature>: <status>: <content_type>` (`; ` between entries), else
  `AIRS scan timed out`, `AIRS scan failed`, or `Unknown AIRS action: <action>`.
- Server text is untrusted (§6 applies to it as to request IDs): each reason part, the
  unknown action, the category, `scan_id` and `report_id` is replaced by `[withheld]`
  when it contains a configured secret (raw, trimmed, form-encoded or base64, or a
  sizeable fragment of one); each reason part is cut to 200 characters plus `...`.
- Exit 0 for `allow` and `block`; for `failed` the result is still printed on stdout
  (in the selected format), then `\n  ✗ Error: AIRS scan did not complete: <reason>\n\n`
  on stderr and exit 1.

### 8.4 Pretty output (stdout)

```
\n  Scan Result\n\n                  (heading: quiet-suppressed)
  Action     <ALLOW|BLOCK|FAILED>
  Category   <category>
  Triggered  <yes|no>
  Scan ID    <scan_id>
  Report ID  <report_id>
[  Error      <reason>]                  (failed only; every value terminal-safe, §2.2)
[\n  Detections\n\n                      (heading: quiet-suppressed, only if any true)
  ● <prompt key>                         (true prompt detections, fixed order)
  ● response.<key>]                      (true response detections, fixed order)
```

The lines are a key/value block of width 9 (§2.7) and flag bullets. Colours (§2.8):
heading and `Detections` bold, keys dim, `BLOCK` and `FAILED` red, `ALLOW` green, `yes`
red, `no` green, the Scan ID and Report ID values dim, `●` yellow (R§3.10).

### 8.5 JSON output (`--output json`, Rust-only)

```json
{
  "profileName": "<P>",
  "scanId": "...",
  "reportId": "...",
  "action": "allow|block|failed",
  "category": "...",
  "triggered": false,
  "detections": { "<prompt key>": true, ... },
  "responseDetections": { "<response key>": false, ... },
  "error": "<reason, failed only>",
  "result": { "<the SDK ScanResponse serialised, unknown fields preserved>": "..." }
}
```
Prompt and response text are never echoed in data output. `scanId`, `reportId`,
`category` and `error` carry the withheld values of §8.3; in `result` every string
that contains a configured secret is `[withheld]` and every object entry whose key
contains one is dropped (D47).

### 8.6 Table output (`--output table`, Rust-only, D5)

The TS detail-table convention: a `Key │ Value` table (§2.7) of the §8.5 record without
`result`, rows in the order `profileName, scanId, reportId, action, category,
triggered, detections, responseDetections`, plus `error` last for a failed scan.
`detections` and `responseDetections` are compact JSON objects in their fixed key order;
`triggered` is `true`/`false`; the values carry the withheld forms of §8.3. No heading.
The status lines, the stderr failure line and the exit code are those of pretty.

## 9. M1 doctor (scoped subset of the TypeScript checks)

After configuration and OAuth lease discovery, every check detail/hint passes the
invocation SecretSet and terminal filter before JSON, pretty or table rendering.
Known credential coincidences in local paths are withheld (§3.15).

Checks, always all nine (seven before 0.10, eight before 8.0), in order: `Executable` (§21.15, D331),
`Tenant`, `Config file`, `Environment`, `Scanner credentials`, `Management credentials`, `Scanner API`,
`Management OAuth`, `Gateway API` (§19.16). `Executable` reads only `PATH` and the running executable and is
evaluated before the tenant; "every later check" below means the checks after `Tenant`.
JSON: array of `{name, status, detail[, hint]}` (`hint` omitted when absent); statuses
`pass|warn|fail|skip`. Exit 1 iff any `fail`. `notEvaluated` =
`skip` / `not evaluated — fix the failed checks above first` (em dash U+2014).

| Check | Outcomes (detail / hint) |
|---|---|
| Tenant | pass `<name> (TSG <tsg>) selected in <D>/config.toml` (with `--tenant`: `<name> (TSG <tsg>) selected by --tenant in <D>/config.toml`); fail `no tenant selected (registered: a, b)` / hint `Run 'airs tenant switch <name>'`; **import case** (D89): when `config.toml` does not exist and the TypeScript registry of §3.13 exists (the existence check of §3.4; the file is not opened), fail `no airs tenants in <D>/config.toml; a TypeScript tenant registry exists at <registry>` / hint `Run 'airs tenant import' to copy its tenants (the TypeScript files are not changed)`, whatever `--tenant` says; otherwise fail `no tenants registered in <D>/config.toml` / hint `Run 'airs tenant create <name>' (prompts for TSG ID, client ID and secret), then 'airs tenant switch <name>'`; fail `Tenant not found: <name> (registered: …)` (`--tenant`); a store error (§3.1, §3.2, §3.8) → fail with the error message and hint `Fix or restore <D>/config.toml` (`Set AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR or XDG_CONFIG_HOME to an absolute path` when no directory can be resolved, D25) — then every later check is notEvaluated. |
| Config file | notEvaluated when no tenant. The checks of §3.3 in order, the first failure reported, `<path>` = `D/tenants/<name>.toml`, `<tenant>` = the selected tenant's name (substituted; `<key>`, `<tsg>` and `<name>` stay literal): fail `not found at <path>` / hint `Restore the file, or delete the tenant with 'airs tenant delete <tenant>' and create it again`; fail `<path> is not private: it must be a regular file (not a symlink) owned by the current user with no group or other permissions` (every §3.8 refusal: a symlink, a directory or other non-regular file, a foreign owner, group/other mode bits; also for an unsafe `D/tenants`, naming that directory) / hint `Make it a regular file owned by you with mode 0600 (directories 0700), then re-run doctor`; fail `<path> cannot be read (not a regular file, larger than 1 MiB, or unreadable)` (larger than 1 MiB, or an I/O error such as missing read permission); fail `<path> is not valid TOML` (also for invalid UTF-8) / hint `Fix the file, then re-run doctor`; fail `<path> has unknown keys: a, b` (byte order) / hint, when any of them is a TypeScript name: `TypeScript names are not accepted: aiGw* keys are now gateway*, agentGuard* keys are now supplychain*, and dataDir, typesafe* and *TokenEndpoint keys were dropped; edit the file or re-import it with 'airs tenant import --replace'`, otherwise `Remove them from the file; 'airs tenant set <tenant> <key>' accepts only the supported keys` (D89: TS warns and points at `tenant unset`, which refuses them); fail `<path> has invalid values for: k1, k2` (key names only, schema order) / hint `Correct them in the file, then re-run doctor (values are never printed here; 'airs tenant set' refuses an invalid file)` (not `tenant set`: it reads the whole file strictly before changing it, D89), extended by `; defaultOutput accepts only pretty, table or json (markdown, csv and yaml were dropped)` when `defaultOutput` is one of the keys (D51); fail `<path> carries a different mgmtTsgId than the registration (TSG <registered>)` / hint `Choose the TSG with 'airs tenant set <tenant> mgmtTsgId <tsg>'; it updates both files` (D83); pass `valid tenant config at <path> (TSG <tsg> matches registration)`. There is no warn outcome: an unknown key makes the file invalid (D72). |
| Environment | warn `ignored N variable(s): A, B` / hint `Configuration comes only from tenant files ('airs tenant set <name> <key>'); unset these`; pass `no configuration variables set`. When any proxy variable (`HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, http_proxy, ALL_PROXY, all_proxy, NO_PROXY, no_proxy`) is non-empty, append `; proxy variables in effect: <names>` (names of the variables set; they apply to https endpoints only, §2.6; a macOS system proxy is not detected or reported). Never `fail`. |
| Scanner credentials | pass `airsApiKey (file)[, airsApiToken (file)]`; skip `not configured — runtime scan, bulk-scan and topics eval are unavailable` / hint remedy(airsApiKey); notEvaluated when the config failed. |
| Management credentials | pass `set: mgmtClientId (file), mgmtClientSecret (file), mgmtTsgId (file)`; missing → **warn** when scanner credentials passed, else **fail**: `missing: <keys> — management, red team, model security, gateway and supplychain commands are unavailable` (from 0.11, D312; 0.10 `… gateway and AgentGuard commands …`, D227; TS `… AI Gateway and AgentGuard commands …`) / hint remedy(missing); notEvaluated when the config failed. |
| Scanner API | `GET {airsApiEndpoint}/v1/scan/results?scan_ids=<random uuid v4>` within 5 s. skip `skipped — no scanner credentials configured`; notEvaluated when credentials were not evaluated; pass `endpoint reachable, API key accepted` (2xx); fail `API key rejected (HTTP <s>): <message>` (401/403) / hint `Verify airsApiKey belongs to this tenant and is not expired`; pass `endpoint reachable, API key accepted (HTTP <s> on probe query)` (other 4xx except 429); warn `endpoint reachable, but rate limited (HTTP 429): <message>` / hint `Retry later`; fail `scanner API error (HTTP <s>): <message>` (5xx) / hint `Retry later; check the AIRS service status`; fail `timed out after 5000ms — network unreachable or endpoint not responding` / hint `Check network connectivity and the airsApiEndpoint setting` (only when no HTTP error status was received). The probe makes exactly one attempt (`RequestOptions::with_retries(0)`, D49): a 429 or 5xx is classified at once, whatever `airsNumRetries` says. A deadline is still classified by the last HTTP error status the client received, so it is never described as a timeout when the endpoint answered; fail `network unreachable: <message>` / hint `Check network connectivity, proxy settings, and DNS`; fail `<endpoint error message>` / hint `Fix airsApiEndpoint in the tenant file`. The timeout text is derived from the 5 s probe budget. |
| Management OAuth | token then `GET {mgmt}/v1/mgmt/topics/tsg/{tsg}` walk (`list_all`, limit 100), all within one 5 s budget. skip `skipped — management credentials not configured`; notEvaluated when credentials were not evaluated; pass `OAuth token obtained, topics API answered (<n> custom topic[s])` (`at least <n>` when truncated); fail `management API error (HTTP <s>): <message>` (token non-2xx — TS wording, observed in docs/research/ts-baseline-observed.md), `authentication failed: <message>` (token decode), `network unreachable: <message>` (token or API transport), `management API error (HTTP <s>): <message>` (API error status; one attempt per request, D49, so a `401`/`403` is reported without the §5 refresh and replay, and a 429/5xx without retries; a deadline is classified by the last HTTP error status, as for the Scanner API), `management API error: <message>` / hint `Fix mgmtEndpoint in the tenant file` (a 2xx topics answer that is malformed or over a size limit: the token worked, so neither an "HTTP 200" error nor a credential hint), timeout text / hint `Check network connectivity and the mgmtTokenEndpoint / mgmtEndpoint settings` for timeouts, otherwise `Verify mgmtClientId / mgmtClientSecret / mgmtTsgId belong to this tenant`; endpoint/TSG configuration errors → fail with that message. |
| Gateway API | (from 0.10, §19.16, D250) `GET {gatewayDataEndpoint}/workspaces` with the `Management OAuth` token, one attempt within its own 5 s budget. skip `skipped — management credentials not configured`; notEvaluated when credentials were not evaluated or `Management OAuth` failed at the token request or could not build its client (choice 100); pass `endpoint reachable (<n> workspace[s] in scope)`; warn `endpoint reachable, but access denied (HTTP 403): <message>` / the data-plane grant hint; warn `endpoint reachable, but rate limited (HTTP 429): <message>` / `Retry later`; fail `gateway API error (HTTP <s>): <message>` (5xx / `Retry later; check the AIRS service status`; other statuses / `Verify the tenant credentials and network connectivity`); fail `gateway API error: <message>` / `Fix gatewayDataEndpoint in the tenant file` (an undecodable 2xx); fail `network unreachable: <message>` / `Check network connectivity, proxy settings, and DNS`; fail `timed out after 5000ms — network unreachable or endpoint not responding` / `Check network connectivity and the gatewayDataEndpoint setting`; an inadmissible `gatewayDataEndpoint` fails with the D48 message / `Fix gatewayDataEndpoint in the tenant file`. |

Pretty rendering (stdout unless noted):
```
\n  Doctor\n  Prisma AIRS CLI preflight checks\n\n         (quiet-suppressed)
  <✓|⚠|✗|○> <name> — <detail>                       (pass|warn|fail|skip)
      <hint>                                          (6 spaces, quiet-suppressed)
\n
  ✓ All checks passed[ (<n> warning[s], <n> skipped)]   (stdout)  |  ✗ <n> check[s] failed (stderr)
\n
```
Summary detail: `(1 warning, 2 skipped)`; only the non-zero parts are shown,
`All checks passed` alone when there are none. Colours (§2.8): header title bold and
subtitle dim, the glyph per status (`✓` green, `⚠` and `○` yellow, `✗` red), the hint
dim, the summary green or red as one span.

Table (`--output table`, R§3.9): the §2.7 table with columns `Name │ Status │ Detail │
Hint` over the nine checks, `status` as the raw `pass|warn|fail|skip`, an absent hint
as an empty cell, `detail` and `hint` through `terminal_safe`. No header, no summary,
nothing on stderr (the failure summary is not printed either), and `--quiet` changes
nothing. Exit 1 iff any check failed. The TS table has eleven rows (D19), so its widths
differ.

## 10. Test architecture

Tiers (specified here; [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) explains how to run and extend them):

1. **Unit** (`cargo test --lib`): pure logic (store, tenant-file and TypeScript-file
   validation, canonical TOML bytes, the lock record, atomic-write steps, JS number
   coercion, env report, output resolution, message mapping, normalisation, signal
   decisions).
2. **Loopback executable tests** (`cargo test`): `tests/*.rs` spawn the real
   `airs` binary (with the inherited `PATH` minus every entry that holds an `airs`, `airs-cli` or
   `airs-cli-rs`, so an installed copy never changes the doctor's `Executable` check, §21.15) (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_airs`, §21.6; and, for `tests/parity_*.rs`, the TypeScript reference
   `node .reference/prisma-airs-cli/dist/cli/index.js`) against the in-process fixture
   server from `crates/airs-test-harness`. They can never reach a non-loopback host:
   every endpoint in every fixture tenant is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`, and a
   planned `location`/`content-location` header must be relative or loopback (the TS
   CLI follows redirects with its credentials, D30), or planning it panics.
3. **Live** (`tests/live.rs`, logic in `airs_test_harness::live`): both CLIs against
   one explicitly selected, existing tenant. Run it with
   `AIRS_RS_LIVE=1 AIRS_E2E_TENANT=<name> [AIRS_E2E_PROFILE=<profile>] cargo test --test live -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`.
   Without both `AIRS_RS_LIVE=1` and `AIRS_E2E_TENANT` the test prints one
   `LIVE SKIPPED: <reason>` line to the real stderr and passes. Without
   `AIRS_E2E_PROFILE` it runs no scans and says so in the summary.
   `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MAX_SCANS` (default 8, at most 20; anything else fails the run) bounds
   scan invocations across both CLIs, and a counter is checked before each scan. With
   `AIRS_E2E_PROFILE` set, the plan has 8 scan invocations, and a budget smaller than
   that fails the run before anything is started. Without a profile no scans run and
   the budget is only range-checked.
   - Isolation: the registry path is resolved as in §3.13 from the test process's
     `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `HOME`. The registry is read only
     to extract the selected entry (`configPath` must be absolute), and an isolated
     registry holding only that entry, active, is written into a temp sandbox. Both
     CLIs run with a cleared environment: `PATH`, `HOME=<sandbox>/home`,
     `TMPDIR=<sandbox>/tmp`, `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH=<isolated registry>`,
     `NO_COLOR=1`; no credential, `PANW_*`, proxy or `NODE_OPTIONS` variable reaches
     them. The TypeScript CLI reads the tenant config in place. The test reads the
     config bytes in memory only, to hash them and to build the leak-check secret set
     (each secret-named value raw, JS-trimmed, URL-encoded and unpadded base64, plus the
     Basic pair); no value is printed, logged or written.
   - Rust store (from 0.3). The Rust side needs the tenant in its TOML store (§3), so
     the flow (`airs_test_harness::live::LiveStore`) creates
     `<store root>/store-<run id>/` (mode 0700, created exclusively; `<run id>` is the
     Unix time, the pid and a per-process counter; the store root is
     `LivePlan::store_root`, default `<workspace>/target/live` for the real tenant and
     `<sandbox>/tmp/live-stores` for a loopback self-test, which refuses, before
     creating or sweeping anything, a store root outside its sandbox and, before each
     run, any path variable or argument outside its sandbox or the session's own,
     `escape_violation_within`) and runs, first of all,
     `airs tenant import --from <isolated registry> --name <tenant> --output json`
     with `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR=<that directory>` and the cleared environment. The
     isolated registry's one entry names the real config, so this copies the real
     tenant while the real registry is read only by the harness, as before. The import
     run is leak- and integrity-checked like every run but is not counted as a check
     run; it must exit 0 with exactly one `import` row for the tenant and the status
     `Selected <tenant> (selected in the TypeScript registry)` (§3.12), or the flow
     stops with a setup error that names no value. Every later Rust run gets
     `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR=<that directory>`; the TypeScript runs do not get it. The
     directory holds a copy of the tenant's secrets, so it is removed with
     `remove_dir_all` on success, on failure and on panic: the checks run inside
     `catch_unwind`, the store is removed, then the panic is re-raised or the result
     returned, and the guard's `Drop` removes it on every other path (a setup failure
     after it was created). The summary records whether the removal succeeded
     (`storeRemoved`; `false` fails the test). A run killed before the guard ran
     (SIGKILL, a power loss) leaves it behind: every flow first removes each
     `store-*` directory under the store root whose modification time is at least
     1 hour old, and reports how many (`staleStoresRemoved`). Younger ones are kept,
     because they may belong to a flow running at the same time (the loopback
     self-tests run in parallel). The import reads the real config read-only (§3.12),
     which the integrity check below confirms.
   - Integrity: the real registry, the real config and the isolated registry are
     fingerprinted (sha256, mode, mtime, the symlink and its target, and sibling names
     that start with the file name, such as `tenants.json.lock`) before the first run
     (the import included) and re-checked after every run. A change stops the run at
     once, as does a secret, or JWT-shaped text, on either CLI's stdout or stderr.
   - Only the orchestrator (the user) runs the live tier. Agents never set
     `AIRS_RS_LIVE=1`.
   - Checks, each on both CLIs with a 90 s timeout per run (a timed-out run is killed
     and counts as a mismatch): `tenant read <name> --output json` and
     `tenant get <name> <key> --output json` for six keys (same keys in the same order,
     secret keys `[REDACTED]` or empty on both, other values equal; D45 tolerated);
     The `tenant read` / `tenant get` comparison maps the TypeScript rows through the
     import conversion of §3.12 first (renamed keys renamed; `dataDir`, `typesafe*`,
     empty values and unknown keys dropped; D71, D72), so the remaining rows must be
     equal;
     `doctor --output json` and `--output pretty` (the seven shared checks have equal
     statuses, and each CLI exits 1 exactly when one of its own checks failed; D19,
     D20 tolerated); `runtime profiles list --all --max 500` and
     `runtime topics list --limit 20` (same multiset of `(name, revision, active)`),
     and the same two listings with `--output table` (both one §2.7 table with the
     §7.6 header and the same multiset of rows of trimmed cells; padding is not
     compared, D53; when airs-cli-rs shows a replaced control character, a TS table
     broken by it is tolerated by row count, D52);
     `runtime profiles get` / `runtime topics get` of the first listed name (every
     §7.5 field semantically equal); `runtime profiles get` of a missing name (same
     non-zero exit). With a profile: a benign prompt, a prompt-injection prompt and a
     prompt + response pair, run with `--output json` (TS prints pretty, D5); each must
     print a verdict on both CLIs; action, category, the true prompt detections and the
     exit codes must be equal, TS Triggered must equal "any Rust prompt detection" and
     Rust Triggered "any prompt or response detection" (D7), and TS must report no
     response detections. The benign prompt must be allowed by both; whether the
     injection was blocked is reported, not asserted. A content scan that does not
     complete on both CLIs (a timeout, a non-zero exit, no verdict, a Rust `failed`, or
     a TS `error` category, which is how TS shows a failed scan, D6) is a mismatch even
     where D6 makes the outputs agree, and it stops the scan series: the scans after it
     are named in a notice and not run. A scan with a missing profile name must exit
     non-zero, identically, on both, or be a Rust `failed` with exit 1 against a TS
     `ALLOW` / `error` with exit 0 (D6). Scan and report IDs, timestamps and latencies
     are never compared. The budget counts invocations, not requests: the TypeScript
     CLI may re-POST a scan on 5xx or network errors up to the tenant's
     `airsNumRetries` (D9). Stopping the series at the first incomplete scan limits
     that to one TypeScript retry chain per run.
   - Results: mismatches are collected and fail the test after every check ran. The
     summary (stderr, and `target/live/summary.json`) holds only check names, exit
     codes, agreement, verdict tokens (`action/category/triggered`), notes made of
     field and check names, counts and §12 row numbers, and the number of scan
     invocations and of runs of each CLI: no IDs, tokens, paths, config values, prompt
     text, or profile and topic content.
   - Guard: the flow never goes through `spawn`, so the loopback guard below is
     unchanged. `LiveTarget::real` refuses unless the test process has
     `AIRS_RS_LIVE=1`. `LiveTarget::loopback` needs no opt-in because it takes a harness
     `Sandbox`: before reading either file, the flow refuses a registry or an entry
     `configPath` that does not resolve inside that sandbox, so a normal run never
     reads a real tenant file. It then refuses a config that fails the loopback-endpoint
     guard. The normal suite uses it to run the whole flow against the fixture server
     (gating, isolation, integrity, budget, comparison, the early scan stop, a planned
     divergence for each comparison rule, a check that both CLIs ran every check, and a
     summary checked free of fixture secrets, IDs and descriptions).
   - **M4 write flow** (0.4, D93–D117; S§11 within the MILESTONES live rules). It runs
     only when `AIRS_RS_LIVE_WRITES=1` is set as well; otherwise the summary says
     `writes skipped` and nothing is written. It is a separate flow (its own run id,
     `LiveStore` and summary) called from `tests/live.rs`, with the isolation,
     integrity and leak checks above and a 90 s timeout per run.
     - Own resources only. The run creates at most 10 resources; a counter is checked
       before every create command and the cap cannot be raised. The planned flow
       creates 4: `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-topic-rs`, `-topic-ts`, `-profile-rs` and
       `-profile-ts`, where `<run id>` is the `LiveStore` run id `<unix>-<pid>-<n>`
       (so a name carries its creation time). Updates, applies and reverts touch only
       these. Nothing that existed before the run is updated or deleted, and no topic is
       applied to a profile the run did not create.
     - Ledger. Every create, update, apply, revert and delete is journalled to
       `<store root>/ledger.jsonl` (`target/live/ledger.jsonl` for the real tenant;
       `<sandbox>/tmp/live-stores/ledger.jsonl` for a loopback self-test): created 0600,
       opened `O_APPEND`, one JSON object per line, never rewritten. A line with outcome
       `pending` is written before the command and a result line after it:
       `{"v":1,"ts":<UTC>,"run":<run id>,"phase":"flow|teardown|cleanup","cli":"rs|ts","op":<op>,"kind":"topic|profile","name":<name>,"id":<uuid or null>,"outcome":"pending|ok|failed|unknown|skipped","exit":<code>,"note":<§12 row numbers or check names>}`.
       It never holds a token, a credential, the tenant name, TSG or endpoints, prompt
       text, descriptions, policy content or error text. The result outcome is `failed`
       only when the write was certainly not applied: exit 0 is `ok`; a timeout or exit
       130/143 is `unknown`; for airs-cli-rs, an `Outcome unknown: …` or
       `(outcome unknown)` line is `unknown`, an `Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but …`
       line (applied, the answer unreadable or without an id) is `ok`, and any other
       failure is `failed`; TypeScript prints no outcome line, so its failures are
       `unknown` unless it exited 2 (usage) or its error block names `HTTP <4xx>` other
       than 404, 408, 409 and 429 (which can follow an applied, retried attempt, D95).
       The teardown and the sweeper count a delete as deleted when it is `ok`.
     - Preflight (read-only): Rust `runtime topics list --all-versions --all` and
       `runtime profiles list --all --all-versions` (json); no planned name may exist.
       When the tenant's `mgmtEndpoint` is set and is not the §5 default, every
       TypeScript `topics create|apply|revert` step is skipped with a D93 note, because
       TypeScript would send it to the default host; the flow never adds `PANW_*`
       variables.
     - Steps: Rust and TypeScript `topics create` (their own names; Rust with
       `--output json`, TypeScript with `--format json`, whose stderr warning is
       expected, D94; where TypeScript has no JSON its id is read from its outcome
       line), polled with
       `topics get` (at most 5 tries, 2 s apart); Rust `topics create` again on
       `topic-rs` (the update path; whether the id changed is recorded) and
       `topics update <id> --config <file>`; Rust and TypeScript
       `profiles create --prompt-injection block` and
       `profiles update <name> --prompt-injection alert` (whether the id changed is
       recorded); `topics apply` (Rust on the `-rs` pair, TypeScript on the `-ts` pair),
       then `profiles get` on both, comparing the topic-guardrails shape semantically
       (action, names, pinned revision; D98 tolerated); `topics revert --force` (Rust
       must exit 0 with the topic deleted, or exit 0 with the D99 kept-topic warning
       when the service still holds a reference, recorded as a note; TypeScript is
       expected to exit 1 with `updatedBy is required` and its topic still present, D99
       evidence, not a mismatch).
     - Teardown, always (also on failure and panic, inside `catch_unwind` like
       `LiveStore`): for every id listed under each planned name (all revisions),
       profiles first and then topics, the Rust CLI's plain `delete` answered `y` on the
       pty helper. It never uses `--force` (a forced topic delete would also strip the
       topic from any other profile). A failure is reported and left to the sweeper.
       The summary records `resourcesCreated`, `resourcesDeleted` and `resourcesLeft`
       (counts only); `resourcesLeft > 0` fails the run.
     - `profiles cleanup` never runs live (it is tenant-wide), and no TypeScript delete
       is used.
   - **Sweeper** (`live_cleanup`, only with `AIRS_RS_LIVE_CLEANUP=1` as well; safe to
     re-run). It lists every topic and profile revision with the Rust CLI (complete
     walks, or it deletes nothing) and selects only names that fully match
     `^airs-rs-e2e-([0-9]{10})-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-(topic|profile)-(rs|ts)$` whose embedded
     Unix time is at least 3,600 s before now; younger ones may belong to a running
     flow. It deletes at most 20 per invocation (the oldest first; the rest are
     reported), profiles first, with the plain Rust delete on the pty; a 409 is reported
     and skipped. Each delete is journalled with phase `cleanup`. A re-run finds only
     what is left.
   - **Eval** (`live_eval`, only with `AIRS_RS_LIVE_EVAL=1` as well). It requires
     `AIRS_E2E_PROFILE` to be `Prisma AIRS Harness` (anything else fails before
     starting) and creates nothing. Its scan budget `AIRS_RS_LIVE_EVAL_MAX_SCANS`
     (default 4, range 4–8; anything else fails the run) counts CSV rows × CLIs before
     each eval run, and the flow is its own run, so the 8-scan cap per run holds. The
     CSV is the Rust `topics sample` output (2 rows, D113). Both CLIs run
     `topics eval --profile "Prisma AIRS Harness" --prompts <csv> --concurrency 1
     --rate 1` (Rust with `--output json`, TypeScript pretty); both must complete with
     equal TP/TN/FP/FN, or Rust must report a scan that did not complete where
     TypeScript counted it (D111). The metrics measure the profile as it is; no topic is
     applied to it.
   - **M4 implementation rules** (`live::writes`, `live::ledger`, `live::cleanup`,
     `live::eval`; tests `live_write_flow`, `live_cleanup`, `live_eval` in
     `tests/live.rs`, each printing `LIVE SKIPPED: <reason>` without its opt-in):
     - Each flow is gated by `AIRS_RS_LIVE=1`, `AIRS_E2E_TENANT` and its own variable
       (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_WRITES=1`, `AIRS_RS_LIVE_CLEANUP=1`, `AIRS_RS_LIVE_EVAL=1`), opens
       its own `Session` (private store, import, fingerprints, leak checks) and writes its
       summary to `target/live/summary-writes.json`, `summary-cleanup.json` or
       `summary-eval.json` (real runs only).
     - The resource counter is checked before each of the 5 planned create commands
       (`topics create` twice on `topic-rs`, once on `topic-ts`, one `profiles create`
       per CLI); `MAX_RESOURCES` is a constant.
     - Listings are Rust `--all --all-versions --max 0 --output json`; one that does not
       exit 0 with an array stops the step and nothing is deleted from it.
     - The teardown deletes only after the preflight proved that no planned name existed;
       a flow stopped by its preflight deletes nothing. `resourcesCreated` is the number
       of distinct ids seen under the planned names, `resourcesDeleted` counts the
       revert's topic deletion and the teardown's, and `resourcesLeft` the rows still
       listed under a planned name (an unreadable final listing counts as left).
     - The session itself refuses to start a TypeScript `topics create|apply|revert`
       unless the target is real and its `mgmtEndpoint` is unset or the default (a
       loopback target never allows it), on top of the flow's skip. The command is found
       among the positionals (flags and the values of `--output` and `--tenant` skipped,
       everything after `--` included; `topics` followed by `create`, `apply` or
       `revert` anywhere after `runtime`), so a leading global flag does not get past
       it; a skipped step is
       journalled with outcome `skipped` and note `D93`.
     - The guardrail comparison is per side: the item's action, each group's action, the
       run's topic as `<topic>`, and whether its ref pins the topic's current revision
       (the two topics have different revisions); Rust must match the `--intent block`
       shape of §13.4, TypeScript (when it ran) the same shape.
     - Ledger lines name only `airs-rs-e2e-…` resources, UUID ids and fixed vocabulary
       (`Ledger::record` refuses anything else); `run` is the store's run id.
     - The eval checks the profile and the 4–8 budget, and the 2 rows × 2 CLIs, before it
       opens anything (no store, no request); each eval run then reserves its CSV rows.
       TypeScript runs even when the Rust eval stopped (the D111 comparison needs both).
   - **M5 bulk flow** (0.5, §14; A§9 within the MILESTONES live rules). Bulk scans are
     billed, so it runs only when `AIRS_RS_LIVE_BULK=1` is set as well (`live_bulk` in
     `tests/live.rs`, `live::bulk` in the harness; otherwise `LIVE SKIPPED: bulk skipped`),
     and it is its own run (run id, `Session`, private store via `tenant import`,
     fingerprints, leak checks, 90 s per run, `target/live/summary-bulk.json`).
     - Profile: `AIRS_E2E_PROFILE` must be `Prisma AIRS Harness` (anything else fails before
       anything is opened).
     - Budget: `AIRS_RS_LIVE_BULK_PROMPTS` prompts per CLI, default 4, range 2–8 (anything
       else fails the run before anything is opened). The planned total (N for Rust, plus N
       for TypeScript when its step runs) must be at most 8, the MILESTONES per-run cap, so
       N is at most 4 while the TypeScript step runs. The TypeScript decision below is made
       first, from the in-memory config, so the whole check happens before any run (the
       session calls it on the parsed config before it creates the private store or runs
       the import, `Session::open_checked`). Each run reserves its prompts before it starts
       (`bulk-scan` N, a `resume-poll` the number of `pending` items in the Rust state, the
       final no-op 0); a run that would exceed the budget is not started. The prompts R1
       did not send are returned (`ScanBudget::release`) before R2 reserves them, so each
       prompt is counted once and `scanInvocations` in the summary is the prompts reserved
       across both CLIs.
     - Prompts: a fixed, harmless 4-line `.txt` written to the run's temporary directory
       (two benign prompts, two plain prompt-injection probes, `live::bulk::BULK_PROMPTS`);
       the first N lines are used (repeated in order above 4, which only a run without the
       TypeScript step can reach).
     - Rust runs: `XDG_STATE_HOME=<sandbox>/tmp/state`, cwd `<sandbox>/tmp/rs`,
       `--output-file <sandbox>/tmp/rs/out.csv`, `--session-id airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-rs`,
       `--debug` (the log is under `tmp/state` too).
     - TypeScript isolation: its state directory is `<dirname(dataDir)>/bulk-scans` when the
       last component of `dataDir` is `runs`, else `<dataDir>/bulk-scans`, with `~`
       expanded from `HOME` (B§4; an absent, `null` or `""` `dataDir` is the default
       `~/.prisma-airs/runs`; `live::bulk::ts_state_dir`). With `HOME=<sandbox>/home` and a
       config without `dataDir`, or with a `dataDir` that starts with `~` and stays inside
       the session sandbox after normalisation, it lands in the sandbox; the run gets cwd `<sandbox>/tmp/ts`,
       `--output-file <sandbox>/tmp/ts/out.csv`, `--session-id airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-ts` and
       never `--debug` (TS would write every prompt verbatim). Afterwards exactly one
       `*.bulk-scan.json` must exist under that sandbox directory, else the flow aborts
       with an integrity error. Any other `dataDir` (absolute or relative) cannot be
       redirected while TypeScript still finds the tenant, so the TypeScript step is
       skipped with `LIVE NOTICE: TypeScript bulk-scan skipped: its state directory cannot be redirected into the sandbox`
       and Rust is compared with nothing. TypeScript never gets the real `HOME`, the
       repository as cwd, or a path outside the sandbox.
     - R1, `bulk-scan --profile "Prisma AIRS Harness" --file <prompts> --batch-size <ceil(N/2)>`:
       the runner sends SIGINT when the first `Scan IDs saved:` line appears on stderr
       (batch 1's receipts are durable then; an event, not a timer; `Session::run_in` reads
       stderr as it arrives and polls the trigger with the exit). Expected: exit 130 with
       `Interrupted; …` naming the state, or exit 0 when the run finished first.
     - The state (exactly one `*.bulk-scan.json` under `tmp/state/airs-cli/bulk-scans/`):
       the submitted prompts counted from its attempt journal are at most N. Two branches
       are accepted, each with deterministic assertions: (a) no `ambiguous` item; (b) the
       signal landed during batch 2's POST and that chunk is `ambiguous`. Anything else
       fails the flow.
     - R2, `resume-poll <state>`: (a) exit 0; the `airs.scan.async` records in its debug log
       equal the chunks of `pending` items at its start; the CSV has N rows in input order,
       each `allow` or `block` with a non-empty scan id and report id. (b) exit 1 with the
       ambiguous refusal and **zero** `airs.scan.async` records; the Rust part then ends as
       passed with a note.
     - R3 ((a) only), `resume-poll <state>` again: exit 0, **zero** debug records of any
       kind, the CSV byte-identical to R2's. Submitted prompts across R1–R3 equal N: the
       proof of recovery without new submissions.
     - T1 (when not skipped), TypeScript `bulk-scan` with the same prompts and batch size,
       uninterrupted: exit 0; the verdict tokens of each row (action, category, triggered,
       the eight detector flags) are compared by input index between the two CSVs
       (mismatches are reported, not fatal). Ids are never compared or printed.
     - Clean-up: the run's sandbox (state, CSVs, logs, the TypeScript state under
       `home/`) is removed with the store, also on failure and panic.
     - Summary: check names, exit codes, the branch taken, prompts planned and submitted,
       `airs.scan.async` records per run, verdict agreement; never prompts, ids, paths or
       values.
     - Self-tests (`live_bulk_self_test_branch_a_against_fixture`,
       `live_bulk_self_test_branch_b_against_fixture`,
       `live_bulk_skips_typescript_when_its_state_cannot_be_sandboxed`,
       `live_bulk_refuses_a_bad_budget_or_profile_before_any_request`) use
       `LiveTarget::loopback` against the async fixture routes. Branch (a) keeps the real
       trigger and adds a fixture event (`Trigger::ScanIdsSavedAnd`: the line was printed
       and the server holds batch 1's first poll), so the signal always lands while that
       receipt is being polled, however late it arrives; the held poll is released after
       the flow. Branch (b) cannot be reached with the `Scan IDs saved:` trigger, because that
       line precedes batch 1's polls; it uses `run_live_bulk_with` and a fixture event
       (`Trigger::When`: the server has received batch 2's POST, which it holds), so neither
       branch depends on timing. Both assert each prompt in exactly one airs-cli-rs POST
       (recovery without resubmission), and (a) that nothing outside the sandboxes changed
       (the target sandbox's snapshot, no default CSV in the repository). The skip test
       gives the tenant an absolute and a relative `dataDir`: the notice, no TypeScript
       run, and a 6-prompt Rust budget that fits once TypeScript is skipped. The refusal
       test covers 1 and 9 prompts, 5 prompts with the TypeScript step (10 > 8), another
       profile and none: no request and no store.
   - **M6a red team** (0.6, §15; RK§12 within the MILESTONES live rules). Three parts, each its
     own run (run id, `Session`, private store via `tenant import`, fingerprints, leak checks,
     90 s per CLI run unless a step says otherwise), in `live::redteam` (reads),
     `live::redteam_writes` and `live::redteam_scan`; tests `live_redteam_reads`,
     `live_redteam_writes` and `live_redteam_scan` in `tests/live.rs`, each printing
     `LIVE SKIPPED: <reason>` without its opt-in; summaries `target/live/summary-redteam.json`,
     `summary-redteam-writes.json`, `summary-redteam-scan.json` (real runs only). Summaries and
     the ledger never hold target, adapter, prompt-set, prompt or category names (other than the
     run's own `airs-rs-e2e-…` names), ids other than the run's own, prompt text, script text,
     credentials, report contents or paths.
     - **Reads** (`AIRS_RS_LIVE=1 AIRS_E2E_TENANT`; no further opt-in; read-only on both CLIs,
       the TypeScript CLI sandboxed as above). The first step is Rust
       `redteam categories --output json`; when it fails with HTTP 401, 403 or 404 the tenant has
       no red team access: the summary notes `redteam unavailable`, the rest is not run, and that
       is not a mismatch. The checks, with the comparison each uses:
       - both CLIs, stdout byte-equal (both pretty; the banner is the same): `redteam categories`,
         `redteam eula status`; D52 tolerated as for management tables.
       - both CLIs `--output json`, semantically equal (D35): `redteam languages`,
         `redteam languages --management`, `redteam properties list`, `redteam network-broker stats`,
         `redteam network-broker channels list`, `redteam adapter list`, `redteam targets metadata`
         (TS prints the document raw), and `redteam prompts list <first set> --limit 5`;
       - both `--output json`, set comparisons: `redteam list --limit 5` (the statuses of the ids
         listed by both; the newest jobs can change between the runs), `redteam targets list`
         (the multiset of `(name, status, type)`; also `--output table` cells as for §7.6 tables),
         `redteam prompt-sets list` (the TypeScript rows must be a subset of the Rust rows, D147);
       - in these json and table comparisons the TypeScript line of an empty list (exit 0,
         `  No scans found`, `  No targets found`, `  No prompt sets found`, `  No channels found`,
         `  No adapters found`; TypeScript prints it in every format) counts as the airs-cli-rs
         `[]` or empty table (D146), so a tenant with nothing listed agrees;
       - both `--output json`: `redteam prompt-sets get <first listed set>` (every field equal);
       - when `redteam list --status COMPLETED --limit 1 --output json` (Rust) names a job:
         `redteam status <id>` and `redteam report <id>` on both CLIs, pretty, byte-equal (D52
         tolerated);
       - **Rust only**, checked in memory and discarded: `redteam targets get <first listed target> --output json`
         must have every §15.4 credential path `[REDACTED]`, empty or absent (from 1.0 the
         management 0.86.0 `audio_curl` too, §15.24; the TypeScript CLI
         would print the credentials, so it is not run, and neither is a TypeScript backup);
         `redteam targets backup --output-dir <run tmp>/backup`: exit 0 or 1, exactly one file,
         mode 0600, parsing as the §15.18 format with as many targets plus failures as
         `targets list` lists (no target listed: exit 0 and no file, §15.18); the directory is removed with the run's sandbox on success,
         failure and panic, and nothing from the file reaches a summary;
       - both CLIs, `redteam report --output-file <run tmp>/<cli>/rt.html` (the environment
         report, read-only): equal exit codes, each file mode 0600, the same
         `<n> source(s) incomplete` status line (or none on both); the HTML is not compared
         (timestamps).
       Not run live: `registry-credentials` (a mint), `eula content`, `targets profile`,
       `targets error-logs`, `targets templates`, `adapter get` (scripts, snapshots and system
       prompts are not needed for the comparison).
     - **Writes** (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_REDTEAM_WRITES=1` as well; otherwise `redteam writes skipped`).
       The only resource type is the **draft adapter**: fully deletable, not tenant-wide, and
       created with `validate=false` and no channel, so the service runs no script (choice 16 of
       §15.22: if a draft create contacts anything external, this flow is dropped).
       - Plan, at most 2 resources (the cap of 10 is a constant checked before each create):
         Rust `redteam adapter create --draft --name airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-adapter-rs --script-b64 <base64 of "# airs-rs-e2e placeholder\n"> --prompt e2e --variables '[{"key":"E2E","value":"1","type":"VAR"}]' --output json`,
         and the TypeScript CLI the same with `-adapter-ts` (no `SECRET` variable, no channel).
       - Preflight (read-only): Rust `redteam adapter list --search airs-rs-e2e-<run id> --all --output json`;
         no planned name may exist.
       - Steps: both creates (ledger `pending` before, the result after; the id from the JSON
         or, for TypeScript, from its `✓ Adapter created: <uuid>` line); `redteam adapter get`
         of each on both CLIs (`--output json`), projections equal apart from ids, timestamps and
         user ids (`scriptB64` compared in memory, never printed); each CLI runs
         `adapter update <its own> --draft --description e2e-updated --prompt e2e`, and a Rust
         `get` must show the `E2E` variable kept (the read-modify-write rule).
       - Teardown, always (also on failure and panic, inside `catch_unwind`): for every id listed
         under a planned name, the Rust `redteam adapter delete <id> --force` (no TypeScript
         delete, as in M4), journalled; then every id captured from a create output that the
         listing did not show is deleted by its id the same way, and the listing's miss is a
         mismatch row (`teardown listing shows every created adapter`; a listing that has not
         indexed the new rows must not leave drafts behind). `resourcesLeft` counts every
         created id not confirmed deleted plus every planned name the final listing still
         shows; `resourcesLeft > 0`, or fewer deletes than creates, fails the run.
       - Excluded, with reasons: targets (`create`, `probe` and `validate-auth` make AIRS contact
         an external endpoint, and targets carry credentials; `update-profile` changes an existing
         target); prompt sets (only archivable, never deletable); prompts (would need a run-owned
         prompt set or change an existing one); properties (tenant-wide, no delete); instances,
         devices, channels (infrastructure; channels have no delete) and registry credentials (a
         mint); `adapter validate` (runs code through an ONLINE broker); `eula accept` (never
         live); `abort` of any scan the run did not start; `restore` (writes targets).
       - Sweeper (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_CLEANUP=1`, §10 above) gains adapters: Rust
         `redteam adapter list --all --max 0 --output json`, names fully matching
         `^airs-rs-e2e-([0-9]{10})-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-adapter-(rs|ts)$` whose embedded Unix time is at
         least 3,600 s old, at most 20 per invocation, each deleted with
         `redteam adapter delete <id> --force` and journalled with phase `cleanup`.
     - **Scan** (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_REDTEAM_SCAN=1` and `AIRS_E2E_REDTEAM_TARGET=<uuid of an existing target the user names>`
       as well; never by default: the orchestrator asks the user first; otherwise
       `redteam scan skipped`). Red team scans are billed and long-running.
       - Gates, all checked before anything is opened (no store, no request): both variables
         set; the target value of the §7.1 id shape; `AIRS_RS_LIVE_REDTEAM_SCAN_MINUTES`
         (default 20) an integer 1–60; the scan budget, a constant **1** with no override, not
         yet used by this run. A violation fails the run with a fixed message naming the
         variable, never its value.
       - Preflight (read-only, Rust): `redteam targets list --all --output json` must list the
         target id (the user's target exists; nothing about it is printed);
         `redteam categories --output json` gives the first category and its first sub-category
         that is not `MULTI_TURN` (none: the run stops before any scan).
       - The one scan, the smallest kind: Rust
         `redteam scan --target <uuid> --name airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-scan --type STATIC --categories '{"<cat>":["<sub>"]}' --no-wait --output json`,
         with the ledger's `pending` line (kind `scan`) first. TypeScript never starts a scan
         (it would re-send the POST on a 5xx, D133).
       - Unknown outcome (exit 1 with the D133 hint): the ledger records `unknown`; the flow
         looks for the job read-only with `redteam list --target <uuid> --all --max 200 --output json`,
         matching the exact run name, up to 5 times a poll interval apart (a failing listing is
         unresolved, never "not found"), and records its id when found. Still unresolved, the
         run fails with `a billed scan named airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-scan may be running on the
         target; abort it manually` (it cannot abort a scan it cannot name). It never starts a
         second scan.
       - Bounded polling: Rust `redteam status <id> --output json` every 30 s until a terminal
         status or the deadline. On a terminal status, TypeScript `redteam status <id>` is
         compared (the normalised fields); on `COMPLETED` or `PARTIALLY_COMPLETE` both CLIs run
         `redteam report <id>` and `redteam report <id> --attacks --limit 5` (pretty, byte-equal,
         D52 tolerated).
       - End: when the job is not terminal at the deadline, or the flow fails or panics after
         the create, the Rust `redteam abort <id> --force` (journalled) and one `status` read

         (the API cannot delete them).
     - **Scan** (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_WRITES=1`, because the flow creates and deletes a group and writes labels,
       **and** the separate `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_SCAN=1` and `AIRS_E2E_MS_MODEL_URI=<a model URI the user names>`
       as well; never by default: the orchestrator asks the user first; otherwise `model-security scan skipped`).
       Model-security scans are billed and long-running.
       - Gates, all checked before anything is opened (no store, no request): the three variables set
       (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_WRITES` or `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_SCAN` not `1`: skipped); the URI
         at most 2,048 bytes, without control characters, and without userinfo, query or fragment when it
         parses as a URL (a credential-bearing URI is refused; the value is never printed);
         `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_SCAN_MINUTES` (default 15) an integer 1–60; the scan budget, a constant **1** with
         no override, not yet used by this run. A violation fails the run with a fixed message naming the
         variable, never its value.
       - Resources (at most 2; the cap of 10 checked before each create): one group
         `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-group-sc` (Rust `groups create`, `source_type` `HUGGING_FACE` for an `hf://` or
         `https://huggingface.co/` URI, else `ALL`; ledger kind `group`) and one scan, created by **Rust only**:
         `scans create --config <run tmp>/scan.json --output json` (`model_uri` the given URI,
         `security_group_uuid` the run's group; ledger `pending` first, kind `model-scan`). TypeScript never
         creates a scan (it re-sends the POST on a 5xx, D179). An unknown outcome (exit 1 with the D179 hint)
         is journalled `unknown`; the flow looks for the scan read-only with Rust
         `scans list --search <the URI's last path segment> --all --max 200 --output json`, matching the run's
         group name in `securityGroupName` and a `createdAt` after the run started, up to 5 times 30 s apart (a
         failing listing is unresolved, never "not found"), and never creates a second scan; still unresolved,
         the run fails with `a billed model-security scan may have been created in group airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-group-sc; check it manually`.
       - Labels, **only on that scan** (keys and values `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-…`; ledger kind `model-scan`,
         ops `labels add|set|delete`): Rust `labels add` of one label, TypeScript `labels add` of another,
         `scans get <scan> --output json` on both CLIs (equal label sets); Rust `labels set --force` with one
         label (the warning names the dropped key), TypeScript `labels set` with two (it never prompts),
         Rust `scans get` showing exactly them; TypeScript `labels delete <scan> --keys <one>` and Rust
         `labels delete <scan> --keys <the other> --force`; Rust `scans get` showing no run label, and
         `labels keys --all --output json` not listing a run key that the scan no longer carries (a
         tenant-wide index may lag: a remaining key is a notice, not a mismatch).
       - Bounded wait: Rust `scans get <scan> --output json` every 30 s until `evalOutcome` is not `PENDING`
         or the deadline; when it ended, both CLIs run `scans evaluations`, `violations` and `files` of it
         (pretty, byte-equal as in the reads). The summary records the final outcome, never the id.
       - End: the scan's run labels are removed (a Rust `labels delete … --force` of any run key it still
         carries, journalled), then the group is deleted as in the write flow (a refusal because a scan
         references it is recorded and left to the sweeper). **The scan itself stays in the tenant**: the API
         has no scan delete (§17, choice 37); the ledger records it with the note `undeletable`, and it is not
         counted in `resourcesLeft`.

       refused before any request (an empty request log: writes without `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_WRITES`, a scan

       `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_SCAN_MINUTES`, a second scan in one run); `Ledger::record` refusing a non-prefixed
