     - **Profile transfer** (`AIRS_RS_LIVE_PROFILE_TRANSFER=1` as well; otherwise
       `profile transfer skipped`). The resource types are the **custom topic** and the **security
       profile** the run creates with the existing Rust `topics create` and `profiles create`.
       - Plan, at most 4 resources created and 6 reserved (both copies for each of the two restores that
         are not dry runs; the cap of 10 is a constant checked before each create, restores included): the topic `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-topic-rs` (T) and the profile
         `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-profile-rs` (P), then the two restored copies under the same names
         (restores never take `--name-prefix`, choice 36). Both names are the existing write flow's shapes
         and match the sweeper's topic and profile kinds; nothing new is added to the sweeper.
       - Preflight (read-only, Rust): `profiles list --all-versions --all --max 0 --output json` and
         `topics list --all-versions --all --max 0 --output json`; no planned name may exist.
       - Steps: Rust `topics create` T and `profiles create` P (ledger `pending` first); Rust
         `topics apply` T to P (a new revision of P, not a resource); Rust and TypeScript
         `profiles backup <P> --output-file <run tmp>/<cli>/backup.json` (two files, read-only on the
         tenant; the Rust file checked against the TS file as in the reads); delete P (every revision, as
         the existing write flow's teardown lists them) and then T, each journalled; Rust
         `profiles restore <run tmp>/rs/backup.json --dry-run --output json` must plan exactly one topic
         create and one profile create (any other plan ends the step with a mismatch and writes nothing),
         then the same with `--expect-tsg <the file's tsgId> --force` instead of `--dry-run`. Every
         restore that is not a dry run is journalled as a write for both copies whatever the dry run
         planned (it replans on its own): a budget reservation and a `pending` line for T and for P first;
         then from its json rows a `created` row is `ok` (its UUID, else the one id the listing that
         follows shows, else `unknown`), a `reused`/`verified`/`skipped` row `skipped`, a copy in
         `notAttempted` or of a run that exited having written nothing `failed`, anything else (named by
         `outcomeUnknown`, a run that did not exit, a missing row in a run that wrote something, an
         unreadable result) `unknown`, which the teardown resolves (choice 69); verification with Rust `profiles get <P> --output json` and `topics get <T> --output json`
         (the policy equal to the backup's apart from the rewritten `topic_id` and `revision`, one record
         per name, no duplicate); `--on-conflict verify --dry-run`, which must plan only `verify` for P and
         `reuse` for T (otherwise a mismatch and no re-run), then the restore again with
         `--on-conflict verify --expect-tsg <tsgId> --force` (journalled as above, op
         `profiles restore verify`), which must exit 0, report `verified` for P and `reused` for T, and
         create nothing (both listings unchanged); the Rust restore of `<run tmp>/ts/backup.json`, which must be refused (D216) before
         the tenant.
         When T cannot be deleted before the restore (an older revision of P still references it, the M4
         observation), the restore may reuse it (identical, `sameTopic`): the dry run plans the topic
         `reuse` or, when the delete was applied after all, `create`; both copies are journalled either way.
       - The TypeScript restore never runs live (choice 35 of §18.20: the Rust reader refuses its file,
         and it replays a write after a 403, D217).
       - Teardown, always (also on failure and panic, inside `catch_unwind`): every id listed under a
         planned name (all revisions) and every id captured from a create output or a restore result is
         deleted with the Rust `profiles delete` / `topics delete` of the existing write flow, journalled
         `pending` before it is sent; a delete that aborts is recorded and the teardown goes on.
         `resourcesLeft` counts every created id not confirmed deleted plus every planned name the final
         listing still shows; `resourcesLeft > 0`, or fewer confirmed deletes than creates, fails the run.
       - Never live: `api-keys create|regenerate|delete`, `customer-apps update|delete` (the run cannot
         create its own customer app, and an app delete also deletes its keys), `profiles restore
         --on-conflict update`, any write to a profile or topic the run did not create, a backup without
         a selector, anything tenant-wide.

         cover every name of this flow, and the restored copies keep the `-rs` shape.

   - **M6f Supplychain** (0.11, §20; SK§14, SC§15 within the MILESTONES live rules; built in chunk 2,

Harness invariants (enforced by the runner on every invocation): stdin is `/dev/null`
unless the test pipes bytes (`RunOptions::stdin`) or holds an empty pipe open
(`RunOptions::stdin_held_open`), or runs the CLI on a pty (below);
temp cwd; allowlisted environment (`PATH`, `HOME=<sandbox>/home`, `TMPDIR`,
`PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH`, `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR=<sandbox>/store` (from 0.3, for both
CLIs; TypeScript ignores it), `NO_COLOR=1`, `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost`, plus
per-test additions, which the 0.3 path guard below confines to the sandbox); a per-run timeout that kills and fails the test; the child must
exit with a status code (never by signal unless the test expects it); no fixture
secret appears in stdout or stderr (each secret-named config value raw, JS-trimmed,
URL-encoded and unpadded base64; the Basic pair; every issued token through the
`mock-token-` prefix and its base64 `bW9jay10b2tl`; test-supplied secrets in the same
forms); and no file in the sandbox outside `tmp/` (registry and configs wherever a test
put them, the Rust store under `store/`, `home/`, `cwd/`, sibling `*.lock` files)
changes in bytes, mode or mtime, or appears or disappears (opt-out
`RunOptions::allow_tenant_writes` for a test that edits files itself mid-run; the
narrower `allow_writes_under` for the write commands, below). The fixture server can issue a distinct token per request
(`set_rotating_tokens`) and echo the received bearer (`Planned::echoing_bearer`), so
refresh-and-replay redaction is tested.

Loopback guard (enforced by the sandbox and the runner): every config written through
the `Sandbox` that is a JSON object must name every harness `ENDPOINT_KEYS` key with a
loopback `http(s)` URL (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`; no credentials), or with a
value that makes both CLIs reject the whole config before building a client (a
non-string, or a scheme-less string for a key TS validates as a URL); otherwise the
write panics, because an omitted key falls back to a production default. A Rust-only
test that proves zero requests opts out explicitly
(`write_config_allowing_external_endpoints`,
`add_fixture_tenant_allowing_external_endpoints`); the runner then refuses to start
the TypeScript CLI in that sandbox, and before every TypeScript run it re-checks each
file under `configs/` and each config the TS registry lookup would load. It also
refuses a TypeScript run whose environment could route a request off loopback: any
variable whose name contains `ENDPOINT` (the TS SDK reads `PANW_*_ENDPOINT` overrides)
or ends in `_PROXY` other than `NO_PROXY`, in any case, must be empty or a loopback
URL, and `NODE_OPTIONS` is refused outright.

The TypeScript reference is built by `scripts/build-reference-cli.sh` into
`.reference/prisma-airs-cli` (gitignored, pinned commit). Parity tests locate it via
`AIRS_TS_CLI_ENTRY` or the default path, and the harness verifies it once per process:
node must be major 24 (the version the expectations were recorded with), and the
default clone must be at the script's `PINNED_COMMIT` (or `AIRS_TS_COMMIT`) with no
modified tracked files (an `AIRS_TS_CLI_ENTRY` override is used as given, with a
notice). An unusable reference **fails** every parity test (and the
`reference_cli_is_usable_and_pinned` sentinel); `AIRS_ALLOW_PARITY_SKIP=1` skips them
instead, with a `PARITY SKIPPED` notice written to the real stderr (visible even for
passing tests); `AIRS_REQUIRE_PARITY=1` forbids that opt-out.

M3.5 additions (the test plans are R§6 and L§3.11, adapted to the rules above):
- Renderer parity tests run piped and compare **exact** stdout and stderr bytes for
  pretty and table, with `dNN_` tests for every row from D50 on. Golden unit tests in
  `src/render` hold the R§3 captures as byte strings.
- Colour tests drop the harness's `NO_COLOR=1` for the run and force colour on both
  sides (`CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` for Rust, `FORCE_COLOR=1` for TS, never both variables for
  TS, which would add a Node warning). Where the layouts coincide the bytes must be
  equal; D58 tests assert the per-stream and `NO_COLOR` differences.
- `--debug` tests set `XDG_STATE_HOME=<sandbox>/tmp/xdg` (the runner allows writes
  under `tmp/`; `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` still selects the TypeScript registry and,
  from 0.3, `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` the Rust store). The runner
  leak-checks every log file a run leaves (under the child's `XDG_STATE_HOME`, under
  `home/.local/state/airs-cli/debug/` and in the working directory) for every fixture
  secret form and `mock-token-` lease, like stdout and stderr;
  `airs_test_harness::debug_log::assert_logs_clean` adds every `x-payload-hash`,
  `authorization` and `x-pan-token` value and every URL query the server received,
  test-supplied text (prompts) and any `"body"` key. A test of the default location uses
  `RunOptions::allow_writes_under("home/.local/state/airs-cli")`, which admits changes
  under that one path (and the directories created on the way to it) and nothing else;
  TS runs with `--debug` use `allow_writes_under("cwd")`. A write failure mid-run is
  produced for real by running the CLI under `/bin/sh` with `trap '' XFSZ; ulimit -f 0`:
  creating the empty log succeeds and every write to it fails with `EFBIG`, while stdout
  and stderr (pipes) are unaffected. The TS reference logs nothing against loopback
  (its host filter, L§1.5), so the D61–D69 parity tests (`tests/parity_debug.rs`) assert
  TS's empty cwd file against the Rust records.

M4t additions (0.3; the research is W§1–W§14 and its acceptance criteria, adapted to §3):

- **Sandbox layout.** `Sandbox::new` adds `store/` (0700), the Rust store directory `D`
  of every run (`AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR=<sandbox>/store`). `state/` (the TypeScript
  registry) and `configs/` (the TypeScript configs) stay as they are.
- **Both CLIs provisioned from the same fixture data.** Every `Sandbox` method that
  writes a TypeScript tenant (`register`, `write_registry`, `add_fixture_tenant*`,
  `single_tenant`) also writes the Rust store, through
  `airs_test_harness::store::provision`, which applies the import conversion of §3.12
  to the same fixture registry and configs and writes the §3.2 and §3.3 canonical bytes
  (files 0600, directories 0700). Existing parity tests therefore keep comparing like
  with like without change to their setup. The mapping for TypeScript files that import
  would not convert keeps the failure class the same on both sides: a config that fails
  the TypeScript pin is provisioned with both TSG values kept (the pin message on both);
  a missing config gets no tenant file (`Cannot read a valid tenant config` on both); a
  config that is otherwise invalid for TypeScript gets the tenant file `invalid = [\n`
  (a TOML syntax error: the same message on both). The store is re-derived from
  `state/tenants.json` and the configs it names after **every** TypeScript-side write
  (raw writes included), so a test that writes a broken TypeScript file after the
  registry still compares like with like; only files inside the sandbox are read
  (a config outside it gets no tenant file). A test that needs a state only one CLI has
  stops the mirroring: `ts_only` (an empty store), `rust_only`, `detach_store`, or any
  direct store write (`write_store_raw`, `write_store_index`, `write_tenant_file_raw`,
  `write_rust_tenant`, `append_tenant_line`, `set_tenant_line`; the raw ones take a
  mode, and symlinks or foreign-mode files for the §3.8 tests are made with `std::fs`
  after `detach_store`). Each `FixtureTenant` carries its `store_path`. The loopback guard
  applies to the Rust store as to the TypeScript configs: a tenant file that parses as
  TOML must name every harness `ENDPOINT_KEYS` key (under its §3.3 name) with a loopback
  URL or a value the reader rejects (a non-string, `""`, or for the three URL-rule keys a
  string that is not a URL), otherwise the write panics; before every airs-cli-rs run
  the runner re-checks each tenant file of the store that run resolves (recorded
  opt-outs excepted), so a file written behind the harness's back is caught too.
  `tenant` commands of either CLI build no API client and send no request, and a tenant
  made by `tenant create` holds only credentials, so for a run whose first positional
  argument is `tenant` (`is_tenant_command`) the runner skips these endpoint checks
  (on configs and on tenant files); the path guards below still apply, and every
  registry, registered config and store such a run could read must lie inside the
  sandbox. A
  test (`tests/tenant_import.rs::store::provision_matches_import`) runs `airs tenant import` on a corpus of
  fixture registries (renamed, dropped, empty, unknown, coerced, dead `defaultOutput`,
  two names for one tenant, mismatched pin) and requires byte-identical store files, so
  the provisioner and the importer cannot drift apart. The one intended difference is
  the mismatched pin: the provisioner keeps both TSG values so both CLIs report the
  pin, while the importer skips the entry (reason 2 of §3.12); the test asserts that
  difference and that every imported tenant file still matches.
- **Normalisation for comparisons** (`compare::normalise_tenant_output`): each side's
  own paths become placeholders (the TypeScript registry path and `D/config.toml` →
  `<REGISTRY>`; a tenant's TypeScript config path and `D/tenants/<name>.toml` →
  `<CONFIG:name>`); the Rust program name `airs` before a command word becomes `airs-cli`
  (`compare::normalise_program`, D73, §21.6); and, for write commands, the
  TypeScript outcome lines on stdout (`  ✓ …`, `  ℹ …`) are compared with the Rust
  outcome lines on stderr (D74), the Rust stdout being required empty. After that the
  bytes must be equal, except where a `dNN_` test asserts the row's difference on both
  sides.
- **Write parity** (create, set, unset, switch, delete, each acceptance criterion of
  W§Acceptance that §12 does not change): provision; run the command on both CLIs in
  the same sandbox (each writes only its own files: TypeScript under `state/`, Rust
  under `store/`, granted with `allow_writes_under("state")` and
  `allow_writes_under("store")` respectively; everything else stays checked by the
  unchanged-sandbox rule); compare exit codes and the normalised outcome or error text;
  then compare the resulting state through the read commands on both CLIs
  (`tenant list --output json`, `tenant read <name> --output json` and
  `tenant get <name> <key> --output json` for every key the command touched),
  normalised. Rust-side tests additionally pin the store bytes against the canonical
  forms of §3.2 and §3.3, the modes (0600/0700), and that a failing command left every
  file unchanged and created nothing (D87).
- **Escape prevention and detection.** For an airs-cli-rs `tenant import` run
  (`is_import_command`) the runner also refuses (`import_source_violation`) a source
  outside the sandbox: every `--from-config` file and every `--from` registry (each
  occurrence, in both the `--flag value` and the `--flag=value` form, because clap keeps
  the last one) or, without them, the registry the child's environment resolves,
  symlinks resolved, and every `configPath` of those registries (a missing one compared
  lexically). A registry the
  TypeScript schema rejects is not inspected further, because airs-cli-rs rejects it
  too before reading any config. The runner refuses to start a run (it panics)
  when any path-bearing variable of the child (`HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`,
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`,
  `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH`) is set to an absolute path outside the sandbox, or when
  an argument that is an absolute path (any value starting with `/`, also after
  `--flag=`) lies outside it, or a value of a path flag (`--from`, `--from-config`,
  TypeScript's `--config`; every occurrence), relative ones resolved against the
  sandbox cwd, lies outside it. Removing `HOME` (the password-database fallback, which
  would name the real home) is allowed only when `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` (or
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) and `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` (or `XDG_STATE_HOME`) are set inside
  the sandbox, for both CLIs (airs-cli-rs checks the TypeScript registry path for the
  import suffix), and, for a `--debug`, `runtime bulk-scan` or `runtime resume-poll`
  run, `XDG_STATE_HOME` (where airs-cli-rs keeps the job state); a TypeScript
  `bulk-scan` or `resume-poll` run with `HOME` removed is refused outright
  (`ts_bulk_home_violation`: Node would expand the default `dataDir` with
  `os.homedir()`); a `~` in `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` without `HOME` is refused. The
  `resume-poll` state argument (which airs-cli-rs reads to classify it) must lie inside
  the sandbox too, a relative one resolved against the sandbox cwd. A relative
  value is allowed only for the tests of the absolute-path errors (it resolves against
  the sandbox cwd). With those rules the only reachable store is inside the sandbox;
  detection inside it is the unchanged-sandbox snapshot, which flags a write anywhere
  but the granted directories, and every write test asserts that the expected store
  files changed (a write that went elsewhere fails it). Harness self-tests prove that
  each refused variable and argument panics before spawning. No test, helper or tool
  ever reads or names the real `~/.config/airs-cli`, `~/.local/state/prisma-airs` or
  `~/.prisma-airs`.
- **Interactive tests** run under a pty helper (`airs_test_harness::pty`, on
  `rustix::pty`): stdin and stderr on the pty (or only stdin, `spawn_pty_with`), stdout
  piped, a script of expect-then-send steps and a timeout. The transcript is
  leak-checked like stdout and stderr. The TypeScript CLI reads the terminal raw, so
  for it Ctrl-C is the byte `\x03`. They cover the prompt gate (both terminals
  required), the three create prompts in order, hidden input (the typed secret never
  appears in the captured pty output or on stdout), the blank and invalid re-asks,
  Ctrl-C and EOF (`\x04`) → `Cancelled; no configuration saved.` and 130 with nothing
  written (Ctrl-C is a SIGINT sent to the child: making the pty its controlling
  terminal would need `pre_exec`, which is `unsafe`), the terminal mode restored after a cancel (checked with `tcgetattr`
  on the pty), and the delete confirmation (`y`, `yes`, `Y`, Enter, `n`, `yolo`, EOF,
  Ctrl-C). Parity under the pty compares the visible prompt texts and outcomes, not
  escape sequences (D88).
- **Lock tests** use a helper process (`airs_test_harness::lock_holder`) that takes the
  §3.9 lock on a sandbox store, writes a holder record, reports readiness on stdout and
  sleeps. It is the test binary itself, re-run on an `#[ignore]`d helper test (a binary
  of the harness crate would not be built for the root package's tests). With it held, a write
  command waits, prints the waiting status once, and fails after 5 s with the message
  naming the helper's pid and host; released after 1 s, the command succeeds; killed
  with SIGKILL, the next command succeeds at once (the kernel released the lock) and the
  stale record is overwritten. Planted stale temporary files are removed by the next
  write and non-matching names are kept. Six concurrent `set`s of different keys all
  succeed and the file holds all six (no lost update, no failure: D77), and so do six
  concurrent creates of different names.
- **Atomic-write unit tests** (`src/store/atomic.rs`) inject a failure at each step
  (temp create, write, fsync, rename, directory fsync) through a `#[cfg(test)]` step
  hook and assert: before the rename the target keeps its old bytes and the temp file
  is gone; after it the new bytes are in place and only the directory-sync warning
  is produced. The multi-file rollback rules of §3.11 and §3.12 are unit-tested the same
  way.
- **Import tests** (`tests/tenant_import.rs`, `tests/parity_tenant_import.rs`): dry run
  writes nothing (no `store/` entries at all) and takes no lock; every conversion note; `--replace`; case conflicts; the active rule; `--from-config`
  without management credentials; registry and config problems; the report in all
  three formats with no fixture secret in any of them; the TypeScript `state/` and
  `configs/` trees unchanged after every import (the unchanged-sandbox rule, with only
  `store/` granted, plus an explicit byte, mode and mtime comparison of every file
  under them). **After-import parity**: the TypeScript side is written, the store
  emptied, and only `airs tenant import` fills it; then `tenant list` (json and
  the table cells), `tenant read` (TypeScript rows through the import conversion),
  `tenant get` of every kept key under its Rust name, `tenant path`, `doctor` (the seven
  shared checks), and `runtime profiles|topics list` must agree on both CLIs.
  `import --from-config` and TypeScript `create --config` must report the same file
  errors. Import-source parity: for every registry-path form of §3.13
  (`PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` with `~`, `~/`, relative; `XDG_STATE_HOME`; `HOME`; an
  empty `HOME`) and every corrupt-registry case, TypeScript `tenant list --output json`
  and Rust `tenant import --dry-run --output json` must agree on success (the same
  names and TSGs) or on the generic registry message. The former registry-path and
  corrupt-registry parity tests become these; D27 and D44 move to them.
- **Store-reader tests** replace the 0.1 registry and config rejection lists with the
  §3.2 and §3.3 TOML equivalents (each rejection gives the generic message with zero
  requests), the §3.8 safety refusals (symlinked, group/other mode bits, read-only for
  writers; a foreign owner only when the suite runs as root, and otherwise through a
  unit test of the owner check), and the §3.1 resolution forms.
- **Doctor**: the import case of the Tenant check (D89), the TOML Config file outcomes,
  and the Rust-named hints, on both CLIs where TypeScript has a counterpart.
- The CI smoke test (TESTING.md) runs `tenant list --output json` with
  `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at an empty directory instead of an empty
  `PRISMA_AIRS_TENANTS_PATH` registry.

M4 additions (0.4; the research is T§15 and S§10, adapted to §13):

- **Stateful management routes.** The fixture server keeps per-test management state
  (topic and profile records in list order, seeded from the fixture dataset) and serves,
  under the tenant base: `POST /v1/mgmt/topic` and `/v1/mgmt/profile` (a fresh v4 id,
  revision 1), `PUT /v1/mgmt/topic/uuid/{id}` and `/v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/{id}` (fields
  replaced from the body, revision + 1, the id kept; a dataset flag appends a new record
  with a new id instead, so both service behaviours are tested),
  `DELETE /v1/mgmt/topic/{id}` and `/v1/mgmt/profile/{id}` (a 409 with the SDK conflict
  payload while a profile record references the topic), and the `/force` variants, which
  answer 400 without a non-blank `updated_by` and remove the topic's refs. Planned
  answers (status, `Retry-After`, delete bodies `{"message": …}`, a bare JSON string or
  `{}`, malformed 2xx bodies) override a route as today. Every request is recorded with
  its base, method, path, query, parsed JSON body and bearer. Datasets with several
  revisions of one name under distinct ids, the older listed first, cover D96 and D110.
  Lists without `latest` serve every revision.
- **Bodies are compared as JSON** (G6, D35): the Rust bodies are key-sorted, the
  TypeScript ones in Zod order, and numbers are compared by value.
- **The TypeScript environment trap** (D93). TypeScript's `topics create`, `apply` and
  `revert` ignore the tenant's `mgmtEndpoint` and fall back to `PANW_MGMT_ENDPOINT`, else
  production. The runner therefore sets, for every TypeScript run whose first positional
  argument is `runtime`, each TS SDK endpoint variable (`PANW_MGMT_ENDPOINT`,
  `PANW_MGMT_TOKEN_ENDPOINT`, `PANW_AI_SEC_API_ENDPOINT`, and any other
  `process.env.PANW_*ENDPOINT*` name in the pinned SDK bundle, listed in the harness) to
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ts-env-trap` unless the test sets it itself (to a loopback URL
  or empty, which `env_guard_violation` enforces). A test that removes one of them
  (`without_env`) is refused before the run (`removing <name> would fall back to
  production`): an unset variable is the SDK's production default
  (`TS_ENDPOINT_VARIABLES`, the 15 names of the pinned bundle; `<port>` is the fixture
  server the sandbox's last fixture tenant was written for). The trap answers `404 {}`
  to everything (4xx is never retried, so it is fast and deterministic) and records what
  it received; a `ClosedPort` is not used for it, because TypeScript retries network
  errors with random backoff. Only a sandbox that never had a fixture tenant (so the
  TypeScript CLI fails before it builds a client) gets a `ClosedPort` URL instead. Family-A commands and scans
  name their endpoints explicitly and never reach the trap; `doctor` and `tenant` runs
  do not get the variables (doctor reports `PANW_*` names). A parity test of a family-B
  command mounts the fixture state under a second base (`/ts-env/…`, sharing the state)
  and sets `PANW_MGMT_ENDPOINT` to it, then asserts that TypeScript's data requests
  reached only that base and Rust's only the tenant base. `env_guard_violation` and the
  loopback guard are unchanged; every fixture tenant names `mgmtTokenEndpoint`.
- **Write parity** (each T§Acceptance criterion that §12 does not change): both CLIs run
  against the same seeded state (reset between the two runs); exit codes, the
  normalised error or outcome text and the recorded write requests are compared, then
  the resulting state through `runtime topics|profiles get --output json` on both CLIs.
  Normalisation adds to `compare`: the TypeScript outcome lines on stdout (`  ✓ …`,
  `  ⚠ …`, `  ℹ …` and cleanup's `  ✗ …` bullets) are compared with the Rust outcome
  lines on stderr (D106), and the rest of the TypeScript stdout with the Rust stdout;
  TypeScript's `--format json` stands in for Rust's `--output json` (D94).
- **Retries are asserted per side** (D95): a 5xx fixture on a write answers with
  `Retry-After: 0`; the Rust side must send exactly one write and print the outcome
  line, the TypeScript side more than one (no exact count, no timing). A 401 on a write
  gives `token, write, token, write` on both.
- **Confirmations** run on the pty helper. TypeScript prompts only when stdout is a
  terminal, so `spawn_pty_all` puts stdout on the pty as well, used
  for the TypeScript side of D105 tests; Rust prompts are tested with stdin and stderr
  on the pty and stdout piped.
- **TypeScript `profiles cleanup` without `--updated-by`** runs `git config user.email`:
  only the one D109 test does that, with `HOME=<sandbox>/home`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<sandbox>/tmp/gitconfig` (written by the test under `tmp/`, so
  `home/` stays unchanged) and `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<sandbox>` (the variables are
  added for that run); every other TS cleanup passes `--updated-by`. No test serves
  TypeScript `cleanup` an unbounded `next_offset: 0` listing or a repeated cursor (it
  would loop forever, D108): the one D108 test answers its first two listing pages
  explicitly (`next_offset: 0`, then a last page), so TypeScript re-fetches offset 0
  exactly once; the repeated cursor is tested on the Rust side only.
- **Eval fixtures** answer each scan through a `scan_rules` entry per prompt with
  `timeout: false, error: false, errors: []` and `prompt_detected.topic_violation`, so
  TP/TN/FP/FN are fixed. Failure fixtures (`error: true`, 5xx) are Rust-side only, or
  asserted on the TypeScript side by outcome, never by retry timing. Rate-limit tests
  assert dispatch order and counts from the recorded requests; the only duration they
  check is the lower bound the limiter guarantees (`--rate 1` with three rows cannot
  finish in under two seconds), never an upper bound. The window itself is unit-tested
  on synthetic instants. Concurrency is asserted with withheld answers: with every scan
  hanging, exactly `--concurrency` scans arrive and no more can.
- **File tests** write inputs under `tmp/` and grant `allow_writes_under("cwd")` or
  `tmp/` for `--output-file`; a symlink and an existing file at the output path are
  covered (D114).
- **Ordering assertions** (what must not be sent): no write after a failed lookup; no
  PUT for an unchanged `apply`; no topic DELETE after a failed `revert` PUT; no further
  scan after the first eval scan that did not complete; no DELETE after an incomplete
  cleanup listing, a changed listing after the prompt, or an unknown outcome.

M5 additions (0.5; the research is B§17, B§Acceptance and A§10, adapted to §14):

- **Async scan routes.** The fixture server keeps per-test async state and serves
  `POST /v1/scan/async/request` (records the raw body, the parsed JSON and the headers;
  checks the payload HMAC as for sync scans; answers a receipt
  `{"received", "scan_id", "report_id"}` whose ids are derived from a per-test counter, so
  both CLIs get the same ids after a reset), `GET /v1/scan/results?scan_ids=` and
  `GET /v1/scan/reports?report_ids=`. Results are scripted per prompt text (like
  `scan_rules`): `allow`/`block`/timeout/`error: true`/unknown action, a number of
  `pending` rounds, failed rows, batch-level terminal rows, reversed row order, `req_id`
  `2.0`/`-1`/`1.5`, rows of another scan, and report-fallback detection results. Planned
  answers override a route as today: a status with `Retry-After` (`0` for 429 tests,
  a far-future HTTP date for D124), an invalid or `null`-field receipt, a non-UUID
  `scan_id`, a dropped connection after the request was read, and a held request that is
  released when the test says so (for the interruption and crash-point tests; the fixture
  reports when the request has arrived, so the test acts on an event).
- **Sandboxes.** Every bulk test sets `XDG_STATE_HOME=<sandbox>/tmp/xdg`, so the Rust state
  is under `tmp/`, and passes `--output-file` under `tmp/`; default-name tests grant
  `allow_writes_under("cwd")`, default-location tests
  `allow_writes_under("home/.local/state/airs-cli")`. The TypeScript fixture config gets
  `dataDir: <sandbox>/tmp/ts-data/runs` (its state lands in `tmp/ts-data/bulk-scans/`; the
  Rust store provisioning drops the key, D71). A Rust state is never given to TypeScript;
  the D118 test gives a TypeScript state to Rust.
- **Timing.** Fixtures answer on the first poll unless a test needs a `pending` round (each
  costs the 5 s interval on both CLIs, so few tests use one); 429 fixtures use
  `Retry-After: 0`; the 120-poll bound and the backoff arithmetic are unit tests with an
  injected interval and clock; no test asserts TypeScript timing or retry counts beyond
  the TS-observed ones (one POST per attempt, B§7). A refused connection uses the harness
  `ClosedPort` (neither CLI retries an async POST).
- **Parity normalisation** adds `<STATE>` (each side's state path) and `<OUTPUT>`; CSV
  bytes are compared exactly; bodies as JSON (D35) with an explicit `--session-id`; the
  TypeScript error texts that carry server text are compared through D11/D131.
- **Locks and crashes.** `lock_holder` takes any lock file path (the job lock as well as
  `config.lock`). Crash points are produced with SIGKILL after the fixture reports the
  held POST; interruptions with SIGINT/SIGTERM at the same events.
- **Ordering assertions**: no POST of a `submitting` or `ambiguous` item, ever; no POST
  after a rejected or unknown submission in the same run; every chunk's C1 state on disk
  before its POST arrives (read by the test while the fixture holds the request); no poll
  of a receipt before its C3 state is on disk; no file created by a run that failed its
  argument, input-file or output checks.

M6a additions (0.6; the research is RS§21, RG§21, RK§11, adapted to §15):

- **Red team routes.** One nested family `Route::RedTeam(..)` under the sandbox bases
  `/redteam/data`, `/redteam/mgmt` and `/redteam/broker` (the fixture tenant's three red team
  endpoints), bearer-checked like management, with per-test state seeded from a dataset and
  every request recorded (base, method, path as received and decoded, ordered query, parsed
  JSON body; for the upload the multipart part name, filename, content type and byte length,
  never the content). The datasets and behaviours are RK§11.1: scans with scripted status
  series per job name (`QUEUED` → `RUNNING` with counts → a terminal status), abort, categories,
  the static, dynamic and custom reports and attack lists, languages on both planes, error logs,
  quota (`GET`; a `POST /v1/metering/quota` trap that must never be hit), statistics, dashboard
  overview; targets (CRUD with the `validate` query recorded, probe, profile, update-profile,
  validate-auth, metadata, templates); prompt sets (version-info answers 500 by default, the
  upstream behaviour), the template download (CSV, optional BOM, an oversized mode), the upload,
  prompts, property names (an empty-2xx mode) and values; adapters (SECRET variables stored and
  returned `is_redacted: true` with a masked value; the PUT applies full replacement with
  null-preserves-stored); EULA (accept flips the state); instances, devices, registry credentials
  (`FAKE-REGISTRY-TOKEN-…`); channels (repeated `status`, pagination) and stats. Planned
  answers (status, `Retry-After: 0`, held, dropped connection, malformed 2xx, an empty page
  before `total_items`) override a route as today.
- **Counters** for the never-duplicated writes: scans created, aborts, EULA accepts, registry
  mints, uploads; tests read them after 5xx, held-then-dropped, refused and SIGINT cases.
- **Secret markers.** Fixture targets carry `FAKE-TARGET-SECRET-<nn>` markers (two digits, so
  no marker is a prefix of another; `fixtures::redteam::secret`) in every §15.4 credential path
  (auth headers, basic and OAuth2 settings, request headers, `curl`, provider keys, a URL query,
  secret-named `extra_info` keys, `adapter_variable_overrides`, error-log `target_object` and
  `extra_info`), adapters in `SECRET` values (one masked as the service does, one sent unmasked),
  validate-auth in `token_preview` (the registry token is not a marker, step 2 above); the runner's leak check
  adds them (raw and in the §10 encoded forms) for every airs-cli-rs red team run
  (`is_redteam_command`; the TypeScript CLI prints them, D140), so redaction is asserted on
  stdout, stderr, the debug log and the pty transcript of every test.
- **Step 1 (reads).** `Route::RedTeam(Rt)` covers the read routes of §15.5–§15.15 over a per-server
  `RedTeamData` (`FixtureServer::seed_redteam`, `redteam(|data| …)`, `redteam_data`); lists page
  with `skip`/`limit` and answer `{pagination: {total_items}, data}`, with
  `RedTeamData::total_override` (an empty page before the total) and `omit_totals`. The fixture
  serialises its bodies with sorted keys (serde_json), so both SDKs re-order the known keys into
  schema order and keep the nested keys sorted. The write routes, their counters and the report
  sources join in steps 2 and 3.
- **Step 2 (writes).** Every non-GET red team request is its own `Rt` write route
  (`Rt::is_write`, so `Route::is_write` covers them) answered over the same `RedTeamData`
  (`server/redteam_writes.rs`), so a later read sees the change: created scans, targets, prompt
  sets, prompts, adapters and channels get ids in fixed ranges (`uuid(180 + n)`, 280, 380,
  480, 580, 680); a created scan is `QUEUED` and each `GET` of it applies the next patch of
  `RedTeamData::scan_polls` (once empty, the scan completes); abort sets `ABORTED`; EULA accept
  checks the content and answers a fixed `accepted_at` (two runs print the same bytes); adapter
  `SECRET` values are served masked (`**********`, `is_redacted: true`); `adapter validate`
  echoes every variable value it got in `stdout` (a script that prints its secrets) and
  `adapter_validation_fails` answers `validated: false`; `empty_property_create` answers an
  empty 2xx (D149); `targets probe` adds the `multi_turn_error_message` noise; validate-auth
  answers marker 30 as its `token_preview`. The registry token is
  `REGISTRY_TOKEN` (not a marker: `--output json` prints it, D139; the tests pass it as an
  extra secret for the pretty and table runs). The counters of the never-duplicated writes are
  the request counts per route (`FixtureServer::rt_requests`). The runner checks the upload
  positional (`upload_file_argument`) like a path flag, relative paths included.
- **Step 3 (reports, backups).** The data-plane routes `Rt::StaticReport`, `StaticAttacks`
  (`severity` filtered, `RedTeamData::attack_totals` overrides the reported total),
  `DynamicReport`, `CustomReport`, `CustomAttacks` (with `total_attacks`/`total_threats`),
  `ScanStatistics`, `Quota` and the management `DashboardOverview`, over
  `RedTeamData::{static_reports, dynamic_reports, custom_reports, attacks, custom_attacks,
  scan_statistics, quota, dashboard_overview}`; `Rt::QuotaPost` is the trap no run may hit.
  The seed has reports for jobs 1 (static) and 2 (dynamic) and a custom report for job 3,
  which tests add to the scan list (`fixtures::redteam::custom_job`). The static attack prompt
  carries marker 31 (never printed).
- **Runner path guards.** `--config`, `--output-file`, `--output-dir`, `--file`,
  `--input-dir`, `--goals`, `--script-file`, `--variables-file` join `PATH_FLAGS`, and the
  positional file of `prompt-sets upload` is checked as an absolute-path argument. TypeScript
  `targets backup` without `--output-dir` writes `./airs-backup/targets`, so its runs use a cwd
  under `tmp/`; TypeScript `download` and `init` default names land in the cwd too.
- **Parity.** Red team writes are asserted per side as in M4 (D133: one Rust request and the
  outcome line, more than one TypeScript request, no exact count, no timing). Outcome lines are
  compared after `split_outcome_lines` (TypeScript stdout ↔ Rust stderr, D145), with the red
  team banner stripped from a failing TypeScript run (D57). Bodies are compared as JSON (D35).
  Target documents are compared after `strip_ts_target_defaults` removes from the TypeScript
  side exactly its two schema defaults (`ws_response_timeout: 110`,
  `basic_auth_location: "HEADER"`) where the Rust side has no such key (D153; the `d153_`
  tests assert both sides), and the byte-parity write scenarios send a
  `ws_response_timeout`, so both CLIs print the server's value; credential paths are compared
  only as "redacted on the Rust side" (D140). No parity
  test lets the TypeScript scan wait loop poll an unknown status (it never ends, D135): every
  scripted series ends in a terminal status, and the bound and unknown statuses are tested on
  the Rust side with an injected interval.
- **Confirmations** run on the pty helper (`spawn_pty` for Rust, `spawn_pty_all` for the
  TypeScript side of `targets delete` and `adapter delete`).
- **Files.** Downloads, scaffolds, backups and reports are written under `tmp/` or the granted
  `cwd/`; each file test covers an existing path, a dangling symlink, a symlinked directory, the
  0600 mode and the absence of temporaries.

M6b additions (0.7; the research is TD§15–§17, TB§7, DK§11–§12, adapted to §16):

- **DLP routes.** One nested family `Route::Dlp(..)` under the sandbox base `/dlp` (the
  fixture tenant's `dlpEndpoint`, already `<base>/dlp`), bearer-checked like management, with
  per-test state seeded from a dataset (`fixtures::dlp`, `FixtureServer::seed_dlp`,
  `dlp(|data| …)`) and every request recorded (method, path as received and decoded, ordered
  query, content type; a JSON body parsed; for a multipart upload the part names, filenames,
  content types, the parsed metadata JSON and the file part's byte length and SHA-256, never
  its bytes). Routes: `GET /dlp/v2/api/{data-filtering-profiles,data-patterns,data-profiles,dictionaries}`
  as Spring pages (`page`, `size`, repeated `sort`, `keywords`), `GET …/<id>`; the writes of
  step 2: `PUT` filtering profiles; `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` (`application/merge-patch+json`
  required, RFC 7386 applied) and `DELETE` (soft: `status: deleted`) patterns; `POST`, `PUT`,
  `PATCH` profiles (a name over 32 units answers 400; a 409 mode for an archived name); `POST`,
  `PUT` (200 with a body, or a 2xx without one, by a knob), `PATCH`, `DELETE` dictionaries with
  the multipart parser. Created records get ids in fixed ranges, `version: 1` and
  `status: active`, and `supported_confidence_levels` expanded as the live service does
  (TB§5.5), so a later read sees the change. **Traps** (counted, every test asserts 0 unless it
  tests them): `DELETE …/data-profiles/<id>` (answers 501) and, outside the replace tests,
  `PUT …/data-filtering-profiles/<id>`.
  Built in step 1 (`src/server/dlp.rs`, `src/fixtures_dlp.rs`): the read routes only,
  `Route::Dlp(Dl::List(Collection) | Dl::Get(Collection))` (every other method under `/dlp` is
  an unknown route until step 2); Spring pages with the default size 20, `sort` applied to the
  named string field, keywords served only with `keywords=true`; the knobs `styles`
  (`PageStyle::Camel`, `Snake` without `last`, `NoLast`, `Bare`), `size_caps` (the seeded
  dictionaries: 50, snake_case), `ignore_page` (a repeated page 0) and `extra_pages` (an empty
  intermediate page); a 404 problem for an unknown id. The runner checks the
  `FAKE-DLP-CONTENT-<nn>` markers on stderr, the pty transcript and the debug log of every
  airs-cli-rs DLP run (`is_dlp_command`, `Running::stderr_secrets`).
  Built in step 2 (`src/server/dlp_writes.rs`): `Dl::Create`, `Dl::Replace`, `Dl::Patch` and
  `Dl::Delete` per `Collection` (no `POST`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` on filtering profiles: an
  unknown route), every one a write (`Route::is_write`) answered over the dataset: created ids
  `p-new-<n>`, `dp-new-<n>`, `d-new-<n>` (`DlpData::created`), `version` bumped on every write,
  a replace drops the request fields the body omits, a pattern `DELETE` sets
  `status: deleted`, a dictionary `DELETE` removes the record, a `PATCH` without
  `application/merge-patch+json` answers 415; the knobs `dictionary_replace_empty` (the
  dictionary `PUT` answers 204 without a body) and `reserved_profile_names` (a profile create
  answers 409); the multipart parser behind `multipart(&RecordedRequest)` (part names,
  filenames, content types, the parsed JSON, the length and `sha256_hex` of each part; a
  dictionary's keywords are the file's non-empty lines); a 400 problem with the
  `originalFileName` field error for a metadata without `original_file_name`. The profile
  `DELETE` trap answers 501 (`Dl::is_trap`; `tests/dlp_writes.rs` asserts after every run that
  it was never hit); filtering-profile `PUT`s are counted with `dl_requests`. The confidence
  expansion of created patterns (TB§5.5) was added in step 3 (`high`, `medium`, `low` appended), with
  the CSV header row a dictionary upload's `.csv` file loses and `DlpData::created_tenant_id`.
- **Datasets and knobs.** Seeded predefined, parent-managed, `deleted` and `disabled` records of
  every kind, mixed `tenant_id`s, a predefined pattern with `regexes: null`, a `basic` profile with
  `detection_rules: null`, `multi_profile` and EDM rules (TB§4.2); page styles: camelCase,
  snake_case (the dictionaries' live style), no `last`, a page-size cap (dictionaries 50),
  inconsistent totals, a repeated id, a missing id, an empty intermediate page, more pages than
  `--max-pages`; planned answers as today (status, `Retry-After: 0`, held, dropped, applied then
  dropped, a malformed 2xx, an empty 2xx), and a 400 problem with an allowlisted, a
  non-allowlisted or no `detail`. Per-route request counters prove one attempt per write.
- **Sensitive markers.** Fixture regexes, proximity keywords, tag values, descriptions of seeded
  custom records and dictionary keywords carry `FAKE-DLP-CONTENT-<nn>` markers (two digits, as
  the red team markers). The runner's leak check adds them (raw and in the §10 encoded forms) for
  every airs-cli-rs DLP run (`is_dlp_command`) on **stderr, the debug log and every summary**;
  stdout may hold them only in the json and table reads that print full records (§16.9), and the
  tests assert where they appear. Error-body fixtures that echo a marker prove no error prints it.
- **Runner path guards.** `--body-file`, `--metadata-file` join `PATH_FLAGS` (`--file`,
  `--output-file` are there); the positional `<file>` of `runtime dlp restore` is checked as an
  absolute-path argument, like the upload positional. TypeScript `backup` without `--output-file`
  writes into the cwd, so its runs use a cwd under `tmp/`.
- **Parity.** DLP writes are asserted per side as in M4 (D160: one Rust request and the outcome
  line, more than one TypeScript request, no exact count, no timing). Outcome lines are compared
  after `split_outcome_lines` (TypeScript stdout ↔ Rust stderr, D172). Bodies are compared as
  JSON (D35); multipart uploads by part names, filenames, content types, metadata JSON and file
  hash (the boundary differs). JSON records are compared after applying TS's camelCasing to the
  tag keys of the Rust side (D171). Backups are compared by counts and name sets only (the
  formats differ, D175).
- **Confirmations** run on the pty helper (`spawn_pty`); the TypeScript `restore` prompt (stdout)
  with `spawn_pty_all`.
- **Files.** Backups are written under `tmp/` or the granted `cwd/`; each file test covers an
  existing path, a dangling symlink, a symlinked directory, a missing parent, the 0600 mode and
  the absence of temporaries, and asserts that the refusals come before any request.

## 11. Module layout

Since M1 of the optional runtime MCP service (RUNTIME_MCP_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN "Workspace
boundary", RUNTIME_MCP_CONTRACT §1) the workspace has these product packages:

- `airs-cli` (the root package, `src/`): the CLI. It owns argument parsing, planning,
  output and signals, the tenant store and its writers, and every command. It re-exports
  the shared modules below at their former paths (`crate::error`, `crate::report::signal`,
  …), so the CLI's behavior and its module paths are unchanged.
- `airs-runtime-core` (`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/`, published in lockstep): the code the
  CLI and the server share. It covers failures and the secret set, ordered JSON,
  terminal-safe text and number formatting (`text.rs`), the output format names, the
  tenant credential model (`tenant/`), SDK client construction and URL admission, the
  `--debug` record format and transport over caller-supplied sinks, pure styling, the read budget, the scan verdict (`scan_verdict.rs`), withholding
  and its rules, and the Signal Brief evidence, privacy, analysis, renderers and live
  collector (`signal/`). The collector reaches persistent history only through
  `signal/sink.rs` (`HistorySink`); the CLI passes no sink. It has no SQLite, no listener
  and no CLI I/O.
- `airs-mcp` (`crates/airs-mcp/`, `publish = false`, from M2): the optional service binary.
  It covers the frozen catalogue (`catalogue.rs`), strict configuration (`config.rs`),
  two-token verification (`auth.rs`), routing, reload and health (`run.rs`), the
  data-subtree admission, owner lock and control seed (`storage.rs`), and the tools
  (`tools.rs`). The CLI never depends on it.
- `airs-history-store` (`crates/airs-history-store/`, `publish = false`): the server-owned
  SQLite archive (database, repository, identity, paths, inspection, work, receipts, sync,
  transfer, compaction and recovery). Its executable tests drive `airs-history-driver`, a
  test-only binary that no release or documented procedure builds or installs (building
  the CLI never compiles it). The CLI never depends on it.

The paths below name each module where it lives now.

```
src/main.rs            thin: std::process::exit(airs_cli_rs::run(std::env::args_os())); the `airs`
                       binary (1.0, §21.2)
src/bin/airs-cli-rs.rs (1.0) the compatibility binary: one doc comment line and
                       `include!("../main.rs");`, so the two binaries cannot differ (§21.2)
src/lib.rs             run(): version pre-scan, clap parse, runtime, dispatch, exit mapping
                       (every module is private; run, VERSION, version_requested are the API)
src/signals.rs         the process-lifetime signal thread and its decisions (§2.5)
src/cli.rs             clap definitions (all 0.2 commands, the global --output, --quiet,
                       --tenant and --debug), per-command --output help
crates/airs-runtime-core/src/error.rs           CliError {Usage, Operational, Interrupted, Reported} + rendering,
                       SDK mapping (§6); re-exports SecretSet
crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs         SecretSet: the registered forms (one ordered set) and their checks, the
                       multi-pattern matcher (Matcher, its step count in test builds only), the
                       base64 forms (§6, §8; choice 187); withhold, the D47 document pass of the
                       runtime, gateway and supplychain output (choice 81 of §18; moved from
                       runtime/views.rs in 0.11)
src/output.rs          Output (stdout buffer, data vs decoration, status, quiet, commit,
                       commit_data: a commit as the command's result, §2.5,
                       per-stream colour state), Format {Pretty, Table, Json} and the
                       per-command format policy (§2.4), terminal_safe; JSON printing
                       delegates to json.rs
crates/airs-runtime-core/src/json.rs            order-preserving JSON values, pretty and compact JSON writers with
                       js_number (§2.2, §2.7), D44 classes, the shared number-member read
                       (json::number: pagination counts of red team, model security and runtime),
                       json_text and escape_c1 (the D212 writer of the runtime, gateway and

Existing modules extended in M4: cli.rs (the §13.1 commands; the `--format` alias),
commands/mod.rs (planning, format and debug policies of the new commands), input.rs (the
runtime confirmation texts and cancel status), views.rs (the M4 records and layouts),
render/table.rs (the two-space indented table of the cleanup preview), error.rs (the
outcome detail lines). M4 adds no dependency: ordered concurrency uses `futures-util`
(`StreamExt::buffered`) and the rate window `tokio::time`, both already present.

Existing modules extended in M5: cli.rs (the §14.1 commands and the hidden `--input`),
commands/mod.rs (planning, format and debug policies; the input file read during
planning), commands/scan.rs (the §8.3 normaliser shared with `bulk::engine`, with a
prompt-only `triggered`), store/lock.rs (holder record and lock-file opening usable for
any lock file, with an immediate-refusal mode), signals.rs (the §14.16 contexts),
error.rs (the §14 detail lines), render/style.rs (the summary colours). M5 adds no
dependency: `rustix` `fs` already gives `openat`, `renameat`, `unlinkat`, `fstat` and
`flock`.

crates/airs-test-harness additions (M5): the async scan routes (`Route::ScanAsync`,
`Route::ScanReports`, the stateful `Route::ScanResults`), scripted results
(`FixtureServer::add_async_rule`, `AsyncRule`, `set_async_reversed`, `receipts`) and planned
timing (`Planned::held` / `builtin` / `disconnect`, `release_held`, `wait_for_route`) in
src/server/; `lock_holder::spawn_file` / `hold_file` on any lock path; `--file` and
`--input` in the runner's `PATH_FLAGS`; the `<STATE>`/`<OUTPUT>` normalisation in the parity
tests; the live bulk flow as `live::bulk` (§10), on `Session::open_checked` (a check of the
in-memory tenant config before anything is created), `Session::run_in` (another working
directory inside the session sandbox, extra sandboxed variables, a SIGINT trigger on the
stderr seen so far or on a fixture event) and `ScanBudget::release`.

New dependencies (exact pins, small and widely used): `toml` (parse only; the writers
are our own, so no serializer feature is needed and `preserve_order` stays off) and
`rustix` with the `fs`, `termios`, `system` and `process` features (already in the lock
file through `tempfile`; it gives `flock`, termios, `uname` and `geteuid` without
`unsafe`). The harness adds `rustix`'s `pty` feature. `rpassword` is not needed.
```

## 12. Intentional differences from the TypeScript CLI

[COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md) lists the tests that pin each row.

| # | Behaviour | TypeScript | airs-cli-rs | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | argument-parse errors (unknown option/command, missing argument/option, excess arguments, bare group; from 0.10 also every `gateway` group and leaf, `report`'s missing `--workspace` included; TypeScript prints a bare `aigateway` group's help on stdout with exit 0, §19.2); from 0.11 also every `supplychain` group and leaf (§20.2) | exit 1 (commander default) | exit 2 | documented contract: 2 = usage error |
| D2 | usage validation vs tenant loading | tenant loaded first (bad `--output` with no tenant exits 1) | usage validated first (exit 2) | usage errors need no tenant |
| D3 | `--debug` (**retired in 0.2**) | private JSONL API log | ported (§2.9); the remaining differences are D61–D69 | replaced by D61–D69; the number is not reused |
| D4 | management and `tenant list`/`tenant read` output formats (**retired in 0.2**) | six formats, pretty default | pretty, table and json at TS parity (§2.4, §3.6, §7.6); the remaining differences are D50, D51 and D57 | replaced by D50, D51 and D57; the number is not reused |
| D5 | scan output | pretty only; `--output` silently ignored (any value, `table`, dropped and invalid names included) | pretty default; `--output json` (§8.5) and `--output table` (§8.6) added; any other value is a usage error (exit 2) | structured outcomes for live comparison; every command has pretty and table (M3.5) |
| D6 | failed / timed-out / unknown-action scans | shown as `ALLOW`, Category `error`, exit 0 | `FAILED`, reason shown, exit 1 | fail closed; matches TS bulk-scan semantics |
| D7 | response detections | ignored | listed as `response.<key>` and count toward Triggered | correctness when `--response` is given |
| D8 | env credential fallback for a token-only or key-only tenant | TS SDK may pick up `PANW_AI_SEC_API_KEY/TOKEN` | never | tenant file is the only credential source |
| D9 | scan POST retries | re-POSTs on 5xx/network up to `airsNumRetries` (default 5) | exactly one POST | SDK never replays submissions; avoids duplicate scans |
| D10 | management retry statuses (narrowed in 0.4 to reads; writes are D95) | 500/502/503/504, 401 refresh free | 429/502/503/504 (SDK), 401 refresh counts against `max_retries = 5` | SDK engine policy |
| D11 | error text (extended in 0.10 to every `gateway` command except the report's fixed lines: TypeScript prints the server's `message`, whole non-JSON bodies and the inference provider's error text verbatim, control characters included, §19.3; extended in 0.6 to every red team command, whose TypeScript errors also echo whole non-JSON bodies, §15.3, in 0.8 to every model-security command, whose TypeScript errors print non-problem bodies and JSON `message` text verbatim, control characters and the PyPI server text included, §17.3, and in 0.9 to the M6d commands other than the dashboard, sessions and report lines, which are TypeScript's own fixed texts: TypeScript prints the server's `message` and whole non-JSON bodies verbatim, so a 409 can echo a key, §18.3) | echoes server message text; transport failures read `AISEC_CLIENT_SIDE_ERROR:fetch failed`, and doctor classifies a refused token endpoint as `authentication failed: AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:Token request failed: fetch failed` | `API error <s>` + allowlisted problem fields + error code; transport failures read `AISEC_CLIENT_SIDE_ERROR:Network request failed (connection refused, reset or unreachable)`, and a refused token endpoint is `network unreachable: AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:Token request failed: network error` | secret safety; SDK transport kinds (a transport failure is not an authentication failure) |
| D12 | `next_offset: 0` on a single profiles page (from 0.9 also `api-keys list` and `customer-apps list`, §18.4, §18.7) | `Showing N (more available)` | `Showing N` | 0 ends pagination |
| D13 | topics latest listing truncated by `--limit` | always `Showing N` | `Showing N (more available)` when more exist | honest status |
| D14 | `--all` truncated by `--max` (from 0.9 also `api-keys list --all` and `customer-apps list --all`, §18.4, §18.7) | `Showing all N` | `Showing first N (stopped at --max M; more available)` | never claim completeness falsely |
| D15 | traversal beyond 10,000 rows in lookups | silent truncation, possible false not-found | error (incomplete walk) | fail closed |
| D16 | `--max 0` for topics | capped at 10,000 | uncapped (1,000,000 safety bound) | flag meaning |
| D17 | `--revision abc`, `--limit 1e2`, `--limit 0x10` | NaN → not found / JS coercion accepted | usage error, decimal integers only | strict parsing |
| D18 | empty scan content, profile name > 100, prompt > 2 MiB | exit 1 after status lines | exit 2 before reading the tenant | usage contract |
| D19 | doctor checks (from 0.10 the `Gateway API` check is the eighth, §9, §19.16; from 8.0 the `Executable` check is the first, D331) | 11 (Node, Typesafe, AI Gateway included) | 7 scoped checks; 8 from 0.10; 9 from 8.0 | release-1 scope |
