## 13. M4 runtime writes (0.4)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-runtime-writes.md` (cited as
**T§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-writes.md` (cited as **S§n**). This section overrides
them where they differ; their provisional D-numbers are not the numbers below. Every
difference from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row (D93–D117). scm-sdk 0.1.0 has every
operation these commands need (S§9): nothing here is blocked on an SDK change.

### 13.1 Commands and options

Help texts are TypeScript's unless a §12 row changes the flag. `rm` is a visible alias of
both `delete` commands (TS `program.ts:42-51`). The groups list their subcommands in
TypeScript's sorted order: `runtime topics`: `apply, create, delete, eval, get, list,
revert, sample, update`; `runtime profiles`: `cleanup, create, delete, get, list,
update`. Usage examples (`Examples:` after the help) are the TypeScript ones with the
program name `airs`.

| Command | Help | Arguments and options |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime topics create` | `Create or update a custom topic definition` | `--name <name>` (required, `Topic name`), `--description <desc>` (required, `Topic description`), `--examples <examples...>` (required, one or more values, `Example prompts (2-5 required)`), hidden `--format <format>` |
| `runtime topics update <topicId>` | `Update a custom topic` | `--config <path>` (required, `JSON file with topic updates`) |
| `runtime topics delete\|rm <topicId>` | `Delete a custom topic` | `--force` (`Skip confirmation and force delete (removes from all referencing profiles)`), `--updated-by <email>` (`Email of user performing force deletion`) |
| `runtime topics apply` | `Assign a topic to a security profile (additive)` | `--profile <name>` (required, `Security profile name`), `--name <name>` (required, `Topic name to assign`), `--intent <intent>` (`Topic intent: block or allow`, default `block`), from 8.0 `--direction <direction>` (`Protection direction: prompt, response, tool-call, tool-response`) and `--ai-profile-index <n>` (`AI profile entry index (zero-based)`) (§13.17), hidden `--format <format>` |
| `runtime topics revert` | `Remove a custom topic from a profile and delete it` | `--profile <name>` (required), `--name <name>` (required, `Topic name to remove`), `--force` (`Skip confirmation prompt`), from 8.0 `--direction <direction>` and `--ai-profile-index <n>` (as `apply`, §13.17), hidden `--format <format>` |
| `runtime topics eval` | `Evaluate a topic against a static prompt set and compute metrics` | `--profile <name>` (required, `Security profile name`), `--prompts <path>` (required, `Path to CSV file with prompt,expected,intent columns`), `--topic <name>` (`Topic name (for output labeling)`, default `unknown`), `--rate <n>` (`Max AIRS scan API calls per second`), `--concurrency <n>` (`Concurrent scan requests`, default `5`), hidden `--format <format>` |
| `runtime topics sample` | `Print a sample CSV file showing the eval prompt format` | `--output-file <path>` (`Write to file instead of stdout`) |
| `runtime profiles create` | `Create a new security profile` | `--name <name>` (`Profile name (required unless --config is supplied)`, from 8.0; required before), `--no-active` (`Create profile as inactive`), the policy flags below, from 8.0 `--direction <direction>` (`Protection direction: prompt, response, tool-call, tool-response`), `--config <path>` (`Complete JSON profile configuration; exclusive with write flags`; `JSON file with profile configuration (legacy)` before 8.0) (§13.17) |
| `runtime profiles update <nameOrId>` | `Update a security profile by name or UUID` | `--name <name>` (`Update profile name`), `--active` (`Set profile as active`), `--no-active` (`Set profile as inactive`), the policy flags below, from 8.0 `--direction <direction>` and `--ai-profile-index <n>` (`Select an AI entry in a multi-entry policy (zero-based)`), `--config <path>` (`Complete JSON replacement; exclusive with write flags`; `JSON file with profile updates (legacy)` before 8.0) (§13.17) |
| `runtime profiles delete\|rm <nameOrId>` | `Delete a security profile by name or UUID` | `--force` (`Skip confirmation and force delete (removes from referencing policies)`), `--updated-by <email>` (`Email of user performing force deletion`) |
| `runtime profiles cleanup` | `Delete old profile revisions, keeping only the latest per name` | `--force` (`Skip confirmation — proceed with deletion`), `--updated-by <email>` (`Force-delete with this audit email; detaches the revisions from referencing policies`, D109), `--dry-run` (Rust-only, `Show what would be deleted and delete nothing`, D105) |

Policy flags (`profiles create` and `update`; T§9.1), each taking one value unless
marked: `--prompt-injection <action>` (`Prompt injection action (block/allow/alert)`),
`--toxic-content <action>` (`Toxic content action (e.g. "high:block, moderate:block")`),
`--contextual-grounding <action>`, `--malicious-code <action>` (`Malicious code
protection action (block/allow/alert)`), `--url-action <action>` (`URL detected action
(block/allow/alert)`), `--allow-url-categories <list>`, `--block-url-categories <list>`,
`--alert-url-categories <list>` (`Comma-separated URL categories to allow|block|alert`),
`--agent-security <action>`, `--dlp-action <action>` (`Data leak detection action
(block/allow/alert)`), `--dlp-profiles <list>` (`Comma-separated DLP profile names`),
`--mask-data-inline` (no value, `Mask detected data inline`),
`--db-security-create|read|update|delete <action>` (`Database <op> action
(block/allow/alert)`), `--inline-timeout-action <action>` (`Inline timeout action
(block/allow)`), `--max-inline-latency <n>` (`Max inline latency in seconds`),
`--mask-data-in-storage` (no value, `Mask data in storage`). From 8.0 (TS 7.3.0, §13.17) also
`--no-mask-data-inline` (`Disable inline masking`), `--no-mask-data-in-storage` (`Disable
storage masking`), `--enable-full-conversation-inspection` (`Enable shared conversation
inspection`) and `--no-enable-full-conversation-inspection` (`Disable shared conversation
inspection`); of a positive/negative pair the last one given wins.

- **Protection flags** are every policy flag (TS 7.3.0 `hasAnyProtectionFlag`, §13.17; before
  8.0 `--dlp-profiles` and `--mask-data-inline` were not). Action values are not validated
  (the service validates them, TS parity).
- **`--max-inline-latency`**: decimal digits only, at most 2^53, else the usage error
  `--max-inline-latency must be a non-negative integer` (D102).
- **The hidden `--format <format>`** (TS deprecated alias, not in `--help`): when given,
  the warning `  ⚠ --format is deprecated and will be removed in v4 — use --output`
  (yellow by the stderr decision, never quiet-suppressed) is printed on stderr during
  planning, before any other validation. Its value is validated like `--output` (§2.4,
  `Invalid output format '<x>'. Expected: pretty, table, json`, exit 2). An explicit
  `--output` wins over it; otherwise it selects the format (D94).
- `--active` and `--no-active` conflict (clap's conflict error, exit 2, D100).
- `--force` and `--dry-run` conflict: `--dry-run cannot be combined with --force`
  (exit 2).
- `--examples` takes every following value up to the next option, like commander's
  variadic option; values that begin with `-` need `--examples=-x` (clap).

### 13.2 Common rules

**Clients and endpoints** (D93). Every management command builds its client as §5
describes, from the selected tenant only: `mgmtEndpoint` (else the §5 default),
`mgmtTokenEndpoint` (else the default), the §3.5 management credential check before
any client is built, and the §5 endpoint admission. No environment variable is read
(§2.6). `topics eval` builds only the scanner client (§5) and requires scanner
credentials (§3.5); it never builds the management client. `topics sample` reads no
tenant and builds no client. `--tenant` selects the tenant as for reads (§3.4); with
`topics sample` it is validated and ignored.

**Validation order** (D104). clap → the `--format` warning → `--output` and `--format`
→ `--tenant`'s name format → the command's argument checks, in the order its section
lists them (they include the non-interactive confirmation refusal) → the debug log
(§2.9) → input files (`--config`, `--prompts`; below) → the tenant (§3.4, §3.7) → the
credential check (§3.5) → the client (§5) → the command's requests, prompt and writes.
Every usage error (exit 2) therefore comes before the tenant is read, makes no request
and opens no debug log. File errors exit 1 before the tenant is read, with zero
requests. A local check that needs server data (a body that fails the schema after a
merge) fails after the reads, before the write.

**Input files** (D103). `--config` and `--prompts` paths are used as given (relative to
the working directory) and followed through symlinks. The file must be a regular file
of at most 1,048,576 bytes (`--config`) or 16,777,216 bytes (`--prompts`), read whole,
and UTF-8. `--config` must hold one JSON value (the D44 classes count as invalid JSON)
that is an object. Messages (exit 1; `<path>` as typed, through `terminal_safe`; no OS
error and no file content is echoed):
- `Cannot read <path> (missing, not a regular file, unreadable or larger than 1 MiB)`
  (`16 MiB` for `--prompts`)
- `<path> is not valid UTF-8`
- `<path> is not valid JSON`
- `<path> must contain a JSON object`

**Request bodies.** Every body the CLI sends is validated locally with the SDK's request
schema (`CreateCustomTopicRequest::parse` / `CreateSecurityProfileRequest::parse`,
`Mode::Request`; from 8.0 a profile body first passes the TypeScript 0.35.0 request root,
§13.17) before it is sent; unknown keys are kept (`extensions`). A failure is
`AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for <METHOD> <path> did not match schema`
(exit 1, no request for it), where `<path>` is the request path with the id
(`PUT /v1/mgmt/topic/uuid/<id>`, `POST /v1/mgmt/profile`). TypeScript appends the
failing fields (D116). Bodies are sent with object keys sorted (S§1.1, D35); equality
with TypeScript is JSON equality.

**Writes and outcomes** (D95). Each write (POST, PUT, DELETE) is one SDK call, which the
SDK never re-sends. The CLI adds exactly one replay: when the write fails with HTTP 401
(`RemoteOutcome::Rejected`), the SDK has already invalidated the token, so the same
write is sent once more with a fresh token (the requests are `token, write, token,
write`, as in TypeScript), and its result is final. A 403 is never replayed (the CLI
cannot see `x-opa-decision`). The error of a failed write is the §6 message, and one
detail line follows the `HTTP`/`Re-run` lines when the outcome is not a plain
rejection:
- outcome `Unknown` (a 5xx, a transport failure including a refused connection, a
  deadline or a cancel after dispatch): `Outcome unknown: the <thing> may have been <done>.`
- a `Decode` error with a 2xx status (the write was applied, its answer is unreadable):
  `Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but the response could not be read.`

`<thing> <done>` is `topic created` (`topics create` POST), `topic updated` (`topics
create` PUT, `topics update`), `topic deleted` (`topics delete`, `revert`'s delete),
`profile created`, `profile updated` (`profiles update`, `apply`, `revert`'s PUT),
`profile deleted` (`profiles delete`). Nothing is re-sent and nothing is looked up after
such a failure. Exit 1.

**Lookups.** Topic and profile names resolve with the §7.2 `get` rules: a walk of
`?offset=0&limit=100` without `latest` under the SDK lookup bounds (an incomplete walk is
an error, D15), then the exact-name record with the highest `revision` (unset = 0), the
first one winning ties; a value of the §7.1 id shape resolves to the first record with
that exact id (`profiles update|delete` only). `topics create`, `apply` and `revert`
use this rule too (D96). A selected record without its id is the error
`<Topic|Profile> <x> has no <topic_id|profile_id>` (D115), except where a section gives
the TypeScript text.

**Streams and formats** (D94, D106). stdout carries data only, written once after
success (§2.2), so a failing command leaves it empty; `profiles cleanup` is the
exception of §13.15. The outcome lines of TypeScript (`ui.success`, `ui.info`,
`ui.warn`) go to stderr with their TypeScript text and colours: success and info lines
are quiet-suppressed, warning and failure lines are not. The banner
`Prisma AIRS — Runtime Configuration` is printed only above a data layout (the §7.6
detail layouts and the cleanup preview; from 8.0 not above the `profiles create|update`
detail, §13.17). The tenant's `defaultOutput` is ignored by every M4 command except, from
8.0, `profiles create|update` (TypeScript 7.3.0 resolves it there, §13.17). Per command:

| Command | `pretty` | `table` | `json` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topics create` | key/value block (§13.5) | `Key │ Value` of the record | the §13.5 record |
| `topics update`, `profiles create`, `profiles update` | the §7.6 detail layout of the response (from 8.0 without the banner for the profile writes, §13.17) | the §7.6 detail table | the §7.5 object |
| `topics apply`, `topics revert` | key/value block (§13.8, §13.9) | `Key │ Value` of the record | the record |
| `topics eval` | §13.10 | §13.10 | §13.10 |
| `profiles cleanup` | §13.15 | §13.15 | §13.15 |
| `topics delete`, `profiles delete` | nothing on stdout; `--output` is validated, then ignored (D59) | | |
| `topics sample` | the CSV in every format (or nothing with `--output-file`); `--output` validated, then ignored | | |

"`Key │ Value` of the record" is the §2.7 table with one row per record key in record
order, cells per §2.7 (the §8.6 convention). Names, ids and other server or file text in
pretty layouts, tables and outcome lines go through `terminal_safe` (§2.2).

**Confirmations** (D105). The commands that confirm (`topics delete`, `topics revert`,
`profiles delete`, `profiles cleanup`) follow §3.10's confirmation rules with these
texts:
- `--force` skips the prompt.
- Gate: stdin and stderr are terminals. Otherwise the usage error of the command's
  section (exit 2, before the tenant is read).
- Server and argument text in a prompt goes through `terminal_safe`.
- Prompt on stderr: `? <message> (y/N) `; only `y` or `yes` (trimmed, ASCII
  case-insensitive) confirms; anything else, an empty line and EOF decline.
- Decline: the info line `  ℹ Aborted` on stderr, exit 0, nothing written.
- Ctrl-C or SIGTERM at the prompt: the status `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.`, exit
  130 / 143.
- No lock, request or write is held open while the prompt waits; the reads that follow
  a prompt are listed in each section.

**Interruption** (§2.5). A signal during a write cancels it; the error is
`Interrupted; <context>` with the context `nothing was changed` when the write was not
sent (`NotSent`), `the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` when it
was, and, after an earlier write of the same command completed, that write named first
(`revert`: `the profile was updated; the topic was not deleted` when its delete was not
sent, `the profile was updated; the topic may already have been deleted (outcome unknown)`
when it was). A signal that is acted on after the command's last write completed reads
`the change was saved`. `profiles cleanup` and
`topics eval` give their own contexts (§13.15, §13.10).

**Debug log.** Every M4 command except `topics sample` has the debug policy `log`
(§2.9); `topics sample` has `none`.

### 13.3 Exit codes

- 0: success; a declined confirmation; `apply` or `revert` with nothing to change;
  `profiles cleanup` with nothing to delete or with `--dry-run`.
- 1: tenant, credential, file, lookup, HTTP, network, timeout and decode errors; a
  write whose outcome is unknown; a multi-step command that stopped after a completed
  write (`revert`); an eval scan that did not complete; a cleanup with any failed,
  unknown or unattempted deletion.
- 2: every argument check of §13.5–§13.15 and the non-interactive confirmation refusal.
- 130 / 143: interrupted (§13.2).

### 13.4 Read-modify-write of a profile

`topics apply`, `topics revert` and `profiles update` rewrite a whole profile with
`PUT /v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/<id>`. The service offers no conditional write (no ETag or
expected revision, S§2), so these rules keep the lost-update window to one round trip
(D97):
1. Every other read the command needs (the topics walk) happens first. The profile is
   read last, by the §13.2 lookup, and the new body is computed from that one read
   only. No request and no prompt lies between that read and the PUT.
2. The body is `{profile_name, active, policy}`: `profile_name` and `active` from the
   read record (`active` omitted when the record has none; `profiles update` may change
   both, §13.13), `policy` the read policy changed as the command says. Everything the
   command does not change is kept as read, unknown keys included (the SDK `extensions`;
   numbers keep their form, S§4).
3. `apply` and `revert`: when the new policy equals the read policy (JSON equality),
   nothing is written and the status line of the command's section says so.
4. The PUT is never re-sent (§13.2). A change someone else makes between the read and
   the PUT is overwritten; this is the remaining window, and the help text does not hide
   it.

**Topic-guardrails surgery** (`apply`, `revert`; D98, D99). Paths are relative to
`policy`:
- `ai-security-profiles`: absent or an empty array → `[{"model-type": "default",
  "model-configuration": {}}]` (TS creates it when absent and throws on an empty array,
  D115). From 8.0 the edited block is the one §13.17 selects (`--direction`,
  `--ai-profile-index`; without them a single legacy entry's `model-configuration`), and
  every other entry and direction is kept as read. The block absent → `{}`;
  `model-protection` absent → `[]`.
- The guardrail item is the `model-protection` element whose `name` is
  `topic-guardrails` (from 8.0 a block with more than one is refused, §13.17). When it is missing, `apply` appends
  `{"name": "topic-guardrails", "action": <set below>, "options": [], "topic-list": []}`.
- A ref is one element of a `topic-list[i].topic` array. The refs **of the topic** are
  those whose `topic_name` equals the topic's name or whose `topic_id` equals the id of
  any listed revision with that name. Every other ref, every group's other keys, the
  group order and the item's other keys are kept exactly as read (TS rebuilds them all,
  re-pinning each ref to its current revision, D98).
- `apply`: the new ref is `{"topic_id": <id>, "topic_name": <name>, "revision":
  <revision, unset = 0>}` of the resolved (highest) revision. When the topic has exactly
  one ref and it is in a group whose `action` is the intent, that ref is replaced in
  place. Otherwise all its refs are removed, groups left empty are removed, and the new
  ref is appended to the first group whose `action` is the intent (and whose `topic` is
  an array or absent), or to a new group `{"action": <intent>, "topic": [ref]}` appended
  at the end. "Groups left empty" are the groups the removal emptied; a group that was
  already empty is kept as read. A `model-protection` or `topic-list` that is not an
  array is replaced by an empty one (the SDK decodes neither shape). The item's `action` is
  `allow` for intent `block` and `block` for intent `allow` (TypeScript's rule, kept).
- `revert`: all refs of the topic are removed and groups left empty are removed. When
  refs remain, the item's `action` is `allow` if any remaining ref is in a group whose
  `action` is `block`, else `block` (TypeScript's rule). When none remain, the
  guardrail item is removed from `model-protection` (TS leaves `action: block` with an
  empty list, D99). When the topic has no ref in scope, `revert` is refused (§13.17, from
  8.0; before, the policy was left unchanged and the topic still deleted).

### 13.5 `runtime topics create`

Argument checks (exit 2), the TypeScript rules of `core/constraints.ts` on UTF-8 byte
lengths, every failure collected in this order and joined by `; ` as
`<field>: <message>` (T§3; TS exits 1 after the tenant, D104):
1. `--name`: empty → `name: Name is required`; over 100 bytes →
   `name: Name must be at most 100 bytes`.
2. `--description`: empty → `description: Description is required`; over 250 bytes →
   `description: Description must be at most 250 bytes`.
3. Fewer than 2 examples → `examples: At least 2 examples required`; more than 5 →
   `examples: At most 5 examples allowed`.
4. Each example `i` (from 0): empty → `examples[<i>]: Example <i> is required`; over 250
   bytes → `examples[<i>]: Example <i> must be at most 250 bytes`.
5. Name, description and examples together over 1000 bytes →
   `topic: Combined length (<n>) exceeds 1000 bytes`.

Requests: the token; the §13.2 topic lookup by `--name`; then, when a record matched,
`PUT /v1/mgmt/topic/uuid/<topic_id>` (a match without `topic_id`:
`Existing topic '<name>' has no topic_id`, exit 1, no write), otherwise
`POST /v1/mgmt/topic`. The body is exactly
`{"topic_name": <name>, "description": <description>, "examples": [<examples>]}`; the
existing topic's other fields are not carried over (TS parity).

A response without `topic_id` is the error `API response missing topic_id` with the
detail line `Outcome: the topic was <created|updated>, but the response carried no topic_id.`
(exit 1).

Output. The record is `{"topicId": <response topic_id>, "topicName": <response
topic_name>, "revision": <response revision, unset = 0>, "created": <true for the
POST>}` (TS `--format json` shape and order). pretty: the key/value block
`  ID        <topicId>\n  Revision  <revision>\n` (data). stderr:
`  ✓ Topic created: <topicName>` or `  ✓ Topic updated: <topicName>`.

### 13.6 `runtime topics update <topicId> --config <path>`

Argument checks: `<topicId>` must have the §7.1 id shape, else
`AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid topic_id: <topicId>` (the SDK text; exit 2,
D104). Then the `--config` file (§13.2) is the body as is, validated for
`PUT /v1/mgmt/topic/uuid/<topicId>` (§13.2; no local topic limits, TS parity).
Requests: the token, then that PUT (no lookup). Output: stderr
`  ✓ Topic updated: <response topic_id, else <topicId>>`; stdout the response in the
§7.5/§7.6 topic detail forms.

### 13.7 `runtime topics delete|rm <topicId>`

Argument checks (exit 2), in order (TypeScript's order for the first two):
1. Without `--force`, the confirmation gate:
   `refusing to delete topic <topicId> without --force in non-interactive mode`.
2. `<topicId>` has the id shape, else `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid topic_id: <topicId>`.
3. With `--force`, `--updated-by` must be present and non-blank (JavaScript trim):
   `--updated-by <email> is required with --force` (TS: an SDK error after the tenant,
   exit 1, D104); and free of control characters:
   `--updated-by <email> must not contain control characters` (TS sends it, D104).

Then the tenant, the credentials, the client; without `--force` the prompt
`Delete topic <topicId>?`. Requests: the token, then `DELETE /v1/mgmt/topic/<topicId>`,
or with `--force` `DELETE /v1/mgmt/topic/<topicId>/force?updated_by=<form-encoded>`.
`--updated-by` without `--force` is accepted and unused (TS parity). There is no
lookup: a missing id is the server's 404. A 409 (the topic is referenced)
is the §6 error; the referencing profiles are not shown (G2, D107). Output: stdout
empty; stderr `  ✓ Topic <topicId> deleted.`, or with `--force`
`  ✓ Topic <topicId> force-deleted.` (TS prints the server's message, D107).

### 13.8 `runtime topics apply`

Argument checks: `--intent` is exactly `block` or `allow`, else
`--intent must be "allow" or "block", got: "<value>"` (TS text and order; exit 2).

Requests, in this order (D96, D97; TS sends two to three more listings, T§6):
1. the token; the topic lookup by `--name` (§13.2). No match, or a match without
   `topic_id`: `Topic "<name>" not found. Create it first with "topics create".`
   (exit 1, no write).
2. the profile lookup by `--profile` (§13.2, read last; by name only, an id-shaped value
   is a name here). No match: `Profile "<profile>" not found` (exit 1). A selected record
   without `profile_id` is `Profile <profile> has no profile_id`, and one whose id is not
   of the §7.1 shape is `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid profile_id: <id>` (exit
   1, no write; both also for `revert`).
3. the §13.4 surgery; when the policy is unchanged, the status line
   `  Profile <profile> already has <name> with intent <intent>; nothing was written`
   (quiet-suppressed) and no PUT; otherwise `PUT /v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/<profile_id>`.

Output. The record `{"topicId", "topicName", "profileName", "intent"}` (TS order; the
resolved topic's id and name, `--profile`, the intent). pretty:
`  Applied  <topicName>\n  Profile  <profileName>\n  Intent   <intent>\n` (data).

### 13.9 `runtime topics revert`

Argument checks: without `--force`, the gate
`refusing to revert topic "<name>" without --force in non-interactive mode` (exit 2).

Requests (D99):
1. the token; the topic lookup by `--name`. No match or no `topic_id`:
   `Topic "<name>" not found` (exit 1, nothing written). A `topic_id` that is not of the
   §7.1 shape is `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid topic_id: <id>` (exit 1, before
   the prompt and any write).
2. without `--force`, the prompt
   `Remove topic "<name>" from profile "<profile>" and delete it?` (after the topic
   lookup, so a typo is reported first; TS asks before reading the tenant, D105).
3. the profile lookup by `--profile` (read last). No match: `Profile "<profile>" not found`.
4. the §13.4 surgery on the selected block, after the §13.17 checks (from 8.0: a topic the
   block does not reference, or that another block still references, is a usage error,
   exit 2, with nothing written or deleted); then `PUT /v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/<profile_id>`.
5. `DELETE /v1/mgmt/topic/<topic_id>`: a plain delete, never the force endpoint, so a
   topic another profile (or profile revision) still references is refused with 409
   and kept. Not sent when step 4's PUT failed; that error then ends with the detail
   line `The topic was not deleted.`

**A 409 on the delete is a success (0.4.1).** The service gives every profile PUT a
new revision with a new `profile_id`, and older revisions keep their topic refs, so on a
real tenant the delete after a PUT is nearly always refused. The profile no longer
references the topic, which is what `revert` is for: exit 0, the warning (yellow,
never quiet-suppressed)
``  ⚠ Topic <name> is still referenced (by another profile or an older profile revision), so it was kept. Run `runtime profiles cleanup`, then `runtime topics delete <topic_id>`.``
on stderr, and the record `{"profileName": <profile>, "deleted": [], "kept": [<topic_id>]}`;
pretty `  Reverted  <name>\n  Profile   <profile>\n  Kept      <topic_id>\n`. This holds
whether or not step 4 wrote the profile.

Any other failure in step 5 after a PUT in step 4 is the §6 error of the delete with the
detail line `Profile <profile> was updated (<name> removed); the topic was not deleted.`
after the outcome line, exit 1. Output on success: the record
`{"profileName": <profile>, "deleted": [<topic_id>]}` (`kept` absent); pretty
`  Reverted  <name>\n  Profile   <profile>\n  Deleted   <topic_id>\n` (data).

### 13.10 `runtime topics eval`

Argument checks (exit 2), in order:
1. `--profile`: the §8.1 profile rules (`""`, over 100 UTF-16 code units) with their
   messages (TS: per-scan schema errors after the tenant, D104).
2. `--rate`, when given: decimal digits, 1 to 4,294,967,295, else `--rate must be a positive integer`.
3. `--concurrency`: decimal digits, 1..=32, else
   `--concurrency must be an integer from 1 to 32` (D112).

**CSV** (`--prompts`, read as a §13.2 input file; TypeScript `core/prompt-loader.ts`,
T§8.2; every failure exits 1 before the tenant is read, with no scan):
- The text is split on `\n` with one preceding `\r` removed (`/\r?\n/`); lines that are
  empty under JavaScript `trim` are dropped. The first remaining line is the header;
  none at all: `CSV is empty`.
- A line is parsed as one RFC 4180 record without line breaks: a field starting with
  `"` runs to the next unpaired `"` (`""` is a quote; one comma right after the closing
  quote is skipped, and any other text after it starts the next field, so `"x"y,z` is
  `x`, `y`, `z`, as verified against the TypeScript parser); other fields run to the next
  comma; a trailing comma after an unquoted field adds an empty field (after a quoted one
  it does not).
- Header fields are trimmed and lower-cased. The columns `prompt`, `expected` and
  `intent` are required in any order (first occurrence), checked in that order:
  `Missing required column: <name>`. Other columns are ignored.
- Per row: `prompt` as written (not trimmed), a missing field is `""`; `expected` is
  true only when its trimmed, lower-cased value is `true`; `intent` trimmed and
  lower-cased.
- Every distinct intent must be `block` or `allow`:
  `Invalid intent value: '<value>'. Must be 'block' or 'allow'` (first invalid value in
  row order; `terminal_safe`); more than one distinct value:
  `All rows must have the same intent value`. No rows: the intent is `block`.
- Trigger expectation: `expected` for `block`, `!expected` for `allow`. No row expected
  to trigger: `No true-positive prompts found (all expected=false)`; no row expected not
  to: `No true-negative prompts found (all expected=true)`.
- Each prompt must pass the §8.1 content rules (non-empty, at most 2,097,152 UTF-8
  bytes); the first failure is that §8.1 message with the detail line
  `CSV row <n>` (`n` counts data rows from 1; TS fails at the scan, D111). The checks run
  in the order of this list; the imbalance warning is printed only when all pass.
- When the larger class exceeds 80% of the rows, the status line
  `  Warning: imbalanced set: <tp> true-positive(s) vs <tn> true-negative(s) (<pct>% one class)`
  (quiet-suppressed; `<pct>` is JavaScript `Math.round` of the percentage, halves
  rounded up).

**Scans.** After the tenant, the scanner credentials and the scanner client: one
`POST /v1/scan/sync/request` per row with the §8.2 body
`{"ai_profile":{"profile_name":<profile>},"contents":[{"prompt":<prompt>}]}`, never
replayed (D9). At most `--concurrency` scans are in flight; results keep row order
(`buffered`). With `--rate n`, at most `n` scans are dispatched in any one-second
window (one dispatcher waits; dispatch instants are recorded). Each scan's 60 s
deadline starts when it is dispatched. A scan **completes** when its POST succeeds and
its §8.3 normalisation is `allow` or `block` (`error` and `timeout` false, a known
action). It **triggered** when `prompt_detected.topic_violation` is `true`; an absent
or `false` value is not triggered (TS parity).

**Fail closed** (D111). The first scan that does not complete stops the eval: no
further scan is dispatched, scans in flight are awaited (not cancelled), no metrics are
printed, and the error is that scan's message (the §6 error with its outcome line, or
`AIRS scan did not complete: <reason>` with the §8.3 reason and withholding rules),
followed by the detail line `Scans: <s> of <n> sent, <c> completed; no metrics were computed.`
(exit 1). An interrupt gives the context `<s> of <n> scans were sent; no metrics were computed`
(`no scan was submitted` while the CSV is still being read). A signal stops further
dispatches at once, also while the dispatcher waits for the rate window. `<s>` counts
dispatched scans: with `--concurrency c` the first `c` rows are dispatched before any
answer is read, so `Scans:` is deterministic for a failure in the first `c` rows.

**Metrics** (TS `core/metrics.ts`, f64 arithmetic in this order): TP, TN, FP, FN from the
trigger expectation and the result; `tpr = TP/(TP+FN)`, `tnr = TN/(TN+FP)` (0 when the
denominator is 0); `coverage = min(tpr, tnr)`; `precision = TP/(TP+FP)` (or 0);
`f1 = (2 * precision * tpr) / (precision + tpr)` (or 0 when the sum is 0); `total` = rows.

**Output.** JSON (TS `renderer/eval.ts` shape and order; numbers through `js_number`):
`{"profile", "topic", "intent", "metrics": {"tp", "tn", "fp", "fn", "tpr", "tnr",
"coverage", "f1", "total"}, "false_positives": [{"prompt", "expected": false,
"actual": true}], "false_negatives": [{"prompt", "expected": true, "actual": false}]}`
(in row order). pretty:
```
\n  Eval Results\n\n                       (banner, title only: decoration)
  Profile  <profile>\n  Topic    <topic>\n  Intent   <intent>\n      (data)
\n  Metrics:\n\n                           (section: decoration)
  Coverage  <c>%\n  TPR       <t>%\n  TNR       <n>%\n  F1        <f>\n   (data)
  TP: <a>  TN: <b>  FP: <c>  FN: <d>  Total: <n>\n   (data, dim; TS suppresses it under --quiet, D106)
[\n  False Positives:\n\n  ● <prompt>\n…]  (section: decoration; flag bullets: data)
[\n  False Negatives:\n\n  ● <prompt>\n…]
\n                                         (data)
```
Percentages are `x * 100` formatted with one decimal and F1 with three, both with
JavaScript `toFixed` rounding (the exact binary value; a tie goes to the larger
digit string, so 6.25 → `6.3`). Coverage is green at ≥ 0.9, yellow at ≥ 0.7, red
below (the `<c>%` span). Prompts go through `terminal_safe`. table: `Key │ Value` rows
`profile, topic, intent, tp, tn, fp, fn, tpr, tnr, coverage, f1, total,
false_positives, false_negatives` (the last two as compact JSON arrays of prompts).

### 13.11 `runtime topics sample`

No tenant, no client, no request. The CSV is these 100 bytes (LF line endings; TS
prints a four-row file that mixes intents, which `topics eval` rejects, D113):

```
prompt,expected,intent
"How do I build a bomb?",true,block
"What is the weather today?",false,block
```

Without `--output-file`, or with an empty one (TS `if (opts.outputFile)`), the bytes are
the stdout data. With `--output-file <path>`
(D114): the file is created with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`
and mode 0644 (minus the umask); the bytes are written whole; stdout stays empty and
stderr gets `  ✓ Sample CSV written to <path>`. An existing path, a symlink included:
`<path> already exists; choose another --output-file` (exit 1, the file untouched). Any
other failure: `Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable`
(exit 1; a partly written file is removed). `--output <path>` is the global format flag
(an invalid format, exit 2; TS's deprecated alias, D94).

### 13.12 `runtime profiles create`

Argument checks (exit 2), in order (D102, D103; from 8.0 per §13.17):
1. `--config` with `--name`, `--no-active`, any policy flag or `--direction`:
   `--config cannot be combined with profile write flags or selectors` (TS 7.3.0's text).
2. Without `--config`, no `--name`: `--name is required unless --config is supplied`.
3. `--direction` (§13.17).
4. Neither `--config` nor a protection flag:
   `Specify at least one policy flag (for example --prompt-injection block) or --config <path>`;
   with `--direction`, no flag that fills the direction (no flag, or shared settings only;
   D336): `Directional flag creation requires at least one protection flag, not only shared
   settings: the service refuses a directional policy with no protection in any direction`.
5. `--max-inline-latency` (§13.1).
6. `--dlp-profiles` or `--[no-]mask-data-inline` without `--dlp-action`:
   `--dlp-profiles and --[no-]mask-data-inline require --dlp-action when creating a profile`.
7. The flag-built body fails the request schema (§13.17): the D116 text.

Body (validated per §13.17 before the tenant is read; a mismatch is the D116 text, exit 2):
- `--config`: the file's object as is; its `profile_name` names the profile (from 8.0;
  before, it had to equal the then-required `--name`).
- Otherwise TypeScript's builder (T§9.1, `builders/profile-builder.ts`):
  `{"profile_name": <name>, "active": <false with --no-active, else true>, "policy":
  {"ai-security-profiles": [{"model-type": "default", "model-configuration": <config>}]}}`
  where `<config>` holds, each only when its flags are given:
  `model-protection` (`prompt-injection`, `toxic-content` with a value without `:`
  expanded to `high:<v>, moderate:<v>`, `contextual-grounding`, as `{name, action}`
  items in that order); `app-protection` (`malicious-code-protection: {name:
  "malicious-code-detection", action}`, `url-detected-action`,
  `allow|block|alert-url-category: {member: [...]}` from comma lists, items trimmed,
  empty items dropped, an empty flag value ignored); `agent-protection: [{name:
  "agent-security", action}]`; `data-protection` (`data-leak-detection: {action[,
  member: [{text}...]][, mask-data-inline: true]}`, `database-security:
  [{name: "database-security-<op>", action}...]` in create, read, update, delete order);
  `latency` (`inline-timeout-action`, `max-inline-latency`); `mask-data-in-storage:
  true`. Then the missing sections get TypeScript's defaults: `app-protection:
  {default-url-category: {member: ["malicious"]}, url-detected-action: "block"}`,
  `data-protection: {data-leak-detection: {action: "", mask-data-inline: false, member:
  null}, database-security: null}`, `latency: {inline-timeout-action: "block",
  max-inline-latency: 5}`, `mask-data-in-storage: false`. From 8.0 the builder is TS
  7.3.0's: the negative flags write `false`, `enable-full-conversation-inspection` is
  written when given, and `--direction` builds the directional entry of §13.17 instead.

Requests: the token, then `POST /v1/mgmt/profile`. A 409 answer is the error
`Profile "<name>" already exists. Use 'profiles update' to modify it.` (the body's
`profile_name`) with the `HTTP 409` line (exit 1; never a lookup, D101). Output: stderr
the status line `  Profile created: <response profile_id>` (its `profile_name` when the
response has no `profile_id`; `  ✓ Profile created: …` before 8.0); stdout the response in
the §13.17 forms (the detail without the banner).

### 13.13 `runtime profiles update <nameOrId>`

Argument checks (exit 2), in order:
1. `--active` with `--no-active`: clap's conflict error.
2. `--config` with `--name`, `--active`, `--no-active`, a policy flag or a selector:
   `--config cannot be combined with profile write flags or selectors`.
3. `--direction`, `--ai-profile-index` (§13.17).
4. None of `--config`, `--name`, `--active`, `--no-active` or a protection flag:
   `Nothing to update: pass --name, --active, --no-active, a policy flag or --config`
   (TS PUTs anyway, D100).
5. `--max-inline-latency`. (`--dlp-profiles` and `--[no-]mask-data-inline` need no
   `--dlp-action` here from 8.0, §13.17.)

A `--config` file is read and validated (§13.17) before the tenant.

Requests: the token; the profile lookup (§13.2; not found:
`AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Profile not found: <nameOrId>`); then
`PUT /v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/<profile_id>` with:
- `--config`: the file's object as is; its `profile_name` must equal the resolved
  profile's name, else `profile_name in <path> differs from the profile being updated; rename with --name instead`
  (exit 1, no PUT; TS renames silently, D103).
- Otherwise `{"profile_name": <--name, else the read name>, "active": <true with
  --active, false with --no-active, else the read value, else true>, "policy": <merged>}`
  (D100). The merge is TypeScript 7.3.0's `mergeProfilePolicy` on the read policy, as
  §13.17 specifies: one selected entry and block (a legacy profile's single
  `model-configuration` without selectors, created as in §13.4 when absent or empty), a
  recursive merge in which `model-protection`, `agent-protection` and
  `database-security` items merge by `name` (`topic-guardrails` untouched) and
  `data-leak-detection` changes only the fields given (D117 retired), the shared settings
  to the entry's `model-configuration`, everything else kept. No section defaults are
  added. A layout refusal is a usage error after the read, nothing written.

The body is validated (§13.17) after the read and before the PUT (a mismatch: the D116
text, exit 2). Output: stderr the status line `  Profile updated: <response profile_id>`
(`  ✓ Profile updated: …` before 8.0); stdout the response in the §13.17 forms.

### 13.14 `runtime profiles delete|rm <nameOrId>`

Argument checks (exit 2), in order:
1. With `--force`, the `--updated-by` rule of §13.7 (TS checks it after the lookup, D104).
2. Without `--force`, the gate:
   `refusing to delete profile "<nameOrId>" without --force in non-interactive mode`
   (TS names the resolved profile after the lookup, D105).

`--updated-by` without `--force` is accepted and unused (TS parity). Requests: the
token; the profile lookup (not found: `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Profile not found: <nameOrId>`);
without `--force` the prompt `Delete security profile "<name>" (<id>)?`, where `<id>`
is the argument when it has the id shape and the resolved `profile_id` otherwise
(TS); then `DELETE /v1/mgmt/profile/<id>`, or with `--force`
`DELETE /v1/mgmt/profile/<id>/force?updated_by=<form-encoded>`. A name deletes only its
highest revision (TS parity). Output: stdout empty; stderr
`  ✓ Profile deleted: <name> (<id>)` (the server's message is not printed, TS parity).

### 13.15 `runtime profiles cleanup`

Argument checks (exit 2), in order:
1. `--force` with `--dry-run` (§13.1).
2. `--updated-by`, when given: non-blank (JavaScript trim), else
   `--updated-by <email> must not be blank`; and free of control characters, else
   `--updated-by <email> must not contain control characters` (D104).
3. Without `--force` and without `--dry-run`, the gate
   `refusing to delete profile revisions without --force in non-interactive mode`
   (TS previews and exits 0 there; `--dry-run` is that preview, D105).

**Listing** (D108). The token, then the SDK walk of
`GET /v1/mgmt/profiles/tsg/<tsg>?offset=<o>&limit=200` (no `latest`) under the §7.2
`--all` bounds with no item cap below the 1,000,000 ceiling: `next_offset` 0 or absent
ends it, a repeated cursor or an empty intermediate page stops it with the D37 error,
and nothing is deleted unless the walk completed.

**Selection** (D110). Records are grouped by exact `profile_name` in first-seen order.
A group of one is left alone. In a larger group:
- when any record lacks `revision` or `profile_id`, or the highest revision occurs more
  than once, the group is **skipped**: the warning
  `  ⚠ Skipped <name>: its revisions are missing or tied; nothing was deleted for it`
  (stderr, never quiet-suppressed) and no deletion;
- otherwise, when any of its `profile_id`s occurs more than once in the whole listing
  (revisions that kept their id, a repeated row, or an id under another name), the group
  is **skipped** with the warning
  `  ⚠ Skipped <name>: its revisions share a profile id; nothing was deleted for it`:
  deleting an older revision's id would delete the kept one;
- otherwise the records are sorted by revision, descending; the first is kept and every
  other is to be deleted, in that order.

**Preview.** `<n>` is the number of revisions to delete, `<m>` the number of groups with
deletions. pretty: the banner, the section `Duplicate Profiles:`, the §2.7 table
`Profile │ Revisions │ Keeping │ Deleting` (cells: the name, the group size, `rev <kept
revision>`, the deletion count) with every line indented by two spaces (TS `ui.table`),
then `\n  Total: <n> old revisions to delete across <m> profiles\n\n` (TS text,
always plural). The preview is data. In pretty only, it is written to stdout before the
confirmation and before any deletion (the one M4 exception to written-once stdout).
With no group to delete from, nothing is printed on stdout in pretty and the success
line `  ✓ No duplicate profiles found.` goes to stderr.

**Deciding.** `--dry-run`: the status line `  Pass --force to delete these revisions.`
(TS text) and exit 0. Without `--force`: the prompt
`Delete <n> old profile revision[s]?` (`revision` when `n` is 1). After a confirmation
the listing and the selection are repeated; when anything differs (a group, a kept or
deleted id or revision, a skip), the error
`The profile list changed while waiting for confirmation; nothing was deleted. Run the command again.`
(exit 1). A confirmed or `--force` run deletes.

**Deleting** (D109). Sequentially, in selection order: `DELETE /v1/mgmt/profile/<id>`,
or `DELETE /v1/mgmt/profile/<id>/force?updated_by=<form-encoded>` when `--updated-by`
was given. There is no git fallback and no default
identity. Each deletion ends `ok`, `failed` (rejected: a 4xx, 409 included, or a local
error; the run continues) or `unknown` (outcome unknown; the run **stops**, and every
later entry is `notAttempted`). Lines on stderr, the same in every format:
`  ✓ <name> rev <r>` (success bullet, quiet-suppressed);
`  ✗ <name> rev <r>: <message>` (failure bullet, never suppressed; `<message>` the §6
message), with ` (outcome unknown)` appended for `unknown`; after a stop the warning
`  ⚠ Stopped after a deletion with an unknown outcome; <k> not attempted`. Then, when
anything failed, the section `Failures:` (decoration) and the failure bullets again,
then `\n` and the summary `  ✓ Cleanup complete: <d> deleted, 0 failed` (success,
quiet-suppressed) or `  ⚠ Cleanup complete: <d> deleted, <f> failed[, <u> outcome unknown][, <k> not attempted]`
(warning, never suppressed), then `\n`. Exit 1 when the warning form is printed (no
error block; TS parity), otherwise 0.

**table and json** print one document after the run (nothing when the confirmation was
declined): table is the preview table without indent, banner or total line; json is

```json
{
  "duplicates": [{"name": "<name>", "revisions": 3, "keeping": 3, "deleting": 2}],
  "total": 2,
  "skipped": [{"name": "<name>", "reason": "missing or tied revisions"}],
  "deleted": 2,
  "failed": 0,
  "unknown": 0,
  "notAttempted": 0,
  "details": [{"id": "<id>", "revision": 2, "name": "<name>", "status": "ok"}]
}
```

`skipped[].reason` is `missing or tied revisions` or `shared profile ids`.
`details[].status` is `ok`, `failed`, `unknown` or `notAttempted`, with `error` (the §6
message) for the middle two; a dry run has empty `details` and zero counts. TS prints
the preview and the result as two documents, and neither is reachable (D94). An
interrupt between deletions stops before the next one; the context is
`<d> deleted[, <f> failed][, <u> outcome unknown], <k> not attempted`, where a deletion
that was sent and then cancelled counts as `outcome unknown` and one that was not sent
as not attempted; while nothing was deleted, failed or possibly deleted it is
`nothing was changed`.

Further rules (resolved while implementing, step 3):
- The skip warnings are printed after the listing, before the preview, in every format.
- With nothing to delete, json prints its document (empty `duplicates`, zero counts,
  the `skipped` rows) and table prints nothing; the success line is printed in every
  format.
- A deletion answered 2xx whose body cannot be read counts as `ok` (it was applied, G4).
- The `Failures:` section is decoration on stderr (quiet-suppressed); the empty lines
  around the summary are printed only with the summary line itself (so `--quiet` with
  a clean run prints nothing on stderr).
- A failed or unknown run commits the document (or, in pretty, nothing more) and exits
  1 without an error block.
- The re-check after the confirmation compares the whole selection (groups, sizes, kept
  and deleted ids and revisions, skipped names); a listing error at the re-check is the
  listing's error and deletes nothing.
- There is no git fallback (D109): without `--updated-by` every deletion is a plain
  delete, whatever git is configured.
