### 13.17 Directional security profiles (8.0, TypeScript 7.3.0)

TypeScript 7.3.0 (the 8.0 reference, §1) adds directional security profiles to `runtime
profiles create|update` and `runtime topics apply|revert`, on TS SDK 0.35.0. The specs are
its `docs-site/docs/cli/runtime/profiles.md`, `src/airs/profile-policy.ts`,
`src/cli/builders/profile-builder.ts`, `src/cli/commands/runtime.ts`, `topics-apply.ts`
and `topics-revert.ts`, and its `tests/integration/directional-security-profiles.spec.ts`,
whose scenarios run on both CLIs in `tests/parity_runtime_directional.rs`. The Rust form is
`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/profile_policy.rs` (layout rules, selector, recursive merge) and `src/policy.rs`
(builders, merge, topic surgery). **Status: accepted live** (8.0 B7, 2026-10-22, against
`redtail-prod`; `docs/research/live-directional-profiles.md`, MILESTONES 8.0): flag creation
of each of the four directions (with D335), a `--config` create, a protection edit of each
direction, a shared-settings edit, a topic applied and reverted in each direction, backup,
delete, restore and `--on-conflict verify`. Supported for profiles with a single AI entry.
scm-sdk 0.2.4 still marks directional live acceptance unverified on its side. The live
service applies rules the request schema does not express, which the CLI does not check
before sending except D336 (a refusal is the service's HTTP 400, exit 1, with no response
body shown): every directional entry needs all four direction keys (D335 builds them on a
flag create; a `--config` body must hold them), a policy whose directions are all empty is
refused (a flag create that would send one is refused locally, D336; a `--config` body is
sent), `response` refuses `prompt-injection`, and `toxic-content` takes `block` or `allow`
per level. Not exercised live: several AI entries (`--ai-profile-index`), DLP blocks inside a
direction, and the runtime report's `Protection configurations` column; the offline contract
below covers them. Every write that changes a profile without a `dlp_tenant_id` (below)
has an unknown effect on the stored DLP tenant binding.

**The two layouts.** A policy holds AI entries (`ai-security-profiles[]`).
- A **legacy** entry keeps its protections (`model-protection`, `app-protection`,
  `agent-protection`, `data-protection`) and its shared settings in `model-configuration`.
- A **directional** entry is one whose `content-type-mode` is `per_content_type` or that
  has a `content-type-configurations` key (any value). Its protections live per direction
  in `content-type-configurations` (`prompt`, `response`, `tool-call`, `tool-response`;
  each optional, unknown keys kept); its `model-configuration` holds the shared settings
  (`latency`, `mask-data-in-storage`, `enable-full-conversation-inspection`). Protection
  blocks left in a directional entry's `model-configuration` are kept but inactive.
- A **protection location** is one block: an entry's `model-configuration` (active only for
  a legacy entry) or one direction (always active). Locations are listed by entry, the
  `model-configuration` first, then the four known directions in that order, then any
  other key. Non-object entries, blocks and directions are skipped.

**Selectors** (usage errors, exit 2, before the tenant): `--direction <direction>` must be
`prompt`, `response`, `tool-call` or `tool-response`, else `--direction must be prompt,
response, tool-call, or tool-response`; `--ai-profile-index <n>` must be decimal digits
(zero-based, at most 2^53 − 1), else `--ai-profile-index must be a nonnegative integer`
(D332). `profiles create` takes `--direction` only (`--ai-profile-index` is clap's
unknown-argument error, D1).

**Selecting an entry and a block** (TS `selectAiProfile`, `selectProfileProtections`). Every
refusal below is a usage error (exit 2, as in 7.3.0) after the profile read, with nothing
written:
1. Several entries without `--ai-profile-index`: `Multiple AI profile entries: specify
   --ai-profile-index or use --config`. An index without an entry (or a non-object entry):
   `--ai-profile-index does not identify an existing AI profile entry`. An absent or empty
   list without an index gets one `{"model-type": "default"}` entry (D115).
2. A directional entry needs `--direction` (`Directional protection edits require
   --direction`, even with one direction); a mode other than `per_content_type` is
   refused (`Unknown content-type-mode: use a complete --config replacement`); the
   direction must exist (`Selected direction is absent; add it with a complete --config
   replacement before editing protections or topics`), except for a shared-only edit,
   which checks the layout and inserts nothing.
3. A legacy entry refuses a direction (`A legacy profile cannot be converted by
   --direction; use a complete --config replacement`) and any `content-type-mode` key
   (the unknown-mode text). The block is its `model-configuration` (created when absent).

**`profiles create`.**
- `--name` is optional (`Profile name (required unless --config is supplied)`); without
  `--config` it is required (`--name is required unless --config is supplied`).
- `--config <path>` is a complete JSON body (`Complete JSON profile configuration;
  exclusive with write flags`) whose `profile_name` names the profile; it is exclusive
  with `--name`, `--no-active`, every policy flag and `--direction` (`--config cannot be
  combined with profile write flags or selectors`, TS 7.3.0's text; D103).
- With `--direction`, the flags build one directional entry: `{"model-type": "default",
  "content-type-mode": "per_content_type", "model-configuration": <shared settings>,
  "content-type-configurations": {<direction>: <protections>, <each other known direction>:
  {}}}`, no section defaults, the malicious-code item named `malicious-code`. The three
  directions the flags do not fill are written as empty objects (D335: the live service
  refuses a directional entry without all four keys; TS 7.3.0 writes the selected direction
  only), so a later flag edit of any direction finds it present. Without a flag that fills
  the direction (no flag, or only the shared settings `--max-inline-latency`,
  `--inline-timeout-action`, `--[no-]mask-data-in-storage` and
  `--[no-]enable-full-conversation-inspection`), the create is refused before the tenant and
  OAuth (exit 2, D336): `Directional flag creation requires at least one protection flag,
  not only shared settings: the service refuses a directional policy with no protection in
  any direction`. TS 7.3.0 refuses only the flagless create (`… requires at least one
  protection or shared setting; use --config for an empty policy`) and sends a shared-only
  one, which the service refuses; an empty policy through `--config` is refused by the
  service too.
- Without `--direction`, the legacy builder of §13.12 (`malicious-code-detection`, the
  section defaults).
- Every body is validated before the tenant (below).

**`profiles update`.** `--config <path>` is a complete replacement (`Complete JSON
replacement; exclusive with write flags`), exclusive with `--name`, `--active`,
`--no-active`, every policy flag and both selectors (the conflict text above); otherwise
the flags are merged (TS 7.3.0 `mergeProfilePolicy`):
- exactly one entry is selected (above); the protection flags go to its selected block,
  the shared settings (`--max-inline-latency`, `--inline-timeout-action`,
  `--[no-]mask-data-in-storage`, `--[no-]enable-full-conversation-inspection`) to its
  `model-configuration` (created when absent), so a shared-only edit needs no direction
  and keeps every direction;
- the merge is recursive (TS `mergeSettings`): `model-protection`, `agent-protection` and
  `database-security` items merge by `name` (a match is merged recursively, keeping its
  severities, topic lists and unknown keys; a new name is appended; a name that occurs
  more than once is refused: `Ambiguous detector identity: <name>`); objects merge
  recursively; other values replace. A `malicious-code-protection` without a `name` gets
  `malicious-code` (also on a legacy entry: the update merge path), an existing name is
  kept;
- every other entry, direction, detector and key is kept as read; an unknown mode is kept
  by a shared-only edit;
- explicit `false` is written (`--no-mask-data-inline`, `--no-mask-data-in-storage`,
  `--no-enable-full-conversation-inspection`); of a positive/negative pair the last one
  given wins (clap `overrides_with`, commander's rule);
- `--dlp-profiles` and `--[no-]mask-data-inline` need no `--dlp-action` on update: they
  overlay their fields on the block's `data-leak-detection` (D117 retired);
- `--active` changes only when given (D100).

**Flag presence** follows TS 7.3.0 `hasAnyProtectionFlag`: the text flags count when
non-empty, except `--dlp-action` and `--dlp-profiles`, which count when given at all (an
empty `--dlp-action ""` writes `"action": ""`; an empty `--dlp-profiles ""` writes no
`member`); the boolean pairs count in both forms.

**Request validation.** Every profile body is validated with the TypeScript 0.35.0 request
root that scm-sdk 0.2.4's create and update also apply,
`typescript:0.35.0:CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema` (`validation::parse`, `Mode::Request`;
the model `parse` keeps its frozen 0.34.0 binding, §15.25). On `profiles create|update` a
mismatch is the D116 text as a usage error (exit 2): before the tenant for a `--config`
file and a flag-built create body (`PUT /v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/<profile_id>` names an
update file's request before the lookup, the id when the argument is one), after the read
for a merged update body. `topics apply|revert` validate their PUT with the same root and
keep exit 1 (TS reports their schema failure as an operational error). The transfer
commands validate with the same roots (`valid_profile_body`, the Basic fallback's
`typescript:0.35.0:PolicySchema`), and a restore checks each mapped body again with the
request root just before its write (`policy::request_body`; a mismatch is the stop text,
nothing sent), never with the model's 0.34.0 `parse` (defence in depth: planning already checks
the source body with the same root, so no tested body reaches this refusal).

**Output** (TS 7.3.0 `emitDetail`). `profiles create|update` print the status line
`  Profile created|updated: <id>` (dim, stderr, quiet-suppressed; D106) and the response:
pretty is the §7.6 detail **without** the runtime banner, json the §7.5 object, table the
`Key │ Value` detail (Rust-only, D94); `yaml` stays refused (D50). The format is
`--output`, else the tenant's `defaultOutput`, else pretty (D94). Every profile view
(`get`, `list`, `create`, `update`) gains:
- json and table: `dlpTenantId` after `policy`, only when the record carries
  `dlp_tenant_id` (a GET may omit it), with the value the record carries (an unexpected
  `null` or number included, D334);
- pretty detail: `DLP tenant  <id>` after `Status` (a value that is not a string as its
  compact JSON, D334), and `Protection locations
  AI[<i>] <model-type, else unspecified> / <direction|legacy>[, …]` (the active locations)
  before `Policy`;
- the printed policy in TypeScript SDK 0.35.0's key order: scm-sdk 0.2.4 serialises an AI
  entry and `model-configuration` in its 0.34.0 field order, so the views reorder those
  two objects (`model-type, content-type, content-type-mode, content-type-configurations,
  model-configuration`; `data-protection, app-protection, model-protection,
  agent-protection, mask-data-in-storage, latency, enable-full-conversation-inspection`),
  the rest as serialised (D35).

**`topics apply|revert`** take `--direction` and `--ai-profile-index` (`AI profile entry
index (zero-based)`) and act on the selected block (the rules above, with the direction
required to exist); the §13.4 surgery is otherwise unchanged. A block with more than one
`topic-guardrails` item is refused (`Ambiguous topic-guardrails identity in selected
protection section`). `apply` keeps every other topic, block and direction. `revert`
refuses, in this order, with nothing written or deleted:
1. with a selector, its layout checks;
2. no ref of the topic in scope (the selected block; without a selector, every active
   block): `Topic "<name>" is not assigned to the selected protection section` (also for a
   legacy profile; D99);
3. with a selector, a ref of the topic in any other block (another direction, another
   entry, or a retained inactive `model-configuration`): `Topic is referenced in another
   direction or AI entry; detach those references before reverting and deleting`;
4. the selection of the write itself (several entries, or a directional entry, without a
   selector).
The refs counted are the §13.4 identity's (D333). The delete stays the plain delete with
the 0.4.1 409 rule (D99).

**Reports and transfer.**
- `runtime report`: the profile table gains `Protection configurations` (between `Storage
  masking` and `Last modified (UTC)`): one `AI[<i>] <model-type> / <direction|legacy>:
  <sections>` per active location, joined by `; `, the sections being those of
  `model-protection`, `agent-protection`, `app-protection`, `data-protection` that hold a
  non-empty object or array (`No modeled protection sections returned` when none,
  `Unknown` when there is no location). Timeout actions and storage masking still read each
  entry's `model-configuration`.
- `runtime profiles backup|restore`: the DLP references and the Basic fallback walk every
  location (directions and retained blocks, the reference paths naming the direction); the
  canonical `database-security: null` and the comparison's server-default allowances apply
  to legacy entries only, so directions compare strictly; topic references were already
  found anywhere in the policy.

**The scm-sdk 0.2.4 fields** (§15.25). The CLI builds and reads JSON documents and types
them with the SDK models only at its edges, so every field keeps the three states the SDK
keeps (`Optional::Unset`, an explicit value, and an unexpected value in the extensions):
- an omitted setting stays omitted: no flag default is written (a boolean pair writes only
  when one of its forms is given), and the merge never inserts a key the read lacked;
  an explicit `false` is written and kept (`Optional::Value(false)`);
- `dlp_tenant_id` is a string. A `--config` body sends it as written; a flag update sends
  TS 7.3.0's `{profile_name, active, policy}` and so no `dlp_tenant_id`; a restore never
  sends the source's (a tenant-bound identifier, TS's body); a backup keeps the record's.
  So every CLI write that changes a profile leaves it out unless a `--config` file holds it:
  a flag `profiles update`, `topics apply|revert`, a restore (create and overwrite) and a
  `profiles update --config` whose file omits the key; TS 7.3.0 does the same, and no read
  returns the field, so the CLI cannot carry it over. Observed live (B7): no `get` or `list`
  answer carries `dlp_tenant_id`; a create or PUT answer carries the value sent, and
  `"none"` when the body omits it. The answer reports `none`; the effect on the stored
  binding is unknown (the evidence cannot tell a cleared binding from an answer that only
  reflects the request; `docs/research/live-directional-profiles.md` records the open
  question and the test that would decide it). This applies to legacy profiles too. The
  CLI prints each answer as sent;
- `content-type-mode` is free text (`per_content_type` is the one observed value); the four
  known directions are independently optional in the schema (the live service requires all
  four keys, D335) and an unknown direction key is kept with its value by every read,
  merge, backup and restore; no read, merge, backup or restore synthesizes a direction (a
  flag create writes the three it does not fill as empty objects, D335);
- an answer holding an unexpected value of a new field is printed and backed up as sent,
  and a write that would send it back fails the request schema (D334).

**Exit codes.** 2 for every check above (before the tenant, or after the read for the
layout refusals and a merged body), 1 for the rest as in §13.3.

## 14. M5 bulk scanning (0.5)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-bulk-scan.md` (cited as
**B§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-async-scan.md` (cited as **A§n**). This section
overrides them where they differ; their provisional D-numbers are not the numbers below.
Every difference from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row (D118–D131, and D30 extended).

**SDK.** scm-sdk 0.1.0 has every operation these commands need (A§0, A§1): nothing here
is blocked on scm-sdk. `Scanner::async_scan` sends one POST and is never replayed for any
status, transport error or `with_retries` value; a local refusal is `NotSent` (verified
for a 101-character session id, 0 requests; a unit test pins it), a 3xx/4xx answer
`Rejected`, everything after dispatch `Unknown` (A§2.1, A§3). Two SDK behaviours are
handled conservatively here and would be optional SDK improvements, not blockers:
- **G1.** A refused connection is `Unknown` (the SDK sets `sent` before the transport
  call), so it makes the chunk ambiguous, as in TypeScript. A wrong `airsApiEndpoint`
  therefore stops the first chunk for good; the user starts a new job. An SDK change
  reporting connect-phase failures as `NotSent` would let those prompts stay pending.
- **G2.** A 4xx whose error body exceeds 64 KiB is `Limit`/`Unknown` and loses its
  `Retry-After`. The CLI classifies by `status()` (the §6 rule "`Limit` with an HTTP error
  status: treat as `Http`"): a 4xx status is a rejection, and a 429 without `Retry-After`
  uses the computed backoff.

### 14.1 Commands and options

Help texts are TypeScript's (B§1); the `Examples:` use the program name `airs`.
`runtime --help` lists the two commands in TypeScript's sorted order.

| Command | Help | Arguments and options |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime bulk-scan` | `Scan multiple prompts via the async AIRS API` | `--profile <name>` (required, `Security profile name`), `--file <file>` (`Input file — .csv (extracts prompt column) or .txt (one per line)`; required by §14.2, not by clap, so the TypeScript message is kept), `--output-file <file>` (`Output CSV file path`), `--session-id <id>` (`Session ID for grouping scans in AIRS dashboard`), `--batch-size <n>` (`Prompts per sequential submit/poll batch`, default `25`), hidden `--input <file>` |
| `runtime resume-poll <stateFile>` | `Resume polling for a previously submitted bulk scan` | `--output-file <file>` (`Output CSV file path`) |

- **The hidden `--input <file>`** (TS deprecated alias): when given, the warning
  `  ⚠ --input is deprecated and will be removed in v4 — use --file` (yellow by the stderr
  decision, never quiet-suppressed) is printed on stderr during planning, before any other
  validation. `--file` wins when both are given (TS).
- **`--output`** is the global format flag on both commands (§14.14). TypeScript's
  `--output <file>` alias for `--output-file` is unreachable there (its root parser
  consumes every `--output`), so it has no counterpart (D130).

From 8.1, `bulk-scan --scanner NAME` selects a named scanner (§3.15, D342),
validated before tenant access. Its saved version-2 reference controls resume;
`resume-poll` offers no selector override. Legacy flat jobs remain version 1.

### 14.2 Validation order and argument checks

`bulk-scan` (D120, D128; TS B§2):
1. clap (exit 2, D1).
2. The `--input` warning.
3. `--output` (§2.4) and `--tenant`'s name format.
4. `--file` (or `--input`) missing or empty (TS `if (!opts.file)`): `--file <file> is required`
   (TS text; exit 2).
5. `--batch-size`: it must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and be at most 2^53 − 1, else
   `--batch-size must be a positive integer` (TS text; exit 2; `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, `abc`,
   `007`, `9007199254740992` and `""` are refused).
6. `--profile`: `""` →
   `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for POST /v1/scan/async/request did not match schema: scan_req.ai_profile: custom`;
   longer than 100 UTF-16 code units →
   `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for POST /v1/scan/async/request did not match schema: scan_req.ai_profile.profile_name: too_big`
   (exit 2; the TS SDK text for the first object without its `0.` prefix and repeats).
7. `--session-id`: longer than 100 UTF-16 code units →
   `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for POST /v1/scan/async/request did not match schema: scan_req.session_id: too_big`
   (exit 2). `--session-id ""` is accepted and means "no session" (TS parity, §14.4).
8. `--output-file ""`: `--output-file needs a path` (exit 2; TS fails with `EISDIR` after
   the state exists, D120).
9. The input file (§14.3), read and parsed during planning: its errors exit 1, and
   `No prompts found in input file` exits 2, all before the tenant is read and before the
   debug log is opened, so no failing run of this list creates a log (§2.9).
10. The debug log (§2.9).
11. The tenant (§3.4, §3.7), the scanner credentials (§3.5), the scanner client (§5).
12. Job setup (§14.4).

Every usage error therefore comes before the tenant, makes no request and creates no file.
TypeScript reads the tenant first and the input file after it (D2, D128).

`resume-poll` (§14.13): clap → `--output` and `--tenant` → `--output-file ""`
(`--output-file needs a path`, exit 2) → the debug log → the state path, its location and
the job lock (§14.13 steps 1–3) → the tenant, the scanner credentials and the client → the
state checks of §14.13 steps 4–9. This is TypeScript's order (it resolves the state path
and takes its lock before it loads the config), so a missing state fails on the path and a
held job is refused naming its holder whatever the tenant's state.

### 14.3 Input file

The `--file` path is used as given (relative to the working directory) and followed
through symlinks. It must be a regular file of at most 16,777,216 bytes, read whole, and
valid UTF-8 (D128). Messages (exit 1; `<path>` as typed, through `terminal_safe`; no OS
error and no content is echoed):
- `Cannot read <path> (missing, not a regular file, unreadable or larger than 16 MiB)`
- `<path> is not valid UTF-8` (TS decodes invalid bytes as U+FFFD)

**Parser choice** (TS `parse-input.ts`): a path ending in `.csv` in any ASCII case is CSV;
everything else (`.txt`, no extension) is line mode.

**Line mode.** Split on `\n`; JavaScript-`trim` each line (`js_trim`: whitespace and line
terminators, U+FEFF included, so CRLF files and a BOM work); drop empty lines. Duplicates
are kept and scanned separately; control characters other than whitespace are kept and
sent (they reach only the server and the CSV, never the terminal).

**CSV mode** (TS's minimal RFC 4180 reader, kept with its quirks):
- A record ends at `\n`, `\r\n` or a bare `\r` outside quotes.
- A field that starts with `"` runs to the next unpaired `"`; `""` inside it is a quote;
  commas, CR and LF inside quotes are kept. **An opening quote with no closing quote**
  is the error `<path> has an unterminated quoted field` (exit 1; TS swallows the rest of
  the file into one field, D128).
- After a closing quote, one comma is consumed when it follows; any other text starts a
  new field (`"ab"cd,1` is `ab`, `cd`, `1`). An unquoted field runs to the next comma or
  line break (` "a,b",1` is ` "a`, `b"`, `1`). A comma just before a line break adds no
  empty field.
- Records with no field or one empty field are dropped, so blank lines anywhere (before
  the header too) are skipped.
- The first remaining record is the header. The prompt column is the first header field
  whose `js_trim`med, ASCII-lower-cased text is `prompt`. None:
  `No "prompt" column found in CSV header` (TS text; exit 1).
- Each later record contributes its prompt-column field, `js_trim`med; a missing field or
  an empty value contributes nothing. Other columns are ignored.

**Prompt checks** (after parsing; D120, D128):
- No prompts (an empty file, a header only, only blank lines):
  `No prompts found in input file` (TS text; exit 2).
- More than 10,000 prompts: `<path> has more than 10000 prompts; split it into several jobs`
  (exit 1). The bound keeps every state file and checkpoint bounded (§14.9).
- A prompt over 2,097,152 UTF-8 bytes (the SDK content limit, A§5 G5):
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:prompt exceeds max length of 2097152 bytes` with the
  detail line `Prompt index <i>` (the 0-based input index, which is also its `req_id`),
  exit 1. The first such prompt is reported.
- A prompt whose scan object (with the profile and the session the job will use; the
  default session has a fixed length) does not fit a request body on its own, `[` +
  object + `]` larger than the §14.5 body budget (D132):
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:prompt exceeds the request size limit of 8323072 bytes once JSON-encoded`
  with the detail line `Prompt index <i>`, exit 1, the first such prompt reported. The
  2 MiB check counts raw bytes, but each C0 control other than `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, `\b` and
  `\f` is written as `\u00XX`, so a 2 MiB prompt can encode to about 12 MiB (a UTF-16LE
  file, valid UTF-8 with a NUL between characters, is the ordinary way to get one).

The B§3 table of 21 cases is the acceptance corpus: every row gives the same prompts as
TypeScript, except `unterminated.csv` (refused) and `latin1.txt` (`is not valid UTF-8`).

### 14.4 Job setup (`bulk-scan`)

After §14.2 steps 1–11, in this order (D121, D123):
1. **Session id.** `--session-id` as given, else `prisma-airs-cli-bulk-<base36>` where
   `<base36>` is the current Unix time in milliseconds in lowercase base 36 (the TS prefix
   and form, kept because it appears in the AIRS dashboard). `""` is kept: the banner shows
   `Session:  ` and every scan object omits `session_id` (TS parity).
2. **Output path** (§14.12): `--output-file`, else the default name in the working
   directory; made absolute against the working directory and lexically normalised (no
   symlink resolution). A path that exists (any type; a symlink is not followed) is refused:
   `<path> already exists; choose another --output-file` (exit 1; the D114 text). Nothing has
   been created yet.
3. **State directory** `S` (§14.9): resolved, created if missing, opened and checked.
4. **Job id** and **job lock** (§14.11): a fresh `<job>`; `<S>/<job>.lock` is created with
   `O_EXCL` and locked.
5. **Output claim** (§14.12): the header-only CSV is created exclusively at the path.
6. **First checkpoint** (§14.10): every item `pending`, the output's identity recorded.
   From here the job exists.
7. The status lines (§14.14), then the batches (§14.5).

A failure in steps 3–6 (or a signal acted on there) removes what this run created, in
reverse order, each only when it is still the file this run made (device and inode): the
state temporary file (and the state itself when the first checkpoint renamed it but its
directory fsync failed), the claimed output, and the lock file (unlinked while held; no other
process can know the fresh job id). The state directory `S` is kept. Then the error, exit 1 (130/143 with
`Interrupted; no prompt was submitted`). TypeScript writes the all-pending state and the
lock before the output and the client (D123).

### 14.5 Batching and chunking

- **Logical batches** of `batchSize` items in input order (`Batches: ceil(n / batchSize)`).
  Batches run one after another: every chunk of a batch is submitted, then every receipt of
  the batch is polled to completion, then the next batch starts (TS B§5).
- **Chunks.** A batch's items to submit (all of them in `bulk-scan`; its `pending` items in
  ascending index order in `resume-poll`) are cut into consecutive chunks of at most 20
  (`MAX_NUMBER_OF_BATCH_SCAN_OBJECTS`). A chunk is also closed early when adding the next
  prompt would make its serialised body (`serde_json::to_vec` of the `AsyncScanObject`
  array the CLI builds) larger than the SDK request limit minus 64 KiB of headroom
  (`Limits::default().max_request_bytes` = 8 MiB; a unit test pins that the SDK accepts
  every chunk the planner builds). A chunk always holds at least one prompt; a prompt
  whose object cannot fit a body on its own is refused at planning (§14.3, D132), and the
  planner refuses it too (the same message) rather than build a chunk the SDK would refuse
  on every attempt. The split only applies where TypeScript would send a body Rust cannot
  (D120).
- **Polls** go receipt by receipt: the batch's `submitted` items grouped by `scanId` in the
  order of each scan id's lowest index, one scan id per request (TS `submittedBatches`).
- Verified TS sequences that Rust reproduces: 45 prompts, size 25 →
  `P[0..19] P[20..24] G G P[25..44] G`; 3 prompts, size 2 → `P[0,1] G P[2] G`; 7 prompts,
  size 5 → `P[0..4] G P[5,6] G`.

### 14.6 Submission

**Request.** `POST <airsApiEndpoint>/v1/scan/async/request` through `Scanner::async_scan`,
one per chunk, with a fresh `RequestOptions::with_timeout(60 s)` built immediately before
the call. The body parses to
`[{"req_id": <index>, "scan_req": {"ai_profile": {"profile_name": <profile>}, "contents": [{"prompt": <prompt>}], "session_id": <session>}}, …]`
(`session_id` omitted when the session is `""`); `req_id` is the item's global input index,
stable across chunks, batches and resumes. Headers and the payload hash are the §8.2 ones.
Keys are sorted (D35): equality with TypeScript is JSON equality, and the HMAC is checked
over the received bytes.

**Outcome classification** (A§4.3; every row is checkpointed before the next step, §14.8):

| SDK result | Items | Attempt outcome | Then |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ok(receipt)`, `scan_id` of the §7.1 id shape that carries no configured secret | `submitted` with `scanId` and `receiptReportId` (when present) | `accepted` | next chunk; after the batch's last chunk the status line `Scan IDs saved: <state>`, then polling |
| `Ok(receipt)`, any other `scan_id` | `ambiguous` | `unusableReceipt` | stop: `AIRS accepted prompts <ranges>, but its receipt has no usable scan id; they will not be resubmitted`, then the detail line `Prompts <ranges> will not be resubmitted; the job was saved in <state>` (exit 1, D126) |
| `Err`, status 429, retries left | `pending` | `rejected` (429) | the status line, a cancellable wait, a new attempt of the same chunk |
| `Err`, `Rejected` (3xx, 4xx), or `Limit` with a 4xx status (G2) | `pending` | `rejected` (status) | stop: the §6 error, then the detail line `The job was saved; resume it with 'airs runtime resume-poll <state>'`, exit 1 |
| `Err`, `NotSent` | `pending` | `notSent` | stop: the §6 error and the same detail line, exit 1 (130/143 for a signal, §14.16) |
| `Err`, `Unknown` (5xx, transport, deadline or cancel after dispatch, a 2xx whose receipt does not decode) | `ambiguous` | `unknown` | stop: the §6 error, the §6 line `Outcome unknown: the scan may have been received and processed by AIRS.`, then `Prompts <ranges> will not be resubmitted; the job was saved in <state>`, exit 1 (130/143 for a signal) |

After a stop, no later chunk or batch is attempted and accepted earlier chunks of the
batch are not polled (TS parity; `resume-poll` polls them). The detail lines come after the
`HTTP`/`Re-run` lines (§2.2) and are Rust-only (D131). `<ranges>` lists the chunk's
indices ascending as comma-separated `a-b` ranges or single numbers (`0-19`, `18, 20-24`).

**429 retries** (TS `submitBatch`): only an `Http` error with status 429 is retried, at most
5 times (6 attempts per chunk). The delay is the error's `retry_after()` capped at 60 s
when present (D124), else `10 s × 2^(n−1)` for retry `n` (10, 20, 40, 80, 160 s). Before
each wait the status line `  ⚠ Rate limited while submitting — retry <n> in <s>s...` (TS
text; `<s>` the delay in seconds rounded half up). After the fifth retry the 429 is the
stop of the `Rejected` row. The wait ends at once on a signal (§14.16).

**Redirects.** A 3xx is `Destination`/`Rejected` and never followed (D30): the prompts stay
pending.

### 14.7 Polling

**Request.** `GET <airsApiEndpoint>/v1/scan/results?scan_ids=<one scan id>` through
`Scanner::query_by_scan_ids`, with `RequestOptions::with_timeout(60 s)?.with_retries(0)?`
built before each call (TS sends exactly one attempt; without the override the SDK would
replay 502/503/504). The report fallback uses `query_by_report_ids` with the same options.

**Loop** per receipt (TS `pollBatch`, B§6.2), until every entry of the receipt is resolved:
1. Query. An error with status 429 while the retry level is below 5 raises the level by 1,
   prints `  ⚠ Rate limited — retry <n> in <s>s...` (`<n>` the new level), waits
   (`retry_after()` capped at 60 s, else `10 s × 2^(level−1)`; cancellable) and queries
   again; this poll is not counted. Only status 429 counts (D125). Any other error stops
   the command (below).
2. Each row, in server order, with `scan_id` defaulting to the receipt's and `status`
   ASCII-lower-cased; `req_id` correlates only when it is a finite number with an
   integral value in `0..=2^53` (so `2.0` is request 2; `-1`, `1.5` and other values match
   nothing; A§5 G7):
   - a row without `req_id`, terminal (`failed`, `complete`, `completed`) and of this scan:
     `failed` resolves every unresolved entry as a failed row (`AIRS async scan failed`);
     `complete`/`completed` records the report id for the fallback: `result.report_id` when
     the row has a `result` (TS `??`: an empty one is not replaced), else the row's
     `report_id`, else the receipt's; none or empty (the last such row wins):
     `AIRS result correlation failed for scan <id>: terminal row has no request or report ID`;
   - a row whose `(scan_id, req_id)` is not an unresolved entry of this receipt is ignored
     (another scan, an unknown id, a duplicate);
   - `failed` → a failed row;
   - `complete`/`completed` with a `result` → the §8.3 normalisation of that result with
     prompt detections only (`triggered` is any prompt detection; response detections are
     ignored, because only prompts were sent). A nested `result.scan_id` that differs from
     the row's: `AIRS result correlation mismatch: nested scan ID <a> does not match <b>`;
   - any other status, or a complete row without `result`, is no progress.
3. **Report fallback**, when step 2 recorded report ids: one query of the distinct ids.
   A 429 follows step 1's rule and then restarts the loop at step 1. Each report's
   `scan_id` (default the receipt's) must be this scan's and its `report_id`, when
   present, the recorded one, else
   `AIRS report correlation mismatch for scan <id>, request <reqId>`. A report whose
   `req_id` (step 2's rule) is an unresolved entry becomes a row: `detection_results[]`
   entries map `detection_service` (ASCII-lower-cased) through TS `REPORT_DETECTION_KEYS`
   (unknown names kept as keys); a detector fires on action `block` or verdict `malicious`,
   `unsafe`, `violation` or `detected`; any `block` → `block`, else any other non-empty
   action than `allow` → `failed` (`Unknown AIRS action in threat report: <a>`), else
   `allow`; category `error` for failed, `malicious` when triggered, else `benign`.
4. Newly resolved rows are checkpointed together (one checkpoint per poll response that
   resolved anything, then one CSV rewrite, §14.10; the results response of step 2 and the
   reports response of step 3 are two responses, so step 2's rows are durable before the
   report query). TypeScript saves after every row;
   either way nothing resolved is lost before the next request. A correlation error stops
   the response at its row: the rows resolved before it in that response are checkpointed
   (with the CSV rewrite) first, then the error stops the command, and a report id
   recorded before it is not queried (TS parity: it saves each row before it throws).
5. After a successful poll the retry level drops by 1 (when above 0). A successful poll
   that resolved nothing raises the no-progress count, progress resets it; at 120:
   `AIRS polling made no progress after 120 polls for scan <id>` (TS text).
6. If entries remain, wait 5 s (cancellable), then go to step 1. The first poll follows
   the batch's last submission at once.

**Bounds.** Each request has its 60 s deadline; per receipt (at most 20 entries) there
are at most about 21 × 120 successful polls and five rate-limit waits per level, so a
receipt is abandoned after a bounded time (about 3.5 h at the worst). No further ceiling is
added (TS parity).

**Failed rows** (fail closed, D6): `timeout: true` (`AIRS scan timed out`), `error: true`
(the joined `errors[]` parts, else `AIRS scan failed`), an unknown or missing action
(`Unknown AIRS action: <action|missing>`), a failed row status (`AIRS async scan failed`,
report id `""`) and an unknown report action are `failed` rows with category `error`. They
are never counted as allowed; their items are `failed` and terminal (never re-polled).

**Server text** in a row (category, scan and report ids, reason parts, unknown detection
keys) gets the §8.3 withholding before it is stored or written: a value carrying a
configured secret is `[withheld]`, a detection key carrying one (also compared ignoring
case, because keys are lower-cased) is dropped, reason parts
are cut to 200 characters plus `...` (D131). Correlation messages print server ids through
`terminal_safe` and the same withholding.

**Errors that end polling** (any non-429 error, five exhausted rate-limit levels, a
correlation error, the no-progress bound): the §6 message (or the text above), then the
detail line `The job was saved; resume it with 'airs runtime resume-poll <state>'`
(exit 1). Items stay `submitted`; rows resolved before the error, a correlation error's
own response included, are checkpointed before it is printed.

### 14.8 Item states and the exactly-once rules

Item states (the TS set): `pending`, `submitting`, `submitted`, `complete`, `failed`,
`ambiguous`. The rules (A§7.3):
1. **Before** a chunk's POST, its items are `submitting` and a new attempt with outcome
   `inFlight` is durable (checkpoint C1).
2. **After** the POST, the outcome of §14.6 is durable (checkpoint C3) before anything
   else: before the next chunk, before the first poll, before a 429 wait, before the
   command stops.
3. A `pending` item may be submitted (its last attempt was refused or never sent). A
   `submitting` or `ambiguous` item is **never** submitted again by the CLI: not by
   `bulk-scan`, not by `resume-poll`. `resume-poll` turns a durable `submitting` (the
   process died between C1 and C3) into `ambiguous` first.
4. `submitted` items are polled (idempotent reads); `complete` and `failed` are terminal.
5. The output is never written ahead of the state (§14.12).

| Durable state when the process dies | `resume-poll` does |
|---|---|
| `pending` (never sent, refused, rate limited, not sent) | submits it |
| `submitting` (between C1 and C3) | treats it as ambiguous; never resubmits |
| `ambiguous` (outcome unknown, unusable receipt) | polls the known receipts, then refuses (§14.13) |
| `submitted` | polls it |
| `complete`, `failed` | nothing |

There is no API to reconcile an ambiguous submission (no lookup by session or request id
in either SDK), so ambiguity is final for the CLI: the user reviews the scans of the
session in the AIRS dashboard. The attempt journal (§14.9) gives the session id and the
time window.

### 14.9 State directory and state file

**Directory** `S` (D118): `$XDG_STATE_HOME/airs-cli/bulk-scans/` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is
set and non-empty (it must be absolute, else `XDG_STATE_HOME must be an absolute path`,
exit 1), otherwise `<home>/.local/state/airs-cli/bulk-scans/` with `<home>` resolved as in
§2.9 (it must be absolute, else
`Cannot store the bulk-scan state: HOME is not an absolute path; set XDG_STATE_HOME`,
exit 1). It is created with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)` (an existing
directory is never chmod'ed). A symlink or non-directory at `S` itself is refused (the §3.8
message) before it is resolved; its parents are resolved: `S` is canonicalised (`realpath`), then opened with
`O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC` and checked on the descriptor (`fstat`) with the
§3.8 directory rule (a directory owned by the effective uid with `mode & 0o022 == 0`), with
the §3.8 messages (`Cannot create <S>; check the permissions of its parent directory`,
`Refusing to use <S>: it must be a directory (not a symlink) owned by the current user and not writable by group or others`).
Every state, temporary and lock file is then opened, renamed and unlinked relative to that
descriptor (`openat`, `renameat`, `unlinkat`), so a directory swapped for a symlink is never
followed. The tenant key `dataDir` does not exist (D71).

**Names.** `<job>` is `<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<16 lowercase hex>` (the hex from 8 random
bytes, the §3.9 temporary-name source), matching `^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z-[0-9a-f]{16}$`. Files
in `S`: `<job>.bulk-scan.json` (the state), `<job>.lock` (§14.11) and temporaries
`.<job>.bulk-scan.json.<pid>.<16 hex>.tmp`. Every state and lock file passes the §3.8 file
rule (`O_NOFOLLOW` open, same device and inode as the `statat`, regular, owned by the
effective uid, `mode & 0o077 == 0`) with the §3.8 refusal text.

**Schema versions.** Flat-credential jobs keep version1 and the exact bytes below.
Named jobs use version2 and add scannerReference after scanEndpoint:
{name, revision, applicationId, endpoint}, all non-secret; no credential material.
Version1 forbids this field and version2 requires a valid matching reference.
The reference endpoint is the admitted/canonical scanner endpoint. Unsupported
versions above2 remain newer-state refusals. Older binaries refuse version2.
Named config resumes load the reference under the job lock before selecting a
credential; legacy scalar-only config preserves its existing validation order.
Same-app rotation checkpoints a changed reference before polling. All other
exactly-once, input/output identity and endpoint/tenant checks remain unchanged.

**Schema** (JSON, written in the §2.2 two-space layout plus `"\n"`, keys in this order,
read with unknown keys refused):

```json
{
  "format": "airs-cli-rs.bulk-scan",
  "version": 1,
  "jobId": "20261017T120000Z-3f9c0a1b2c3d4e5f",
  "tenant": "redtail-prod",
  "scanEndpoint": "https://service.api.aisecurity.paloaltonetworks.com",
  "profile": "Prisma AIRS Harness",
  "sessionId": "prisma-airs-cli-bulk-mgx1a2b3",
  "batchSize": 25,
  "output": {"path": "/abs/out.csv", "dev": "16777230", "ino": "1234567", "next": null},
  "createdAt": "2026-10-17T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-17T12:00:09.412Z",
  "sequence": 7,
  "attempts": [
    {"id": 1, "indices": [0, 1], "startedAt": "…", "endedAt": "…", "outcome": "accepted", "httpStatus": 200, "scanId": "…"},
    {"id": 2, "indices": [2, 3], "startedAt": "…", "endedAt": null, "outcome": "inFlight"}
  ],
  "items": [
    {"index": 0, "reqId": 0, "prompt": "…", "status": "complete", "attempt": 1, "scanId": "…", "receiptReportId": "R…",
     "result": {"action": "allow", "category": "benign", "triggered": false, "detections": {"injection": false}, "scanId": "…", "reportId": "R…"}},
    {"index": 2, "reqId": 2, "prompt": "…", "status": "submitting", "attempt": 2}
  ]
}
```

- `tenant` is the store name of the tenant that started the job; `scanEndpoint` its
  effective `airsApiEndpoint` as admitted by §5 (never a credential). `sessionId` is always
  present (`""` allowed).
- `output`: the absolute path, the device and inode (decimal strings) of the file this job
  last put there, and `next` (`null`, or `{"dev", "ino", "temp"}` for a rewrite in
  progress, §14.12).
- `sequence` counts checkpoints. Timestamps are UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`.
- **Attempts** (the journal; new in Rust): one per POST attempt, ids from 1, `indices` the
  chunk's input indices, `outcome` ∈ `inFlight`, `accepted`, `unusableReceipt`,
  `rejected`, `notSent`, `unknown`; `httpStatus` when there was one (for `accepted`, the
  status of the receipt's response); `error` (the §6 message, which never contains server
  text; for a submission a signal cancelled, the §2.5 `Interrupted; …` text) for every
  outcome but `accepted` and `inFlight`; `scanId` for `accepted`. `endedAt` is `null` only while `inFlight`.
- **Items**: `index`, `reqId` (equal), `prompt` (the full text; prompts are kept with the
  job, as in TypeScript), `status`, `attempt` (the last attempt that carried it, absent
  while never sent), `scanId` and `receiptReportId` (from the accepted receipt), `result`
  (`action` ∈ `allow|block|failed`, `category`, `triggered`, `detections` (key → boolean,
  only the keys the row reported), `scanId`, `reportId`, `error` for failed rows), with the
  §14.7 withholding already applied, so the state and the CSV hold the same values.

**Invariants** (checked on load and before every write; a write that would break one is a
bug and fails the checkpoint): `format` and `version` exact; `jobId` matches the file name;
`profile` 1–100 UTF-16 units; `sessionId` at most 100; `batchSize` in `1..=2^53−1`; 1 to
10,000 items with `index` equal to the position and `reqId` equal to `index`;
`submitted|complete|failed` have a `scanId` of the §7.1 id shape and
`pending|submitting|ambiguous` none; `complete|failed` have a `result` and the others none;
`result.scanId` equals the item's `scanId`; `failed` ⇔ `result.action == "failed"`;
`submitting` ⇔ its `attempt` is `inFlight`, and at most one attempt is `inFlight`; every
attempt index names an item; the items of one `scanId` (at most 20) share
`receiptReportId`; the timestamps parse. The serialised state is at most 128 MiB; a
checkpoint that would exceed it fails (`Cannot save <state>; the job state would exceed 128 MiB`).

**Loading** (`resume-poll`, under the lock): a bounded read (at most 128 MiB) of the §3.8
file, then:
- not JSON, or JSON the parser refuses (the D44 classes):
  `Invalid bulk-scan state <path>: malformed JSON`;
- a JSON object without `format` that has a `version` or a `scanIds` key (TypeScript v2 or
  the TypeScript legacy shape):
  `<path> is a TypeScript airs-cli bulk-scan state; airs cannot resume it. Resume it with the TypeScript airs-cli, or start a new job with 'airs runtime bulk-scan'.`
  (exit 1; there is no TypeScript checkpoint import, D118);
- `format` correct and `version` greater than 1:
  `<path> was written by a newer version of airs; upgrade airs to resume it`;
- anything else: `Invalid bulk-scan state <path>: <reason>`, `<reason>` a fixed text per
  invariant (the TypeScript texts where they exist: `reqId must match the stable input index`,
  `submitted, complete and failed entries require a scanId`,
  `stored result scanId does not match its receipt`, `duplicate input index <n>`,
  `prompt entries must remain in input order`, …; never file content).

**Retention.** State files are never deleted (TS parity; a completed job can be resumed
again with no request, §14.13), so prompts stay in `S` until the user removes the job's
files. Each job also leaves its empty `.lock` file.

### 14.10 Checkpoints

`checkpoint(state)`, the only way the state is written:
1. Check the invariants; `sequence += 1`; `updatedAt = now`; serialise.
2. Create the temporary in `S` (`openat` with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`,
   mode 0600, then `fchmod` 0600), `write_all`, `fsync`, close.
3. When `<job>.bulk-scan.json` exists it must pass the §3.8 file rule and have the device
   and inode this process last renamed into place (or loaded); otherwise:
   `<state> was changed by another program; the job was stopped` (exit 1, the temporary
   removed, nothing sent).
4. `renameat(temp, state)`, then `fsync` of `S`. A failed directory fsync is a checkpoint
   failure here (unlike §3.9), because the checkpoint is the exactly-once guarantee.
5. A failure in 2–4 removes the temporary (best effort) and fails with
   `Cannot save <state>; <consequence>` (exit 1; the OS error is never echoed), where
   `<consequence>` is:
   - before a submission (C1) or at setup: `no further prompts were submitted`;
   - after an accepted receipt (C3):
     `prompts <ranges> were accepted under scan <scan id>, but the job state could not be saved`
     (the durable state still says `submitting`, so a resume treats them as ambiguous);
   - after other C3 outcomes: `no further prompts were submitted`;
   - after results: `results since the last save will be polled again by resume-poll`.

Stale temporaries of the job (`^\.<job>\.bulk-scan\.json\.[0-9]{1,10}\.[0-9a-f]{16}\.tmp$`,
regular, owned by the effective uid) are removed by `resume-poll` under the job lock
(only the lock holder writes them). A signal during a checkpoint lets it finish (§2.5).

Checkpoints are taken: at setup (all `pending`); C1 and C3 of every attempt; after every
poll response that resolved rows; in `resume-poll` after `submitting` became `ambiguous`
and after the output was re-pointed or re-claimed; at the end of every run that reaches
the summary or the ambiguous refusal. Each one that records results, and the last one,
carries a CSV rewrite: the new CSV is written to its temporary before the checkpoint and
renamed into place after it (§14.12), so the CSV is never ahead of the state.

### 14.11 Job lock

- **File** `<S>/<job>.lock`, opened relative to `S` with
  `O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, mode 0600 (`fchmod` on creation), checked with
  the §3.8 file rule; `bulk-scan` adds `O_EXCL` (its job id is fresh).
- **Acquire**: `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`. There is no wait (TS refuses at once too).
  After the `flock`, the descriptor (`fstat`) must still be the file at `<job>.lock`
  (`statat` relative to `S`): a file removed or replaced between the open and the lock is
  opened again (at most 3 times, then `Cannot lock <lock>; …`), so the lock taken is always
  the one on the file another process would open.
  `EWOULDBLOCK`:
  `Bulk-scan job is already active in process <pid> on <host> since <since>. Wait for it to finish before resuming <state>.`
  (the TS text with the §3.9 holder record; `in another process` when the record is
  missing or malformed), exit 1, nothing sent and nothing written. Any other `flock` error,
  or a failure to open or create the file other than a §3.8 refusal:
  `Cannot lock <lock>; the file system may not support file locks` (exit 1).
- **Holder record**: once held, `ftruncate(0)` and the §3.9 record
  (`pid=…\nhost=…\nsince=…\n`, not fsynced), shared with `store::lock`.
- **Held** by `bulk-scan` from step 4 of §14.4 until after its last CSV write, and by
  `resume-poll` from before the state is read until after its last CSV write. Released with
  `ftruncate(0)` and close.
- **Held, checked.** Before every submission's C1 the holder checks that its lock is
  still the file at `<job>.lock`. A lock file removed or replaced while it is held (for
  example by a clean-up of `S`) no longer keeps a `resume-poll` out, so the holder stops
  before it sends anything more:
  `<lock> was removed or replaced by another program; the job was stopped` with the detail
  line `The job was saved; resume it with 'airs runtime resume-poll <state>'`
  (exit 1). A resume then takes a new lock file. The window left (a removal between the
  holder's check and its C1 rename, while a resume starts) is narrowed further by the C1
  identity check of §14.10.
- **Crashes** release it in the kernel: no stale lock, no liveness guess, no manual
  removal (D119). The file is never deleted (unlinking a `flock` file races with a process
  that already opened it), except by a `bulk-scan` whose setup failed (§14.4).
- The lock covers one job: different jobs run concurrently (TS parity), and two jobs cannot
  share an output because the claim is exclusive. The tenant-store lock (`D/config.lock`)
  is unrelated and never taken.

### 14.12 Output CSV and the overwrite rules

**Content** (TS `formatResultsCsv`, byte for byte): the header
`prompt,action,category,triggered,topic_violation,injection,toxic_content,dlp,url_cats,malicious_code,source_code,agent,scan_id,report_id,error`
(unquoted), then one row per item with a result (`complete` or `failed`) in input-index
order; every field is double-quoted with `"` doubled and nothing else escaped (commas, CR,
LF, control characters and leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` are kept: the CSV is a data file);
`triggered` and the eight detector columns are `true`/`false` (an absent detector is
`false`); `error` is empty when absent; lines are joined with `\n` and there is **no**
trailing newline (a header-only file is exactly the header). Values carry the §14.7
withholding (D131).

**Default name** (D122): `<profile>-bulk-scan.csv` in the working directory, where every run
of JavaScript whitespace (the `js_trim` set), every `/` and every C0, DEL and C1 control in
the profile name becomes one `-` (TS replaces whitespace runs only). The result is always a
single file name in the working directory; a name the file system refuses (longer than its
limit) is the claim failure below.

**Claim** (`bulk-scan` §14.4 step 5, and `resume-poll` when the job's file is absent or
re-pointed): the path is created with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`,
mode 0600 (`fchmod`; TS also leaves the file 0600), the projection written, `fsync`, then
the parent directory `fsync`ed (a failed directory fsync is the step 4 warning below, not a
failure). Its parent must exist; no directory is created (D121). Before the path is created,
a rewrite temporary of the longest form (`.<file name>.<10-digit pid>.<16 hex>.tmp`, about
28 bytes longer than the name) is created exclusively in the directory and removed: a name
the file system accepts but whose temporaries it would refuse (`NAME_MAX`) is the claim
failure below, before any job exists or any prompt is sent.
Failures: an existing path or symlink: `<path> already exists; choose another --output-file`;
anything else: `Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable` (exit
1, a partly written file removed).

**Rewrite** (the job's own file, around a checkpoint; D121):
1. Create `.<file name>.<pid>.<16 hex>.tmp` in the output's directory (`O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`,
   0600), write the projection of the state about to be checkpointed, `fsync`, `fstat` it.
2. Take the checkpoint, with `output.next = {dev, ino, temp}` recorded in it.
3. `lstat` the path: it must be absent (the user removed it; the rename recreates it), or a
   regular file owned by the effective uid whose device and inode equal `output`'s (or
   `next`'s). Otherwise the temporary is removed and the job stops with
   `<path> is not the file this job wrote (it was replaced, moved or edited); the results are saved in <state>: resume with --output-file <new path>`
   (exit 1).
4. `rename(temp, path)`, then `fsync` the directory; a failed directory fsync is the §3.9
   warning (`  ⚠ <path> was saved, but its directory could not be synced; the change may not survive a system crash`,
   once per run), not a failure: the CSV can always be rebuilt from the state.
5. `output` becomes `next` and `next` becomes `null` (persisted by the next checkpoint).
   `resume-poll` accepts either identity, removes a leftover `next.temp` (when it is a
   regular file of ours with that inode) and promotes `next` when the path has it.
A failed rewrite (1, 3, 4) stops the job with
`Cannot write <path>; the results are saved in <state>: run 'airs runtime resume-poll <state>' to write it again`
(exit 1), except for the identity refusal of step 3. When step 1 fails, the checkpoint of
step 2 is still taken (with `output.next` `null`) before the failure is reported, so the
results are durable whatever happens to the CSV's directory; a failed checkpoint is then
§14.10's error instead. The check in step 3 and the rename are
two calls: a file created at the path in between is replaced (the remaining window,
documented like §13.4's).

**`resume-poll` and `--output-file`** (D121):
- without it: the recorded path, rewritten under the rules above (absent → claimed again;
  present, its directory must accept a rewrite temporary as at the claim, else
  `Cannot write <path>; the results are saved in <state>: resume with --output-file <new path>`,
  exit 1, before anything is written or sent);
- with the recorded path (compared as absolute, lexically normalised paths): the same;
- with another path that exists (any type): `<path> already exists; choose another --output-file`
  (exit 1, before anything is written or sent);
- with a new path: it is claimed and becomes the job's output (recorded by a checkpoint,
  TS also re-points `outputFile`); the previous file is left as it is.

### 14.13 `runtime resume-poll <stateFile>`

After §14.2's checks (the tenant, the credentials and the client come after step 3):
1. **State directory** `S` resolved as in §14.9 (not created). The argument is
   canonicalised (`realpath`); a failure is
   `Cannot read <stateFile> (missing, not a regular file, unreadable or larger than 128 MiB)`.
2. **Location** (D127): the canonical path's directory must be the canonical `S` and its name
   `<job>.bulk-scan.json`. Otherwise the file is read once (bounded, read-only, not
   locked) only to classify it: a TypeScript state gets the §14.9 TypeScript message;
   anything else
   `<stateFile> is not an airs bulk-scan job in <S>; resume-poll resumes only jobs in its state directory (a moved or copied state cannot be resumed)`
   (exit 1).
3. `S` opened and checked (§14.9); the job lock taken (§14.11). No state decision is made
   before the lock is held. Then the tenant, the scanner credentials and the client.
4. The state read and validated (§14.9); `jobId` must equal the name's job id.
5. **Tenant** (D127): the selected tenant's name must equal `tenant`, else
   `<state> was started with tenant <a>; select that tenant (for example with --tenant <a>) to resume it`;
   its effective `airsApiEndpoint` must equal `scanEndpoint`, else
   `<state> was started against <recorded endpoint>, but tenant <a> now uses <current endpoint>; restore its airsApiEndpoint to resume it`
   (exit 1, nothing sent).
6. The output resolved (§14.12; its refusals come before anything is written); stale
   temporaries (§14.10, §14.12) removed; every `submitting` item turned `ambiguous` (its
   attempt `unknown`, `endedAt` now, error
   `the process stopped before the outcome was recorded`); a checkpoint when anything
   changed.
7. **Ambiguous path** (any `ambiguous` item): no status lines; every `submitted` receipt of
   the job is polled (§14.7, batch by batch), the CSV rewritten, then the TS error
   `Cannot safely resubmit prompt <i>: its submission outcome is ambiguous. Known accepted results were preserved; inspect <state> before taking manual action.`
   (`<i>` the lowest ambiguous index) with the detail line
   `<a> prompt(s) have an unknown submission outcome and <p> were not submitted; nothing will be resubmitted automatically.`
   (exit 1). `pending` items are not submitted. A poll error on this path is §14.7's
   error.
8. **Normal path**: the status lines (§14.14), then per stored logical batch (the stored
   `batchSize`): poll its `submitted` receipts, submit its `pending` items (§14.5, §14.6,
   with the stored profile and session), poll again. A submission stop follows §14.6.
9. A final checkpoint and CSV rewrite, the summary, exit as §14.15.

On a completed job steps 7–8 send **no request**, the CSV is rewritten byte-identically and
the exit code repeats the job's (1 when it has a failed row; failed rows are terminal and
never re-polled). An abandon option for ambiguous items is not part of 0.5.

**Details settled by the implementation:**
- Paths in the messages: the location refusal and the TypeScript message of step 2 show the
  argument as typed (through `terminal_safe`); every message after step 3 shows the canonical
  state path `<canonical S>/<job>.bulk-scan.json`. `<S>` in the location refusal is the
  canonical directory when it exists, else the resolved one.
- The step-2 classification read only opens a regular file; anything else (a directory, a
  FIFO, a file over 128 MiB) gets the location refusal. The path is checked before it is
  opened, the open is non-blocking and the descriptor is checked again, so a FIFO never
  blocks the command.
- The job lock is acquired with `O_CREAT` (a job whose lock file was removed gets a new one,
  0600); an existing lock file must pass the §3.8 file rule (`Refusing to use …`).
- The output of step 6 is decided before anything is written or sent: a re-pointed
  `--output-file` that exists is refused, and the recorded output, when present, must be a
  regular file of ours with the `output` or `output.next` identity, else the §14.12 identity
  refusal (`… is not the file this job wrote …`) comes at once instead of at the first rewrite.
  Then `output.next` is promoted when the path has it, a leftover `next.temp` is removed only
  when it is a regular file of ours with that identity, in the output's directory and named
  `.<file name>.*.tmp`, and an absent or re-pointed output is claimed with the projection of
  the loaded state. When the step-6 checkpoint fails, a file claimed by this run is removed
  again (its identity checked).
- Interruption: `nothing was changed` until the state is loaded; from the load on, the job's
  `<s> of <n> prompts were submitted; …` context (§14.16).
- Only this job's stale temporaries are swept (another job's are left to that job's resume).
- On the ambiguous path the lock is released after the CSV write and before the refusal is
  printed; the refusal is the last line on stderr (no status line precedes it).

### 14.14 Status lines, summary, formats and streams

Profile/session previews, state/output paths in summaries and status, save warnings
and dynamic interruption/error text are filtered against all invocation credentials,
including unselected named entries (§3.15). Safe legacy bytes remain unchanged.

**Status lines** (stderr, dim, quiet-suppressed, the same in every format; TS B§12), after
the debug notice:

```
  Prisma AIRS Bulk Scan
  Profile:  <profile>
  Session:  <session id>
  Prompts:  <n>
  Batches:  <b> (size <batchSize>)
  State:    <state path>
  Submitting batch <k>...                    (per logical batch)
  ⚠ Rate limited while submitting — retry <n> in <s>s...
  Scan IDs saved: <state path>               (per logical batch, after its submissions)
  ⚠ Rate limited — retry <n> in <s>s...
```

`resume-poll` (normal path only): `Prisma AIRS Resume Poll`, `Profile:  <profile>`,
`Scan IDs: <distinct scan ids in the state>`, `Prompts:  <n>`, then only the rate-limit
lines. Profile, session and paths go through `terminal_safe`. `<state path>` is
`<canonical S>/<job>.bulk-scan.json`.

**Summary** (stdout, after the final CSV write):
- pretty (TS bytes): the banner `Bulk Scan Complete` (`Resume Poll Complete` for
  `resume-poll`; decoration), then the key/value block (data)
  `Total`, `Blocked`, `Allowed`, `Failed`, `Output` (width 7): `Total` the number of
  rows in the CSV, the three counts by action, `Output` the absolute output path.
  Colours (§2.8): keys dim; the `Blocked` and `Failed` values red, `Allowed` green (also
  for `0`), `Output` cyan, `Total` plain.
- json (Rust-only, D130):
  `{"profile", "sessionId", "state", "output", "prompts", "total", "blocked", "allowed", "failed"}`
  (paths absolute, `prompts` the job's item count); never prompts or results.
- table (Rust-only, D130): the §2.7 `Key │ Value` table of the json record, in its order.

**Failed rows.** When `failed > 0`, after the summary:
`  ✗ <n> prompt(s) failed; successful results were preserved.` on stderr (red as one span,
never quiet-suppressed, no error block; TS `ui.error`), exit 1, in every format.

**Streams.** stdout carries only the summary and is empty when the command fails
(§2.2); the CSV goes only to its file, never to stdout. `--quiet` suppresses the status
lines, the debug notice and the banner; the summary data, the failure line, warnings and
errors stay. The tenant's `defaultOutput` is ignored.

### 14.15 Exit codes

- 0: every item has an `allow` or `block` row (a resume with nothing to do included).
- 1: tenant, credential, client, input-file (except "no prompts"), state-directory,
  state, lock, output and checkpoint errors; any submission stop (rejected, rate limit
  exhausted, not sent, unknown outcome, unusable receipt); any polling error; the
  `resume-poll` location, tenant and ambiguous refusals; any failed row (after the
  summary).
- 2: every §14.2 argument check, and `No prompts found in input file`.
- 130 / 143: interrupted (§14.16).

### 14.16 Interruption

The §2.5 signal thread cancels the session; the CLI's own waits (the 5 s poll interval, the
429 backoff) `select!` on `session.cancelled()`; checkpoints, the claim and CSV rewrites are
local I/O that finish before the signal is acted on (D129). Then
`\n  ✗ Error: Interrupted; <context>\n\n` and exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM):
- before the first checkpoint (setup, §14.4): `no prompt was submitted` (nothing is left);
- a cancelled POST that the SDK reports `NotSent` (items back to `pending`), a signal
  during polling or a wait, or between steps:
  `<s> of <n> prompts were submitted; the job was saved: resume it with 'airs runtime resume-poll <state>'`
  (`<s>` the items `submitted`, `complete` or `failed`);
- a cancelled POST reported `Unknown` (items `ambiguous`):
  `prompts <ranges> may already have been submitted (outcome unknown); the job was saved in <state>`;
- `resume-poll` before the state is loaded (under the lock): `nothing was changed`.

A second signal exits at once (§2.5); the worst case is a durable `submitting`, which a
resume treats as ambiguous: never a duplicate. The kernel releases the job lock.

### 14.17 `--debug` and doctor

Both commands have the debug policy `log` (§2.9). The log records each attempt's status and
headers under the SDK operation names `airs.scan.async`, `airs.scan.results` and
`airs.scan.reports`, never a body, so no prompt is logged (TypeScript logs every prompt
verbatim in the working directory, D61–D64). The live tier counts submissions from the
`airs.scan.async` records (§10).

Doctor is unchanged: its scanner-credentials skip detail
`not configured — runtime scan, bulk-scan and topics eval are unavailable` (§9) is the TS
text and is now accurate. There is no doctor check of the state directory (TS has none
either).

### 14.18 Acceptance tests

Every behaviour above gets an executable test (`tests/bulk_scan.rs`), unit tests in
`src/bulk/`, parity tests (`tests/parity_bulk_scan.rs`) and a `dNN_` test per §12 row.
The TypeScript specs (B§17) are ported first:

| # | TypeScript (`state-spec`, `lock-spec`, `int-spec`) | Rust acceptance test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | a save writes version, profile, per-item correlation and `updatedAt` | unit: the serialiser's bytes carry `format`, `version`, `profile`, each item's `index`, `reqId`, `prompt`, `scanId`, and `updatedAt` |
| 2 | state names end `.bulk-scan.json`; the directory is created | one `<job>.bulk-scan.json` in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/airs-cli/bulk-scans/`, created 0700 |
| 3 | re-saving rewrites one path | after a multi-checkpoint run exactly one state file and no temporary |
| 4 | an invalid state is refused and nothing written | unit: a checkpoint of a state breaking an invariant fails before the temporary exists |
| 5 | directory 0700, file 0600 | the same modes (and 0600 for the CSV and the lock) |
| 6 | round trip; missing, malformed, legacy, duplicate, out-of-order, receipt-less and mismatched states | unit for each; executable: `resume-poll` prints the §14.9 texts (the TS file gets the TypeScript message, D118) |
| 7 | one owner at a time; released for a later run | `lock_holder` holds `<job>.lock`: `resume-poll` refuses at once naming the holder, 0 requests; after release it succeeds (D119) |
| 8 | a dead owner's lock is recovered | after the holder is SIGKILLed the next `resume-poll` succeeds with no manual step; the lock file stays (D119) |
| 9 | 7 prompts, rows out of order | 7 rows in input order with the right actions and detector columns |
| 10 | a poll failure exits 1; resume completes | the same, with the §14.7 detail line naming the state |
| 11 | overlapping resumes submit once | two concurrent `resume-poll` runs: one refused, one POST in total |
| 12 | 21 prompts, the second chunk exhausts 429 | 6 POSTs of `req_id` 20 (`Retry-After: 0`); resume submits only `req_id` 20; 21 rows |
| 13 | a 4xx-rejected chunk stays pending; resume submits it once | the same |
| 14 | a failed row: both rows written, exit 1, also on resume | the same, with the failure line |
| 15 | an ambiguous (network) submission: one POST; resume sends nothing, exit 1 | the same (`ClosedPort` and a dropped connection), the ambiguous refusal and detail line |
| 16 | stale output replaced before the first POST | **inverted** (D121): an existing output or symlink is refused before any file or request |
| 17 | accepted + ambiguous chunk: resume polls once, 20 rows, no POST, exit 1 | the same |
| 18 | accepted + rejected chunk: resume polls before it submits; a retried submission that is ambiguous | the same (`complete` ×20, `ambiguous`) |
| 19 | a later batch's poll fails; resume completes; a second resume is byte-identical with no request | the same |
| 20 | results are checkpointed as they resolve | rows resolved by a poll are in the state before the next request (one checkpoint per response, §14.7 step 4) |
| 21 | invalid batch sizes exit 2 with no request | the same, with no file created |
| 22 | batches are sequential; resume keeps the stored batch size | the recorded request order of §14.5 on both commands |

Rust additions: each crash point of §14.8 (a SIGKILL after C1 with the POST held by the
fixture leaves `submitting`, and `resume-poll` then sends no POST); `NotSent` and
`Rejected` stay pending, `Unknown` is ambiguous (§14.6 table, each row); a non-UUID
receipt (D126); `req_id` `2.0`, `-1`, `1.5` and foreign scan ids (§14.7); the report
fallback; the no-progress bound (unit, with an injected zero interval); the `Retry-After`
cap with a far-future HTTP date (D124); a 500 whose body says "rate limit" is not retried
(D125); the body-budget split (D120); every §14.3 parser case, the prompt cap and the
unterminated quote (D128); the setup clean-up of §14.4 (D123); the output identity, the
re-claim of a removed output and `--output-file` re-pointing (D121); the default name
(D122); the location and tenant refusals (D127); interruption in each §14.16 case (D129);
the three formats and `--quiet` (D130); withholding in the CSV and state (D131); every
checkpoint and rewrite failure through a `#[cfg(test)]` step hook (§3.9 style).
