  file step). `SECRET` values join the `SecretSet` (§15.4). The order is the `<uuid>` of
  `update`, the script checks, the variables checks, then `--channel` and `--adapter` (§15.3
  ID texts). A channel lookup that a signal cancels is an interruption, not an ignored failure.
- **`adapter create`**: when `--channel` is given and not `--draft`,
  `GET <broker>/v1/channels/<channel>`; a status other than `ONLINE` is the TS error
  `network broker channel <uuid> is <STATUS> — adapter validation requires an ONLINE channel (network broker v1.4.0+). Check 'airs redteam network-broker channels list'.`
  (exit 1, no write); a failing lookup is ignored (TS parity: the service decides). Then
  `POST <mgmt>/v1/adapters?validate=<false with --draft, else true>` once, body (strict)
  `{"name", "description"?, "script_b64", "network_broker_channel_uuid"?, "variables"?, "prompt"}`.
  stderr `  ✓ Adapter created: <uuid>`; stdout the redacted detail (TS ignores `--output`, D144).
- **`adapter update <uuid>`**: the channel check as for create; then the read-modify-write of
  RG§16.2: `GET <mgmt>/v1/adapters/<uuid>`, the body `{"name": --name ?? current, "description":
  --description ?? current (omitted when null), "script_b64": the script ?? current,
  "network_broker_channel_uuid": --channel ?? current (omitted when null; from 0.9.1 a current
  value that is not a UUID is refused after the read and before the PUT, exit 1, D307), "variables":
  --variables ?? preserveVariablesForUpdate(current) (redacted values sent as null: keep
  stored), "prompt"}`, validated, then `PUT <mgmt>/v1/adapters/<uuid>?validate=<…>` once, with
  no request between the read and the PUT (the §13.4 window, documented). stderr
  `  ✓ Adapter updated: <uuid>`; stdout the detail. The read values are never printed.
- **`adapter delete|rm <uuid> [--force]`** (D137): the gate (before the tenant; TS checks it
  after the banner), the prompt `Delete adapter <uuid>?`, then `DELETE <mgmt>/v1/adapters/<uuid>`;
  stderr `  ✓ Adapter <uuid> deleted.`.
- **`adapter validate`**: the channel check (always; not `ONLINE` → the error above); with
  `--adapter` and no variables flag, `GET <mgmt>/v1/adapters/<adapter>` and its
  `preserveVariablesForUpdate` set; then `POST <mgmt>/v1/adapters/validate` once,
  `{"script_b64", "network_broker_channel_uuid", "prompt"[, "variables"][, "adapter_uuid"]}`
  (it runs the script through the customer's broker). Document `{"validated", "stdout",
  "stderr", "traceback"}` with the §15.4 withholding; pretty the TS sections (`stdout:`,
  `stderr:` and `traceback:` red, each `\n  <label>\n\n<text>\n`, terminal-safe), stderr
  `  ✓ Adapter script validated` or `  ✗ Adapter script validation FAILED` (never suppressed);
  exit 1 when `validated` is false (TS), after the data.

### 15.15 Network broker

- **`channels list|ls`** (RG§19.1): `GET <broker>/v1/channels?[skip][&limit][&search][&status=…]*`
  (`status` repeated in argument order). `--all`: the CLI walk (§15.3; the SDK has no
  `list_all` for channels) with page size `--limit`, else 100. Rows (TS) `{"id", "name",
  "status", "clients", "lastOnline"}` (nulls → `""`); table `ID │ Name │ Status │ Clients │ Last Online`;
  pretty `Network Broker Channels:` (TS).
- **`channels get <channelId>`**: `GET <broker>/v1/channels/<channelId>`. json the TS
  `normalizeChannel` object; table `Key │ Value` (TS prints YAML); pretty `Channel Detail:` (TS).
- **`channels create --name [--description]`**: argument check `--name` 1–64 characters (the
  TS SDK text `…POST /v1/channels did not match schema: name: too_small|too_big`, exit 2) →
  `POST <broker>/v1/channels` once; stderr `  ✓ Channel created: <uuid>`; stdout the detail.
- **`channels update <channelId> [--name] [--description]`**: neither flag is the TS usage error
  `Specify --name and/or --description to update` (checked before the `<channelId>` shape, TS
  order; an empty value counts as given, TS); `PATCH <broker>/v1/channels/<channelId>`
  with the given fields; stderr `  ✓ Channel updated: <uuid>`; stdout the detail. There is no
  channel delete in either SDK: channels are never created live.
- **`stats`**: `GET <broker>/v1/channels/stats`. json (TS) `{"serverDomain", "dockerRegistry",
  "helmChart", "dockerImage", "onlineChannels", "totalChannels", "clientVersion"}`; table
  `Key │ Value`; pretty `Network Broker Stats:` (TS).

### 15.16 `report|dashboard <jobId>` (one scan)

Argument checks (exit 2): the job id; `--output-file`, `--title`, `--max-pages` or `--strict`
given explicitly: `Environment report options cannot be combined with a scan job ID` (TS);
`--limit` (§15.3); `--severity` (filter rule). `--severity` without `--attacks` is accepted and
unused (TS). From 0.9.1, with `--attacks`: `--limit` at most 100 and `--severity` one of `LOW`,
`MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL` (D301, D303, §15.23). `--debug` is allowed (TS). Requests (RS§10): `GET <data>/v1/scan/<jobId>`, then by
`job_type`: `CUSTOM` → `GET <data>/v1/custom-attacks/report/<jobId>` and, with `--attacks`,
`GET <data>/v1/custom-attacks/job/<jobId>/list-custom-attacks?limit=<n>`; `DYNAMIC` →
`GET <data>/v1/report/dynamic/<jobId>/report` (`--attacks` unused); anything else →
`GET <data>/v1/report/static/<jobId>/report` and, with `--attacks`,
`GET <data>/v1/report/static/<jobId>/list-attacks?limit=<n>[&severity=<s>]`.

Output. pretty: the banner, the `Scan Status:` block, then the TS static, dynamic or custom
report layout (RS§10: severity lines, the two-space-indented categories table, the summary with
the `{{…_RISK}}` interpolation as `    <summary>`, multi-line server text whose continuation
lines start at column 0 (§15.3), the attack lines and the footnote of `buildAttackListFootnote`;
the attack prompt is never printed; custom attack prompts use the 80-unit preview; static and
custom ASR as given, dynamic ASR × 100, TS parity). json (Rust-only, D144):
`{"job": <the §15.5 job document>, "report": <the TS service's normalised report>,
"attacks"?: {"items": [<normalised attacks>], "totalItems"}}` (`src/airs/redteam.ts:524-631`;
`attacks` only with `--attacks` and a static or custom job). table: `Key │ Value` of that
document. TS ignores `--output` here.

Step-3 details (resolved while implementing; all TS parity unless a row is named):
- The argument checks run in the order above (the job id first); the tenant's `defaultOutput`
  is not consulted (§15.3 "Formats").
- `totalItems` is the list answer's `pagination.total_items` and is omitted when the answer
  has none; a custom attack list carries it too.
- The footnote is a `ui.dim` line: decoration (quiet-suppressed), after the attack lines (or
  after `No attacks found`, with no blank line after it). Its counts are `String(number)`.
- The withheld server texts include the step-3 keys of §15.3 (`reportSummary`,
  `promptSetName`, `subCategoryDisplayName`); a withheld summary prints `[withheld]` in its
  line.
- A failed read is the §6 error with nothing on stdout (no banner, D57).
- The `--output` help line of `redteam report` (the format policy `Report`, §2.4) reads
  `Output format of a scan job report: pretty, table, json; the environment report is written as HTML (omit --output)`.

### 15.17 `report|dashboard` (the environment report)

The TypeScript collector and renderer (`src/reports/redteam.ts`, `environment-render.ts`,
`io.ts`; RS§11) are ported unchanged except for the format (D155), the debug refusal (D156)
and G7. The report is already safe in TypeScript (aggregates only, no-clobber, 0600).

**Argument checks** (exit 2, in TS order, before the tenant and any request):
1. `--debug` (debug policy `refused`, §2.9):
   `Disable --debug for environment reports to avoid persisting sensitive traffic content`
   (TS names `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG` too, which airs-cli-rs never reads, D156).
2. `--attacks`, `--severity` or `--limit` given: `--attacks, --severity and --limit require a scan job ID` (TS).
3. `--output` given (any of `pretty`, `table`, `json`; `html` and `markdown` already failed the
   §2.4 check): `The environment report is written as HTML; omit --output` (D155: TS writes
   Markdown with `--output markdown` and refuses other values with
   `Report output must be html or markdown`).
4. `--max-pages`: `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, at most 100, else `--max-pages must be an integer from 1 to 100` (TS).
5. `--title`: non-blank under JavaScript trim and at most 240 UTF-16 units, else
   `--title must contain 1–240 characters` (TS).
6. `--output-file` blank under JavaScript trim: `--output-file cannot be empty` (TS).

**Destination.** `--output-file -` is stdout. Otherwise `--output-file`, else
`airs-redteam-report-<UTC ISO time with ':' → '-'>-<first 8 hex of a v4 UUID>.html` in the
working directory (TS name), made absolute. Before the tenant: `lstat` the path; anything
there, a dangling symlink included, fails with the generic message below (exit 1, no request).

**Collection** (TS order and rules): the status line
`  Collecting Red Team statistics and current configuration (read-only)...`, then the seven
sources of RS§11.3 in order, one client, every request with `with_retries(0)` (TS
`numRetries: 0`) and one CLI re-read after an `Http` 401 or 403 `Rejected` (G7, TS's free
replay), each source under one 300 s budget. Paged sources (`targets`, `scans`, `adapters`,
page size 15, `include_target_count=true` for adapters) use the TS page loop and its checks
(identity, total, page size, the `--max-pages` budget; RS§11.3 notes), not `redteam::walk`.
Counters must be safe non-negative integers; labels are cut and cleaned as TS does. The
findings, health and both labels are TypeScript's. Only aggregates are kept: no target names,
ids, connection settings, scripts, variables, prompts or error bodies (TS unit test
"excludes sensitive fields").

**Rendering.** The TS self-contained HTML byte for byte (`renderRedTeamReportHtml`: the
hash-based CSP computed over the same inline style and script, `&#<code>;` escaping, the
sections, the footer `Prisma AIRS CLI · Red Team report schema 1 · Works offline and without JavaScript.`,
one trailing `\n`). The Markdown renderer is not ported (D155).

**Publishing** (TS `writeReportFile`, the shared exclusive publisher of §15.18). stdout delivery
writes the document as the stdout data. A file: the status line
`  Report → <abs path, \p{Cc}\p{Cf} → _> (mode 0600)` (TS). Then, when any source is not
complete, `  <n> source(s) incomplete; review the evidence section.` (TS status line).

**Exit.** 1 when the health is `unknown` (the file is still written) or `--strict` and a source
is incomplete; otherwise 0. Any error after the checks (an existing path, a tenant, config or
credential error, a write failure) prints only the TS line
`  ✗ Report generation failed. Verify Management API configuration and a writable, new output path. Existing files are never overwritten.`
(stderr, red as one span, no error block; never quiet-suppressed) and exits 1 (TS parity: no
path, OS error or server text). Interrupt contexts: `no report was written`, or
`the report was saved in <path>` once it was published.

**Step-3 details** (resolved while implementing; `src/report/`, `commands/redteam_report.rs`):
- **Client and token.** The client is built without an upfront token request (as TS, whose
  token is fetched by the first read), so a token failure is a failure of each source, not of
  the report: the sources are `unavailable` with the TS `HTTP <code>: source unavailable…`
  note when the failure carries an HTTP status, else the generic note; the file is still
  written (`Unable to assess`, exit 1). A tenant or credential error (before the client) is the
  failure line. The `Collecting …` status line is printed once the client is built.
- **Budgets and G7.** Each source has one `with_timeout(300 s).with_retries(0)` budget for all
  its pages; the G7 re-read reuses it. A cancelled read (a signal) stops the report:
  `Interrupted; no report was written`, no file, no temporary.
- **The page loop** is TS `pages` verbatim: `skip` = rows collected so far, at most
  `--max-pages` pages, the notes of RS§11.3 (`Reached the <n>-page budget; inventory is
  incomplete.` included); with rows collected a failure makes the source `partial`.
- **Labels.** `\p{Cc}` (`char::is_control`) and the Unicode `Cf` table become spaces; a cut
  at 120 UTF-16 units that splits a surrogate pair ends in U+FFFD (what Node writes for TS's
  lone surrogate). Groups are sorted by an approximation of `localeCompare`: lowercased first
  (for ASCII this is ICU's punctuation < digits < letters order), then lowercase before
  uppercase, then code points; it can differ from ICU only for labels that differ in accents
  or non-ASCII case alone.
- **Times.** `Date.parse` of the created times admitted by the TS zone regex
  (`/(?:Z|[+-]\d{2}:\d{2})$/i`) is the ISO-8601 date-time form
  `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm[:ss[.fff…]]` with `Z`, `z` or `±hh:mm`; any other text counts as an
  unusable timestamp (TS `NaN`). The window is the 24 hours before the collection start.
- **stdout delivery** writes the document and commits stdout at once; a write error, a closed
  pipe included, is the failure line and exit 1 (TS's stream-error test). Then the status
  lines.
- **The file** is published with `files::publish_new` (temp `.airs-<16 hex>.tmp`, TS
  `.airs-report-<uuid>.tmp`); a directory-sync failure is the §3.9 warning. The existence check
  `lstat`s the path made absolute (TS `resolve`) before the tenant.
- **Debug policy.** `DebugPolicy::Refused`: the refusal is planning check 1, so no log is ever
  opened for the environment report.

### 15.18 `targets backup`

**Argument checks** (exit 2): the `--format` warning; `--file-format` (or `--format`) other than
`json`: `--file-format must be json (yaml was dropped)` (TS writes `.json` for any value but
`yaml`, D151); `--name ""`: `--name needs a target name`; `--output-dir ""`:
`--output-dir needs a path`. The TS hidden `--output <format>` alias is the global format flag.

**Location** (before the tenant): `--output-dir` (default the working directory) must be an
existing directory (followed through symlinks; no directory is created), else
`Cannot write a backup into <dir>; it must be an existing directory` (exit 1). The file is
`<dir>/airs-redteam-targets-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<8 lowercase hex>.json`; anything at that
path (`lstat`) is `<path> already exists; choose another --output-dir` (exit 1, no request).

**Requests.** The complete `targets list` walk (§15.12). `--name <n>`: every target whose name is
exactly `<n>` (all of them when several share it; TS takes the first); none:
`Target not found: <n>` (TS, exit 1, no file). No target at all: pretty `  No targets found`,
json `{"file": null, "backedUp": 0, "failed": [], "targets": []}`, table nothing; no file;
exit 0. Then, in list order, `GET <mgmt>/v1/target/<uuid>` per target (a failure is that
target's failed row; the run continues, TS parity).

**Format** (Rust-only; D151). One JSON document in the §2.2 layout plus `"\n"`, keys in this
order:

```json
{
  "format": "airs-cli-rs.redteam-targets",
  "version": 1,
  "exportedAt": "2026-10-17T12:00:00.000Z",
  "tenant": "redtail-prod",
  "tsgId": "100",
  "complete": true,
  "targets": [
    {"uuid": "…", "name": "Rest Target One", "credentialsWithheld": false, "target": {"name": "Rest Target One", "target_type": "APPLICATION", "connection_params": {…}, "auth_config": {…}}}
  ],
  "failed": [{"uuid": "…", "name": "…", "error": "<the §6 message>"}]
}
```

- `tenant` is the store name of the tenant and `tsgId` its `mgmtTsgId` (§3.7); `complete` is
  `false` exactly when `failed` is not empty. A target stored with withheld credentials is not
  a failure: `complete` stays `true`, but that target is not restorable (below).
- `target` is the create-request projection of the GET response: the `TargetCreateRequest` keys
  in schema order (`name, description, target_type, connection_type, api_endpoint_type,
  response_mode, connection_params, auth_config, auth_type, canonical_id, session_supported,
  target_metadata, target_background, additional_context, extra_info,
  network_broker_channel_uuid, adapter_uuid, adapter_variable_overrides`), each when present
  and not `null`; nested values as returned (unknown nested keys kept: the request unions are
  passthrough); `target_metadata` without `multi_turn_error_message` when `multi_turn` is
  `false` (TS); `adapter_variable_overrides` as `{key, value, type}`. TS drops `description`,
  `canonical_id`, `adapter_uuid` and `adapter_variable_overrides`, so adapter-backed targets
  cannot be restored, and writes the fabricated `ws_response_timeout` (D151, D153). A
  projection that fails `TargetCreateRequest::parse` is a failed row
  (`its settings do not match the target create schema`), so every stored target can be sent;
  from 1.0 that includes a Vertex AI target whose answer masks a patterned field, whose row
  names the masked fields and the remedy instead when they alone fail the schema (`the service
  masked its Vertex AI location and engine_id, which the target create schema refuses;
  recreate the target or set its identifiers by hand`; D329, §15.24 choice 13).
- `credentialsWithheld` (D157) is `true` when the service withheld the target's credentials (the
  §15.19 plan rule 2 test on the projection: a credential path holding `[REDACTED]` or a server
  mask of four or more `*`, or a `SECRET` override without a value). On a real tenant the GET
  masks the credentials of every credentialed target. Such a target is stored as returned,
  masks included (nothing is fabricated or blanked), counted as backed up, and refused by
  restore: the target must be recreated, or its credentials set by hand (TS stores the mask
  with nothing to mark it, and its restore sends the mask as the credential). A later option
  could take the credentials from a separate file.
- **Secrets** (choice 5 of §15.22): the file holds every credential the API returned, as
  returned (a restore must be able to recreate the target; TS does the same, at 0644). After
  writing, when at least one stored target holds a credential the service returned (a value the
  §15.4 target rules redact as a credential that is not `[REDACTED]` or a mask, also after a
  `<scheme> ` prefix), the warning
  `  ⚠ <path> contains target credentials; keep it private (mode 0600)` (yellow, never
  quiet-suppressed). With no stored target, or only withheld or no credentials, it is not
  printed; the file is 0600 either way.

**Publishing** (`files::publish_new`, shared with downloads and the environment report; TS
`writeReportFile`): only after every read. Create `.airs-<16 hex>.tmp` in the destination
directory with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, mode 0600 (`fchmod`),
write, `fsync`, close; `link(temp, path)` (an existing path, a symlink included, is
`<path> already exists; choose another --output-dir`, or `--output-file` for the other users;
nothing is overwritten); unlink the temporary; `fsync` the directory (a failure is the §3.9
directory-sync warning). Any other failure: `Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable`
(exit 1), the temporary removed. A reader never sees a partial file, and an interruption before
the link leaves none (only a SIGKILL can leave a `.airs-*.tmp`).

**Output.** stdout: pretty the backup banner, the section `Backed up <n> target(s) to <path>:`
(decoration), `  ✓ <name>` per stored target, or
`  ⚠ <name> — credentials withheld by the service; restore will refuse it` (the yellow `⚠`) for one
stored with withheld credentials (data; `<n>` counts both), then, when any failed, the section
`Failed (<f>):` and `  ✗ <name>: <message>` per failure, then `\n` (TS layout with one file in
place of per-target files); json `{"file", "backedUp", "failed": [{"uuid", "name", "error"}],
"targets": [{"uuid", "name", "credentialsWithheld"}]}`; table `Target │ UUID │ Status` (`ok`,
`withheld` or `failed`). Exit 1
when any target failed (after the file and the summary; no error block, TS parity); otherwise
0. Interrupt contexts: `no backup file was written`, or `the backup was saved in <path>` once
it was linked.

**Step-3 details** (resolved while implementing; `redteam::backup`, `commands/redteam_backup.rs`):
- **Reads.** The per-target read is the typed `GET` of the G10 note above, without the SDK's
  schema defaults (`red_team.targets.get` in the `--debug` log; 0.6 sent a raw read named
  `custom.read`), so the stored projection holds only keys the server sent (no
  `ws_response_timeout: 110`, no `basic_auth_location` default; D153), `null`s and unknown
  nested keys included. Nested objects keep the order serde_json gives them (keys sorted, the
  typed answer re-serialised through `serde_json::Value`, byte for byte what the 0.6 raw read
  stored); only the top level is in schema order. Every credential of a read joins the invocation's secret set (the §15.4 target
  rules on a copy), so a name or an error that echoes one is `[withheld]`. A read that fails
  the response schema is a failed row with the §6 decode message.
- **The path** is shown as `<dir as given>/<name>` (`./airs-redteam-targets-….json` by default);
  the credentials warning follows a written file that holds a returned credential; the `Backed up <n> target(s) to <path>:`
  section is printed whenever a file was written (also with `0`, when every target failed), so
  the path is always shown.
- `--file-format` and its deprecated `--format` share the check (`--file-format` wins when both
  are given).

### 15.19 `targets restore`

**Argument checks** (exit 2, in order): `--input-dir` given:
`--input-dir is not supported: an airs backup is one file; pass --file <backup>`;
`--file` missing or empty: `Specify --file <path>` (TS: `Specify --file <path> or --input-dir <path>`);
`--dry-run` with `--force`: `--dry-run cannot be combined with --force`; `--overwrite` without
`--force` and without `--dry-run`: the confirmation gate
(`refusing to overwrite targets without --force in non-interactive mode`).

**The file** (before the tenant; the §15.3 input rules, 16 MiB, UTF-8; exit 1; nothing from the
file is echoed but names through `terminal_safe`):
- not JSON (the D44 classes included): `Invalid red team target backup <path>: malformed JSON`;
- a TypeScript backup (an object with a `resourceType` key, or a string `version`; a
  `--file-format yaml` envelope, which is not JSON, is recognised by a `resourceType:` line or
  a `version: '1'` / `version: "1"` line):
  `<path> is a TypeScript airs-cli backup; airs cannot restore it. Restore it with the TypeScript airs-cli, or back the targets up again with 'airs redteam targets backup'.`
  (D152; there is no import of TypeScript backups);
- `format` correct and `version` above 1: `<path> was written by a newer version of airs; upgrade airs to restore it`;
- anything else that breaks the §15.18 schema (unknown keys refused at every level of the
  envelope; each `target` must pass `TargetCreateRequest::parse`):
  `Invalid red team target backup <path>: <reason>` (`<reason>` a fixed text, never content).
- `complete: false`: the warning `  ⚠ <path> is incomplete: <f> target(s) could not be backed up`
  (not fatal).

**Tenant check.** After the tenant and credential checks: the file's `tsgId` must equal the
tenant's `mgmtTsgId`, else
`<path> was exported from TSG <a>; the selected tenant uses TSG <b>. Pass --allow-other-tenant to restore it here.`
(exit 1, no request; TS checks nothing).

**Plan** (no write yet). The complete `targets list` walk (an incomplete one deletes nothing and
writes nothing: its error, exit 1), then one row per backup target in file order, the first
rule that applies:
1. Another backup target has the same name: `failed`, `the backup holds more than one target named <name>`
   (TS creates both).
2. The entry is marked `"credentialsWithheld": true`, or a credential path (§15.4 target rules
   1–4, 6, 7) holds `[REDACTED]`, a string of four or more `*` only (a server mask), or a
   `SECRET` override without a value (recomputed, whatever the marker says; the marker is
   trusted as written, so a marked target is refused even after its values were edited):
   `failed`,
   `the service withheld its credentials when it was backed up, so it cannot be restored; recreate the target or set its credentials by hand`
   (D157).
3. More than one tenant target has that name: `failed`, `more than one target named <name> exists`
   (TS updates the last one listed).
4. One tenant target has that name: without `--overwrite` `skipped`; with it `update`.
5. Otherwise `create`.

**`--dry-run`** prints the plan (the summary layout below with `would create`, `would update`,
`skipped` and `failed` rows; the `would …` rows use the neutral `•` bullet and lead the
`Total:` counts) and writes nothing; exit 1 when a row is `failed`, else 0.

**Confirmation.** With `--overwrite`, at least one `update` row and no `--force`: the prompt
`Overwrite <n> existing target[s] with the settings in <file>?` (after the plan, before any
write).

**Writes**, in plan order, one attempt each (D133):
- `create`: the stored body with TS's routing defaults when missing (`connection_type` `CUSTOM`,
  `api_endpoint_type` `PUBLIC`, `response_mode` `REST`) → `POST <mgmt>/v1/target[?validate=true]`.
- `update`: `GET <mgmt>/v1/target/<uuid>`, the stored body with the missing routing fields taken
  from the current target first (TS `prepareTargetPayload`) → `PUT <mgmt>/v1/target/<uuid>[?validate=true]`.
- A rejected write (3xx, 4xx, a local check) is the row's `failed` with its §6 message; the run
  continues. An unknown or unreadable outcome is the row's `unknown` (unreadable: `created` or
  `updated` with the outcome note) and **stops** the run: every later row is `notAttempted`
  (choice 10 of §15.22; TS re-sends the write up to five times, then continues).

**Output.** stdout: pretty the backup banner, the section `Restore results:` (decoration), per row
`  ✓ <name> — created|updated`, `  ○ <name> — skipped`, `  ✗ <name> — failed: <message>`,
`  ✗ <name> — outcome unknown: <message>`, `  ○ <name> — not attempted`, then
`\n  Total: <counts>\n\n` with the non-zero counts in the order created, updated, skipped,
failed, outcome unknown, not attempted, joined by `, ` (TS layout and glyph colours; the last
two kinds are Rust-only); json `{"file", "dryRun", "created", "updated", "skipped", "failed",
"unknown", "notAttempted", "details": [{"name", "uuid"?, "action", "status", "error"?}]}`;
table `Target │ Action │ Status │ Error`. The `action` is `create`, `update`, `skip` or `fail`
(a refusal of rules 1–3); the `status` `created`, `updated`, `skipped`, `failed`, `unknown`,
`notAttempted`, or for a dry run `wouldCreate` and `wouldUpdate`; `uuid` is the tenant
target's id (an update or a skip) or the created one. Exit 1 when any row is `failed`, `unknown` or
`notAttempted`, or a write's answer could not be read (the last write included), after the
summary (no error block); otherwise 0. Interrupt context:
`<c> created, <u> updated[, <k> outcome unknown], <n> not attempted`, or `nothing was changed`
before the first write.

**Step-3 details** (resolved while implementing):
- **The file.** A `target` must carry the entry's `name`, and `complete` must equal "`failed`
  is empty"; the fixed reasons are `the file does not hold a JSON object`, `it is not an
  airs red team target backup`, `version must be 1`, `the envelope has an unknown key`,
  `<key> must be a string`, `complete must be true or false`, `targets must be an array`,
  `failed must be an array`, `targets[<i>] must be an object`, `targets[<i>] must have exactly
  the keys uuid, name, credentialsWithheld, target`, `targets[<i>] uuid and name must be
  strings`, `targets[<i>] name must be the target's name`, `targets[<i>] credentialsWithheld must be true or false`, `targets[<i>] does not
  match the target create schema`, for `failed[<i>]` `must be an object`, `must have exactly
  the keys uuid, name, error` and `uuid, name and error must be strings`, and `complete does
  not match the failed list`. The stored credentials join the secret set before anything
  is printed.
- **Order.** The file, then the tenant and the TSG check, then the token and the listing (the
  TSG refusal sends nothing).
- **Updates.** The current target is read before its `PUT` (a read with the SDK retries); a
  failure of that read is the row's `failed` (nothing was sent) and the run continues.
- **An unreadable outcome** (a 2xx whose body could not be read) is the row's `created` or
  `updated` with the note `Outcome: the target was created|updated, but the response could not be read.`,
  and the run stops there like an unknown outcome (every later write row `notAttempted`) and
  exits 1, also when it was the last write.
- **Interruption.** Before the first write `nothing was changed`; then the counts context of
  the section (a write cancelled after it was sent counts as `outcome unknown`).

### 15.21 Acceptance tests

Every behaviour above gets an executable test (`tests/redteam_*.rs`), unit tests in
`src/redteam/` and `src/report/`, parity tests (`tests/parity_redteam_*.rs`) and a `dNN_` test
per §12 row. The TypeScript specs (RS§19, RG§21) are ported first:

| TypeScript spec | Rust acceptance tests (adjusted by the §12 rows) |
|---|---|
| `unit/cli/redteam-scan-helpers.spec.ts` | `--goals` inline, leading whitespace, file, invalid JSON, non-strings, empty strings; `--depth`/`--breadth` positive, non-numeric, zero, negative (exit 2, D134); the default categories (mapping, `MULTI_TURN` excluded, empty catalogue `{}`) |
| `unit/cli/redteam-attacks-renderer.spec.ts`, `redteam-footnote.spec.ts` | the attack lines (display name, sub-category fallback, `—`, BYPASSED/BLOCKED) and the footnote cases, as layout unit tests and one executable report |
| `unit/cli/redteam-categories-renderer.spec.ts`, `redteam-dynamic-renderer.spec.ts` | the categories and dynamic layouts (empty, inline ids, no descriptions; header, score, ASR × 100, goals, no summary, missing numbers) |
| `unit/cli/redteam-output-flag.spec.ts` | prompt-set detail json with `versionInfo`; property values and names json, pretty, empty; target detail pretty never prints `[object Object]` and expands nested JSON; json carries the target with credentials redacted (D140); yaml cases become usage errors (D50) |
| `unit/cli/redteam-init.spec.ts` | the scaffold per provider family, the case-insensitive provider, the unknown-provider text |
| `unit/cli/redteam-adapter-helpers.spec.ts` | `--script-b64` passthrough, `--script-file` encoding (raw bytes, D143), both/neither, `--variables` with `null` values, invalid JSON, bad `type`, non-arrays (exit 2, D141) |
| `unit/airs/redteam.spec.ts`, `redteam-adapters.spec.ts` | request shapes and normalisation of every command against the fixture routes: scan bodies per type, list filters and `skip`, abort, reports and `{{…}}` interpolation, attacks, custom attacks, categories, the wait loop (COMPLETED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE, ABORTED and FAILED as §15.6 says, progress per poll), EULA, instances, devices, registry credentials, languages on both planes, targets (CRUD, probe, `multi_turn_error_message`, profile, update-profile, validate-auth with and without `--target-id`, metadata, templates, error logs), channels (filters, total, get, create, update, stats), adapters (offset → skip, redaction flags, create with `validate`, the read-modify-write that keeps variables, delete, validate filling variables from `--adapter`) |
| `unit/reports/redteam.spec.ts` | the seven sources with no sensitive field; partial records on budget, repeated identity and a later page failure; the stop at the total; quota by GET only (a `POST /v1/metering/quota` trap never hit); exhausted and unlimited quotas; no broker outage inferred; the timestamp window; the HTML escaping, inline assets and CSP |
| `integration/cli/redteam-dashboard.spec.ts` | the `dashboard` alias; `--debug` refused through both names (exit 2, no client, D156); HTML by default whatever `defaultOutput` says; `--output markdown` refused (D155); stdout delivery and a stream error exit 1; unique default names; a partial report exit 0, `--strict` exit 1; all sources unavailable → file written, `Unable to assess`, exit 1, no `PRIVATE-ERROR`; an existing path refused before credentials and requests; an invalid config without echoing content; the invalid-option cases exit 2 before any client |
| `unit/cli/backup.spec.ts`, `restore.spec.ts`, `backup/io.spec.ts`, `backup-renderer.spec.ts` | backup of all targets and by `--name` (`Target not found`), server fields stripped, the summary counts and failed rows; restore create, skip, `--overwrite` update, errors collected, `--validate` passed; the file format, naming and TypeScript-backup refusal are the Rust rules (D151, D152) |

Rust additions: every §15.3 argument check with zero requests and no debug log; the D133 sequences
on each write (a 5xx with `Retry-After: 0`: one Rust request and the outcome line, more than one
TypeScript request with no exact count; a 401: `token, write, token, write` on both; a 403: one
Rust request); the server counters prove one scan start, one abort, one EULA accept, one
registry mint and one upload after 5xx, held-then-dropped and SIGINT cases; the wait loop's
bound, poll failure and progress stream with an injected interval (unit) and one executable run
with a `pending` round; every confirmation on the pty (`y`, `yes`, Enter, `n`, EOF, Ctrl-C) and
its non-interactive refusal; the §15.4 rules on fixtures carrying secret markers in every
credential path (no marker on stdout, stderr, in the debug log or in a summary, in any format);
the empty-page walk error (D147); the download, init, backup and report publishing (an existing
path, a dangling symlink, a symlinked directory, 0600, no temporary left, a held-then-killed run);
the backup and restore rules of §15.18–§15.19 (including a round trip that recreates an
adapter-backed target, D151); interruption in every context of §15.20.

### 15.22 Choices recorded for confirmation

These are the spec's resolutions (1–9 for step 2, 10–16 for step 3), the resolutions of the
0.6 review (17–21) and the step-3 details listed after them; each is safe as written, and the
user confirmed all of them (2026-10-18), with item 19 replaced by the decision written there.
1. `scan` does not confirm (it is billed, but starting a scan is the command's purpose and CI
   runs it); no §12 row.
2. `eula accept` without a terminal and without `--force` is a usage error (D138); the
   alternative keeps TypeScript's "print the EULA and exit 0".
3. The registry token is withheld in pretty and table and printed in json (D139); the
   alternative is a `--show-token` flag even for json.
4. Target and adapter credentials are redacted in every format with no reveal flag; the
   validate-auth token preview is withheld; adapter `scriptB64` stays in json (D140).
5. `ABORTED` exits 1 and `PARTIALLY_COMPLETE` exits 0 with a warning (D136).
6. The scan wait is bounded by `--wait-timeout` (default 24 h); a single failed poll (after the
   SDK read retries) ends the wait, as in TypeScript (D135).
7. `abort`, `instances delete`, `devices delete` and `prompts delete` confirm (D137);
   `prompt-sets archive` does not.
8. `prompt-sets download`, `targets init` and backups are written 0600 (D142, D150, D151);
   `-` means stdout for downloads.
9. A `SECRET` adapter variable on argv is refused and `--variables-file` is added (D154).
10. The environment report is HTML only: Markdown is dropped and an explicit `--output` is a
    usage error (D155); the alternative keeps Markdown under a report-only `--format markdown`.
11. The report's `--debug` refusal is kept (TypeScript parity in exit code; the text drops the
    environment variable, D156).
12. One backup file per run, in an existing directory (default the working directory; no
    directory is created), with every credential as returned at 0600 and a warning (D151);
    the alternatives are one file per target, or withholding credentials (then restore cannot
    recreate targets).
13. `--file-format` stays with `json` only; `yaml` is a usage error (D151).
14. Restore refuses a backup from another TSG unless `--allow-other-tenant`, refuses duplicate
    and ambiguous names and withheld credentials before any write, and has `--dry-run` (D152).
15. Restore stops at the first write with an unknown outcome (the `profiles cleanup` rule, D110);
    the alternative continues with the next target.
16. The live write flow creates draft adapters only, on the assumption that a draft create
    (`validate=false`, no channel) contacts nothing external; if it does, the write flow has no
    resource type and is dropped. The live scan flow's smallest kind is one STATIC
    sub-category with a 20-minute default deadline (§10).

Resolved while fixing the 0.6 review:
17. Secret registration (§15.4): a value the redaction rules only guess at (a plain header
    value, an `auth_config` or `target_connection_config` field) joins the secret set only when
    it is at least 8 bytes long and not a `client_id`, `grant_type`, `scope` or `audience` (from
    1.0 nor a Vertex AI `project_id`, `location` or `engine_id` of a `target_connection_config`,
    §15.24 choice 12); known credentials (`SECRET` values, secret-named keys and headers) join
    whatever their length.
    It is still `[REDACTED]` in place. The alternative withholds every text containing any
    redacted value (names such as `prod chatbot` become `[withheld]` when a header says `prod`).
18. In a printed red team document every string under any key that contains a registered
    secret is `[withheld]` (exact containment; the server-text fields keep the §6 fragment
    rule, which elsewhere would withhold values such as `SECRET`).
19. `targets backup` stores a target whose credentials the service withheld as returned (masks
    included) with `credentialsWithheld: true` and a `⚠` summary row, counts it as backed up
    (exit 0, `complete` stays `true`), and prints the credentials warning only when the file
    holds a returned credential; restore refuses a marked or detected target by name before any
    write (D157). This replaces the earlier failed row, which made every backup of a real tenant
    fail, since the service masks the credentials of every credentialed target on GET.
20. Help texts are TypeScript's; the `Examples:` blocks that TypeScript lacks were removed
    (`redteam list`, `prompt-sets download`, the extra `report <jobId>` example) except where
    they show Rust-only options (`adapter create --variables-file`, `targets backup`,
    `targets restore`), §15.2.
21. Live tier (§10): a teardown listing that misses a created draft is a mismatch (the live
    test fails) after the draft is deleted by its id; a scan start whose outcome stays unknown
    after 5 listings a poll interval apart fails the run with a manual-abort message (no
    second scan, no abort of a scan the run cannot name).

The step-3 details recorded in §15.17–§15.18:
- The environment report's groups are sorted by the `localeCompare` approximation of §15.17
  "Labels" (lowercased first, then lowercase before uppercase, then code points).
- The `Backed up <n> target(s) to <path>:` section is printed whenever a file was written,
  also as `Backed up 0` when every target failed, so the path is always shown (§15.18).
- A token failure of the environment report is a failure of each source (`unavailable`, the
  file still written), not of the report (§15.17 "Client and token").
- The backup's per-target read was a raw read named `custom.read` in the `--debug` log (G10,
  §15.18); from 0.7 it is the typed `red_team.targets.get` without schema defaults.

### 15.23 scm-sdk 0.2.2 (0.9.1)

0.9.1 adopts scm-sdk 0.2.2 at the user's request. The pin becomes
`scm = { package = "scm-sdk", version = "=0.2.2", default-features = false, features = ["reqwest-transport", "scan", "management", "red-team", "dlp", "model-security"] }`.
The features are unchanged and `gateway` is not enabled (0.10 enables it at this pin, §19). In `Cargo.lock` only the `scm-sdk`
entry changes: the version and the checksum (`c908cad8…db7c`, from
`cargo update -p scm-sdk --precise 0.2.2`, measured). 0.2.x adds no dependency.
`serde_json/preserve_order` stays off, and every G10 call keeps
`RequestOptions::without_response_defaults()`. Every difference from the TypeScript CLI below
is a §12 row (D300–D307). The sources are the published crate
(`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/scm-sdk-0.2.2`) and the SDK repository's `CHANGELOG.md` (0.2.0, 0.2.1
and 0.2.2) and `docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md`.

**What 0.2.x changes for this CLI** (each point measured against the published source on the
0.9.0 tree with the pin moved, 2026-10-19):
1. **Responses (G25 closed).** See the G25 entry at the top of §15. A red team read whose answer
   holds a non-UUID id, a timestamp that is not RFC 3339 or an unlisted enum value succeeds on
   both CLIs. Unknown keys are kept, as before. The format relaxation is not limited to the red
   team data plane: it reaches every SDK response schema. Wherever a frozen TypeScript response
   schema declares a `uuid`, `datetime`, `email` or `url` format, TypeScript (and 0.9.0, whose
   scm-sdk 0.1.1 checked formats in response mode too) refuses an answer that breaks it, and
   airs-cli-rs now reads it. The adapter schemas are the measured case: `AdapterResponseSchema`
   and `AdapterListSchema` check `uuid`, `network_broker_channel_uuid`, `created_by_user_id` and
   `updated_by_user_id`, so an adapter listed with `created_by_user_id` `system` fails `adapter
   list` on TypeScript (`…data.0.created_by_user_id: invalid_string`, exit 1) and prints on
   airs-cli-rs. `adapter get`, the create and update answers and the environment report's
   adapter walk behave the same way. Rust is more lenient than TypeScript there (D306, choice
   21).
2. **Caller UUID checks.** All 76 `common::uuid` sites are kept. Every SDK method the CLI calls
   already had its check in 0.1.1 (61 sites; `grep -rho 'common::uuid(' src/airs/red_team | wc -l`
   in the pinned registry source gives 61 for 0.1.1 and 76 for 0.2.2). The 15 new sites belong to operations the CLI does
   not call: the four verdict overrides, static and dynamic ASR, regenerate, report status,
   runtime profile, error-log download and the V2 download URL. D141 already refuses every
   user-supplied id before the tenant (the inventory below), so nothing new reaches the SDK
   check. An id the server returns and the CLI sends back is not checked by the CLI. With 0.1.1
   the read itself refused such an id wherever the frozen TypeScript response schema declares a
   format; from 0.2.2 the read accepts it (point 1) and the SDK refuses it only when it is sent
   back. That covers the scan wait's `uuid`, the `targets backup` listing's `uuid` and restore's
   existing-target `uuid`. A non-UUID one fails in the SDK as `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Validation error`:
   the scan wait reports it with the §15.6 detail line, and the backup row and the restore row
   fail (exit 1). Choice 7 covers this. The one stored value a write copies into a format-checked
   body field is `adapter update`'s `network_broker_channel_uuid` (when `--channel` is not
   given), which the PUT body checks as a UUID: the CLI refuses a non-UUID one after the read
   and before the PUT, naming the field and `--channel` (D307, choice 22). `adapter validate
   --adapter` copies only the stored variables, whose key bound and `VAR`/`SECRET` type the
   response schema still enforces, so no stored value can break its body.
3. **Refused query options.** The SDK refuses 12 options before transport. The CLI sends only
   two of them: `skip` and `search` of `get_target_profile_error_logs`, from `targets error-logs
   --offset` and `--search` (D300). `report --attacks` sends `limit` and `severity` of
   `list_attacks` and `limit` of `list_custom_attacks`, never `search`. The environment report
   calls `get_scan_statistics` with no option. The CLI never calls `list_goal_streams`,
   `get_prompt_sets`, `get_prompts_by_set` or `get_error_logs`. No refused option was ever sent
   by default, so the CLI drops no value silently and no output changes for want of one.
4. **Query values.** The changelog's table leaves this out. Every data-plane query is validated
   in request mode against the vendor 0.93.0 query schema (`common::current_query`) before
   authentication. For the values the CLI sends, the schema requires:
   - `list_jobs`: `limit` from 1 to 100, `skip` an integer of at least 0, `status` one of
     `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, `PARTIALLY_COMPLETE`, `FAILED` or `ABORTED`, `job_type`
     one of `STATIC`, `DYNAMIC`, `CUSTOM` or `CLARA`, and `target_id` a UUID;
   - `list_attacks`: `limit` from 1 to 100 and `severity` one of `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH` or
     `CRITICAL`;
   - `list_custom_attacks`: `limit` from 1 to 1,000;
   - `list_error_logs_for_target_profile`: `limit` from 1 to 100 and nothing else.

   Enums are exact and case-sensitive, and an empty string fails them. The management-plane
   modules (`adapters`, `custom_attacks`, `eula`, `instances`, `network_broker`, `targets`) are
   byte-identical to 0.1.1, so their lists keep the §15.3 rules. The environment report sends
   page size 15 and no filter, which is valid.
5. **Request bodies.** `scans().create` validates the body against the vendor `create_job` body:
   `name` must have 3 to 255 code points, `target.uuid` must be a UUID, `job_type` comes from the
   vendor enum, and DYNAMIC `stream_depth` and `stream_breadth` must each be 1 to 20. The CLI's
   own `JobCreateRequest::parse` (the frozen TypeScript schema, which counts UTF-16 units) still
   runs first (§15.6 step 3). STATIC `categories` pass with any keys and sub-category ids,
   unknown ones and the server catalogue's included (measured). An empty `custom_prompt_sets`
   also passes, but the CLI never sends one. `abort` sends no body. No other data-plane body
   comes from user input.
6. **Typed fields.** 0.2.0 adds 55 optional typed fields to existing red team models. The CLI
   builds no red team model with a struct literal: the 0.9.0 tree compiles unchanged and clippy
   is clean (measured). The normalisers read the re-serialised JSON, and omitted fields stay
   omitted (projections keep their raw value), so no printed document changes.
7. **User agent.** Requests carry `PAN-AIRS/0.2.2-rust-sdk` in 0.9.1–0.11; `0.2.3` from 1.0
   (§15.24 point 8). The debug log shows it, and so do the `tests/debug.rs` and
   `tests/parity_debug.rs` expectations, the §2.9 example and the README example.
8. **0.2.1** adds the gateway access-policy APIs, which are out of scope: the TypeScript CLI
   has no such commands and `gateway` stays disabled (0.10 enables `gateway` and still leaves the access-policy
   API unused, §19 choice 135).

**Affected commands** (every check is a usage error: exit 2, before the debug log and the
tenant, nothing sent, the §15.3 validation order; messages name the argument and a short
reason, never the value):

| Command | Argument / option | SDK check (0.2.2) | CLI behaviour | Message | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redteam targets error-logs <targetId>` | `--offset <n>`, any value (`0` included, not parsed) | `skip` refused before transport | refused when given (D300) | `--offset is not supported for target error logs (the red team API accepts only --limit)` | 2 |
| `redteam targets error-logs <targetId>` | `--search <text>`, any value (`""` included) | `search` refused before transport | refused when given (D300) | `--search is not supported for target error logs (the red team API accepts only --limit)` | 2 |
| `redteam targets error-logs <targetId>` | `--limit <n>` | `limit` 1–100 | the existing TypeScript-text positive check, then above 100 refused (D301) | `--limit must be at most 100 (the red team API maximum)` | 2 |
| `redteam list\|ls` | `--limit <n>` (the one page and the `--all` page size) | `limit` 1–100 | the existing check, then above 100 refused (D301) | `--limit must be at most 100 (the red team API maximum)` | 2 |
| `redteam list\|ls` | `--status <status>` | `status` enum | after the filter rule, a non-empty value outside the six refused; `""` still sends nothing (D302) | `--status must be one of QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE, FAILED, ABORTED` | 2 |
| `redteam list\|ls` | `--type <type>` | `job_type` enum | after the filter rule, a non-empty value outside the four refused; `""` sends nothing (D302) | `--type must be one of STATIC, DYNAMIC, CUSTOM, CLARA` | 2 |
| `redteam list\|ls` | `--target <uuid>` | `target_id` UUID | after the filter rule, a non-empty non-UUID refused; `""` sends nothing (D302) | `--target must be a target UUID` | 2 |
| `redteam report <jobId>` | `--limit <n>` with `--attacks` | `list_attacks` `limit` 1–100 (`list_custom_attacks` 1–1,000) | the existing check, then above 100 refused for every job type, although a DYNAMIC job sends no limit (choice 20); without `--attacks` unused, as before (D301) | `--limit must be at most 100 (the red team API maximum)` | 2 |
| `redteam report <jobId>` | `--severity <level>` with `--attacks` | `severity` enum | after the filter rule, any value outside the four (`""` included) refused for every job type, although only a STATIC job sends it (choice 20); without `--attacks` unused, filter rule only, as before (D303) | `--severity must be one of LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL` | 2 |
| `redteam scan` | `--depth <number>`, `--breadth <number>` | `stream_depth`, `stream_breadth` 1–20 | §15.6 check 7, then above 20 refused (D304) | `--depth must be at most 20 (the red team API maximum)` (`--breadth` alike) | 2 |
| `redteam scan` | `--name <name>` | `name` 3–255 code points | §15.6 check 2 also needs at least 3 code points; the 255-unit maximum stays (D305) | `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for POST /v1/scan did not match schema: name: too_small` | 2 |

Unchanged, because the CLI check already equals or is stricter than the SDK's:
- `scan --target` (§15.6 check 3), `scan --type` (check 1, `CLARA` refused), `scan --prompt-sets`
  (check 8).
- `list --offset` (0 to 2^53 − 1).
- The ids of the inventory below (D141, with the TypeScript texts, which name the field and echo
  the value through `terminal_safe`).
- Every management-plane option.

**UUID inventory** (user-supplied ids that reach a UUID-checked SDK method; every one is checked
by D141 first):

| SDK method (checked argument) | CLI argument | D141 `<field>` |
|---|---|---|

**Help texts.** Only the two refused flags change. `targets error-logs` keeps `--offset <n>` and
`--search <text>` in its help. `--offset` reads `Not supported by the red team API (refused; use
--limit)`, because `--limit` still pages; `--search` reads `Not supported by the red team API
(refused)`, because no option replaces a text search (choice 23). Every other help text stays TypeScript's (`list --status` keeps TypeScript's list of
five values). `help_texts_match_typescript` gets these two lines as named exceptions.

**Tests** (COMPATIBILITY.md §4 rows D300–D307 cite them):
- One `dNN_` test per row, in the `divergence` module of the matching parity file, asserting
  both sides: TypeScript sends the value (the fixture's request log), while airs-cli-rs exits 2
  with the message, an empty stdout, no request and no tenant read. `d300_` and `d301_` go in
  `tests/parity_redteam_reads.rs` (D301's `report` half in `tests/parity_redteam_reports.rs`),
  `d302_` in `tests/parity_redteam_reads.rs`, `d303_` in `tests/parity_redteam_reports.rs`,
  `d304_` and `d305_` in `tests/parity_redteam_writes.rs`. The executable tests in
  `tests/redteam_reads.rs`, `redteam_reports.rs` and `redteam_writes.rs` also pin both
  boundaries: `--limit 100`, `--depth 20`, the six statuses and `CLARA` are sent, and `101`
  and `21` are refused. `walks_and_filters_send_the_typescript_requests` and
  `requests::error_logs_send_only_the_given_query` drop `--offset` and `--search` from their
  error-logs case and keep `--limit`.
- A contract guard, `src/redteam/contract_tests.rs` (unit tests). Each vocabulary and bound the
  CLI accepts passes `scm::validation::parse(<vendor query or body schema>, …, Mode::Request)`,
  and the first value past each bound is refused. A later pin that tightens the contract then
  fails here, before an SDK error could reach a user.
- G25 closure: `tests/redteam_reads.rs::g25::opaque_ids_dates_and_new_enum_values_are_read`
  seeds a `redteam list` job with `uuid` `job-1`, `target_id` `t-1`, `created_at`
  `2026-10-17 10:00:00` and `status` `PROFILING`, and a `targets error-logs` log with `job_id`
  `job-1`, `created_at` `2026-01-05 00:00:00` and `error_type` `SOMETHING_NEW`. Both reads exit 0
  and print the values unchanged in json and pretty.
  `tests/redteam_reports.rs::g25::attack_lists_keep_opaque_ids` covers a `report <jobId>
  --attacks` answer whose attacks carry `prompt_id` `p-1` and `prompt_mapping_id` `map-1`, and a
  CUSTOM job's custom attack with `prompt_id` `cp-1` and `prompt_set_id` `set-1`, whose json row
  (`promptId` `cp-1`) and pretty preview and goal lines are asserted.
  `tests/parity_redteam_reads.rs::parity::g25_opaque_response_values_match_typescript` asserts
  that both CLIs agree on the first two. These tests are the only fixtures that keep opaque ids.
- D306, D307 (found in review): `tests/parity_redteam_reads.rs::divergence::d306_adapter_answers_are_read_without_format_checks`
  seeds an adapter with `created_by_user_id` and `updated_by_user_id` `system` and channel
  `chan-1`: TypeScript's `adapter list` and `adapter get` exit 1 with
  `AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION`, and airs-cli-rs prints both, with the same requests.
  `tests/parity_redteam_writes.rs::divergence::d307_a_stored_channel_that_is_not_a_uuid_is_named`
  and `tests/redteam_writes.rs::adapters::update_refuses_a_stored_channel_that_is_not_a_uuid_d307`
  pin the `adapter update` refusal after the read (only the GET sent), the update with

  `tests/parity_redteam_reports.rs::divergence::d303_attack_values_are_checked_whatever_the_job_type`
  pins choice 20 on the CUSTOM and DYNAMIC jobs.
- Fixture ids: the remaining non-UUID red team response ids switch to fixed UUIDs from the
  fixture helpers. Those are the error log's `job_id` `job-1` (`fixtures_redteam.rs::error_log`,
  and the strings that print it) and the custom attacks' `prompt_id` `cp-1`, `cp-2`. Instance

**Built (0.9.1).** The spec planned two chunks, the pin with the D300–D305 checks and then the
G25 closure. They landed together in one change, because the pin alone fails the two
error-logs tests, with the checks green (a fresh `cargo clean -p airs-cli` build,
`AIRS_REQUIRE_PARITY=1`, no `PARITY SKIPPED` line). The change:
- bumps the pin and the lock, and updates the user-agent expectations, the §2.9 and README debug
  examples and the pin mentions in AGENTS.md and README;
- adds the D300–D305 checks to the planning code (`src/commands/redteam.rs`,
  `src/redteam/mod.rs`, `src/redteam/args.rs`) and the two help texts (`src/cli.rs`), and the
  D307 check (`carried_channel` in `src/commands/redteam_adapters.rs`);
- adds the contract guard, the executable and `dNN_` parity tests for D300–D307, and updates the
  two error-logs tests; COMPATIBILITY.md §4 rows D300–D307 cite them;
- switches the fixture ids, adds the three G25 tests (cited in COMPATIBILITY.md §3.16), and
  records G25 closed in README and the 0.9.1 MILESTONES row.

The helpers are `rt::at_most`, `rt::check_one_of`, `rt::vocabulary_filter`,
`rt::target_filter`, `rt::attack_list_args`, `rt::refuse_option` and `rt::bounded_list_params`
(`src/redteam/mod.rs`), with the vocabularies `JOB_STATUSES`, `LIST_JOB_TYPES`, `SEVERITIES` and
the bounds `MAX_PAGE` (100), `MAX_STREAM` (20). `RtPlan::ErrorLogs` carries only `limit`, and
`targets::error_logs` sends only `limit`. The check order the table leaves open (choices 14–17)
and the extra fixture switch (choice 18) were settled while building. The review settled choices
20–23 (the job-type note on D301 and D303, D306, D307 and the `--search` help text) and gave
choices 13 and 19 their rejected alternatives. The version bump, release notes and release are
the orchestrator's.

**SDK gaps.**
- **G60 (0.9.1, not blocking).** SDK request validation errors carry no field: a refused
  query value, refused option or body field is reported only as
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Validation error`, so the CLI cannot name the argument from
  the error. The CLI therefore checks every user-controlled value against the 0.93.0 contract
  itself (the table above), and the contract guard keeps those checks in step with the pinned
  SDK.

**Choices decided.**
1. `targets error-logs --offset` and `--search` are kept as flags and refused whenever given,
   `--offset 0` and `--search ""` included (D300). Rejected: removing the flags, which would give
   scripts clap's generic `unexpected argument` with no reason. Also rejected: dropping them
   silently or filtering client-side, which TypeScript never did and which would show a
   different page than asked for.
2. The `--limit` bound is 100 for `report --attacks` on every job type, checked before the
   tenant (D301), although `list_custom_attacks` allows 1,000. Rejected: allowing 1,000 and
   refusing a static job's 101–1,000 after the job read, which would be a usage error after
   requests (D2). Also rejected: clamping, which would print fewer attacks than asked for
   without saying so.
3. `report`'s new `--limit` and `--severity` checks apply only with `--attacks`, the only case in
   which a value can be sent; without it both stay accepted and unused (TS parity, §15.16).
   Rejected: checking them always, which would refuse commands that read no attack list at
   all. With `--attacks` the checks apply to every job type, including those whose call does
   not send the value (choice 20).
4. `report --attacks --severity ""` is a usage error (D303). Rejected: treating it as no filter.
   TypeScript sends `severity=`, so either choice differs from TypeScript, and an explicit
   empty value is more likely a script fault than a request for every severity.
5. The list filter vocabularies are the vendor's (`PARTIALLY_COMPLETE` and `CLARA` accepted),
   exact and case-sensitive, and `""` keeps sending nothing (D302). Rejected: TypeScript's help
   lists (five statuses, three types), which would refuse values the API serves. Also rejected:
   upper-casing input, because the CLI never rewrites a filter.
6. The new messages name the flag and the API limit and never echo the value. The D141 id checks
   keep their TypeScript texts (`Invalid <field>: <value>`), which already name the field and
   pass the value through `terminal_safe`. Rejected: rewriting the D141 texts, which would
   break TypeScript-text parity pinned since 0.6 and gain nothing for safety.
7. Ids the server returns are not checked again before they are sent back (§15.23 point 2):
   a well-formed answer behaves as with 0.1.1, and a malformed id now fails when it is sent back
   instead of at the read. Rejected: a CLI check with its own message, because it would
   duplicate the SDK's refusal for a case no service has shown. The exception is `adapter
   update`'s stored channel (choice 22), a setting the user can replace with `--channel`.
8. `scan --name` must have at least 3 code points as well as 3 to 255 UTF-16 units (D305), so a
   name passes both the frozen TypeScript schema and the vendor body. Rejected: code points only,
   which would let a 128-emoji name pass the CLI and then fail `JobCreateRequest::parse` with
   exit 1.
9. `scan --depth` and `--breadth` above 20 are refused (D304). Rejected: clamping to 20, which
   would scan with settings other than those asked for.
10. Help texts change only for the two refused flags. Rejected: adding the API bounds to the
    `--limit`, `--status`, `--type`, `--depth` and `--breadth` help lines, which would break
    help parity with TypeScript for text the error message already gives.
11. The non-UUID fixture ids switch to fixed UUIDs, and opaque ids survive only in the dedicated
    G25 tests. Rejected: keeping `job-1` and `cp-1` scattered through unrelated tests, where they
    would cover G25 only by accident.
12. The live tier is unchanged. Rejected: adding a live `targets error-logs` read, because the
    tenant has no error logs (G25) and so the read would prove nothing.
13. No new SDK gap blocks 0.9.1. G60 (above) is a limitation handled CLI-side. Rejected:
    treating G60 as blocking, or waiting for an SDK whose validation errors name the field,
    because the CLI's own checks already name every argument before the SDK sees it.
14. `targets error-logs` checks, in order: `--limit` (the TypeScript-text positive rule, then
    at most 100), `--offset` refused, `--search` refused, then the `<targetId>` UUID (D141). A
    refused option is therefore reported before a bad id, as the other option checks already
    were. Rejected: checking the id first, which would make `error-logs t-1 --search x` name the
    id while the option is refused whatever the id.
15. `redteam list` checks each filter's rule and then its vocabulary (`--status`, `--type`,
    `--target`, in that order), then `--limit` (positive, then at most 100, inside
    `bounded_list_params` before `--offset`). Rejected: all filter rules first, then all
    vocabularies, which reports a later flag's control character before an earlier flag's
    unknown value.
16. `scan --depth` is checked whole (positive, then at most 20) before `--breadth`. Rejected:
    both positive rules first, which would report `--breadth 0` before `--depth 21`.
17. `report <jobId>` checks `--limit` (positive, then at most 100 with `--attacks`) before
    `--severity` (the filter rule, then the vocabulary with `--attacks`), the existing order.
    Rejected: checking `--severity` first, which would reorder the 0.6 checks for no gain.
18. The static attack fixture's `prompt_id` and `prompt_mapping_id` (`p-<n>`, `map-<n>`) also
    switch to fixed UUIDs (`prompt_id(n)`, `uuid(950 + n)`), as do the custom attacks'
    (`prompt_id(1)`, `prompt_id(2)`), so the G25 tests are the only red team fixtures with
    opaque ids (choice 11). Rejected: leaving the attack ids, which the list above omitted.
19. The G25 parity test compares pretty bytes for `list` and `targets error-logs` and json for
    `list` only, because TypeScript ignores `--output` for error logs (D144). Rejected:
    comparing json for error logs as well, which would fail on D144 rather than on G25.
20. `report <jobId> --attacks` checks `--severity` against the four severities and `--limit`
    against 100 for every job type, before the tenant, although TypeScript sends `--severity`
    only for a STATIC job (`list_attacks`), sends `--limit` only for STATIC and CUSTOM jobs
    (`list_custom_attacks` takes no severity) and lists no attacks for a DYNAMIC job. The job
    type is known only after the job read, so `report <customJob> --attacks --severity high`
    and `report <dynamicJob> --attacks --limit 500`, which succeed on TypeScript and on 0.9.0,
    are usage errors from 0.9.1 (D301, D303). Rejected: checking each value after the job read,
    only for the job types that send it, which would make a usage error follow requests (D2)
    and make the same arguments valid or not depending on the job. Pinned by
    `tests/parity_redteam_reports.rs::divergence::d303_attack_values_are_checked_whatever_the_job_type`.
21. Response formats are not checked anywhere, so airs-cli-rs reads answers that TypeScript's
    zod schemas refuse on a format (D306; the adapter case is pinned by
    `tests/parity_redteam_reads.rs::divergence::d306_adapter_answers_are_read_without_format_checks`).
    Rejected: a CLI-side format check to keep TypeScript parity, which would bring back the G25
    failure (a whole read fails on a value the user cannot change) and need a per-schema format
    inventory that the pinned SDK no longer enforces.
22. `adapter update` without `--channel` refuses a stored `network_broker_channel_uuid` that is
    not a UUID after the read and before the PUT, exit 1 (the stored data is at fault, not the
    arguments), with a fixed message that names the field and `--channel` and never echoes the
    value (D307). Rejected: TypeScript's text (`AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION:…invalid_string`),
    which would report a response failure the CLI did not have and offer no remedy. Also
    rejected: leaving the refusal to the body check, whose `Request body for PUT … did not match
    schema` blames a body the user never supplied; and leaving the channel out of the body,
    which could detach the adapter from its channel without being asked.
23. `targets error-logs --search` has its own help text, `Not supported by the red team API
    (refused)`, while `--offset` keeps `(refused; use --limit)`. `--limit` replaces an offset
    as the way to page, but nothing replaces a text search. Rejected: one shared text, whose
    `use --limit` hint would point a `--search` user at an option that does not search.

### 15.24 scm-sdk 0.2.3 (1.0)

1.0 adopts scm-sdk 0.2.3 (published 2026-10-20), the AIRS red team management 0.86.0 update. The pin becomes
`scm = { package = "scm-sdk", version = "=0.2.3", default-features = false, features = ["reqwest-transport", "scan", "management", "red-team", "dlp", "model-security", "gateway", "agentguard"] }`.
The features are unchanged. In `Cargo.lock` only the `scm-sdk` entry changes: the version and the checksum
(`80a58b7b…e809`, from `cargo update -p scm-sdk --precise 0.2.3 --offline`, measured); its dependency list and every
other entry are unchanged, so 0.2.3 adds no dependency. `serde_json/preserve_order` stays off, every G10 call keeps
`RequestOptions::without_response_defaults()`, and the G25 relaxation of 0.2.2 is retained (response validation
checks no string format and no `regex` check, as in 0.2.2, so the three new Vertex AI request patterns are not
enforced on answers). Every difference from the TypeScript CLI below is a
§12 row (D327–D329, and D35 extended). The source is the published crate
(`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/scm-sdk-0.2.3`, read only) against 0.2.2.

**What 0.2.3 changes for this CLI** (each point measured on the 1.0 tree with the pin moved, 2026-10-20):
1. **The diff.** `diff -rq` of the two published crates lists only the README, NOTICE and Cargo metadata,
   `examples/` (`live_qualification` gains `--read-only`; the new offline `red_team_management` example),
   `src/airs/red_team/targets.rs`, `src/models/{generated,mod,red_team}.rs`, the new
   `src/models/red_team_management.rs`, `src/validation.rs` (three request patterns),
   `src/validation/schema_graph.json` and `src/fixtures/model-regressions.json`. The scan, management, DLP,
   model-security, gateway and AgentGuard modules, the transport, the engine and the authentication are
   byte-identical, so every statement §16–§21 make on 0.2.2 holds on 0.2.3 (the gateway, AgentGuard and debug
   behaviour included; the full parity suite is green on the new pin with only the user agent changed).
2. **Target list query.** `TargetListOptions` gains `profiling_status` (`NOT_STARTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`,
   `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`, checked before authentication), and the legacy `status` is documented as `DRAFT` and
   `ACTIVE` only. The CLI sets neither: `targets list`, the backup and restore listings and the environment report
   send `skip` and `limit` only, so no request changes (choice 4).
3. **Request bodies.** The frozen `TargetCreateRequestSchema`, `TargetUpdateRequestSchema` and
   `TargetProbeRequestSchema` are widened, never narrowed: `connection_type` adds `VERTEX_AI` and `N8N`,
   `response_mode` adds `REALTIME`, `connection_params.multi_turn_config` adds `{"type": "client_session"}` and
   `connection_params.target_connection_config` adds the Vertex AI object (`project_id`
   `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, `location` `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, `engine_id` `^[0-9]+$`, `customer_sa_email` any string,
   unknown keys allowed). No schema node was removed or tightened, so every body 0.2.2 accepted is still accepted.
   The new typed fields (`basic_username`, `basic_password`, `audio_request_json`, `audio_curl`) have no schema
   node: the frozen objects pass them through as before, any JSON value included. `TargetContextUpdate` and the
   `validate-auth` body are unchanged. TypeScript refuses the four new values (D328); the CLI sends them (choice 2).
   A Vertex AI field outside its pattern, a server mask included, fails the body check with the D116 text before
   the tenant is used (exit 1, nothing sent).
4. **Responses.** `TargetResponseSchema` takes the same widening, without the request patterns, so a target with a
   Vertex AI config (masked or not) or the `client_session` config is read where 0.11 and TypeScript refused the
   answer (D329). The list row schema holds these fields as plain strings on both SDKs: the listing is unchanged
   (`management_0_86_listings_match_typescript`). `TargetResponseSchema` never checked the `connection_type` and
   `response_mode` vocabularies, so a target whose answer carries `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N` or `REALTIME` without either
   new config was already read by 0.11 (`targets get` unchanged), but its backup projection failed 0.2.2's create
   schema: 0.11 recorded the failed row `its settings do not match the target create schema` and exited 1. The
   widened create schema (point 3) accepts it, so from 1.0 such a target is stored (D329; TypeScript stores it
   too, under D151).
5. **Typed decoding and key order.** The four new fields decode as `Patch` values with a raw fallback (a value of
   another type stays an unknown key), so every printed value is the server's. Printed documents keep the
   serialiser's order (§15.12): the new fields follow the declared ones in contract order (`audio_request_json`,
   `audio_curl`; `basic_username`, `basic_password`) ahead of the sorted unknown keys, where 0.11 sorted them among
   the unknown keys (D35, extended). Backup files store nested settings sorted (§15.18), unchanged.
6. **Secrets.** `audio_curl` is a curl template and gets §15.4 rule 3 (D327; `redteam::secrets`, one match arm).
   The basic credentials are `auth_config` strings (rule 1) and the Vertex AI fields `target_connection_config`
   strings (rule 4), so they were already redacted by the existing rules, which the unit test now pins (choice 3).
   The identifiers `project_id`, `location` and `engine_id` are no longer registered (choice 12), so the endpoint,
   name and description that hold them print; `customer_sa_email` still registers by the length rule, and a
   secret-named key registers under any key (choice 14). `audio_request_json` is printed like `request_json`
   (choice 6).
7. **Struct literals and names.** The CLI builds no target model with a struct literal: the tree compiles
   unchanged and clippy is clean (measured). The debug operation names (`red_team.targets.*`) are unchanged.
8. **User agent.** Requests carry `PAN-AIRS/0.2.3-rust-sdk` (the §2.9 example, README, `tests/debug.rs`,
   `tests/parity_debug.rs`, `tests/gateway_inventory.rs`).

**Affected commands** (everything else is byte-identical; the full parity suite is the proof):

| Command | Behaviour from 1.0 | Row |
|---|---|---|
| `targets create\|update\|probe --config` | the 0.86.0 values are sent as given; a Vertex AI field outside its pattern is the D116 refusal (exit 1, nothing sent) | D328 |
| `targets restore` | a stored body with the 0.86.0 values passes the file check and is sent | D328 |
| `targets get`; the `create`, `update`, `probe` and `update-profile` answers | a Vertex AI or `client_session` target is read and printed, redacted; its endpoint, name and description print although they hold the redacted identifiers (choice 12) | D329 |
| the same, and an error log's `target_object` | `audio_curl` is `[REDACTED]` whole, its credentials registered | D327 |
| `targets backup` | a Vertex AI target is stored (masks in `customer_sa_email`: `credentialsWithheld`); a mask in a patterned field is a failed row naming the masked fields and the remedy (choices 7, 13); the credentials warning ignores the identifiers (choice 12); a target carrying `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N` or `REALTIME`, which 0.11 read but recorded as the create-schema failed row (exit 1), is stored (point 4) | D329, D157 |
| every printed target document | the 0.86.0 fields in contract order after the declared fields | D35 |
| `targets list`, the environment report, every other command | unchanged | none |

**Tests** (COMPATIBILITY.md §3.16–§3.19 and §4 rows D327–D329 cite them). Fixtures in the 0.86.0 shapes (the SDK

additions; markers 36–38), both outside the default dataset (choice 11).
- `src/redteam/contract_tests.rs::management_0_86_target_contract`: the contract guard for the three request

**Built (1.0).** One change: the pin and the lock; the user-agent expectations and examples; the `audio_curl` arm
of rule 3 (`src/redteam/secrets.rs`); the live check; the fixtures, the unit, executable and parity tests above;
§12 rows D327–D329 and the D35 and D140 extensions; §15.4, §15.13, §15.18 and §10 notes; README, AGENTS.md,
COMPATIBILITY.md and MILESTONES. The version bump and release are the orchestrator's. Fixed after the chunk's
review, in three rounds: the identifiers' registration (choice 12: an identifier string directly under the config,
its embedded credentials still registered, `redteam::secrets::identifier`), a secret-named key registering under any
key (choice 14, which closes the regression the first round's version opened), the named failed-row reason with its
remedy (choice 13: `redteam::backup::create_schema_reason`, the placeholders in `VERTEX_AI_IDS` and the contract
guard; `render::join_and`, moved from `gateway::provision`), the camelCase scope of rules 2–5 (choice 15), the
fixture's endpoint and description, the README and MILESTONES backup caveat, the §15.23 and §19 user-agent tenses,
and the tests marked above.

**SDK gaps.** None opened (G72 stays unused). Re-checked on 0.2.3: G60 holds (request validation errors still name
no field; the CLI's own checks of §15.23 are unchanged and the contract guard still passes), G10 is handled as
before, G25 stays closed, G71 is unchanged (AgentGuard is byte-identical).

**Choices decided.**
1. 1.0 ships on `=0.2.3` with the same features. Rejected: shipping 1.0 on 0.2.2, which fails every read of a
   Vertex AI or `client_session` target (a decode error) and every backup of one, on the release meant to be the
   stable line.
2. The 0.86.0 request values are accepted as the pinned SDK accepts them, with no CLI vocabulary check (D328).
   Rejected: refusing them for TypeScript parity, which would refuse targets the service creates and serves. Also
   rejected: a CLI check that names the Vertex AI field outside its pattern; a `--config` body is reported with
   the D116 text like every other body (G60), and the patterns are listed in point 3.
3. All four Vertex AI fields stay redacted under rule 4 (the three identifiers without registration, choice 12).
   Rejected: keeping `project_id`, `location` and `engine_id` like `region` and `model_id`, because the vendor
   declares a masked response shape for this config (`VertexAIConnectionRedactParams`), so the service treats them
   as sensitive, and the CLI never prints what the service masks.
4. No `--profiling-status` (or `--status`) flag on `targets list`. Rejected: adding one: TypeScript has none, the
   listing is walked whole and sliced client-side (D147), and 1.0 adds no command surface.
5. `audio_curl` is redacted whole like `curl`, only its extracted credentials registered (D327). Rejected:
   printing it as TypeScript does, because the template carries the target's headers, keys included. Also
   rejected: registering it whole, which would withhold every name inside the template (§15.4 "Structured values").
6. `audio_request_json` is printed like `request_json` (rule 7 inside it). Rejected: redacting it whole, which
   would hide the request template TypeScript prints while rule 7 already catches its secret-named keys.
7. A backup read whose Vertex AI field breaks its request pattern (a server mask) stays a failed row (its reason
   names the masked fields, choice 13). Rejected: storing it marked `credentialsWithheld`, because restore requires
   every stored target to pass the create schema, so one such entry would make the whole file unrestorable.
8. The new key order is recorded on D35, not in a new row. Rejected: a new row, because D35's rule (model fields
   in schema order, unknown keys sorted) already describes it.
9. No new SDK gap. Rejected: opening G72 for the masked Vertex AI shape; the patterns are the vendor's request
   contract and the CLI's handling of a masked target is defined (choice 7).
10. `targets init` keeps TypeScript's provider list. Rejected: `VERTEX_AI` and `N8N` scaffolds, which TypeScript
    does not have; `targets templates` already prints the service's templates.
11. The 0.86.0 fixtures are seeded only by the tests that need them. Rejected: adding them to the default dataset,
    where TypeScript refuses the Vertex AI answer and every existing listing, backup and report count would change.
12. A Vertex AI identifier string (`project_id`, `location` or `engine_id`, directly under `target_connection_config`,
    matched case-sensitively; `redteam::secrets::VERTEX_AI_IDS`) is `[REDACTED]` in place but not registered itself;
    the credentials embedded in it still register (a URL's userinfo and credential fields, and the credential after
    a `<scheme> ` prefix by the length rule, as for a plain header; `secrets::identifier`), and anything else keeps the length rule: the same names
    elsewhere (a `Location` header, an `auth_config.location`), in another case (`Project_Id`), deeper in the config
    or holding an object. The identifiers no longer count for the backup's credentials warning
    (`carries_credentials`), and `customer_sa_email` keeps the length rule. A real target's `api_endpoint`
    (`https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/us-central1/…`), name and
    description hold the identifiers; registered, `example-project` and `us-central1` made `views::withhold` print the
    endpoint and description as `[withheld]`, and the backup summary's fragment rule withheld every name that is a
    4-byte or longer fragment of them (`us-central1`, `central`). They are identifiers, not credentials, and the
    SDK's Vertex AI config is flat, so the exemption covers exactly its three strings and nothing a credential could
    hide in. A service account names the principal the service acts as, so its address stays registered; a real one
    holds the project (`<name>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com`), so a name that is exactly a fragment of it
    (`example-project`) is still withheld, which is accepted. Restore's withheld test (`secrets::withheld`) reads the
    rule paths, not the registration, so a mask in any of the four fields is still detected, and the backup still
    fails a patterned mask and stores a `customer_sa_email` mask with `credentialsWithheld` (choice 7). Rejected:
    adding the three names to `UNREGISTERED_KEYS`, which apply at any depth under rules 1, 2 and 4,
    case-insensitively, so a `Location` header's value or an `auth_config.location` would stop registering. Also
    rejected: the exemption at any depth inside the config (the second round's key list of the `all_strings` walk),
