    under which a credential in an identifier name's object or a nested `location` no longer registered; the first
    round's `Reg::Config`, a registration state that only meant "inside rule 4's config" and, inheriting `Never`, hid
    a credential nested under an identifier (choice 14); and printing the identifiers (choice 3 stands).
13. A backup read whose create-schema failure is a masked Vertex AI identifier names the masked fields and the
    remedy: `the service masked its Vertex AI project_id, which the target create schema refuses; recreate the
    target or set its identifiers by hand` (`location and engine_id` for two, `project_id, location and engine_id`
    for three, contract order, `render::join_and`). A field is masked when it holds `[REDACTED]` or four or more `*`
    (`redteam::backup::masked_vertex_ids`). The reason names the masks only when they alone fail the schema: the
    projection with each masked field replaced by its placeholder in `VERTEX_AI_IDS` (the smallest value of its
    pattern, `placeholder` or `0`; `backup::with_vertex_placeholders`) passes it (`backup::create_schema_reason`,
    pure, with the schema check passed in). Any other failure, a mask beside it included, keeps the §15.18 reason
    `its settings do not match the target create schema`. The contract guard runs the placeholders through the real
    `TargetCreateRequest::parse`, so a pattern change in a later pin fails there. The generic reason reads as a fault
    in the target or the CLI and hides that the service's own answer cannot be sent back; the remedy follows the
    house style of `WITHHELD_REASON`; the path is Rust-only (TypeScript refuses the answer, D329), so no parity text
    is at stake. Rejected: keeping the generic reason. Also rejected: naming the masks whenever one is present, which
    blames them for a projection that fails for another reason too.
14. A secret-named key (rule 7's names) registers its value as a known credential whatever key it is nested under:
    `Reg::under` checks the name before it inherits a non-registering parent. So `{"scope": {"token": …}}` in
    `auth_config`, a non-string `curl` holding a header map, and `{"location": {"api_key": …}}` in a config register
    the credential, and an echo of it elsewhere is `[withheld]`; the other values under such a key still do not
    register. Rule 7 cannot catch them, because it skips a value rule 1 or 4 already replaced, and the review found
    an echo printed in clear: the first round's version of choice 12 for the identifier case, and the
    `UNREGISTERED_KEYS` case before 1.0. Rejected: relying on choice 12's string-only scope alone, which closes the
    identifier case but not the `scope` one.
15. Rules 2–5 match only the snake_case keys inside `connection_params`; no camelCase `targetConnectionConfig`,
    `requestHeaders` or `apiEndpoint` form is added (§15.4 "Target"). Normalisation renames only the top-level keys
    and copies their values unchanged, and the API and the SDK model name the nested keys in snake_case, so a
    camelCase form inside `connection_params` comes from neither; rule 7 still reads its secret-named keys. Rejected:
    camelCase aliases for every nested rule, which would describe a shape no answer or normalised document has.

### 15.25 scm-sdk 0.2.4, the TypeScript 0.35.0 overlay (8.0)

8.0 adopts scm-sdk 0.2.4, the additive patch release that adds the final TypeScript SDK,
0.35.0 (`780c985`), as versioned schema roots (`typescript:0.35.0:`) beside the unchanged
0.34.0 baseline (the SDK's `docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md`, its offline example
`examples/directional_profiles.rs` and its CHANGELOG).

**The pin** (adopted 2026-10-22; 0.2.4 was published on crates.io at 2026-10-22T17:49Z
from the annotated tag `v0.2.4`, commit `6f18529a47cc273feca1000af6e4fc0d96da757e`):
`scm = { package = "scm-sdk", version = "=0.2.4", default-features = false, features = ["reqwest-transport", "scan", "management", "red-team", "dlp", "model-security", "gateway", "agentguard"] }`.
The features are unchanged; `management` (the profile clients) was already enabled.
`cargo update -p scm-sdk --precise 0.2.4` changed only the `scm-sdk` entry of
`Cargo.lock`: version 0.2.4, the crates.io source and checksum
`533294fe977e26e251e01dd2de64a896aa22ce45e97ac6264a0df6af879edd55`. Requests carry
`PAN-AIRS/0.2.4-rust-sdk` (§2.9, README, `tests/debug.rs`, `tests/parity_debug.rs`,
`tests/gateway_inventory.rs`). Before publication the tree built the exact Forgejo commit
`4825616ccf4c29272aff9a1ec3dcffb8b2e91535` of the overlay (branch
`feat/typescript-035-parity`, crate version 0.2.3, user agent `PAN-AIRS/0.2.3-rust-sdk`) as
a temporary git dependency; that line is gone, so nothing blocks `cargo publish` on it.

**The published crate against `4825616`** (checked 2026-10-22). The downloaded
`scm-sdk-0.2.4.crate` (the checksum above) names `6f18529` in `.cargo_vcs_info.json`; its
`src/**`, `examples/**`, `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` are byte-identical to `crates/scm-sdk` at
`v0.2.4`, and its `Cargo.toml.orig` is the tag's manifest. Between `4825616` and `v0.2.4`,
`crates/scm-sdk` changes only the manifest's `version` (0.2.3 → 0.2.4); the seven commits
between them change release documentation, receipts and tests outside the crate. So the
swap changes no behaviour of this CLI except the user agent; the full definition of done
ran again on it.

**What 0.2.4 changes for this CLI** (measured on the 8.0 tree):
1. **The diff.** Against tag `v0.2.3` (`14a6754`) the crate changes only
   `src/airs/management/profiles.rs` (create and update validate their body with
   `typescript:0.35.0:CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema` before authentication),
   `src/models/{generated,management}.rs` (the two new types and five fields),
   `src/validation/{schema_graph,semantics}.json` (the versioned roots),
   `src/fixtures/model-regressions.json`, its tests and the new offline example. The scan,
   red team, DLP, model-security, gateway and AgentGuard modules, the streaming and SSE
   decoder, the transport, the engine and the authentication are unchanged.
2. **Types.** `ContentTypeConfiguration` (`data-protection`, `app-protection`,
   `model-protection`, `agent-protection`) and `ContentTypeConfigurations` (`prompt`,
   `response`, `tool-call`, `tool-response`, unknown directions kept); `AiSecurityProfile`
   gains `content_type_mode` and `content_type_configurations`, `ModelConfiguration`
   `enable_full_conversation_inspection`, `SecurityProfile` and
   `CreateSecurityProfileRequest` `dlp_tenant_id`, all `Optional<T>`. The CLI builds no
   profile model with a struct literal, so the tree compiled unchanged. How the CLI carries
   them is §13.17 ("The scm-sdk 0.2.4 fields").
3. **Validation.** Existing model `parse` and `build_validated` methods keep their 0.34.0
   binding; the operation paths validate with the 0.35.0 root, which refuses an explicit
   `null` or a wrong type for the new fields and known directions, also through raw
   extensions. The CLI validates every profile body with the same root itself
   (`policy::request_body`, `validation::parse`), before the tenant where it can, so the
   SDK's own refusal is never what a user sees (§13.17). Responses keep 0.34.0's tolerant
   binding in both response modes: unknown fields, directions and modes and invalid values
   of the new fields survive in extensions (D334).
4. **Response defaults (G10).** No schema reachable from a profile carries a default except
   the list's `ai_profiles: []` (also through the versioned alias `s_ts035_s009653`; the
   graph walked from `SecurityProfileSchema`, `PolicySchema`, `AiSecurityProfileSchema`,
   `ModelConfigurationSchema`, `CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema` and their
   `typescript:0.35.0:` roots reaches no other `ZodDefault`), and an absent list already
   reads as empty, so nothing printed depends on it. Still, from the 0.2.4 gap closure
   **every profile read** runs without the defaults, on every page: `profiles list` (one
   page: `runtime::options`, the 60 s budget `None` gave), `list --all`, `get` and its
   walks (`get_by_name`, `--all-versions`), the `profiles update|delete` lookups, the
   profile read of `topics apply|revert` and the `profiles cleanup` listings
   (`commands::profile_walk_options`; the deadlines are as before: one 300 s deadline
   shared by the token and the walk for `list --all`, `get` and the update and delete
   lookups, while `profiles cleanup` keeps its token's deadline and gives each listing, the
   first and the re-check after the confirmation, its own), plus the backup (§18.15),
   restore (§18.16) and report (§18.13) reads that already did. Every profile write
   (`profiles create|update`, the `topics apply|revert` PUTs, whose answers are discarded,
   and the restore's writes) builds per attempt
   `runtime::request_options(SINGLE_REQUEST_BUDGET)` (no defaults, the same 60 s; one
   attempt and the single 401 replay unchanged, D95), so one rule covers every profile
   PUT and POST. Excluded with reason: the profile and topic deletes (their answers are
   neither printed nor kept), the topic walks (their `examples: []` default is
   TypeScript's output, G27) and the DLP reads (no default is reachable, §16 "G10 does not
   apply"). No output can show the option while no profile default is reachable, so the
   evidence is `src/commands/mod.rs::tests::profile_reads_and_writes_skip_the_response_defaults`
   (the options, and the SDK half: the option keeps an absent `ai_profiles` absent and a
   directional record reads identically in both modes), the call-site guard
   `src/commands/mod.rs::tests::profile_call_sites_use_the_no_default_options` (no profile
   read or write in the profile commands passes `None` or the defaulted `walk_options()`)
   and the multi-page tests
   `tests/management.rs::sdk_0_2_4_pages` and
   `tests/runtime_transfer.rs::backup::directional_records_are_stored_losslessly_on_every_page`.
   **Faithful output.** `profiles backup` is the lossless path: it stores each record as
   the page carried it (unknown top-level keys, `csp_id`, `tsg_id`, explicit `null`s
   included). The `get`, `list`, `create` and `update` JSON stays the §7.5 projection,
   TypeScript's output: its `policy` is the complete SDK model with its extensions and
   `dlpTenantId` falls back to the extension value (D334), but unknown top-level keys are
   dropped there by contract. G25 is unchanged: response ids, timestamps, unknown enum
   strings and object keys stay accepted, and the CLI adds no UUID or date check of a
   response document.
5. **Dependencies.** 0.2.4 adds no dependency and changes no feature or MSRV (1.89). Before
   the swap, following the SDK's RUSTSEC-2026-0382/0383 advisory for downstream lockfiles,
   `Cargo.lock` moved `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15 → 0.103.16 and `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.5 →
   1.0.10, the versions of the SDK's qualified lockfile. The audit of the resolved graph
   (2026-10-22, RustSec database `640bf5a9`): `cargo audit` reports no vulnerability on
   the 236 locked packages (the 1.0 lockfile, with 0.103.15 and 1.0.5, reports exactly
   those two advisories), and `cargo deny check advisories sources` passes (crates.io the
   only source; no git dependency is left). This repository configures no `deny.toml` or
   audit job; the policy it keeps is exact pins for new direct dependencies and no
   `serde_json/preserve_order`. Against the SDK's own qualified `Cargo.lock`, the CLI
   resolves every shared package at the same version except `schannel` (Windows only,
   0.1.30 here, 0.1.29 there).
6. **Status.** The SDK marks directional live acceptance unverified. This CLI's B7 live run
   (2026-10-22, `redtail-prod`) accepted every directional create, edit, topic, backup and
   restore operation on all four directions once the flag create wrote all four direction
   keys (D335); the service rules it found are listed in §13.17 and
   `docs/research/live-directional-profiles.md`.

**Workarounds, decided on 0.2.4** (both kept; neither is an SDK change):
- **The 0.35.0 request root.** 0.2.4's documentation (`DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md`,
  "Construction and current request validation") keeps the model `parse` and
  `build_validated` methods on their historical binding, and directs standalone callers to
  `validation::parse` with `typescript:0.35.0:<SchemaName>`. The CLI therefore keeps
  validating with the versioned root: `CreateSecurityProfileRequest::parse` alone accepts a
  `null` `dlp_tenant_id` that the create call then refuses
  (`src/policy.rs::tests::request_bodies_keep_the_directional_fields_as_given`). The new
  named schemas (`ContentTypeConfigurationSchema`, `ContentTypeConfigurationsSchema`) are
  reached through the request root and need no separate call.
- **The printed key order.** 0.2.4 serialises an AI entry and `model-configuration` in
  0.34.0 field order (the new fields last), where TypeScript SDK 0.35.0 prints
  `content-type-mode` and `content-type-configurations` before `model-configuration` and
  the protections first. The views keep reordering those two objects; the reorder moves
  keys only and drops none (`src/views.rs::tests::the_printed_policy_reorders_keys_and_drops_nothing`).

**Streaming and SSE.** The SDK's SSE decoder (`scm::streaming::sse`) and the typed
`ContractStream` date from 0.2.0 and are unchanged by 0.2.4. The only streamed responses
this CLI reads are `gateway inference chat|responses --stream` (§19.14), which already
consume `create_chat_completion_stream` and `create_response_stream`; the CLI keeps only
rendering, secret withholding and interruption. No command parses SSE or another streamed
format by hand (`DirectTransport` hands the SDK raw body chunks; `model-security install
--fetch-uv` reads a download, not an event stream), so nothing moved.

**Cumulative migrations.** The CLI adopted 0.2.3 in 1.0 (§15.24: the Vertex AI, N8N and
realtime values, the client-session config, the basic-auth and audio fields, with their
unknown-value fallbacks; `profiling_status` is reconciled without a flag, choice 4);
`targets error-logs --offset` and `--search` stay usage errors before the tenant (D300).
0.2.4 adds nothing to reconcile there. Pinned by the 0.2.4 gap closure:
- `profiling_status`: the CLI sends no profiling or status filter, so nothing is
  translated; answers carrying `NOT_STARTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or an
  unknown value are read by `targets list|get|backup`, and no view or backup prints the
  field (the TS projections, §15.18)
  (`tests/redteam_reads.rs::management_0_86::every_profiling_status_is_read_and_never_sent`,
  `tests/redteam_reports.rs::management_0_86::profiling_statuses_are_accepted_and_unknown_unions_fail_the_row`).
- The 0.86.0 unions are closed in the response schema on both SDKs: a `multi_turn_config`
  type or a `target_connection_config` shape that is no known branch fails the read (D38
  text, exit 1; a failed row in a backup), as TypeScript does; scm-sdk's typed `Unknown`
  fallback applies only to documents the schema accepts. The CLI keeps that check (the
  brief's retained required-field and type checks) and opens no gap: a future vendor branch
  needs an SDK release (`tests/parity_redteam_reads.rs::parity::unknown_union_shapes_are_refused_like_typescript`,
  `tests/redteam_reads.rs::management_0_86::unknown_union_shapes_fail_the_response_schema`).
- `targets error-logs --skip` (the API name) is no flag: clap's usage error (exit 2, D1)
  before the tenant (`tests/redteam_reads.rs::contract::an_error_log_skip_is_a_usage_error_before_the_tenant`).
- The `api.apps` defaults stay and no endpoint is rewritten: the CLI's red team and
  management defaults equal scm-sdk's, and a tenant's `api.sase` endpoint is used as
  written (`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/clients.rs::tests::red_team_endpoints_are_the_defaults_or_the_tenant_values_unchanged`).
- `serde_json` is built without `preserve_order` (`cargo tree -e features -i serde_json`:
  `default`, `raw_value`, `std`), guarded by
  `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/json.rs::tests::serde_json_is_built_without_preserve_order`.

## 16. M6b DLP (0.7)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-dlp.md` (cited as **TD§n**),
`docs/research/ts-dlp-backup.md` (cited as **TB§n**) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-dlp.md` (cited
as **DK§n**). This section overrides them where they differ; their provisional numbers and
recommendations are not binding. Every difference from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row
(D160–D178; D50, D52, D56 and D116 extended). The byte captures of the TypeScript layouts
are in TD§3–§11 and TB§4–§5; "the TS layout" below means those bytes, with the changes this
section lists.

**SDK.** scm-sdk 0.1.0 has every operation these commands need, with the TypeScript paths,
methods, queries and request and response schemas (DK§0, DK§4): **nothing in §16 is blocked
on scm-sdk.** The `dlp` feature is already compiled in (the CLI's `management` feature pulls
it in, `scm-sdk Cargo.toml:62-65`); 0.7 lists `"dlp"` explicitly in the `scm` dependency's
features (no lock-file change). The findings of DK§9 are handled as follows:
- **G10 does not apply.** No DLP request, response or page schema carries a default (the
  frozen schema graph walked from all 14 DLP roots, DK§0, TB§4.3), so typed SDK reads are
  lossless apart from key order (D35): no DLP output and no DLP backup shows a fabricated
  field, and no raw-read workaround is used. scm-sdk 0.1.1's `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults`
  changes nothing here.
- **G11 (the DLP API, not scm-sdk).** The API has no data-profile DELETE (an advertised
  DELETE answered 501, a status PATCH/PUT 500) and a deleted profile keeps its name reserved
  (409 on the next create). The SDK correctly has no `delete`. `profiles delete` needs no SDK
  operation (§16.7). **It blocks the live rule** "create … delete a data profile": no CLI, API
  or SDK change can delete a run-created profile, so the live write flow creates no data
  profile (§10, choice 1 of §16.15). This is blocked on the service, not on an SDK fix.
- **G12.** The SDK Spring walks (`list_pages`, `list_items`, `list_all`) have no
  duplicate-id or metadata checks, read only the camelCase totals and stop early when a
  service caps its page size. The CLI never calls them: every walk is the CLI page loop
  `dlp::walk` over the single-page `list()` (§16.3 "Lists and walks"), a read-only check
  like `redteam::walk` (D147), so the workaround is safe.
- **G13.** A keyword-bearing dictionary page can exceed the default 8 MiB response limit or
  the validation node cap. The DLP client raises `max_response_bytes` to 32 MiB (validation
  then allows 400,000 nodes), and `backup` and the custom-only `dictionaries list --keywords`
  read keywords per dictionary (§16.10, §16.4). Safe.
- **G14, G15** (differences, not gaps): the SDK caps request bodies at 8 MiB, refuses unsafe
  multipart file names, and validates dictionary metadata with `DictionaryRequestSchema`
  before sending; the CLI checks all three during planning (§16.8, D164, D173).
- **G16** (`DictionaryListParams`, `DataFilteringProfileListParams` have no constructor):
  built with `Default::default()` and field assignment.
- **G17** (operation names): the `--debug` log records them as they are
  (`dlp.filtering_profiles.*`, `dlp.data_patterns.*`, `dlp.data_profiles.*`,
  `dlp.dictionaries.*`); the debug tests pin them, as G9.

### 16.1 Build steps

0.7 is built in three steps. Each step ships its executable, parity and `dNN_` tests and
leaves the checks green.

| Step | Commands and work |
|---|---|
| 1. Reads (built) | `runtime dlp filtering-profiles list\|ls`, `get`; `patterns list\|ls`, `get`; `profiles list\|ls`, `get`; `dictionaries list\|ls`, `get`. Shared: `DlpClients::build`, the argument checks of §16.3, `dlp::walk` (CRUD mode), the visibility filter, the camelCase JSON, the list and get layouts of §16.4, the fixture's DLP read routes |
| 2. Writes (built) | `filtering-profiles replace`; `patterns create\|replace\|patch\|delete`; `profiles create\|replace\|patch` and the `profiles delete` refusal; `dictionaries create\|replace\|patch\|delete` (the multipart upload). Shared: the body escape hatches, the merge patch, the predefined guard, the confirmations, the DLP `Change` words, the write fixture routes, counters and traps |
| 3. Backup, restore, live (built) | `runtime dlp backup`, `runtime dlp restore <file>` (§16.10, §16.11), the inventory sweep (`dlp::backup::Sweep`, the inventory mode of the walk), the restore planner (`dlp::plan`); the live tier's DLP reads, the DLP write flow and the sweeper's DLP kinds, with their loopback self-tests (§10) |

Each step registers its own commands: until a step lands, its commands are not in the clap
tree (`runtime dlp patterns create` is an unrecognised subcommand in a step-1 build, exit 2,
D1), and the group help lists only the commands that exist.

`runtime dlp generate` is not a command (dropped, MILESTONES; as `redteam judge`, §15.1): clap
reports an unrecognised subcommand (exit 2, D1), no help lists it, and the `runtime dlp`
description drops the word. The TypeScript specs `tests/unit/dlp/**` and
`tests/unit/cli/dlp-generate-*.spec.ts` test only `generate` and are not ported.

### 16.2 Commands and options

Help texts, group descriptions and `Examples:` are TypeScript's (TD§1, TB§1, the captured
`--help` of every leaf) with the program name `airs`, the `--output` line generated
from the format policy (§2.4), and the changes below (pinned leaf by leaf against the
reference by `help_texts_match_typescript`): the `runtime dlp` description reads
`DLP management (filtering-profiles, patterns, profiles, dictionaries, backup/restore)`; the
options marked **(Rust)** with the help text given here; `patterns replace --type` and
`--technique` read `Pattern type: predefined|custom|file_property (default: the current type)`
and `Detection technique (default: the current technique)` (D169); `backup --file-format`
reads `Backup file format: json` (`(default: "json")`); `backup --output-file` reads
`New private backup file; defaults to the current directory; never overwrite`;
`dictionaries create --metadata-file` reads
`JSON metadata file (cannot be combined with --name/--category/...)` (D165; TS: `overrides …`);
the `dictionaries replace` description reads
`Full-replace via multipart upload. --file required. May return 200 (body) or 204 (re-get; when the re-get fails, warns and prints the id).`
(D172; TS: `… falls back to "(state not echoed)" on transient failure`, a line this CLI never
prints); and the
`Examples:` of `backup` and `restore` drop the YAML example and show Rust options
(`airs runtime dlp backup --output-file ./dlp-backup.json`,
`airs runtime dlp restore ./dlp-backup.json --dry-run --output json`,
`airs runtime dlp restore ./dlp-backup.json --name-prefix migrated- --expect-tsg <destination-tsg> --force`).
TypeScript's empty help strings (`dictionaries get` and `patch` descriptions, `--name`,
`--category`, `--description`, `--keywords`) stay empty (choice 25). Groups list their
subcommands in TypeScript's sorted order: `runtime dlp`: `backup, dictionaries,
filtering-profiles, patterns, profiles, restore`; `filtering-profiles`: `get, list|ls,
replace`; `patterns`, `profiles` and `dictionaries`: `create, delete|rm, get, list|ls, patch,
replace` (no `help`, no `generate`). The `runtime` group gains `dlp` in its sorted place with
the description above. Every `list` has the visible alias `ls` and every `delete` the alias
`rm`. A group without a subcommand prints its help on stderr, exit 2 (D1). Options marked
**hidden** are not in `--help`.

| Command | Arguments and options |
|---|---|
| `runtime dlp filtering-profiles list\|ls` | `--limit <n>` (`Max results per page (API page size)`), `--offset <n>` (`Starting offset — rounds down to a page boundary`), `--sort <field,dir>` (`Sort criteria (repeatable)`), `--all` (`Walk all pages`), `--max <n>` (default `10000`); hidden `--size <n>` and `--page <n>` (TS deprecated aliases of `--limit` and `--offset`). No `--include-predefined` (TS: an unknown option) |
| `filtering-profiles get <id>` | none |
| `filtering-profiles replace <id>` | `--file-based`, `--non-file-based`, `--description <s>`, `--direction <s>`, `--log-severity <s>`, `--scan-type <s>`, `--data-profile-id <n>`, `--euc-template-id <s>`, `--end-user-coaching`, `--granular`, `--file-type <s>` (repeatable), `--body <json\|->`, `--body-file <path>`, `--force` (Rust, `Skip the confirmation prompt`) |
| `patterns list\|ls`, `profiles list\|ls` | as `filtering-profiles list`, plus `--include-predefined` (TS text) |
| `dictionaries list\|ls` | as `patterns list`, plus `--keywords`, `--include-keywords` (`Alias for --keywords`) |
| `patterns get <id>`, `profiles get <id>` | none |
| `dictionaries get <id>` | `--keywords`, `--include-keywords` |
| `patterns create` | `--name <s>`, `--type <s>` (default `custom`), `--description <s>`, `--technique <s>` (default `regex`), `--confidence-levels <csv>`, `--regex <pattern>` (repeatable), `--weighted-regex <PATTERN\|N>` (repeatable), `--delimiter <s>`, `--proximity-distance <n>`, `--proximity-keyword <s>` (repeatable), `--tag <k=v>` (repeatable), `--body <json\|->`, `--body-file <path>` |
| `patterns replace <id>` | the `create` options, and `--force` (Rust) |
| `patterns patch <id>`, `profiles patch <id>`, `dictionaries patch <id>` | `--body-file <path>`, `--set <k=v...>`, `--clear <key...>` (each takes every following value up to the next option, and repeats; a positional after them is taken as a value, TS) |
| `patterns delete\|rm <id>`, `dictionaries delete\|rm <id>` | `--force` (Rust) |
| `profiles create` | `--name <s>`, `--profile-type <s>`, `--description <s>`, `--granular`, `--pattern-id <id>` (repeatable), `--combinator <op>` (default `or`), `--confidence <level>` (default `high`), `--body <json\|->`, `--body-file <path>` |
| `profiles replace <id>` | the `create` options, and `--force` (Rust) |
| `profiles delete\|rm <id>` | none (always the refusal of §16.7; no `--force`, TS) |
| `dictionaries create` | `--name <s>`, `--category <s>`, `--description <s>`, `--region <s>`, `--classification <s>`, `--file <path>`, `--metadata-file <path>`, `--include-keywords` |
| `dictionaries replace <id>` | the `create` options, and `--force` (Rust) |
| `runtime dlp backup` | `--output-file <path>`, `--resources <list>` (default all), `--skip-unsupported`, `--max-pages <n>` (default `100`), `--file-format <format>` (default `json`) |
| `runtime dlp restore <file>` | `--dry-run`, `--expect-tsg <id>`, `--force` (TS text), `--allow-other-tenant` (Rust, `Restore a backup exported from another TSG`), `--max-pages <n>` (default `100`), `--name-prefix <prefix>`, `--on-conflict <policy>` (default `error`), `--pattern-map <source=destination>` (repeatable), `--skip-unresolved` |

The leaf `--output <fmt>` options of TypeScript are the global `--output` here (§2.3). Boolean
options take no value; "repeatable" options take one value per occurrence.

### 16.3 Common rules

**Clients and endpoints.** Every DLP command that sends requests builds its client with
`DlpClients::build` (`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/clients.rs`, DK§1.2) from the selected tenant only:
- `dlpEndpoint` (else `https://api.dlp.paloaltonetworks.com`, `scm::constants::DEFAULT_DLP_ENDPOINT`)
  and `mgmtTokenEndpoint` (else the §5 default), each admitted by §5 (the D48 message names the
  key, never the value); a trailing `/` of the base is ignored (both SDKs), and requests go to
  `<dlpEndpoint>/v2/api/data-filtering-profiles|data-patterns|data-profiles|dictionaries`.
  `mgmtEndpoint` is not used;
- the §3.5 management credential check (`mgmtClientId`, `mgmtClientSecret`, `mgmtTsgId`)
  before any client is built, with the §3.5 messages (TS transfer's own
  `DLP transfer requires configured Management client ID, secret and TSG ID`, exit 2, is not
  used, D161); the DLP plane is the management OAuth plane and never sends scanner
  credentials;
- the shared `oauth_parts` (the lease-recording provider of §6, one transport, the direct one
  when either endpoint is loopback http, one `OriginPolicy` admitting the DLP base and the
  issuer), `max_retries = 5` for reads, `max_response_bytes` 32 MiB (G13), the default 8 MiB
  `max_request_bytes`, then `scm::dlp::DlpClient::new`. A construction failure is
  `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:The DLP client could not be configured` (exit 1). Each command awaits the
  token before its first request (`DlpClients::authenticate`), so a token failure is the §6
  `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:…` message.
No environment variable is read (§2.6; TS reads none for the DLP base either, TD§0), no
`x-tsg-id` header is sent, and `--tenant` selects the tenant as for every command (§3.4). There
is no DLP doctor check (TS parity); `dlpEndpoint` stays the §3.3 endpoint key (row 11), shown by
`tenant read` with the D45 rule.

**Validation order.** clap → the deprecation warnings (`--size`, `--page`; each
`  ⚠ --<old> is deprecated and will be removed in v4 — use --<new>`, yellow by the stderr
decision, never quiet-suppressed) → `--output` (§2.4) → `--tenant`'s name format → the
command's argument checks in the order of its section, including the non-interactive
confirmation refusal → the debug log (§2.9) → input files, piped stdin and output-path checks
(below) → the request bodies built from them (schema checks) → the tenant (§3.4, §3.7) → the
credential check (§3.5) → the restore TSG checks (§16.11) → the client and token → the
command's reads, the predefined guard, prompts and writes. Every usage error (exit 2) comes
before the tenant is read, makes no request and opens no debug log (D162). File and
output-path errors exit 1 before the tenant, with zero requests. A check that needs server data
(a body completed from the current record, a `--confidence` the referenced patterns lack)
fails after its reads and before any write, with exit 1 (D161).

**IDs** (D162). Every `<id>` argument, every `--pattern-id` and every `--data-profile-id`
check runs before the tenant. `<id>` and `--pattern-id` must pass the SDK segment rule
(`rs:config.rs:121-151`: non-empty, not `.` or `..`, no `\` and no control character, also once
percent-decoded; `segment::check_segment`), else `Invalid <resource> id: <value>` (exit 2;
`<value>` through `terminal_safe`; `<resource>` is `filtering profile`, `data pattern`,
`data profile` or `dictionary`; `--pattern-id` uses `data pattern`). A valid id is sent as one
percent-encoded segment (`a/b?c` → `a%2Fb%3Fc`, TS parity); TS sends `''`, `.` and `..`
unencoded, so `patterns delete ''` reaches the collection (TD§2.7). No id format is imposed
(DLP ids are not UUIDs). `profiles delete <id>` sends nothing and is not checked (§16.7).

**List flags** (D162; decimal digits only, as §7.1):
- `--limit`: 1 to 4,294,967,295, else `--limit must be a positive integer` (TS sends `0`,
  `-1` and `1.5` as `size=0|-1|1`, and drops `abc`). No default: without `--limit` no `size`
  is sent on a single server page (TS), a server-paged `--all` walk uses 50 (TS `listAll`), and
a client-sliced walk uses 100 (below).
- `--offset`: 0 to 2^53 − 1, else `--offset must be a non-negative integer`. `--max`: the
  §7.1 rule (`--max must be a non-negative integer`; `0` means no item cap, the 1,000,000
  safety bound), validated even without `--all` (TS: `abc` fails after the tenant, exit 1).
  `--all` with an explicit `--offset` (even `0`) or `--page`: `--all cannot be combined with --offset`.
- Hidden aliases (TS `pagination.ts:64-123`): `--size <n>` is `--limit` (an explicit `--limit`
  wins); `--page <n>` (the `--offset` number rule, `--offset must be a non-negative integer`)
  gives the page directly, and an explicit `--offset` wins over it (TS).
- `--sort <field,dir>`: repeatable, sent in order (`sort=id,desc&sort=name`); default
  `name,asc` (TS, always sent). At most 128 values, each 1–1,024 bytes without control
  characters (the SDK bound), else `--sort accepts at most 128 values` or
  `--sort values must be 1-1024 bytes with no control characters` (exit 2). Values are
  otherwise free text (the service validates them).

**Lists and walks** (D170). Two kinds of list:
- **Server-paged** (`filtering-profiles list` always; `patterns|profiles|dictionaries list`
  with `--include-predefined`): without `--all` one request,
  `GET <path>?[page=<p>&][size=<n>&]sort=…[&keywords=true]` in that order (TS), where
  `size` is `--limit` and `page = floor(offset / (--limit or 50))` when `--offset` (or
  `--page`) is given; when `--offset` is given without `--limit`, `size=50` is sent too (TS
  sends no `size`, so its rounded page addresses the server's default page size, D170). The
  rows are printed as the service returned them.
- **Client-sliced** (`patterns|profiles|dictionaries list` without `--include-predefined`, the
  default): TS fetches one page and drops the predefined rows from it, so a page of predefined
  rows prints `No data patterns found` while custom ones exist (TD§3.3). airs-cli-rs reads every
  page (the walk below, page size 100, the given `--sort`), drops the rows whose `type` is
  `predefined`, then slices: without `--all` the rows `[offset, offset + limit)` (no `--limit`:
  to the end); with `--all` the first `--max` rows (`0`: all).
- **`--all` on a server-paged list** walks from `page=0` with `size` = `--limit` or 50 and
  stops at `--max` rows.

Every walk is `dlp::walk` (CRUD mode) under the §7.2 `--all` bounds (`max_pages` 100,000,
512 MiB, the item cap) and the 300 s walk budget (§5): pages `0, 1, …`; the page size used by the
end rule is the page's own reported size (`size`, `pageable.pageSize` or the snake_case
`pageable.page_size`, read from the typed fields or the extensions), else the requested size;
the walk ends at `last: true`, else when `page + 1 >= totalPages` (`totalPages` or
`total_pages`), else at a page shorter than its size. It fails with the D37 message (exit 1, no
partial data) at an empty page that is not the last, and at a row whose non-empty `id` an
earlier row of the walk already had (a service that ignores `page` would otherwise repeat
rows); the D40 rule at a bound. The inventory mode of `backup` and `restore` adds the TS checks
of §16.10.

**Status lines** (stderr, quiet-suppressed, every format):
- a server page: `  Showing <rows> of <totalElements>[ (next --offset <k>)]` with the server
  total (`totalElements` or `total_elements`) and `k = (page + 1) × size` when `k < total` (TS
  prints this only for filtering profiles; with `--include-predefined` it prints
  `Showing <n> of <n>`, D170); a page without a total: `  Showing <rows>`;
- a client slice: `  Showing <rows> of <custom rows>[ (next --offset <offset + limit>)]`
  (the second number counts the custom rows of the whole tenant; TS prints `<n> of <n>`);
- `--all`, complete: `  Showing <n> of <n>` (TS); stopped by `--max` while more rows exist:
  `  Showing first <n> (stopped at --max <m>; more available)` (D14).

**Input files and stdin** (D164). Read with the §13.2 input-file rules (path as given, symlinks
followed, a regular file, bounded, read whole, the §13.2 messages with the cap named, no OS
error and no content echoed), after the debug log and before the tenant:

| Input | Cap | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `--body-file` (create, replace, patch) | 1 MiB | UTF-8, one JSON value that is an object |
| `--body -` (create, replace) | 1 MiB | piped stdin, UTF-8, one JSON object; stdin a terminal: `--body - requires piped input on stdin` (exit 2, checked with the arguments) |
| `--metadata-file` | 1 MiB | UTF-8, one JSON object |
| `--file` (the dictionary keyword file) | 7 MiB (`files::UPLOAD_LIMIT`) | any bytes, sent as read (choice 13: no UTF-8, CSV-header or line check, TS parity) |
| `restore <file>` | 20 MiB (TS) | UTF-8 JSON (§16.11) |

`--body <json>` (an argument) is parsed as one JSON object too. Messages: the §13.2 ones for
files; for `--body` and stdin `--body is not valid JSON` and `--body must contain a JSON object`
(TS echoes an excerpt of the input, D163). TypeScript's resource-specific texts are kept where
they echo nothing: profiles `Cannot read profile body as JSON; verify the file and JSON syntax`
and `Profile body must be a JSON object`; dictionaries `Invalid JSON in dictionary metadata file`
and `Dictionary metadata must be a JSON object`. These are exit 2 for `--body` and stdin (usage)
and exit 1 for a file (as §13.2).

**Request bodies and the escape hatches** (D165). A create or replace body comes from exactly
one source: `--body-file`, `--body -`, `--body <json>` or the build flags. Usage errors (exit 2,
before the files are read): `--body and --body-file are mutually exclusive` (TS text, profiles);
a body together with a build flag: `--body and --body-file cannot be combined with --<flag>`
(the first build flag in help order; TS ignores the flags silently); `--body ""` and
`--body-file ""`: `--body needs a JSON object` / `--body-file needs a path` (TS falls through to
the builder). A parsed `null`, `0`, `false` or `""` is `--body must contain a JSON object` (TS:
`--body or --body-file was empty`). The body (from a hatch or the builder) is validated with the
SDK request schema (`DataPatternRequest`, `AdvancedDataProfileRequest`,
`DataFilteringProfileRequest`, `DictionaryRequest`, the `…PatchRequest`s; `Mode::Request`;
unknown keys kept as extensions) during planning; a failure is exit 2 with:
- patterns and filtering profiles: the D116 text
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for <METHOD> <path> did not match schema`
  (`<path>` the SDK path with the id, `/v2/api/data-patterns/<id>`; TS appends the field paths
  and zod codes, D116);
- profiles: `Invalid profile metadata: verify required fields and value types` (TS);
- dictionaries (metadata and patch): `Invalid dictionary metadata: verify required fields and value types` (TS).
A body that is completed from server data (§16.6 replace without `--type`) is validated again
after its read; that failure is the same text with exit 1. Bodies are sent with sorted keys
(D35); equality with TypeScript is JSON equality (TS sends schema order).

**`type: predefined`** (D166): a create, replace or patch body (hatch, `--set type=predefined`,
`patterns create|replace --type predefined`, dictionary metadata) whose top-level `type` is
`"predefined"` is refused during planning:
`<resource> bodies cannot set "type": "predefined"; predefined resources are shipped by Palo Alto Networks and never written by airs`
(exit 2).

**Merge patch** (`--set`/`--clear`, `dlp::patch`, TS `patch.ts:10-79`; D163). `--set k=v` splits at
the first `=`; the value is coerced as TS: `true`/`false` → booleans; `^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$` → a JSON
number (a fraction becomes the nearest double, as `Number()`; an integer part beyond 2^53 is the
error below, where TS rounds `12345678901234567890` silently); a value starting
with `{`, `[` or `"` → JSON, falling back to the raw string when it does not parse (TS); otherwise
the string. `--clear k` sets `k: null`, applied after every `--set` (so
`--set k=v --clear k` sends `null`); a repeated `--set` of one key keeps the last. Errors (exit 2,
no value or key echoed): an entry without `=` or with an empty key: `--set expects key=value`
(TS `--set expected key=value, got: <entry>`); a key with `.`:
`--set and --clear take top-level fields; use --body-file for nested fields`; the raw value
`null`: `--set cannot set null; use --clear for that field`; a number the coercion cannot
represent exactly: `--set numbers must keep their exact value; quote them to send a string`. Profiles report every
such failure with TS's `Invalid profile patch: verify JSON syntax and --set key=value/--clear key flags`
and dictionaries with `Invalid dictionary patch flags: use --set key=value, --clear key, or --body-file for nested fields`
(TS masks them the same way). `--body-file` with `--set` or `--clear`:
`--body-file is mutually exclusive with --set/--clear` (TS). No flag at all sends `{}` through
the schema, which refuses it (the required fields, TS parity). The patch schemas require
`name`, `type`, `detection_config` (patterns), `name`, `profile_type` (profiles) and `name`,
`category`, `original_file_name` (dictionaries), so a patch must repeat them (TS parity; the CLI
does not fill them from the current record, choice 14). PATCH bodies are sent with
`Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json` (the SDK).

**Writes and outcomes** (D160). Every DLP request that is not a GET is a write: one SDK call
(`RawRequest::new`, never re-sent by the SDK; the multipart uploads included), through
`writes::attempt` (§13.2): one replay after an `Http` 401 with outcome `Rejected`, never after a
403, never after a 5xx, a timeout or a transport error. The error of a failed write is the §6
message (allowlisted problem fields only, such as `originalFileName: must not be blank`, TD§11.6),
and when the outcome is not a plain rejection one detail line follows the `HTTP`/`Re-run` lines:
`Outcome unknown: the <thing> may have been <done>.` or
`Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but the response could not be read.`, then the hint line below
when the table has one. Nothing is re-sent and nothing is looked up after such a failure. Exit 1.
The words (`writes::Change`):

| Command | `<thing>` / `<done>` | Hint after an unknown or unreadable outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `patterns create\|replace\|patch\|delete` | `data pattern` / `created\|replaced\|patched\|deleted` | create: `Check 'airs runtime dlp patterns list' before creating it again.` |
| `profiles create\|replace\|patch` | `data profile` / `created\|replaced\|patched` | create: `Check 'airs runtime dlp profiles list' before creating it again; data profiles cannot be deleted.` |
| `dictionaries create\|replace\|patch\|delete` | `dictionary` / `created\|replaced\|patched\|deleted` | create: `Check 'airs runtime dlp dictionaries list' before creating it again.` |
| `filtering-profiles replace` | `filtering profile` / `replaced` | — |
| restore (each create) | `dictionary`, `data pattern`, `data profile` / `created` (in the restore result, §16.11) | — |

**Predefined guard** (D166). Before `replace`, `patch` and `delete` of a pattern, profile,
dictionary or filtering profile, the command reads the record (`get(<id>)`, a replay-safe read
with the SDK retries; dictionaries without keywords) after the token and before any prompt or
write. It refuses (exit 1, no write) when:
- the record's `id` is absent or differs from the argument:
  `The service returned a different <resource> for <id>; nothing was changed`;
- its `type` is `predefined` (profiles: the subtype `type`; filtering profiles: the free-string
  `type`): `<id> is a predefined <resource>; airs never modifies or deletes predefined resources`;
- its `type` is a string outside the tenant-created vocabulary of its SDK enum (patterns
  `custom` and `file_property`; profiles and dictionaries `custom`; filtering profiles have a
  free-string `type`, where only `predefined` is refused), a value scm-sdk's tolerant response
  mode keeps (D178; choice 28):
  `<id> has a <resource> type airs does not recognise; it modifies or deletes only tenant-created resources`;
  an absent or `null` `type` passes;
- its `is_parent_managed` is `true` (choice 2):
  `<id> is managed by a parent tenant; airs never modifies or deletes it here`.
A failure of the read is the §6 read error (a 404 included; exit 1). `<id>` goes through
`terminal_safe`. The record's `name` (when present) is used in the prompt. TS has no guard and
writes to predefined records (a pattern replace also rewrites `type` to `custom`, TD§12).

**Confirmations** (D167). `patterns delete`, `dictionaries delete`, every `replace` and
`restore` confirm under the §3.10 and §13.2 rules: `--force` skips the prompt; the gate is stdin
**and** stderr being terminals, otherwise the command's usage error (exit 2, before the tenant);
the prompt `? <message> (y/N) ` on stderr; only `y`/`yes` (trimmed, ASCII case-insensitive)
confirm; anything else, an empty line and EOF decline with the info line `  ℹ Aborted` (exit 0,
nothing sent); Ctrl-C or SIGTERM print `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` and exit 130/143.
Server and argument text in a prompt goes through `terminal_safe`; ` (<name>)` is omitted when
the record has no name. The prompt is asked after the guard read and before the write; no
request is open while it waits. `patch` does not confirm (a partial change, choice 4);
`create` does not confirm.

| Command | Prompt | Non-interactive refusal |
|---|---|---|
| `patterns delete <id>` | `Delete data pattern <id> (<name>)?` | `refusing to delete data pattern <id> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `dictionaries delete <id>` | `Delete dictionary <id> (<name>)?` | `refusing to delete dictionary <id> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `patterns\|profiles\|dictionaries\|filtering-profiles replace <id>` | `Replace <resource> <id> (<name>)?[ The replacement omits <n> field(s) it has now: <fields>.]` | `refusing to replace <resource> <id> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `restore <file>` (§16.11) | `Restore <n> DLP resources from TSG <a> to TSG <b>?` (TS) | `refusing to restore DLP resources without --force in non-interactive mode` |

**Omitted fields of a replace** (D168). A replace is a full replacement (TS semantics; the
flag builders build a complete body). After the guard read, the command lists the top-level
request-schema fields the current record holds (present and not `null`) that the replacement
body does not set (for a filtering profile, for example, `criteria_details`, `exclusions`,
`exception_rules`, `rule1`, `rule2`), in schema order, by name only. When the list is not empty
it is part of the prompt above, and with `--force` the warning
`  ⚠ The replacement omits <n> field(s) the <resource> has now: <fields>` is printed on stderr
before the write (yellow, never quiet-suppressed). TS replaces silently (a flag-built
filtering-profile PUT drops the exclusions and rules, TD§8.2). A read-modify-write overlay was
considered and not taken: the service's response vocabulary differs from the request enums
(`direction: c2s`, `log_severity: low` versus `BOTH|UPLOAD|DOWNLOAD`, `CRITICAL|…`), so copying
the current values into a PUT could fail or change them (choice 5).

**Streams, quiet and formats** (D172, D50). stdout carries data only, written once after
success (§2.2). `pretty`, `table` and `json` exist for every DLP command; `markdown`, `csv` and
`yaml` are invalid formats (D50, exit 2, before the tenant). The tenant's `defaultOutput` is
honoured by every DLP command that prints data (TS resolves it for the reads, the writes and
the transfer commands, TD§2.2, TB§1). There is no banner (TS prints none for DLP).
- **Acks** (`create`, `replace`, `patch`; TS `emitAck`, TD§5.1): the ack document is `{action}`
  plus, when not `null`, `id`, `name`, `type`, `status` (from `status`, overwritten by
  `profile_status`), `version`, in that order (`action` is `created`, `replaced` or `patched`).
  json prints it on stdout; table prints the one-row table whose columns are its keys (TS); pretty
  prints nothing on stdout. In every format the success line `  ✓ <action> <id>  <name>[ v<version>]`
  (TS text; green; quiet-suppressed) goes to stderr (TS: stdout, not suppressed).
- **Deletes**: stdout stays empty in every format (`--output` is validated, then ignored, D59);
  the success line `  ✓ archived <id>` (patterns) or `  ✓ deleted <id>` (dictionaries) goes to
  stderr (TS: stdout in every format).
- **The dictionary replace without a body** (§16.8): the warning on stderr and the reduced ack.
- **Lists and gets**: §16.4. `--quiet` drops the status lines and the success lines, never
  data (TS keeps acks under `--quiet`).

**JSON** (D171). Lists print a bare array, gets a bare object, of the full validated record with
every object key converted from snake or kebab case to camelCase (TS `rdlp.ts:58-73`, regex
`[_-]([a-z0-9])`), except the keys of objects under a `tags` key and under
`exclusions.exclusion_list`, which are data and are kept verbatim (TS renames a tag `my_tag` to
`myTag`, TD§2.10; choice 9). Known keys come in schema order, extensions sorted (D35). Numbers
through `js_number`. `[]` for an empty list (TS).

**Colour** (§2.8). TS's DLP spans (TD§2.3): section headings bold; ids, technique, `dir:`,
`sev:`, `v<n>`, `<n> kw` and get keys dim; the record type cyan; a `status`/`profile_status` of
`active` green, `deleted` and `disabled` yellow, any other dim, a missing one a dim `—`; the
status line dim; success lines green; warnings yellow; failures red. Tables and JSON are never
coloured.

**Server text** (D11, D47, D52). Error messages are §6 messages. Every server string in a pretty
layout, table cell, outcome line, prompt or message goes through `terminal_safe` (TS prints it
raw, TD§4); the `description` of a get goes through `terminal_safe_lines` (line breaks kept,
§15.3). A printed `name`, `description`, `region_name` or `category` that contains a value of
the invocation's `SecretSet` (raw, trimmed, form-encoded or base64) is `[withheld]` in every
format (`dlp::views::withhold`, as §15.3); ids, statuses, versions and timestamps are not checked.

**Sensitive data** (§16.9). Dictionary keywords, regexes, proximity keywords, tag values,
metadata and rule trees are sensitive content: they are printed only on stdout, only by the
reads that print full records (json, the get table) and, for keywords, only when
`--keywords`/`--include-keywords` asked for them (TS parity, choice 10). They never appear in an
error, a warning, a status or outcome line, a prompt, a summary or the debug log; argument and
file errors name the flag or the path only (D163).

**Debug log.** Every DLP command has the debug policy `log` (§2.9): status and headers only,
never a body or a URL query (TS forces `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG_BODY=0` and omits bodies for every
`runtime dlp` action, `program.ts:111-127`; the Rust log never records them anywhere, D64).
`profiles delete` always fails in planning, so it never opens a log.

**Interruption** (§2.5, §13.2). Reads: `Interrupted; no data was written`. A single write:
`nothing was changed` when it was not sent (the guard read, the token or the prompt included),
`the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` when it was, and
`the change was saved` after the write succeeded. `profiles create|replace --pattern-id`: the
pattern reads count as reads. While `--body -` waits for piped stdin the wait is marked for the
signal thread (as `tenant set --stdin`, §2.5): the first signal ends the process at once with
`Interrupted; nothing was changed`, also while the writer keeps the pipe open; a signal that
arrived just before the wait stops the command before it reads. Backup and restore contexts are
in their sections. A signal at a confirmation prints `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` (exit 130/143). TS exits by the signal
with nothing printed (D174).

**Exit codes** (D161). 0: success, a declined confirmation, a `--dry-run`, a dictionary replace
answered without a body. 1: tenant, credential, file, HTTP, network, timeout and decode errors;
a write whose outcome is unknown or unreadable; the guard's refusals; the checks that need server
data; a backup with failed rows or nothing to back up; a restore that refused its plan or did not
complete. 2: every argument check of §16 and the non-interactive confirmation refusals; the
`profiles delete` refusal. 130 / 143: interrupted.

### 16.4 Lists and gets

**Requests.** Lists as §16.3; `dictionaries list --keywords|--include-keywords` adds
`keywords=true` (after the `sort` values, TS order) to the single server page
(`--include-predefined`). The custom-only view (the default) walks its pages **without**
`keywords=true` and then reads the keywords of the shown rows only, one
`GET /v2/api/dictionaries/<id>?keywords=true` per row in row order, each row replaced by that
record (G13: a tenant's keyword lists can exceed the per-response limit, and `--limit 1` would
otherwise download all of them; D170). A failed keyword read fails the list (its §6 message,
exit 1, nothing printed); a record whose `id` differs is
`Dictionary <name> changed while it was listed; retry the operation` (exit 1); a row without an
`id` is shown as listed. Gets: `GET <path>/<id>`
(`dictionaries get --keywords|--include-keywords`: `?keywords=true`). Responses are validated
by the SDK response schemas in their tolerant response mode: the known structure is checked (a
string `version` is a decode error, exit 1), and an unfamiliar enum value (a new `status`) is
kept and printed as server text, where TS fails the read (D178; the research's TS-parity claim,
DK§2, did not hold for scm-sdk 0.1.0, `rs:validation.rs:647-660`).

**Pretty lists** (stdout, TS `rdlp.ts:75-106`): `"\n  <Header>:\n\n"` (the heading is
decoration, quiet-suppressed), one entry per row, then `"\n"`; an empty list prints
`  No <header lower-cased> found\n` (data, dim; `No data patterns found`, `No data profiles found`,
`No data filtering profiles found`, `No data dictionaries found`). Entries (`[…]` only when the
field is set; a row without `id` omits its id line and a missing `name` prints as empty, D56):

| Resource | Header | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| filtering profiles | `Data Filtering Profiles` | `  <id>\n    <name>  <type or ''>[ dir:<direction>][ sev:<log_severity>][ v<version>]` |
| patterns | `Data Patterns` | `  <id>\n    <name>  <type>  <status>[ <technique>][ v<version>]` |
| profiles | `Data Profiles` | `  <id>\n    <name>  <type>  <profile_status>[ <profile_type>][ v<version>]` |
| dictionaries | `Data Dictionaries` | `  <id>\n    <name>  <type>  <status>[ <keywords.length> kw][ v<version>]` |

**Table lists** (TS `common.ts:127-140`, the §2.7 table): columns `ID, Name, Type, Direction,
Severity, Version` (filtering profiles), `ID, Name, Type, Status, Technique, Version` (patterns),
`ID, Name, Type, Profile Type, Status, Version` (profiles), `ID, Name, Type, Status, Keywords,
Version` (dictionaries; `Keywords` is the count, empty without `--keywords`). Empty: nothing on
stdout.

**Pretty gets** (TS `rdlp.ts:108-134`): `"\n  <Title>:\n\n"` (decoration), the key/value block
of the fields whose value is not absent, `null` or `""` (dim keys padded to the longest kept
key), then `"\n"`:

| Resource (title) | Fields in order |
|---|---|
| filtering profile (`Data Filtering Profile`) | `ID`, `Name`, `Type`, `Data Profile` (data_profile_id), `Direction`, `Severity` (log_severity), `Scan Type`, `File Based` (`yes`/`no`, always), `Non-File Based` (`yes`/`no`, always), `Version`, `File Types` (count), `Updated` |
| pattern (`Data Pattern`) | `ID`, `Name`, `Description`, `Type`, `Status`, `Technique`, `Confidence` (levels joined `, `), `Regexes` (count), `Version`, `Updated` |
| profile (`Data Profile`) | `ID`, `Name`, `Description`, `Type`, `Profile Type`, `Status` (profile_status), `Version`, `Updated` |
| dictionary (`Data Dictionary`) | `ID`, `Name`, `Description`, `Type`, `Status`, `Keywords` (count, only when keywords were returned), `Version`, `Updated` |

`Updated` is `audit_metadata.updated_at` as JavaScript `toISOString` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`):
a number is epoch milliseconds (within ±8.64e15, else dropped); a string is accepted when it is
an ISO 8601 date or date-time (normalised to UTC), else dropped (D56: TS `Date` parses some other
forms). Pretty never prints regexes, keywords, proximity keywords or rule trees (TS).

**Table gets**: the §2.7 `Key │ Value` table of the camelCase record in record order, objects and
arrays as compact JSON (TS `view.ts:63-88`; the keyword list and regexes appear here as TS prints
them). **JSON gets**: the camelCase record.

### 16.5 `filtering-profiles replace <id>`

**Body** (TS `bb.ts:99-117`). From `--body`/`--body-file`/stdin, or from the flags:
`--file-based` and `--non-file-based` are both required
(`--file-based and --non-file-based are both required`, TS; as presence flags they send `true`,
so `false` needs a body); then `description`, `direction`, `log_severity`, `scan_type`,
`data_profile_id` (`--data-profile-id`: decimal digits, at most 2^53 − 1, else
`--data-profile-id must be a non-negative integer`, D162; TS drops `abc` and reads `1e3` as
1000), `euc_template_id`, `is_end_user_coaching_enabled` (`--end-user-coaching`),
`is_granular_profile` (`--granular`), `file_type` (every `--file-type`, in order). Enum values are
not case-converted (the schema refuses `--direction sideways`). Planning validates the body with
`DataFilteringProfileRequest` (exit 2).

**Requests.** Token, the guard read `GET …/data-filtering-profiles/<id>`, the omitted-fields
list, the confirmation, `PUT …/data-filtering-profiles/<id>` (one attempt), then the ack
(`replaced`; TS `  ✓ replaced fp-1   v2` when the response has no name). Never live (§10).

### 16.6 `patterns create`, `replace <id>`, `patch <id>`, `delete|rm <id>`

**Builder** (TS `bb.ts:65-93`; D162, D163). `--name` is required (`--name is required`, TS).
`type` = `--type` (create: default `custom`); `detection_config = {technique: --technique (create:
default regex), supported_confidence_levels?}` from `--confidence-levels` split on `,`, trimmed,
empties dropped. `matching_rules` only when one of its flags is given: `delimiter`;
`proximity_distance` (`--proximity-distance`: an integer 2–1000, else
`--proximity-distance must be an integer from 2 to 1000`; TS drops `abc` and still sends
`matching_rules: {}`); `proximity_keywords` (every `--proximity-keyword`); `regexes` = each
`--regex` as `{regex, weight: 1}`, then each `--weighted-regex` split at its **last** `|` into a
non-empty regex and a weight that is a finite decimal number (`^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$`), else
`--weighted-regex must be PATTERN|weight with a numeric weight` (TS echoes the value and accepts
`a|` as weight 0). `tags` from `--tag k=v[,v…]` (values split on `,`, trimmed, empties dropped,
appended per key across repeats); no `=` or an empty key: `--tag must be key=value[,value...]`;
no value left: `--tag needs at least one value` (TS sends `[]`, and echoes the value in its
errors). Body key order as TS (`name, type, detection_config, description, matching_rules, tags`)
before the SDK's sorted serialisation.

**`create`**: planning (body, schema, `type: predefined` refusal) → tenant → token →
`POST /v2/api/data-patterns` → ack `created`.

**`replace <id>`** (D169): the same body; when `--type` or `--technique` is absent (and the body
comes from the flags), the value is taken from the current record (the guard read) instead of
TS's `custom`/`regex` defaults (TS rewrites a `file_property` or `weighted_regex` pattern to
`custom`/`regex`), and the body is validated again (exit 1). Requests: token, guard read,
omitted fields, confirmation, `PUT /v2/api/data-patterns/<id>`, ack `replaced`.

**`patch <id>`**: the merge patch of §16.3 (`DataPatternPatchRequest`), token, guard read,
`PATCH /v2/api/data-patterns/<id>`, ack `patched`.

**`delete|rm <id>`**: token, guard read, confirmation, `DELETE /v2/api/data-patterns/<id>`,
`  ✓ archived <id>` (stderr). The service archives the pattern (it stays readable with
`status: "deleted"`, TD§9.4).

### 16.7 `profiles create`, `replace <id>`, `patch <id>`, `delete|rm <id>`

**Builder and flag checks** (TS `bb.ts:127-213`, all before the tenant, exit 2, TS texts):
`--profile-type` (even with a body): `basic` →
`Basic profile writes are unsupported: the API returned advanced for basic requests. Use advanced or manage basic profiles in SCM.`,
any other value but `advanced` → `Profile type must be advanced`; with the flags: `--name is required`;
the name: `Profile name is required and must be a nonblank string`,
`Profile name must be at most 32 characters` (counted in UTF-16 units; also for a body's
`name`); `--combinator` (lower-cased) ∈ `and|or|not|and_not|or_not`
(`--combinator must be one of and|or|not|and_not|or_not`); `--confidence` ∈ `low|medium|high`
(`--confidence must be low|medium|high`, case-sensitive); a repeated `--pattern-id`:
`--pattern-id lists the same data pattern twice` (TS sends duplicate leaves, choice 11). A body
(`--body`, `--body-file`, stdin) must be a JSON object with a valid `name` and a `profile_type`
that is `advanced` or absent (TS `validateBodyType`). Body:
`{name, profile_type: "advanced", description?, is_granular_data_profile?, detection_rules?}`
(`profile_type` travels as an extension; the schema requires `detection_rules`, so a flag body
without `--pattern-id` fails with `Invalid profile metadata: …`, exit 2, no request, TS).

**Pattern resolution** (flags with `--pattern-id`; TD§10.2): after the token, one
`GET /v2/api/data-patterns/<id>` per `--pattern-id` in order (reads with the SDK retries); each
record must have that `id`, a `name`, a `detection_config.technique` and an integer
`version ≥ 1`, else `Referenced pattern did not return a matching ID, name, technique, and version; no profile was written`;
`status` other than `active`: `Referenced pattern is not active; no profile was written`; a read
failure: its §6 message; a `--confidence` outside a pattern's levels:
`Requested confidence is not supported by every referenced pattern` (all exit 1, before any write;
TS exits 2 for the last, D161). Predefined patterns may be referenced (TS). Then one
`expression_tree` rule: `operator_type` = the combinator, one leaf per pattern:
`rule_item {id, name, version, detection_technique, confidence_level, supported_confidence_levels
(the pattern's, or [confidence]), match_type: "include", occurrence_operator_type:
"more_than_equal_to", occurrence_count: 1}` (TS), validated again (exit 1).

**`create`**: `POST /v2/api/data-profiles`, ack `created`. **`replace <id>`**: token, guard read,
pattern resolution, omitted fields, confirmation, `PUT /v2/api/data-profiles/<id>`, ack
`replaced`. **`patch <id>`**: the merge patch (`DataProfilePatchRequest`; TS's masked text), the
body check above (a missing `name` is `Profile name is required and must be a nonblank string`),
token, guard read, `PATCH`, ack `patched`. `--set profile_status=deleted` is passed through (TS;
the live API answered 500).

**`delete|rm <id>`**: no tenant, no client, no request, no debug log; stderr (exit 2):

```
\n  ✗ This DLP API has no DELETE for data profiles.
  Status-based retirement is not live-verified: the latest owned-fixture
  PATCH/PUT returned HTTP 500; an advertised DELETE returned HTTP 501.
  No API request was sent by this command. Do not assume the profile was removed.
  Inspect current state with: airs runtime dlp profiles get <id> --output json\n\n
```

(TS text; `<id>` through `terminal_safe`, the program name `airs`, D73.)

### 16.8 `dictionaries create`, `replace <id>`, `patch <id>`, `delete|rm <id>`

**Metadata** (TS `dict.ts:55-70`; D165, D173). `--metadata-file` and the metadata flags
(`--name`, `--category`, `--description`, `--region`, `--classification`) are exclusive:
`--metadata-file cannot be combined with --<flag>` (exit 2; TS ignores the flags). From the flags,
`--name`, `--category`, `--region` and `--file` are required
(`--name, --category, --region, and --file are required`, TS), and the metadata is
`{name, category, region_name: --region, original_file_name: <basename of --file>,
description?, classification?}`. From the file it is sent as written (TS; no
`original_file_name` is added). `--file` is required in both cases
(`--file is required (multipart upload)`, TS). The metadata is validated with
`DictionaryRequest::parse(…, Mode::Request)` during planning (`category` one of `Academic,
Confidential, Employment, Financial, Government, Healthcare, Legal, Marketing, Source Code`;
`name`, `original_file_name`, `region_name` required; TS sends any metadata, G15), and
`original_file_name` must be a file name the SDK accepts (1–255 bytes, not `.` or `..`, no
control character, `/`, `\` or `"`; G14): either failure is
`Invalid dictionary metadata: verify required fields and value types` (exit 2). The keyword file
plus the serialised metadata must fit the SDK body budget (8 MiB − 64 KiB, as D132), else
`<path> and its metadata exceed the 8 MiB upload limit` (exit 1, before the tenant).

**Multipart** (TD§11.3, both SDKs): `POST /v2/api/dictionaries[?keywords=true]` (create) or
`PUT /v2/api/dictionaries/<id>[?keywords=true]` (replace; `keywords=true` with
`--include-keywords`), `multipart/form-data` with two parts: `json` (`filename="metadata.json"`,
`application/json`, the metadata with sorted keys) and `file` (`filename="<original_file_name>"`,
`application/octet-stream`, the file bytes). Built as
`DictionaryUpload::new(metadata, BinaryFile::new(bytes)).include_keywords(…)`; the D160 401
replay re-sends the same upload once. The region hint: a 400 whose problem has no `detail` and
no `errors` (`error.problem()`, or no problem at all) prints, before the error block,
`Dictionary upload rejected. Verify the SCM region display name (for example, --region "United States"); region codes such as GLOBAL or us-west-2 are not equivalent.`
on stderr (TS text and placement).

**`create`**: planning → tenant → token → POST → ack `created`.

**`replace <id>`**: token, guard read, omitted fields, confirmation, PUT. A 2xx with a body →
ack `replaced`. A 2xx without a body (`Ok(None)`) → `GET /v2/api/dictionaries/<id>` (a read, no
keywords) → ack from it; when that read fails: the warning
`  ⚠ replaced <id>; the service did not return the new state` on stderr, json
`{"action": "replaced", "id": "<id>"}`, table that one-row table, exit 0 (TS prints
`  ✓ replaced <id> (state not echoed by region)` on stdout in every format, D172).

**`patch <id>`**: the merge patch (`DictionaryPatchRequest`; `--body-file` must be a JSON object,
TS `readMetadata`), token, guard read, `PATCH`, ack `patched`.

**`delete|rm <id>`**: token, guard read, confirmation, `DELETE /v2/api/dictionaries/<id>`,
`  ✓ deleted <id>` (stderr).

### 16.9 Sensitive data per command

| Command | Printed | Never printed |
|---|---|---|
| `list`, `get` (all four) | pretty: names, types, statuses, versions, counts; table and json: the full record (regexes, proximity keywords, tags, rule trees, `audit_metadata`), keywords only with `--keywords` | — (the user asked for the record) |
| `create`, `replace`, `patch` | the ack (id, name, type, status, version) | the body, the merge patch, the keyword file, the metadata, in any message |
| `delete`, `profiles delete` | the id | — |
| `backup` | the summary counts and the path; the warning names no content | keywords, regexes, records (they are only in the 0600 file) |
| `restore` | names, actions, ids, TSGs and outcomes | file content, keywords, regexes |
| every command | §6 errors (allowlisted problem fields only) | body excerpts, `--set`/`--tag`/`--weighted-regex` values, file content (D163); in the debug log: bodies and queries (§2.9) |

`--body <json>`, `--regex`, `--weighted-regex` and `--proximity-keyword` put content on the
command line (the process list, shell history), as in TS; `--body-file` and `--body -` avoid it.
They are not refused (they are detection definitions, not credentials).

### 16.10 `runtime dlp backup`

**Argument checks** (exit 2, in order): `--file-format` other than `json` (exactly):
`--file-format must be json (yaml was dropped)` (TS accepts `yaml`, D175); `--resources`: split on
`,`, items trimmed, each `dictionaries`, `patterns` or `profiles`, none repeated, at least one,
else `--resources takes a unique list of dictionaries, patterns, profiles` (TS text; TS crashes
with a stack trace, exit 1, D162); `--max-pages`: `^\d+$`, 1–1000, else
`--max-pages must be an integer from 1 to 1000` (TS); `--output-file -`:
`Backups contain dictionary keywords and require a private file destination, not stdout` (TS);
`--output-file ""`: `--output-file needs a path`; a path whose extension is not `.json` (ASCII
case-insensitive): `Backup filename extension must match --file-format` (TS).

**Location** (before the tenant, exit 1): the default path is
`./airs-dlp-backup-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<8 lowercase hex>.json`; the parent directory of
`--output-file` must exist (followed through symlinks; nothing is created), else
`Cannot write a backup into <dir>; it must be an existing directory`; anything at the path
(`lstat`, a dangling symlink included) is `<path> already exists; choose another --output-file`
(TS refuses it only after reading every keyword of the tenant, D175). Paths are shown as given.

**Requests.** Token, then the three inventories in this order: dictionaries (without
keywords, G13), data patterns, data profiles; each `dlp::walk` in inventory mode: pages
`0, 1, …` with `size=100` and `sort=name,asc`, reads with the SDK retries (TS sends each read
once, D175), under the TS checks (TB§2.3): the effective page size (the first `size` or
`pageable.pageSize|page_size`, 1–100, constant; else 100); `number`, `numberOfElements|
number_of_elements`, `first`, `empty`, `pageable.pageNumber|page_number`, `pageable.offset`
consistent with the index and the length; `totalPages|total_pages` and
`totalElements|total_elements` non-negative safe integers, constant, consistent with each other,
the index, the lengths and `last`; camelCase and snake_case spellings that disagree; ids
non-empty and unique across the sweep; at most 10,000 records; `last` from the page, else the
totals, else a short page; at most `--max-pages` pages. Messages (TS, exit 1, no file):
`Inventory of <label> has inconsistent pagination metadata; retry the operation`,
`Inventory of <label> contains a missing resource ID; retry the operation`,
`Inventory of <label> contains duplicate resource IDs; retry the operation`,
`Inventory of <label> exceeds the 10000-record safety limit`, `Inventory of <label> did not advance`,
`Inventory of <label> is incomplete: increase --max-pages` (`<label>` `dictionaries`,
`data patterns`, `data profiles`); a failed page read is its §6 message (TS:
`DLP transfer API request failed[ (HTTP <s>)]; no automatic retry was made.`, D175). More than one
distinct non-null `tenant_id` across the patterns and profiles:
`Inventory reports mixed DLP tenant identities` (TS).

**Selection** (TS `dr.ts:357-507`, TB§4.2, unchanged): primaries by `--resources` (dictionaries
not `predefined`; patterns and profiles not `predefined` and not retired: `status`/`profile_status`
`deleted|disabled`); each kept profile's referenced dictionaries and patterns are added whatever
`--resources` says; predefined dependencies are stored as TS's stubs (dictionary `{id, name,
type}`; pattern `{id, name, type, version?, detection_config?: {technique}}`); every other record
as the inventory returned it. The per-profile checks and reasons of TB§4.2 (no rules, rule shape
and type, tree depth 100, a leaf without a technique, a non-string reference id, a direct EDM
dataset, an unknown or version-pinned dictionary, an unknown, retired, technique-mismatched or
version-mismatched pattern): without `--skip-unsupported` any failing profile fails the run with
every reason at once (`Profiles cannot be exported: <name> (<reason>); …; exclude unsupported profiles explicitly with --skip-unsupported`,
exit 1, no file; names through `terminal_safe`); with it each is skipped, recorded in `skipped`
and reported on stderr with `  ⚠ Skipped unsupported data profile: <name> (<reason>)`, and its
dependencies are not added. Names: missing → `Backup contains a <label> without a name`; empty
after trim or holding a C0 control or DEL →
`DLP resource names must be nonempty and contain no control characters`; duplicate within a kind →
`Backup contains duplicate <label> names: <name>` (`<label>` `dictionary`, `data pattern`,
`data profile`; exit 1, no file). Nothing selected: `No matching DLP resources to back up` (exit 1,
no file, TS; choice 23).

**Keywords** (G13). For each stored custom dictionary, in name order,
`GET /v2/api/dictionaries/<id>?keywords=true` (a read with the SDK retries): the record must carry
the same `id` and `name` and a `keywords` string array, and it is the stored record. A failure (the
§6 message; `Dictionary keywords were not returned by the region: <name>` for a missing array, TS
text) is that dictionary's `failed` row; the run continues, the dictionary is not stored, and
`complete` is `false` (TS fails the whole backup; with the keyword-bearing listing a single large
page could fail it, D175). A profile that references such a dictionary stays stored; restore
treats that reference as unresolved (§16.11).

**Format** (Rust-only; D175). One JSON document in the §2.2 layout plus `"\n"`, keys in this
order:

```json
{
  "format": "airs-cli-rs.dlp-resources",
  "version": 1,
  "exportedAt": "2026-10-18T12:00:00.000Z",
  "tenant": "redtail-prod",
  "tsgId": "100",
  "dlpTenantId": "src-tenant",
  "resources": ["dictionaries", "patterns", "profiles"],
  "complete": true,
  "dictionaries": [{"id": "…", "name": "Secret Words", "predefined": false, "record": {…}}],
  "patterns": [{"id": "…", "name": "Social Security Numbers", "predefined": true, "record": {"id": "…", "name": "…", "type": "predefined", "version": 3, "detection_config": {"technique": "ml"}}}],
  "profiles": [{"id": "…", "name": "PII Guardrail", "predefined": false, "record": {…}}],
  "skipped": [{"kind": "profile", "id": "…", "name": "Multi", "reason": "Unsupported detection rule type: multi_profile"}],
  "failed": [{"kind": "dictionary", "id": "…", "name": "…", "error": "<the §6 message>"}]
}
```

- `tenant` is the store name, `tsgId` the tenant's `mgmtTsgId` (§3.7), `dlpTenantId` the uniform
  `tenant_id` of the inventories (`null` when none), `resources` the selection in canonical
  order; `complete` is `true` exactly when `skipped` and `failed` are empty.
- Entries are sorted by name (the `localeCompare` approximation of §15.17), predefined stubs
  included; `predefined` is `record.type == "predefined"`; an entry's `id` and `name` equal its
  record's. `record` is the SDK response model re-serialised (lossless: absent and `null` kept,
  unknown keys kept, schema order with sorted extensions; no default is inserted, G10).
- Serialised size at most 20 MiB, else `Backup exceeds the 20 MiB size limit; select fewer --resources`
  (TS, exit 1, no file).
- **Content**: the file holds every keyword, regex, proximity keyword, description and
  `audit_metadata` of the stored custom resources in clear (a restore must recreate them; TS does
  the same at 0600). After writing, when it stores any custom dictionary or pattern, the warning
  `  ⚠ <path> contains DLP dictionary keywords and pattern definitions; keep it private (mode 0600)`
  (yellow, never quiet-suppressed).

**Publishing.** `files::publish_new` (§15.18: temp `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` 0600 in the destination
directory, `fsync`, `link`, unlink, directory `fsync`) after every read; an existing path at link
time is `<path> already exists; choose another --output-file`; any other failure
`Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable` (exit 1). Nothing is
written when the run fails before publishing.

**Output** (stdout; the progress line `  ℹ Reading inventories (dictionaries, data patterns, data profiles)…`
on stderr, cyan, quiet-suppressed, every format; TS: stdout, pretty only, D172). pretty and table:
the TS one-row table `Backup file │ Source TSG │ Dictionaries │ Patterns │ Profiles │ Skipped │ Failed`
(the counts are the entry counts, predefined stubs included; `Failed` is Rust-only); json:
`[{"file", "sourceTsgId", "dictionaries", "patterns", "profiles", "skipped", "failed", "complete"}]`
(TS's one-element array; `file` as given, TS absolute; `failed` and `complete` Rust-only). Each
failed row is also a stderr warning `  ⚠ Could not back up <kind> <name>: <message>`. Exit 1 when
any row failed (after the file and the summary); otherwise 0. Interrupt contexts:
`no backup file was written`, or `the backup was saved in <path>` once it was linked.

### 16.11 `runtime dlp restore <file>`

**Argument checks** (exit 2, in order, before the file): `--on-conflict` ∉
`error|verify|skip|reconcile`: `--on-conflict must be error, verify, skip or reconcile` (TS);
`--force` without `--expect-tsg`: `--force requires --expect-tsg <destination-tsg>` (TS);
`--dry-run` with `--force`: `--dry-run cannot be combined with --force` (§15.19; TS accepts it,
D176); `--pattern-map` without a `=` inside (index 0, the end, or none):
`--pattern-map requires source-name=destination-name`, a repeated source:
`Duplicate source names in --pattern-map` (TS); `--name-prefix` longer than 64 UTF-16 units or
holding a C0 control or DEL: `Invalid --name-prefix` (TS: exit 1 in the plan, D162);
`--max-pages` as backup; `--expect-tsg` not 1–32 ASCII digits:
`--expect-tsg must be a TSG ID (1-32 digits)`; without `--dry-run` and `--force`, stdin or
stderr not a terminal: `refusing to restore DLP resources without --force in non-interactive mode`
(D167; TS decides after the plan and only when something would be created, choice 18).

**The file** (after the debug log, before the tenant; the §16.3 input rules, 20 MiB, UTF-8;
exit 1; nothing from the file is echoed but names through `terminal_safe`):
- not JSON (the D44 classes included) and not recognised as TypeScript YAML:
  `Invalid DLP backup <path>: malformed JSON`;
- a TypeScript backup (a JSON object with a `resourceType` key, or a `version` without a
  `format`; a text with a `resourceType:` line or a `version: 1` line, the `--file-format yaml`
  envelope): `<path> is a TypeScript airs-cli backup; airs cannot restore it. Restore it with the TypeScript airs-cli, or back the resources up again with 'airs runtime dlp backup'.`
  (D176; no import of TypeScript backups). No file-name extension is required (TS requires
  `.json|.yaml|.yml`);
- `format` correct and `version` above 1: `<path> was written by a newer version of airs; upgrade airs to restore it`;
- anything else that breaks the §16.10 format: `Invalid DLP backup <path>: <reason>` with a fixed
  `<reason>`: `the file does not hold a JSON object`, `it is not an airs DLP backup` (a
  `format` other than `airs-cli-rs.dlp-resources`, the red team targets backup included),
  `version must be 1`, `the envelope has an unknown key`, `<key> must be a string`,
  `dlpTenantId must be a string or null`, `resources must be a unique list of dictionaries, patterns, profiles`,
  `complete must be true or false`, `<kind> must be an array`, `<kind> holds more than 10000 entries`,
  `<kind>[<i>] must have exactly the keys id, name, predefined, record`,
  `<kind>[<i>] does not match the <label> response schema`, `<kind>[<i>] id and name must be its record's`,
  `<kind>[<i>] predefined must match its record's type`, `skipped[<i>] must have exactly the keys kind, id, name, reason`,
  `failed[<i>] must have exactly the keys kind, id, name, error`, `complete does not match the skipped and failed lists`
  (records checked with the SDK response schemas, `Mode::Response`);
- `complete: false`: the warning
  `  ⚠ <path> is incomplete: <n> resource(s) were skipped or could not be backed up` (not fatal);
- every `--pattern-map` source must be a backup pattern name, else
  `--pattern-map names absent from the backup: <a>, <b>` (TS text; exit 1, before the tenant).

**Tenant checks** (after the tenant and credential checks, before the client and any request;
exit 1): the file's
`tsgId` must equal the tenant's `mgmtTsgId`, else
`<path> was exported from TSG <a>; the selected tenant uses TSG <b>. Pass --allow-other-tenant to restore it here.`
(§15.19; TS checks nothing here, D176, choice 17); then `--expect-tsg`, when given, must equal
`mgmtTsgId`: `--expect-tsg does not match the selected destination tenant; no API request was made`
