(TS text; TS exit 2, D161).

**Plan** (no write; TS `planDlpResourcesRestore`, TB§5.2–§5.5, unchanged except as listed): the
validation before any request (duplicate names per kind, duplicate dependency ids across
dictionaries and patterns, `crossTenant`), then `  ℹ Reading inventories (dictionaries, data patterns, data profiles)…`
(stderr, quiet-suppressed) and the three destination inventories (§16.10 inventory mode; an
incomplete one plans nothing: its error, exit 1), then the keywords of every destination dictionary
whose name a custom backup dictionary's (prefixed) name matches, read per id
(`GET /v2/api/dictionaries/<id>?keywords=true`, a read with the SDK retries; the inventory carries no
keywords, G13; TS lists them with `keywords=true`), the DLP `tenant_id` checks (TS texts:
`Destination credentials report the source DLP tenant; check the selected tenant before restoring`,
`Destination DLP tenant does not match the backup source; use distinct tenant credentials deliberately`),
then the dictionary, pattern and profile rows of TB§5.4–§5.5 with every TS refusal and text
(missing predefined destinations with ranked candidates, `--pattern-map` binding, tenant-bound
techniques, unexported content, differing destinations, ambiguous names, cross-tenant id
references, references absent from the backup, version pins, the 32-unit profile name,
`basic` profiles, `--on-conflict error` on an existing profile, `verify` echoes, `compareEcho`,
the CSV/TXT upload text rules). Additions: a profile that references a dependency listed under
the file's `failed` is unresolved (`its <kind> <name> could not be backed up`; skipped with
`--skip-unresolved`, else `Backup data profile references a resource that could not be backed up: <name>`,
exit 1); every server name in a message goes through `terminal_safe`. The plan's warnings
(`  ⚠ Unresolved dictionary: …`, `  ⚠ Unresolved data pattern: …`, `  ⚠ Skipping data profile: …`,
TS texts) go to stderr, never suppressed.

**Never duplicates, never overwrites** (D177). Restore sends only `POST` creates and `GET`s: no
`PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` ever (TS invariant, kept and tested), and no write to a predefined
resource. An existing same-name dictionary or pattern is reused only when it echoes the backup
(`compareEcho`), otherwise the plan is refused; a profile follows `--on-conflict`. Under
`reconcile`, the suffixed name of a profile is deterministic: `<base>-<6 hex>`, the hex the first
6 lowercase hex digits of SHA-256 over `<backup tsgId>:<source profile id>`, `<base>` the prefixed
name cut so the result fits 32 UTF-16 units (TS cut rule); the planner looks the suffixed name up
too, and an active profile there plans `verify` (it must echo, else
`Destination data profile does not match restore plan: <name>; verification made no changes`), so
a re-run never creates another copy (TS draws a random suffix, so every re-run after an
archived-name collision creates one more permanent profile, choice 19).

**`--dry-run`** prints the plan (below) and writes nothing; exit 0 (TS), exit 1 when the plan was
refused (its error).

**Confirmation.** Without `--force`, when the plan has at least one `create`: the prompt
`Restore <n> DLP resources from TSG <a> to TSG <b>?` (TS text; `<n>` the create rows) after the
plan and its warnings, before the recheck. A plan without a `create` runs without a prompt.

**Recheck and writes** (TB§5.9; D160, D177). `  ℹ Rechecking destination state before writing…`,
the three inventories again; a planned item whose current name match is not canonically equal to
the planned one (or exists for a `create`) is `Destination <kind> changed after planning: <name>`
(exit 1, no write). Then the stages in order (`  ℹ Restoring <dictionaries|data patterns|data profiles> (<n>)…`,
stderr, quiet-suppressed), items in plan order, each bullet
`  ✓ <dictionary|data pattern|data profile> <action>: <name> (<i>/<n>)` (or `  ○ … skipped: …`) on
stderr, quiet-suppressed (TS: stdout, not suppressed, D172):
- a `create` is **one attempt** (`writes::attempt`: a 401 replayed once, a 403 never, no replay
  after a 5xx, a timeout or a transport error; TS replays after a 403, TB§5.11): dictionaries
  `POST /v2/api/dictionaries?keywords=true` with `DictionaryUpload::text(<rebuilt metadata>,
  <the TS keyword text>)` (`text/plain`, TS), patterns and profiles their JSON `POST`; then the
  read-back `GET` (a read with the SDK retries; dictionaries with `keywords=true`), which must
  carry the created id and name, echo the request and not be retired (TS); the binding is set
  from it;
- under `--on-conflict reconcile`, a profile create answered 409 (`Rejected`, nothing created) is
  followed by one create under the deterministic suffixed name (a different body after a
  definite rejection, one attempt), row `created` with `renamedFrom`;
- **the run stops at the first failure of any kind** (TS): every later item is `notAttempted`.
  A rejected create (3xx, 4xx) reports `API request failed (HTTP <s>); verify destination state before retrying`
  (TS text); an `Unknown` outcome (5xx, transport, timeout, a cancel after dispatch) reports
  `Outcome unknown: the <dictionary|data pattern|data profile> <name> may have been created; run the restore again to reuse it (a data profile needs --on-conflict verify)`
  (for the reconcile copy under its suffixed name:
  `…; run the restore again with --on-conflict reconcile to verify it`, the only mode whose plan
  looks the copy up) and is recorded in `outcomeUnknown` (TS: `API request failed (HTTP 502)` or
  `Restore stopped; …`, with nothing saying the resource may exist); a 2xx whose answer or
  read-back fails or does not echo keeps TS's unverified-create receipt and suffix
  (`; unverified create: <kind> <name> (id <id>); inspect this resource before retrying`); a
  local failure before dispatch is `Restore stopped; verify destination state before retrying` (TS).

**Output** (stdout data; TS `renderRestore`, TB§5.7, §5.10). pretty and table: the TS blocks
joined by `"\n\n"`: the heading (`Restore preview — no changes made`, `Restore complete` or
`Restore incomplete — completed writes remain`), `Source TSG: <a>`, `Destination TSG: <b>`, the
`Dictionaries (<n>)`, `Data patterns (<n>)`, `Data profiles (<n>)` tables (`Action │ Name`, or
`(none)`), then when present `Unresolved references — dependent profiles skipped` with
`<kind> <name>: <reason>` lines, `Created resources awaiting verification` (`Resource │ Name │ Created ID`),
`Renamed around archived-name collisions` (`<from> -> <to>`),
`Verified server-added fields (source omitted these)`, and the Rust-only blocks
`Possibly created (outcome unknown)` (`Resource │ Name`) and `Not attempted` (`Resource │ Name`),
then `Error: <message>` when incomplete. json: TS's one-element array, dry run
`[{"sourceTsgId", "destinationTsgId", "dryRun": true, "dictionaries", "patterns", "profiles", "unresolved"}]`
(rows `{name, action[, reason]}`, actions `create|reuse|resolve|map|verify|skip`), execution
`[{"sourceTsgId", "destinationTsgId", "complete", "dictionaries", "patterns", "profiles", "serverAdded", "unverifiedCreates", "unresolved", "outcomeUnknown", "notAttempted", "error"?}]`
(rows `{name, action, id[, reason][, renamedFrom]}` with `created|reused|resolved|mapped|verified|skipped`;
`outcomeUnknown` `{kind, name}` or `null` and `notAttempted` `[{kind, name}]` are Rust-only). An
incomplete run also prints `  ✗ <error>` on stderr. Exit 1 when not complete; 0 when complete.

**Interruption.** Before the first write: `nothing was changed`. After it:
`<c> resource(s) created[; the <kind> <name> may also have been created (outcome unknown)]; run the restore again to resume`
(a create cancelled after it was sent counts as outcome unknown). TS dies by the signal with
nothing printed (D174).

**Filtering profiles** are neither backed up nor restored (TS parity: tenant configuration with
no create).

### 16.12 Details resolved for the implementer

- **Unknown pages.** A list page without `content` (or with a non-array `content`) is a decode
  error (the SDK schema).
- **`--include-predefined` on `filtering-profiles list`** stays an unknown option (clap, exit 2, D1).
- **Patch of an archived pattern** (`status: deleted`) is sent (the service decides); only
  `predefined` and parent-managed records are refused.
- **The soft delete.** A pattern `delete` answered 2xx is a success even though the record stays
  readable; nothing reads it back.
- **Restore names.** The 32-unit profile limit and the prefix length are counted in UTF-16 units.

Resolved while building step 3 (backup, restore, live):
- **Inventory metadata types.** A page metadata field present with a value of the wrong type
  (`null` included) is `Inventory of <label> has inconsistent pagination metadata; retry the
  operation` (fail closed; TS's `alias` treats a `null` on one spelling of an aliased field as
  absent); a `pageable` that is not an object supplies nothing (TS optional chaining). The sweep is
  `dlp::backup::Sweep`, one deadline (§5 walk budget) for the three inventories of a run.
- **Skipped profiles add nothing.** A profile's dependencies are added only when every one of its
  leaves passes (TS adds the dependencies of the leaves before the failing one).
- **Order of the backup.** The progress line, then the skipped-profile warnings, then the keyword
  reads and their `Could not back up` warnings, then the file and its content warning, then the
  summary. A keyword read interrupted reports `no backup file was written`.
- **Restore file checks before the tenant.** After the file is parsed: the `complete: false`
  warning, the `--pattern-map` absence check and the name and dependency-identity checks of the
  plan (file-only, exit 1); then the tenant, the credentials and the TSG checks.
- **Keywords at planning** (G13): see §16.11 "Plan"; the recheck compares the inventory records
  (without keywords) canonically.
- **Upload order.** The keyword text is the backup's keywords sorted by UTF-16 code units (TS
  `keywordSet`, which the plan stores and uploads; the research said backup order).
- **Rebuilt metadata** must also pass the SDK's multipart file-name rule
  (`Dictionary cannot be rebuilt from the backup: <name>` during planning; the SDK would refuse it
  at the upload).
- **A rebuilt profile body that fails `AdvancedDataProfileRequest`** is TS's
  `Invalid DLP backup/request schema; content is not logged.` (exit 1, during planning).
- **Recheck texts** are TS's two: an existing match that changed is
  `Destination <kind>: <name> changed after planning`; a match where a create was planned is
  `Destination <kind> changed after planning: <name>` (`<kind>` `dictionary`, `data pattern`,
  `data profile`).
- **A 2xx create whose answer cannot be read**, or that decodes but carries no usable `id`:
  the error
  `Outcome: the <kind> <name> was created, but the response could not be read; run the restore again to reuse it (a data profile needs --on-conflict verify)`
  (the reconcile copy: `…; run the restore again with --on-conflict reconcile to verify it`),
  recorded in `outcomeUnknown` (its id is unknown), so the interrupt context is never
  `nothing was changed`; TS reports `Restored <kind> did not verify: <name>`.
- **Failed dependencies**: a profile skipped by them under `--skip-unresolved` reads
  `its <dictionary|data pattern> <name> could not be backed up`, after
  `unresolved references: …` and joined with `; `.
- **Reconcile verify.** A suffixed copy found by the planner is a `verify` row named by the suffixed
  name; the result row carries `renamedFrom`.
- **Result json.** `unresolved` keeps TS's full execution shape `{kind, sourceId, name, reason[,
  candidates]}`; `outcomeUnknown` and `notAttempted` use the `unverifiedCreates` kinds
  (`dictionaries`, `patterns`, `profiles`); `notAttempted` lists every planned row after the one
  that stopped the run (all of them when the recheck stopped it). `serverAdded` field paths are
  listed in key order (D35).
- **Progress and bullets.** `ℹ` lines (`Output::info`) and the item bullets (glyph coloured, TS
  `ui.bullet`) on stderr in every format, quiet-suppressed; not printed after a signal.

Resolved while building step 2 (the writes):
- **Planning order.** The `<id>` check comes first, then the command's builder or hatch checks
  in the order of its section, then the D81 gate (the last argument check). `profiles
  create|replace` check `--profile-type` before the hatch (TS, also with a body). A body known
  during planning (flag-built, `--body <json>`, a merge patch) passes its whole §16.3 check then
  (`type: predefined`, the profile name and type, the schema; exit 2, no debug log); a file or
  stdin body passes the same checks after its read, before the tenant (still exit 2: only the
  read and the JSON parse of a file exit 1).
- **Bodies completed from server data.** A flag-built `patterns replace` without `--type` or
  `--technique` is checked during planning with TS's defaults, then completed from the guard
  read and checked again (exit 1). A flag-built profile body with `--pattern-id` has no rules
  during planning, so only its flag rules are checked then; the body is checked once its rules
  are built from the pattern reads (exit 1).
- **`--body -`.** Piped stdin is read whole up to 1 MiB; more, an unreadable stream or bytes
  that are not UTF-8 are `--body - must be UTF-8 JSON of at most 1 MiB on stdin` (exit 2, no
  content echoed); empty stdin is `--body is not valid JSON` (profiles: TS's texts).
- **File texts per resource.** A `--body-file` that is not JSON or not an object reads
  `<path> is not valid JSON` / `<path> must contain a JSON object` (patterns, filtering
  profiles; §13.2), `Cannot read profile body as JSON; …` / `Profile body must be a JSON object`
  (profile create and replace), `Invalid profile patch: …` / `Profile body must be a JSON
  object` (profile patch, TS's masked text) and `Invalid JSON in dictionary metadata file` /
  `Dictionary metadata must be a JSON object` (`--metadata-file`, dictionary patch); all exit 1.
  `--metadata-file ""` is `--metadata-file needs a path` (exit 2).
- **`--metadata-file` help.** `dictionaries create` says `JSON metadata file (cannot be combined
  with --name/--category/...)` (TS: `overrides …`, which D165 no longer does); `replace` keeps
  TS's `JSON metadata file`.
- **Merge patch.** `--set`/`--clear` take every following value up to the next option (clap
  `num_args = 1..`, as commander's variadic options); `--clear ''` sends `"": null` (TS). A
  `--weighted-regex` weight is sent as JavaScript `Number()` would (an integral value as an
  integer); weights are not subject to the 2^53 rule.
- **The omitted fields.** A key present in the replacement body counts as set even when its
  value is `null`; the list names only the fields of the request schema of §16.3.
- **Acks.** The table ack is the §2.7 table of the ack keys with `cell_text` values. The success
  line is `Output::success` (terminal-safe, quiet-suppressed, not printed after a signal); a name
  carrying a tenant secret is `[withheld]` there and in the prompt.
- **The region hint** follows any `Http` 400 whose problem is absent or has neither `detail`
  nor field `errors`; it is written uncoloured on stderr before the error block and is not
  quiet-suppressed (it belongs to the error).
- **The dictionary replace without a body.** An interruption during the re-read reports
  `the change was saved` (the PUT succeeded).
- **`profiles delete`** validates `--output`, does not check the id (TS), opens no debug log
  (its plan's debug policy is `None`) and prints TS's red multi-line block.
- **Prompts.** No request is open while a prompt waits; the guard read and, for profiles, the
  pattern reads come before it.

Resolved while building step 1 (the reads):
- **The hidden aliases.** Only the effective value is checked: an explicit `--limit` wins over
  `--size` and an explicit `--offset` over `--page`, and the losing alias is neither sent nor
  validated (TS ignores it too); a `--size` error reads `--limit must be a positive integer`.
  The `--size` warning comes before the `--page` warning. `--page <p>` on a server page sends
  `page=<p>` with no `size` unless `--limit` is given (TS: the page of the server's default
  size); on a custom-only list it starts the slice at `p × (--limit or 50)`.
- **Status numbers.** A single server page's line takes TS `pageMeta`'s numbers: the page from
  `pageable.pageNumber` (or `page_number`, else 0), the size from `pageable.pageSize` (or
  `page_size`, else the rows returned), the total from `totalElements` (or `total_elements`).
- **`Updated`.** A number `0` is dropped (falsy in TS) and a fraction is truncated (TS
  `TimeClip`); the date-only forms `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` and `YYYY-MM-DD` are UTC midnight; a
  date-time needs a `Z` or `±hh:mm` offset; one without is dropped (JavaScript reads it as local
  time, which depends on the machine). Years outside 0–9999 print in the six-digit signed form,
  as `toISOString`.
- **`[withheld]`.** The check applies to the `name`, `description`, `region_name` and `category`
  strings at any depth of a record (a rule item's `name` included), with the "contains a
  registered form" rule (`SecretSet::carried_by`, no fragment rule), before the camelCasing.
- **Enum vocabulary** (D178): scm-sdk's response mode keeps an unfamiliar enum value (TS fails the
  read); a pretty status that is not `active`, `deleted` or `disabled` is dim, as TS.
- **Help.** The group descriptions keep TypeScript's final period (clap would strip a doc
  comment's); clap adds ` [aliases: ls]` to the `list` entries.
- **The custom-only walk** has no user cap: it reads up to the 1,000,000-row safety bound (D40
  beyond it) before the predefined rows are dropped; `--max` applies to the custom rows.

### 16.14 Acceptance tests

Every behaviour above gets an executable test (`tests/dlp_*.rs`), unit tests in `src/dlp/`,
parity tests (`tests/parity_dlp_*.rs`) and a `dNN_` test per §12 row. The TypeScript specs (TD§15,
TB§7) are ported first:

| TypeScript spec | Rust acceptance tests (adjusted by the §12 rows) |
|---|---|
| `unit/cli/dlp-build-body.spec.ts` | the pattern builder (defaults, weighted regex at the last pipe, confidence CSV, tags CSV and errors, proximity fields; errors without values, D163, D162), the filtering-profile builder (both booleans, optional fields), the profile builder (32 characters, `advanced`, `or` default, combinators, confidence support, `basic` refused) |
| `unit/cli/dlp-patch.spec.ts` | the coercion table, `--set k=null`, dotted keys, malformed entries, the empty patch; the body file, piped stdin and malformed bodies (fixed texts, D163) |
| `unit/cli/dlp-renderer.spec.ts` | json lists and gets are the camelCase records (tag keys kept, D171), a bare array, the acks in each format, the `archived`/`deleted` lines and the 204 warning on stderr (D172) |
| `unit/cli/dlp-visibility.spec.ts` | predefined rows hidden by default across every page and shown with `--include-predefined` (D170) |
| `unit/cli/dlp-delete-safety.spec.ts` | `profiles delete`: no request, exit 2, the texts (`not live-verified`, `No API request was sent`), no `--set profile_status`; and the D166 guard on every replace, patch and delete |
| `unit/cli/dlp-debug.spec.ts` | the debug log of every DLP command holds status and headers only, never a body or query, with `--debug` before and after the subcommand |
| `unit/airs/dlp/*.spec.ts` | the request shapes per operation, the dictionary replace 200, the empty 2xx with its re-get and fallback (D172), `client-wiring`: the DLP base only from the tenant's `dlpEndpoint` or the default |
| `integration/dlp-dictionary-errors.spec.ts` | the multipart parts, field errors exit 1, the region hint, usage errors before any request, no keyword or metadata value in any output, debug bodies absent |
| `integration/dlp-profile-pattern-flags.spec.ts` | the GET sequence and leaf shape, missing, inactive and mismatched patterns stop before the write, `basic` refused, 32/33-character names for flags and bodies, a repeated `--pattern-id` refused |
| `integration/dlp-tenant-auth.spec.ts` | each group uses only the selected tenant's credentials and `dlpEndpoint`, per-tenant TSG, environment ignored, tenant files unchanged (COMPATIBILITY.md §5.2 gains the DLP rows) |
| `unit/backup/dlp-resources.spec.ts` | `backupDlpResources` (closure, sorting, selection, retired and predefined exclusion, every unsupported reason at once, `--skip-unsupported` now recorded, EDM, unknown ids, keyword failures as failed rows, duplicate names, every inventory check), `planDlpResourcesRestore` (every plan case and text) and `restoreDlpResources` (prefixed restore with remapped ids and versions, resumable second pass, recheck, read-back failures, receipts, reconcile with the deterministic suffix and its re-run, D177), over the Rust format (D175, D176) |
| `integration/dlp-transfer-contract.spec.ts` | the HTTP contract over the binary: aggregated misses with no write, `--pattern-map` with its re-GET, a mixed profile skipped while another is created, a dictionary create then a 400 stopping before patterns without leaking keywords, a Rust-format file restored with ids remapped, no `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` ever, no marker in any output |

Rust additions: every §16.3 argument check with zero requests and no debug log; the D160 sequences
on each write (a 5xx with `Retry-After: 0`: one Rust request and the outcome line, more than one
TypeScript request with no exact count; a 401: `token, write, token, write` on both; a 403: one Rust
request), the upload counters after 5xx, held-then-dropped and SIGINT cases; every confirmation on
the pty (`y`, `yes`, Enter, `n`, EOF, Ctrl-C) and its non-interactive refusal; the omitted-fields
list (D168); the guard on seeded predefined and parent-managed records of every kind with a
never-hit write counter (D166); the client-sliced listing across pages and its status lines (D170);
the walk errors (repeated id, empty intermediate page, a capped page size that continues); the
backup publishing (an existing path, a dangling symlink, a symlinked directory, 0600, no temporary
left, a held-then-killed run) before any request; the restore file rules, TSG checks and the stop at
the first failure with `outcomeUnknown` (a 5xx, a held-then-dropped create); sensitive markers in
every fixture body never on stderr, in the debug log or in a summary (§10); interruption in every
context of §16.13.

### 16.15 Choices recorded for confirmation

These are the spec's resolutions (1–27), the details resolved while building (28–31) and the
resolutions of the 0.7 review (32–35); each is safe as written, and the user confirmed all of
them (2026-10-18).
1. **Live data-profile writes are dropped** (G11): the API cannot delete a profile and a deleted
   name stays reserved, so any live profile create leaves a permanent resource; profile
   create/replace/patch are tested on loopback only. This departs from the live rule as written
   ("… and a data profile that references only run-created patterns"); the alternative is one
   permanent, ledgered `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-profile…` per CLI per run (not recommended).
2. The predefined guard also refuses records with `is_parent_managed: true` (D166); the
   alternative refuses only `type: predefined`.
3. Predefined filtering profiles are refused like the other kinds (D166).
4. Confirmations on both deletes, every replace and restore; `patch` and `create` do not confirm
   (D167).
5. A replace stays a full replacement (TS semantics) and lists the fields it would drop in the
   prompt or a `--force` warning (D168); the read-modify-write overlay for filtering profiles was
   rejected because response values (`c2s`, `low`) do not fit the request enums.
6. `patterns replace` keeps the current `type` and technique when `--type`/`--technique` are
   absent (D169).
7. Default listings (custom only) read every page and slice locally; `--include-predefined` and
   filtering-profile lists stay single server pages (D170).
8. The hidden `--size`/`--page` aliases are kept with their deprecation warnings (as `--format`,
   `--input`, `--confirm`).
9. JSON keeps the keys under `tags` and `exclusions.exclusion_list` verbatim (D171); the
   alternative is full parity with TS's camelCasing of data keys.
10. Keyword lists, regexes and rule trees are printed by json and the get table when the record
    (and `--keywords`) is asked for (TS parity); the alternative restricts them to json only.
11. A repeated `--pattern-id` is a usage error (D162); the alternative de-duplicates silently.
12. Body-shaped input on argv (`--body`, `--regex`) is not refused (it is not a credential).
13. The keyword file is sent as bytes (no UTF-8 or CSV-header check), at most 7 MiB.
14. A merge patch must repeat the schema's required fields (TS parity); the CLI does not fill
    them from the current record.
15. `--body -` on a terminal is a usage error (TS blocks waiting for input).
16. Backups read keywords per dictionary and record a failed read as a failed row (`complete:
    false`, exit 1) instead of failing the run (D175, G13).
17. Restore refuses a backup from another TSG unless `--allow-other-tenant` (as §15.19), keeps
    `--expect-tsg` and TS's "`--force` requires `--expect-tsg`" (D176). TS documents cross-TSG
    migration (prod → dev) as the main use; with this choice it needs the flag.
18. A non-dry-run restore without `--force` and without a terminal is refused up front, before
    the tenant, even when the plan would create nothing (D167); TS refuses after the plan and
    only when something would be created. Scripted runs pass `--force --expect-tsg <tsg>`.
19. `--on-conflict reconcile` uses a deterministic suffix and looks it up while planning, so a
    re-run never creates another permanent profile copy (D177).
20. Restore stops at the first failure of any kind (TS), not only at an unknown outcome.
21. Backup and restore reads use the SDK's replay-safe retries (TS sends every read once); the
    inventory consistency checks still apply (D175).
22. Restore accepts any file name and decides by content; backup keeps TS's `.json` extension
    rule.
23. A backup with nothing to back up exits 1 with no file (TS), unlike `targets backup` (exit 0).
24. Checks that need server data (`--confidence` support, a re-validated body) and the
    `--expect-tsg` mismatch exit 1 (TS: 2) (D161).
25. TypeScript's empty help strings stay empty.
26. Live restore (§10): Rust only, a `--dry-run` and then a real restore of a composed backup that
    holds only the run's own Rust pattern and dictionary under the run prefix, both copies deleted
    in teardown (6 resources per run at most); a restore of a real tenant backup never runs live.
27. Live pattern and dictionary deletes count as cleaned up when the record then reads back with
    `status: "deleted"` or 404 (soft deletes).
28. An unfamiliar enum value in a DLP response is printed rather than failing the read (D178,
    found in step 1: scm-sdk's tolerant response mode). Resolved in step 2 toward safety: the
    predefined guard also refuses a record whose `type` is outside the tenant-created
    vocabulary of its SDK enum (§16.3), so a new `type` is never written; reads still print it.
    The alternative is a CLI-side strict enum check on reads too (TS parity for reads).
29. Restore reads the keywords of each same-name destination dictionary per id before planning
    (G13; the reuse check needs them); a failed read stops the plan (its §6 message, exit 1).
30. A 2xx create whose answer cannot be read stops the run and is recorded in `outcomeUnknown`
    (the resource exists, its id is unknown); the alternative is a separate json key.
31. A page metadata field of the wrong type, `null` included, fails the inventory (stricter than
    TS for a `null` on one spelling).

Resolved while fixing the step-3 review findings:
32. A restore create answered 2xx without a usable `id` is choice 30's unreadable outcome
    (`outcomeUnknown`, `created` not counted, so the interrupt context names it as possibly
    created); the alternative is counting it in `created` too.
33. The outcome-unknown hint of a reconcile copy names `--on-conflict reconcile` (the only mode
    whose plan looks the suffixed copy up); the alternative is making `--on-conflict verify`
    look the suffixed name up as well.
34. The custom-only `dictionaries list --keywords` walks without keywords and reads the shown
    rows' keywords per id (G13); a failed keyword read fails the list. The alternative is a
    smaller page size with `keywords=true` (still every keyword of the tenant for `--limit 1`).
35. The live DLP ledger journals a restore copy left in `unverifiedCreates` as `unknown` with
    its id (the create was confirmed, its read-back was not); the alternative is `ok`. Extra
    same-name records left by TypeScript's SDK retries are deleted at teardown and counted in
    `resourcesCreated`, but not charged to the run's 10-create budget before they exist.

## 17. M6c Model Security (0.8)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-model-security.md` (cited as
**MS§n**), `docs/research/ts-model-security-install.md` (cited as **MI§n**) and
`docs/research/rs-sdk-model-security.md` (cited as **MK§n**). This section overrides them where
they differ (the two install proposals disagree on names, markers and rules; this section is the
decision); their provisional row numbers and recommendations are not binding. Every difference
from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row (D179–D203; D11, D50, D52, D64 and D116 extended). The byte
captures of the TypeScript layouts are in MS§5–§11 and MI§3–§4; "the TS layout" below means
those bytes, with the changes this section lists.

**SDK.** scm-sdk 0.1.1 has an operation for every command of this section, with the TypeScript
paths, methods, queries and request and response schemas (MK§0, MK§4). 0.8 adds `"model-security"`
to the `scm` dependency's features (`model-security = ["models"]`, `scm-sdk Cargo.toml:66`; no new
crate). The findings of MK§9:
- **G18 — blocked on scm-sdk (server-side filter); CLI workaround adopted.**
  `ModelSecurityScanListOptions` has no `scan_origin` field (`rs:airs/model_security/query.rs:62-97`),
  so no scm-sdk 0.1.1 call can send the `scans list --scan-origin` filter to the service (the TS
  SDK drops it too, `SDK:13622-13638`, so TS silently lists every origin). The SDK is not patched.
  The CLI filters locally over a complete walk (§17.5, D181), which is exact; only the server-side
  filtering (fewer bytes, fewer pages) waits for an SDK release that adds the field. Whether the
  service honours a `scan_origin` query at all is unverified; no raw request is used.
- **G19.** The SDK skip/limit walks (`pages`, `list_all`, `model_pages`, `version_pages`,
  `file_pages`) have no repeated-row check and end silently at an empty page while
  `total_items` says more rows exist (`ms:mod.rs:63-73`). The CLI never calls them: every walk is
  the shared page loop `walk` over the single-page calls (§17.3 "Lists and walks"), the D147 loop
  of red team moved to `src/walk.rs`. Safe.
- **G20 (G10 for M6c).** The frozen schemas default `EvalSummary.rules_failed`, `rules_passed` and
  `total_rules` to `0` (reached from `ScanBaseResponse`, `ScanList`, `ModelVersionResponse`,
  `ModelVersionList`), so a typed read with the default options turns a summary the server sent
  without counts into "0 failed". **Every model-security SDK call passes
  `RequestOptions::…without_response_defaults()`** (one options helper, `modelsec::options`), also
  where it changes nothing (groups, rules, rule instances, evaluations, violations, files, labels,
  models, `get_pypi_auth`, whose schema has no default): the output never shows a count the server
  did not send (D180). The request-side default `description: ""` of
  `ModelSecurityGroupCreateRequest` is applied by both SDKs (TS parity, not a difference).
- **G21** (difference): `labels values <key>` goes through the SDK segment rule (`.segment(key)`,
  `rs:config.rs:121-151`), which refuses `''`, `.`, `..`, `\`, control characters and encoded
  traversal; the CLI checks it during planning (§17.3, D184).
- **G22** (ergonomics): the options structs are `#[non_exhaustive]` with `Default` only (and
  `ModelSecurityViolationListOptions`, `ModelSecurityModelVersionFileListOptions` alias
  `ModelSecurityLabelListOptions`); built with `Default::default()` and field assignment.
- **G23** (operation names): the `--debug` log records them as they are
  (`airs.model_security.groups.*`, `….rules.*`, `….scans.*`, `….models.*`,
  `airs.model_security.get_pypi_auth`, MK§3); the debug tests pin them, as G9 and G17.
- **G24** (shape): `PyPIAuthResponse.url` is a plain `String` (only its `Debug` is redacted,
  `gen:159042-159046`); the CLI parses it and registers its credential in the `SecretSet` before
  anything else uses it (§17.12).
- G3, G4 and G7 apply unchanged. **Nothing else in §17 is blocked on scm-sdk.**
- **Blocked on the service, not on the SDK:** the API has no scan DELETE (neither SDK has one), so a
  scan created by the live scan flow stays in the tenant (§10, choice 37).

### 17.1 Build steps

0.8 is built in three steps. Each step ships its executable, parity and `dNN_` tests and leaves
the checks green.

| Step | Commands and work |
|---|---|
| 1. Reads | `model-security groups list\|ls`, `groups get`; `rules list\|ls`, `rules get`; `rule-instances list\|ls`, `rule-instances get`; `scans list\|ls`, `scans get`, `scans evaluations`, `scans evaluation`, `scans violations`, `scans violation`, `scans files`; `models list\|ls`, `models get`, `models versions`, `models version`, `models files`; `labels keys`, `labels values`. Shared: the `model-security` feature, `ModelSecurityClients::build`, the argument checks of §17.3, `src/walk.rs` (moved from `src/redteam/walk.rs`, with the `count_capped` latch), the views and layouts of §17.4–§17.7, the withheld URI form, the fixture's model-security read routes |
| 2. Writes | `groups create`, `groups update`, `groups delete\|rm`; `rule-instances update`; `scans create`; `labels add`, `labels set`, `labels delete\|rm`. Shared: the `--config` readers and body checks, `--labels`/`--keys`, the confirmations, the delete verification, the model-security `Change` words and hints, the write fixture routes, counters and traps |
| 3. `pypi-auth`, `install`, live | `pypi-auth` (with `--url-file`), `install` (uv only, with `--fetch-uv`): `src/modelsec/pypi.rs`, `uv.rs`, `fetch.rs`, the child-process signal phase, the fake uv and the uv archive fixture; the live tier's model-security reads, the Rust-only `pypi-auth` leak check, the write flow, the scan flow and the sweeper's `group` kind, with their loopback self-tests (§10) |

Each step registers its own commands: until a step lands, its commands are not in the clap tree
(`model-security groups create` is an unrecognised subcommand in a step-1 build, exit 2, D1), and
the group help lists only the commands that exist (`install` and `pypi-auth` are not listed before
step 3).

**Step 1 is built** (`src/walk.rs`, `src/modelsec/{mod,views}.rs`, `src/commands/modelsec.rs`,
`src/commands/modelsec_reads.rs`, `ModelSecurityClients` in `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/clients.rs`; the fixture's
`Route::ModelSecurity(Ms)` read routes and `fixtures::modelsec`; `tests/modelsec_reads.rs`,
`tests/parity_modelsec_reads.rs`). The details it settled are choices 41–48 of §17.18.

**Step 2 is built** (`src/modelsec/body.rs`, the `change` words and hints in `src/modelsec/mod.rs`,
`src/commands/modelsec_write.rs`, `modelsec_groups.rs`, `modelsec_rules.rs`, `modelsec_scans.rs`,
`modelsec_labels.rs`, the `MsWrite` plans in `src/commands/modelsec.rs`; the fixture's write routes in
`server/modelsec_writes.rs` with `ModelSecData::group_delete`; `tests/modelsec_writes.rs`,
`tests/parity_modelsec_writes.rs`). No dependency or lock-file change, and nothing of step 2 is blocked
on scm-sdk 0.1.1: every write is the SDK's typed operation (`groups.create|update|delete`,
`groups.update_rule_instance`, `scans.create|add_labels|set_labels|delete_labels`), sent through
`writes::attempt`. The details it settled are choices 49–59 of §17.18.

**Step 3 is built** (`src/modelsec/pypi.rs`, `uv.rs`, `fetch.rs`, `src/commands/modelsec_install.rs`,
the `MsPlan::PypiAuth`/`Install` plans, the child phase of `src/signals.rs` (`attach_child`,
`forward_once`, `Action::ForwardToChild`/`KillChild`), `SecretSet::redact`; the fixture's
`Ms::PypiAuth` and `Route::UvRelease` routes, `airs_test_harness::fake_uv`, the runner's
`XDG_DATA_HOME` default, path flags and hook guards; `tests/modelsec_install.rs`,
`tests/parity_modelsec_install.rs`; the live flows `live::modelsec`, `live::modelsec_writes`,
`live::modelsec_scan`, the sweeper's groups and their `tests/live.rs` self-tests). `flate2 =1.1.10`
(`rust_backend`) became a direct dependency of the CLI and the harness; `Cargo.lock` gained only
those two dependency edges (the crate was already locked). Nothing of step 3 is blocked on scm-sdk
0.1.1 (`get_pypi_auth` serves both commands). The details it settled are choices 60–76 of §17.18.

### 17.2 Commands and options

Help texts, group descriptions and `Examples:` are TypeScript's (MS§1, MI§1, the captured
`--help` of every leaf) with the program name `airs`, the `--output` line generated from the
format policy (§2.4) and the options marked **(Rust)** with the help text given here (pinned leaf by
leaf against the reference by `help_texts_match_typescript`). The `model-security` description is
TypeScript's `AI Model Security operations — groups, rules, scans`; its subcommands are listed in
TypeScript's sorted order: `groups, install, labels, models, pypi-auth, rule-instances, rules,
scans` (no `help`). The root gains `model-security` in its sorted place. Every `list` has the
visible alias `ls` and every `delete` the alias `rm`. A group without a subcommand prints its help
on stderr, exit 2 (D1). The `scans list` and `models list` `Examples:` are TypeScript's, with the
program name (the `--eval-outcome MALICIOUS` example is kept, choice 20). `install`'s description
and options keep the TS text except `--fetch-uv`; the docs-site sentence "auto-detects uv or pip"
is not used anywhere.

The read-contract options TypeScript adds to every `list` (`--offset <n>` `Item offset`, `--all`
`Walk all pages`, `--max <n>` `Maximum items with --all; 0 removes the cap`, default `10000`) keep
their TS texts; where they are **(Rust)** below they use the same texts.

| Command | Arguments and options |
|---|---|
| `groups list\|ls` | `--source-types <types>`, `--search <query>`, `--sort-field <field>`, `--sort-dir <dir>`, `--enabled-rules <uuids>`, `--limit <n>` (default `20`), `--offset <n>`, `--all`, `--max <n>` |

| `groups delete\|rm <uuid>` | `--force` (Rust, `Skip the confirmation prompt`) |

The leaf `--output <format>` options of TypeScript are the global `--output` here (§2.3). Boolean
