### 17.3 Common rules

**Clients and endpoints.** Every model-security command that sends requests builds its client with
`ModelSecurityClients::build` (`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/clients.rs`, MK§1.2) from the selected tenant only:
- `modelSecDataEndpoint` (else `https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/aims/data`,
  `scm::constants::DEFAULT_MODEL_SEC_DATA_ENDPOINT`), `modelSecMgmtEndpoint` (else
  `…/aims/mgmt`) and `mgmtTokenEndpoint` (else the §5 default), each admitted by §5 (the D48
  message names the key, never the value); a trailing `/` of a base is ignored (both SDKs).
  Groups, rule instances, rules and `pypi/authenticate` use the management base; scans,
  evaluations, violations, files, labels and models the data base (MS§2.1). `mgmtEndpoint` is
  not used; the retired `modelSecTokenEndpoint` stays a §3.3 rejection;
- the §3.5 management credential check (`mgmtClientId`, `mgmtClientSecret`, `mgmtTsgId`) before any
  client is built, with the §3.5 messages; the model-security plane is the management OAuth plane
  and never sends scanner credentials;
- the shared `oauth_parts` (the lease-recording provider of §6, one transport, the direct one when
  any of the three endpoints is loopback http, one `OriginPolicy` admitting both bases and the
  issuer), `max_retries = 5` for reads, the default 8 MiB response bound, then
  `ModelSecurityClient::new(client, data, management)` (OAuth required, no TSG header, TS parity).
  A construction failure is `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:The model security client could not be configured`
  (exit 1). Each command awaits the token before its first request, so a token failure is the §6
  `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:…` message.

No environment variable is read for the API (§2.6; the TS SDK's `PANW_MODEL_SEC_*` and `PANW_MGMT_*`
fallbacks never apply on either side, MS§0); `install` reads `PATH`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `HOME` for
uv only (§17.13, §17.14). `--tenant` selects the tenant as for every command (§3.4). There is no
model-security doctor check (TS parity): the management-credential line already names model
security (`doctor.rs:323`, TS `doctor.ts:299`), and `modelSecDataEndpoint`/`modelSecMgmtEndpoint`
stay §3.3 endpoint keys shown by `tenant read` with the D45 rule (MS§13). No doctor or tenant
wording changes.

**Validation order.** clap → `--output` (§2.4) → `--tenant`'s name format → the command's argument
checks in the order of its section, including the non-interactive confirmation refusal → the debug
log (§2.9) → input files and the path checks (`--config`, `--url-file`, `--dir`; below and §17.12,
§17.13) → the bodies built from them (schema checks) → `install`'s uv resolution and download
(§17.13, §17.14) → the tenant (§3.4, §3.7) → the credential check (§3.5) → the client and token →
the command's reads, prompts and writes. Every usage error (exit 2) comes before the tenant is read,
makes no request and opens no debug log (D184; TS reports most of them with exit 1 after the banner
and the tenant read, MS§2.5). File and path errors exit 1 before the tenant, with zero requests.

**IDs** (D184). Every UUID positional is checked during planning with the §7.1 id shape
(`pagination::is_uuid`, the SDK and zod rule: 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits, any case), else the TypeScript
SDK text `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid <field>: <value>` (exit 2; `<value>` through
`terminal_safe`; TS: exit 1 after the banner and the tenant):

| Argument | `<field>` |
|---|---|
| `groups get\|update\|delete <uuid>`, `rule-instances * <groupUuid>` | `security group uuid` |
| `rule-instances get\|update … <instanceUuid>` | `rule instance uuid` |
| `rules get <uuid>` | `security rule uuid` |
| `scans get <uuid>`, `scans evaluations\|violations\|files <scanUuid>`, `labels add\|set\|delete <scanUuid>` | `scan uuid` |
| `scans evaluation <uuid>` | `evaluation uuid` |
| `scans violation <uuid>` | `violation uuid` |
| `models get <uuid>`, `models versions <modelUuid>` | `model uuid` |
| `models version <uuid>`, `models files <modelVersionUuid>` | `model version uuid` |

`labels values <key>` must pass the SDK segment rule (non-empty, not `.` or `..`, no `\` and no
control character, also once percent-decoded; `segment::check_segment`), else
`Invalid label key: <value>` (exit 2; G21). A valid key is sent as one percent-encoded segment
(`a/b c?d` → `a%2Fb%20c%3Fd`, as TS). The SDK encodes every byte outside `A-Za-z0-9-._~`, so the
sub-delimiters `( ) ! * '`, which TS's `encodeURIComponent` leaves as they are, are sent
percent-encoded (`a(b)` → `a%28b%29`; TS `a(b)`; D202). TS sends `''` and `..` unencoded, so
`labels values ..` reaches `GET /v1/scans/values`, another endpoint (MS§2.8).

**The window** (`scans list`, `models list`; TS `supplyChainWindow`, `ms.ts:38-54`): `--start` and
`--end` must match zod 3's `datetime({ offset: true })` (a leap-year-checked `YYYY-MM-DD`, `T`,
`HH:MM`, optional `:SS` with an optional fraction, then `Z` or `±HH:MM` / `±HHMM`), `--model-version`
must be a UUID (the §7.1 shape), and when both bounds are given the start instant must not be after
the end instant; any failure is TS's usage error
`Use valid ISO timestamps with start <= end and a valid model-version UUID.` (exit 2, before the
tenant; TS: after the banner and the tenant). The values are sent as typed (TS).

**Filter values** (`--search`, `--search-query`, `--sort-field`, `--sort-dir`, `--sort-order`,
`--source-type`, `--eval-outcome`, `--scan-origin`, `--security-rule-uuid`, `--state`, `--type`,
`--result`, each item of `--source-types`, `--enabled-rules` and `--keys`): at most 4,096 bytes and
no control character (the SDK query bound), else `<flag> must be at most 4096 bytes and contain no control characters`
(exit 2). They are otherwise free text (TS parity: the service validates them; `--state bogus` and
`--eval-outcome MALICIOUS` are sent). An empty single-value filter sends no parameter (TS skips a
falsy filter). The comma lists are split on `,` and each item trimmed (TS); an empty item
(`--source-types 'LOCAL,,S3'`, `--source-types ''`) is `<flag> values must not be empty` (exit 2;
TS sends `source_types=`, choice 8); at most 256 query values in all (the SDK bound), else
`<flag> accepts at most 256 values`. `--eval-outcome` and `--source-type` of `scans list` are sent
as one-element arrays (`eval_outcomes=`, `source_types=`, TS).

**Numbers** (D184; decimal digits only, as §7.1):
- `--limit`: 1 to 4,294,967,295 (the SDK's `u32`), else `--limit must be a positive integer` (TS
  sends `limit=NaN` for `abc`, `limit=0`, `limit=1` for `1.5`, MS§3.1). Defaults are TS's: `20` where
  TS declares one, none for `models list|versions|files`.
- `--offset`: 0 to 2^53 − 1, else `--offset must be a non-negative integer` (TS sends `skip=-2` and
  `skip=NaN`). `--max`: the §7.1 rule (`--max must be a non-negative integer`; `0` means no item cap,
  the 1,000,000 safety bound), validated even without `--all` (TS: `max must be a non-negative integer`
  after the tenant, exit 1). `--all` with an explicit `--offset` (even `0`):
  `--all cannot be combined with --offset` (TS drops the offset, MS§3.1). `--max` without `--all` is
  validated, then ignored (TS).

**Lists and walks** (D183). Without `--all` a list sends one page, with `skip` and `limit` as
TypeScript sends them:
- `groups list`, `rules list`, `scans list`: always `skip=<--offset or 0>` and `limit=<--limit or 20>`;
- `rule-instances list`, `scans evaluations|violations|files`, `labels keys|values`: always
  `limit=<--limit or 20>`, and `skip` only when `--offset` is given (Rust-only for the last five);
- `models list|versions|files`: each of `skip` and `limit` only when given (TS: the server's default
  page size).

The query keys come in the SDK order, which is TypeScript's for every key TypeScript sends (MS§3.3;
`scans list` adds nothing TS does not send). With `--all` a list walks from `skip=0` with page size
`--limit` (default: the command's default, else 50, TS `collectSkipPages`) under the §7.2 bounds
(`max_pages` 100,000, 512 MiB, the item cap) and the 300 s walk budget (§5). Every walk is the
shared page loop (`src/walk.rs`, D147): the next skip is `skip + rows`; a page whose
`pagination.total_items` is a safe integer continues while `next < total_items` (a service may cap
pages below `--limit`, so a short page there is not the end); a page without it ends the walk when it
is short; `--max` ends it. It fails with the D37 message (exit 1, no partial data) at an empty page
while `total_items` says more rows exist and at a row whose key an earlier row of the walk already
had (the row `uuid`; for `labels keys|values` the string itself), and with the D40 rule at a bound.
**`count_capped`** (`scans list` only, D182): once a page says `count_capped: true`, the walk ignores
`total_items` for the rest of the walk (it is a cap, not a count; the SDK's own rule,
`ms:scans.rs:160-168`) and ends at a short page.

**`scans list --search`** keeps TypeScript's per-mode parameter (choice 4): `search=<value>` on a
single page, `search_query=<value>` on every walk (`--all` and the `--scan-origin` mode below)
(MS§3.3, `svc.ts:409,433`).

**Status lines** (stderr, quiet-suppressed, every format; TS prints none for these lists, MS§2.3):
- a single page whose `total_items` (a safe integer) exceeds `skip + rows`:
  `  Showing <rows> of <total> (next --offset <skip + rows>)`;
- a single page without a total, or a `scans list` page that says `count_capped: true` (its total is a cap,
  not a count, D182), that is full (`rows == limit`): `  Showing <rows> (more may be available; use --all)`;
- an `--all` walk stopped by `--max` while more rows exist: `  Showing first <n> (stopped at --max <m>; more available)` (D14);
- the `--scan-origin` slice: §17.5;
- otherwise no line (TS parity), so a complete listing prints exactly the TS stderr (choice 6).

**Input files** (D188). `--config` (`groups create`, `rule-instances update`, `scans create`) is
read with the §13.2 input-file rules (path as given, symlinks followed, a regular file of at most
1 MiB, read whole, UTF-8, one JSON value that is an object; the §13.2 messages with the cap named;
no OS error and no content echoed), after the debug log and before the tenant (TS: after the banner
and the tenant, with raw Node errors and V8 messages that quote the content, MS§2.4). The command's
config checks (§17.8–§17.10) and the schema check follow, still before the tenant; their failures
exit 1 (file errors, TS's exit code) and name the path and, for an unknown key, the key (through
`terminal_safe`, cut to 64 characters), never a value.

**JSON arguments** (D188). `--labels` (`labels add|set`) is parsed during planning (exit 2, before
the tenant): it must be one JSON value (the D44 classes count as invalid), else
`--labels is not valid JSON`; it must be an array of at least one object, each validated by the SDK's
`LabelsCreateRequest` schema (`{labels}`, `Mode::Request`: `key` 1–128 and `value` 1–256
characters, unknown keys kept), else
`--labels must be a JSON array of {"key", "value"} objects (key 1-128, value 1-256 characters)`. No
excerpt of the input is echoed (TS: `Unexpected token …, "<input>" is not valid JSON`). `--keys`
(`labels delete`) is split on `,` and trimmed (TS); every item must be non-empty (D187), within the
filter bound above.

**Request bodies** are validated with the SDK request schema (`<Model>::parse(value, Mode::Request)`,
unknown keys kept as extensions) before the tenant; a failure is the D116 text
`AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for <METHOD> <path> did not match schema` (`<path>` the
SDK path with its ids, `/v1/security-groups/<uuid>`; TS appends the fields and zod codes), exit 1 for
a body from a `--config` file and exit 2 for a body built from arguments (`groups update`).
Bodies are sent with sorted keys (D35); equality with TypeScript is JSON equality.

**Writes and outcomes** (D179). Every model-security request that is not a GET is a write: one SDK
call (`RawRequest::new`, never re-sent by the SDK), through `writes::attempt` (§13.2): one replay after
an `Http` 401 with outcome `Rejected`, never after a 403, never after a 5xx, a timeout or a transport
error. The error of a failed write is the §6 message, and when the outcome is not a plain rejection
one detail line follows the `HTTP`/`Re-run` lines: `Outcome unknown: the <thing> may have been <done>.`
or `Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but the response could not be read.`, then the hint line below
when the table has one. Nothing is re-sent and nothing is looked up after such a failure. Exit 1.
TypeScript re-sends every write up to 5 times (4 group POSTs and 3 billed scan POSTs captured,
MS§2.6). The words (`writes::Change`):

| Command | `<thing>` / `<done>` | Hint after an unknown or unreadable outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `groups create\|update\|delete` | `security group` / `created\|updated\|deleted` | create: `Check 'airs model-security groups list' before creating it again.`; delete: `Check it with 'airs model-security groups get <uuid>'.` |
| `rule-instances update` | `rule instance` / `updated` | — |
| `scans create` | `scan` / `created` | `Check 'airs model-security scans list' before creating another scan; scans are billed and cannot be deleted.` |
| `labels add\|set\|delete` | `labels` / `added\|replaced\|deleted` | — |

`scans create` is billed and long-running: it is sent once, an unknown outcome stops the command (no
follow-up read), and the live tier relies on that (§10).

**Confirmations** (D185). `groups delete`, `labels set` and `labels delete` confirm under the §3.10 and
§13.2 rules: `--force` skips the prompt; the gate is stdin **and** stderr being terminals, otherwise
the command's usage error (exit 2, before the tenant); the prompt `? <message> (y/N) ` on stderr; only
`y`/`yes` (trimmed, ASCII case-insensitive) confirm; anything else, an empty line and EOF decline with
the info line `  ℹ Aborted` (exit 0, nothing sent); Ctrl-C or SIGTERM print
`  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` and exit 130/143. Server and argument text in a prompt goes through
`terminal_safe` (and the `[withheld]` rule). The prompt is asked after the reads its section lists and
before the write; no request is open while it waits. `groups create|update`, `rule-instances update`,
`scans create` and `labels add` do not confirm (choice 9). TypeScript never asks (MS§1).

| Command | Prompt | Non-interactive refusal |
|---|---|---|
| `groups delete <uuid>` | `Delete security group <uuid> (<name>)?` | `refusing to delete security group <uuid> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `labels set <scanUuid>` | `Replace all labels on scan <uuid>?[ It drops <n> label(s) the scan has now: <keys>.]` | `refusing to replace the labels of scan <uuid> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `labels delete <scanUuid>` | `Delete label(s) <keys> from scan <uuid>?` | `refusing to delete labels from scan <uuid> without --force in non-interactive mode` |

`<keys>` lists label keys joined `, `, at most 20, then `, and <k> more`; ` (<name>)` is omitted when
the record has no name.

**Streams, banner, quiet and formats** (D189, D190, D50). stdout carries data only, written once after
success (§2.2), so a failing command leaves it empty. `pretty`, `table` and `json` exist for every
command that prints data, `markdown`, `csv` and `yaml` are invalid formats (D50, exit 2, before the
tenant). The tenant's `defaultOutput` is honoured by the reads TypeScript resolves it for (MS§2.2 class
A: `groups list|get`, `rules list|get`, `rule-instances list|get`, `scans list|get`,
`models list|get|versions|version|files`) and ignored by every other model-security command (choice 19).
- **Banner** `"\n  Prisma AIRS — Model Security\n  ML model supply chain security\n\n"` (bold title, dim
  subtitle; decoration): pretty only, at the top of stdout, only above a data layout of a successful run
  (TS prints it first, before the tenant and the argument checks, so failing runs leave it on stdout,
  MS§2.3; D57).
- **Sections** (`"\n  <Title>\n\n"`, bold) are decoration (quiet-suppressed); every data line stays under
  `--quiet`, including the dim ID lines of the pretty lists and the remediation URL of `rules get` (TS
  drops its `ui.dim` lines, so quiet lists lose their identifiers, MS§2.3).
- **Outcome lines** (`ui.success`, `ui.warn` and their dim hints) go to stderr with their TypeScript
  text (program name `airs`, D73) and colours: success lines and hints are quiet-suppressed,
  warnings and failures are not (TS: stdout, success lines kept under `--quiet`).
- **Writes**: a write whose TypeScript output is an outcome line followed by a detail layout
  (`groups create|update`, `rule-instances update`, `scans create`) prints the response on stdout in the
  chosen format (pretty: the banner and the detail layout; json: the record; table: `Key │ Value`) and
  the outcome line on stderr. `groups delete` and the three label writes leave stdout empty in every
  format (`--output` validated, then ignored, D59).
- **Commands TypeScript prints in pretty only** (MS§2.2 class B: `scans evaluations|evaluation|violations|violation|files`,
  `labels keys|values`; and `pypi-auth`) honour `--output`: pretty is the TS layout, json and table the
  documents of their sections (TS ignores `--output` there; its JSON and table branches are unreachable,
  MS§11.3).
- Empty lists: pretty `  No <things> found\n` (dim, data) after the banner; table nothing on stdout;
  json `[]\n` (TS class A already prints `[]`; class B prints the pretty line in every format).

**JSON** (D180). Lists print a bare array, gets a bare object, of the TypeScript projection of §17.4–§17.7
(MS§2.11, `svc.ts:29-192`: its camelCase keys in its order). What changes is only what TypeScript
invents: a field the server did not send is **omitted** where TS prints `''`, `0`, `[]` or `{}` (a scan's
`modelUri`, `scanOrigin`, `labels`; a file's `formats`, `path`; an evaluation's `violationCount`; a
violation's `threat`, `file`; a rule instance's `fieldValues`), a `null` the server sent is printed as
`null` (TS), and an `evalSummary` / `lastEvalSummary` keeps TS's keys with `null` for a count the server
did not send (`"evalSummary": null` when the summary itself is absent or `null`, TS). Nested server objects
that TypeScript copies raw stay raw (`rule` of a rule instance keeps its snake_case keys, TS; choice 17).
Numbers through `js_number`; `[]` for an empty list (TS).

**Table** (MS§11.1). Lists use TypeScript's columns (§17.4–§17.7); every other document is the §2.7
`Key │ Value` table of its projection keys in projection order, with objects and arrays as compact JSON
(§2.7 cell rules) and an empty cell for a key TS prints but the server did not send (TS prints every own
key, `undefined` empty). Tables and JSON are never coloured.

**Colour** (§2.8, MS§4). TypeScript's spans: section titles bold; ids, dim fields and hints dim;
`stateColor`: `ACTIVE`, `ALLOWED`, `ALLOWING`, `PASSED`, `SUCCESS` green, `BLOCKED`, `BLOCKING`, `FAILED`
red, `DISABLED` dim, every other value (`ERROR`, `PENDING` included) yellow; groups green for `ACTIVE`,
else yellow; files green `SUCCESS`, yellow `SKIPPED`, red otherwise; `unscanned` dim; success lines green,
warnings yellow, failures red. Colour per stream (§2.8; TS follows stdout for both).

**Server text** (D11, D52). Error messages are §6 messages (TS prints non-problem bodies and JSON
`message` text verbatim, control characters included, MS§2.6). Every server string in a pretty layout,
table cell, outcome line, prompt or message goes through `terminal_safe`; rule, group, evaluation and
violation `description`s, remediation `description` and steps keep their line breaks
(`terminal_safe_lines`, §15.3). The string values of the keys `name`, `description`, `displayName`,
`ruleName`, `ruleDescription`, `threatDescription`, `securityGroupName`, `path`, `file`, label `key` and
`value` and the label key and value lists that contain a value of the invocation's `SecretSet` (raw,
trimmed, form-encoded or base64) are `[withheld]` in every format (`modelsec::views::withhold`, as §15.3);
ids, states, outcomes and timestamps are not checked.

**Model URIs** (D191). A `modelUri` (`model_uri`) is printed in its withheld form in every format and
every layout: when the value parses as a URL with an authority (`url::Url`, any scheme: `https`, `s3`,
`gs`, `hf`, …), its userinfo is replaced by `[withheld]` (`https://[withheld]@host/path`), and a query or
fragment by `?[withheld]` / `#[withheld]`; scheme, host, port and path are kept (through `terminal_safe`).
A value that does not parse that way is printed through `terminal_safe` as it is (`hf://org/model` and
plain paths have none of these parts). The credential parts of every URI the CLI reads or sends (a
`scans create` config included) join the invocation's `SecretSet` before anything is printed, so they
never appear in an error, a debug record or a summary: raw and percent-decoded, the password and the value
of every credential query key (`X-Amz-Signature`, `X-Amz-Credential`, `X-Amz-Security-Token`,
`X-Goog-Signature`, `X-Goog-Credential`, `sig`, `token`, … `modelsec::views::CREDENTIAL_QUERY_KEYS`, ASCII
case ignored) whatever their length, and the username, the fragment and every other query value (a bare
query word included) of at least 8 characters. Shorter ordinary words (`X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host`,
`X-Amz-Expires=3600`, Azure's `ss=b&sp=r`) never join it, so they cannot withhold an unrelated group name,
label or path (choice 44). TS prints them raw (MS§12).

**Sensitive data** (§17.15). Group and scan configs, rule field values, label values and model URIs are
user data: they are printed only on stdout, by the commands whose purpose is to print them, never in an
error, a warning, a status or outcome line, the debug log or a summary; argument and file errors name the
flag, the path or the key only (D188).

**Debug log** (D64). Every model-security command has the debug policy `log` (§2.9): status and headers
only, never a body or a URL query (TS records every model-security request and response body, label
values, configs and the PyPI URL with its credential included, MS§2.10, MI§2.6; and lets
`PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG_BODY=1` print them). `install`'s uv download (§17.14) is not an API request and is not
recorded; the uv child processes are not recorded either.

**Interruption** (D193; §2.5, §13.2). Reads: `Interrupted; no data was written`. A single write:
`nothing was changed` when it was not sent (a read, the token or the prompt before it included),
`the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` when it was, and `the change was saved`
after the write succeeded; `groups delete` after its DELETE succeeded and during the verification read:
`the delete request was accepted; its result was not verified`. A signal at a confirmation prints
`  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` (exit 130/143). `pypi-auth` and `install` contexts are in their
sections. TS exits by the signal with nothing printed (MS§2.9).

**Exit codes.** 0: success, a declined confirmation, a `--dry-run`, a `groups delete` whose
verification found the group still present or could not read it (§17.8). 1: tenant, credential, file,
HTTP, network, timeout and decode errors; an incomplete walk; a write whose outcome is unknown or
unreadable; the config checks of §17.8–§17.10; a failed or interrupted-by-signal uv step, a uv that is
missing or too old, a failed `--fetch-uv`, a refused `--dir`, an unusable PyPI index URL, a credential
found in a written project file. 2: every argument check of §17 and the non-interactive confirmation
refusals. 130 / 143: interrupted.

### 17.4 Reads: `groups`, `rules`, `rule-instances`

**Requests** (MS§3.3): `GET <mgmt>/v1/security-groups?skip&limit[&sort_field][&sort_dir][&source_types…][&search_query][&enabled_rules…]`
(`--search` is `search_query`, TS); `GET <mgmt>/v1/security-groups/<uuid>`;
`GET <mgmt>/v1/security-rules?skip&limit[&source_type][&search_query]`; `GET <mgmt>/v1/security-rules/<uuid>`;
`GET <mgmt>/v1/security-groups/<g>/rule-instances?[skip&]limit[&security_rule_uuid][&state]`;
`GET <mgmt>/v1/security-groups/<g>/rule-instances/<i>`.

**Projections** (MS§2.11): group `uuid, name, description, sourceType, state, createdAt, updatedAt`
(`tsg_id`, `is_tombstone`, `enabled_rule_count` dropped, TS); rule `uuid, name, description, ruleType,
compatibleSources, defaultState, remediation, editableFields[{attributeName, type, displayName,
displayType, description, dropdownValues}], constantValues, defaultValues`; rule instance `uuid,
securityGroupUuid, securityRuleUuid, customRuleUuid, state, createdAt, updatedAt, rule, customRule,
fieldValues`, where `customRuleUuid` (`custom_rule_uuid`) and `customRule` (the raw `custom_rule`
object) are Rust additions present only when the server sent them (D192; TS drops them).

**Pretty** (the TS bytes of MS§5.1, §5.2, §6.1, §6.2, §7.1, §7.2; banner first):
- `groups list`: section `Security Groups:`, per group the dim `uuid` line and
  `    <name>  <state coloured>  source: <dim sourceType>`, then `"\n"`; empty `  No security groups found`.
- `groups get` (and the create and update detail): section `Security Group Detail:`, keys `UUID`,
  `Name`, `Description` (dim `(none)` when empty or absent), `Source Type`, `State`, `Created`,
  `Updated`, then `"\n"`.
- `rules list`: section `Security Rules:`, per rule the dim `uuid`,
  `    <name>  type: <dim ruleType>  default: <dim defaultState>`, `    <dim description>`,
  `    Sources: <dim s1>, <dim s2>`; empty `  No security rules found`.
- `rules get`: section `Security Rule Detail:` (`UUID`, `Name`, `Description`, `Rule Type`,
  `Default State`, `Sources` joined `, `); section `Remediation:` when `remediation.description` is
  non-empty (the description, one bullet per step, the dim URL when non-empty); section
  `Editable Fields:` when non-empty (`  <displayName> (<dim attributeName>): <displayType>` and
  `    <dim description>` when present); then `"\n"`. Under `--quiet` the section headings go and the
  URL stays (data).
- `rule-instances list`: section `Rule Instances:`, per instance the dim `uuid` and
  `    <label>  <stateColor(state)>` where `<label>` is the first of `rule.name`, `custom_rule.name`,
  `securityRuleUuid`, `customRuleUuid` that is present, else empty (TS prints `undefined` for a
  custom-rule instance, D192); empty `  No rule instances found`.
- `rule-instances get` (and the update detail): section `Rule Instance Detail:` (`UUID`, `Group UUID`,
  `Rule UUID` (`securityRuleUuid`, else `customRuleUuid`), `State`, `Rule Name` (the name part of the
  label above: `rule.name`, else `custom_rule.name`, when non-empty; never a uuid, choice 41), `Created`,
  `Updated`; a key whose value is absent prints an empty value, TS); section
  `Field Values:` when non-empty, one key per field, arrays joined `, `, objects as compact JSON (TS
  prints `[object Object]`, D192), other values `String(v)` through `js_number`.

**Table lists** (MS§11.1): groups `ID, Name, State, Source Type`; rules `ID, Name, Type, Default State,
Sources` (joined `, `); rule instances `ID, Rule ID, State` (`Rule ID` is `securityRuleUuid`, else
`customRuleUuid`).

### 17.5 Reads: `scans`

**Requests**: `scans list` §17.3 (`GET <data>/v1/scans?skip&limit[&search][&model_version_uuid][&eval_outcomes][&source_types][&start_time][&end_time]`,
on a walk `search_query` in the place of `search`); `GET <data>/v1/scans/<uuid>`;
`GET <data>/v1/scans/<s>/evaluations?[skip&]limit`; `GET <data>/v1/evaluations/<uuid>`;
`GET <data>/v1/scans/<s>/rule-violations?[skip&]limit`; `GET <data>/v1/violations/<uuid>`;
`GET <data>/v1/scans/<s>/files?[skip&]limit[&type][&result]`.

**`--scan-origin`** (D181, G18). With a non-empty `--scan-origin`, `scans list` is a client-filtered list:
it walks every page (the §17.3 walk, page size 100, every other filter sent,
`search_query` for `--search`), keeps the rows whose `scan_origin` equals the value exactly (a row
without one is dropped), then slices: without `--all` the rows `[offset, offset + limit)`; with `--all`
the first `--max` rows (`0`: all). The walk itself has no user cap (the §7.2 bounds; D40 beyond them).
Status line: `  Showing <rows> of <matching>[ (next --offset <offset + limit>)]` without `--all`; with
`--all` the §17.3 `--max` line when it cut rows. TS sends no `scan_origin` and prints every origin.

`model_uri`, `scan_origin`, `eval_outcome` and the other required scan fields are required by both SDK
schemas, so a scan without one is the response-validation error on both sides (choice 42); "a scan
without a model URI" in a layout is one whose `model_uri` is empty (no `Model URI` line, TS).

**Projections** (MS§2.11): scan `uuid, evalOutcome, modelUri, scanOrigin, sourceType, securityGroupName,
evalSummary{rulesFailed, rulesPassed, totalRules}|null, createdAt, updatedAt, labels[{key, value}]`;
evaluation `uuid, result, violationCount, ruleInstanceUuid, ruleName, ruleDescription, ruleInstanceState`;
violation `uuid, description, threat, threatDescription, file, ruleName, ruleDescription,
ruleInstanceState`; file `uuid, path, type, formats, result`. The §17.3 JSON rule applies (absent values
omitted, counts `null`), `modelUri` in its withheld form (D191).

**Pretty** (MS§8):
- `scans list`: section `Model Security Scans:`, per scan the dim `uuid`,
  `    <stateColor(evalOutcome)>  <dim scanOrigin>  <dim createdAt>`, `    <dim modelUri>` when present,
  and `    Rules: <green N passed>  <red N failed>  / T total` when the summary has a count (an absent
  count prints `?`; no line when the summary is absent, `null` or has no count, D180; TS prints `0`);
  empty `  No scans found`.
- `scans get` (and the create detail): section `Scan Detail:` (`UUID`, `Outcome`, `Model URI` when
  present, `Origin`, `Source`, `Group`, `Created`, `Updated`, `Rules` as above); section `Labels:` with
  `  <key padded>  <value>` per label when there are labels.
- `scans evaluations`: section `Rule Evaluations:`, per item the dim `uuid` and
  `    <ruleName>  <stateColor(result)>  <dim ruleInstanceState>`; empty `  No evaluations found`.
  `scans evaluation`: section `Evaluation Detail:` (`UUID`, `Rule`, `Description`, `Instance UUID`,
  `Instance State`, `Result`, `Violations`).
- `scans violations`: section `Violations:`, per item the dim `uuid`, `    <red ruleName>  <dim file>`,
  `    <description>`, `    Threat: <dim threat>`; empty `  No violations found`. `scans violation`:
  section `Violation Detail:` (`UUID`, `Rule` red, `Description` (the rule description), `State`, `File`,
  `Threat`, `Detail` (the violation description)).
- `scans files`: section `Scanned Files:`, per file `    <coloured result>  <type>  <path>[<dim " [f1, f2]">]`
  (no id line, TS), then `"\n"`; empty `  No files found`.

**Table lists**: scans `ID, Outcome, Origin, Model URI, Created` (MS§11.1); the TS renderers' dead
branches give evaluations `ID, Rule, Result, State`, violations `ID, Rule, File, Threat` and files
`ID, Path, Type, Result` (MS§11.3). Details: `Key │ Value`.

### 17.6 Reads: `models`

**Requests**: `GET <data>/v1/models[?skip][&limit][&search][&search_query][&sort_field][&sort_order][&start_time][&end_time]`;
`GET <data>/v1/models/<uuid>`; `GET <data>/v1/models/<m>/model-versions[?skip][&limit][&sort_order]`;
`GET <data>/v1/model-versions/<uuid>`; `GET <data>/v1/model-versions/<v>/files[?skip][&limit]`.

**Projections** (MS§2.11): model `uuid, tsgId, name, createdAt, updatedAt, latestVersionUuid,
latestVersionFingerprint, latestVersionRevision, latestVersionHfCommitSha, latestVersionOutcome,
latestVersionFormats, latestVersionSourceTypes, latestVersionScanTime` (absent keys omitted, TS); model
version `uuid, tsgId, modelUuid, revision, createdAt, updatedAt, fingerprint, fileCount, license,
latestScanTime, hfCommitSha, hfCommitTitle, hfCommitAuthors, hfModelName, hfOrganization, modelFormats,
sourceTypes, lastEvalOutcome, lastEvalSummary` (`lastEvalSummary` as `evalSummary`, D180); files as §17.5.

**Pretty** (MS§9): `models list`: section `Models:`, per model the dim `uuid` and
`    <name>  <stateColor(outcome) or dim 'unscanned'>[<dim " [formats]">]`, an empty line after each
model; empty `  No models found`. `models get`: section `Model Detail:` (`UUID`, `Name`, `Created`,
`Updated`, then when present `Latest Version`, `Latest Revision`, `Latest Outcome`, `Formats`,
`Source Types` (non-empty), `Last Scan`). `models versions`: section `Model Versions:`, per version the
dim `uuid` and `    <revision>  <outcome or dim 'unscanned'>[  files: N]`, an empty line after each;
empty `  No versions found`. `models version`: section `Model Version Detail:` (`UUID`, `Model`,
`Revision`, `Created`, `Updated`, then when present `File Count`, `License`, `Formats`, `Source Types`,
`HF Model`, `HF Organization`, `Last Outcome`, `Last Scan`); section `Last Eval Summary:` with `Passed`,
`Failed`, `Total` when the summary has a count (an absent count `?`, D180). `models files`: the
`scans files` layout.

**Table lists**: models `ID, Name, Outcome, Formats, Last Scan`; model versions `ID, Revision, Files,
Outcome, Last Scan`; model files `ID, Path, Type, Result` (MS§11.1).

### 17.7 Reads: `labels keys`, `labels values <key>`

`GET <data>/v1/scans/label-keys?[skip&]limit` and `GET <data>/v1/scans/label-keys/<encoded key>/values?[skip&]limit`
(tenant-wide reads). Pretty (MS§10): section `Label Keys:`, `  <key>` each, `"\n"`; empty
`  No label keys found`; section `Label Values for "<key>":`, `  <value>` each; empty
`  No values for key "<key>" found` (`<key>` through `terminal_safe`). json: a bare array of strings
(choice 13). table: one column `Key` / `Value`.

### 17.8 `groups create`, `update <uuid>`, `delete|rm <uuid>`

**`create --config <path>`** (D188). The file (§17.3) must be an object whose keys are among `name`,
`source_type`, `description`, `rule_configurations`; another key is
`<path> has an unknown key <key>; a security group config takes name, source_type, description and rule_configurations`
(exit 1; TS copies the four keys and drops the rest silently, MS§2.7, choice 15). The body is those keys,
validated with `ModelSecurityGroupCreateRequest` (`name` 1–255, `source_type` one of
`LOCAL HUGGING_FACE S3 GCS AZURE ARTIFACTORY GITLAB ALL`, `description` ≤ 1000, defaulting to `""` in
both SDKs, `rule_configurations` a map of `{field_values?, state?}`). Requests: token,
`POST <mgmt>/v1/security-groups` (one attempt). stdout: the group (§17.4 detail); stderr
`  ✓ Group created: <uuid>`.

**`update <uuid> [--name] [--description]`** (D187). At least one of the two must be given, else
`groups update needs --name or --description` (exit 2; TS sends `{}` and reports success). A given
`--name` is sent as given (`--name ''` fails the schema); a given `--description` is sent as given, so
`--description ''` clears the description (TS drops a falsy value, so it cannot clear one; choice 13).
The body `{name?, description?}` is validated with `ModelSecurityGroupUpdateRequest` during planning
(the D116 text, exit 2). Requests: token, `PUT <mgmt>/v1/security-groups/<uuid>` (one attempt). stdout:
the group; stderr `  ✓ Group updated: <uuid>`. No confirmation.

**`delete|rm <uuid> [--force]`** (D185, D186). With a prompt (no `--force`, terminals): token,
`GET …/security-groups/<uuid>` (the name for the prompt; a failure is its §6 error, exit 1, nothing
sent), the prompt, then the DELETE. With `--force` the TS sequence: token, DELETE. Then
`DELETE <mgmt>/v1/security-groups/<uuid>` (one attempt; a failure is its §6 error and the D179 lines,
exit 1; a 404 is TS's `AISEC_CLIENT_SIDE_ERROR:API error 404` error), then one verification read
`GET …/security-groups/<uuid>` (SDK read retries; TS `deleteGroupAndVerify`, `svc.ts:284-292`):

| Verification result | stderr | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `Http` 404 | `  ✓ Group <uuid> deleted.` (TS) | 0 |
| 2xx with `is_tombstone: true` | `  ✓ Group <uuid> deleted (the service is removing it).` | 0 |
| 2xx with `is_tombstone: false` | `  ⚠ Delete request accepted, but group <uuid> still reports state '<state>'.` and the dim hint `  Deletion is asynchronous (soft-delete) — re-check with 'airs model-security groups get <uuid>'.` (TS text, quiet-suppressed hint) | 0 |
| any other failure | `  ⚠ Delete request accepted, but its result could not be verified; re-check with 'airs model-security groups get <uuid>'.` | 0 |

TS prints `✓ Group <uuid> deleted.` whenever the verification read fails for any reason (a 500 or a 401
was enough, MS§5.5) and never reads `is_tombstone`. stdout stays empty in every format.

### 17.9 `rule-instances update <groupUuid> <instanceUuid> --config <path>`

The file (§17.3) must be an object whose keys are among `state`, `field_values` and
`security_group_uuid` (another key: `<path> has an unknown key <key>; a rule instance config takes state, field_values and security_group_uuid`,
exit 1); a `security_group_uuid` in it must equal `<groupUuid>` (ASCII case-insensitively), else
`<path> names another security group than <groupUuid>` (exit 1; TS ignores it); at least one of `state`
and `field_values` must be present (a `null` counts, TS sends it), else
`<path> must set state or field_values` (exit 1, D187; TS sends `{security_group_uuid}` and reports
success). The body is `{security_group_uuid: <groupUuid>, state?, field_values?}` (TS, `svc.ts:330-347`),
validated with `ModelSecurityRuleInstanceUpdateRequest` (`state` one of `DISABLED ALLOWING BLOCKING` or
`null`). Only the named fields are sent (no read-modify-write, choice 14). Requests: token,
`PUT <mgmt>/v1/security-groups/<g>/rule-instances/<i>` (one attempt). stdout: the instance (§17.4
detail); stderr `  ✓ Rule instance updated: <uuid>`. No confirmation.

### 17.10 `scans create --config <path>`

The parsed file is the body (TS, `ms.ts:582-583`): validated with `ScanCreateRequest` (`model_uri` and
`security_group_uuid` required, `scan_origin` one of `MODEL_SECURITY_SDK MODEL_SECURITY_API
MODEL_SECURITY_FRONTEND HUGGING_FACE`), unknown keys kept and sent (TS; choice 15). The withheld parts of
its `model_uri` join the `SecretSet` during planning (D191). Requests: token, `POST <data>/v1/scans`
(one attempt; billed). stdout: the scan (§17.5 detail, `without_response_defaults`, so a pending scan
shows no `Rules` line); stderr `  ✓ Scan created: <uuid>`. An unknown or unreadable outcome prints the
§17.3 lines and the billed-scan hint and stops (no read, no retry). Never sent by the TypeScript side of
any live flow (§10).

### 17.11 `labels add|set|delete <scanUuid>`

- **`add --labels <json>`**: token, `POST <data>/v1/scans/<s>/labels` `{"labels": [...]}` (one attempt);
  stderr `  ✓ Labels added.` (TS). The service merges by key (a present key's value is replaced; no
  confirmation, choice 9).
- **`set --labels <json> [--force]`** (D185): token, `GET <data>/v1/scans/<s>` (the current labels; a
  failure is its §6 error, exit 1, nothing sent), the dropped keys (the current keys the new list does
  not name, in the scan's order), the prompt (or, with `--force` and a non-empty list, the warning
  `  ⚠ The replacement drops <n> label(s) the scan has now: <keys>` on stderr, never quiet-suppressed),
  then `PUT <data>/v1/scans/<s>/labels` (one attempt); stderr `  ✓ Labels set.` (TS). TS replaces every
  label without asking (three labels became one, MS§10).
- **`delete|rm --keys <keys> [--force]`** (D185, D187): the gate, token, the prompt, then
  `DELETE <data>/v1/scans/<s>/labels?keys=<k1>&keys=<k2>…` (one attempt, keys in the given order, a
  repeated key sent as given); stderr `  ✓ Labels deleted.` (TS). Keys the scan does not have are not
  reported (TS; the service answers 2xx).

stdout stays empty for all three (`LabelsResponse` is an empty object); a 2xx without a JSON body is the
"was <done>, but the response could not be read" line (G4).

### 17.12 `pypi-auth [--url-file <path>]`

**The credential** (D194, G24). The `url` of `GET <mgmt>/v1/pypi/authenticate` is a credential-bearing
Google Artifact Registry index URL (`https://oauth2accesstoken:<access token>@<region>-python.pkg.dev/<project>/<repo>/simple/`,
MI§2.2). As soon as the response is decoded, before anything is printed, written or spawned
(`modelsec::pypi::IndexUrl`): the full URL, its raw (percent-encoded) userinfo, its raw and
percent-decoded password, and the username too when there is no password, join the invocation's
`SecretSet` (so every output path, the error lines, the debug log and the live summary withhold them).
**The credential-bearing URL is never printed to stdout or stderr, never written to the debug log, an
error or a summary**; the only channel that returns it is `--url-file` (choice 23).

**The withheld form** (every format): when `url::Url` parses the value with a host, `<scheme>://` +
`[withheld]@` when it has a userinfo + `<host>[:<port>]<path>` + `?[withheld]` when it has a query +
`#[withheld]` when it has a fragment (through `terminal_safe`); otherwise `[withheld]`. A form that still
contains a `SecretSet` value is `[withheld]` as a whole.

**Arguments** (before the tenant): `--url-file ""` is `--url-file needs a path` (exit 2); `--url-file -`
is `--url-file - would print the credential; give a file path` (exit 2); an existing path (`lstat`, a
dangling symlink included) is `<path> already exists; choose another --url-file` (`files::refuse_existing`,
exit 1); a missing or unusable parent is the `files::publish_new` message (exit 1).

**Requests.** Token, one `GET <mgmt>/v1/pypi/authenticate` (`get_pypi_auth`, a read with the SDK read
retries, choice 24; each attempt may mint a token server-side, as in TS), `without_response_defaults()`
(a no-op, G20).

**`--url-file`.** The URL must pass the index check of §17.13 (https, a host, a non-empty username and
password once percent-decoded, no query, no fragment, no control character, at most 8 KiB), else
`The PyPI auth response is not a usable index URL; nothing was written` (exit 1). The file receives
`<url>\n` through `files::publish_new` (temp, `fsync`, exclusive `link`, mode 0600, never overwrites,
§15.18), after the response and before rendering; stderr
`  ✓ Wrote the PyPI index URL, credential included, to <path> (mode 0600).` (success line, quiet-suppressed;
`<path>` as given, through `terminal_safe`). A failed write renders nothing (exit 1, the `publish_new`
message).

**Output.**
- pretty (stdout): the banner, the section `PyPI Authentication` (no colon, TS; decoration), then
  `  URL      <withheld form>\n  Expires  <expires_at>\n` (TS keyValue, keys padded to 7, values
  `terminal_safe`, no trailing blank line; MI§3). Without `--url-file` stderr adds the dim hint
  `  The index credential is withheld; pass --url-file <path> to save the full URL in a new private file.`
  (quiet-suppressed).
- json: `{"url": "<withheld form>", "expiresAt": "<expires_at>"}` (TS's service shape, `types.ts:915-918`).
- table: `Key │ Value` with the rows `url` and `expiresAt`.
TS prints the full URL in its only (pretty) layout, also under `--quiet` (MI§3).

**Interruption.** Before the response: `Interrupted; no data was written`. After the URL file was
published: `Interrupted; <path> was written`.

As built: a URL without any credential is still the registered full URL, so its form is
`[withheld]` as a whole (choice 64); `expires_at` is printed through `terminal_safe` and withheld
when it carries a registered value.

### 17.13 `install [--extras <type>] [--dir <path>] [--dry-run] [--fetch-uv]`

uv only (D195): the TypeScript `python3 -m venv` + `pip install --extra-index-url <credential URL>`
fallback is not ported (MILESTONES). The steps, in order:

1. **Arguments** (exit 2, before the tenant): `--extras` must be exactly one of `all, aws, gcp, azure,
   artifactory, gitlab` (case-sensitive), else TS's `Invalid extras "<value>". Valid: all, aws, gcp, azure, artifactory, gitlab`
   (`<value>` through `terminal_safe`); `--dir ""` is `--dir needs a path`. `--output` is validated, then
   ignored (the dry-run plan is shell text in every format, choice 32).
2. **The debug log** (§2.9), when asked for.
3. **`--dir`** (D198; exit 1, no request): the path is made absolute against the working directory,
   lexically (no symlink resolution; `.` and `..` components are kept as typed, so the parent check sees
   the real parent); an existing path (`lstat`: a file, a directory, a symlink, a dangling one included)
   is `<dir> already exists; choose another --dir`; a parent that is missing or not a directory is
   `Cannot create <dir>; its parent directory does not exist`; a parent inside a uv workspace (the
   parent or one of its ancestors holds a `pyproject.toml` that, read with the §13.2
   rules up to 1 MiB and parsed as TOML, has a `[tool.uv.workspace]` table; the ancestors of the parent
   as typed, of its lexically normalised form and of its canonical form are all checked, because uv
   discovers a workspace along the path it is given, so a parent reached through a symlink is checked on
   both sides of the link) is `<dir> is inside the uv workspace at <ancestor>; choose a --dir outside it`
   (`uv add --project` there writes the parent's `uv.lock`, MK§12.2); an ancestor `pyproject.toml` that
   cannot be read or parsed is `Cannot check <path> for a uv workspace; choose a --dir outside it`.
   `<dir>` in messages is as typed (through `terminal_safe`).
4. **uv** (D195): with `--fetch-uv`, the managed copy of §17.14 (verified, or downloaded when absent;
   `PATH` is not consulted). Without it, the first `uv` on `PATH`: the entries split on `:`, empty and
   relative entries skipped, `<entry>/uv` a regular file once symlinks are followed (Homebrew installs a
   symlink), executable by the effective user; the managed copy is not used (choice 28). None found:
   `uv was not found on PATH. Install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) or re-run with --fetch-uv to download uv 0.12.17 into <tools dir>.`
   (exit 1; TS: `Neither uv nor python3 found on PATH. Install one first.`). Then `<uv> --version`
   (stdin `/dev/null`, output captured, at most 64 KiB, a 10 s limit; a `--dry-run` whose managed copy
   is not downloaded yet skips it): its first line must start with
   `uv <major>.<minor>.<patch>`, and the version must be at least 0.12.0 (a managed copy: exactly 0.12.17),
   else `<uv path> is not a usable uv (model-security install needs uv 0.12.0 or later; re-run with --fetch-uv to use uv 0.12.17)`
   (exit 1). Status `  Using uv <version> (<path>)` (stderr, quiet-suppressed).
5. **The tenant, the credentials, the client, the token**, then `GET <mgmt>/v1/pypi/authenticate` (as
   §17.12, the `SecretSet` registration first). A `--dry-run` sends it too (TS parity: it shows the real
   index host and proves the tenant works, choice 31).
6. **The index check** (D201): the URL parses with `url::Url`; the scheme is `https`; it has a host; the
   username and the password are non-empty once percent-decoded; there is no query and no fragment; it
   has no control character and is at most 8 KiB. Otherwise
   `The PyPI auth response is not a usable index URL; nothing was installed.` (exit 1, no uv run; the URL
   is never printed). The **index** is the URL with its userinfo removed (`https://<host>[:<port>]<path>`).
   TS hands any string to uv (MI§2.2).
7. **`--dry-run`** (D197): the plan on stdout (below), exit 0. Nothing is created, run (but `--version`)
   or downloaded.
8. **The directory**: `mkdir <abs dir>` (exclusive, mode `0o777` minus the umask, as `uv init` would);
   `EEXIST` is the step-3 message (a directory that appeared meanwhile), any other failure
   `Cannot create <dir>; check the permissions of its parent directory` (exit 1).
9. **`uv init`**: `<uv> [--quiet] init --no-workspace -- <abs dir>`; status `  → uv init` (TS label).
10. **`uv add`**: `<uv> [--quiet] add --no-build --project <abs dir> --index airs-model-security=<index> -- model-security-client[<extras>]`;
    status `  → uv add`. `--no-build` (D203): uv passes its whole environment, the credential variables
    included, to every PEP 517 build backend it starts for a source distribution, so no build runs while
    the credential is set (measured with uv 0.12.17, offline against a loopback index: without it an
    sdist's in-tree backend saw both variables; with it uv refuses with `Wheels are required for <pkg>
    because building from source is disabled` and runs no backend; a wheel-only install succeeds and
    the project itself is still installed).
11. **The persistence check** (D196): `<abs dir>/pyproject.toml` and `<abs dir>/uv.lock` (regular files,
    read up to 16 MiB each) must not contain the password (raw or
    percent-decoded), the raw userinfo or the base64 of `<username>:<password>`; a hit is
    `The PyPI index credential was written to <file>; remove it from the file before sharing the project.`
    (exit 1, the value never shown). uv 0.12.17 strips it in every measured variant (MI§7.3, MK§12.2).
    A missing `uv.lock` after a successful `uv add` means uv locked somewhere else (a uv workspace above
    the project that the step-3 check did not see, or `UV_FROZEN`), so that lock went unchecked:
    `uv did not write <abs dir>/uv.lock; it may have locked a uv workspace above the project (or UV_FROZEN is set). Check any parent uv.lock for the PyPI index credential before sharing it.`
    (exit 1).
12. **Success** (stderr, D199): `  ✓ model-security-client installed successfully.` (TS text,
    quiet-suppressed), `  Activate:  cd <POSIX-quoted abs dir>` (dim, quiet-suppressed; TS: the dir as
    typed), then the dim note
    `  Later uv commands that use the AIRS index need the credential again: set UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_USERNAME and UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_PASSWORD from the URL that 'airs model-security pypi-auth --url-file <file>' saves.`
    (quiet-suppressed). stdout stays empty.

**The credential channel** (D196, choice 25). argv never carries the credential: `uv add` gets the
credential-free named index `airs-model-security=<index>` and, in its environment only,
`UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_USERNAME=<percent-decoded username>` and
`UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_PASSWORD=<percent-decoded password>` (uv takes environment values
literally, MI§7.3). Both children otherwise inherit the CLI's environment; `uv init` gets it with those
two variables removed (so a user's own values never reach `uv init`, its `git` or a build backend), and
`uv add` with them overridden. The CLI never sets `UV_NO_CONFIG` (with it, uv ignores the project's
`[tool.uv.index]` on later syncs, MI§7.3). `pyproject.toml` therefore records
`[[tool.uv.index]] name = "airs-model-security"` with the credential-free URL (TS: the same URL without a
name). Every child uv starts inherits its environment, so `uv add` runs with `--no-build` (step 10, D203)
and no third-party build code runs while the credential is set. TS passes `--index <URL with the credential>` as an argv element of `uv add`, readable by any local
user with `ps` for the whole install (MI§4.3).

**Children** (D199). Spawned by absolute path (`std::process::Command`, no shell) in their own process
group (`process_group(0)`), stdin `/dev/null`, stdout and stderr piped. Two forwarding threads write each
line of either stream to the CLI's stderr after the `SecretSet` scrub (every occurrence of a registered
form replaced by `[withheld]`) and `terminal_safe` (a line longer than 64 KiB is split, where no
registered form straddles the split: up to the longest form's length less one, at most 32 KiB, is kept
for the next piece, and the split moves back to the start of any form that crosses it, so each piece's
scrub sees every form whole); uv sees pipes, so
it prints no colours or progress bars. With the CLI's `--quiet`, `--quiet` is passed to uv (after `uv`);
the forwarded lines are never suppressed. No time limit applies to `init` or `add` (installs are slow;
the user interrupts). Failures (exit 1): a spawn failure `Cannot start <uv path>`; a non-zero exit
`<label> failed with exit code <n>` (TS text); a child ended by a signal
`<label> was terminated by signal <n>` (TS prints `exit code null`); after a failed `uv add` two more lines
`<dir> was created, but model-security-client was not added. Remove <dir> and re-run, or add it with uv yourself.`
and `uv add runs with --no-build so that no package build code sees the index credential; if uv reports a dependency that needs building, build it yourself without the credential in the environment, then add model-security-client with uv.`
The CLI never deletes `<dir>` (choice 30).

**Dry-run plan** (D197; stdout, data, printed under `--quiet` too; TS prints dim, quiet-suppressed lines,
so `--quiet --dry-run` prints nothing, and shows the credential, MI§4.4). In every format: the banner and
the section `Commands that would be executed` (decoration), then, with `--fetch-uv` and no managed copy
yet, `  # would download uv 0.12.17 (uv-<target>.tar.gz, sha256 <hex>) into <tools dir>`, then one line
per command, `  $ ` followed by POSIX shell words: a word is single-quoted unless it matches
`[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+`, and `'` inside becomes `'\''`:

```
  $ /opt/homebrew/bin/uv init --no-workspace -- /abs/cwd/model-security
  $ UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_USERNAME=[withheld] UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_PASSWORD=[withheld] /opt/homebrew/bin/uv add --no-build --project /abs/cwd/model-security --index airs-model-security=https://us-west1-python.pkg.dev/fake-proj/fake-repo/simple/ -- 'model-security-client[all]'
```

The uv shown is the resolved absolute path (the managed path with `--fetch-uv`); `--quiet` appears when
the real run would pass it. The two `[withheld]` words are left unquoted on purpose (a pasted line sets the
literal value and cannot authenticate). TS quotes only words containing `[` or a space, so
`--dir '/abs/$(id)'` is printed unquoted (MI§4.4).

**As built** (choices 61–69): a `--version` that cannot be started, exits non-zero, prints no
`uv X.Y.Z` first line or exceeds 10 s is the "not a usable uv" message; the `--version` child runs in
its own process group and is killed on a signal; the index check also refuses an index whose path holds
`@`; the persistence check skips a missing `pyproject.toml` (a missing `uv.lock` fails it, step 11), and a file it
cannot read is `Cannot check <file> for the PyPI index credential; check it before sharing the project.`
(exit 1); forwarding stops 2 s after a child exited when a grandchild keeps its pipes open.

**Interruption** (D200). Before a child runs, the §13.2 phases: `Interrupted; nothing was installed`
(the PyPI read, the `--version` check and the dry run included; a download: §17.14). While `uv init` or
`uv add` runs, the signal thread forwards the received signal once to the child's process group
(`rustix::process::kill_process_group`) and the command waits for the child; a second signal sends
`SIGKILL` to the group and the command waits again (the child is reaped; none outlives the CLI except
after a `SIGKILL` of the CLI itself). Then `Interrupted; uv <init|add> was stopped; <dir> may be incomplete`
(exit 130/143). During the persistence check: `Interrupted; model-security-client was installed in <dir>`.
Because the child has its own process group, a terminal Ctrl-C reaches only the CLI, which forwards it,
so uv sees one signal. TS exits at once and leaves the child running (MI§2.7).

### 17.14 `--fetch-uv`

**The pin** (D195, choice 26): uv **0.12.17** (the version whose persistence behaviour MI§7.3 and MK§12.2
measured), from `https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/0.12.17/uv-<target>.tar.gz`. The
SHA-256 values are hard-coded in `src/modelsec/fetch.rs`, taken from the release's official `sha256.sum`
(fetched 2026-10-18 and again while writing this section; each asset's own `.sha256` agrees, MI§7.1):

| Host (`cfg(target_os, target_arch)`) | Archive | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| macOS aarch64 | `uv-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | `85f00cbdc6dd3e97eba4c31b4d014375a9fdfe8f570023b84e5102fc3456896b` |
| macOS x86_64 | `uv-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | `8dcf05a8c809bb3c471d2b614788ba27a6e41298fc8c31ac84b5f4339fd468e5` |
| Linux aarch64 | `uv-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | `a6096da273d548cb9f277d237a01ac7344a39ef0f455c0e148e4dc9737c1596b` |
| Linux x86_64 | `uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | `6401c4665d8fa2a9893e087c91f585430738e3170f5398a1141483efb4a93310` |

Linux always uses the static musl asset (it runs on glibc too, and a musl-built CLI cannot reliably detect
the libc; choice 26); the gnu values (`d636d1b6…f86c`, `fa82fd8d…0a63`) are recorded in MI§7.1 and not
used. Any other host: `--fetch-uv has no pinned uv release for this platform; install uv yourself.` (exit 1).

**The tools directory.** `T = <data>/airs-cli/tools`, where `<data>` is `$XDG_DATA_HOME` when it is set and
non-empty (it must be absolute, else `XDG_DATA_HOME must be an absolute path`, exit 1), otherwise
`<home>/.local/share` with `<home>` resolved as in §2.9 (absolute, else
`Cannot install uv: HOME is not an absolute path; set XDG_DATA_HOME`, exit 1). `T` follows the §14.9
directory rules: created with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)` (an existing directory is
never chmod'ed), a symlink or non-directory at `T` refused before it is resolved, `T` canonicalised and
opened `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, checked on the descriptor (a directory owned by the
effective uid with `mode & 0o022 == 0`), with the §3.8 messages; every later name is opened, created and
renamed relative to that descriptor. The managed copy is `T/uv-0.12.17-<target>/` (0700) holding `uv`
(0755) and `SHA256SUMS` (0600):

```
<archive sha256>  uv-<target>.tar.gz
<uv sha256>  uv
```

**Reuse.** When `T/uv-0.12.17-<target>` exists it is verified and never replaced: the directory passes the
§3.8 directory rule, `SHA256SUMS` passes the §3.8 file rule and holds exactly those two lines with the
pinned archive hash, `uv` is a regular file (`O_NOFOLLOW`) owned by the effective uid, not writable by group
or others, whose SHA-256 equals the recorded one. Verified: used with no request. Otherwise
`<path> exists but is not the verified uv 0.12.17; remove it to download again.` (exit 1, nothing changed).

**Download** (absent copy, not `--dry-run`; before the tenant, so a failed download never mints a
credential): one `GET` with the CLI's reqwest client: one attempt, `https` only on every hop, at most 5
redirects, no gzip decoding (the hash covers the exact bytes), no credential or cookie, the user agent
`airs/<version>`, the proxy policy of the API's https transport (§2.6), a 64 MiB body cap and a
120 s total limit; status `  → Downloading uv 0.12.17 (<target>)` (stderr, quiet-suppressed). Errors name
only the class: `Cannot download uv 0.12.17: <HTTP <status>|network error|timed out|response too large|redirect refused>`
(exit 1).

**Verify before anything else.** The SHA-256 of the whole body (`sha2`) must equal the pinned value, else
`The downloaded uv archive does not match its pinned SHA-256; nothing was installed.` (exit 1). Nothing has
touched the disk before this point.

**Extract** (in memory; no archive path is ever used to write): gunzip with `flate2` (output capped at
256 MiB, else `The uv archive is larger than expected; nothing was installed.`), then an in-house strict tar
reader (choice 35): 512-byte headers with their checksums verified; sizes in octal (base-256 refused);
names from ustar `prefix` + `name`, with a pax `x` `path` record or a GNU `L` long name applying to the next
entry and pax `g` records skipped; a leading `./` stripped, nothing else normalised; data within the bound;
the end at two zero blocks or at the end of the data after a complete entry. Exactly one entry named
`uv-<target>/uv` with type `0` or NUL is taken; the same name with any other type (a symlink, a hard link, a
device) or twice, a truncated entry or a bad header is
`The uv archive is malformed or has an unexpected layout; nothing was installed.`, and no such entry is
`The uv archive does not contain uv-<target>/uv; nothing was installed.` (exit 1). Every other entry
(`uvx`, directories, links, `..` names) is skipped without touching the filesystem. The layout
`uv-<target>/uv` is the cargo-dist one. It was confirmed before the 0.8.0 tag (2026-10-18): the four
pinned archives were downloaded, matched the pinned SHA-256 values and the release's `sha256.sum`, and
`read_tar`/`extract_uv` took `uv-<target>/uv` from each (entries: the directory, `uv`, `uvx`). A
different layout in a later pin still fails closed.

**Install.** `mkdirat(T, ".uv-0.12.17-<target>.<16 hex>.tmp", 0o700)` (exclusive); `uv` and `SHA256SUMS`
created in it with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, `fchmod` 0755 / 0600, written, `fsync`ed;
the directory `fsync`ed; renamed to `uv-0.12.17-<target>` without replacing (`renameat_with(NOREPLACE)`
where the platform offers it, else `renameat`, which refuses a non-empty target), then `T` `fsync`ed. On any
failure the temporary directory is removed (best effort) and the command fails with
`Cannot install uv 0.12.17 in <T>; check the permissions of that directory` (exit 1); an existing file
is never overwritten, and a copy another run renamed into place first is verified and used (choice 66). A
temporary left by a killed run (`.uv-*.tmp` older than 1 hour) is removed by the next `--fetch-uv`. Then
`<uv> --version` must report `uv 0.12.17`. Status `  ✓ Installed uv 0.12.17 in <dir>` (stderr,
quiet-suppressed).

**Interruption.** During the download or the install: `Interrupted; uv was not installed` (the temporary
removed), or `Interrupted; uv 0.12.17 was installed in <dir>; nothing else was installed` once the rename
succeeded.

**Test hook** (choice 36). Compiled only with `cfg(debug_assertions)`; a release build contains neither the
code nor the variable names. `AIRS_CLI_TEST_UV_ARCHIVE_URL` (an `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/…` or
`http://[::1]:<port>/…` URL) and `AIRS_CLI_TEST_UV_ARCHIVE_SHA256` (64 lowercase hex), both or neither,
replace the release URL and the pinned hash (and allow that one loopback http hop); any other value is the
usage error `AIRS_CLI_TEST_UV_ARCHIVE_URL must be a loopback http URL with AIRS_CLI_TEST_UV_ARCHIVE_SHA256`
(exit 2). The target, the version and every other rule are unchanged. A unit test pins that the release
configuration compiles the hook out (a `cfg(not(debug_assertions))` constant check).

### 17.15 Sensitive data per command

| Command | Printed | Never printed |
|---|---|---|
| lists, gets | pretty: names, states, outcomes, counts, label keys and values, file paths, URIs in their withheld form; table and json: the projections | URI userinfo, queries and fragments (D191) |
| `groups create\|update`, `rule-instances update`, `scans create` | the response record | the config file content, in any message (D188) |
| `labels add\|set\|delete` | the outcome line; label keys in prompts and the `set` warning | label values in any message |
| `pypi-auth` | the withheld URL form, `expires_at`; the full URL only into the `--url-file` file | the credential-bearing URL anywhere else: stdout, stderr, errors, the debug log, summaries (D194) |
| `install` | the plan with `[withheld]` env words and the credential-free index; uv's output scrubbed | the credential in argv, output, the debug log, `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` (checked, D196) |
| every command | §6 errors (allowlisted problem fields only) | server message text, body excerpts, `--labels` and config content (D11, D188); in the debug log: bodies and queries (D64) |

`--labels` values, `--keys`, `--name` and `--description` are on the command line (the process list,
shell history), as in TS; they are not refused (labels are not credentials, choice 21). `install` reads the
credential only from the service and passes it only through one child's environment, readable by the same
user and root only (argv is world-readable).
