### 17.17 Acceptance tests

Every behaviour above gets an executable test (`tests/modelsec_*.rs`), unit tests in `src/modelsec/` and
`src/walk.rs`, parity tests (`tests/parity_modelsec_*.rs`) and a `dNN_` test per §12 row. The TypeScript
specs (MS§14, MI§5) are ported first:

| TypeScript spec | Rust acceptance tests (adjusted by the §12 rows) |
|---|---|
| `unit/airs/modelsecurity.spec.ts` | per operation the request built from the options: group filters (`:150-174`), rule-instance filters (`:338-354`), rule filters (`:445-455`), scan filters (`:525-548`; `--scan-origin` as D181), file filters (`:729-739`), model list filters with unset filters omitted (`:814-880`), version sort and pagination (`:897-945`), version files (`:964-1000`); the normalised records (D180: absent values omitted, `null` summaries kept, `:947-962`); create with rule configurations (`:220-243`); the rule-instance body with `security_group_uuid` (`:375-403`); the label add and set bodies and delete keys (`:741-767`); label keys and values (`:769-794`); `deleteGroupAndVerify` (`:274-304`: a 404 confirms, a present record warns with its state, a failed delete propagates; D186 adds the tombstone and the unverified case); `getPyPIAuth` (`:794-809`) as the json `{url, expiresAt}` with the withheld URL (D194) |
| `unit/cli/modelsecurity-groupdetail-output.spec.ts` | `groups get --output json` is the full projection; pretty keeps `Security Group Detail`; list json is the bare array, `[]` when empty; table columns `ID, Name, State, Source Type`; the yaml and markdown cases are usage errors (D50) |
| `unit/cli/aliases.spec.ts:66-86` | `ls` on the `groups`, `rules`, `rule-instances`, `scans` and `models` lists; `rm` on `groups delete` and `labels delete` |
| `unit/cli/help-examples.spec.ts:42` | `scans list --help` has the `Examples:` block with `$ airs …` lines |
| `unit/config/client-options.spec.ts:38,55,71,100-107,146-152` | the shared management OAuth credentials and `mgmtTokenEndpoint`; refused without them (§3.5); `PANW_*` ignored; the `modelSecMgmtEndpoint`/`modelSecDataEndpoint` overrides and the SDK default bases (COMPATIBILITY.md §5.2 gains the model-security rows) |
| `unit/cli/completion.spec.ts:38,82` | not ported (`completion` is dropped, MILESTONES) |
| `unit/config/schema.spec.ts:50` | already covered: `modelSecTokenEndpoint` is a retired key (§3.3) |

No TypeScript integration spec covers model security (MS§14). Rust additions: every §17.3 argument check
with zero requests and no debug log; the D179 sequences on each write (a 5xx with `Retry-After: 0`: one
Rust request and the outcome line, more than one TypeScript request with no exact count; a 401:
`token, write, token, write` on both; a 403: one Rust request; a held-then-dropped `scans create`: exactly
one POST); every confirmation on the pty (`y`, `yes`, Enter, `n`, EOF, Ctrl-C) and its non-interactive
refusal; the `labels set` dropped keys in the prompt and the `--force` warning; the four delete verification
outcomes; the walk errors (repeated uuid, empty intermediate page, `count_capped`, a capped page size that
continues); the `--scan-origin` slice across pages; the fabricated-default fixtures (a summary without
counts, a scan without `model_uri`, a file without `formats`); URIs with userinfo and signed queries in every
format and their absence from stderr and the debug log; the custom-rule instance; `pypi-auth`'s marker never
on stdout, stderr or in the debug log (4xx, 5xx, validation failures included) and the `--url-file` rules (an
existing path, a dangling symlink, `-`, 0600, no temporary left); `install` with the fake uv (argv exactly
`uv init --no-workspace -- <abs>` then `uv add --project <abs> --index airs-model-security=<index> -- model-security-client[<extras>]`,
the env of `uv add` holding the decoded pair and that of `uv init` not, no `UV_NO_CONFIG`, stdout empty, the
fake's output on stderr and scrubbed, the dry run under `--quiet` with POSIX quoting of a `$(id)` dir, every
`--dir` refusal before any request, the workspace refusal, a missing and a too-old uv, the init and add
failures, a signalled child, the persistence check with a fake that writes the credential, the signal
forwarded to the fake's process group and no child left); `--fetch-uv` against the loopback archive (a bad
hash leaves nothing, traversal and link entries skipped, a symlink named `uv-<target>/uv` refused, a duplicate
and a missing `uv` refused, 0755/0600 under 0700, a second run reuses with no request, a tampered copy, a
symlinked `tools` and a group-writable directory refused and unchanged, the real `~/.local/share/airs-cli`
untouched); interruption in every context of §17.16.

### 17.18 Choices decided

The user delegated every decision; each choice below takes the safest option that keeps the command useful
(the rejected alternative in each item).
1. `without_response_defaults()` on every model-security call through one helper (G20). Rejected: passing it
   only on the five calls whose schemas carry a default (easy to miss when a view grows).
2. Every walk is the shared CLI page loop (`src/walk.rs`, moved from `src/redteam/walk.rs`) with the scans
   `count_capped` latch. Rejected: the SDK `pages`/`list_all` walks (G19: no repeated-row or empty-page check).
3. `--scan-origin` is an exact local filter over a complete walk, then sliced (G18, D181). Rejected: a usage
   error naming the gap (breaks a documented TS flag), a filter on the single fetched page (a page of other
   origins would print nothing while matches exist), and a raw request with an unverified query parameter.
4. `scans list --search` keeps TypeScript's per-mode parameter (`search` on a page, `search_query` on a walk).
   Rejected: unifying on one parameter without evidence of which the API honours (a change could break the
   working path); the live read comparison exercises the single-page form.
5. `scans evaluations|violations|files`, `labels keys|values` and `models versions|files` gain the read
   contract (`--offset`, `--all`, `--max`) (D183). Rejected: TS's single page with no sign that more exist.
6. A status line only when a page does not show everything (else none, TS parity). Rejected: always printing
   `Showing …` (changes TS's stderr for complete listings) and never printing it (a truncated list looks complete).
7. `--limit` accepts 1–4,294,967,295 (the SDK's `u32`), with TS's defaults. Rejected: a 100 cap (no evidence of
   the server maximum).
8. An empty item in a comma list (`--source-types`, `--enabled-rules`, `--keys`) is a usage error. Rejected:
   sending an empty value (TS), which filters on nothing or deletes nothing while reporting success.
9. Confirmations on `groups delete`, `labels set` and `labels delete` only (D185). Rejected: confirming
   `labels add` (it changes only the keys the user names), `rule-instances update` (one named instance,
   reversible), `groups update` and `scans create` (their purpose; they run in CI).
10. `groups delete` reads the group before the prompt only when it prompts (to name it); with `--force` it sends
    TypeScript's sequence (DELETE, then the verification read). Rejected: a pre-read in every mode (an extra
    request with nothing to show).
11. `labels set` reads the scan first and names the keys it drops, in the prompt or a `--force` warning.
    Rejected: a silent replace (TS) and refusing a replace that drops labels.
12. The delete is confirmed by a 404 or `is_tombstone: true`; a group still present gets TS's warning; any other
    verification failure is a warning that the result could not be verified; all exit 0, because the DELETE was
    accepted (D186). Rejected: TS's success on any failure, and exit 1 after an accepted DELETE.
13. `groups update` needs a flag; `--description ''` clears the description; label keys and values print as json
    string arrays. Rejected: TS's `PUT {}` reported as an update, and TS's truthiness rule (cannot clear).
14. `rule-instances update` sends only the fields its file names and needs one of `state`/`field_values`.
    Rejected: a read-modify-write overlay of the current values (the PUT's handling of omitted fields is unknown,
    and copying values the user did not name could fail validation or change them).
15. Group and rule-instance configs refuse unknown keys; the scan config forwards them (TS; a passthrough schema).
    Rejected: TS's silent drop for groups (the user's field is lost), and refusing unknown scan keys (could block
    API fields the SDK schema does not model).
16. JSON keeps TS's projections and key order but omits what the server did not send, keeps `null`, and keeps the
    summary keys with `null` counts (D180); the table detail lists every projection key. Rejected: the wire objects
    (breaks TS's documented JSON) and TS's invented `''`, `0`, `[]` and `{}`.
17. A rule instance's nested `rule` (and the added `customRule`) stay raw snake_case, as TS. Rejected: camelCasing
    nested server objects (breaks TS's JSON for no safety gain).
18. Model URIs withhold userinfo, query and fragment in every format, and their credential parts join the `SecretSet` (D191, choice 44).
    Rejected: printing them raw (TS), which shows S3/GCS/Azure signed URLs and inline credentials.
19. The tenant `defaultOutput` is honoured by the reads TypeScript resolves it for (class A) only. Rejected: honouring
    it everywhere (a json default would change the writes' and `pypi-auth`'s output unasked).
20. TypeScript's `scans list` example with `--eval-outcome MALICIOUS` is kept. Rejected: rewording a TS help example
    (not a safety or correctness fix of behaviour; the value is sent and the service decides).
21. `--labels` stays an inline JSON argument; no `--labels-file`. Rejected: adding a file option (labels are not
    credentials; the surface stays TS's).
22. `pypi-auth` withholds the whole userinfo (the username too) with `[withheld]` in every format; there is no reveal
    flag. Rejected: D139's "json prints it" (the scope forbids printing the credential) and masking only the password.
23. The only channel for the full URL is `--url-file <path>`: a new 0600 file through `publish_new`, checked before the
    tenant, written only for a URL that passes the index check (D194). Rejected: a dotenv or shell-export file
    (quoting injection), a netrc entry (a host-wide credential that outlives the run), stdout behind a flag, and the
    name `--credential-file` (the file holds a URL).
24. `pypi-auth` is a read with the SDK's read retries. Rejected: one attempt (a GET duplicates nothing; each attempt
    only mints a fresh short-lived token, as in TS).
25. The credential reaches uv only through `UV_INDEX_AIRS_MODEL_SECURITY_USERNAME/PASSWORD` in `uv add`'s environment,
    with the credential-free named index `airs-model-security` in argv (D196). Rejected: the URL with userinfo in argv
    (TS; world-readable in `ps`), `UV_INDEX` with userinfo (clobbers the user's own `UV_INDEX`), and a `NETRC` file
    (writes a credential to disk).
26. uv 0.12.17 is pinned (the measured version), Linux uses the musl assets only. Rejected: the newest release (its
    persistence behaviour unmeasured) and glibc detection (unreliable from a static musl CLI).
27. A uv from `PATH` must be at least 0.12.0; the managed copy must report 0.12.17. Rejected: any uv (older behaviour
    unverified) and exactly 0.12.17 on `PATH` (too strict for package-manager installs).
28. The managed uv is used only with `--fetch-uv` (and then reused when it verifies). Rejected: using it implicitly when
    `PATH` has none (the user did not ask for a downloaded binary in this run) and re-downloading on every run.
29. `--dir` must not exist; the CLI creates it exclusively just before `uv init`; a target inside a uv workspace is
    refused; `uv init --no-workspace` and `--` with an absolute path (D198). Rejected: allowing an existing empty
    directory (a check-then-use race and reuse ambiguity) and TS's anything-goes.
30. A failed uv step leaves `<dir>` in place and says so. Rejected: deleting a directory after an external tool ran in it.
31. A dry run still sends the PyPI auth request (it shows the real index host and checks the tenant; TS parity).
    Rejected: skipping the request (a plan that does not prove the tenant works).
32. The dry-run plan is shell text in every format (`--output` validated, then ignored), printed under `--quiet`.
    Rejected: a json plan document (a second, unneeded surface) and TS's quiet-suppressed plan.
33. uv's output is piped, scrubbed and written to stderr; stdin is `/dev/null`; each child runs in its own process group.
    Rejected: inherited stdio (stdout would carry uv's text, and a future uv that printed the credential could not be
    scrubbed) and the shared process group (uv would get a terminal Ctrl-C twice).
34. After `uv add`, `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` are checked for the credential (D196). Rejected: trusting uv's measured
    stripping without a check (a future uv could change it).
35. Extraction is `flate2` (already in the lock file, exact-pinned `=1.1.10`) plus an in-house strict tar reader that takes
    one regular entry and writes no archive path. Rejected: the `tar` crate (a new dependency whose unpack API
    materialises links) and refusing any unexpected entry type (would fail on harmless extras such as `uvx`).
36. The `--fetch-uv` test hook exists only in debug builds and only for loopback http URLs. Rejected: a hidden flag or a
    release-build environment override (a checksum bypass) and real downloads in tests (forbidden).
37. Live scan flow: the Rust CLI creates the one budgeted scan, the TypeScript CLI only reads it and writes labels on it;
    the scan stays in the tenant because the API cannot delete it. Rejected: one scan per CLI (exceeds the budget of 1,
    and TS replays a billed POST on a 5xx).
38. A live group counts as cleaned up on a 404, `is_tombstone: true` or its absence from the prefixed listing, after a
    bounded re-check. Rejected: re-sending deletes in a loop (soft deletes are asynchronous, MS§16).
39. The uv download and the uv children are not recorded in the debug log. Rejected: adding non-API traffic to the API log
    (its schema is the SDK request record; the child output is already on stderr, scrubbed).
40. No PyPI index host restriction (the service names its own registry). Rejected: requiring `*.pkg.dev` (would break a
    regional or future registry; the credential belongs to the host the service names).

Decided while building step 1 (the reads):

41. `rule-instances get` prints `Rule Name` from `rule.name`, else `custom_rule.name`, when non-empty, never a
    uuid; the list's label keeps the uuid fallbacks of §17.4. Rejected: the whole label (TS prints no `Rule
    Name` line for an instance without an embedded rule, so a uuid there would break the TS bytes of a
    built-in instance).
42. The fixture's seeded dataset is the TypeScript-capture data, parity-clean; every §12 variant is added by the
    test that pins it, and a required field (`model_uri`, `scan_origin`, …) missing from a record is pinned as
    the response-validation error (`tests/modelsec_reads.rs`, `errors::a_broken_record_is_a_decode_error`).
    Rejected: seeding every variant (each byte-parity test would need its own tolerance) and a scan without
    `model_uri` (neither SDK can read one).
43. A field value that is an array prints its items joined `, `, an item that is an object or an array as compact
    JSON (the D192 rule at item level), `null` items empty. Rejected: JavaScript `join` (`[object Object]`).
44. A model URI registers, raw and percent-decoded, its password and the value of every credential query key
    (`CREDENTIAL_QUERY_KEYS`: the S3, GCS and Azure signature, credential and token keys, `sig`, `token`,
    `key`, …) whatever their length, and its username, fragment and every other query value (a bare query word
    included) of at least 8 characters; the fragment rule of §6 then withholds a server name of four or more
    characters that occurs inside one of them (the safe direction). Rejected: the userinfo only (a signature in
    a query value could reach an error or a name); every part of any length, the whole query included (as
    first built: every presigned URL's `X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host` and `X-Amz-Expires=3600`, or Azure's
    `ss=b`, withheld every group name, label key or value and path containing `host`, `3600` or `b` on every
    row of a listing, and failed the debug log's line check; review finding).
45. The server-text keys of §17.3 are checked at any depth (a nested raw `rule`'s `name`, `description` and
    `display_name` included) and the label `key` and `value` of every `labels` array; the label key and value
    lists of `labels keys|values` are checked item by item. Rejected: the top level only (the nested rule
    prints the same names).
46. `--start ''`, `--end ''` and `--model-version ''` are the window usage error (zod refuses `""`, TS fails too).
    Rejected: treating an empty bound as absent (a silently widened window).
47. The `--scan-origin` slice line is printed whenever the client filter ran without `--all` (also
    `Showing 0 of 0`), so a filtered page is never mistaken for the service's page. Rejected: no line for a
    complete slice (the user cannot tell the filter was local).
48. The runner's `XDG_DATA_HOME` default lands with step 3, the first step whose commands read it; no step-1
    command reads `XDG_DATA_HOME` or writes outside the tenant store. Rejected: adding it in step 1 (it would
    change the TypeScript runs' environment for no step-1 test).

Decided while building step 2 (the writes):

49. The `--config` files are read when the command runs (after the debug log, before the tenant) and
    their bodies built then; the bodies built from arguments (`groups update`, `--labels`, `--keys`) are
    built and checked during planning. Rejected: reading files during planning (before the debug notice,
    against the §17.3 order).
50. The unknown-key refusal names the first unknown key in byte order (the order of serde_json's map;
    `preserve_order` stays off), terminal-safe and cut to 64 characters with `…`. Rejected: listing every
    unknown key (more user text in an error) and the file's order (needs `preserve_order`).
51. A `null` for an optional group key (`description`, `rule_configurations`) is the schema's refusal
    (D116, exit 1). TypeScript drops a `null` `rule_configurations` by truthiness and sends the rest (its
    schema refuses `description: null` as well). Rejected: dropping a `null` silently (a key the user
    wrote would vanish, the D188 reason).
52. Each attempt of a write builds its own request options (the 60 s budget, no response defaults), so the
    one 401 replay has a whole budget. Rejected: one options value for both attempts (its deadline is
    absolute, so the replay could start with no time left).
53. The reads a write makes first (the `groups delete` prompt read, the `labels set` scan read) and the
    delete verification read use the SDK read retries and validate without response defaults; an
    interruption during the first two changed nothing. Rejected: one attempt for those reads (a GET
    duplicates nothing).
54. Once a `groups delete` DELETE was accepted, every later interruption reports
    `the delete request was accepted; its result was not verified`, also after the verification printed
    its line; a delete never reports `the change was saved`. Rejected: `the change was saved` (a soft
    delete may still be pending).
55. `labels set` registers the read scan's model-URI parts in the secret set and checks the dropped keys
    against it (`[withheld]`), and the `labels delete` prompt checks the given keys the same way, as the
    read layouts do. Rejected: printing the keys unchecked.
56. The `labels set --force` warning is printed only when the replacement drops at least one key, and a
    key the scan holds twice is named once. Rejected: a warning on every forced replace (noise) and
    repeated names.
57. `labels delete` reads nothing before its prompt (TypeScript's single request); the prompt names the
    given keys. Rejected: reading the scan to name only the keys it has (one more request; the service
    does not report absent keys either, TS parity).
58. The outcome line's `<uuid>` is the answered record's `uuid` (terminal-safe), printed on stderr before
    the record is written to stdout. Rejected: the requested id (a create has none).
59. The fixture's created ids are deterministic (`U(101 + n)` groups, `U(451 + n)` scans), and every write
    test fails a run other than `scans create` that sends the billed `POST /v1/scans`. Rejected: random ids
    (the parity bytes would differ between the sides).

Decided while building step 3 (`pypi-auth`, `install`, the live tier):

60. The fake uv records each invocation in its own directory `tmp/uv-calls/<n>/` (`argv` NUL-separated,
    `info` lines, `signals`, `finished`) instead of one JSON line per call. Rejected: JSON lines from a
    `/bin/sh` script (argv elements cannot be JSON-escaped safely in POSIX shell).
61. The debug-build test hook is read only when `--fetch-uv` is given (a plain `install` never reads it).
    Rejected: refusing every `install` whose environment holds a malformed hook variable.
62. A `uv --version` that cannot be started, times out, exits non-zero or prints no version line is the one
    "not a usable uv" message. Rejected: a separate `Cannot start` for the version check (two messages for
    one remedy).
63. The index check also refuses an index (the URL without its userinfo) that still contains `@` or a control
    character. Rejected: passing such a path to uv.
64. A PyPI URL without a credential is printed `[withheld]` whole by `pypi-auth`: the full URL is registered
    whatever it holds, and a form that carries a registered value is withheld. Rejected: registering the URL
    only when it has a userinfo (one rule for every answer is the safe direction).
65. The persistence check skips a missing `pyproject.toml` like a missing `uv.lock`; an unreadable or
    oversized one fails the install with a message naming the file. Rejected: treating an unreadable file as
    clean.
66. A managed copy that another run renamed into place first is verified and used; a failed temporary is
    removed; any other install failure names the tools directory. Rejected: replacing the other run's copy.
67. A `--fetch-uv --dry-run` with no tools directory creates nothing and shows the path as computed (not
    canonicalised). Rejected: creating the tools directory for a dry run.
68. The first signal while a child runs is forwarded by whichever thread sees both the signal and the child
    (an atomic once-flag), so a signal that arrives between the spawn and the registration is not lost; every
    later signal sends `SIGKILL` to the group. Rejected: forwarding from the signal thread only.
69. The `--version` child also runs in its own process group and is killed (not forwarded) on a signal, then
    `Interrupted; nothing was installed`. Rejected: waiting for it (it may hang on a broken install).
70. Live: the group json projection has no `is_tombstone` (TS parity), so the harness counts a group deleted on
    the Rust delete's own verification line (`deleted.` or `(the service is removing it).`), on a 404, or on
    its absence from the prefixed listing (the service is assumed to hide tombstones there; the self-tests'
    fixture does, `ModelSecData::list_hides_tombstones`); the sweeper skips a 404 and otherwise sends one
    delete per sweep. Rejected: adding `is_tombstone` to the json (breaks TS's documented JSON).
71. Live scan flow names: label keys and values `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-k<n>` / `-v<n>`; the scan's ledger name
    `airs-rs-e2e-<run id>-scan-sc` (the sweeper never parses it, scans are never swept). Rejected: journalling
    the scan under its group's name (the ledger would show two kinds under one name).
72. Live `pypi-auth`: one summary row for the four Rust runs (choice 81) plus the `pypi-auth credential withheld` notice;
    the credential forms join the session's leak set, and the summary itself is leak-checked before it is
    returned (`Session::summary_check`). Every live run refuses a TypeScript `pypi-auth` and any `install`
    (`live::model_security_refusal`). Rejected: one row per format (the same fact three times).
73. The runner refuses a `--fetch-uv` run that is not a dry run unless `AIRS_CLI_TEST_UV_ARCHIVE_URL` is set, so
    no test can reach github.com. Rejected: relying on each test to set the hook.
74. A scan-flow group the service refuses to delete (its scan references it) stays in `resourcesLeft`, so the
    live test fails visibly and the sweeper finishes it later. Rejected: passing with a notice (a leftover
    would go unnoticed).
75. The fixture knobs of the live self-tests: `created_at: "now"` (records created now, so the read-only
    resolution of an unknown scan create can match "created after the run started"), `list_hides_tombstones`,
    `GroupDeleteMode::Lagging(n)` (a soft delete visible to `n` more reads), `instances_for_created_groups`
    and `created_scans_finish_as`. Rejected: changing the defaults (the step-1 and step-2 parity bytes rely
    on them).
76. The live reads compare JSON with an explicit tolerance function (`live::modelsec::ms_json_equal`: an
    absent Rust key matches TS's invented `''`/`0`/`[]`/`{}`, a `null` count TS's `0`, the TS `modelUri`
    withheld first, the Rust-only `customRuleUuid`/`customRule` ignored) and the scan table after the TS
    `Model URI` cells are withheld. Rejected: comparing only exit codes for documents that legitimately differ.
77. The live scan flow needs `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_WRITES=1` as well as its own `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_SCAN=1`: it creates
    and deletes a group and writes labels on both CLIs, so the write opt-in is required and the billed scan is
    an extra one; without the write opt-in it is `model-security scan skipped` before anything opens. Rejected:
    `AIRS_RS_LIVE_MS_SCAN` alone (the flow wrote without the write opt-in; review finding).
78. The live teardown goes on with the next group after a delete that aborts (a spawn failure, a leak or
    integrity check on its output) and reports every id still unconfirmed; the first abort is the run's
    error. A ledger failure needs no stop: `delete` journals `pending` before it sends anything, so no delete
    is ever sent unjournalled. Rejected: stopping at the first abort (the later run groups were left to the
    sweeper; review finding).
79. `uv add` runs with the `--no-build` flag (D203), with a detail line after a failed `uv add` saying how to
    build a dependency without the credential. Rejected: allowing builds and recording the exposure as a
    residual risk (any sdist dependency would run third-party code holding the registry token);
    `UV_NO_BUILD=1` in the child's environment (the same effect, but invisible in the dry-run plan; the
    flag is explicit in argv and in the plan); removing the credential from the build environment only (uv
    has no such control).
80. The uv-workspace check reads the ancestors of the parent as typed, lexically normalised and canonical,
    and a successful `uv add` that left no `<dir>/uv.lock` fails the install (the lock it wrote elsewhere is
    unchecked). Rejected: the canonical ancestors only (uv took over a workspace reached through a
    symlinked parent and wrote its `uv.lock` and `.venv`; review finding, reproduced with uv 0.12.17);
    adding an empty `[tool.uv.workspace]` to the new project's `pyproject.toml` (it rewrites the file uv
    generated and relies on uv's unmeasured discovery order); skipping a missing `uv.lock` (as first built).
81. The live `pypi-auth` check runs json, pretty and table each with its own `--url-file`, then pretty without
    one; every output is checked against the forms of every saved URL, for any URI userinfo but
    `[withheld]@`, and for exactly the withheld form of its own URL. Rejected: one URL file for all runs (each
    call may mint a new token, so a rotated token printed by a later run went unseen; review finding).
82. A forwarded uv line longer than 64 KiB is split where no registered form straddles the split (up to the
    longest form less one byte, at most 32 KiB, is kept for the next piece). Rejected: splitting at exactly
    64 KiB (a credential across the split printed as two clear halves; review finding); dropping the rest of
    a long line (a credential prefix before the drop point would still print); unbounded line buffering.
83. A `scans list` single page whose response says `count_capped: true` is given no total for its status
    line, so a full page prints `Showing <rows> (more may be available; use --all)` (D182). Rejected:
    `Showing <rows> of <cap>` (it states a cap as a count) and no line when the cap equals the rows shown (a
    truncated page looked complete; review finding).
84. The `labels values <key>` segment keeps the SDK encoding and the difference from `encodeURIComponent`
    is recorded (D202). Rejected: a CLI-encoded raw segment with `( ) ! * '` unescaped (it would bypass the
    SDK's segment rule, G21, for a cosmetic difference; percent-encoded sub-delimiters decode to the same
    key).
85. The model-security colour spans have a forced-colour parity test over every pretty list and get
    (`CLICOLOR_FORCE` for Rust, `FORCE_COLOR` for TS). Rejected: citing the `NO_COLOR` byte-parity test for
    the colours (it compared no colour byte; review finding).
86. The D200 parity test gives the Rust side the fake uv's long default sleep (30 s) and only the TS side the
    3 s sleep its orphan wait needs. Rejected: 3 s on both sides (a loaded machine could let the Rust child
    finish before the forwarded signal; review finding).

## 18. M6d Runtime extras (0.9)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-runtime-extras.md` (cited as **TX§n**:
`api-keys`, `customer-apps`, `deployment-profiles`, `scan-logs`), `docs/research/ts-runtime-dashboard-report.md`
(cited as **TR§n**: `dashboard`, `sessions`, `report`, profile backup and restore) and
`docs/research/rs-sdk-runtime-extras.md` (cited as **RX§n**). This section overrides them where they
differ (they disagree on the key channel, on `--unit`, on auth codes and on the consumption window; this
section is the decision); their provisional row numbers and recommendations are not binding. Every
difference from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row (D204–D226; D11, D12, D14, D35, D37, D50, D52, D64, D73,
D95, D155 and D156 extended). The byte captures of the TypeScript layouts are in TX§1–§9 and TR§1–§7;
"the TS layout" below means those bytes, with the changes this section lists.

**SDK.** scm-sdk 0.1.1 has an operation for every command of this section, with the TypeScript paths,
methods, query names and request and response schemas (RX§0, RX§4). The `management` feature (already
enabled) covers every M6d client, and it pulls in `dlp`, which restore needs; there is no `Cargo.toml`
or lock-file change. The findings of RX§9:
- **G26** (shape; CLI workaround adopted). The API key value of a `create` or `regenerate` answer is a
  plain `Optional<String>` (`gen:4645-4646`; only `ApiKey`'s whole-struct `Debug` is redacted,
  `gen:4965-4967`; `Serialize` writes it), and the typed `api_keys().create|regenerate` validate the
  answer against `ApiKeySchema` before the CLI sees it (`mg:api_keys.rs:46-61`, `:138-155`), so a 2xx
  answer that lacks a required field (`auth_code`, `expiration`, …) is a decode error and its shown-once
  key value is lost (TX§5.2 captured this in TS). The SDK is not patched. The CLI sends these two writes
  as raw requests on the management plane (`RawRequest::new(POST, "/v1/mgmt/apikey")` and
  `RawRequest::new(POST, "/v1/mgmt/apikey/regenerate").segment(id)`, `.json_value(..)` of the body the CLI
  validated with `ApiKeyCreateRequest::parse` / `ApiKeyRegenerateRequest::parse` in `Mode::Request` (re-serialised,
  sorted keys, D35), sent with `ManagementClient::client().send_json::<serde_json::Value>` through `writes::attempt`,
  never replayed by the SDK; the method is `reqwest::Method`, the same `http` crate the SDK uses, so no dependency
  changes), then validates the answer itself with
  `ApiKey::parse(value, Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults)`. The `api_key` string is taken out and registered
  in the `SecretSet` before the answer is validated, so a schema mismatch still saves the key (§18.5).
  Safe: same path, method, body and schemas as the typed call; only the order of "save the key" and
  "validate the rest" changes. **Amended while building step 2:** `RawRequest::named` is `pub(crate)` in 0.1.1
  (`rs:engine.rs:108-111`), so the two raw POSTs cannot carry the SDK's operation names: the `--debug` log records them
  as the raw default `custom.request` (as the 0.6 raw read was `custom.read`, §15). Only the record's `operation` field
  differs; it is pinned by `tests/runtime_extras_writes.rs::debug::writes_record_their_operations_and_no_body` (choice 50).
- **G27** (G10 for M6d). The frozen schemas default `SecurityProfileListResponse.ai_profiles`,
  `CustomTopicListResponse.custom_topics` and `CustomTopic.examples` to `[]`, so a typed read with the
  default options turns an absent profile or topic list into an empty one and a topic without `examples`
  into one with `examples: []` (TR§2.2). **Every M6d SDK call passes
  `RequestOptions::…without_response_defaults()`** (one options helper, `runtime::options`), also where it
  changes nothing (api-keys, customer apps, deployment profiles, the dashboard: no response default,
  TX§2.11). It matters for the report (D214), the backup's stored topics (D215) and restore's planning
  (D218). Request-side defaults (the dashboard query defaults, `CreateCustomTopicRequest`) are applied by
  both SDKs (TS parity, not a difference).
- **G28.** `ApiKeysClient::list_all` and `CustomerAppsClient::list_all` detect a repeated cursor and an
  empty non-final page but not a repeated row (`mg:api_keys.rs:78-120`, `mg:customer_apps.rs:73-115`,
  `rs:pagination.rs:346-391`). The CLI checks the row identity (`api_key_id`, `customer_appId`) over the
  collected rows; a repeat is the D37 error (D219). Safe.
- **G29** (difference). `api-keys delete <name>` and `regenerate <id>` go through the SDK segment rule
  (`.segment(..)`, `rs:config.rs:121-151`), which refuses `''`, `.`, `..`, `\`, control characters and
  encoded traversal; the CLI checks it during planning (D213). TS `encodeURIComponent`s anything, and its
  URL parser then resolves `..` (TX§2.8).
- **G30.** The dashboard client is derived from the management client and needs
  `with_dashboard_endpoint` with an origin the shared destination policy already admits (`mg:mod.rs:59-78`,
  `rs:engine.rs:438-444`); `ManagementClients::build_for` admits `mgmtDashboardEndpoint` (§18.3). There is
  no customer-app read by id (`get` takes `app_name`, `mg:customer_apps.rs:46-56`), so `customer-apps
  update <appId>` finds the current record through the list walk when it prompts (§18.8). Safe.
- **G31.** `ManagementClient::dlp(endpoint)` inherits the management client's limits (8 MiB responses);
  restore's transfer client is built with the M6b `max_response_bytes` (32 MiB) and admits `dlpEndpoint`,
  one OAuth identity (§18.3). Safe.
- **G32–G35** (notes): `scan_logs().query` is a non-replay-safe POST the TS CLI never calls and the port
  never calls either (§18.11); the option and query structs are `#[non_exhaustive]` with `Default`
  (built with `Default::default()` or `new` and field assignment); the `--debug` log records the SDK
  operation names as they are (`airs.management.api_keys.list|delete` — the two raw key POSTs are `custom.request`,
  G26 —, `….customer_apps.*`,
  `….deployment_profiles.list`, `….dashboard.*`, `….profiles.*`, `….topics.*`, the M6b DLP data-profile
  list; the debug tests pin them, as G9, G17, G23); `ApiKeyDeleteResponse` and `CustomerAppDeleteResponse`
  are unions with an `Unknown(JsonValue)` arm, so any decodable 2xx JSON is a delete answer and the CLI
  prints a fixed acknowledgement, never the value (D208).
- G3, G4 and G7 apply unchanged. **Nothing in §18 is blocked on scm-sdk.**

### 18.1 Build steps

0.9 is built in three steps. Each step ships its executable, parity and `dNN_` tests and leaves the checks
green.

| Step | Commands and work |
|---|---|
| 1. Reads | `runtime api-keys list\|ls`; `runtime customer-apps list\|ls`, `get`, `consumption`; `runtime deployment-profiles list\|ls`; `runtime scan-logs query` (repaired by D338; direct lookups D339); `runtime dashboard applications`, `application`, `application-violations`, `top-applications`, `violations-trend`, `apps-list`; `runtime sessions chart`, `list\|ls`, `get`, `transaction`, `scan-content`. Shared: `ManagementClients::build_for` with the dashboard plane, the argument checks of §18.3, the options helper, `walk.rs` extended with `walk_with` (§18.13), the views and layouts of §18.4, §18.7, §18.9–§18.13, the `api_key` withholding (D205), the fixture's runtime read and dashboard routes |
| 2. Writes and the report | `runtime api-keys create`, `regenerate`, `delete\|rm`; `runtime customer-apps update`, `delete\|rm`; `runtime report`. Shared: the `--key-file` reservation (`files::Reservation`), the G26 raw writes, the `--config` readers, the confirmations, the M6d `Change` words and hints, the original runtime model (now test-only) and replacement Signal Brief (`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/signal/`, D340), the fixture's write routes, counters and markers |
| 3. Transfer and live | `runtime profiles backup [profile]`, `runtime profiles restore <file>`: the Rust format, the strict reader, the TS planner, `compareRuntimePolicies`, the executor; the live tier's M6d reads and the profile-transfer write flow with their loopback self-tests (§10) |

Each step registers its own commands: until a step lands, its commands are not in the clap tree (`runtime
api-keys create` is an unrecognised subcommand in a step-1 build, exit 2, D1), and the group help lists
only the commands that exist (`runtime report` is not listed before step 2).

**Step 1 is built** (`src/runtime/{mod,list,views,consumption}.rs`, `src/commands/runtime_extras.rs`, `runtime_keys.rs`,
`runtime_apps.rs`, `runtime_inventory.rs`, `runtime_dashboard.rs`; `ManagementClients::build_for`; `walk_with`; the
fixture's `Route::Runtime(Rx)` read and dashboard routes; `tests/runtime_extras_reads.rs`, `tests/runtime_dashboard.rs`,
`tests/parity_runtime_extras.rs`, `tests/parity_runtime_dashboard.rs`). The details it settled are choices 41–46,
73 and 74.

**Step 2 is built** (`src/runtime/keys.rs`, `files::Reservation`, `src/commands/runtime_write.rs`, the writes in
`runtime_keys.rs` and `runtime_apps.rs`, `src/commands/runtime_report.rs`, `src/report/runtime.rs`, `runtime_html.rs`,
`runtime_tests.rs`, the `HtmlReport` format policy; the fixture's write routes (`Rx::ApiKeyCreate`, `ApiKeyRegenerate`,
`ApiKeyDelete`, `CustomerAppUpdate`, `CustomerAppDelete`) with the `RuntimeData` knobs `omit_key_value`,
`omit_auth_code`, `key_delete_answer` and `app_delete_answer` (the 401, 403, 5xx, undecodable, held and
applied-then-dropped answers are the generic `Planned` overrides), `--key-file` in the runner's `PATH_FLAGS` and
`report` in its runtime-extras groups; `tests/runtime_extras_writes.rs`, `tests/runtime_report.rs`,
`tests/parity_runtime_extras_writes.rs`, `tests/parity_runtime_report.rs`). No dependency or lock-file change, and
nothing of step 2 is blocked on scm-sdk 0.1.1: the deletes and `update` are the SDK's typed operations, the key writes
the G26 raw POSTs (amended: named `custom.request` in the debug log). The details it settled are choices 47–56; its
review added choices 75 and 76 and the runner knob `RunOptions::stall_stderr` (`Running::release_stderr`), which
holds a run between two known stderr writes so a signal can be sent after a key was saved.

**Step 3 is built** (`src/runtime/transfer/{mod,plan,policy}.rs` with the planner unit tests in
`src/runtime/transfer/plan_tests.rs`, `src/commands/profile_backup.rs`, `profile_restore.rs`; `ManagementClients::dlp`
(the DLP client of `Planes { dlp: true }`, G31); `writes::Failure` and `writes::classify`, now shared by the DLP and the
profile restore; the fixture's `FixtureServer::set_profile_write_edit` knob (the service adding defaults or changing a
policy after a profile write) and the restore positional and `--dlp-map`/`--on-missing-dlp` values in the runner's
argument checks; the live flows `live::runtime` and `live::profile_transfer` with their gates, hooks and self-tests;
`tests/runtime_transfer.rs`, `tests/parity_runtime_transfer.rs`). No dependency or lock-file change, and nothing of
step 3 is blocked on scm-sdk 0.1.1: the inventories, creates and updates are the SDK's typed operations (with
`without_response_defaults()`, G27), the DLP catalog the M6b sweep. The details it settled are choices 57–66.

### 18.2 Commands and options

Help texts, group descriptions and arguments are TypeScript's (TX§1, TR§1, the captured `--help` of every
leaf) with the program name `airs`, the `--output` line generated from the format policy (§2.4),
one `(default: …)` where commander printed two (TX§1), and the options marked **(Rust)** with the help
text given here (pinned leaf by leaf against the reference by `help_texts_match_typescript`). The `runtime`
group gains `api-keys`, `customer-apps`, `dashboard`, `deployment-profiles`, `report`, `scan-logs` and
`sessions` in TypeScript's sorted order; `runtime profiles` gains `backup` and `restore`. Every `list` has
the visible alias `ls` (`sessions list` included) and every `delete` the alias `rm`. A group without a
subcommand prints its help on stderr, exit 2 (D1). `runtime report` has no `dashboard` alias (TS
`report-naming.spec.ts`). The `Examples:` blocks of `report` and `profiles backup|restore` are TypeScript's
with the program name, except that the report example with `--output markdown` is dropped (D155) and the backup example
`"Production" --file-format yaml --output-file ./production.yaml` reads `"Production" --output-file ./production.json`
(D215).

| Command | Arguments and options |
|---|---|
| `api-keys list\|ls` | `--limit <n>` (default `100`), `--offset <n>` (default `0`), `--all`, `--max <n>` (default `10000`) |
| `api-keys create` | `--config <path>` (required), `--key-file <path>` (Rust, required, `New private file (mode 0600) that receives the API key; never overwritten (the key is never printed)`) |
| `api-keys regenerate <apiKeyId>` | `--interval <n>` (required), `--unit <unit>` (required), `--updated-by <email>`, `--key-file <path>` (Rust, required, as `create`), `--force` (Rust, `Skip the confirmation prompt`) |
| `api-keys delete\|rm <apiKeyName>` | `--updated-by <email>` (required), `--force` (Rust) |
| `customer-apps list\|ls` | as `api-keys list` |
| `customer-apps get <appName>` | none |
| `customer-apps update <appId>` | `--config <path>` (required), `--force` (Rust) |
| `customer-apps delete\|rm <appName>` | `--updated-by <email>` (required), `--force` (Rust) |
| `customer-apps consumption [appName]` | `--time-interval <n>` (default `30`) |
| `deployment-profiles list\|ls` | `--unactivated` |
| `scan-logs query` | `--interval <n>` (required), `--unit <unit>` (required), `--filter <filter>` (default `all`), `--limit <n>` (default `50`), `--offset <n>` (default `0`); hidden `--page <n>`, `--page-size <n>` |
| `dashboard applications` | `--interval <n>` (`1`), `--unit <unit>` (`day`), `--limit <n>` (`25`), `--offset <n>` (`0`) |
| `dashboard application`, `dashboard application-violations` | `--app-id <id>` (required), `--app-name <name>` (required), `--interval <n>` (`30`), `--unit <unit>` (`days`) |
| `dashboard top-applications`, `dashboard violations-trend` | `--interval <n>` (`1`), `--unit <unit>` (`day`) |
| `dashboard apps-list` | `--interval <n>` (`30`), `--unit <unit>` (`days`) |
| `sessions chart` | `--interval <n>` (`1`), `--unit <unit>` (`day`) |
| `sessions list\|ls` | `--interval <n>` (`1`), `--unit <unit>` (`day`), `--limit <n>` (`25`), `--offset <n>` (`0`), `--all`, `--max <n>` (`10000`) |
| `sessions get` | `--session-id <id>`, `--app-id <id>`, `--app-name <name>` (required); `--interval <n>` (`30`), `--unit <unit>` (`days`), `--limit <n>` (`25`), `--offset <n>` (`0`) |
| `sessions transaction` | `--session-id`, `--app-id`, `--app-name`, `--scan-id <id>`, `--scan-sub-req-id <n>` (required); `--interval <n>` (`30`), `--unit <unit>` (`days`) |
| `sessions scan-content` | `--scan-id <id>`, `--scan-sub-req-id <n>` (required); `--show-content`, `--output-file <path>` |
| `report` | `--output-file <path>`, `--title <text>` (`Daily environment report`), `--max-pages <n>` (`40`), `--strict`; the leaf `--output` of TS is the global flag (refused, D155) |
| `profiles backup [profile]` | `--all`, `--file-format <format>` (`json`), `--output-file <path>`, `--max-pages <n>` (`100`) |
| `profiles restore <file>` | `--dry-run`, `--name-prefix <prefix>`, `--on-conflict <policy>` (`error`), `--on-missing-dlp <policy>` (`error`), `--dlp-map <source=destination>` (repeatable), `--max-pages <n>` (`100`), `--expect-tsg <id>`, `--force`, `--allow-other-tenant` (Rust, `Restore a backup exported from another TSG into the selected tenant`) |

The leaf `--output <format>` options of TypeScript are the global `--output` here (§2.3). Boolean options
take no value; a repeated option takes its last value (TS), except `--dlp-map`, which collects. No other
option is added: there is no `--show-key` or reveal flag for API keys (choice 3), no `--show-auth-codes`
(choice 6) and no `--app-id` on `consumption` (choice 20).

### 18.3 Common rules

**Clients and planes** (RX§1.2). Every M6d command that sends requests builds its client with
`ManagementClients::build_for(config, session, secrets, debug, Planes { dashboard, dlp })`
(`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/clients.rs`; the existing `build` is `build_for(.., Planes::default())`, so no existing command's
destination policy widens) from the selected tenant only:
- `mgmtEndpoint` (else `https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/aisec`) for api keys, customer apps,
  deployment profiles, profiles and topics; with `dashboard`, `mgmtDashboardEndpoint` (else the same TS
  default, `co.ts:27`; **not** `mgmtEndpoint`, TS parity) for every `/v1/mgmt/dashboard/v2/…` route and
  `/v1/mgmt/reports/scancontent`, sent with `x-tsg-id: <mgmtTsgId>` (the SDK's dashboard client, TS
  parity); with `dlp` (restore only), `dlpEndpoint` (else the §16.3 default); and `mgmtTokenEndpoint`.
  Each is admitted by §5 (the D48 message names the key, never the value); one `OriginPolicy` admits them
  all, one OAuth identity (one token per invocation, TS parity).
- `Planes { dashboard: true }`: `customer-apps consumption`, every `dashboard` and `sessions` command,
  `report`; `Planes { dlp: true }`: `profiles restore`, whose client has `max_response_bytes` 32 MiB (G31).
- The §3.5 management credential check (`mgmtClientId`, `mgmtClientSecret`, `mgmtTsgId`) before any client
  is built, with the §3.5 messages (TS transfer's own `Profile transfer requires configured Management
  client ID, secret and TSG ID`, exit 2, is not used, as D161); the management OAuth plane only, never
  scanner credentials.
- `max_retries = 5` for replay-safe reads (D10). A construction failure is
  `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:The management client could not be configured` (exit 1). Every command except `report`
  awaits the token before its first request, so a token failure is the §6 `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:…` message
  (the dashboard and sessions generic line for those commands, below).

No environment variable is read (§2.6; the docs' `PANW_MGMT_DASHBOARD_ENDPOINT` is read by neither CLI,
TR§0). `--tenant` selects the tenant as for every command (§3.4). **No doctor or tenant wording changes**:
the management-credential line already names the management commands generically, no TS doctor probe reads
`mgmtDashboardEndpoint`, and `mgmtDashboardEndpoint` and `dlpEndpoint` are already §3.3 endpoint keys shown
by `tenant read` with the D45 rule (TX§11).

**Request options** (one helper, `runtime::options`; every call `.without_response_defaults()`, G27):

| Calls | Options |
|---|---|
| api-keys, customer-apps and deployment-profiles reads; the `consumption` reads | the SDK read retries (D10), `SINGLE_REQUEST_BUDGET` per read, `WALK_BUDGET` per walk (a walk's token included) |
| `dashboard` and `sessions` reads | `with_retries(0)` (TS `numRetries: 0`) and one CLI re-read after an `Http` 401 or 403 `Rejected` (G7, TS's free replay; a read, so the 403 re-read is harmless); the token under its own options of the command's budget; `sessions list --all` shares one `WALK_BUDGET` across its pages |

The SDK's `with_timeout` fixes an absolute deadline when the options are built, so the options of each read are
built just before it is sent (choice 73): a one-request read's budget starts after the token, and each `consumption`
application read (two per app) gets its own `SINGLE_REQUEST_BUDGET` however long the overview walk and the apps
before it took.
| `report` sources | §15.17: each source one `with_timeout(300 s).with_retries(0)` budget with the G7 re-read inside it |
| `profiles backup` and restore reads | the SDK read retries (as D175), `WALK_BUDGET` per inventory |
| every write | `writes::attempt` (one attempt, a 401 replayed once, a 403 never; D95); never `with_retries(0)` on a write (it would also drop the 401 refresh) |

**Validation order.** clap → `--output` (§2.4) → `--tenant`'s name format → the command's argument checks
in the order of its section, including the `--debug` refusal of the `refused` commands and the
non-interactive confirmation refusal → the debug log (§2.9) → input files and path checks (`--config`,
`--key-file`, `--output-file`, the restore file; below and in each section) → the bodies built from them
(schema checks) → the tenant (§3.4, §3.7) → the tenant `defaultOutput` where honoured → the credential
check (§3.5) → the restore TSG checks (§18.16) → the client and token → the command's reads, prompts and
writes. Every usage error (exit 2) comes before the tenant is read, makes no request and opens no debug log
(D220; TS checks most of them after the tenant, and `sessions list|get` and every dashboard command after
loading the tenant config, TX§2.5, TR§2.3). File and path errors exit 1 before the tenant, with zero
requests.

**Argument checks** (D220, D213; exit 2; values in messages through `terminal_safe`):
- **List flags** (`api-keys list`, `customer-apps list`): the §7.1 rules and messages
  (`--limit must be a positive integer`, `--offset must be a non-negative integer`,
  `--max must be a non-negative integer`, `--all cannot be combined with --offset`).
- **Dashboard numbers** (TS `integer`, `rd.ts:16-93`): `--interval` (minimum 1), `--limit` (minimum 1),
  `--offset`, `--max`, `--scan-sub-req-id` (minimum 0): `^[0-9]+$` and a safe integer at least the
  minimum, else `<flag> must be a safe integer >= <minimum>` (TS text; leading zeros accepted and the value
  sent as a number, `01` → `1`, TS).
- **Dashboard text** (TS `text`): `--app-id`, `--app-name`, `--session-id`, `--scan-id`: non-blank under
  JavaScript trim, else `<flag> is required` (TS text); the value is sent untrimmed (TS).
- **Units** (TS parse-time check, run first): an exact, case-sensitive member of the command's list, else
  `Unsupported --unit. Supported units: <list joined ', '>. For one week, use --interval 7 --unit days.`
  (TS text). Lists: `applications` `day, days, hour`; `application`, `application-violations` `days`;
  every other dashboard and sessions command `hour, hours, day, days` (TR§3.1).
- **Sent free text** (the query values `<appName>`, `<appId>`, `--updated-by`, `[appName]` and the
  dashboard text flags, and the body field `regenerate --unit`): at most 4,096 bytes and no control
  character (the SDK query bound), else `<flag> must be at most 4096 bytes and contain no control characters`
  (`<flag>` is the option, or `appName`/`appId` for a positional).
- **Names and ids that are sent** (D220): `customer-apps get|delete <appName>` non-blank after trim, else
  `Customer app name must not be empty`; `customer-apps update <appId>`: `Customer app id must not be empty`;
  `--updated-by` (`api-keys delete`, `regenerate`, `customer-apps delete`): `--updated-by must not be empty`
  when given (TS sends `updated_by=`); `consumption ''` (blank after trim):
  `appName must not be empty; omit it to report every dashboard application` (TS reads `''` as "all apps").
- **Path segments** (D213, G29): `api-keys delete <apiKeyName>` and `regenerate <apiKeyId>` must pass the
  SDK segment rule (non-empty, not `.` or `..`, no `\`, no control character, also once percent-decoded;
  `segment::check_segment`), else `Invalid API key name: <value>` / `Invalid API key id: <value>`. A valid
  value is one percent-encoded segment (`a/b c` → `a%2Fb%20c`, TS); the sub-delimiters `( ) ! * '` are sent
  percent-encoded (the SDK encoding, as D202; no separate row: the decoded segment is the same).
- The command-specific checks of §18.5–§18.16.

**Input files** (D221). `--config` (`api-keys create`, `customer-apps update`) is read with the §13.2 input
rules (path as given, symlinks followed, a regular file of at most 1 MiB, read whole, UTF-8, one JSON value
that is an object; the §13.2 messages; no OS error and no content echoed), after the debug log and before the
tenant (TS: after the banner and the tenant, with raw Node errors and V8 messages that quote the content,
TX§2.4). Unknown keys are kept and sent (TS; every M6d request schema is passthrough, choice 10). The body is
the whole object, validated with the SDK request schema in `Mode::Request` (`ApiKeyCreateRequest`,
`CustomerApp`); a failure is the D116 text
`AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for <METHOD> <path> did not match schema` (exit 1; `<path>`
`/v1/mgmt/apikey`, `/v1/mgmt/customerapp`). Bodies are sent with sorted keys (D35); equality with TypeScript
is JSON equality.

**Writes and outcomes** (D95 extended). Every M6d request that is not a GET is a write: one SDK call
(`RawRequest::new`, never re-sent by the SDK; the two G26 raw POSTs included), through `writes::attempt`:
one replay after an `Http` 401 with outcome `Rejected`, never after a 403, a 5xx, a timeout or a transport
error. The error of a failed write is the §6 message, and when the outcome is not a plain rejection one detail
line follows the `HTTP`/`Re-run` lines: `Outcome unknown: the <thing> may have been <done>.` or
`Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but the response could not be read.`, then the hint line of the table.
Nothing is re-sent and nothing is looked up after such a failure. Exit 1. TypeScript re-sends every write up
to 5 times (4 key POSTs after three 502s and 6 after timeouts, captured, TX§2.6). The words
(`writes::Change`):

| Command | `<thing>` / `<done>` | Hint after an unknown or unreadable outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `api-keys create` | `API key` / `created` | `Check 'airs runtime api-keys list' before creating another key; a key whose value was not saved cannot be shown again (regenerate or delete it).` |
| `api-keys regenerate` | `API key` / `regenerated` | `The old key may no longer work; check 'airs runtime api-keys list' and regenerate it again only if needed.` |
| `api-keys delete` | `API key` / `deleted` | `Check it with 'airs runtime api-keys list'.` |
| `customer-apps update` | `customer app` / `updated` | `Check it with 'airs runtime customer-apps get <name>'.` (`<name>` the file's `app_name`) |
| `customer-apps delete` | `customer app` / `deleted` | `Check 'airs runtime customer-apps list'; its API keys may have been deleted too.` |
| restore | `custom topic <name>` / `created`; `security profile <name>` / `created\|updated` | §18.16 |

**Confirmations** (D206). `api-keys regenerate`, `api-keys delete`, `customer-apps update` and
`customer-apps delete` confirm under the §3.10 and §13.2 rules: `--force` skips the prompt; the gate is stdin
**and** stderr being terminals, otherwise the command's usage error (exit 2, before the tenant); the prompt
`? <message> (y/N) ` on stderr; only `y`/`yes` (trimmed, ASCII case-insensitive) confirm; anything else, an
empty line and EOF decline with the info line `  ℹ Aborted` (exit 0, nothing sent, the `--key-file` path not
created); Ctrl-C or SIGTERM print `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` and exit 130/143. Server and argument
text in a prompt goes through `terminal_safe` (and the `[withheld]` rule). The prompt is asked after the reads
its section lists and before the write; no request is open while it waits, and the commands that read nothing
first ask before the token request. `api-keys create` does not confirm (choice 8). Restore confirms per
§18.16. TypeScript never asks (TX§1).

| Command | Prompt | Non-interactive refusal |
|---|---|---|
| `api-keys regenerate <id>` | `Regenerate API key <id>? The current key stops working; the new key is written to <key-file>.` | `refusing to regenerate API key <id> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `api-keys delete <name>` | `Delete API key <name>? Integrations that use it stop working.` | `refusing to delete API key <name> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `customer-apps update <appId>` | `Replace customer app <name> (<appId>) with the settings in <file>?[ It drops <n> field(s) the app has now: <keys>.][ It renames the app to <new name>.]` | `refusing to replace customer app <appId> without --force in non-interactive mode` |
| `customer-apps delete <name>` | `Delete customer app <name> and its API keys?` | `refusing to delete customer app <name> without --force in non-interactive mode` |

`<keys>` lists field names joined `, `, at most 20, then `, and <k> more`.

**Streams, banner, quiet and formats** (D222, D223, D50). stdout carries data only, written once after
success (§2.2), except where a section says it prints and then exits 1 (`consumption` all-apps with a failed
app, `sessions list --all` at a cap). `pretty`, `table` and `json` exist for every command that prints data;
`markdown`, `csv` and `yaml` are invalid formats (D50, exit 2, before the tenant; TS dashboard and sessions
take `yaml`, the others all six). The tenant's `defaultOutput` is honoured by the reads TypeScript resolves it
for (`api-keys list`, `customer-apps list|get|consumption`, `deployment-profiles list`, every `dashboard` and
`sessions` command, `profiles backup|restore`; TX§2.2, TR§2.3) and ignored by the writes and the report
(choice 18).
- **Banner** `"\n  Prisma AIRS — Runtime Configuration\n  Security profile and topic management\n\n"` (§7.6;
  decoration): pretty only, at the top of stdout, only above a data layout of a successful run of the
  `api-keys`, `customer-apps` and `deployment-profiles` commands (TS prints it before the tenant for the reads
  and before every check for the writes, so failing runs leave it on stdout, TX§2.3; D57 extended by D222).
  `dashboard`, `sessions`, `scan-logs`, `report` and `profiles backup|restore` print no banner (TS).
- **Sections** (`"\n  <Title>\n\n"`, bold) are decoration (quiet-suppressed); every data line stays under
  `--quiet`: the dim key-id lines of `api-keys list`, the app-id lines of `customer-apps list`, the
  consumption app title and its id line, `no detector violations in window` (TS drops them, TX§2.3; D222).
- **Outcome lines** (`ui.success` and its hints) go to stderr with their TypeScript text (program name
  `airs`, D73) and colours: success lines and hints quiet-suppressed, warnings and failures never
  (TS: stdout, kept under `--quiet`, D222).
- **Writes** (D223): `api-keys create|regenerate` and `customer-apps update` print their record on stdout in
  the chosen format (pretty: the banner and the detail layout; json: the record; table: `Key │ Value`) and the
  outcome line on stderr (TS ignores `--output` and prints pretty). The deletes leave stdout empty in every
  format (`--output` validated, then ignored, D59).
- Empty lists: pretty `  No <things> found\n` (dim, data) after the banner; table nothing on stdout; json
  `[]\n` (TS: `deployment-profiles list` prints its pretty phrase in every format, json included, TX§7, D222).

**JSON.** Lists print a bare array, gets and writes a bare object, of the TS projection of each section (its
keys in its order; a key whose value the server did not send is omitted, TS parity except where D207 and D209
say otherwise). Objects TypeScript copies raw (`raw`, the dashboard envelopes, backup records) are the SDK
models re-serialised: schema order, unknown keys sorted (D35). Numbers through `js_number`. The `dashboard`
and `sessions` documents (pretty and json) additionally write every C1 control (U+0080–U+009F) as a `\u00XX`
escape, so the JSON text that is their terminal layout carries no raw C1 byte (D212; JSON's own escaping
already covers C0; TS prints C1 raw, TR§3.3).

**Table.** Lists use TypeScript's columns (§18.4–§18.13); every other document is the §2.7 `Key │ Value` table
of its projection keys in projection order, objects and arrays as compact JSON (§2.7 cell rules), an empty cell
for a key the server did not send. Tables and JSON are never coloured.

**Colour** (§2.8, TX§4): section titles bold; ids, dim fields and hints dim; the deployment status green for
exactly `active`, else dim; success lines green, warnings yellow, failures red. Colour per stream (§2.8; TS
follows stdout for both).

**Server text** (D11, D52). Error messages are §6 messages (TS prints the server's `message` text and whole
non-JSON bodies verbatim, control characters included, so a 409 can echo a key, TX§2.6), except the dashboard
and sessions failure line and the report failure line (TS's own fixed lines, below and §18.14). Every server
string in a pretty layout, table cell, outcome line, prompt or message goes through `terminal_safe`; the
customer-app `Data` JSON text keeps its line breaks (`terminal_safe_lines`). Any printed server string (any
field, any format, the dashboard documents included) that contains a value of the invocation's `SecretSet`
(raw, trimmed, form-encoded or base64) is `[withheld]` (as §15.3 and §17.3), and an object member whose name
contains one is dropped with its value (the D47 rule; the `customer-apps update` prompt never names it either,
choice 81).

**Secrets** (D204, D205). The API key value is a credential: it is registered in the invocation's `SecretSet`
the moment it is read from an answer (G26), and it never appears on stdout, stderr, in the debug log, an error,
a summary or the ledger; the `--key-file` file of §18.5 is its only channel. In every M6d read output, an object
member named `api_key` (at any depth: a key list row, a customer-app `raw`) is omitted, and its string value
joins the `SecretSet` before anything is printed (TS json prints `apiKey` whenever a list row carries it,
TX§5.1). `api_key_last8` is printed (choice 5); `auth_code` values are printed only on stdout by the reads whose
records carry them (`deployment-profiles list`, the customer-app `raw`; choice 6), never in an error, a status
line, the debug log or a live summary. Scan content (`prompt`, `response`) reaches only `scan-content`'s stdout
(`--show-content`) or its `--output-file` (§18.13).

**Debug log** (D64 extended). Every M6d command that sends requests has the debug policy `log` (§2.9): status
and headers only, never a body or a URL query (TS logs customer-app bodies, `updated_by` emails, `app_name`,
`session_id` and `scan_id` query values, and key-named redaction only, TX§2.10, TR§2.5). `scan-logs query`
has the policy `none` (it sends nothing). `report`, `profiles backup` and `profiles restore` have the policy
`refused` (D156 extended): `--debug` is a usage error during planning, before any log is opened (texts in
§18.14–§18.16; TS also refuses `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG`, which airs-cli-rs never reads).

**Interruption** (D224; §2.5, §13.2). Reads: `Interrupted; no data was written`. A single write: `nothing was
changed` when it was not sent (a read, the token, the reservation or the prompt before it included), `the
change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` when it was, and `the change was saved` after it
succeeded; the contexts of `api-keys create|regenerate`, `scan-content --output-file`, `report`, backup and
restore are in their sections. A signal at a confirmation prints `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` (exit
130/143). TS exits by the signal with nothing printed (TX§2.9, TR§2.7).

**Exit codes.** 0: success, a declined confirmation, a `--dry-run` with a valid plan, a report whose health is
known (without `--strict`, or with every source complete). 1: tenant, credential, file, HTTP, network, timeout
and decode errors; an incomplete or inconsistent walk; a write whose outcome is unknown or unreadable; an API
key answer without a usable key; `consumption` when any app failed; `sessions list --all` at its item or page
cap; `scan-logs query` (always); a report with `unknown` health or `--strict` with an incomplete source; a
backup or restore that did not complete; the TSG and plan refusals of restore. 2: every argument check of §18
and the non-interactive confirmation refusals. 130 / 143: interrupted.

### 18.4 `api-keys list|ls`

**Requests** (TX§3.2): one page `GET <mgmt>/v1/mgmt/apikeys/tsg/<tsg>?offset=<o>&limit=<l>`; `--all` the SDK
offset walk (`api_keys().list_all`, the `profiles list --all` pattern: §7.2 bounds, `pagination::collect_options`,
D46 for an empty page with a fresh cursor) with the G28 check on `api_key_id` (D219). Status lines: §7.3
(`Showing <n> (more available)` only for `next_offset > 0`, D12; `Showing all <n>`; the D14 line).

**Projection** (D207): `{id, name, last8, createdAt, expiresAt}` in that order; `id` and `name` always (TS's `?? ''`,
choice 41), the others when present: `id` from
`id`, else `api_key_id`; `name` from `name`, else `api_key_name`; `last8` from `api_key_last8`; `createdAt` from
`created_at`, else `creation_ts`; `expiresAt` from `expires_at`, else `expiration` (TS reads only `created_at` /
`expires_at`, which the API never sends, so its `Expires` is always empty). Never `apiKey` (D205).

**Layouts** (TX§5.1): pretty: section `API Keys:`, per key the dim id line `  <id>` (data) and
`    <name>[<dim " key: …" + last8>][<dim " expires: " + expiresAt>]` (U+2026), then `"\n"`; empty
`  No API keys found`. table: `ID │ Name │ Last 8 │ Expires`. json: the bare array.

### 18.5 `api-keys create`, `regenerate <apiKeyId>` and the key file

**Arguments** (before the tenant, in order): `regenerate`: the G29 segment check of `<apiKeyId>`;
`--interval`: decimal digits only, 1 to 2^53 − 1, else `--interval must be a positive integer` (TS `parseInt`:
`1.9` → 1, `-5` sent, `abc` a schema error after the tenant); `--unit`: non-blank after trim, else
`--unit must not be empty`, and the query-value bound (free text otherwise: the service validates it, TS parity,
choice 9); `--updated-by` as §18.3. Both: `--key-file ""` is `--key-file needs a path`;
`--key-file -` is `--key-file - would print the key; give a file path` (as D194). `regenerate` then validates its body
`{rotation_time_interval, rotation_time_unit, updated_by?}` (TS, `updated_by` only when given) with
`ApiKeyRegenerateRequest` (the D116 text naming `POST /v1/mgmt/apikey/regenerate/<id>`, exit 2: an argument-built
body) and last checks the confirmation gate (choice 47).

**Paths** (after the debug log, before the tenant; exit 1): `create`'s `--config` (§18.3); the `--key-file` path
(as given): anything there (`lstat`, a dangling symlink included) is `<path> already exists; choose another --key-file`
(`files::refuse_existing`); a parent that is missing or not a directory is
`Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable` (`files::check_new`), also for a path whose last
component is not a file name (`newdir/`, `a/.`, `a/..`; D226). `create`'s body is the
file validated with `ApiKeyCreateRequest` (the D116 text, exit 1), after both path checks.

**Sequence.** `create`: tenant, credentials, client, the **reservation**, token, `POST <mgmt>/v1/mgmt/apikey`
(one attempt). `regenerate`: tenant, credentials, client, the prompt (unless `--force`), the reservation, token,
`POST <mgmt>/v1/mgmt/apikey/regenerate/<encoded id>` (one attempt). The reservation (`files::Reservation`, the
first half of `publish_new`) creates `.airs-<16 hex>.tmp` in the key file's directory with
`O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`, mode 0600; a failure is the `Cannot write <path>; …` message and
nothing is sent, so a key is never created that cannot be stored. Dropping the reservation removes the temporary.

**The answer** (G26). A 2xx body parsed as one JSON object:
1. A string member `api_key` that is not empty: added to the `SecretSet`, then written to the reservation as
   `<key>\n`, `fsync`ed and linked to the path (`link`; never overwrites), the temporary unlinked, the directory
   `fsync`ed (a failure is the §3.9 warning). Then the rest is validated with `ApiKey::parse(…,
   Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults)`.
2. **Success**: stderr `  ✓ API key created: <id>` (or `regenerated`; TS text, green, quiet-suppressed) and
   `  ✓ Wrote the API key to <path> (mode 0600); it is shown only once.` (success line); stdout the detail below.
3. The key saved but the rest invalid: the §6 text
   `AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION:Response did not match the expected schema` with the one detail line
   `Outcome: the API key was <created|regenerated> and its value was saved in <path>, but the rest of the response could not be read.`
   and no hint (the key is saved; choice 48) (exit 1, stdout empty). A key file that is not durable (its directory
   or, step 6, the key file itself could not be synced) gets its warning on stderr before the error (choice 75).
4. No usable `api_key` (absent, not a string, empty) in an otherwise valid answer (an answer that is also invalid is
   step 5's unreadable outcome): the reservation removed;
   `The service <created|regenerated> API key <id> but returned no key value; nothing was written to <path>. Regenerate the key to obtain a usable value.`
   (exit 1, stdout empty; TS prints `Key  …<last8>`).
5. A body that is not a JSON object: the §18.3 unreadable line and the hint (exit 1); the reservation removed.
6. The link fails because the path appeared meanwhile: the temporary is **kept** and
   `The API key was <created|regenerated>, but <path> now exists; the key is in <temporary path> (mode 0600). Move it before running again.`
   (exit 1). Any other link failure keeps the temporary:
   `The API key was <created|regenerated>, but the key is in <temporary path> (mode 0600) because <path> could not be written. Move it before running again.`
   Either way an interruption from then on reports `the API key was <created|regenerated>; it is in <temporary path>
   (mode 0600)`. The key is never lost to a race. Writing the temporary failing part-way (a full disk) removes it and is
   `The API key was <created|regenerated>, but its value could not be written to <path>; regenerate the key to obtain a usable value.`
   (exit 1; choice 49). A whole write whose `fsync` alone fails (a network or FUSE volume refusing `F_FULLFSYNC`) is
   still linked: the success lines with the warning
   `⚠ <path> was saved, but it could not be synced; the key may not survive a system crash` (choice 67).
7. A failed write (no 2xx): the reservation removed; the §18.3 lines.

**Output** (stdout). pretty: the banner, the section `API Key Detail:` (decoration), then the TS key/value block
`ID`, `Name`, `Key` (`…<last8>`, never the key), `Created` and `Expires` when present (D207), and the Rust row
`Key file` (the path as given), then `"\n"`; json `{id, name, last8, createdAt, expiresAt, keyFile}` (the §18.4
projection plus `keyFile`); table `Key │ Value` of that object. TS prints the full key in the `Key` row on stdout,
also under `--quiet`, and ignores `--output` (TX§5.2, D204, D223).

**Interruption.** Before dispatch: `nothing was changed` (the reservation removed). After dispatch and before
the answer: `the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` (the reservation removed: it holds no
key). From a 2xx answer on, until the key is saved or a temporary kept:
`the API key was <created|regenerated>, but its value was not saved; regenerate the key to obtain a usable value`
(steps 4, 5 and a failed write; choice 72). Once an answer with a key was read, the key file is completed before the signal is acted on (no
cancellation point between decoding and the link), then `Interrupted; the API key was saved in <path>` (also when the
signal arrives while the outcome lines are being written: the record is not printed).

### 18.6 `api-keys delete|rm <apiKeyName> --updated-by <email>`

Sequence: the gate, tenant, credentials, client, the prompt (unless `--force`), token,
`DELETE <mgmt>/v1/mgmt/apikey/delete/<encoded name>?updated_by=<email>` (one attempt). Any 2xx JSON answer (a
string, `{message}`, `{}`; G35) is success: stderr `  ✓ API key <name> deleted.` (`<name>` the argument; D208:
TS prints the server's `message`, `✓ undefined` for `{}`). The service's message is never printed. No
verification read (there is no single-key read; choice 12). stdout stays empty in every format.

§18.4 with the G28 check on `customer_appId`; `get`: `GET <mgmt>/v1/mgmt/customerapp?app_name=<name>` (a 404 is

`customer_appId` (TS reads only the first two, which the API never sends); `name` from `app_name`, else `name`,
else `''` (TS); `description` from `description` (no schema has it; kept for TS parity); `raw` the wire record
re-serialised (D35), without `api_key` members (D205), `api_keys_dp_info` with its `auth_code` values kept
(choice 6).

present) and `    <name>[<dim " — " + description cut to 80 UTF-16 units>]` (the D54 helper, no ellipsis), then

`Data` (the `JSON.stringify(raw, null, 2)` text through `terminal_safe_lines`, cut at 500 UTF-16 units without

`  … (cut at 500 characters; use --output json for the whole record)` (D207; TS cuts mid-string with no sign),
then `"\n"`. table `Key │ Value` of `id, name, description, raw`. json the object.

### 18.9 `customer-apps consumption [appName] [--time-interval 7|30|60]`

**Arguments** (before the tenant): `--time-interval`: decimal digits only, value 7, 30 or 60, else
`--time-interval must be 7, 30, or 60 (the API rejects other values)` (TS text; TS `parseInt` takes `7.5` and
`60abc`, after the tenant); `[appName]` as §18.3.

**The application list** (D211). One walk of
`GET <dash>/v1/mgmt/dashboard/v2/apps/applicationsoverview?time_interval=<n>&time_unit=days&limit=100&offset=<o>`
(`x-tsg-id`; **the `--time-interval` window**: TS always looks up over the default 30 days, so an app active only
in the last 60 days is "not found" with `--time-interval 60`) through the shared page loop (`src/walk.rs`: next
offset = offset + rows; a page whose `pagination.total_items` is a safe integer continues while
`next < total_items`, so a capped short page is not the end; a page without a total ends at a short page; the D37
error at an empty page before the total and at a repeated `[id, name]`; the §7.2 bounds, D40). Items whose `id` or
`name` is not a string are skipped (TS), with the warning `  ⚠ <n> dashboard application(s) without an id or name were skipped`
(stderr, never suppressed). TS stops at the first short page (a false not-found, TX§6.5).

**Single app** (`appName` given). The buckets whose `name` equals `appName` exactly: none →
`Dashboard application not found: "<name>". Available (as shown in SCM AI Applications view): "<n1>", …` (TS text,
the first five names and `, ... (<N> total)`, every name through `terminal_safe` and the `[withheld]` rule);
two or more with different ids → `Dashboard application name "<name>" matches <k> applications with different ids; use 'airs runtime dashboard application --app-id <id> --app-name <name>' for one of them`
(exit 1; TS takes the first); otherwise that bucket. Then, in this order (TS: in parallel),
`GET <dash>/…/apps/application?appid=<id>&appname=<name>&time_interval=<n>&time_unit=days` and
`GET <dash>/…/apps/applicationviolationbreakdown?…` (the same query).

**All apps** (no `appName`; D210). The one overview walk, then for each bucket in overview order its two reads (TS
walks the overview again per app: 1 + 3N requests). An app whose read fails prints
`  ✗ [<name>] <§6 message first line>[ (HTTP <s>)]` on stderr (red, never suppressed; TS text shape) and the run
continues; the command prints the apps that succeeded and **exits 1** when any failed (TS exits 0). An empty
overview (no bucket): pretty `  No dashboard applications found`, json `[]`, table nothing. An overview whose every
app failed is not empty: pretty prints the banner alone (choice 74), json `[]`, table nothing, exit 1.

**Projection** (D209): per app `{appId, appName, cloud, source, monitoringSince, profiles, tokens{dailyAverage,
dailyAverageScale, monthlyTotal, monthlyTotalScale}, sessions{total, violating}, detectors[{type, critical, high,
medium, low, total}], totalViolating}` (TS `mg.ts:476-503`) with only what the server sent: TS's `?? 0` counts,
`type ?? 'unknown'` and `profiles ?? []` are not invented (an absent value stays absent).

**Layouts** (TX§6.5). pretty, per app: the title `"\n  <bold name>\n  <dim (appId)>\n\n"` (data, so `--quiet` keeps
it), the metadata pairs `Monitoring since`, `Source`, `Cloud`, `Profiles` (joined `, `) when present, sections
`Token consumption:` (`Daily avg`, `Monthly total`: `<n><scale>` or `-`), `Sessions:` (`Total`, `Violating`: the
count or `-`; TS `0`), `Detectors (<totalViolating or ?> violating, <firing>/<all> firing):` and the TS firing table
(` Detector │ Total │ Severity`, rows with `total > 0`, severity `c=<n> h=<n> m=<n> l=<n>` with `?` for an absent
count) or `  no detector violations in window` (dim, data). json: **one** bare array for the run (TS: one array per
app, several documents) of one row per detector with the TS keys `app_name, app_id, monitoring_since, daily_avg,
monthly_total, sessions_total, sessions_violating, detector, critical, high, medium, low, total`; an absent value is

prints nothing for it, so it vanishes). table: the same rows under TS's labels `App, AppId, MonitoringSince,
