### 18.20 Choices decided

The user delegated every decision; each choice below takes the safest option that keeps the command useful (the rejected
alternative in each item).
1. `without_response_defaults()` on every M6d call through one helper (G27). Rejected: passing it only on the profile and
   topic calls whose schemas carry a default (easy to miss when a command grows).
2. One OAuth identity per invocation: the dashboard and DLP origins are admitted into the management client's policy only
   for the commands that need them (`build_for`). Rejected: a separate `DlpClients` for restore (a second token request)
   and widening every management command's destination policy.
3. The API key channel is a required `--key-file <new path>` on `create` and `regenerate`: 0600, never overwritten,
   checked before the tenant, reserved before the request, the temporary kept if the final link loses a race; the key is
   never printed. Rejected: stdout (TS: terminals and CI logs), stdout as the fallback of an optional `--key-file` (a
   forgotten flag prints the credential), an optional `--key-file` with the key withheld otherwise (a forgotten flag
   destroys a shown-once key), and a `--show-key` stdout opt-in (refused for consistency with D194's `--url-file -`).
4. `api_key` members are omitted from every read, at any depth, and their values join the `SecretSet`. Rejected:
   `[withheld]` placeholders (they suggest the field is normally present) and checking only the top level of key rows.
5. `api_key_last8` stays visible. It is the service's designed fingerprint (8 of about 48 characters, not a recoverable
   part of the key), and keys could otherwise be told apart only by name. Rejected: withholding it.
6. Auth codes are printed where TS prints them (deployment profiles, the customer-app `raw`), on stdout only. An auth code
   is the entitlement code `api-keys create --config` requires, not a bearer credential (it does nothing without the
   tenant's OAuth credentials); the report keeps only counts, as TS. Rejected: withholding them (the CLI could no longer
   feed `create`) and a `--show-auth-codes` flag (no use case).
7. The G26 raw `create`/`regenerate` POSTs, so a 2xx whose rest fails the schema still saves the key. Rejected: the typed
   calls (a missing `auth_code` in the answer loses a created key's only copy, as TS does).
8. Confirmations for `api-keys regenerate` and `delete` and `customer-apps update` and `delete` (D206); `create` does not
   confirm. Rejected: confirming `create` (its purpose; it runs in CI) and confirming only the deletes (`regenerate`
   revokes the key in use and `update` replaces the whole record).
9. `regenerate --unit` stays free text (non-blank, the query bound); the service validates it. Rejected: a closed
   `hours|days|months` vocabulary (no evidence of the service's full vocabulary; a wrong unit is rejected by the service
   and rotates nothing).
10. `--config` files keep and send unknown keys (TS; every request schema is passthrough). Rejected: refusing them (could
    block API fields the SDK schema does not model).
11. `customer-apps update` stays a full replacement; when it prompts it reads the current record through the list walk
    (there is no read by id, G30) to name the fields the file drops and a rename; with `--force` it sends TS's single PUT.
    Rejected: a read-modify-write overlay (it changes TS's documented replace semantics and could copy values the user
    did not name) and a read in every mode (an extra walk with nothing to show).
12. Deletes are not verified (there is no single-key read; an app re-read by name proves little), and their
    acknowledgements are fixed texts from the argument (D208). Rejected: a list walk after every delete, and printing the
    server's message (it can be anything).
13. Dashboard and sessions failures print TS's generic line verbatim (it is already secret-safe and its spec pins it);
    tenant, store and credential errors keep their §3 messages. Rejected: §6 messages for these commands (parity loss
    without a safety gain) and the generic line for tenant errors (the Rust store has its own precise messages).
14. `sessions list --all` keeps TS's stricter page checks and its exit-1 partial results at `--max` and at 100 pages,
    through `walk_with`. Rejected: plain `walk.rs` semantics (`--max` is a success there and the echo checks are missing).
15. `sessions get|transaction` print `attributes.user_id`/`user_ip` and passthrough fields as TS (explicit reads of the
    user's own tenant); they never reach a live summary. Rejected: withholding them (the commands exist to show them).
16. `scan-content --output-file` writes the JSON text in every format and validates, then ignores `--output`; its path
    and parent are checked before the tenant. Rejected: a table in a file, and a usage error for `--output table` (the
    file format is fixed, so the flag cannot mislead).
17. Historical runtime report ordering is superseded by §18.14/D340. `consumption` keeps its two per-app reads sequentially, in TS order. Rejected: TS's
    concurrent `Promise.all` (a nondeterministic request order in tests for no observable gain; each read evaluates its
    own server window either way).
18. The tenant `defaultOutput` is honoured by the reads and transfer commands TS resolves it for, ignored by the writes and
    the report. Rejected: honouring it everywhere (a json default would change write output unasked) and nowhere (breaks
    TS's documented default for reads).
19. The consumption lookup uses the `--time-interval` window. Rejected: TS's fixed 30-day lookup (a false not-found for an
    app active only within 60 days) and a 60-day lookup always (requests TS never sends, for a window the user did not
    ask for).
20. The consumption lookup refuses a name shared by buckets with different ids and points to `dashboard application
    --app-id`. Rejected: TS's first match (the wrong app's data) and a new `--app-id` option on `consumption` (not in TS;
    the dashboard command already takes it).
21. TypeScript profile backups are refused by restore with a fixed message (MILESTONES: no compatibility with TS-made
    files; D176): they carry the fabricated `examples: []`, zod's reordering and no tenant name. Rejected: importing TS
    envelopes (a second, looser format, and YAML).
22. The backup format `airs-cli-rs.runtime-profiles` v1 has no `complete` key: a backup is complete or not written, as TS.
    Rejected: DLP's `complete`/`failed` rows (no per-resource partial read exists here).
23. Restore keeps `--on-conflict update` (a PUT of the destination profile) inside the confirmation count, one attempt,
    with TS's `unchanged` re-check just before the PUT. Rejected: dropping `update` (TS's documented migration path).
24. `sameTopic` treats an absent `examples` as `[]` when comparing, so a topic without examples is reused, never refused.
    Rejected: strict absence-versus-`[]` inequality (a spurious `Destination topic differs` for identical topics) and
    storing `[]` in the backup (a fabricated value).
25. Restore's non-interactive refusal comes before the file and the tenant (D167 pattern), so a non-interactive
    `verify`-only run also needs `--force --expect-tsg`. Rejected: TS's late refusal after the plan's reads.
26. Restore's DLP catalog uses the M6b inventory sweep (`dlp::backup::Sweep`) and its messages. Rejected: TS's looser
    loop (a second, weaker inventory walk over the same API).
27. The restore TSG mismatch and the `--expect-tsg` mismatch exit 1 after the tenant (the Rust exit-code contract: usage
    errors come before the tenant). Rejected: TS's exit 2 after reading the tenant.
28. The restore keeps TS's `Error: <message>` block in the data and the stderr line, as the DLP restore does. Rejected:
    removing the block from stdout (the json and table consumers would lose the reason).
29. The report checks the destination parent before the tenant (D214), unlike the red team report. Rejected: TS's
    eight-request run that then fails to write.
30. Reads keep the G7 re-read after a 401 or 403 where TS reads with `numRetries: 0` (dashboard, sessions, the report);
    the "403 never" rule is for writes. Rejected: no re-read after a 403 on reads (a GET duplicates nothing; it would
    only lose TS's free replay).
31. The dashboard JSON escapes C1 controls as `\u00XX` (lossless) in pretty and json. Rejected: TS's raw C1 (a terminal
    can read U+009B as CSI) and `terminal_safe` replacement in JSON (it changes the data). `Cf` characters stay as they
    are in JSON, as in every other command (only the report's labels strip them, TS).
32. Historical stub choice superseded by §18.11/D338. The frozen TypeScript `scan-logs query` stub reads the tenant selection, sends nothing and names `airs` in its hint
    (D73). Rejected: implementing the broken legacy query (TS removed it on purpose) and keeping `airs-cli` (the hint
    would name a program that is not running).
33. `consumption ''` and the other empty names and ids that are sent are usage errors. Rejected: TS's empty query values
    (`app_name=`), which run the all-apps loop or ask the service to resolve an empty name.
34. Consumption skips buckets without a string id or name, as TS, but says how many it skipped. Rejected: a silent skip
    (an app could vanish from all-apps output) and failing the run (one bad bucket would hide every other app).
35. The live tier never runs the TypeScript restore: the Rust reader refuses TS files (choice 21), so the scope's
    condition for it does not hold, and the TS restore replays a POST after a 403 (D217). Rejected: running it on its own
    file (it is the TS write path the port replaces, and its replays could create duplicates the ledger cannot predict).
36. The live write flow creates one topic and one profile that references it, and restores them without `--name-prefix`
    after deleting the originals, so every resource keeps the existing write flow's `-rs` names that the sweeper already
    covers (at most 4 of the 10 allowed). Rejected: prefixed restores (names that escape the sweeper), a second profile
    (it would need a name shape the sweeper and the other flows do not reserve), and a profile without a topic (the topic
    half of the planner would go untested live).
37. Live `scan-content` runs on both CLIs only with `--output-file` into each sandbox (0600, compared in memory, removed);
    `--show-content` never runs live. Rejected: `--show-content` (tenant prompts in captured stdout) and skipping the
    command (its file rules would go unchecked live).
38. Live `api-keys list` compares the TypeScript `--output table` (which cannot show a key) with the Rust table, and checks
    the Rust json for the withheld key; TS json never runs. Rejected: TS json (it prints `apiKey` if the service sends one)
    and Rust only (no comparison).
39. The offset-cursor lists (`api-keys`, `customer-apps`) walk with the SDK's `list_all`, as `runtime profiles list --all`
    does (repeated cursors and empty pages with a fresh cursor already fail, D46), plus the CLI's repeated-row check (G28);
    the skip/limit walks with a total (the consumption lookup, `sessions list --all`) use `src/walk.rs`; the report and
    transfer inventories keep TS's own loops and notes (as §15.17). Rejected: moving the offset-cursor lists onto
    `src/walk.rs` (a second implementation of a walk the SDK already checks) and the SDK walks without the row check.
40. Interrupting `api-keys create|regenerate` after the answer was read completes the key file before the signal is acted
    on. Rejected: cancelling between the answer and the link (the only copy of the key would be lost).
41. The `api-keys` projection keeps TS's `id` and `name` (`?? ''`) on every row, so a key without a name is `"name": ""` in
    json (the TS key consumers read); `last8`, `createdAt` and `expiresAt` appear only when sent (resolved while building
    step 1). Rejected: omitting an absent name (a json shape TS never prints).
42. `sessions list --all` runs its page checks before any row of a page is taken (the echo of `skip` and `limit` as the
    page arrives, the total, the row bound, the overlap and `offset > total` in `walk_with`'s per-page check), so an
    overlapping page fails even when `--max` falls inside it, as in TS; `--max 0` keeps the walk's safety bound of
    1,000,000 items (D40). Rejected: checking the overlap row by row with the cap (a partial list where TS fails), and no
    item bound (TS has none, but every other walk is bounded).
43. A dashboard or sessions token failure is the dashboard line, with ` (HTTP <s>)` when the token answer had a status of
    400–599 (TS: its error's `statusCode`); the token is fetched under options of the command's budget and retries
    (the walk budget for `sessions list --all`), built for it alone (choice 73), with no re-read (G7 is for reads of the
    dashboard). Rejected: the §6 token message (the
    dashboard commands print no SDK text, choice 13).
44. `consumption` fetches its token and walks the overview under one walk budget, and gives each per-app read (each of
    the two GETs of an app) its own single-request budget, from when it is sent, with the SDK read retries (D10); an all-apps failure line is the first line of the §6 message
    plus ` (HTTP <s>)` when the failure has a status. Rejected: one budget for the whole all-apps loop (a slow tenant would
    fail apps that never ran).
45. The consumption overview's repeated-row key (D37) is the compact JSON of `[id, name]` of the buckets that have both;
    an item without a string id or name is not key-checked: it is skipped and counted (choice 34). Rejected: keying the
    skipped items too (a service sending several `{id: null}` items would fail the lookup for a valid app).
46. D205 and the `[withheld]` rule apply to every M6d read document, the dashboard and sessions envelopes and the two
    consumption answers included; every `api_key` member of a listing is removed and registered before any string of the
    listing is checked, so a key echoed by another row is withheld too. Rejected: per-row stripping (a later row's key could
    already have been printed by an earlier one).
47. `regenerate`'s checks run in the order segment, `--interval`, `--unit`, `--updated-by`, `--key-file` value, body
    schema, then the non-interactive confirmation gate (resolved while building step 2), so every value error is reported
    before a refusal that only `--force` would lift. Rejected: the gate before `--key-file` (a non-interactive run would
    learn about a bad key-file value only after adding `--force`).
48. A G26 answer whose key was saved but whose other fields fail the schema is the §6 validation text with the single
    `Outcome: … its value was saved in <path> …` detail and no hint (the key is not lost, so the create hint's "a key
    whose value was not saved cannot be shown again" would mislead). Rejected: the unreadable line plus the hint.
49. When writing or syncing the reserved temporary fails after the key arrived (a full disk), the temporary is removed
    and the error says the key was created or regenerated but not written, and to regenerate it. Rejected: keeping a
    temporary that may hold a truncated key (a wrong credential that looks saved).
50. The two raw key POSTs carry `custom.request` in the `--debug` log (G26 amended: `RawRequest::named` is crate-private
    in scm-sdk 0.1.1). Rejected: the typed `api_keys().create|regenerate` to get the SDK's operation names (a schema
    mismatch would lose a shown-once key, choice 7) and patching the SDK (the pin is fixed).
51. The `update` prompt counts a member of the current record as dropped only when its value is not `null`, and treats
    keys ending in `_ts` or `_at` as service timestamps; the names follow the record's order. Rejected: listing `null`
    members (nothing is lost) and a fixed timestamp list (the API adds `*_ts` members over time).
52. The runtime report reads timestamps with the §15.17 `Date.parse` approximation plus the date-only form as UTC midnight
    (which `Date.parse` accepts); a timestamp without a zone is not a valid time (TS reads it in the host's zone).
    Rejected: the approximation alone (a date-only `last_modified_ts` would show `Unknown` where TS shows a time) and
    local-time parsing (a report that depends on the host's zone).
53. Where TypeScript's report analysis would throw on an odd record (a non-string label, a missing breakdown, a non-array
    collection inside a record), the port reads the value as absent. Rejected: failing the whole report with the generic
    line (one malformed record would hide six good sources).
54. `api-keys create` checks the `--config` file, then the `--key-file` path, then the body schema, all before the
    tenant; the reservation is made after the client is built and before the token, so a destination that cannot be
    written sends nothing. Rejected: reserving before the tenant (a temporary left in the directory when the tenant
    turns out to be broken).
55. The `customer-apps update` prompt's list walk runs after the token under its own walk budget and maps an
    interruption to `nothing was changed`; the PUT is sent only after the answer. Rejected: one budget for the walk and
    the write (a slow walk would leave the write no time).
56. The runtime report's `--output` help line is the fixed `Refused by this command: the report is written as HTML (omit
    --output)` (format policy `HtmlReport`). Rejected: reusing the red team `Report` policy text (it describes job
    reports that `runtime report` does not have).
57. An absent destination collection read after the first restore write says `Destination inventory of <security
    profiles|custom topics> was not returned; verify destination state before retrying` (resolved while building step
    3); before any write it keeps D218's `…; nothing was changed`. Rejected: the planning text in every phase (it would
    say nothing changed after a topic was created).
58. The Rust-only result rows name a resource `topic` or `profile` and an action `create` or `update`: json
    `outcomeUnknown {kind, name, action}` and `notAttempted [{kind, name}]`, pretty and table `Possibly written (outcome
    unknown)` (`Resource │ Name │ Action`) and `Not attempted` (`Resource │ Name`). Rejected: the DLP restore's plural
    stage keys (a runtime restore has two kinds, both singular in its messages).
59. `notAttempted` lists every planned topic and profile after the item that stopped the run, all of them when the
    recheck stopped it, `skip` rows included, as the DLP restore does (§16.11). Rejected: dropping the `skip` rows (a
    second rule for the same Rust-only list).
60. The DLP-mapping refusal names `airs` in its hint (`Inspect destination resources with airs runtime dlp
    profiles list --all --output json`, D73 extended). Rejected: TS's `airs-cli` (a program that is not running).
61. The backup selector is matched exactly, untrimmed, against `profile_id` or `profile_name` (TS); only a selector that
    is blank after trim is a usage error. Rejected: trimming the selector (a name with surrounding spaces could not be
    selected).
62. `--all` with any selector, the empty string included, is `Choose either a profile selector or --all`. Rejected: TS's
    falsy-string rule (`--all ''` accepted and read as "all").
63. Restore reads the DLP catalog through `ManagementClients::dlp`, the `dlpEndpoint` client built only for
    `Planes { dlp: true }` (the 32 MiB bound, G31), with the M6b sweep's query (`page`, `size=100`, `sort=name,asc`).
    Rejected: TS's unsorted `page,size` loop (a second inventory walk over the same API, choice 26).
64. A profile create or update whose answer was read but whose read-back inventory then fails or does not verify keeps
    its `created`/`updated` row and stops with TS's text (`API request failed (HTTP <s>); …`, `Restored profile did not
    verify: <name>`); it is not `outcomeUnknown` (the write's outcome is known). Rejected: an outcome-unknown row for a
    write whose answer was read.
65. The live runtime reads compare the dashboard and sessions documents by shape (the keys where both sides have a
    value, the JSON types, the first array item), the report by its section ids, evidence source names and statuses
    (D214 tolerated), the `api-keys list` table cell by cell except `Expires` (D207), and consumption with the D209
    tolerance. Rejected: byte comparison (the rolling windows move between the two runs).
66. The live transfer flow's panic self-test injects its panic through a test-only `TransferHooks::after_creates`; a real
    run passes none. Rejected: a panic switch read from an environment variable (a live run could then be told to
    panic).
67. A key file whose bytes were written whole but whose `fsync` alone failed (network and FUSE volumes can refuse
    `F_FULLFSYNC`) is still linked into place, with the success lines and the warning
    `⚠ <path> was saved, but it could not be synced; the key may not survive a system crash`
    (`LinkError::NotSynced`, `Reservation::link_unsynced`, `Published::FileNotSynced`); only a write that fails part-way
    removes the temporary (choice 49). Reports and backups (`files::publish_new`) keep treating a failed `fsync` as
    `Cannot write <path>; …` (their content can be produced again). Rejected: removing the temporary on any sync failure
    (it threw away a shown-once key after the service had created or rotated it) and keeping the temporary with an error
    (a complete key the user would still have to move by hand).
68. A topic the restore created whose answer does not verify (`topic_id`, `topic_name`, an integer `revision`,
    `sameTopic`) keeps its `created` row (the answer's `topic_id` when not empty) before the run stops with TS's
    `Topic response did not verify: <name>`, as a created profile's row does (choice 64); it is not `outcomeUnknown` (the
    create's outcome is known). Rejected: TS's empty result (nothing says the topic exists) and an outcome-unknown row for
    a write whose answer was read.
69. In the live profile-transfer flow every restore that is not a dry run (the restore and the `--on-conflict verify`
    re-run) is journalled as a write for both copies, T and P, whatever the earlier dry run planned, because each run
    replans on its own (`(None, _) => Action::Create` in every conflict mode): a budget reservation and a `pending` line
    for each copy first, then the outcome from the run's json rows (`created` → `ok` with the row's UUID or the single id
    listed afterwards, else `unknown`; `reused`/`verified`/`skipped` → `skipped`; `notAttempted`, or a run that exited
    having written nothing → `failed`; anything else `unknown`). The verify re-run runs only after its own
    `--on-conflict verify --dry-run` planned nothing but `verify` and `reuse`. The dry run before the restore accepts a
    topic `create` when the topic's delete outcome was unknown (it may have been applied). `PLANNED_TRANSFER_CREATES`
    counts the six reservations; at most four resources are created. Rejected: pending lines only for what the dry run
    planned (a replanned create would have no ledger line and no reservation), keeping the verify check as a dry run only
    (the verify execution path would go untested live), and `failed` for a created row without a UUID (the copy exists).
70. The live reads run the TypeScript `customer-apps list` only with `--output table` (columns `ID`, `Name`,
    `Description`; never `raw`) and never compare the TypeScript `customer-apps get` (its pretty `Data`, table and json
    all print `raw`, where an `api_keys_dp_info[].api_key` occurs, D205); the Rust list and get run with `--output json`
    and must hold no `apiKey`/`api_key` member. The tables compare cell by cell, the TS `ID` cell allowed empty (D207).
    Only after a failed Rust get does the TS get run, once, `--output table`, with its stdout sent to `/dev/null`
    (`RunPlace::discard_stdout`; the harness never holds it): its exit code and whether its stderr names HTTP 403
    decide between the agreeing `unavailable: HTTP 403 on both CLIs` row and the failure. Rejected: the TS json
    comparison with its `api_key` members stripped afterwards (the key values still reach the harness's buffers),
    skipping the TS list too (no comparison at all), capturing the TS get's stdout and dropping it (the key would
    reach the buffers), and a Rust-only 403 as a notice (a 403 TypeScript is not given is a real difference).
71. A new-file destination whose last component is not a file name (a trailing `/`, `.` or `..`, `files::names_a_file`)
    is refused before the tenant with the existing `Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable`
    (the report: its failure line), in `files::refuse_existing` (so also `check_new`) and the two report checks (D226).
    Rejected: TS's `resolve()` normalisation (`out.json/` silently written as `out.json`: a path the user did not type,
    and for `newdir/` a file where a directory was meant) and a new message (the existing one already names the path).
72. From a 2xx key answer on, the interruption context is
    `the API key was <created|regenerated>, but its value was not saved; regenerate the key to obtain a usable value`
    until the key file is linked or a temporary kept (then their contexts), set before the answer is read, so a signal
    that arrives while a no-key answer, an unreadable answer or a failed write is being reported never prints
    `nothing was changed`. Rejected: keeping the plan's `nothing was changed` fallback (false once the key was created or
    the old key revoked) and `the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` (the outcome is known).
73. The request options of every M6d read are built just before the read is sent (`runtime::options` or
    `runtime::request_options` per GET; a walk's options before its token), because scm-sdk 0.1.1's
    `RequestOptions::with_timeout` fixes an absolute deadline. Rejected: building them when the command starts (the
    token, the overview walk and the earlier apps then ate a later read's budget: after 60 s every remaining
    `consumption` app failed and the run exited 1) and one options value per app (its second read got what the first
    left).
74. `consumption`'s empty-overview phrase follows the overview (no bucket after the walk), not the apps that were read:
    when the overview has apps and every read fails, pretty prints the banner alone, stderr names each app and the run
    exits 1. Rejected: the phrase whenever no app was printed (it would say no application exists while stderr lists
    each one failing).
75. A key file that was linked but is not durable (`Published::FileNotSynced`, choice 67, or
    `Published::DirectoryNotSynced`, §3.9) keeps its warning when the rest of the answer then fails its schema (§18.5
    step 3): `runtime::keys::save_answer` returns the durability with the step-3 error (`Saved::record` is the
    `Result`), and `runtime_keys::finish` prints the warning before the
    `AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION` error block (`keys::durability_warning` is the one text of both paths). Rejected:
    printing the warning only on the success path (a key that may not survive a crash was reported only as saved).
76. The write machinery shared by every feature (the D81 gate and prompt, the one-attempt send and its interruption
    `Contexts`, `config_object`, `body`) lives in `commands/write_common.rs`; `redteam_write`, `dlp_write`,
    `modelsec_write` and `runtime_write` are thin wrappers, and every M6d read and write attempt builds its options with
    `runtime::request_options` (no second builder). The stages the two HTML environment reports share (destination
    checks, `SourceBudget`, `NO_REPORT`, publishing, the incomplete line, the exit code and `GENERATION_FAILED`) live in
    `commands/report_command.rs`; each report keeps its reader, collector and collection status line, and `ParentCheck`
    keeps the red team report's parent check at the write (choice 29). No observable change. Rejected: the M6d writes
    importing the red team module, and two copies of the report pipeline (D226 had to be applied twice).
77. The transfer commands load the tenant and check its credentials (`Invocation::runtime_tenant`) before any client is
    built, and restore runs its two tenant checks (the file's `tsgId`, `--expect-tsg`) between that and
    `connect_tenant`, as §18.3 and §18.16 order them: a destination whose `dlpEndpoint` (or `mgmtEndpoint`,
    `mgmtTokenEndpoint`) is inadmissible and whose TSG does not match reports the TSG refusal, and the D48 refusal only
    once the TSG checks pass. Rejected: building the client in the same step as loading the tenant (the D48 error then
    hid the TSG refusal; no request was sent either way).
78. Which restore failures keep their own text in `result.error` (TS: the message matches
    `^(Destination|Topic response|Missing planned|Restored profile|Inventory|DLP inventory)`, else the generic
    `Restore stopped; …`) is typed where the rule refuses: `plan::Refusal::Stated` or `Refusal::Withheld` (the inventory
    walk, `latestProfiles`, `assertTenant`, the topic and DLP reference walks, `mappedPolicy`; the DLP catalog sweep's
    messages are stated); the executor's own messages are its own texts. TS's pattern is the oracle of a unit test over
    every refusal kind, not a classifier at run time. No observable change. Rejected: matching message prefixes at run
    time (a reworded or new message silently became the generic stop).
79. `api-keys list` and `customer-apps list` share one walk-or-page reader, `runtime::list::OffsetList`: each command
    supplies only its page call, its `list_all` call, the row identity of the G28 check and its projection. The backup
    reader's duplicate profile-name and topic-key checks use hash sets (linear in files of up to 10,000 entries each).
    No observable change. Rejected: two copies of the token, budget, walk, status and sanitising sequence.
80. Helpers that belong to no feature live in feature-neutral modules and the old homes re-export them: the segment rule
    in `segment.rs` (every caller imports it from there; `redteam` keeps no re-export), the SDK-model and record conversions and the JSON paths in `json.rs`, the TypeScript YAML sniffer
    and `parent_dir` in `files.rs`, `--max-pages` in `pagination.rs`. The runtime modules import no red team code; their
    DLP imports are the DLP catalog itself (the `Sweep`, its page size and sort, `retired_profile`; choice 26). No
    observable change. Rejected: the runtime commands reaching into the red team and DLP modules for generic code.
81. A runtime read document's object member whose name carries a `SecretSet` value (exact containment,
    `carried_by`, as for the values) is dropped with its value (`runtime::views::withhold`; `secrets::withhold` from 0.11), and the
    `customer-apps update` prompt leaves such a name out of the fields it says a replacement drops (the current
    record is withheld first; the filter repeats the check). Consistent with D47's `result` entries and with the
    `api_key` members of D205, which are dropped too. Rejected: renaming the member to `[withheld]` with a suffix to
    keep the names unique (an invented name that looks like data and can collide with a real one) and keeping the
    value (a value filed under a secret is tied to it).

## 19. M6e Gateway (0.10)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-gateway.md` (cited as **GW§n**: every
`aigateway` command, its shared runners, structured input, telemetry, the inventory groups, admin
guardrails, inference and the report's command surface), `docs/research/ts-gateway-report.md` (cited as
**GR§n**: the report collector, renderer and the doctor check) and `docs/research/rs-sdk-gateway.md`
(cited as **GK§n**). This section overrides them where they differ; their provisional row numbers
(GW§"Open questions", GK§14) and gap numbers (GW1–GW13) are not binding. TypeScript's `aigateway` is
`gateway` here, with every subcommand, option and alias, and with no `aigateway` alias (MILESTONES
renames; D227). Every difference from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row (D227–D254; D1, D11, D19, D35, D49,
D50, D52, D64, D73, D155, D156, D178, D214 and D226 extended). The byte captures of the TypeScript layouts
are in GW§1–§9 and GR§1–§14; "the TS layout" below means those bytes, with the changes this section lists.

**SDK.** The pin is scm-sdk `=0.2.2` (adopted by 0.9.1, §15.23) with the `gateway` feature. The research
(GK§0, GK§4) measured scm-sdk 0.1.1, on which this section was first built; 0.10 was then merged onto 0.9.1 and
re-measured on 0.2.2 (2026-10-19, the published `~/.cargo/registry/src/*/scm-sdk-0.2.2` against 0.1.1, and the SDK
repository's `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/ACCESS_POLICIES.md`). scm-sdk 0.2.2 has an operation for every command of this
section, with the TypeScript paths, methods, query names and request and response schemas. `Cargo.toml` adds
`"gateway"` to the `scm` features (`gateway = ["models", "iam"]`, and `iam` pulls `dep:getrandom`); `getrandom
0.4.3` is already locked, so the lock file gains only the `scm-sdk → getrandom` edge and no crate (measured: the
`Cargo.lock` diff against the 0.9.1 release is exactly that edge). `realtime` and `ws-transport` are not enabled (no
command opens the realtime socket). The walk of every response and request schema the commands use finds no
`ZodDefault` (GK§3.4), so G10 changes nothing today; **every gateway SDK call still passes
`RequestOptions::…without_response_defaults()`** through one options helper (`gateway::options`, choice 2).
**What 0.2.x changes for this section** (measured; choice 135):
- The gateway sources are byte-identical to 0.1.1 but for `src/airs/gateway/mod.rs`, which only adds the
  access-policy module (0.2.1, below). Every schema node reachable from a gateway root of `schema_graph.json`
  (7,600 nodes) is identical in both versions, so the request schemas, their refinements and strictness (G49) and
  the response structures are unchanged.
- The relaxed response formats (D306): from 0.2.2 both response modes ignore the `uuid`, `rfc3339`, `datetime`,
  `date`, `duration`, `email`, `url` and `regex` string checks. No gateway response schema declares one: the only
  gateway nodes with such checks are reached from request, query and option schemas (the window and chart
  filters, the workspace, provider, API-key, integration, MCP, deployment and plugin request bodies, and the
  standalone routing-configuration schemas no command decodes), and request validation keeps every format check.
  So no gateway read or write answer changes and no test expectation moves; D306 needs no gateway extension.
- The user agent is `PAN-AIRS/0.2.2-rust-sdk` on every gateway request in 0.10 and 0.11, and
  `PAN-AIRS/0.2.3-rust-sdk` in 1.0 (§15.24 point 8) and `PAN-AIRS/0.2.4-rust-sdk` from 8.0 (§15.25; the §2.9 header list; `tests/gateway_inventory.rs` expects it).
- G36–G49 are unchanged by 0.2.2 (each re-checked below); G49 is settled on 0.2.2.
- 0.2.1 adds the experimental Portkey access-policy API (`AccessPoliciesClient`: create, list, get, update and
  delete on an explicitly configured, key-authenticated Portkey control plane, separate from SCM OAuth). The
  TypeScript CLI has no access-policy command, so it stays out of scope: no command, client or option uses it
  (choice 135).

The findings of GK§9, numbered from G36:
- **G36** (GW1, shape; CLI workaround adopted, the G26 pattern). The one-time credentials of
  `api_keys().create_service|create_user|rotate_service|rotate_user`, `deployments().create` and
  `deployments().update` with `rotate_auth` are plain `String` fields of typed answers that are decoded
  before the CLI sees them (`gw:api_keys.rs:59-115`, `:159-215`, `gw:deployments.rs:43-77`), so a 2xx
  answer that fails its schema (a rotate answer without `key_transition_expires_at`, a deployment answer
  without `credentials`) loses a credential the service shows once. The CLI sends these writes as raw
  requests (`RawRequest::new(POST|PUT, <path>).segment(..).json_value(..)` of the body it validated with
  the SDK request schema in `Mode::Request`, through `AIGatewayClient::client()` (data) or
  `deployments().client()` (admin) with `send_json::<serde_json::Value>`, under `writes::attempt`), takes
  the credential members out of the raw answer and registers them first, writes the reservation (§19.11),
  and only then validates the rest with `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults`. `RawRequest::named` is
  crate-private, so the `--debug` log records these writes as `custom.request` (as G26). Safe: the same
  path, method, body and schemas as the typed calls.
- **G37** (GW2, attempt shape; CLI workaround adopted). `workspaces().provision` spans the IAM scope create,
  the workspace create, the scope read and the scope PUT in one call, so `writes::attempt`'s single 401
  replay cannot be applied per step and the recovery is stage-level. The CLI composes the public steps
  (`iam_scopes().create`, `workspaces().create`, `iam_scopes().bind_workspace`, `workspaces().get`), each
  write under `writes::attempt`, and keeps the SDK's cleanup rule: the scope it created is deleted only
  after a **rejected** workspace create (§19.6). `generate_workspace_scope_name` (rejection sampling,
  `rs:helpers.rs:466-502`) makes the default scope name.
- **G38** (GW3, message). `integrations().resolve_provider_id` refuses an unknown slug with a bare
  `ErrorKind::Validation`. The CLI reads `integrations().catalog()` and applies TypeScript's rule itself
  (§19.12).
- **G39** (GW4, API). No gateway list has a continuation contract; answers carry `total` and sometimes
  `has_more`. The CLI prints what it received and says when it is incomplete (D248, §19.3).
- **G40** (GW5, difference; D178 extended). The SDK's response modes keep unknown keys of strict objects and
  widen closed vocabularies (a guardrail `target` other than `llm|mcp_tools`, an admin guardrail `status`
  other than `active|archived`, a new `pricing_adjustments.multiplier` key, a non-empty MCP workspace-set
  answer, an unknown inference `finish_reason`), where TypeScript fails with `AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION`.
  The record is printed (terminal-safe); no workaround.
- **G41** (GW6, difference; D242). The SDK formats `timeOfGenerationMin/Max` with `offset_minutes` (0 by
  default: `+00:00`, seconds precision); TypeScript uses the process's local zone. Rust keeps UTC.
- **G42** (GW7, difference; D234). The SDK's `Error::service_code()` reads `code`, `error.code`,
  `data.errorCode` and `errorCode`; TypeScript chooses its grant hint from message text that never carries
  a top-level `errorCode`. The CLI chooses the hint from the service code and the failing plane (§19.3).
- **G43** (GW8, shape). Secret-bearing request and response fields are plain `String`/`TypedMap<String>`
  (`GatewayApiKeyCreateResponse.key`, `GatewayDeploymentCreateResponse.client_auth`/`credentials`,
  `GatewayIntegrationCreateRequest.key`, `GatewayPluginCreateRequest.credentials`,
  `GatewayOrganisationAuthSettingsUpdateRequest.scim_token`, `GatewayProviderDetail.key`): the CLI registers
  each value in the `SecretSet` when it reads or decodes it and never formats a model with `{:?}`.
- **G44** (GW9, faithful bodies; D239). `audit_logs().list` returns `request_body`, `request_headers` and
  `query_params` faithfully (JSON in strings); the CLI withholds them (§19.3).
- **G45** (GW10, names). The `--debug` operation names are the SDK's: `airs.gateway.<client>.<op>`
  (`airs.gateway.workspaces.list`, `.get`, …), every window-only chart (the 13 of §19.8 without filters)
  `airs.gateway.telemetry.chart`, the filtered charts `airs.gateway.telemetry.cost`, `.requests`, `.latency`,
  `.tokens`, `filter-boundaries` `airs.gateway.telemetry.filter_boundaries`, `logs list`
  `airs.gateway.telemetry.logs`, the four grouped dimensions and `status_code` `airs.gateway.telemetry.group`,
  `users` `airs.gateway.telemetry.by_user`, IAM `shared.iam.scopes.*`, the runtime calls `airs.gateway.chat`,
  `airs.gateway.chat_stream`, `gateway.embedding`, `gateway.response`, `gateway.response_stream`, and the G36
  writes `custom.request`. The debug tests pin them (as G9, G17, G23; chunk 1:
  `tests/gateway_reads.rs::debug`).
- **G46** (GW11, ergonomics). The option structs are `#[non_exhaustive]` with `new`/`Default`
  (`AIGatewayWindowOptions::new(slug)`, `AIGatewayChartOptions::new(window)?`, `AIGatewayLogsOptions::new`,
  `AIGatewayWorkspaceScopedListOptions::new`, `AIGatewayAuditLogListOptions::new`,
  `AIGatewayChartFilters::builder()`); request models are `Deserialize`, so a merged JSON body becomes a
  typed request with `serde_json::from_value`.
- **G47** (GW12, G10 result). No response default is reachable (GK§3.4; the reachable gateway nodes are identical
  in 0.2.2, so still none); `without_response_defaults()` is passed anyway (above).
- **G48** (GW13, difference; D240). `RuntimeClient` has no environment fallback; TypeScript reads
  `PANW_AI_GW_INFERENCE_ENDPOINT` and `PANW_AI_GW_INFERENCE_API_KEY`. The CLI adds none.
- **G49** (confirmed in chunk 3). TypeScript's request schemas carry refinements (`checks: LLM guardrails
  require checks`, `actions: LLM guardrails require actions`, `key_transition_period_ms` ≥ 1,800,000, an
  update with at least one field). The CLI checks each of these itself before the SDK schema with the TS text
  (§19.3). Chunk 3 confirmed on 0.1.1 that the frozen Rust request schemas enforce every one of them too (and
  that they are `strict`: an unknown body key fails them, as TypeScript's `.strict()` objects do), so the CLI
  check only chooses the message: TS's text instead of the D116 text. **Settled on 0.2.2:** the schema nodes are
  identical and request mode keeps every check, and
  `src/gateway/writes.rs::tests::g49_the_sdk_request_schemas_enforce_the_refinements` pins it on the pinned SDK:
  for each refinement a body the schema accepts and the same body breaking only that refinement, which the schema
  refuses (an update with no field, for every update schema; an LLM guardrail without `checks` or `actions`, an
  MCP one needing neither; `key_transition_period_ms` below 1,800,000; an empty or missing `models`; an empty
  `capabilities`; empty plugin `credentials`; an unknown key). Not a gap: a CLI that skipped its own check would
  still never send such a body.
- G3, G4 and G7 apply unchanged. **Nothing in §19 is blocked on scm-sdk.**

### 19.1 Build chunks

0.10 is built in four chunks. Each chunk ships its executable, parity and `dNN_` tests, registers only its
own commands (until a chunk lands its commands are not in the clap tree, exit 2, D1, and the group help lists
only the commands that exist) and leaves the checks green.

| Chunk | Commands | Shared work it introduces |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Foundation and core reads | `gateway workspaces list\|ls`, `workspaces get`; `gateway scopes list\|ls`, `scopes get`; every `gateway telemetry` read: `cost`, `requests`, `errors`, `users`, `latency`, `tokens`, `error-trends`, `error-category-trends`, `grouped-errors`, `rescued-retries`, `user-trends`, `cache summary`, `cache trend`, `feedback distribution`, `feedback models`, `feedback trend`, `feedback weighted`, `filter-boundaries`, `group-by <dimension>`, `logs list\|ls` | the `gateway` feature; `clients::GatewayClients` (data, admin and IAM planes, one OAuth identity); `src/gateway/` (ids, planes, `options`, the grant hint, workspace resolution, the window and chart filters, the views, the generic list and detail renderers, the withholding policy); the planning of §19.3; the fixture's `Route::Gateway(Gw)` read routes (workspaces, IAM scopes, charts, groups, logs, filter boundaries) and markers |
| 2. Inventory and admin-guardrail reads | `gateway api-keys service\|user list\|ls`, `get`; `audit-logs list\|ls`; `configs list\|ls`, `get`, `versions`; `deployments list\|ls`, `get`, `ping`; `guardrails list\|ls`, `get`, `catalog`; `integrations list\|ls`, `get`, `providers`, `models list\|ls`, `workspaces list\|ls`; `mcp integrations list\|ls`, `get`, `capabilities list\|ls`, `metadata`, `workspaces list\|ls`; `organisations info`, `self get`, `auth-settings get`; `plugins list\|ls`; `providers list\|ls`, `get`; `admin-guardrails list\|ls`, `get`, `mcp-servers list\|ls` (every read that is not in chunk 1) | the per-resource path rules of the withholding policy, the audit-log rule, `--reveal-sensitive`, the paged-read status lines, the fixture's inventory and admin read routes with their secret markers |
| 3. Writes | `workspaces create` (provisioning), `update`, `archive`, hidden `delete`; `scopes create`, `bind`, `delete\|rm`; `configs`, `guardrails`, `providers` `create`, `update`, `delete\|rm`; `api-keys service\|user create`, `update`, `rotate`, `delete\|rm`; `deployments create`, `update` (`--rotate-auth` included), `archive`; `integrations create`, `update`, `delete\|rm`, `models set`, `workspaces set`; `mcp integrations create`, `update`, `delete\|rm`, `capabilities set`, `workspaces set`; `organisations self update`, `auth-settings update`; `plugins create`; `admin-guardrails create`, `update`, `delete\|rm`, `mcp-servers sync`, `mcp-servers upsert` | structured input (`--file`, named flags, `--set`, `--set-string`), the G37 provisioning, the G36 raw credential writes and the `--secret-output` reservation, the provider-credential inputs, the confirmations, the gateway `Change` words and hints, the fixture's write routes, counters, held and dropped answers |
| 4. Inference, report, doctor, live | `gateway inference chat`, `responses`, `embeddings`; `gateway report\|dashboard`; the doctor's `Gateway API` check; the live tier's gateway reads | `clients::GatewayRuntime`, the stream writer; the gateway collector (`src/report/gateway.rs`) and the generalised renderer (`src/report/html.rs` profiles, `Cell::Null`, `Cell::Number`); the doctor probe; `live::gateway` and its self-tests; the fixture's inference and report routes |

### 19.2 Commands and options

Help texts, group descriptions and arguments are TypeScript's (GW§1, the captured `--help` of every leaf)
with the program name `airs`, `aigateway` read as `gateway`, the `--output` line generated from the
format policy (§2.4), one `(default: …)` where commander printed two (`report --days`), and the changes of
this section. A group without a subcommand prints its help on stderr, exit 2 (D1). Every `list` has the
visible alias `ls` and every visible `delete` the alias `rm` (the hidden `workspaces delete` has none, TS);
`workspaces` has the alias `workspace` and `report` the alias `dashboard` (TS). The `Examples:` blocks of
`workspaces list|get|create|update|archive`, `scopes list|get|create|bind|delete`, `telemetry cost` and
`report` are TypeScript's with the program name, except that the report example with `--output markdown`
is dropped (D155) and `--output-file - > daily.html` stays. Pinned leaf by leaf against the reference by
`help_texts_match_typescript`.

The leaves and options are GW§1's table (105 visible leaves plus the hidden `workspaces delete`), with:

| Leaf | Change |
|---|---|
| every leaf | the leaf `--output <format>` is the global `--output` (§2.3): `pretty`, `table`, `json` (D50) |
| `api-keys service\|user create`, `rotate`; `deployments create`, `update` | `--secret-output <path>` is the only credential channel (help `New private file (mode 0600) that receives the one-time credential; never overwritten (the credential is never printed)`); `--show-secret` stays in the tree, hidden, as a usage error (D237) |
| `api-keys service\|user list`, `get`; `providers get`; `organisations auth-settings get` | `--reveal-sensitive` stays in the tree, hidden, as a usage error (D238); `audit-logs list --reveal-sensitive` keeps its option with the help `Show request fields; credentials inside them stay withheld` (D239) |
| `providers create` | no `--reset-usage` (D245) |
| every write with structured input | `--file <path>` help `Advanced JSON request base; named flags override it` (TS: `JSON/YAML`; D246, choice 97) |
| `organisations info`, `auth-settings get\|update` | `--tsg-id <tsg>` optional (help `Numeric TSG id (default: the selected tenant's mgmtTsgId; another value is refused)`) (D245) |
| every `--organisation-id <tsg>` (`api-keys … create`, `deployments create\|archive`, `integrations create\|delete`, `mcp integrations create`, `plugins create`) | optional, with the same default and refusal (D245) |
| every `telemetry` leaf except `cost` | `--workspace <ref>` (help `Workspace slug, UUID, or unique display name`, resolved, D235) |
| `scopes delete`, `workspaces archive\|delete`, every visible `delete`, `deployments archive`, every `set`/`sync` and `rotate` | `--force` as TS (`Skip confirmation prompt`) |
| `workspaces update`, `api-keys … update`, `providers update`, `integrations update`, `mcp integrations update`, `deployments update`, `organisations self update`, `auth-settings update` | `--force` (Rust, `Skip the confirmation prompt`) for the confirmations of §19.3 |
| `inference *` | `--output` help `Output format: pretty, table, json; streaming json emits one event per line (JSONL)` |
| `report\|dashboard` | `--workspace <ref>` (required), `--days <n>` (`1`), `--start <iso>`, `--end <iso>`, `--output-file <path>`, `--title <text>` (`AI Gateway environment report`), `--max-pages <n>` (`40`), `--strict`; the leaf `--output` is refused (D155), help `Refused by this command: the report is written as HTML (omit --output)` |

No other option is added or removed. Boolean flags take no value; options whose TypeScript form takes
`<boolean>` (`--is-default`, `--reset-usage`, `--rotate-auth`, `--allow-all-models`, …) keep their value;
a repeated scalar option takes its last value (TS); the repeatable options of GW§1 (`--set`,
`--set-string`, `--header`, `--model`, `--workspace-binding`, `--capability`, `--credential`) collect.

### 19.3 Common rules

**Clients and planes** (GK§2.2). Every management-plane gateway command builds
`clients::GatewayClients::build(config, session, secrets, debug)` from the selected tenant only:
- `gatewayDataEndpoint` (else `scm::constants::DEFAULT_AI_GW_DATA_ENDPOINT`,
  `https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/ai_gw/v2`), `gatewayAdminEndpoint` (else
  `…/ai_gw/admin/v2`), `iamEndpoint` (else `…/iam/v1`) and `mgmtTokenEndpoint`, each admitted by §5 (the
  D48 message names the key, never the value; a trailing `/` of a base is ignored, both SDKs);
- the §3.5 management credential check before any client is built, with the §3.5 messages;
- `oauth_parts` (the lease-recording provider, one transport, one `OriginPolicy` admitting the three bases
  and the issuer), `max_retries = 5` for replay-safe reads (D10), the 8 MiB response bound, then
  `AIGatewayClient::new(client, admin, iam)` (OAuth required, the `x-tsg-id: <mgmtTsgId>` header forced on
  every request, IAM included: TS parity). A construction failure is
  `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:The gateway client could not be configured` (exit 1). Every command except `report` awaits
  the token before its first request, so a token failure is the §6 `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR:…` message. One token
  per invocation (TS parity).
- Planes (GW§2.1): **data** — every `telemetry` read, `workspaces list|get` without `--plane admin`,
  `configs`, workspace `guardrails` (except `catalog`), `providers`, `api-keys`; **admin** — `workspaces`
  `--plane admin` reads and every workspace write, `admin-guardrails`, `guardrails catalog`, `integrations`
  (the provider catalog included), `mcp integrations`, `deployments`, `plugins`, `organisations`,
  `audit-logs`; **IAM** — `scopes` and the scope steps of `workspaces create`.

`gateway inference` builds `clients::GatewayRuntime::build` instead (§19.14): no OAuth, no §3.5 check, no
`x-tsg-id`. No environment variable is read for any gateway command (§2.6): `PANW_AI_GW_*`, `PANW_IAM_ENDPOINT`,
`PANW_AI_GW_INFERENCE_*`, `PANW_AI_SEC_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG`, `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG_BODY` and `TZ`
change nothing (D240, D242). The tenant keys are the 0.3 `gateway*` names (§3.3 rows 19–25); **no tenant
wording changes**. The doctor gains the `Gateway API` check (§9, §19.16) and its management-credential line
names `gateway` commands (D227).

**Request options** (one helper, `gateway::options`, built just before each request is sent, as §18.20
choice 73; every call `.without_response_defaults()`):

| Calls | Options |
|---|---|
| single reads, resolution lists | the SDK read retries (D10), `SINGLE_REQUEST_BUDGET` each |
| every write (POST, PUT, DELETE) | `writes::attempt` (one attempt, a 401 replayed once, a 403 never; D228), `SINGLE_REQUEST_BUDGET`; never `with_retries(0)` on a write |
| `report` sources | §15.17: one `with_timeout(300 s).with_retries(0)` budget per source with the G7 re-read inside it; the log pages share their source's budget |
| doctor probe | `with_retries(0)` under the doctor's 5 s budget (D49, §19.16) |
| inference | `with_timeout(--timeout)` covering the whole stream, `RuntimeReplay::Never` |

**Validation order.** clap → `--output` (§2.4) → `--tenant`'s name format → the command's argument checks
in the order of its section (the `--debug` refusal of `report`, the `--show-secret` and `--reveal-sensitive`
refusals, the secret destination rule, the ids, the flags, then the non-interactive refusal of a write that always
confirms; choices 88, 124) → the debug log (§2.9) → input files and path checks (`--file`,
`--key-file`, `--key-stdin`, the hidden key prompt, `--secret-output`, `report --output-file`) → the bodies
built from them (named flags, `--set`, the CLI refinements, the SDK request schema) → the non-interactive
refusal of a confirmation the body decides (`reset_usage`, a credential path, `rotate_auth`, a deployment's
`auth_settings`, an MCP `auth_type`) → the
tenant (§3.4, §3.7) → the tenant `defaultOutput` → the credential check (§3.5) or the inference
configuration → the TSG comparisons (`--tsg-id`, `--organisation-id`) → the client and token → the command's
resolution reads, prompts, reservation and writes. Every usage error (exit 2) comes before the tenant is
read, makes no request and opens no debug log (D232; TS checks most of them after the tenant, the banner or
the client, GW§2.5). File and path errors exit 1 before the tenant, with zero requests.

**Argument checks** (D232; exit 2; values in messages through `terminal_safe`, at most 200 characters with
`…`):
- **UUIDs** (the §7.1 shape, `pagination::is_uuid`): else the TypeScript SDK text
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid <field>: <value>`, `<field>` as TS: `workspaceId`
  (`--workspace <uuid>` of the workspace-scoped lists, creates and `admin-guardrails list|create`),
  `configId`, `guardrailId`, `providerId`, `keyId`, `integrationId` (positional and `--integration-id`),
  `mcpIntegrationId`, `deploymentId`, `mcpServerId`, `userId` (`--user-id`), `aiProviderId`
  (`--ai-provider-id`), `organisationId` (`admin-guardrails create --organisation`, an organisation UUID).
- **Numeric TSGs** (`--organisation-id`, `--tsg-id`): 1–32 ASCII digits, else
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid organisationId: <value>` / `Invalid tsgId: <value>`. The
  comparison with the tenant's `mgmtTsgId` comes after the tenant (D245, exit 1).
- **Workspace references.** `workspaces get <ref>`: a UUID or `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`, else
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid workspaceRef: <value> (expected a workspace UUID or slug)` (TS
  SDK text). `workspaces update|archive|delete <ref>` and every `--workspace <ref>` that is resolved
  (`scopes bind`, every `telemetry` leaf, `report`): non-blank under JavaScript trim (`<flag> cannot be
  empty`, `report` TS text) and at most 4,096 bytes without control characters
  (`<flag> must be at most 4096 bytes and contain no control characters`); a display name may contain
  spaces (§19.4).
- **IAM scope names** (`scopes get|bind|delete <name>`, `scopes create --name`, `workspaces create
  --scope-name`): `scm::shared::iam::validate_scope_name` (`^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` and the SDK
  segment rule), else `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid name: <value> (expected an IAM scope name such as ws_production_bx7qw0)`
  (TS text; `scopes create` is checked too, D236).
- **Flags with fixed vocabularies** (TS texts): `Invalid --plane '<v>'. Valid planes: data, admin`,
  `Invalid --status '<v>'. Valid statuses: active, archived`,
  `--all already merges admin-plane active + archived; drop --plane/--status`, the `group-by`, `logs`,
  window and filter texts of §19.8, the admin-guardrail paging texts of §19.13, the inference texts of
  §19.14, the report texts of §19.15.
- **Scalar flags** (the TS parsers of GW§2.8, TS texts, `Invalid --<flag>: <reason>` with the flag as typed,
  never a derived name, D233): booleans `true|false` only (`Expected true or false`); integers
  `^-?(0|[1-9]\d*)$` and safe (`Expected an integer`, `Expected a safe integer`); timestamps
  (`--expires-at`) the zod `datetime({offset: true})` grammar of §17.3 (`Expected an ISO-8601 timestamp`;
  TS accepts anything `new Date` parses and sends the string, which the schema then refuses); comma lists
  trimmed with empty items dropped, at least one item (`Expected a non-empty comma-separated list`); JSON
  objects and arrays (`Expected valid JSON`, never echoed); bindings `id=true|false`, `slug=true|false`,
  `type:name=true|false` (`Expected id=value`, `Expected slug=value`, `Expected type:name=enabled`); string
  maps `key=value` (`--header`, `--credential`) refusing `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`
  (`Unsafe key: <key>`) and duplicates (`Duplicate key: <key>`; key names are printed, values never).
- **One-time credential destinations** (D237): `api-keys … create|rotate`, `deployments create` and a
  rotating `deployments update` need `--secret-output <path>`, else
  `A one-time credential needs --secret-output <new file>; airs never prints it` (TS:
  `Choose --secret-output <path> (recommended) or --show-secret before requesting a one-time credential`);
  `--secret-output ""` is `--secret-output needs a path`; `--secret-output -` is
  `--secret-output - would print the credential; give a file path` (as D194); `--secret-output` on a
  `deployments update` that does not rotate is `--secret-output is used only with --rotate-auth true`;
  `--show-secret` is `--show-secret is not supported: one-time credentials are written only to --secret-output <new file>`.
- `--reveal-sensitive` where it is hidden (§19.2):
  `--reveal-sensitive is not supported here: airs never prints credentials` (D238).
- The command-specific checks of §19.5–§19.16.

**Request bodies** (structured input, GW§2.8; D246, D233). Every create, update, set, sync and upsert builds
its JSON body in TypeScript's order: the `--file` base < the named flags < `--set path=value` /
`--set-string path=value`.
- `--file <path>`: the §13.2 input rules (the path as given, symlinks followed, a regular file of at most
  1 MiB, read whole, UTF-8, one JSON value that is an object, the §13.2 messages with `--file`, no content
  and no OS error echoed), after the debug log and before the tenant. YAML is not read: a file that is not
  one JSON object (also a `.yaml`/`.yml` file, which TypeScript parses with js-yaml) is
  `--file must contain one JSON object (YAML request files are not supported)` (exit 2; choice 32).
- Named flags map to TypeScript's request paths (GW§6.2–§6.9, GW§7; dotted paths allowed), parsed with the
  scalar rules above.
- `--set path=value` parses `value` as JSON and falls back to the literal string; `--set-string` keeps the
  string. A missing `=` (or `=` first) is `Invalid --set: Expected path=value` / `Invalid --set-string: Expected path=value`
  (TS echoes the argument, which can carry a credential, D233). Paths go through a port of TypeScript's dotted
  paths (`nested-values.ts`: `.` properties, `[n]` indices, `\` escapes; choice 86; the SDK's
  `set_dotted_value` / `build_dotted_object` refuse with a bare validation error), whose refusals are TypeScript's
  texts `Invalid AI Gateway request: AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:<reason>` (`Dotted path must not be empty`,
  `Invalid empty segment in dotted path: <path>`, `Unsafe dotted path segment: <segment>`,
  `Duplicate dotted path`, `Dotted path shape conflict`, `Array index conflicts with an object path`,
  `Sparse arrays are not supported`, `Dotted value must be finite JSON`, and the other `parsePath` texts naming the
  path). Assignments may overwrite file or flag values, not each other (TS).
- **Numbers** are read as JS `JSON.parse` reads them and sent in their `JSON.stringify` form, in `--set` values, the
  JSON flags (`--rate-limit`, `--configurations`, the workspace JSON flags, …) and `--file` (`body::js_json`): a
  number literal that overflows a double (`1e400`) is JS `Infinity`, so `--set n=1e400` and a JSON flag holding one
  are `Invalid AI Gateway request: AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Dotted value must be finite JSON` and a `--file`
  object holding one is `Invalid AI Gateway request: <root>: Expected a finite, prototype-safe JSON object` (exit 2,
  TS texts; never the literal string); an integral double within the safe-integer range is sent as an integer
  (`1e2` → `100`, `1.0` → `1`, `-0` → `0`), other numbers as parsed. Parity tested byte for byte (choice 122).
- The CLI refinements (G49, TS texts, exit 2): an update whose body has no member is
  `Invalid AI Gateway request: <root>: Provide at least one field`; a workspace guardrail whose `target` is
  not `mcp_tools` without `checks` or `actions` is
  `Invalid AI Gateway request: checks: LLM guardrails require checks; actions: LLM guardrails require actions`
  (the parts that apply); `key_transition_period_ms` below 1,800,000 is
  `Invalid AI Gateway request: key_transition_period_ms: Number must be greater than or equal to 1800000`;
  `integrations models set` without a model binding is zod's `Invalid AI Gateway request: models: Required` (no
  `models` member: the flag omitted), `Invalid AI Gateway request: models: Array must contain at least 1 element(s)`
  (an explicit `[]`, `--set models=[]`) or `Invalid AI Gateway request: models: Expected array, received <type>`
  (another value) (TS texts; parity tested); `plugins create` without
  a credential is `Invalid AI Gateway request: credentials: Provide at least one field`.
- Then the SDK request schema in `Mode::Request` (the schema of GK§4.4 for the operation); a failure is the
  D116 text `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Request body for <METHOD> <path> did not match schema` (exit 2,
  an argument- or file-built body; `<path>` the route with its ids; TS: `Invalid AI Gateway request: <path>: <zod message>`,
  which quotes received enum values, D233). Unknown keys are kept and sent where the schema keeps them
  (TS: `strip` objects with a `finite_json` catchall keep them, GK§3.4). Bodies are sent with sorted keys
  (D35); equality with TypeScript is JSON equality.

**Writes and outcomes** (D228). Every gateway request that is not a GET is a write: one SDK call (never
re-sent by the SDK; the G36 raw writes included) through `writes::attempt`: one replay after an `Http` 401
with outcome `Rejected`, never after a 403, a 5xx, a timeout or a transport error. The error of a failed
write is the §6 message; when the outcome is not a plain rejection one detail line follows the
`HTTP`/`Re-run` lines (`Outcome unknown: the <thing> may have been <done>.` or
`Outcome: the <thing> was <done>, but the response could not be read.`), then the hint line. Nothing is
re-sent and nothing is looked up after such a failure. Exit 1. TypeScript re-sends every write up to 5 times
on 500/502/503/504, transport errors and timeouts and once after a 401 or 403 (3 API-key POSTs after two
502s, 6 workspace DELETEs, GW§2.6). The words (`writes::Change`; `<id>` the argument, `<kind>` `service` or
`user`):

| Command | `<thing>` / `<done>` | Hint after an unknown or unreadable outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `configs\|guardrails\|providers create` | `config` / `guardrail` / `provider` · `created` | `Check 'airs gateway <group> list --workspace <uuid>' before creating it again.` |
| `configs\|guardrails\|providers update <id>`, `delete <id>` | `config <id>` (…) · `updated` / `deleted` | `Check it with 'airs gateway <group> get <id>'.` |
| `api-keys <kind> create`, `rotate <id>` | `<kind> API key` / `<kind> API key <id>` · `created` / `rotated` | §19.11 |
| `api-keys <kind> update <id>`, `delete <id>` | `<kind> API key <id>` · `updated` / `revoked` | `Check it with 'airs gateway api-keys <kind> get <id>'.` |
| `integrations create`, `mcp integrations create`, `admin-guardrails create`, `plugins create` | `integration` / `MCP integration` / `admin guardrail` / `plugin` · `created` | `Check 'airs gateway <group> list' before creating it again.` |
| `integrations\|mcp integrations\|admin-guardrails update <id>`, `delete <id>` | `integration <id>` (…) · `updated` / `deleted` | `Check it with 'airs gateway <group> get <id>'.` |
| `integrations models set <id>`, `workspaces set <id>` | `model bindings of integration <id>` / `workspace bindings of integration <id>` · `replaced` | `Check them with 'airs gateway integrations models list <id>'` (`workspaces list <id>`) |
| `mcp integrations capabilities set <id>`, `workspaces set <id>` | `MCP capabilities of <id>` / `MCP workspace access of <id>` · `replaced` | `Check them with 'airs gateway mcp integrations capabilities list <id>'` (`workspaces list <id>`) |
| `admin-guardrails mcp-servers sync <id>`, `upsert <id> <server>` | `MCP mappings of admin guardrail <id>` · `replaced` / `MCP mapping <server> of admin guardrail <id>` · `set` | `Check them with 'airs gateway admin-guardrails mcp-servers list <id>'.` |
| `deployments create`, `update <id>`, `archive <id>` | `deployment` · `registered` (§19.11) / `deployment <id>` · `updated` / `archived` | `Check it with 'airs gateway deployments get <id>'.` (create: §19.11) |
| `organisations self update`, `auth-settings update` | `current organisation` · `updated` / `authentication settings of organisation <tsg>` · `replaced` | `Check it with 'airs gateway organisations self get'` (`auth-settings get`) |
| workspaces and scopes | §19.6, §19.7 | §19.6, §19.7 |

A successful write prints its acknowledgement on stderr (green, quiet-suppressed): the TypeScript lines of
§19.6 and §19.7 for workspaces and scopes, and for every other write the Rust line `  ✓ <Thing> <done>[: <id>]`
(`<Thing>` the thing with a capital first letter; `<id>` the argument, else the answer's `id` when it is a
string) — TypeScript prints none, so an empty `{}` answer was silent (D244). Deletes, archives and revocations
leave stdout empty in every format (`--output` validated, then ignored; TS prints a fabricated
`{"success": true}`, D244). Every other write prints its answer on stdout in the chosen format through the
generic detail renderer, after the withholding policy (below).

**Confirmations** (D243). The writes below confirm under the §3.10 and §13.2 rules: `--force` skips the
prompt; the gate is stdin **and** stderr being terminals, otherwise the refusal (exit 2, before the tenant);
the prompt `? <message> (y/N) ` on stderr; only `y`/`yes` (trimmed, ASCII case-insensitive) confirm; anything
else, an empty line and EOF decline with `  ℹ Aborted` (exit 0, nothing sent, a reserved `--secret-output`
removed, the path never created); Ctrl-C or SIGTERM print `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` and exit
130/143. Argument and server text in a prompt goes through `terminal_safe` (and the `[withheld]` rule). The
prompt is asked after the reads its section lists and before the write (and before a reservation); no request
is open while it waits; commands that read nothing first ask before the token request. The TypeScript prompts
are kept (GW§2.10); TypeScript asks on stdout when stdout is a terminal, accepts any answer starting with `y`
and exits 1 on Ctrl-C (D81).
