Creates (including `workspaces create`, `scopes create`, the secret creates), `scopes bind`, `admin-guardrails
mcp-servers upsert` and updates that change none of the above do not confirm (choice 28).

**Streams, banner, quiet and formats** (D230, D231, D50). stdout carries data only, written once after success
(§2.2), except the inference stream (§19.14). `pretty`, `table` and `json` exist for every command that prints
data, writes included; `markdown`, `csv` and `yaml` are invalid formats (D50, exit 2, before the tenant; TS
offers six, the writes `pretty|json|yaml`). The tenant's `defaultOutput` is honoured by every gateway command
except `report` (TS resolves it for every command but the report; GW§2.2, GR§1).
- **Banner** `"\n  Prisma AIRS — AI Gateway\n  Gateway workspace operations\n\n"` (TS text; decoration): pretty
  only, at the top of stdout, only above the data of a successful `workspaces list|get|create|update`,
  `scopes list|get|create|bind` or `telemetry cost` (TS prints it before its checks for these and for the
  archives and deletes whatever the format, so failing runs leave it on stdout, GW§2.3). Archives and deletes
  print no banner (their stdout is empty). No other gateway command prints a banner (TS).
- **Sections** (`"\n  <Title>:\n\n"`, bold) are decoration (quiet-suppressed); every data line stays under
  `--quiet`, the dim workspace id lines of `workspaces list` included (TS drops them, GW§2.3).
- **Acknowledgements** (`✓ …`) and **warnings** (`⚠ …`: the scope-name warning, the deprecated `delete`, the
  inline-credential warnings, the incomplete-list and quota warnings, the grant hint, the read-back failures)
  go to stderr: acknowledgements and status lines quiet-suppressed, warnings never (TS writes `ui.success` and
  `ui.warn` on stdout, before a JSON document; D230).
- **Empty lists**: pretty `  No <label> found\n` (dim, data; TS labels, `workspaces` and `IAM scopes`
  included); table nothing on stdout; json `[]\n` (TS: `No workspaces found` in every format, json included;
  D231).

**Generic list and detail renderers** (GW§2.9; the inventory reads, the paged and telemetry reads except
`cost`, and every write answer). The list is TS `responseItems` (an array; else `data` when an array; else
`data.records`; else `records`; else no rows). Columns are TS `displayColumns`: a key is eligible when no row
holds an object or array there; first the preferred `id, slug, name, type, status, enabled, created_at,
last_updated_at` that are eligible and present, then every other eligible key in UTF-16 code-unit order (JS
sort), at most 8; labels `_` → space and each word capitalised (`created_at` → `Created At`). Cells: absent or
`null` empty, scalars as text (`js_number`), through `terminal_safe`. `pretty` and `table` print the same §2.7
table (TS); json the rows after withholding. A detail is TS `renderGatewayDetail`: pretty and table a two-column
`Field │ Value` table of the top-level members in record order, objects and arrays as compact JSON; json the
object; a non-object answer is `{"value": <it>}` (TS). An empty object prints pretty `  No fields returned\n`
(dim, data), table nothing and json `{}` (TS prints nothing in pretty and `{}` in json; D231).

**Lists without continuation** (G39, D248). After printing a list whose answer says `has_more: true`, or whose
`total` is a safe non-negative integer other than the number of rows, the warning
`  ⚠ The service returned <n> of <total> <label>; the list is incomplete (the API offers no continuation)`
(`<total>` `more than <n>` when only `has_more` says so) goes to stderr; exit 0 (choice 16). The paged reads
(`telemetry logs list`, `admin-guardrails list`) print a status line instead (§19.8, §19.13).

**JSON.** Lists print a bare array, gets and writes a bare object: the TS projection where a section names one
(workspaces, scopes, `cost`), else the server's record after withholding, re-serialised from the SDK model
(schema order, unknown keys sorted, D35). Numbers through `js_number`. Every C1 control (U+0080–U+009F) is
written as a `\u00XX` escape (the D212 writer option; choice 43).

**Table and colour.** Tables are never coloured. Pretty colours are TypeScript's (GW§2.3): section titles bold;
key/value keys dim; the workspace status `active` green, `archived` yellow, anything else dim; `  default` cyan;
slugs, `scope: …`, scope descriptions and bindings dim; `unbound` and `none — unbound` yellow; `(none)` dim;
success lines green, warnings yellow, failures red. Colour per stream (§2.8).

**Server text** (D11, D52). Error messages are §6 messages (TS prints the server's `message`, whole non-JSON
bodies and provider error text verbatim, control characters included, GW§2.6), except the report's fixed lines
(§19.15). Every server string in a pretty layout, table cell, acknowledgement, prompt or message goes through
`terminal_safe`. Any printed server string (any field, any format) that contains a value of the invocation's
`SecretSet` (raw, trimmed, form-encoded or base64) is `[withheld]`, and an object member whose name carries one
is dropped with its value (D47, §18.20 choice 81).

**The grant hint** (G42, D234). A command whose failure is an `Http` 403 prints, on stderr before the error
block, one warning: `  ⚠ 403: the service account is missing a workspace-scope grant (data plane, /ai_gw/v2). SCM Access Management edits the existing role row by default — use "Add Role" so the account ends up with both role rows, not one row moved.`
when the error's `service_code()` is `AB03`, or when it has no service code and the failing request was on the
data plane; `  ⚠ 403: the service account is missing a tenant-root admin grant (admin plane, /ai_gw/admin/v2). SCM Access Management edits …`
(the same tail) when the request was on the admin plane and the code is not `AB03`; nothing for an IAM request
(TS texts; TS chooses by `AB03` in the message text, which never carries a top-level `errorCode`, prints the
hint on stdout, and gives IAM 403s the admin hint).

**Secrets and the withholding policy** (D238, D239, D251, G43). Every credential the gateway returns, and every
credential the user supplies, is a secret of the invocation: it joins the `SecretSet` before anything is printed
and never appears on stdout, stderr, in an error, a prompt, the debug log, a summary or the ledger. One policy
applies to **every gateway document printed** (every read, every write answer, every format), in this order:
1. **Subtree rules** (TS parity; the SDK's `Subtree` rules of `telemetry.filterBoundaries` and
   `organisations.getInfo`): the `data` of `telemetry filter-boundaries` and the `settings` of
   `organisations info` are replaced whole (choice 18).
2. **Path rules** (the SDK's `AI_GATEWAY_SECRET_FIELDS` request and response paths of the resource's
   operations, `rs:constants.rs:167-…`, read from that public constant by operation and never copied; `*` is any
   member or array item, as the SDK reads it; choice 133), applied to a detail and to every list row: providers `key`,
   `model_config`, `credentials`, `configurations.azure_entra_client_secret`,
   `configurations.aws_secret_access_key`, `configurations.vertex_service_account_json`,
   `configurations.custom_headers.*`; integrations `key` and the four `configurations` paths; MCP integrations
   `configurations.custom_headers.*`, `configurations.client_secret`, `configurations.oauth_client_secret`,
   `configurations.oauth_metadata`; authentication settings `scim_token`, `data.scim_token`,
   `auth_settings.client_secret`, `data.auth_settings.client_secret` (the last a CLI addition); API keys `key` at
   any depth (TS `redactApiKeyMaterial`); deployments `client_auth`, `credentials.password`; plugins `credentials.*`.
   The secret-reference operations (`auth_config`; `data.*.auth_config`) have no command and reach the CLI only
   through rule 5. What a path rule withholds is registered by rule 3g (a final `*` member by its own name).
3. **The name rule**, at any depth of every document (inside a revealed audit field as rule 5 says). One module
   decides it for the CLI and the live tier alike, `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/` (choice 172; the harness compiles
   the same files by `#[path]`, choice 185), in
   three steps, each data rather than code paths:
   1. the member name is **normalised**: lowercased; every character that is not a letter or a digit read as `_`,
      a run of them as one and none at either end; a camelCase boundary read as `_` (an uppercase letter after a
      lowercase letter or a digit, or the last of an uppercase run a lowercase letter follows). So `clientSecret`,
      `X-API-Key`, `API KEY`, `api.key` and `APIKey` are `client_secret`, `x_api_key`, `api_key`, `api_key` and
      `api_key` (choices 157, 170);
   2. the **first row** of "Rule 3 by name" that matches the normalised name gives its class (`names::NAME_RULES`;
      the table below is generated from it, and `withhold::tests::name_rule::the_design_table_is_the_name_rules` fails when the
      two differ). Rows 6, 7 and 10–14 are sub-rule 3a, row 4 is 3b, row 5 is 3d and rows 15–16 are 3c's maps;
      rows 1–3, 8 and 9 are the printed exceptions to the rows below them: the names TypeScript's `redactDeep`
      masks that airs-cli-rs prints, and key-name lists (`metadata_keys`, `unique_metadata_keys`,
      `unique_virtual_keys`) that only row 11's `_keys` suffix would withhold and TypeScript never masks (choice
      188) (none holds a credential: row 8 is a credential's fingerprint, printed unless its value looks like a credential, and row 9
      a name whose last words describe a credential, a count, a lifetime, a timestamp, a type, a name, an
      identifier or where it is kept or sent, choice 187), and with the `tokenizer` and `tokenizers` words row 14
      excepts they are all of them, so TypeScript's vocabulary is the floor (row 14 reads `token` in the name's
      letters, as TypeScript's `/token/i` does, so `tokenvalue`, `accesstokenhash` and `TOKENvalue` are withheld;
      choice 176). Rows 6 and 7 keep two names with a row-9 ending credentials: a Vault AppRole SecretID and a
      capability URL named after a stored secret (`secret_url`; `token_url` and `auth_uri` name where a credential
      is sent and print);
   3. the class and the value's **shape** give the action ("Rule 3 by shape", `names::action`).

   **Rule 3 by name**

   | # | A normalised name that | Class | Choices | Why |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | is `secret_key` in a secret mapping or reference | printed | 164 | a key name inside the referenced secret, beside `secret_path` or `secret_reference_id` |
   | 2 | starts with `masked_` | printed | §18.20 c5, 157 | the service's fingerprints |
   | 3 | is `api_key_id`, `api_key_ids`, `api_key_defaults_id`, `header_key`, `max_token_age`, `max_tokens`, `metadata_key`, `metadata_keys`, `rotate_auth`, `secret_mappings`, `secret_path`, `secret_reference_id`, `secrets_categories`, `total_tokens`, `unique_metadata_keys`, `unique_virtual_keys`, `value_key`, `virtual_key`, `virtual_keys` | printed | 157, 165, 170, 176, 188 | identifiers, references, text-capable counts, guardrail settings, key names, a request flag |
   | 4 | is `key`, `keys`, `token` | generic | 120, 141, 176 | a tag name or a word as often as a credential |
   | 5 | is `vertex_service_account_json`, `oauth_metadata`, `model_config`, `auth_config` | credential member | 136 | the SDK's credential members |
   | 6 | ends with the `_` word(s) `secret_id` | credential | 187 | a Vault AppRole SecretID, a credential that ends in `id` |
   | 7 | ends with the `_` word `url`, `uri`, `endpoint` after a part that, with `_` removed, contains `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `pwd`, `passphrase`, `passcode`, `credential`, `cookie`, `privatekey`, `connectionstring` | credential | 187 | a capability URL named after a stored secret |
   | 8 | ends with the `_` word(s) `prefix`, `last4`, `last8`, `last_four`, `hint` | fingerprint | 187 | a credential's fingerprint, withheld only where it looks like a credential |
   | 9 | ends with the `_` word(s) `count`, `counts`, `limit`, `limits`, `length`, `size`, `max`, `min`, `ttl`, `period`, `interval`, `duration`, `ms`, `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `at`, `date`, `timestamp`, `expiry`, `expiration`, `expires`, `expires_in`, `enabled`, `disabled`, `required`, `type`, `types`, `kind`, `mode`, `format`, `name`, `names`, `id`, `ids`, `version`, `status`, `location`, `path`, `url`, `uri`, `endpoint` | printed | 187 | what describes a credential: a count, a lifetime, a timestamp, a type, a name, an id, a location |
   | 10 | is `auth`, `jwt`, `bearer`, `auth_header`, `authheader`, `accesskey`, `masterkey`, `accountkey`, `shared_access_signature`, `sharedaccesssignature`, `sig`, `signature` | credential | 170, 181, 183, 187 | a credential named by its kind |
   | 11 | ends with `_key`, `_keys`, `_auth`, `_jwt`, `_signature` | credential | 157, 170, 176, 181, 187 | a key, an authentication, a token or a signature of something |
   | 12 | contains, with `_` removed, `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `pwd`, `passphrase`, `passcode`, `credential`, `apikey`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `clientauth`, `authcode`, `privatekey`, `connectionstring` | credential | 131, 157, 170, 176, 187 | a credential word anywhere in the name |
   | 13 | has a `_` word that is `pass`, `pat`, `otp` | credential | 176, 187 | a credential word that is ordinary inside a word |
   | 14 | contains, with the `_` words `tokenizer`, `tokenizers` and `_` removed, `token` | count | 163, 165, 171, 176 | a token or a token count |
   | 15 | is `headers` | header map | 138 | a header map |
   | 16 | ends with `_headers` | header map | 138, 177 | a header map of something |
   | 17 | matches no row | printed | | |

   **Rule 3 by shape** (what a member of the class becomes; "read" is by these rules again; a withheld value is the
   string `"[withheld]"` and joins the `SecretSet` as 3g says of its kind)

   | Class | `null`, boolean | number | string that looks like a credential | any other string (the empty string too) | object or array without text | any other object or array |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | printed | read | read | read | read | read | read |
   | fingerprint | read | read | withheld, a credential's value | read | read | read |
   | header map | printed | printed | read as a header map (3c) | read as a header map | read as a header map | read as a header map |
   | count | printed | printed | withheld, a credential's value | withheld, a credential's value | printed | withheld, its credentials |
   | generic | printed | withheld, a generic value | withheld, a generic value | withheld, a generic value | withheld, its credentials | withheld, its credentials |
   | credential, credential member | printed | withheld, a credential's value | withheld, a credential's value | withheld, a credential's value | withheld, its credentials | withheld, its credentials |

   An object or array is *without text* when it holds no string at any depth and every member name inside it is
   printed, a fingerprint or a count and shows no credential (3e's test; `view::text_free`): a model price
   (`pay_as_you_go.request_token: {"price": 0.5}`) or a usage breakdown (`completion_tokens_details`) under a count
   name (choices 165, 171). `null` and booleans print under every class: no credential is a flag or an absence, and
   the organisation's `user_api_key_auto_create` prints on `workspaces get` as TypeScript prints it there. A number
   and the empty string are withheld under every withholding class but a count's number (choices 171, 187):
   TypeScript's `redactDeep` masks every value under a name it matches on the reads it runs on (the inventory gets
   and `audit-logs list`), whatever its type, and a numeric password or PIN under a credential name is a credential
   (`{"password": 12345678}`); a count, a lifetime or an unset period is printed by its name instead (rows 8 and 9:
   `user_api_key_count`, `user_api_key_ttl`, `user_api_key_rotation_period: ""`), as TypeScript prints it on
   `workspaces get`. Under a path rule (rule 2) a number is withheld, and so is any non-`null` audit request field
   (rule 5).

   The structural sub-rules:
   - **3c. Header maps and pairs** (choices 138, 139, 142, 159, 170, 177). A header map's (rows 15 and 16:
     `headers` and every name ending in `_headers`, so `custom_headers`, `extra_headers` and `forward_headers`)
     header names are printed and each value is read under its header's class (`names::header_class`): a safe header's (rule 5's
     list; never a credential name) by the document's rules; a name of a withholding class as that class; a name one
     of whose words is `auth`, `authorization`, `key`, `apikey`, `token`, `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `pwd`,
     `cookie`, `credential`, `credentials` or `signature` (`X-Functions-Key`, `X-Custom-Auth`; not
     `x-portkey-workspace`) as a credential; any other header as generic (withheld in place, registered only where
     it looks like a credential: `x-env: prod`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`; its `null`, boolean or number
     printed, `x-retries: 3`). A credential, credential member or count header's value is read as a credential
     name's (a header is never a usage count), so its number and its empty string are withheld and an
     eight-character number registered (`{"Authorization": 12345678}`, a pair `{"key": "password", "value":
     12345678}`; choice 187). The
     map is an object, a list of objects, header names or values, or a JSON text holding one (printed as that
     compact document when something was withheld); a list item that is a header name (`values::looks_like_header_name`:
     1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter, each part between the separators letters
     only or digits only and at most 20 long: `x-trace`, `Authorization`) is read by the document's rules
     (`names::header_item_action`, choice 177), any other item and any other string is withheld whole. A **pair** is
     an object with a `value` member and a string `key`, `name` or `header` member (a tag, a header list, a
     Kubernetes-style `env` list, a `{"header": …, "value": …}` rule): its names are printed
     (read by the string rules, never registered) and its value is read as a header's value under the strongest of
     its names (`names::Pair`); outside a header map a pair whose names are no credential header has its value read
     by these rules, so `{"key": "region", "value": "us-east"}` prints and `{"name": "OPENAI_API_KEY", "value": …}`
     is withheld in every document (choice 170).
   - **3e. Schemas** (choices 146, 150, 152). A member named `properties` whose value is an object is a JSON Schema
     property map: its member names are property names, not values. A member whose value is a schema (an object
     whose `type` is `array`, `boolean`, `integer`, `null`, `number`, `object` or `string`, or a non-empty list of
     them) is read as that property's schema: its describing members (`names::SCHEMA_KEYWORDS`: the JSON Schema
     annotation and validation keywords and the manifest's `label`, `encrypted`, `hidden`) are read by these rules,
     and under a property of any class but printed a describing string that shows a credential (a word, trimmed of
     the punctuation around it, of at least 16 characters with a digit or a symbol other than `-` and `_` that is not
     an absolute URL; a word after `Basic`, `Bearer` or `Token` that looks like a credential or a password; a private
     key) is `[withheld]` in place and not registered; its `properties` is a property map again and its subschemas
     (`names::SUBSCHEMA_KEYWORDS`) are schemas of the same property; an empty `default`, `const`, `enum` or
     `examples` (the empty string, `[]`, `{}`; `names::SCHEMA_VALUE_KEYWORDS`, `view::is_empty`) says there is no
     value and is printed under every property, as TypeScript prints it (choice 188); every other member (`default`,
     `const`, `enum`, `examples` that are not empty, anything outside the vocabulary) is a value, read under whichever of its own name and the
     property's has the stronger class (the order of the "Class" column, weakest first: printed, fingerprint,
     header map, count, generic, credential, credential member; its own on a tie). Any other member of a property map is read by
     its name. So a vendor schema catalog prints as the service sends it. A revealed audit field has no schema
     sub-rule.
   - **3f. Credentials held as text** (choices 81, 136, 138, 167, 170). A string that holds a JSON object or array
     (it starts, after whitespace, with `{` or `[` and parses) is withheld inside by rules 3 and 4 and printed as
     that withheld document (compact JSON) when anything changed, otherwise as received; a text *shaped* as one
     that serde_json cannot read (`values::looks_like_json_text`: a lone surrogate escape, a number beyond `f64`,
     nesting deeper than 128, a truncated text) is `[withheld]` whole, its string literals and bare words registered
     as strings inside a credential. A string holding a PEM private key block (`-----BEGIN `, a label containing
     `PRIVATE KEY`, `-----`: PKCS #8, RSA, EC, encrypted, OpenSSH, PGP) is withheld and registered whole under any
     name (choice 170). A member withheld whole whose value is a JSON text registers that document's credentials.
   - **3g. Registration** (choice 154: one rule, `names::registered`, read by every walker). What joins the
     `SecretSet` of a withheld value:
     - *a path rule's value* (a rule 1 or 2 path's, `names::Leaf::Path`): the whole string, each of its
       whitespace-separated words that looks like a credential, and every word after an authorization scheme
       (`Basic`, `Bearer`, `Token`, any case; never the scheme word), so the token of `{"authorization": "Bearer
       <token>"}` is withheld where it is echoed bare, however short (choices 142, 148, 161);
     - *a credential's value by its name* (a credential's, a credential member's, a count's, a credential header's or
       pair's, a fingerprint's that looks like a credential, `names::Leaf::Credential`): as a path rule's, but the
       whole string only where it can be a credential by its shape (`values::registers_whole`: it has at least 8
       characters once trimmed and is no placeholder or mask, or it carries a symbol other than the word separators
       or holds whitespace; never a date; choice 187), so `{"password": "Bearer"}` or a short `hunter2` is withheld
       in place and `Bearer` in another member prints, while a dictionary password (`dragonfly`, `sunshine`),
       `p@ss`, `hunter2x` and `correct horse battery` are registered and withheld where they are echoed (the names
       whose word-shaped values cascaded, `token_type: Bearer` and `api_key_name: production`, are row 9's and
       print);
     - *an unrevealed audit field's text* (never printed): only the credentials inside it
       (`values::unprinted_credentials`: what the text rules withhold of it, the strings of a JSON-shaped text and
       each word that looks like a credential and is no URL nor `key=value` run), never the text itself (choice
       187);
     - *a generic value* (a generic name's, a non-credential header's): only where it, or one of its words, looks
       like a credential, and a word after an authorization scheme that looks like a credential or a password
       (choices 120, 139, 141, 161);
     - *an object, an array or a JSON text* withheld whole: what 3a–3f and rule 4 withhold inside it (each by this
       rule), then every other string inside it that looks like a credential or a password, its credential-looking
       words and a word after a scheme that looks like a credential or a password; a string under a describing member
       of a schema object inside it only when it looks like a credential (choices 147, 151). So `{"credentials":
       {"user": "u", "pwd": "hunter2x"}}` registers `hunter2x`, not `u`;
     - *a member a final `*` of a path rule reaches* (a plugin's `credentials.*`): by its own name's class, any
       other as a string inside a credential (choice 153); an array item there is a credential's value;
     - *a number* (a credential name's, member's, header's or pair's, a generic name's, a path rule's or a
       container's): under a path rule's or a credential's value one of at least 8 characters, elsewhere one that
       looks like a credential (choices 171, 187), so a withheld PIN or numeric password is withheld where it is
       echoed and a withheld `2026` withholds no date;
     - *a private key*: the whole text, under any leaf (choice 170).

     A string *looks like a credential* when it has at least 16 characters, no whitespace and is not a date; a
     *date* is a whole ISO 8601 date or timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DD`, alone or followed by `T`, `HH:MM`, optional `:SS`,
     optional fractional seconds and an optional `Z` or `±HH:MM`; choice 160). It *looks like a password* when it has
     at least 8 characters, no whitespace, is not an absolute URL nor a date, and holds a symbol other than `-`, `_`,
     `.`, `/`, `:` or a part between those separators mixing letters and digits (`hunter2x`, `P@ss!word`; not
     `us-east-1`, `10.0.0.1`; choice 151). Every registered string of at least 4 characters joins the `SecretSet`,
     never one that carries the placeholder (choices 69, 144), a word that says the value is absent, unset or
     hidden (`true`, `false`, `null`, `none`, `nil`, `undefined`, `empty`, `unset`, `redacted`, any case), a word
     that names a state, a mode or an OAuth grant type (`names::MODE_WORDS`: `enabled`, `disabled`, `required`,
     `optional`, `mandatory`, `anonymous`, `unauthenticated`, `inherited`, `client_credentials`,
     `oauth2_client_credentials`, `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, `device_code`, `jwt_bearer`, `implicit`, …;
     any case, `-` and `_` ignored; choice 188) or a mask (`****`, `••••`, `xxxx`, `####`): such a value is withheld
     in place only (choice 183). Nor is a credential name's value that repeats a sibling `*_type` or `*_mode`
     member's and that the name rule reads as a credential name itself (`{"auth": "password", "auth_type":
     "password"}`, `names::repeats_a_mode`; choice 188). The one filter is
     `names::registrable` of the rules module, applied by every rules function that hands the CLI a registration, so
     what a rule says it registers is what is registered.

   The `SecretSet` (`crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs`) holds its forms as one ordered set (a form joins once, in logarithmic time, and
   is stored once) and checks a string for a form in one pass over its bytes (`carried_by` and
   `appears_in_ignoring_case`: a multi-pattern matcher, rebuilt on the first read after a form joins), so the final
   pass over a printed document is linear in its bytes, whatever the number of forms; only the fragment half of
   `taints` (a text of at least four bytes found inside a form, the §6 metadata checks and the red team, model
   security and scan views) still reads each form (choice 187).

   The rules module also holds the read-only checker of a printed document (`check::violations`, the paths of every
   value that shows what the rules withhold, and `check::withheld`, none; generic over `check::Document`, a JSON value
   view (`view::Json`, which the CLI's traversal reads shapes through too) that parses a JSON text, implemented by the
   CLI's tests for its own value and by `check.rs` for `serde_json::Value`; compiled into the CLI's test builds only
   and into the harness in every build, choice 187), which the live tier runs on every Rust-only
   read and the CLI's tests run on everything the CLI prints for the pinned documents (one per sub-rule,
   `corpus::PINNED_DOCUMENTS`), the generated ones (`corpus::planted`: a credential under every name shape of
   every withholding row and under every name of the rule-independent list `corpus::REAL_WORLD_NAMES`, in every
   container shape, never printed in json, pretty or table; choices 173, 176, 177) and the rule-independent texts
   (`corpus::REAL_WORLD_TEXTS`: `curl` lines with authorization and API-key headers, connection strings with a
   shared access signature among them, a form body, a JDBC URL, and the limits: prose that names a model after
   `token` or `basic`, a credential key set to `none`, `true` or a mask, an ODBC string with an empty password, and
   header or `key=value` text that names no credential, each with its exact printed form, what it registers and what
   must stay printed elsewhere, checked by the CLI's traversal, the harness's checker and the rules module's own
   `values::text_withheld`; choices 181, 183, 186). The corpus is test data, compiled into test builds only
   (`#[cfg(test)]` in the CLI; the harness compiles the file for the workspace's other tests), never into the binary
   (choices 182, 185). On every pinned and generated
   document as received, the values the CLI's traversal changes are exactly the paths `check::violations` names
   (`withhold::tests::corpus::the_checker_names_every_value_the_cli_changes`, choice 179), so the two traversals are held
   equal path by path. TESTING.md §5.19 says how to add a name or a sub-rule.
4. **The URL rule**: every absolute URL (`<scheme>://`) inside a string value, at its start or after other text
   (an upstream error's `connect ECONNREFUSED https://…`, prose, a leading space; choice 169), with a userinfo, a
   query or a fragment is printed with each of them replaced: `https://[withheld]@host/path?[withheld]#[withheld]`
   (`request_url` of log rows, a `custom_host` with a query; D251). A URL runs from its scheme (the letters, digits,
   `+`, `.` and `-` before `://`, from the first letter) to the next whitespace; its userinfo is everything before
   the URL's last `@`, so a password holding an unencoded `/`, `?` or `#` (an AWS secret access key) is withheld
   whole; after the host the path ends at the first `?` or `#` and the query at the first `#` (choice 168). The
   userinfo, query and fragment are registered; a userinfo read up to an `@` of a path or query (no `:` but a `/`,
   `?` or `#`: `https://social.example/@someone`) is withheld but not registered, so no host joins the
   `SecretSet`. One parser, `values::urls_in` of the rules module, serves the CLI and the live tier's check. A part that is already
   `[withheld]` (an earlier rule's, or a revealed audit field's when the shared rules read the printed rows again)
   is kept as it is and never registered, so the rule is idempotent and the placeholder never joins the
   `SecretSet` (choice 144).

   With it, the **scheme rule** (choices 177, 181): in every string value under any name, each word after an
   authorization scheme (`Basic`, `Bearer`, `Token`, any case, the punctuation around the scheme word ignored; a
   scheme joined to the header name before it with `:` or `=` and no space, `Authorization:Bearer` or
   `Proxy-Authorization:Basic`, is a scheme too), trimmed of the quotes, brackets, `,` and `;` around it, that looks
   like a credential or a password, or after `Basic` is base64 of at least 8 characters that decodes to printable
   text holding a `:` (`dXNlcjpwYXNz`), is replaced by `[withheld]` in place (`values::scheme_withheld`):
   `authentication: "Basic [withheld]"`, `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer [withheld]' https://…`, `curl -H
   Authorization:Bearer [withheld]`; prose keeps its words (`a basic introduction`, `Bearer token`). It is
   **registered** only where the text says it is a credential: after `Bearer`, after an `Authorization` header
   name (`Authorization: Token x`), or as a whole header value written with the capitalised scheme a header uses
   (`Token x`, `Basic x`; choice 183). After the English words `token` and `basic` in other prose (`token
   gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 quota exceeded`, `basic claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 routing`, the two-word label `token
   gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`) the long word is withheld in that text only, so a model id there does not withhold the
   `model` column of every other row (choices 181, 183).

   With it, the **header rule** (choice 183): in every string value under any name, a word `<name>:` (or
   `<name>:<value>` in one word) whose name is a credential header as a text writes one (shaped as a header name,
   written with a `-` or `Authorization` or `Cookie`, and a credential by the name rule or by a credential header
   word: `X-Api-Key`, `api-key`, `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`; not a count header such as
   `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`) has the value after it, trimmed of the quotes and brackets around it, replaced
   by `[withheld]` and registered when it looks like a credential or a password (`curl -H 'X-Api-Key:
   [withheld]'`, `-H "api-key:[withheld]"`, `Authorization: [withheld]` with no scheme). A scheme word after the
   name is the scheme rule's, and an absolute URL, `[withheld]` and prose naming a header (`the x-api-key:
   header`) are kept (`values::header_withheld`).

   And the **key=value rule** (choices 181, 183, 186): in every string value under any name, a `key=value` segment
   whose key the name rule classes as a credential, a generic name or a count (`values::key_value_withheld`):
   - **the key** is the run of letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` before an `=`, from its first letter
     (`--password=` reads `password`); with a space or a tab on either side of the `=` (an INI or TOML line,
     `aws_secret_access_key = …`, `password = …`) only a credential name is read, so prose (`a = b`,
     `sort key = name`, `max_tokens = 100`) keeps its words; `==` and `=>` are not a segment's `=`;
   - **the value** runs to whitespace, `;`, `&`, a closing quote or bracket, or the text's end, or is the text
     inside its quotes. A credential's value runs further: an ODBC braced value (`PWD={p@ss;w0rd};`) to its closing
     `}` (`}}` is an escaped `}`; the braces are withheld with it, the value without them registered); one whose key
     starts a `;`-separated segment (after a `;`, or first in a text that holds a `;`: a connection string) to the
     next `;`, a line break or the end, so `Server=db;User Id=sa;Password=p@ss w0rd;` prints
     `Password=[withheld];`; and one that is itself a run of `key=value` parameters (an Azure
     `SharedAccessSignature=sv=…&sig=…` in prose) to the end of its parameters (`&` does not end it), with its
     `sig` registered too;
   - **under a credential name** the value is replaced by `[withheld]` whatever it is
     (`Server=x;User Id=sa;Password=[withheld];`, `AccountKey=[withheld]`, `client_secret=[withheld]`,
     `SharedAccessSignature=[withheld]`) and registered when it looks like a credential or a password, carries a
     symbol other than `-`, `_`, `.`, `/` and `:` at any length (`abc+/==`, `p@ss`), or holds whitespace inside the
     delimiters that make it one value (its quotes, its braces, its segment). A shorter word of letters and digits
     (`auth=oauth2`, `secret=sha256`, `pwd=v2.0`, `Pwd=hunter2`), a placeholder word and a mask (`auth=none`,
     `Password=true`, `Pwd=1234`, `Pwd=****`) are withheld in that text only and never withhold `oauth2`,
     `mode: none` or `enabled: "true"` in another row (choices 183, 186);
   - **under a generic or count key** (`token=`, `key=`, `--access-token=`) the value is withheld when it looks like
     a credential or a password and registered when it looks like a credential, as rule 3b treats a generic name's
     value; **any other key** prints (`AccountName=acct`, `max_tokens=100`).

   An empty value, `[withheld]` and a scheme word (`Authorization=Bearer x`, which the scheme rule reads) are not
   withheld. A credential-named value inside a URL's query is registered on its own as well as inside the query the
   URL rule withholds: the URL rule's parts include it (`values::url_withheld`). What the text rules do not
   recognise prints: a credential under a neutral member name with no scheme, header or `key=value` around it, a
   `name: value` line (`password: hunter2x`, YAML and prose write every field so; choice 181), and a key with
   spaces around its `=` that is not a credential name (`token = …`).

   The four text rules run in that order, each on what the one before printed, as one function,
   `values::text_withheld`, which returns the printed text and everything to register; the CLI calls it once per
   string (choice 183). Model output (§19.14) gets the URL and scheme rules in that order, nothing registered
   (`values::model_output_withheld`); not the header and key=value rules, which read names inside a text as the name
   rule reads members (an answer's code sample `password=os.environ[…]` or `"api-key": os.environ[…]`). One function
   each, `values::scheme_credential_spans`, `values::header_credential_spans` and
   `values::key_value_credential_spans`, serves the CLI and the checker; the first also serves rule 3e's
   `shows_credential`.
5. **The audit-log rule** (G44, D239): `request_body`, `request_headers` and `query_params` of every audit
   record are `[withheld]`; with `--reveal-sensitive` each one that parses as a JSON object or array is
   printed as that JSON text (compact) with rules 2–4 applied inside it, and one that does not parse stays
   `[withheld]`; a field that arrives as a JSON object or array (the pinned SDK's model holds text, so only a
   future SDK could deliver one) is printed as that withheld object or array, not as text (choice 162). Inside a
   revealed field: the request and response paths of **every** operation of
   `AI_GATEWAY_SECRET_FIELDS` (API keys, providers, integrations, MCP integrations, authentication settings,
   deployments, plugins, organisation settings and secret references; all but `telemetry.filterBoundaries`, a
   data-plane read the admin audit log never records, whose `data` rule would withhold every body's `data`) plus
   rule 2's CLI additions, at its root and under its `data` member (choice 131); the 3a credential names (camelCase
   and credential words included, choice 157) at any depth
   plus the credential members `vertex_service_account_json`, `oauth_metadata`, `model_config` and `auth_config`,
   each withheld whole (with the credentials of a JSON document it holds as text registered, as in rule 3), a number
   under one too (choice 171); a `{"key"|"name": <name>, "value": …}` pair prints its names (never registered) and
   shows its value only for a safe header named below (choices 132, 170); a private key is withheld (3f); a header map (`request_headers` itself, any `headers` or
   `custom_headers` member) shows its header names and only the values of `accept`, `accept-encoding`,
   `accept-language`, `cache-control`, `connection`, `content-encoding`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `host`,
   `user-agent`, `x-request-id` and `x-portkey-provider`; a string member holding a JSON object or array is
   withheld inside by the same rules (printed as that compact document when something was withheld); the URL
   rule. So a request body of a provider or integration create or update never shows its credentials (choice
   121). The credentials of every field are registered whether or not it is shown (choice 80), each by rule 3g:
   a header value (a header map's or a non-safe pair's) as a credential header's or a generic value (choice 139),
   so the transport headers of an audit record (`x-forwarded-for`, `x-real-ip`, `x-tsg-id`,
   `x-portkey-workspace`, `x-forwarded-proto`) are withheld but never registered and the record's `client_ip`,
   `uri` and `workspace_id` stay printed (choice 138); a value under `key` or `token`, by the name rule or by a
   path that ends at one (the SDK's `key`, applied to every body, so a root `key` is not known to be an API key),
   as a generic value, so a logged `{"key": "prod"}` does not withhold every string of the listing that carries
   `prod` (choice 141); a field left `[withheld]` (unrevealed, or not JSON) is never printed, so only the
   credentials inside it are registered, never the field's text (`values::unprinted_credentials`: what the text rules
   withhold of it, the strings of a JSON-shaped text and each word that looks like a credential; choice 187).

A withheld value is printed as the string `"[withheld]"` (the D47 word; TS prints `***` or `[REDACTED]`, choice
17); `null` and booleans are printed as they are under every rule, and a number and an object or array without text
only under a count name ("Rule 3 by shape"; choices 165, 171). The rules withhold what they recognise: a bare credential under a
name no row classifies and in no recognised shape (a neutral member holding an unmarked secret) is printed, so a
new shape the service sends is a new row or sub-rule (TESTING.md §5.19), and README says so to users. Every withheld string the
rules above register (rule 3g, and each withheld URL part) of at least 4 characters joins the `SecretSet` before the
first byte is printed, so the same value elsewhere (another row, a name, an error) is `[withheld]` too (§18.20
choice 46; a shorter one is withheld in place only, choice 69); a string that carries the placeholder `[withheld]` is
never registered (choice 144), nor a placeholder word, a mode word or a mask (`none`, `true`, `disabled`, `****`;
choices 183, 188). `--reveal-sensitive` never shows a credential: it exists only on `audit-logs list` (rule 5); elsewhere it is the usage error above.
**Model output** (an inference answer and each stream event, §19.14) is not a service resource: only the URL rule
(nothing registered) and the `SecretSet` rule apply, so a logprobs `token` or an answer's words are never withheld by
name (choice 120).
The one-time credentials of §19.11 reach only their `--secret-output` file; the provider, SCIM, SSO, plugin and
header credentials of §19.12 reach only the request body.

**Debug log** (D64 extended). Every gateway command that sends requests has the debug policy `log` (§2.9):
status and headers only, never a body or a URL query (TS records request and response bodies redacted by key
name only, and prints bodies on stderr with `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG_BODY`, GW§2.12). The inference header
`x-portkey-api-key` is a credential header of the §2.9 log, recorded with the value `***` (never the key; chunk 4,
choice 101). `report` has the policy `refused` (D156, §19.15).

**Interruption** (D252; §2.5, §13.2). Reads: `Interrupted; no data was written`. A single write:
`nothing was changed` when it was not sent (a read, the token, the reservation or the prompt before it
included), `the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` when it was, and `the change was saved`
after it succeeded. The contexts of `workspaces create`, the secret writes, inference and the report are in
their sections. A signal at a confirmation prints `  Cancelled; nothing was changed.` (exit 130/143). TS exits by
the signal with nothing printed (GW§2.11), leaving an empty `--secret-output` file behind.

**Exit codes.** 0: success, a declined confirmation, an incomplete list (with its warning), a report whose
health is known (without `--strict`, or with every source complete). 1: tenant, credential, configuration,
file, HTTP, network, timeout and decode errors; a TSG mismatch; a resolution failure; a write whose outcome is
unknown or unreadable; a credential answer without a usable credential; a failed read-back after a write;
inference that ends `failed` or `incomplete`; a report with `unknown` health or `--strict` with an incomplete
source. 2: every argument check of §19 and the non-interactive confirmation refusals. 130 / 143: interrupted.

### 19.4 Workspace references

The CLI resolves a workspace reference itself (TS `resolveWorkspaceRef`, GW§3.6, with the D235 changes):
1. Read the lists of the command's planes **in order** (each `GET <plane>/workspaces[?status=archived]`, one
   read each, SDK read retries). A list that fails stops the resolution with its §6 error (exit 1; nothing is
   sent after it; TS skips a failing list silently). When a telemetry list after the data-plane one answers an
   HTTP error (the reference was no `id` or `slug` on the data-plane list), a warning follows the grant hint:
   `⚠ '<ref>' is no workspace id or slug on the data-plane list, so the admin-plane lists were read too: use the workspace slug or UUID (a display name also reads the admin-plane lists, which need the admin grant)`
   (choice 134).
2. Exact references first: the lists are read one after the other until one holds a row whose `id` or `slug`
   equals the reference exactly; that row resolves and later lists are not read. Without such a row on any list,
   a display name is matched once every list has been read: exactly one row whose `name` equals the reference
   exactly, on the first list that has one (later lists' rows with the name are not consulted); several name
   matches on that list are TS's `workspace name '<ref>' is ambiguous (<slug>, <slug>) — use a slug or UUID`
   (exit 1; a row without a slug shown `(no slug)`). So an exact slug on the admin plane is never shadowed by a
   data-plane workspace whose display name is that slug (choice 127; TS lets the first list with any match decide).
   A matched row whose `slug` is not a non-empty string (the SDK schema requires the member, so only `""` decodes)
   is `Workspace '<ref>' cannot be resolved: the matching workspace carries no slug in the list answer; nothing was sent`
   (exit 1; `workspaces get` without `; nothing was sent`; choice 128): the request would go to an empty path
   segment.
3. Nothing matched in any list: `Workspace '<ref>' was not found on the <planes>; nothing was sent`, `<planes>`
   `admin plane` (the admin lists) or `data and admin planes` (the telemetry lists; choice 71) (exit 1; TS sends
   the reference unchanged, so `scopes bind` binds a slug that does not exist, GW§3.6).
4. An incomplete list (the G39 rule: `has_more: true`, or a safe non-negative integer `total` other than its rows)
   resolves only an exact `id` or `slug`; without an exact match on any list, an incomplete list among the
   command's lists stops a name match or a miss with
   `Workspace '<ref>' cannot be resolved: the workspace list is incomplete (the API offers no continuation); use the workspace slug or UUID; nothing was sent`
   (exit 1, no write or telemetry read sent; `workspaces get`, whose detail read was sent, without
   `; nothing was sent`). A second workspace with the name may sit beyond the answer (D254, choice 119; TS resolves
   the visible row). The report applies the same rule to its source 1 (a name on a partial list resolves nothing).

| Command | Lists, in order | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaces update <ref>`, `archive <ref>`, hidden `delete <ref>`, `scopes bind --workspace <ref>` | admin active | the slug (TS: `update`/`archive` keep a UUID or slug as typed; the request path is the same workspace) |
| `telemetry cost` and every other `telemetry` leaf `--workspace <ref>` | data active, admin active, admin archived (an exact `id` or `slug` stops at its list; a display name reads all three first, choice 127) | the slug, once per invocation (TS: `cost` reads data and admin and stops at the first list with any match; the other leaves send the value unresolved, so a display name is sent as a slug, D235) |
| `workspaces get <ref>` after a 404 | the requested plane's active list | §19.5 |
| `report --workspace <ref>` | the report's own source 1 (§19.15, TS; a name on a partial list resolves nothing, D254) | — |

### 19.5 `workspaces list|ls`, `workspaces get <ref>`

**`list [--plane data|admin] [--status active|archived] [--all]`** (GW§3.1). Checks (exit 2): the `--plane` and
`--status` vocabularies, then `--all` with `--plane` or `--status`. Requests: `GET <data>/workspaces`;
`--plane admin` → `GET <admin>/workspaces`; `--status <s>` adds `?status=<s>` on the chosen plane; `--all` reads
`GET <admin>/workspaces` then `GET <admin>/workspaces?status=archived` **one after the other** (TS reads them
concurrently; choice 15) and concatenates them, active first. One read each (no pagination; G39 rule). The record
is TS `normalizeWorkspace` (`id, slug, name, icon, description, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt, isDefault, status,
scopeName`).
- pretty: the banner, the section `AI Gateway Workspaces:`, per workspace the dim id line `  <id>` (data, kept
  under `--quiet`), `    <name>  <slug>  <status>[  default]` (`unknown` for a `null` status), `    scope: <scopeName>`
  when set, and a blank line (TS bytes). Then, for a data-plane read (no `--all`, no `--plane admin`), the status
  line `  Data-plane list shows only active workspaces you are scoped to — use --plane admin or --all for the whole tenant.`
  on stderr in every format (quiet-suppressed; TS: pretty only; choice 8).
- table: TS columns `ID, Slug, Name, Status, Default, Scope` (`true`/`false`, `unknown`, `""`).
- json: the TS rows `{id, slug, name, status, isDefault, scopeName}`.

**`get <ref> [--plane data|admin]`** (GW§3.2). Checks: the `--plane` vocabulary and the ref grammar (§19.3).
Request `GET <plane>/workspaces/<ref>` (the data plane by default). On a **404** only, the ref is resolved by
exact `name` on the requested plane's active list (one read); exactly one match whose slug differs from the ref
is read once more with `GET <plane>/workspaces/<slug>`; no match is the original 404 error; several matches the
ambiguity error. TS also lists the admin plane and then re-reads on the requested plane, which cannot succeed for
a workspace found only there (choice 14). The record is TS `normalizeWorkspaceDetail` (the list record plus
`defaults`, `usageLimits` and `rateLimits` normalised to arrays, `securitySettings`, `dataPlaneSecuritySettings`,
`settings`; `scopeName` only when the detail carries `scope_name`).
- pretty: the banner, the section `Workspace Detail:`, the TS key/value block (`ID, Slug, Name, Status, Default`
  (`yes`/`no`), then `Description`, `Scope`, `Created`, `Updated` when not null, keys padded to the longest
  present), then the non-empty `Defaults:`, `Usage Limits:`, `Rate Limits:` sections, each the pretty JSON text
  (dim, not indented, `terminal_safe_lines`), and `Security Settings:` key/value lines; then `"\n"` (TS bytes).
- table: `Key │ Value` of the projection in projection order, objects and arrays as compact JSON (TS prints
  YAML for `table`, `markdown` and `csv`, D231).
- json: the projection (absent keys omitted, TS).

### 19.6 `workspaces create`, `update <ref>`, `archive <ref>` and the hidden `delete <ref>`

**`create --name <name> [--scope-name <s>] [--existing-scope] [--description <t>] [--icon <i>] [--metadata <json>] [--defaults <json>] [--users <ids>] [--usage-limits <json>] [--rate-limits <json>]`**
(GW§3.3). Checks, in order (exit 2): `--existing-scope requires --scope-name` (TS); the scope-name grammar;
`--defaults` and `--metadata` valid JSON (`--defaults must be valid JSON`, TS text, TS exit 1) and objects
(`--defaults must be a JSON object`; TS silently replaces a non-object by `{}`, D246), `--metadata` a flat map
of strings; `--usage-limits` and `--rate-limits` JSON **arrays** validated with the SDK input schemas
(`GatewayUsageLimitInputSchema`, `GatewayRateLimitInputSchema`, `Mode::Request`), else
`Invalid --usage-limits: expected a JSON array of usage-limit policies` / `Invalid --rate-limits: expected a JSON array of rate-limit policies`
(TS prints the zod issue array, quoting the input, exit 1; D233); `--users` split on commas, trimmed, empty items
dropped (TS). The body is TS `buildWorkspaceWriteRequest`: only the flags given; `defaults` = `--defaults` with
`metadata` replaced whole by `--metadata` when given (TS; choice 19); then the SDK request schema. When
`--scope-name` shares no token with `--name` (TS `scopeNameLooksUnrelated`), the warning
`  ⚠ --scope-name '<s>' shares no token with --name '<n>'. Operators find workspaces by scope in SCM Access Management; an unrelated name is easy to lose.`
goes to stderr after the checks (TS: stdout). Without `--scope-name` the scope is
`scm::airs::gateway::generate_workspace_scope_name(name)` (`ws_<stem>_<6 random [a-z0-9]>`, as TS).

Sequence (G37; each write one attempt under `writes::attempt`; IAM and admin planes):
1. unless `--existing-scope`: `POST <iam>/scopes` `{"description": <--description or "">, "name": <scope>, "resources": []}`;
2. `POST <admin>/workspaces` `{name, scope_name, description?, icon?, defaults?, users?, usage_limits?, rate_limits?}`;
3. `iam_scopes().bind_workspace(<scope>, <new slug>)`: `GET <iam>/scopes/<scope>` then
   `PUT <iam>/scopes/<scope>` with the existing resources plus `{"metadata": [], "resource_id": <slug>, "resource_type": "workspace"}`
   (an identical binding is not duplicated), under one `writes::attempt` (a 401 on the PUT replays the read and
   the PUT; the PUT is idempotent);
4. `GET <admin>/workspaces/<new id>` (the read-back).

Outcomes (stderr; the scope always named; D229):

| Step and outcome | What the CLI does and prints | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 rejected (a 409 included) | the §6 error; nothing else sent | 1 |
| 1 unknown | `Outcome unknown: the IAM scope <scope> may have been created.` / hint `Check it with 'airs gateway scopes get <scope>'; reuse it with 'airs gateway workspaces create --existing-scope --scope-name <scope> …' or delete it with 'airs gateway scopes delete <scope>'.` | 1 |
| 2 rejected (any 3xx or 4xx, a redirect included, whatever the SDK's error kind) or never sent (a local failure, such as a refused token request), scope created by step 1 | `DELETE <iam>/scopes/<scope>` (one attempt); the §6 error of step 2, then `Outcome: the workspace was not created; IAM scope <scope> was deleted again.` (delete succeeded) or `Outcome: the workspace was not created; IAM scope <scope> was created and is still present.` / hint `Delete it with 'airs gateway scopes delete <scope>' or reuse it with --existing-scope.` (delete failed or unknown) | 1 |
| 2 rejected or never sent with `--existing-scope` | the §6 error; no scope delete | 1 |
| 2 unknown | **no scope delete** (the workspace may reference it); `Outcome unknown: the workspace may have been created; IAM scope <scope> is kept.` / hint `Check 'airs gateway workspaces list --plane admin'; if the workspace exists, finish with 'airs gateway scopes bind <scope> --workspace <slug or name>'; otherwise delete the scope with 'airs gateway scopes delete <scope>'.` (TS deletes the scope after any error, a 5xx and a timeout included) | 1 |
| 2 succeeded, its answer unreadable | `Outcome: the workspace was created, but the response could not be read; IAM scope <scope> is not bound to it yet.` / the step-2-unknown hint | 1 |
| 3 rejected | `The workspace <slug> (<id>) was created, but IAM scope <scope> could not be bound to it.` / hint `Finish with 'airs gateway scopes bind <scope> --workspace <slug>'.` (TS names `iamScopes.bindWorkspace(…)`, an SDK method) | 1 |
| 3 unknown | `Outcome unknown: IAM scope <scope> may now bind workspace <slug> (<id>).` / hint `Check it with 'airs gateway scopes get <scope>'; finish with 'airs gateway scopes bind <scope> --workspace <slug>' if needed.` | 1 |
| 4 fails | the acknowledgement and the status line below, then the §6 error with `Outcome: the workspace <slug> (<id>) was created and bound to IAM scope <scope>, but reading it back failed.`; stdout empty (TS renders the create answer silently, GW§3.3; choice 26) | 1 |
| all succeed | stderr `  ✓ Workspace created: <id>` and the status line `  IAM scope <scope> created and bound to workspace <slug>. Grant that scope to the service accounts that should reach the workspace on the data plane.` (`created and ` omitted with `--existing-scope`; TS); stdout the §19.5 detail of the read-back (banner in pretty) | 0 |

Interruption: before step 1 is sent `nothing was changed`; during step 1 `the IAM scope <scope> may have been
created (outcome unknown)`; after step 1 and before step 2 is sent `IAM scope <scope> was created; the workspace
was not`; during step 2 `IAM scope <scope> was created; the workspace may have been created (outcome unknown)`;
during step 3 `the workspace <slug> was created; IAM scope <scope> may not bind it yet`; during step 4 `the
workspace <slug> was created and bound to IAM scope <scope>`. The rollback DELETE is never started after a signal.

**`update <ref> [--name] [--description] [--icon] [--metadata] [--defaults] [--usage-limits] [--rate-limits]`**
(GW§3.4). Checks: no flag is TS's
`Specify at least one of --name --description --icon --metadata --defaults --usage-limits --rate-limits` (exit 2);
the JSON flags as `create`; the body schema (`--name ''` is the D116 text, exit 2, before the tenant; TS exit 1
after a resolution read); the confirmation when the body has `defaults`, `usage_limits` or `rate_limits` (§19.3;
TS: none, although the service replaces the whole block, so `--metadata` alone replaces every default). Sequence:
the §19.4 resolution (admin), the prompt, `PUT <admin>/workspaces/<slug>` with the partial body (one attempt; its
`{}` answer ignored, TS), `GET <admin>/workspaces/<slug>`. Output: stderr `  ✓ Workspace updated: <id>` (TS),
stdout the §19.5 detail (banner in pretty). A failing read-back after the PUT: the acknowledgement, then the §6
error with `Outcome: the workspace <slug> was updated, but reading it back failed.`, stdout empty, exit 1.

**`archive <ref> [--force]`, hidden `delete <ref> [--force]`** (GW§3.5). The hidden `delete` first prints the
warning ``  ⚠ `gateway workspace delete` is deprecated because this operation archives; use `gateway workspaces archive`.``
(stderr; TS: stdout). The gate, then the prompt (before the token request: no request is open while it waits), then the §19.4
resolution (admin) and `DELETE <admin>/workspaces/<slug>` (one attempt; no verification read: an archived workspace answers
404, TS). Output: stdout empty; stderr `  ✓ Workspace archived: <ref>` (`<ref>` as typed, TS) and the status line
``  This is a soft delete — the workspace remains visible via `workspaces list --plane admin --status archived`. A `get` on it now answers 404; that is expected.``
(TS). Unknown outcome hint: `Check it with 'airs gateway workspaces list --plane admin --status archived'.`

### 19.7 `scopes`

**`list|ls`** (GW§4): `GET <iam>/scopes` (`{count, items}`, one read; G39 rule with `count`). Record
`{name, description, resources: [{resourceType, resourceId}], tsgId, id}`. pretty: the banner, the section
`IAM Scopes:`, per scope `    <name>  <type:id, type:id>` (bindings dim) or `    <name>  unbound` (yellow), the
dim description line when non-empty, a blank line (TS bytes); table TS columns `Name, Description, Bound resources,
TSG` (bindings joined `, `); json the TS rows (`resources` joined as a string, TS); empty: §19.3.

**`get <name>`**: the scope-name check, `GET <iam>/scopes/<name>`. pretty: the banner, the section `IAM Scope:`,
the TS key/value block `Name, Description ((none) dim when empty), TSG, ID, Bound resources (type:id joined, or
none — unbound yellow)`; table `Key │ Value` of the json record (TS prints YAML for table, D231); json the record
with the resource array (TS).

**`create --name <n> [--description <t>]`**: the scope-name check (D236; TS sends any name, and the SDK then
refuses to read, bind or delete it); `POST <iam>/scopes` `{"description": <t or "">, "name": <n>, "resources": []}`
(one attempt; `<thing>` `IAM scope <n>`, `<done>` `created`, hint
`Check it with 'airs gateway scopes get <n>'.`). Output: stderr `  ✓ IAM scope created: <n>` and the status
line ``  The scope is not bound to anything yet — `workspaces create --existing-scope` or `scopes bind` finishes the job.``
(TS); stdout the `get` detail of the answer (banner in pretty).

**`bind <name> --workspace <ref>`**: the checks; the §19.4 resolution (admin; the slug); then
`iam_scopes().bind_workspace(<name>, <slug>)` (`GET` then `PUT <iam>/scopes/<name>` with the existing resources
plus the workspace, under one `writes::attempt`, as §19.6 step 3); then a verification read
`GET <iam>/scopes/<name>` (D236): the binding missing from it is
`IAM scope <name> was updated, but it does not bind workspace <slug>; another change may have replaced it. Check it with 'airs gateway scopes get <name>'.`
(exit 1; the SDK's read-modify-write has no concurrency token, so a concurrent writer can win, GK§4.2). Unknown
outcome: `Outcome unknown: IAM scope <name> may now bind workspace <slug>.` with the `scopes get` hint. Output:
stderr `  ✓ IAM scope <name> now binds <n> resource(s)` (TS; `<n>` from the verification read); stdout the
detail of the verification read (banner in pretty).

**`delete|rm <name> [--force]`**: the checks and the gate; without `--force`, after the token, `GET
<iam>/scopes/<name>` (for the prompt's bound resources; a failure of this read is its §6 error, nothing deleted),
then the prompt; then `DELETE <iam>/scopes/<name>` (one attempt; a 2xx without a body accepted; the route is the
SDK's inferred one, "experimental", GK§4.2). Output: stdout empty; stderr `  ✓ IAM scope deleted: <name>` (TS).
Unknown outcome hint `Check it with 'airs gateway scopes get <name>'.` With `--force` nothing is read
first (TS parity: no binding check; choice 27).

### 19.8 `telemetry`

**Window** (D242, G41; every leaf except `cost`): `--days <n>` (default `7`), `--start <iso>`, `--end <iso>`,
`--workspace <ref>` (required, §19.4).
- `--days`: `^-?(0|[1-9]\d*)$`, safe, greater than 0, else `Invalid --days: Expected an integer`,
  `Invalid --days: Expected a safe integer`, `Invalid --days: Expected a positive integer` (TS texts).
- `--start`, `--end`: the zod `datetime({offset: true})` grammar of §17.3 (an offset or `Z` is required), else
  `Invalid --start: Expected an ISO-8601 timestamp` / `Invalid --end: …` (TS text; TS accepts anything
  `new Date` parses: `2026-10-01`, `Oct 2 2026`, a zone-less time read in the host's zone).
- `--days` given on the command line (clap's value source, so `--days 7` counts) together with `--start` is
  `Use --days or --start/--end, not both` (the report's TS text; TS ignores `--days` then, even an invalid one).
- `end` = `--end`, else the time of the check; `start` = `--start`, else `end − days × 86,400,000 ms`.
  `start` after `end`, or either outside the years 0000–9999 in UTC, is TS's
  `AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Invalid telemetry query options or time window` (exit 2, before the tenant;
  TS exit 1 after it).
- Sent as `organisationId=<mgmtTsgId>&workspaceSlug=<slug>&timeOfGenerationMin=<start>&timeOfGenerationMax=<end>`
  (TS key order, the SDK's `AIGatewayWindowOptions` with `offset_minutes` 0): `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00`,
  seconds truncated (TS: the process's local zone, `+05:30` under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`; the instants are equal).
  `filter-boundaries` omits `organisationId` (TS).

**Check order** (D232; choice 70): `group-by`'s dimension, then the window (or `cost`'s `--days`), the chart
filters, the leaf's own flags (`--columns`, the `logs` paging) and last `--workspace` (§19.3).

**Chart filters** (`cost`, `latency`, `requests`, `tokens`, `group-by`; GW§5.1): `--trace-id`, `--metadata <json>`,
`--status-codes`, `--api-key-ids`, `--ai-org-models`, `--total-units-min|max`, `--cost-min|max`, parsed and then
validated by the CLI with TS's rules (`chartFilterFields`, `validChartBounds`: non-negative safe integers, UUIDs,
`^[^,\s]+__[^,\s]+$` pairs, a string-valued metadata object without `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`,
inclusive bounds; choice 73) and then with the SDK's `AIGatewayChartFiltersSchema`
(`AIGatewayChartFilters::parse(…, Mode::Request)`); TS's two texts
`Invalid chart filters: check JSON, CSV and numeric flag syntax` and
`Invalid chart filters: check status codes, UUIDs, provider__model pairs, string metadata and inclusive nonnegative bounds`
(exit 2, before the tenant, never echoing a value; TS parity). Query keys after the window in TS order: `traceId`,
`metadata` (compact JSON), `statusCode`, `apiKeyIds`, `aiOrgModel`, `totalUnitsMin`, `totalUnitsMax`, `costMin`,
`costMax`, then `columns`; numbers in JS form (`2e1` → `20`).

**`cost --workspace <ref> [--days <n>] [filters]`** (GW§5.2; class W): `--days` and the filters (no `--start`
or `--end`, TS), the §19.4 resolution (data, admin, admin archived), `GET <data>/logs/charts/cost?<window>[&filters]`.
The record is TS's (`{workspaceSlug, days, totalCents, totalUsd, avgCents, avgUsd, quotaExceeded, records:
[{date, costCents, costUsd}]}`, cents from the API, `*Usd` = cents / 100 as a JS number). pretty: the banner,
`"\n  Cost — <slug> (last <d>d):\n\n"` (bold section), `  Total          $<t>`, `  Daily average  $<a>`, the
`Per day:` section and its `  <date>  $<c>` rows, `"\n"`; dollars are JS `(cents / 100).toFixed(2)` (the exact
binary value rounded half away from zero, ported, not Rust's `{:.2}`; choice 11). The TS stdout line
`  ⚠ Telemetry quota exceeded — data may be truncated` becomes the stderr warning below (D230). table:
`Key │ Value` of the record, `records` as compact JSON (TS); json: the record.

**Metric reads** (class D; `runDetail`, GW§5.3), each after the §19.4 resolution:

| Leaf | Request (`GET <data>…`) |
|---|---|
| `errors`, `users`, `error-trends`, `error-category-trends`, `grouped-errors`, `rescued-retries`, `user-trends` | `/logs/charts/<leaf>` |
| `cache summary`, `cache trend` | `/logs/charts/cache-summary`, `/logs/charts/cache-hit-trend` |
| `feedback distribution`, `models`, `trend`, `weighted` | `/logs/charts/feedback-score-distribution`, `feedback-models`, `feedback-trend`, `feedback-weighted` |
| `latency`, `requests`, `tokens` | `/logs/charts/<leaf>` + filters |
| `filter-boundaries` | `/analytics/filter-boundaries` (no `organisationId`); `data` withheld (§19.3 rule 1) |
| `group-by <dimension> [--columns c1,c2]` (+ filters) | `/logs/groups/<ai_service\|model\|api_key\|provider>`, `/logs/groups/status_code`, `/logs/groups/users` |
| `logs list\|ls [--page-size <n>] [--current-page <n>] [--status-code <code>] [--trace-id <id>]` | `/logs?<window>&pageSize=<n>&currentPage=<n>[&traceId=…][&statusCode=…]` |

`group-by` checks (TS texts, exit 2): `Invalid grouping dimension: choose from ai_service, model, api_key, provider, status_code, users`,
`User grouping does not support --columns`,
`Invalid --columns: choose from cost, avg_latency, avg_tokens, total_tokens, success_rate, last_seen`. `logs list`
checks (TS texts): `Invalid --page-size: Expected a positive integer` (default `50`),
`--current-page must be a nonnegative safe integer` (default `0`), `Invalid --status-code: Expected a positive integer`
(TS refuses `0`), `--trace-id` non-blank (`--trace-id cannot be empty`), at most 4,096 bytes, no control character
(`--trace-id must be at most 4096 bytes and contain no control characters`; the SDK bound); an empty `--status-code`
or `--trace-id` sends nothing (TS, falsy; choice 72). One page per invocation; after it the status line `  Returned <n> of <total> request logs (page <p>, <size> per page); this is one page.`
when the answer's `total` is a safe integer larger than `p × size + n` (stderr, quiet-suppressed).

Output: the response envelope through the generic detail renderer (pretty and table the TS `Field │ Value` table of
its top level, `data` as compact JSON; json the envelope; choice 9), after the withholding policy (log rows: the
credential-name and URL rules, D251). When the envelope's `data.isQuotaExceeded` (or a top-level
`is_quota_exceeded`) is `true`, the warning `  ⚠ Telemetry quota exceeded — data may be truncated` goes to stderr
(never suppressed) for every telemetry leaf, `cost` included (TS: only `cost`, on stdout). Numbers are printed as
the server sent them.

### 19.11 One-time credentials (`--secret-output`)

`api-keys service|user create`, `api-keys service|user rotate <id>`, `deployments create` and a
`deployments update <id>` whose body has `rotate_auth: true` mint credentials the service shows once (`key`;
`client_auth` and `credentials.password`). Their only channel is `--secret-output <path>` (D237; the D204 pattern).

**Arguments** (before the tenant, in the §19.3 order; choices 88, 124): during planning the `--show-secret` refusal and
the §19.3 destination rule, the id check (`rotate`, `update`), the flags (`create`'s `--organisation-id` and
`--workspace` checks) and the refusal of a `rotate` without `--force` in non-interactive mode; after the debug log
the body (named flags, `--file`, `--set`; `rotate --transition-ms <ms>` → `{"key_transition_period_ms": <ms>}`
with the refinement; `create`'s defaults), the body-dependent destination rule of `deployments update` and the
body-dependent refusal. So `rotate <id> --transition-ms 5` without `--secret-output` is the destination error, where
TypeScript (which has no destination rule) prints the refinement. **Paths** (after the debug
log, before the tenant; exit 1): anything at the path (`lstat`, a dangling symlink included) is
`<path> already exists; choose another --secret-output` (`files::refuse_existing`); a parent that is missing or not
a directory, or a last component that is not a file name (D226), is
`Cannot write <path>; check that its directory exists and is writable` (`files::check_new`; TS opens the path with
`wx` and echoes the OS error, `EEXIST: file already exists, open '<path>'`).

**Sequence.** The tenant, credentials, the TSG comparison, the client, the prompt (`rotate` and a rotating
`update`), the **reservation** (`files::Reservation`: `.airs-<16 hex>.tmp` beside the path, `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`,
0600; a failure is the `Cannot write <path>; …` message and nothing is sent), the token, then the G36 raw write
(one attempt): `POST <data>/api-keys/<kind>`, `POST <data>/api-keys/<kind>/<id>/rotate`,
`POST <admin>/deployments`, `PUT <admin>/deployments/<id>`.

**The answer** (G36; a 2xx body parsed as one JSON object):
1. The credential members (`key`; or `client_auth` and `credentials.password`) that are non-empty strings are added
   to the `SecretSet`; when at least one is present, the **whole answer object** (TS writes the whole response) is
   written to the reservation as pretty JSON (sorted keys) + `\n`, `fsync`ed and linked to the path (never
   overwriting), the temporary unlinked, the directory `fsync`ed (the §3.9 warning on failure). Then the rest is
   validated with the operation's response schema in `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults`.
2. **Success**: stderr `  ✓ <Service|User> API key created: <id>` (`rotated`), `  ✓ Deployment registered: <id>`
   or `  ✓ Deployment authentication rotated: <id>`, then
   `  ✓ Wrote the one-time credential to <path> (mode 0600); it is shown only once.`; stdout the TS result
   `{"saved_to": "<path as typed>"}` (pretty and table `Field │ Value`, `saved_to │ <path>`; TS bytes).
3. Saved, but the rest invalid: `AISEC_RESPONSE_VALIDATION:Response did not match the expected schema` with the one
   detail line `Outcome: the <thing> was <done> and its one-time credential was saved in <path>, but the rest of the response could not be read.`
   (no hint; exit 1, stdout empty), after any durability warning (as §18.20 choice 75).
4. No credential member in an otherwise valid answer: the reservation removed;
   `The service <done> <thing> <id> but returned no one-time credential; nothing was written to <path>.` with the
   hint of the table below (exit 1).
5. A body that is not a JSON object: the §19.3 unreadable line and the hint; the reservation removed.
6. The link loses a race or fails: the temporary is **kept**,
   `The <thing> was <done>, but <path> now exists; the credential is in <temporary path> (mode 0600). Move it before running again.`
   (or `… because <path> could not be written. …`), exit 1; a part-way write failure removes the temporary with
   `The <thing> was <done>, but its credential could not be written to <path>; <remedy>.`; a whole write whose
   `fsync` alone fails is linked with the warning `⚠ <path> was saved, but it could not be synced; the credential may not survive a system crash`
   (§18.20 choices 49, 67).
7. A failed write (no 2xx): the reservation removed; the §19.3 lines.

| Command | `<thing>` / `<done>` | Hint after an unknown or unreadable outcome, or a missing credential |
|---|---|---|
| `api-keys <kind> create` | `<kind> API key` / `created` | `Check 'airs gateway api-keys <kind> list --workspace <uuid>' before creating another key; revoke a key whose credential was not saved.` |
| `api-keys <kind> rotate <id>` | `<kind> API key <id>` / `rotated` | `The old key stops working after its transition period; check 'airs gateway api-keys <kind> get <id>' and rotate it again to obtain a usable credential.` |
| `deployments create` | `deployment` / `registered` | `Check 'airs gateway deployments list'; a registration whose credentials were not saved needs 'airs gateway deployments update <id> --rotate-auth true --secret-output <new file>'.` |
| `deployments update <id>` (rotating) | `deployment <id> authentication` / `rotated` | `Its old credentials may no longer work; rotate it again with --secret-output <new file> to obtain usable ones.` |

TypeScript prints every credential with `--show-secret` on stdout, writes it unreservedly with `--secret-output`
(an empty 0600 file stays after SIGINT, GW§2.11), and loses it when a 2xx answer fails its schema or after a
replay mints several (GW§2.6).

**Interruption.** Before dispatch: `nothing was changed` (the reservation removed). After dispatch, before the
answer: `the change may already have been applied (outcome unknown)` (the reservation removed: it holds nothing).
From a 2xx answer on, until the file is linked or a temporary kept:
`the <thing> was <done>, but its credential was not saved; <remedy>`; once an answer with a credential was read, the
file is completed before the signal is acted on, then `Interrupted; the one-time credential was saved in <path>`.

### 19.12 Provider, organisation and plugin credentials (inputs)

**`integrations create`** (GW§6.6): `--ai-provider <slug-or-uuid>` or `--ai-provider-id <uuid>` (both:
`Use --ai-provider or --ai-provider-id, not both`, TS), `--base-url <url>` (an absolute http or https URL, else TS's
`Invalid --base-url: AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:custom host must use http or https` /
`…must be an absolute http(s) URL including its API prefix`; sets `configurations.provider_auth_type = "apiKey"`
and `configurations.custom_host` through the SDK's `custom_host_configuration`), `--header <name=value>`…
(`configurations.custom_headers`), `--configurations <json>`, `--description`, `--name`, `--organisation-id`
(default the tenant TSG), `--secret-mappings <json>`, `--slug`, and one credential source (D247):
- `--key <credential>`: accepted with the warning
  `  ⚠ Inline --key is visible in shell history and process listings; prefer --key-stdin, --key-file, or --secret-mappings`
  (TS text, stderr, never suppressed);
- `--key-file <path>`: an **input** (TS name; not the D204 output): the §13.2 input rules with a 64 KiB cap, UTF-8,
  one trailing `\n` or `\r\n` removed; empty, multi-line or NUL is TS's
  `--key-file must contain exactly one nonempty credential`; unreadable is `Cannot read --key-file <path>` (TS, no OS
  text);
- `--key-stdin`: the §3.10 piped-stdin rules (64 KiB, UTF-8, one trailing newline, no CR/LF/NUL); on a terminal it is
  `--key-stdin reads one credential from piped stdin, e.g. 'airs gateway integrations create ... --key-stdin < provider.key'; in a terminal, omit every key flag to be prompted`
  (TS text with the program name; TS falls back to a prompt);
- several sources: `Use only one of --key, --key-stdin, or --key-file` (TS);
- none, with stdin and stderr terminals, no `--secret-mappings` and no `--file`: the §3.10 hidden prompt
  `? Provider API key: [input is masked] ` (after the debug log, before the tenant).

Without a credential (`key` or a non-empty `secret_mappings`) after the body is built:
``A provider credential is required: run in a terminal to be prompted, or pass --key-file, --key-stdin (piped), --secret-mappings, or --key (the gateway rejects a credential-less integration with a generic AB01)``
(TS text, exit 2, before the tenant and before the catalog request; TS checks it after building the client and
reading the catalog). Every credential read joins the `SecretSet`.

Provider resolution (G38): a UUID `--ai-provider` is lowercased and used without a request (TS); a slug is matched,
after the token and before the POST, against `GET <admin>/utils/static-resources/ai-providers` (one read, ASCII
case-insensitive, trimmed); no match is
`Unknown provider '<slug>'[; did you mean <a>, <b>?] (list slugs with 'airs gateway integrations providers')`
(exit 1, nothing written; at most 5 suggestions by alphanumeric containment, TS rule, through `terminal_safe`; TS
names the SDK method `integrations.catalog()`, D73).

**`integrations update <id>`**: the shared flags (`--base-url`, `--configurations`, `--description`, `--header`, the
three key sources, `--name`, `--secret-mappings`); never prompts (TS); a body carrying a credential confirms
(§19.3).

**Inline secret flags** (D247): `--scim-token <token>` (`auth-settings update`), `--credential <key=value>`
(`plugins create`) and `--header <name=value>` (`integrations create|update`) are accepted with the warning
`  ⚠ Inline --<flag> is visible in shell history and process listings; prefer a --file request body (mode 0600)`
(stderr, never suppressed; TS warns only for `--key`). Their values, the `--key*` credentials, every
`--configurations`/`--auth-settings` value under a §19.3 path or credential name, and every such value of a `--file`
body join the `SecretSet` during planning; they are sent only in the request body and never echoed (D233).

### 19.13 `admin-guardrails` (admin plane)

- `list|ls [--workspace <uuid>] [--page-size <1–1000>] [--current-page <n>]`: TS's parse-time checks
  (`--page-size must be an integer from 1 to 1000`, `Expected an integer`; `--current-page` 0 to 2^53 − 1), the
  `workspaceId` check (TS prints a raw zod issue array, exit 1); `GET <admin>/guardrails?workspace_id=…&page_size=…&current_page=…`
  (only the given keys, TS order; an explicit page 0 is sent); one page; label `Admin guardrails` (TS); the status
  line `  Returned <n> of <total> admin guardrails (page <p>); this is one page.` when `total` says more exist: `total`
  is a safe non-negative integer larger than `p × s + n`, `p` the given `--current-page` (else 0), `s` the given
  `--page-size` (else `n`, the rows of this page, as the service's default size is unknown) (choice 83). The
  `--current-page` range text is `--current-page must be an integer from 0 to 9007199254740991` (TS).
- `get <id>` → `GET <admin>/guardrails/<id>`.
- `create [--name] [--checks <json>] [--actions <json>] [--target llm|mcp_tools] [--workspace <uuid>] [--organisation <uuid>]`
  → `POST <admin>/guardrails` (the admin schema; no LLM refinement, TS); `update <id> [--name] [--checks] [--actions]`
  → `PUT <admin>/guardrails/<id>`; `delete|rm <id>` (confirms) → `DELETE <admin>/guardrails/<id>`.
- `mcp-servers list|ls <guardrail-id>` → `GET <admin>/guardrails/<id>/mcp-servers` (an array or `{data: […]}`, label
  `MCP mappings`); `sync <guardrail-id>` (structured input only; confirms) → `PUT …/mcp-servers` (replaces every
  mapping); `upsert <guardrail-id> <server-id>` (`{run_on?, mcp_integration_capability_ids?}`) →
  `PUT …/mcp-servers/<server-id>` (does not confirm; choice 29).

Built in chunk 3 (§19.6–§19.13; `src/gateway/{body,writes,provision,provider,secrets}.rs`,
