### 19.14 `inference chat|responses|embeddings [prompt]` (chunk 4)

**Never live** (billed model calls). Options (GW§8.1): `--model <id>`, `--endpoint <url>`, `--file <path>` (a JSON
request file), `--timeout <ms>` (default `60000`), and `--stream`, `--max-tokens <n>` (`chat`, `responses`) or
`--dimensions <n>`, `--encoding <format>` (`embeddings`).

**Checks** (exit 2, before the tenant, TS texts unless marked): `Pass a prompt or --file, not both`;
`A prompt or --file is required`; `--max-tokens must be a positive integer`; `--dimensions` a positive safe integer
(`--dimensions must be a positive integer`, Rust); `--encoding` `float` or `base64`
(`--encoding must be float or base64`, Rust; TS: a schema error after the tenant); `--timeout must be a positive integer`
(a safe integer); `--stream` with `--output table` is
`Streaming supports --output pretty or json (JSONL), not table` (TS's yaml text, D50); `--endpoint` admitted by §5
(https, or http on a loopback host, no userinfo, query or fragment), else TS's
`AISEC_USER_REQUEST_PAYLOAD_ERROR:Inference endpoint requires HTTPS (HTTP is allowed only on loopback), without credentials, query or fragment`
(the value is never echoed). Then `--file` with the §13.2 input rules (1 MiB, one JSON object; TS's
`--file must name a readable JSON request file` and `--file must contain a JSON object`, no content echoed).

**Body** (TS `inferenceBody`, GW§8.2): a prompt makes `chat` `{"messages": [{"content": <prompt>, "role": "user"}]}`
and the others `{"input": <prompt>}`; `--file` is the base; `model` = `--model`, else the file's `model`, else the
tenant's `gatewayInferenceModel` (`gatewayEmbeddingModel` for `embeddings`); `--stream` adds `"stream": true`;
`--max-tokens` sets `max_completion_tokens` (`chat`) or `max_output_tokens` (`responses`); `--dimensions` and
`--encoding` set `dimensions` and `encoding_format`; `responses` sends `"store": false` unless the body sets
`store` (TS). The body is validated with the SDK input schema in `Mode::Request` once its model is known (the D116 text naming
`POST /chat/completions`, `/responses` or `/embeddings`): before the tenant, exit 2, when `--model` or the file names the
model; after the tenant, exit 1 and no request, when the model is the tenant's. A model that is
still missing after the tenant is read is `Set --model, the request model, or gatewayInferenceModel in the tenant (gatewayEmbeddingModel for embeddings)`
(exit 1, after the tenant, no request; TS exit 2 with `… or the matching inference model config`).

**Client** (`clients::GatewayRuntime::build`, D240, G48): the endpoint is `--endpoint`, else the tenant's
`gatewayInferenceEndpoint` (admitted by §5, the D48 message naming the key); the key is the tenant's
`gatewayInferenceApiKey`, wrapped in `Secret`, registered in the `SecretSet`, non-empty and without CR or LF.
Missing values are
`gatewayInferenceEndpoint is not configured; set it with 'airs tenant set <tenant> gatewayInferenceEndpoint <url>' or pass --endpoint`
and `gatewayInferenceApiKey is not configured; set it with 'airs tenant set <tenant> gatewayInferenceApiKey' (secrets prompt hidden, or use --stdin)`
(exit 1, after the tenant, no request). **No environment variable is read**: TS falls back to
`PANW_AI_GW_INFERENCE_ENDPOINT` and `PANW_AI_GW_INFERENCE_API_KEY` (captured, GW§8.2). Management credentials are not
needed (TS). `Authentication::runtime_key`, `RuntimeClient::new`; a construction failure of the client is
`AISEC_SDK_ERROR:The gateway runtime client could not be configured` (exit 1, no request; `clients::runtime_client`).

**Requests** (GW§8.3): `POST <endpoint>/chat/completions`, `/responses` or `/embeddings`, headers
`x-portkey-api-key: <key>` and `content-type: application/json` only (no `Authorization`, no `x-tsg-id`, no OAuth),
one attempt (`RuntimeReplay::Never`, no 401 replay), redirects are errors, `--timeout` the deadline of the whole
request including the stream (`ContractStream::next` under the same options). The streaming calls are
`create_chat_completion_stream` (`[DONE]`-terminated) and `create_response_stream` (ends on `response.completed`,
`response.failed` or `response.incomplete`).

**Output** (stdout; D241):
- Non-streaming `pretty`: `chat` the `choices[].message.content` texts joined, `responses` the `output[].content[]`
  parts of type `output_text` joined, then `\n` (an answer without text prints `\n`), through
  `output::terminal_safe_lines` (line breaks and tabs kept; TS writes model text raw); `embeddings` the pretty JSON
  of the answer. `table`: `Key │ Value` of the answer's top level (Rust-only). `json`: the answer (C1 escaped).
- Streaming `pretty`: each event's text as it arrives (`choices[].delta.content`, `response.output_text.delta`),
  then `\n` at the end; streaming `json`: one compact JSON event per line (JSONL; `[DONE]` not echoed). Streamed text
  is written as it arrives (the one exception to §2.2's single commit); a secret of the `SecretSet` split across two
  deltas is still withheld: pretty holds back the last (longest secret form − 1) characters until the next delta or
  the end (as D199); json (`gateway::inference::StreamEvents`) holds a whole event while the text of the held events
  ends with the start of a registered form, and when the next event completes a form the text of every held event
  (`choices[].delta.content`, a `response.output_text.delta`'s `delta`) is `[withheld]` before they are printed; held
  events are released at the end, before a failure line and before a failed event (choice 123). Every answer and
  event goes through the model-output policy of §19.3 (no credential-name rule).
- An answer or terminal event whose status is `failed` or `incomplete`: the text so far (pretty: without the final
  `\n`), then `Gateway generation ended with <status>` (`response.failed`, `response.incomplete` for a stream; TS
  text), exit 1.
- A closed stdout is §2.2's rule (TS: exit 0 on `EPIPE`); provider errors are §6 messages (TS prints the provider's
  `error.message`, GW§2.6).
- The tenant `defaultOutput` is honoured (TS); with `--stream` a `defaultOutput` of `table` is
  `The tenant's defaultOutput table cannot stream; pass --output pretty or --output json` (exit 1, after the tenant,
  no request; choice 41).

**Interruption** (D241): before the request is sent `Interrupted; nothing was sent`; after it was sent
`Interrupted; the model request was sent and may have been processed (and billed)`; the stream is closed
(`ContractStream::close`) before exit; streamed text already written stays on stdout. Exit 130/143 (TS: `✗ Error:
Inference interrupted`, exit 1).

**Secrets.** The key is sent only as `x-portkey-api-key`, never printed and never recorded in the debug log (§19.3).
Prompts and model output are never written to stderr, an error, the debug log or a summary.

Built in chunk 4 (`src/gateway/inference.rs` the body, the text, the terminal statuses and the stream writer;
`src/commands/gateway_inference.rs` planning and the run; `clients::GatewayRuntime`; `tests/gateway_inference.rs`,
`tests/parity_gateway_inference.rs`):
- **Planning** (before the debug log and the tenant, in this order): the prompt or `--file`, `--max-tokens`,
  `--dimensions` (decimal digits only, positive and safe; TS's `Number()` accepts `1e3`, `0x10` and spaces; choice 103),
  `--encoding`, `--timeout`, `--stream` with an explicit `--output table`, `--endpoint` (§5; the TS text, never the value;
  §5 also admits `127.0.0.0/8`, choice 109).
- **Dispatch, before the tenant**: `--file` (the TS texts, exit 2; nothing of the file echoed), the body, a body whose
  `stream` is `true` (from `--stream` or the file, choice 107) with an explicit `table` refused, and, when `--model` or
  the file names the model, the SDK schema (the D116 text, exit 2). A `--model` or file `model` that is not a non-blank
  string is the model text (exit 2, choice 102).
- **Dispatch, after the tenant**: the format (the tenant `defaultOutput`; a streaming `table` default is exit 1), the
  tenant's model and the schema check (exit 1), the endpoint, the key (blank or absent: the not-configured text; with a
  CR or LF: `Invalid gatewayInferenceApiKey: it must be a nonempty header value on one line`, exit 1, choice 104), then
  the one request. The interrupt context is `nothing was sent` until the request is built and `the model request was sent
  and may have been processed (and billed)` from then on.
- **Output**: pretty model text replaces each registered secret in place (`[withheld]`) and goes through
  `terminal_safe_lines`; json, table (`Key │ Value`) and the pretty embeddings JSON go through the §19.3 withholding
  policy (choice 106). A non-streamed `failed`/`incomplete` answer prints its text with its newline, then the error; a
  streamed failure prints the text so far without it (TS; choice 105). Streamed text is committed chunk by chunk; a
  closed stdout ends the command quietly, exit 0 (§2.2's EPIPE rule; choice 108); the stream is closed before the
  command returns, also after an error.

### 19.15 `report|dashboard` (the gateway environment report; chunk 4)

The TypeScript collector (`src/reports/aigateway.ts`, GR§6–§7) and renderer (`environment-render.ts`, GR§8.1) are
ported unchanged except for the format (D155), the debug refusal (D156), G7, the query offsets (G41), the time
parsing, the window bounds, the destination parent (D214) and the file name (D227; D249). The report is already safe
in TypeScript (aggregates only, no-clobber, 0600, CSP).

**Argument checks** (exit 2, in TS order, before the tenant and any request; GR§3): clap's missing `--workspace`
(D1; TS exit 1); 1. `--debug` (policy `refused`): `Disable --debug for environment reports to avoid persisting sensitive traffic content`
(D156); 2. `--output` given: `The environment report is written as HTML; omit --output` (D155; TS
`Report output must be html or markdown`); 3. `--workspace cannot be empty` (blank under JavaScript trim; the value
is otherwise used untrimmed, TS); 4. `--days must be a positive integer` (`^[1-9][0-9]*$`, safe; checked even with
`--start`, TS); 5. `--start and --end must be supplied together` (an empty value counts as absent, TS);
6. `Use --days or --start/--end, not both` (`--days` given on the command line, its value source; `--days 1` counts,
TS); 7. the window `Provide a valid increasing ISO-8601 window with timezone`: with `--start`, both match the zod
`datetime({offset: true})` grammar (§17.3; uppercase `Z`, `±HH:MM` or `±HHMM`, real calendar dates, `24:00` and
`:60` refused), both are valid instants (`+24:00` refused), milliseconds kept and further digits truncated,
`start < end`; without it `end` = the time of the check and `start` = `end − days × 24 h`; in both cases a `start`
before `0000-01-01T00:00:00Z` or an `end` after `9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z` is refused with the same text (TS accepts
`--days 100000000`, then every telemetry source fails, GR§4.2; D249); 8. `--max-pages must be an integer from 1 to 100`;
9. `--title must contain 1–240 characters` (UTF-16 units, blank under trim refused); 10. `--output-file cannot be empty`.
The window is fixed here.

**Destination** (§15.17, §18.14): `--output-file -` is stdout; otherwise `--output-file`, else
`airs-gateway-report-<UTC ISO time with ':' → '-'>-<first 8 hex of a v4 UUID>.html` in the working directory (TS
`airs-aigateway-report-…`, D227), made absolute. Before the tenant: a last component that is not a file name (D226),
anything at the path (`lstat`, a dangling symlink included) and a parent that is not an existing directory (D214
extended; TS reads all 25 sources first, GR§5) are the failure line (exit 1, no request).

**Collection.** The client (`GatewayClients::build`, no upfront token: a token failure is a failure of each source,
GR§10), then the status line `  Collecting AI Gateway statistics and current configuration (read-only)...` (TS),
then the 25 sources of GR§6.1 **in TS order, one after the other**, each under its own budget (§19.3; the G7 re-read
after an `Http` 401 or 403 `Rejected`, which also repeats an OPA-denied 403 TypeScript sends once, harmless for a
read):

| # | Source / method | Window label | Request |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `workspaces.list` | `Current active tenant workspaces (admin)` | `GET <admin>/workspaces` |
| 2–18 | `telemetry.<m>`, `m` in `requests, errors, users, cost, latency, tokens, cacheSummary, cacheHitTrend, userTrends, errorTrends, errorCategoryTrends, groupedErrors, rescuedRetries, feedbackTrend, feedbackWeighted, feedbackScoreDistribution, feedbackModels` | `Displayed telemetry window` | `GET <data>/logs/charts/<kebab m>?<window>` |
| 19 | `telemetry.filterBoundaries` | `Displayed telemetry window` | `GET <data>/analytics/filter-boundaries?workspaceSlug=…&timeOfGenerationMin=…&timeOfGenerationMax=…` |
| 20 | `telemetry.logs` | `Displayed telemetry window` | `GET <data>/logs?<window>&pageSize=50&currentPage=<p>`, `p` = 0, 1, … up to `--max-pages` pages |
| 21–23 | `configs.list`, `apiKeys.listService`, `apiKeys.listUser` | `Current selected workspace configuration` | `GET <data>/configs?workspace_id=<uuid>`, `/api-keys/service?…`, `/api-keys/user?…` |
| 24 | `organisations.getInfo` | `Current tenant configuration` | `GET <admin>/organisations/<mgmtTsgId>/info` |
| 25 | `guardrails.getCatalog` | `Current tenant capability catalog (not enabled guardrails)` | `GET <admin>/utils/static-resources/schema?resource=guardrails` |

The window query is the §19.8 form (UTC `+00:00`, seconds; G41). The collector is TS's verbatim over the JSON of each
answer (GR§6.1–§6.8): the source wrapper and its two notes
`HTTP <code>: request failed; check access and service availability.` (an integer status 400–599) and
`Request, scope or response validation failed; upstream details omitted.`; `envelope` and the quota note
`Quota exceeded or quota state unknown; aggregates may be incomplete.` (once per call); `list` and
`List is truncated or total differs; continuation is not documented.`; the workspace match (exact `id` or `slug`,
else exact `name`; zero or several make source 1 `partial` and every workspace-bound source `unavailable` without a
request); the chart field rules (`null` kept, finite numbers, non-negative except feedback, integers except the
fractional fields), the `Error categories` rows and the three findings in TS order, the `Error timeline` rows; the
filter-boundary counts (never the values); the log page loop with its checks (stable total, at most 50 records, a

status code, the premature-empty-page and budget rules, the note
`Transaction page budget reached. Increase --max-pages to collect the remaining rows.`) and the coverage rows always
written; the inventory rows (`Rows returned`, `Configured limit categories`, `Available evaluators`); one
`Incomplete evidence: <name>` finding per incomplete source after the error-category findings (**not sorted**, TS);
health (`unknown` when no `telemetry.*` source is complete, `telemetry.logs` included). Times (`created_at`, the
`groupedErrors` bucket `x`) are read with `report::parse_iso` plus the date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` form as UTC midnight
(§18.20 choice 52); a zone-less or other form is not a valid time (TS reads zone-less and RFC-2822-like forms in the
host's zone; D249). Only aggregates are kept: no workspace name, slug or id, key, user, model, URL, metadata,
filter-boundary value, catalog entry or server text.

**Model and rendering.** `{schema 1, product "Prisma AIRS AI Gateway", window label "Telemetry window (UTC)", the
footer label "AI Gateway", title, collectionStartedAt, generatedAt, window (ISO with milliseconds, Z), health, sources,
findings, tables, limitations}` with the six tables and notes of GR§7 (`Telemetry metrics`, `Error categories`,
`Error timeline`, `Current configuration and capabilities`, `Transaction coverage`, and the renderer's `Evidence and

cells, numbers through `render::js_number` (`-0` → `0`, `1e+21`, `1e-7`), one trailing `\n`. The Markdown renderer
is not ported (D155). `--title` is written as given (escaped for HTML; control characters kept: the document is data,
TS parity; choice 49).

**The shared renderer** (`src/report/html.rs`, generalised in this chunk; choice 50). `html::render(report, profile)`
takes an `html::Profile { product, window_label, footer_label, limitations }`: `RED_TEAM` (`Prisma AIRS AI Red Teaming`,
`Scan creation window (UTC)`, `Red Team`, the product and labels moved from `html.rs`, and a reference to the seven red
team limitations, which stay in `report/mod.rs` as `report::LIMITATIONS`), `GATEWAY` (above; its limitations are

team and runtime reports stay byte-identical: their parity and unit tests are unchanged and must stay green.

**Publishing and exit** (§15.17): stdout delivery writes the document as the stdout data (a closed pipe is the
failure line, exit 1; TS crashes with a Node stack trace, GR§9); a file goes through `files::publish_new`, then

(stderr, red, never suppressed), exit 1. The tenant `defaultOutput` is ignored (TS). Interrupt contexts:

### 19.16 doctor `Gateway API` (chunk 4)

The eighth check, after `Management OAuth` (§9; D19, D250; TS's tenth check `AI Gateway API`, GR§14, renamed per
MILESTONES):
- **Gating**: `skip` / `skipped — management credentials not configured` when `Management credentials` did not pass;
  notEvaluated when it was not evaluated, and when `Management OAuth` failed at the token request (the probe would
  repeat the same token failure; TS requests a second token) or could not build its client (choice 100).
- **Probe**: the `GatewayClients` data client with the same OAuth provider as `Management OAuth` (one token for both
  probes), `workspaces().list(&Default::default(), …)` = `GET <gatewayDataEndpoint>/workspaces` (no query,
  `Authorization: Bearer`, `x-tsg-id`), `with_retries(0)` (D49: no 429/5xx retry, no 401/403 refresh and replay),
  within its own 5 s budget; a cancel is `Interrupted` with nothing written.
- **Outcomes** (detail / hint; `<message>` is `error::facts_message`, §6, never server text):

| Case | Status | Detail | Hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2xx | pass | `endpoint reachable (<n> workspace[s] in scope)` (TS; `0 workspaces`, `1 workspace`) | — |
| HTTP 403 | warn | `endpoint reachable, but access denied (HTTP 403): <message>` (TS) | the data-plane grant text of §19.3 without `⚠ 403: ` and with a capital first letter, whatever the service code (the probe reads only the data plane) |
| HTTP 429 | warn | `endpoint reachable, but rate limited (HTTP 429): <message>` | `Retry later` |
| HTTP 5xx | fail | `gateway API error (HTTP <s>): <message>` | `Retry later; check the AIRS service status` |
| other HTTP (401, 404, …) | fail | `gateway API error (HTTP <s>): <message>` | `Verify the tenant credentials and network connectivity` (TS) |
| a 2xx that does not decode or is over a size limit | fail | `gateway API error: <message>` | `Fix gatewayDataEndpoint in the tenant file` |
| transport | fail | `network unreachable: <message>` | `Check network connectivity, proxy settings, and DNS` |
| deadline, no HTTP status received | fail | `timed out after 5000ms — network unreachable or endpoint not responding` (TS) | `Check network connectivity and the gatewayDataEndpoint setting` |
| `gatewayDataEndpoint` inadmissible (§5) | fail | the D48 message | `Fix gatewayDataEndpoint in the tenant file` |

TS retries a 5xx into its 5 s timeout and reports `timed out`, warns only on 403, reports a malformed 2xx as
`network unreachable`, names `api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com` in its hint and prints the token response's
`error_description` (GR§14.3). JSON, table and pretty rendering are those of §9; a warn never fails the doctor.

Built in chunk 4 (`commands/doctor.rs` `probe_gateway` and `classify_gateway`, `clients::gateway_probe`; the cases in
`tests/doctor.rs::gateway_api` and `tests/parity_doctor.rs::divergence::d250_the_gateway_api_check`): the probe client
admits only `gatewayDataEndpoint` (its admin and IAM bases are the data base and are never used, so an inadmissible
admin or IAM setting does not fail the doctor); a Management OAuth client that could not be built leaves the check not
evaluated (choice 100); after the topics probe's 401 or 403 the SDK drops the shared lease, so the gateway probe's
request fetches one new token (choice 99).

### 19.17 Sensitive data per command

| Command | Printed | Never printed |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaces`, `scopes` | names, slugs, ids, statuses, scope names and bindings, defaults and limits (credential names withheld) | — |
| `telemetry` | aggregates; log rows (users, key ids, trace ids, metadata) with credential-named members and URL userinfo, queries and fragments withheld (D251); `filter-boundaries` `data` withheld (TS) | credentials, URL queries |
| `api-keys` reads | ids, names, scopes, dates; `key` `[withheld]` | key material (also with `--reveal-sensitive`, refused) |
| `api-keys create\|rotate`, `deployments create`, rotating `deployments update` | `{saved_to}`; the credential only in the `--secret-output` file | the credential on stdout, stderr, in errors, the debug log, summaries or the ledger (D237) |
| `providers`, `integrations`, `mcp integrations`, `plugins`, `deployments`, `configs`, `guardrails`, `admin-guardrails` | the records with the §19.3 path and name rules applied | provider keys, custom header values, client secrets, OAuth metadata, service-account JSON, plugin credentials, deployment credentials, the provider keys inside a config's `config` text (choice 81) (D238) |
| `organisations info`, `self get`, `auth-settings get` | the records; `settings` withheld (TS); `scim_token` and `auth_settings.client_secret` withheld | SCIM tokens, SSO secrets |
| `audit-logs list` | the records; `request_body`, `request_headers`, `query_params` withheld, or with `--reveal-sensitive` their JSON with credentials withheld (D239) | credentials inside them |
| writes with credential inputs (`integrations create\|update`, `plugins create`, `auth-settings update`, `mcp integrations create\|update`) | the answer, withheld; the inline-flag warnings | the credential in any message, prompt or debug record (D233, D247) |
| `inference` | the model output (stdout only) | the key; prompts and output anywhere but stdout (D240) |
| `report` | aggregates, counts, status codes, bucket times, the title and window | workspace names, slugs and ids, keys, users, models, URLs, metadata, server text (TS) |
| doctor `Gateway API` | the workspace count, the HTTP status | workspace names; server text (D250) |
| every command | §6 errors (allowlisted problem fields only) | server message text, body excerpts, file content, flag values in parser errors (D11, D233); bodies and queries in the debug log (D64) |

Inline credential flags (`--key`, `--scim-token`, `--credential`, `--header`) put the value on the command line (the
process list, shell history), as in TS; each is warned about (D247), and `--file`, `--key-file` and `--key-stdin` are
the private alternatives.

### 19.20 Choices decided

The user delegated every decision; each choice below takes the safest option that keeps the command useful (the
rejected alternative in each item). §19.3 is the single normative text of the withholding policy: a choice records a
decision as it was made, and a clause a later choice changed is marked *Superseded* with the choice that replaced it,
so a choice is read with its marks, never with the amending choices alone.
1. Enable scm-sdk's `gateway` feature; the lock file gains only the `scm-sdk → getrandom` edge. Built at the `=0.1.1`
   pin and merged onto 0.9.1's `=0.2.2` (choice 135), which 0.10 ships. Rejected: scm-sdk 0.2.0 (G25, refused
   answers 0.2.2 reads), `realtime`/`ws-transport` (no command needs them), patching or vendoring the SDK.
2. `without_response_defaults()` on every gateway call through one helper whose options are built just before each
   request (§18.20 choice 73). Rejected: passing it only where a schema default exists (none today, G47; easy to
   miss when a schema changes) and options built once per command (a resolution read would eat a later write's
   budget).
3. A separate `GatewayClients` (data, admin, IAM; one OAuth identity, `x-tsg-id`). Rejected: widening
   `ManagementClients`' destination policy for every management command, and a second token for the IAM plane.
4. Four chunks (core reads, inventory reads, writes, inference/report/doctor/live), so the shared read machinery and
   the withholding policy land before any write. Rejected: the research's three steps (reads, writes,
   inference+live), which put 60 reads and the whole policy in one step.
5. `pretty`, `table` and `json` on every command that prints data, writes included; the tenant `defaultOutput`
   honoured by every command but the report (TS resolves it everywhere else). Rejected: ignoring it on writes (TS
   honours it there; §18.20 choice 18 followed TS's M6d behaviour, which ignored `--output` on writes) and refusing
   `table` on writes (TS's `not supported here` breaks a tenant default of `table`).
6. The banner and report keep the product name `AI Gateway` (`Prisma AIRS — AI Gateway`, `Prisma AIRS AI Gateway`,
   `AI Gateway environment report`); only command names, help, the doctor check, the file name and hints are
   renamed. Rejected: renaming the product text to `Gateway` (it names Palo Alto Networks' product, not the command).
7. The banner prints only above the data of a successful pretty `workspaces`/`scopes`/`cost` command; archives and
   deletes print none. Rejected: TS's banner before the checks (a failing run leaves decoration on stdout, D57).
8. The data-plane status line of `workspaces list` is printed in every format (stderr, quiet-suppressed), as every
   status line (§2.4). Rejected: TS's pretty-only line (a json reader would not learn the list is scoped).
9. Telemetry reads other than `cost` keep TS's `Field │ Value` table in pretty and table. Rejected: a new pretty
   layout per chart (17 layouts with no TypeScript reference to pin).
10. A quota-exceeded flag becomes a stderr warning on every telemetry read. Rejected: TS's stdout line on `cost`
    only (truncated data shown as complete on 19 other reads, and a warning inside the data).
11. `cost` dollars use a port of JavaScript `toFixed(2)` on the exact binary value. Rejected: Rust `{:.2}` (rounds
    ties to even: `12.5` cents would differ) and integer-cent arithmetic (the API sends fractional cents).
12. Workspace resolution fails closed: a failed list is an error and an unmatched reference is refused. Rejected:
    TS's silent skip and pass-through (`scopes bind` bound a slug that does not exist; an update reached a workspace
    the user did not name).
13. Every telemetry leaf resolves `--workspace` over data active, admin active and admin archived, stopping at the
    first match (an exact `id` or `slug` on any list before a display name since choice 127). Rejected: TS's unresolved slug (a display name is sent as a slug and returns empty telemetry) and
    refusing anything but a slug (breaks `cost`'s documented name and UUID forms).
14. `workspaces get` resolves a name after a 404 on the requested plane only. Rejected: TS's extra admin list,
    whose result is then re-read on the data plane and fails anyway.
15. `workspaces list --all` reads its two admin lists one after the other. Rejected: TS's concurrent reads (a
    nondeterministic request order in tests for no observable gain).
16. A list whose `total` or `has_more` says it is incomplete prints its rows with a stderr warning and exits 0
    (G39). Rejected: exit 1 (no continuation exists, so the command would always fail on large tenants with no
    remedy) and silence (TS: a partial list shown as complete).
17. One withholding policy for every gateway document (subtrees, SDK paths, the credential-name rule, URLs, audit
    fields), with `[withheld]` for a withheld value. Rejected: TS's per-command rules (`providers list`,
    integrations, MCP and auth settings print secrets), omitting members as D205 does (a user could not tell a
    credential is configured), and TS's `***`/`[REDACTED]` (two placeholders for one rule).
18. `telemetry filter-boundaries` `data` and `organisations info` `settings` stay withheld whole (TS). Rejected:
    leaf-level withholding (shows more than TypeScript does, where the SDK calls the values possibly sensitive).
19. `workspaces create|update --metadata` replaces `defaults.metadata` whole (TS). Rejected: merging into
    `--defaults` metadata (a silent behaviour change for scripts written against TS).
20. `--reveal-sensitive` exists only on `audit-logs list`, where it shows request fields with credentials still
    withheld; on `api-keys`, `providers get` and `auth-settings get` it is a usage error. Rejected: accepting it as a
    no-op (a script would read `[withheld]` as a key) and honouring it (prints credentials).
21. Audit-log `request_body`, `request_headers` and `query_params` are withheld by default; with
    `--reveal-sensitive` only JSON values are shown, with the path, name and URL rules applied inside; other text
    stays withheld. Rejected: TS's key-name-only redaction (printed bearer headers and keys in bodies) and showing
    non-JSON bodies (no rule can find a credential in free text).
22. URL userinfo, queries and fragments in printed strings are withheld (`request_url`, `custom_host`). Rejected:
    printing them (Gemini-style `?key=` URLs carry credentials) and withholding whole URLs (hosts and paths are the
    useful part).
23. One-time credentials go only to a required `--secret-output <new file>` (0600, never overwritten, reserved before
    the request, kept as a temporary on a lost race), holding the whole answer as TS writes it; `--show-secret` is a
    usage error. Rejected: stdout (`--show-secret`; terminals and CI logs), the credential alone in the file (a
    deployment answer carries a username, a password and `client_auth` that belong together).
24. After a credential write stdout carries TS's `{"saved_to": "<path>"}`. Rejected: the withheld answer record (a
    second shape for scripts written against TS).
25. The G36 raw writes, so a 2xx whose rest fails the schema still saves the credential. Rejected: the typed calls (a
    missing `key_transition_expires_at` loses a rotated key's only copy).

    leaf out of reach) and an allowlist of read leaves (a new read leaf would need a guard change to run, a write leaf

127. A workspace reference resolves an exact `id` or `slug` on any of the command's lists before a display name: the
    lists are read until one holds the exact reference, and a name is matched only once every list was read, on the
    first list that has it; an incomplete list without the exact reference stops a name (review). A display name now
    reads all three telemetry lists, and a failing admin list stops a name that the data plane holds (fail closed; a
    slug or UUID on the data plane still needs that list only). Rejected: the first list with any match deciding (TS;
    a data-plane workspace whose display name is another workspace's slug or UUID shadowed it, so telemetry read the
    wrong workspace) and treating one name on several lists as ambiguous (an archived workspace and its recreated
    successor would make the name unusable).
128. A matched workspace row whose `slug` is not a non-empty string is refused with its own message and nothing sent;
    in an ambiguity list it is shown `(no slug)` (review). Rejected: an empty slug (the write or telemetry read went to
    an empty path segment and failed with an unrelated local error) and treating the row as not found (the message
    would deny a workspace the list shows).
129. A debug-build test marker (`AIRS_CLI_TEST_SIGNAL_MARKER`, §2.5) lets the harness wait until the signal thread has
    recorded a signal before releasing a stalled stream (`Running::send_signal_recorded`), in the gateway and runtime
    tests that signal a run after its credential was saved (review). Rejected: a fixed sleep (a loaded host could
    release the stream before the signal is seen, and the run would end with exit 0), a signal record in the `--debug`
    log (a second record kind in the §2.9 contract for a test need) and a release-build variable.
130. The live tier's credential-name rule is a copy of `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold.rs`'s two lists, pinned equal and in
    order by `withhold::tests::the_live_tier_checks_the_same_credential_names` (review). Rejected: sharing the constant
    (the harness cannot depend on the CLI crate, which dev-depends on it; a cycle builds two copies of the crate) and
    the shorter list the live check had (it missed `access_key`, `secret_key`, `subscription_key`, `signing_key` and
    their suffixes, so a live answer printing one would have passed). *Superseded* by choice 158: the live check no
    longer carries a copy; it includes the CLI's `src/gateway/names.rs` by path.
131. `--reveal-sensitive` applies the secret paths of every SDK operation, secret references included (`auth_config`
    withheld whole at any depth), and the name rule treats `secret_id` and `_secret_id` as credentials (review: an
    audited secret-reference create with HashiCorp AppRole auth printed its `vault_secret_id`, which neither the seven
    hand-copied resources nor a name suffix covered). Rejected: a hand-maintained list of resources (it had already
    dropped secret references) and withholding every revealed body whole (the flag would show nothing).
132. Inside a revealed audit field a `{"key": <name>, "value": …}` pair is read as one header or tag: the name is
    printed and never registered, the value is withheld unless the name is a safe header (review). Rejected: the bare
    name rule (it printed the value of `[{"key":"Authorization","value":"Bearer …"}]` and registered the word
    `Authorization`, withholding every later string equal to it) and rule 3's pair rule (it shows a value whose name is
    no credential name; a revealed request is the stricter case, so only the safe headers show).
133. The per-resource secret paths are read from the SDK's public `AI_GATEWAY_SECRET_FIELDS` by
    `AIGatewaySecretOperation`, with only the CLI's additions (`data.auth_settings.client_secret`; the `config` JSON
    texts of choice 81, from choice 136 rule 3's JSON-text clause) kept locally, and a unit test (`every_sdk_secret_path_is_withheld`) places every operation
    of the SDK table in a policy or in the commented audit-only list and proves each path withheld by its policy and
    by the audit rule (review). `*` reads array items as well as members, as the SDK does. Rejected: the hand copy
    (two sources of truth that had drifted) and copying the SDK's redaction helper (`[REDACTED]`, no `SecretSet`
    registration, no CLI additions).
134. A display name under a data-plane-only grant keeps failing closed on the admin list (choice 127), and the
    failure adds a hint that a slug or UUID resolves from the data plane alone (review). Rejected: skipping a
    failing admin list (an exact slug there could be shadowed by a data-plane name, the defect of choice 127), the
    data-plane grant hint for the admin list (the admin grant is the one missing) and the hint on an interruption or
    a transport failure (no grant is in question there).
135. 0.10 ships on scm-sdk `=0.2.2` with the `gateway` feature (merged from 0.9.1), re-measured against the 0.1.1 the
    section was built on (§19 "What 0.2.x changes"): no gateway schema node changes, no gateway response schema
    declares a format the 0.2.2 relaxation (D306) skips, G36–G49 hold and G49 is settled by a unit test on the pinned
    SDK. The access-policy API of 0.2.1 is left unused: the TypeScript CLI has no access-policy command, so a command
    would be new surface without a parity reference, on a key-authenticated control plane outside the tenant model
    (the SDK marks it experimental and live-unverified). Rejected: an `access-policies` command group (outside the
    port's scope; it would need its own credential plane and live rules), a D306 gateway extension (nothing to
    extend: no gateway answer is format-checked on either SDK) and keeping the 0.1.1 texts (the shipped pin is 0.2.2).
136. Rule 3 withholds the credential members (`vertex_service_account_json`, `oauth_metadata`, `model_config`,
    `auth_config`) at any depth of every document and every credential held as JSON text, at any depth (review: a
    `configs get` or `configs versions` config whose Portkey target held a stringified service account printed its
    `private_key`, because only the path rules named those members and only the top-level `config` member was parsed;
    the same member at a depth no path names printed too). The credentials of a withheld JSON text are registered:
    what rules 3 and 4 withhold inside it and every other string inside it that looks like a credential (choice 120's
    test), plus the whole text. The per-resource `json_texts` member of the policy is dropped (`CONFIGS` was its one
    user; the config reads use the shared rules). Rejected: adding the members to the config policy only (another
    resource or depth would leak the same way), the audit rule's whole walk for every document (it withholds every
    header value, which would hide the non-secret headers TypeScript prints; header maps alone are now withheld in
    every document, choice 138) and registering every string inside a
    withheld JSON text, as the audit rule did (a service account's `"type": "service_account"` joined the
    `SecretSet`, so the member name `vertex_service_account_json` that carries it was dropped from the output and
    every string containing a project id was withheld).
137. The options of a call whose failures are SDK errors (a write's attempt closure, a `workspaces create` step, the
    workspace reads they share) come from one helper, `gateway::sdk_options` (`write_options` until choice 187), which maps an options failure to
    the SDK's `Configuration` error (review: the mapping was repeated at every such site); the shared G39 rule is one
    `gateway::incomplete_total`, read by the list warnings and by the workspace resolution (review: two copies).
    Behaviour unchanged. Rejected: keeping the copies (a change to one would silently diverge from the other).
138. Header maps are withheld at any depth of every gateway document, not only inside a revealed audit field: every
    value but a safe header's is `[withheld]`, in an object map, a `{key, value}` pair, a list of them or a JSON text
    holding one (review: `integrations models list` printed a model's `configurations.custom_headers` value, the
    SDK's `configurations.custom_headers.*` path being matched only at the document root or a row; `models set`
    never registered the header in its body; `guardrails get` and `admin-guardrails get` printed a webhook check's
    `parameters.headers`). Which withheld header values join the `SecretSet` is choice 139's one rule for every
    document (it replaced this choice's first rule, which registered every header value of a resource document and
    only the credential-looking ones of an audit record), so a proxied request's `x-forwarded-for` no longer
    withholds the log's `client_ip` and a workspace header its `workspace_id` and `uri` (review). A JSON text is printed withheld whenever a rule
    changed it, not only when a value was registered (a short `token` inside a config text printed as received).
    The live tier's withholding check reads pairs and header maps the same way (review: it flagged a tag pair's
    `key` as a printed credential and checked only `custom_headers` maps). Rejected: per-resource paths only
    (`models.*.configurations.custom_headers`; another depth or resource, such as a guardrail's webhook, would leak
    the same way), the names-only rule (choice 136's earlier rejection of the audit walk kept TypeScript's printed
    header values, which carry credentials under any header name) and registering every audit header value (a
    value such as an IP address withheld every string carrying it, silently emptying the log's forensic
    columns).
139. A withheld header value joins the `SecretSet` by one rule in every document, the audit log's and the resource
    documents' alike, and at a path rule's `custom_headers.*` too: a credential header's value (a credential name, or
    a header name with one of the words `auth`, `authorization`, `key`, `apikey`, `token`, `secret`, `password`,
    `passwd`, `cookie`, `credential`, `credentials`, `signature`) whole, and also as its credential-looking words
    (choice 142); any other value only when it, or one of its whitespace-separated words, looks like a credential (at
    least 16 characters, no whitespace). Every non-safe value
    stays `[withheld]` in place; a `{key, value}` item's name is never registered (review: a configuration header such
    as `x-env: prod` or `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` joined the `SecretSet`, so the D47 rule withheld every
    `created_at` on that date and every name containing `prod`, and dropped every member named after it, with no
    notice). Rejected: registering every value (the defect), a longer minimum length for every header value (a
    `prod-eu-west-1` or a date-time is long and still harmless, while a short value under `X-Auth-Key` is a credential)
    and registering nothing but credential-named headers (`X-Tenant: <long token>` and the token of a `Bearer` value
    under a custom header name would no longer withhold their echoes). Tests:
    `withhold::tests::headers::d238_a_short_configuration_header_does_not_withhold_other_data`,
    `tests/gateway_inventory.rs::withholding::d238_a_short_configuration_header_does_not_withhold_other_data`.
140. The outcome lines of every write go through one rule in `src/writes.rs`: the `OutcomeLines` trait (the unknown

168. A URL's userinfo runs to its last `@` (review): a password may hold an unencoded `/`, `?` or `#` (AWS secret

    in a path or query then withholds what precedes it (`https://[withheld]@someone/post`), the safe failure; that
    userinfo is registered only when it holds a `:` or no `/`, `?` or `#`, so a host such as `social.example/`
    never joins the `SecretSet` and withholds every other URL on it. Rejected: the RFC 3986 authority (the leak),

169. The URL rule reads every URL inside a string (review): the scheme is found before each `://` (from its first
    letter, so `9ttp://h?q` reads as `ttp://` and its query is withheld) and the URL ends at the next whitespace,

    are withheld as a whole URL is; model output (§19.14) gets the same reading. A query or fragment ends at

    `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_more_credential_name_shapes_are_withheld`,

    `tests/gateway_inventory.rs::withholding::d238_name_value_pairs_private_keys_and_numbers_are_withheld`,

171. *Amended by choice 187: a number under a name whose last words describe a credential (`user_api_key_count`)
    is printed by that name, and under a generic header it prints; under every other withholding class but a count,
    under a credential header or pair, a path rule and inside a withheld credential object it is withheld as
    below, and so is the empty string under every withholding class.*
    A number is withheld under every withholding class but a count, and under a path rule, inside a withheld
    credential and as an audit request field, as TypeScript's `redactDeep` masks every value under a sensitive key
    (review: `{"password": 12345678}` and a numeric `credentials.*` member of a revealed audit body printed). The

183. The text rules register only what can be a credential, read two more shapes, and the crate makes the last
    registration decision (review: under a credential-named key the key=value rule registered any value of 4 or more
    characters, so `auth=none` or `password=true` in one row withheld `mode: none`, `enabled: "true"` and a
    `guardrail` named `nonexistent-check` in other rows, the cross-row cascade choice 181 removed for the scheme
    rule; the whole two-word label `token gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` was read as a header value and registered the model
    id; an Azure shared access signature and an `X-Api-Key: …` header line printed their credentials; the 4-character
    minimum and the placeholder exclusion lived only in the CLI, so the crate's registration flags overstated what
    is registered; and every string with an `=` ran the key=value rule twice). Decided:
    1. A credential-named key's value is withheld in place whatever it is and registered only when it can be a
       credential by its shape: it looks like a credential or a password (8 or more characters with a symbol or a
       part mixing letters and digits), carries a symbol other than the word separators at any length (`abc+/==`,
       `p@ss`), or is a quoted value holding whitespace (`Password="a b;c"`). So `abc+/==` and `hunter2x` are
       registered and `none`, `basic`, `true`, `1234` and (choice 186) a shorter word of letters and digits
       (`oauth2`, `sha256`, `v2.0`, `hunter2`) are not. (As first written this item registered any value "shaped as
       a password at any length", `values::password_shaped`, which registered `oauth2` and withheld it in every
       other row; choice 186 narrows it to the reading above.) Rejected: the old "whatever it is" (the cascade) and
       "looks like a credential or a password" alone, which would stop registering the short symbol-bearing
       passwords and test account keys the rule registers now. `auth=oauth2-client-credentials` is still
       registered: by shape it cannot be told from a credential, and registering fails safe (only its echo is
       withheld).
    2. One registration filter in the crate, `names::registrable` (with `names::MIN_REGISTERED`, moved from the
       CLI): at least 4 characters once trimmed, never one carrying `[withheld]`, never a placeholder word
       (`names::PLACEHOLDER_WORDS`: `true`, `false`, `null`, `none`, `nil`, `undefined`, `empty`, `unset`,
       `redacted`, `[redacted]`, any case) and never a mask (`names::MASK_CHARACTERS` alone: `****`, `••••`,
       `xxxx`, `####`). `names::registered`, `names::registered_number`, every `TextCredential::registered` flag,
       the URL rule's parts and `values::unreadable_json_strings` apply it, so a flag says what is registered and
       the checker's side reads registration by the same rule; the CLI only adds to the `SecretSet` (reading the
       predicate once more as a guard). The placeholder words apply under a credential member too
       (`{"password": "none"}` is withheld and not registered), since they give no value to withhold elsewhere.
       Rejected: excluding only in the key=value rule (the same word under a member name would still cascade).
    3. The scheme rule reads a whole two-word text as a header value only with the capitalised scheme a header writes
       (`Token x`, `Basic x`; `Bearer` is registered in any case, as before); `token x` is withheld in place only.
       Rejected: a credential shape for the lowercase word (a model id mixes letters and digits, so it would still
       register).
    4. `shared_access_signature` (`SharedAccessSignature`), the run-together `sharedaccesssignature` and `sig` are
       credential names (row 6), everywhere, since a member named `sig` holds a signature as often as the SAS
       parameter does; under a credential key, a value that is itself a run of `key=value` parameters
       (`SharedAccessSignature=sv=…&ss=b&sig=…`, an `=` before its end padding) runs to the end of its segment, so
       `&` does not cut it at `sv=…`, and the registered parameters inside it (its `sig`) are registered too.
       Rejected: `sig` only inside a key=value text (a JSON member `sig` would print the same signature).
    5. The **header rule**: `<credential header>: <value>` and `<credential header>:<value>` inside a text (`curl -H
       'X-Api-Key: …'`, `-H "api-key:…"`, `Authorization: <key>` with no scheme) withhold and register a value that
       looks like a credential or a password. The name must be shaped as a header name and written with a `-` (or be
       `Authorization` or `Cookie`), and a credential by the name rule or a credential header word; count headers
       (`x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`) and prose naming a header keep their words. Model output does not get it (an
       answer's code sample). Rejected again: a general `name: value` rule (choice 181: YAML and prose write every
       field so).
    6. The four text rules are one crate function, `values::text_withheld` (URL, scheme, header, key=value, each on
       what the one before printed); the URL rule returns the credentials of the `key=value` segments inside each part
       it withholds, so the CLI runs each rule once per string instead of the key=value rule twice. Rejected: a
       pre-pass on the original text (the double scan the review named).
    Tests: `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/corpus.rs::tests::every_real_world_text_registers_as_pinned` (the crate's
    `text_withheld` against every `REAL_WORLD_TEXTS` entry: printed form, idempotence, each registration
    registrable, each `registered` carried and no `kept` word carried), the new entries (two-word lowercase labels,
    `auth=none`, `Password=true`, `Pwd=********`, ODBC `Trusted_Connection=yes;Uid=;Pwd=;`, a SAS connection
    string, `sig=` in prose, `curl` with `X-Api-Key:` and `api-key:`, and header text that names no credential) run
    by `withhold::tests::corpus::d238_real_world_texts_print_as_pinned` and the harness's
    `the_real_world_texts_are_checked_as_the_cli_prints_them`,
    `withhold::tests::texts::d238_a_credential_key_word_stays_printed_elsewhere` (the review's documents: `mode`,
    `guardrail`, `enabled` and `ai_model` printed in other rows, in json, pretty and table),
    `withhold::tests::texts::d238_shared_access_signatures_and_api_key_headers_are_withheld`,
