184. *Superseded by choice 185.*
    The withholding crate ships its licence and a README (review: `airs-cli-withhold` would have been published to
    crates.io with neither; Apache-2.0 §4(a) expects a copy of the licence with each redistribution, and the
    crates.io page would have no readme). `crates/airs-cli-withhold/LICENSE` is a copy of the root `LICENSE` (a
    copy, not a symlink, so a checkout without symlink support packages the same file) and
    `crates/airs-cli-withhold/README.md` says what the crate is, that it follows the CLI's version and that `corpus`
    is test data; both are in the crate's `include` list and `readme = "README.md"` is set, so `cargo package --list
    -p airs-cli-withhold` lists `LICENSE` and `README.md`. Rejected: a symlink (Windows checkouts and some archive
    tools turn it into a text file holding the path) and `license-file` (the SPDX `license` field already names
    Apache-2.0; the file is the copy the licence asks for). Tests:
    `withhold::tests::corpus::the_withholding_crate_ships_its_licence_and_readme` (the copy equals the root licence,
    the manifest lists both); `scripts/release.sh --dry-run` packages the crate (choice 180).
    *Superseded* by choice 185: no second crate is published, so its licence copy, its README and their test are
    gone (the CLI package ships the root `LICENSE` and `README.md` as before).
185. *Amended by choice 187: the checker is compiled into the CLI's test builds only, and no blanket `dead_code` allow
    remains.*
    The withholding rules are a module of the CLI, `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/` (`mod.rs`, `names.rs`,
    `values.rs`, `check.rs`, and `corpus.rs` under `#[cfg(test)]`), and the unpublished test harness compiles the
    same files by `#[path]` (`crates/airs-test-harness/src/withhold.rs`: the module root, re-exported as
    `airs_test_harness::withhold::{check, names, values, WITHHELD}`, and `corpus.rs` again outside the harness's own
    test build, for the CLI's and the workspace's other tests), the pattern `fixtures.rs` uses (orchestrator's
    decision on review: `airs-cli` must depend on no second crates.io crate). Inside the files a sibling is
    `super::`, never `crate::` (the two crate roots differ), and they use `std` and `serde_json` only; the
    `serde_json::Value` impl of `check::Json` is in `check.rs` with no feature (both crates already depend on
    serde_json), and the CLI implements it for `OValue` in `withhold.rs`, so the CLI's tests compare the checker on
    both value types in its own build and against the harness's build. In the CLI the module is private, so the
    checker the binary never calls is `allow(dead_code)` outside tests; the binary carries no test data. The
    workspace has two members again, `Cargo.lock` loses only the crate's entry and its two edges, and
    `scripts/release.sh` and RELEASING.md lose the withholding-crate checks, the publish order and the crates.io
    name check (choices 172, 180, 182 and 184 are superseded in those parts). Rejected: a separately published
    crate (every release would publish and pin a second crate name, and claim it on crates.io, for rules no other
    program uses), duplicated pinned copies in the CLI and the harness (choice 130's copies drifted, choice 158),
    and the harness depending on the CLI crate (a dependency cycle through the CLI's dev-dependency builds two
    copies of it, choice 172). Tests: `withhold::tests::corpus::the_rules_compile_outside_the_cli` (the module's
    file list, no `crate::`, `airs_cli_rs::`, `scm::` or `airs_test_harness::` path in them, the harness's two
    includes, and no manifest naming a withholding crate), `withhold::tests::corpus::the_checker_reads_both_value_types_alike`
    (the CLI's checker on `OValue` and on `serde_json::Value`, and the harness's, agree on every pinned document),
    and every harness test of the live check (`crates/airs-test-harness/src/live/gateway.rs::tests`), which now run
    the CLI's files; `cargo package -p airs-cli --list` lists `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/*.rs`, and `cargo publish
    -p airs-cli --dry-run` builds the packaged crate alone.
186. The key=value rule reads three more shapes and registers less (review): `Server=db;User Id=sa;Password=p@ss
    w0rd;` printed `w0rd` and `PWD={p@ss;w0rd};` printed `w0rd}` (a value ended at whitespace or `;`), `password =
    hunter2x!` and `aws_secret_access_key = wJalr…` printed whole (no spaces were read around the `=`), and
    `auth=oauth2` registered `oauth2` (shaped as a password at any length, choice 183.1), so `oauth2` was withheld
    in every other row. Decided:
    1. A credential key that starts a `;`-separated segment (after a `;`, or first in a text that holds a `;`) has
       its value read to the next `;`, a line break or the end, whitespace included, and an ODBC braced value
       (`{…}`, `}}` an escaped `}`) is read to its closing `}` under any credential key; the whole value is withheld
       (the braces too) and registered whole (without the braces, `}}` read as `}`). A line break ends a segment,
       so a connection string on one line of a longer text withholds only that line's value. A key after prose (`note:
       Password=p@ss w0rd`) or in a text without `;` keeps the whitespace end, so a sentence that starts with
       `password=…` loses one word, not the sentence. Rejected: whitespace ending every value (the leak), and every
       text start being a segment (`secret=sha256 and pwd=v2.0` would withhold the rest of the sentence).
    2. Under a credential key a value is registered when it looks like a credential or a password, carries a
       symbol other than the word separators at any length, or holds whitespace inside the delimiters that make it
       one value (its quotes, braces or segment); a shorter word of letters and digits (`oauth2`, `sha256`, `v2.0`,
       `hunter2`) is withheld in that text only, so it never withholds the same word in another row. Rejected:
       keeping `password_shaped` at any length (the cascade), and registering every value of 8 or more characters
       (`auth=disabled` would withhold `disabled` everywhere).
    3. Spaces or tabs around the `=` are read only after a credential name (an INI or TOML line, `password = …`),
       so prose (`a = b`, `sort key = name`, `max_tokens = 100`) keeps its words; `==` and `=>` are never a
       segment's `=`. Rejected: reading spaces after every key (prose would lose words after `key =`, `token =`),
       and not reading them at all (an AWS credentials file printed its secret).
    4. The model-output rule pair is a rules function, `values::model_output_withheld` (the URL rule, then the scheme
       rule on what it printed, nothing registered), which `withhold::value_rules` calls, beside `text_withheld`
       (both run one `in_order` over their list of rules). Rejected: the CLI listing the two rules itself (the
       subset was the CLI's knowledge, outside the rules module).
    README's gateway paragraph lists what the text rules recognise and what they do not, as §19.3 does. Tests:
    `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/values.rs::tests::connection_string_values_run_to_their_segment_end`,
    `…::spaced_key_values_are_read_under_credential_names_only`, `…::key_value_credentials_are_withheld_in_place`
    (`Pwd=hunter2`, `auth=oauth2`, `secret=sha256`, `pwd=v2.0` not registered; `Pwd=hunter2x`, `Pwd=p@ss`
    registered), `…::model_output_gets_the_url_and_scheme_rules_only`,
    `withhold::tests::texts::d238_short_key_words_stay_local_and_connection_passwords_are_whole` (the review's
    documents in json, pretty and table), and the new `corpus::REAL_WORLD_TEXTS` entries (an ADO.NET password holding
    a space, an ODBC braced password holding `;` and `}}`, an AWS credentials file, a configuration line, `Use
    auth=oauth2 for remote` with `oauth2` kept, `secret=sha256 and pwd=v2.0`, and spaced `key = value` text that
    names no credential) run by `withhold::tests::corpus::d238_real_world_texts_print_as_pinned`, the harness's
    `the_real_world_texts_are_checked_as_the_cli_prints_them` and
    `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/corpus.rs::tests::every_real_world_text_registers_as_pinned`.
187. The name rule reads what describes a credential, registers less, and the `SecretSet` is linear (live run of
    `workspaces get <slug> --output json` against a tenant, compared with TypeScript: the workspace `settings`
    members `user_api_key_count`, `user_api_key_max_ttl`, `user_api_key_ttl` (numbers in TypeScript) and
    `user_api_key_rotation_period` (an empty string) printed `[withheld]`, the widened rule reading every name that
    holds `api_key` as a credential; and the milestone review). Decided:
    1. *As amended by the milestone's second review.* The name rule never withholds `null` or a boolean, under any
       class, in a header map or a pair (`names::action`, `names::header_action`): no credential is a flag or an
       absence, and the organisation's `user_api_key_auto_create: false`, under a credential name, prints on
       `workspaces get` as TypeScript prints it there (the live run). A number and the empty string are withheld as
       choice 171 withheld them, under a credential name or member, a generic name (`key`, `token`) and a
       credential, member or count header or pair (`Authorization: 12345678`, `{"key": "password", "value":
       12345678}`), and printed under a count (`prompt_tokens: 5`), a header map's own name and a generic header
       (`x-retries: 3`); a withheld number joins the `SecretSet` by `names::registered_number` (at least 8
       characters as a credential's value, so `{"password": 12345678}` withholds its echo). The live mismatch is
       met by 2 instead: the workspace settings (`user_api_key_count: 5`, `user_api_key_ttl`,
       `user_api_key_rotation_period: ""`) are row 9's names, printed whatever their value. TypeScript's
       `redactDeep` masks every value under a name it matches, of any type (`debug-logger.ts:50-62`), on the reads
       it runs on: every inventory get (`inventory.ts:106`) and `audit-logs list` (`inventory.ts:387`), not
       `workspaces get`; so a number or an empty string printed under a credential name would be less safe than
       TypeScript there, and the safer of the two readings is kept: withheld, but a flag and an absence, which carry
       no secret and which the live tier compares, printed (`null` and booleans are the one place this rule prints
       what `redactDeep` masks, recorded in COMPATIBILITY). Rejected, after the first build of this choice: printing
       every number and empty string under every name (`{"password": 12345678, "api_key": 9876543210123, "token":
       123456789}`, `{"headers": {"Authorization": 12345678}}` and `{"key": "password", "value": 12345678}` printed
       unchanged and unregistered on the integrations reads, which TypeScript masks: the review's major finding);
       withholding booleans and `null` too (the live `user_api_key_auto_create` and the guardrail catalog's flags
       would mismatch for no secret); and a list of the numeric names to print (each new setting the service adds
       would be withheld again).
    2. A name whose last `_` word or words describe a credential is printed (`names::METADATA_WORDS`, row 9 of
       "Rule 3 by name", `names::Pattern::Last`): `count`, `counts`, `limit`, `limits`, `length`, `size`, `max`,
       `min`, `ttl`, `period`, `interval`, `duration` and the units `ms`, `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`; `at`
       (every `_at` timestamp), `date`, `timestamp`, `expiry`, `expiration`, `expires`, `expires_in`; `enabled`,
       `disabled`, `required`; `type`, `types`, `kind`, `mode`, `format`; `name`, `names`, `id`, `ids`, `version`,
       `status`; and where a credential is kept or sent, `location`, `path`, `url`, `uri`, `endpoint`. The
       fingerprints `prefix`, `last4`, `last8`, `last_four` and `hint` are row 8 (`names::FINGERPRINT_WORDS`,
       `names::Class::Fingerprint`): read as a printed name's value, but a string that looks like a credential
       (16 characters, no whitespace, no date; `names::Shape::CredentialLike`) is withheld and registered as a
       credential's value (review: `api_key_hint: "sk-live-1234567890abcdefghij"` and `token_prefix: "ghp_…"`
       printed, which TypeScript masks on the inventory gets), so `api_key_last4: "wxyz"` and `api_key_hint: "the one
       ending in wxyz"` print. Rejected: keeping them metadata words (a credential sent under a fingerprint name
       printed) and making them credential names (`api_key_last8`, the SDK's fingerprint, would be withheld for
       nothing). The list is TypeScript's `redactDeep` vocabulary
       (`/token|secret|password|passwd|credential|authorization|cookie|api[-_]?key|client[-_]?auth|auth[-_]?code|^key$/i`)
       crossed with the names of the pinned SDK's schemas that the earlier rows withheld (`scm-sdk 0.2.2`
       `validation/schema_graph.json`): `user_api_key_count`, `user_api_key_max_ttl`, `user_api_key_ttl`,
       `user_api_key_rotation_period`, `api_key_name`, `api_key_last8`, `token_type`, `oauth2_token_url`,
       `secret_version`, `private_key_id`, and the review's
       `token_limit`, `token_expires_at`, `clientSecretExpiresAt`, `credential_type`. Two shapes stay credentials,
       by rows before them: a HashiCorp Vault AppRole SecretID (`secret_id`, `vault_secret_id`, row 6: the role's
       password, not an identifier) and a URL named after a stored secret (`secret_url`, `credentials_uri`,
       `db_password_uri`, row 7, `names::Pattern::LastAfter`: a capability URL is the credential itself), while a URL
       named after a token, a key or an authentication (`token_url`, `auth_uri`, `token_endpoint`) is where one is
       sent and prints, with rule 4 still withholding its userinfo, query and fragment. `api_key`, `user_api_key`,
       `x_api_key`, `api_key_value` and `token_preview` stay credentials (their last word is no metadata word).
       Rejected: an exact list of the SDK's names (the next setting would be withheld again), every `_id` and `_url`
       printed (a SecretID and a capability URL would print), and a metadata word anywhere in the name (`id_token`, an OpenID Connect
       token, would print).
    3. *As amended by the milestone's second review.* A credential name's value joins the `SecretSet` whole only
       where it can be a credential by its shape (`values::registers_whole`): it has at least 8 characters once
       trimmed (`values::PASSWORD_LOOK`) and is no placeholder word or mask (`names::registrable`), or, shorter, it
       passes the key=value rule's test of choice 186 read as one value (a symbol other than the word separators, or
       whitespace); never a date. A path rule's value (rules 1 and 2) is registered whole always, the SDK naming it
       a secret (`names::Leaf::Path`, split from `Leaf::Credential`). So `{"password": "Bearer"}` withholds `Bearer`
       in place only and a timestamp never withholds every other timestamp, while a dictionary password
       (`{"password": "dragonfly"}`, `{"secret": "sunshine"}`) is registered and its echo (`"description":
       "dragonfly"`, `"note": "pw sunshine"`) withheld; the cascade the review saw (`{"token_type": "Bearer"}`
       withholding `Send a Bearer header`, `api_key_name: production` the `env: production` of another row) is
       gone by 2, those names being row 9's. Rejected: registering every credential name's value whole (a
       four-letter word would withhold every string that holds it), registering none whole (a `p@ss` echoed in an
       error would print), and, after the first build of this choice, registering a word of letters and digits
       only when it looks like a password (a weak dictionary password under `password` was withheld in place and
       its echo printed: the review's second finding).
    4. `signature` and the `_signature` suffix (`webhook_signature`, `X-Signature`), the word `passcode` anywhere
       (`userPasscode`) and `otp` as a whole `_` word (`sms_otp`; not `hotpot`) are credential names, so `sig`,
       `signature` and the header rule's `signature` agree. `pin` is not one, recorded: as a word it names a pinned
       version or certificate as often as a PIN (`pin_version`, `cert_pin`, `pin_model`), so a numeric PIN under a
       bare `pin` name prints, while one under a credential name or inside a credential object is withheld (1).
       Rejected: a `pin` row (a pinned model id would be withheld and registered).
    5. The audit read is linear (review: `audit-logs list` took 0.09, 0.23, 0.88 and 3.45 s for 500 to 4000
       records, release): an unrevealed audit request field is never printed, so its text is not registered, only
       the credentials inside it (`values::unprinted_credentials` for a text that is no JSON document, the walk of
       rule 5 for one that is; a number only when it looks like a credential); the `SecretSet` keeps its forms as
       one ordered set (`BTreeSet`: a form joins once, in logarithmic time, and is stored once), and `carried_by`
       and `appears_in_ignoring_case` check a string against every form in one pass (an Aho–Corasick matcher in
       `std`, `secrets::Matcher`: a byte trie with failure links, at most two steps per byte, rebuilt on the first
       read after a form joins, exact and ASCII-folded); the fragment half of `taints` (a text of at least four
       bytes found inside a form) still reads each form, and only the §6 metadata checks, `scrub` and the red team,
       model security and scan views call it, never the gateway's document pass. Measured on the release build with a 4000-record log of three text
       fields per record: 14.5 s before, 0.12 s after (0.03, 0.05, 0.08, 0.12 s for 500 to 4000). Rejected: a crates.io
       matcher (no new dependency), grouping the forms by their first byte or length (still quadratic when forms
       share a prefix, as every `Bearer …` value and every base64 form does), keeping the whole field text
       registered (four forms per field for nothing printed), and, after the first build of this choice, a list in
       join order beside a hash index (every form stored twice; no reader needs the join order).
    6. The checker is compiled into the CLI's test builds only (`#[cfg(test)] pub mod check;`), and the harness
       compiles `check.rs` by `#[path]` in its own non-test builds, as it does `corpus.rs`; the value view both
       traversals read shapes through moves to `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/view.rs` (`view::Json`, `view::shape`,
       `view::is_schema`, `view::text_free`), and the checker's parsing reading is its own trait,
       `check::Document`, which the CLI's tests implement for `OValue`. The test-only helpers
       (`names::rules_table`, `names::is_credential_header`) are `#[cfg(test)]`, the checker-only string tests
       (`schemes_withheld`, `urls_withheld`) move into `check.rs`, and the one remaining allow is on
       `names::Pattern::words`, which the harness's corpus reads; the blanket `allow(dead_code)` on the module is
       gone. Rejected: moving `check.rs` into the harness crate (the CLI's tests could not run it on the CLI's own
       value, the harness's `Json` trait being another crate's), and keeping the blanket allow (it hid 15 unused
       items).
    7. `gateway::write_options` is `gateway::sdk_options`: reads use it too (`resolve::read_list`,
       `gateway_workspaces::read_detail`). No behaviour change.
    8. The workspace fixture's detail carries the live tenant's `settings` (`user_api_key_auto_create`,
       `user_api_key_count`, `user_api_key_max_ttl`, `user_api_key_ttl`, `user_api_key_rotation_period: ""`), so the
       loopback parity test of `workspaces get --output json` reads them against TypeScript.
    9. *Added by the milestone's second review.* The `SecretSet`, its forms and its matcher are their own module,
       `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs` (with the base64 forms), and `error.rs` re-exports `SecretSet` and `base64_standard`, so every
       caller is unchanged; the matcher's step count, the scale test's structural bound, is a test build's only
       (`secrets::Steps`, a zero-sized type elsewhere, which a `const` assertion holds in the binary). Rejected:
       keeping them in `error.rs` (an error-mapping module holding the CLI's central secret store and a string
       matcher) and a plain `u64` counter (every read of the binary counted steps nobody reads).
    Tests: `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/names.rs::tests::metadata_names_describe_a_credential`,
    `…::a_credential_name_registers_only_credential_shaped_values`,
    `…::the_action_table_prints_only_what_carries_no_credential`, `withhold::tests::name_rule::credential_names`,
    `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_word_shaped_values_do_not_cascade`,
    `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_numbers_under_credential_names_and_path_rules_are_withheld_counts_and_flags_print`,
    `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_numbers_under_credential_headers_and_pairs_are_withheld`,
    `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_a_weak_password_under_a_credential_name_withholds_its_echo`,
    `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_a_credential_under_a_fingerprint_name_is_withheld`,
    `withhold::tests::headers::d238_header_maps_withhold_every_value_but_the_safe_headers`, the generated numbers of
    `corpus::planted` (an eight-digit number under every credential name and member, in every container shape and
    echoed),
    `withhold::tests::audit::d239_a_large_audit_log_is_withheld_in_linear_work` (4000 records: no field text
    registered, at most four forms per record, at most two matcher steps per printed byte),
    `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs::tests::the_matcher_agrees_with_contains_per_form`,
    `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs::tests::forms_join_once_and_every_read_sees_the_latest`,
    `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs::tests::the_forms_are_one_ordered_set`, `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs::tests::only_taints_reads_fragments`,
    `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs::tests::the_step_counter_counts_reads`, `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/secrets.rs::tests::the_secret_set_is_its_own_module`,
    `withhold::tests::corpus::the_rules_compile_outside_the_cli` (the file list with `view.rs`, the harness's three
    includes, the checker and the corpus under `#[cfg(test)]`, no `dead_code` allow on the module), the new pinned
    document of `corpus::PINNED_DOCUMENTS`, `tests/gateway_reads.rs::workspaces::d238_workspace_api_key_settings_print_as_sent`,
    `tests/parity_gateway_reads.rs::parity::json_documents_match_typescript` and the harness's
    `live::gateway::tests::name_value_pairs_are_read_as_headers`.
188. The withholding rules print what they over-withheld (the release's independent review: no credential printed;
    over-withholding and wording). Decided:
    1. The lists of key names that row 11's `_keys` suffix read as credentials are printed (row 3,
       `names::PRINTED_NAMES`): `metadata_keys`, the required-metadata guardrail's `metadataKeys`
       (`GatewayRequiredMetadataKeysParameters`, also a parameter of the guardrail catalog), which printed
       `checks[].parameters.metadataKeys: [withheld]` on `guardrails get` and `admin-guardrails get` and withheld the
       catalog's `default: []` and `examples`; and the analytics filter boundaries' `unique_metadata_keys` (metadata
       key names) and `unique_virtual_keys` (Portkey virtual key slugs, as `virtual_keys` of choice 176). Every
       `*_keys` and `*Keys` name of the pinned SDK's gateway schemas (`scm-sdk 0.2.2`, `models/generated.rs` and
       `validation/schema_graph.json`) was read: `unique_api_keys` (the API keys a filter saw) and `api_keys` (a list
       of API key records, each with its `auth_code`) stay credentials; `preserveReservedKeys` is a validation
       annotation, never a wire member. TypeScript's `redactDeep` reads none of these names (its only key words are
       `api[-_]?key` and `^key$`). Rejected: making `_keys` a generic suffix (a list of access keys would register
       only where it looks like a credential) and dropping the `_keys` suffix (`access_keys`, `secret_keys` would
       print).
    2. A state, mode or OAuth grant-type word is never registered (`names::MODE_WORDS`, read by
       `names::registrable`, the one filter, so under every leaf: `enabled`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`,
       `mandatory`, `anonymous`, `unauthenticated`, `inherited`, `client_credentials`, `oauth2_client_credentials`,
       `authorization_code`, `oauth2_authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, `device_code`, `jwt_bearer`, `implicit`,
       `oauth2_implicit`; any case, `-` and `_` ignored, letters, digits, `-` and `_` only, so `disabled!` is not one):
       `{"auth": "disabled"}`, eight characters and so registered whole by 187.3, withheld `status: "disabled"` and
       `"Server is disabled"` everywhere else. And a credential name's value that repeats a sibling member whose name
       ends in `type` or `mode` (`names::mode_values`, `names::repeats_a_mode`) and that the name rule reads as a
       credential name itself (`password`, `api_key`, `bearer`) is a mode: `{"auth": "password", "auth_type":
       "password"}` withheld `auth_type` and every `password` in prose. Both are still withheld in place; `password`
       with no such sibling, and a value that names no kind of credential beside a sibling that repeats it
       (`{"auth": "hunter2x-pw", "auth_type": "hunter2x-pw"}`), are registered as before. Rejected: raising the
       registration length (a dictionary password would print where echoed, the finding 187.3 fixed), a list of
       sibling names (`auth_type`, `grant_type`: the next mode member would cascade again), dropping a repeated value
       of any shape (a real password sent twice would print in the second member), and `password` as a mode word
       everywhere (`{"password": "password"}` would print its echo).
    3. An empty instance value of a schema (`default`, `const`, `enum`, `examples` holding `""`, `[]` or `{}`;
       `names::SCHEMA_VALUE_KEYWORDS`, `view::is_empty`) is printed under every property, in the traversal and the
       checker alike (rule 3e): the catalog's `client_secret` `"default": ""` printed `[withheld]` where TypeScript
       prints `""`. A non-empty value (`" "`, `[""]`) is still read under the stronger name and withheld, and so is an
       empty value under any other member of the schema. Rejected: printing every empty string under a credential
       name (an empty password is the password, 187.1) and printing an empty value under any schema member (a
       vendor's own member is a value of unknown meaning).
    4. Wording: COMPATIBILITY's "Rule 3a, the printed names" row no longer says the names TypeScript masks that
       airs-cli-rs prints are "exactly the `masked_*` fingerprints" (it lists more), and the doc of
       `names::CREDENTIAL_WORDS` says what 187.4 decided (a numeric PIN under a bare `pin` prints, under a credential
       name or inside a credential object it is withheld) instead of "a numeric PIN is a number, which no name
       withholds", stale since 187.1.
    5. §11 names where a change to the withholding rules starts (the name table, the value rules, the corpus, the
       checker, the traversal and the tests that pin them); TESTING.md §5.19 stays the procedure.
    Tests: `crates/airs-runtime-core/src/withhold_rules/names.rs::tests::key_name_lists_are_printed`,
    `…::mode_words_are_never_registered`, `withhold::tests::name_rule::d238_mode_words_under_credential_names_do_not_cascade`,
    `withhold::tests::schemas::d238_an_empty_schema_value_prints`, `withhold::tests::name_rule::the_design_table_is_the_name_rules`,
    the three new documents of `corpus::PINNED_DOCUMENTS` (run by `withhold::tests::corpus::the_live_tier_accepts_what_the_cli_prints`,
    `…::the_checker_names_every_value_the_cli_changes` and the harness's
    `live::gateway::tests::the_pinned_documents_are_checked_as_the_cli_prints_them`),
    `tests/gateway_inventory.rs::withholding::d238_guardrail_metadata_keys_and_empty_schema_defaults_print`,
    `…::d238_the_guardrail_catalog_withholds_nothing_ordinary` (the catalog fixture with the required-metadata eval
    and the empty `client_secret` default, printed as received), and the parity tests
    `tests/parity_gateway_inventory.rs::parity::inventory_reads_match_typescript` (`guardrails get` and
    `admin-guardrails get` with the `metadataKeys` check, byte for byte) and
    `…::divergence::d35_the_guardrail_catalog_differs_only_in_member_order`.

## 20. M6f Supplychain (0.11)

The specs this section is derived from are `docs/research/ts-supplychain.md` (cited as **SC§n**: every TS
`agentguard` command, the `inventory` walk, the layouts, the report collector and renderer, with byte captures) and
`docs/research/rs-sdk-supplychain.md` (cited as **SK§n**). This section overrides them where they differ; their
provisional candidate rows (SK§11 C1–C8) and gap numbers (SK§10 SC1–SC10) are not binding: the rows are D308–D325
and the gaps G61–G71 below (G71 is the first live run's finding, §20.16). TypeScript's `agentguard` is `supplychain` here, with every subcommand, option and alias,
and with no `agentguard` alias (MILESTONES renames; D308). Every difference from the TypeScript CLI is a §12 row
(D308–D325; D1, D30, D35, D47, D50, D52, D53, D64, D155, D156, D212, D214 and D226 extended). "The TS layout" below
means the bytes captured in SC§4–§5 and SC§9.4, with the changes this section lists. There are no writes: every
request of §20 is a `GET` (SC§10), and the only local files are the report and the debug log.

**SDK.** The pin stays scm-sdk `=0.2.2` (§15.23) with the `agentguard` feature added (`agentguard = ["models"]`;
`models` is already enabled by the existing features, so `Cargo.lock` does not change: chunk 1 verifies that the
lock-file diff is empty). The research measured scm-sdk 0.1.1; it was re-measured on 0.2.2 (2026-10-20): the
`src/airs/agentguard/` sources and `src/models/agentguard.rs` are byte-identical in both versions, the generated
AgentGuard models (`gen:1815-3990`) are identical, and the 107 schema nodes reachable from the ten AgentGuard roots
of `schema_graph.json` are identical. No AgentGuard response schema declares a string format (the only format checks
are the request `datetime` checks of `start_time` and `end_time`, nodes `s000201` and `s000203`), so the relaxed
response formats of 0.2.2 (D306) change nothing here; no response schema has a `ZodDefault` (G10 does not arise) or a
closed enum (D178 does not arise). `AgentGuardClient` has exactly the four reads `list_scans`, `get_scan_stats`,
`list_scan_vulnerabilities` and `list_rules`, with TypeScript's paths, planes, query keys and order, headers and
schemas (SK§0, SK§2). **Every supplychain SDK call still passes `RequestOptions::…without_response_defaults()`**
through one options helper (`supplychain::options`, choice 2). **Nothing in §20 is blocked on scm-sdk**; the scan list
works around a contract defect of it (G71, §20.16).

The findings of SK§10, numbered from G61:
- **G61** (SC1, API; CLI workaround adopted). `list_scan_vulnerabilities` takes no query at all (no `skip`, no
  `limit`): neither SDK can page findings, and whether the service pages them is unverified. The CLI compares
  `pagination.total_items` with the rows returned and fails closed when the answer is short (D319, §20.6). No raw
  request with an invented `skip` is sent.
- **G62** (SC2, semantics). `list_rules`'s `pagination.total_items` is the current page's row count, not the catalog
  size (the SDK documents it, `ag:client.rs:126`). The rules walk ignores it and continues only on a full page
  (§20.4); the pagination document's `total_items` is TypeScript's rule (§20.4).
- **G63** (SC3 = G7). With `with_retries(0)` the SDK makes no 401/403 refresh-and-replay; TypeScript replays once
  without counting. The CLI re-reads once after an `Http` 401 or 403 `Rejected` (`clients::reread`, as §15.17 and
  §18.12). It cannot see `x-opa-decision`, so it also re-reads an OPA-denied 403 that TypeScript sends once: harmless
  for a read (as §19.15).
- **G64** (SC4 = D35). `extensions` is a `BTreeMap`, so passthrough keys serialise sorted after the known keys
  (schema order); TypeScript keeps the server order of the passthrough keys. D35 is extended to the stats,
  rules and `--include-content` records, the vulnerabilities `pagination` and the rules table columns.
- **G65** (SC5 = D30). A 3xx is `Destination` and never followed; TypeScript's fetch follows it, re-sending
  `x-tsg-id` to the target and, when the target has the same origin, the bearer (fetch drops `Authorization` across
  origins; measured in chunk 1, `d30_supplychain_redirects_are_not_followed`). The CLI prints its request failure line
  without a status; TypeScript prints the line its followed request earns (no status for a network failure, the
  target's status otherwise); D30 extended.
- **G66** (SC6, limit; CLI setting adopted). The SDK's default response bound is 8 MiB (`rs:config.rs:290`), and the
  unpaged, content-bearing finding list can exceed it. `SupplychainClients` sets `Limits::max_response_bytes` to
  32 MiB and its validation bounds explicitly to the SDK's maxima (`clients::supplychain_validation_limits`:
  1,000,000 values, 16,000,000 work units): the engine would scale them from 32 MiB to 400,000 values
  (`ValidationLimits::for_bytes`, `rs:engine.rs:416`), which refuses an ordinary list of about 24,000 findings
  (about 16 MB) with the request failure line. With the maxima an ordinary finding list or scan page reads whole up
  to the 32 MiB bound (about 51,000 findings); a larger answer fails closed with its own line (D320). The SDK's
  decoder caps a document at 1,000,000 JSON values whatever is set and reports a denser answer within 32 MiB as a
  decode failure, which the CLI cannot tell from a malformed answer: it prints the request failure line (exit 1,
  nothing printed; fail closed; §20.17 choice 59). The raw scan read of G71, decoded without the SDK's schema, checks
  the same bounds on its answer (depth 64, 1,000,000 values; §20.16, choice 77).
- **G67** (SC7, names). The `--debug` operation names are the SDK's: `airs.agentguard.list_scans`,
  `airs.agentguard.get_scan_stats`, `airs.agentguard.list_scan_vulnerabilities`, `airs.agentguard.list_rules`. The
  debug tests pin them (as G9, G17, G23, G45); "AgentGuard" names the API (D308).
- **G68** (SC8, contract). The contracts are browser-derived and not yet live-qualified (the SDK's "Phase 8
  qualification is still required"). The required field sets are TypeScript 0.34.0's, so a response missing one fails
  both CLIs alike (a decode failure: the request failure line), except the scan list, which the first live run showed
  to break the contract (G71). The live tier (§10) is the qualification.
- **G69** (SC9, ergonomics). The option structs are `#[non_exhaustive]` with builders, numbers are
  `Optional<FiniteNumber>` and `extensions` must stay empty (a non-empty one is refused as an unknown key):
  `AgentGuardScanListOptions::builder().skip(Optional::Value(n.into()))…build()?`.
- **G70** (SC10, ergonomics). `AgentGuardStatsOptionsTimePeriod` is a one-variant `#[non_exhaustive]` enum
  (`Model30DAYS` ↔ `"30_DAYS"`): `--time-period` is checked against the literal during planning (§20.3) and the
  variant is sent.
- **G71** (live finding, 2026-10-20; contract defect of scm-sdk 0.2.2 and TypeScript 0.34.0; CLI workaround adopted,
  §20.16). The live service sends `null` in scan members both SDKs require as non-null strings: at least one row of
  the real tenant's `GET /v1/scans` has `"fingerprint": null` (a locally instrumented copy of the 0.2.2 validator
  reported the path only, `scans[] → fingerprint present=null`; it stops at the first issue, so other members may be
  `null` too: the SDK's `AgentGuardScanSchema` (`s000106`) rejects `null` in `uuid`, `tsg_id`, `created_at`,
  `updated_at`, `name`, `artifact_type`, `status`, `fingerprint`, `is_batch` and `child_scan_uuids`). `list_scans`
  then fails on both CLIs with a 2xx and the request failure line, so `scans list` is unusable, `scans vulnerabilities`
  cannot be given a uuid from a listing, and the report's Scans source is `unavailable`. The only AgentGuard response
  that contains `AgentGuardScan` is `AgentGuardScanList` (`list_scans`); the findings, statistics and rules reads are
  unaffected. A fix (`fingerprint` nullable; `name`, `artifact_type`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at` re-checked)
  is requested from the SDK's maintainer; the SDK is neither patched nor vendored. Workaround: the scan list is sent as
  the SDK's raw read on its AgentGuard data client and read by a CLI-side tolerant projection (§20.16; D324, D325);
  when an SDK release fixes the contract, the typed call can return (the projection's tests pin that the output is
  the typed model's for every page it accepts).
- G3, G4 and G7 apply unchanged (G7 is G63 here).

### 20.1 Build chunks

0.11 is built in two chunks. Each chunk ships its executable, parity and `dNN_` tests, registers only its own
commands (until a chunk lands its commands are not in the clap tree, exit 2, D1, and the group help lists only the
commands that exist) and leaves the checks green.

| Chunk | Commands | Shared work it introduces |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Clients and reads | `supplychain scans list\|ls`, `supplychain scans vulnerabilities <scanUuid> [--include-content]`, `supplychain stats`, `supplychain rules list\|ls` | the `agentguard` feature (no lock-file change); `clients::SupplychainClients` (data and management planes, one OAuth identity, 32 MiB); `src/supplychain/` (the argument checks, `options`, the failure lines, the page checks and pagination document on `walk_with` with `Spec::shrink_last_page`, the projections, the record and field tables, the status lines, the sensitive-data policy of §20.11); the planning of §20.3; the window checks on the shared zod datetime checker; the fixture's `Route::Supplychain(Sc)` read routes with their real shapes and markers (§20.13); D308 and D313–D321, D323 (reads) |
| 2. Report, doctor wording, live tier | `supplychain report`; the doctor's management-credential line (D312); the live tier's `live_supplychain_reads` | the collector `src/report/supplychain.rs` and its unit tests; `html::SUPPLYCHAIN` and an owned `report::Source::window` (the red team, runtime and gateway reports byte-identical); `commands/supplychain_report.rs` on `commands/report_command.rs`; `live::supplychain` and its self-tests; the TypeScript `--include-content` refusal of the live session guard; D309–D312, D322, D323 (report) |

### 20.2 Commands and options

Help texts, group descriptions and arguments are TypeScript's (SC§1, the captured `--help` of every leaf) with the
program name `airs`, `agentguard` read as `supplychain`, the `--output` line generated from the format policy
(§2.4), options and subcommands sorted (TS; a leaf's own options keep that order around the interleaved global
options, `cli::sc_order`, choice 81), and the changes below. A group without a subcommand (`supplychain`,
`supplychain scans`, `supplychain rules`) prints its help on stderr, exit 2 (D1). Both `list`s have the visible alias
`ls` (TS); there is no other alias and no `rm` (nothing is named `delete`, TS). Pinned leaf by leaf against the
reference by `help_texts_match_typescript` (the TypeScript side run under `agentguard`).

The root line is `supplychain  AI Supply Chain agent and skill scan telemetry (experimental, OAuth)` (TS). The leaves:

| Leaf | Arguments and options (TS help; defaults) | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `scans list\|ls` | `--limit <n>` (`Page size`, `10`), `--offset <n>` (`Starting offset`, `0`), `--all` (`Walk all pages`), `--max <n>` (`Maximum items with --all; 0 removes the cap`, `10000`), `--start <iso>` (`Inclusive creation time start (ISO timestamp)`), `--end <iso>` (`Creation time end (ISO timestamp)`) | the leaf `--output` is the global `--output` (§2.3): `pretty`, `table`, `json` (D50) |
| `scans vulnerabilities <scanUuid>` | `--include-content` (`Include source code, paths and finding text (sensitive)`) | as above |
| `stats` | `--time-period <period>` (`Verified period: 30_DAYS`, `"30_DAYS"`) | as above |
| `rules list\|ls` | `--limit`, `--offset`, `--all`, `--max` as `scans list` | as above |
| `report` | `--output-file <path>` (`New file in CWD by default; - for stdout; never overwrite`), `--max-pages <n>` (`Page budget per inventory (1–100, 10 rows/page)`, `40`), `--title <text>` (`Report title`, `"Supply chain environment report"`, D309), `--strict` (`Exit 1 after writing if any source is incomplete`) | description `Generate an aggregate-only 30-day HTML report` (TS `HTML/Markdown`, D155); the leaf `--output` is refused (D155), help `Refused by this command: the report is written as HTML (omit --output)` |

No other option is added or removed. Boolean flags take no value; a repeated scalar option takes its last value
(TS). The group descriptions are TS's: `scans` `Inspect agent and skill scans (read-only)`, `rules`
`Rule catalog (not effective tenant policy)`, the leaves `List one page of scans; sensitive metadata is excluded`,
`List finding metadata; --include-content explicitly reveals sensitive details`,
`Read server rolling 30-day skill statistics`, `List rule catalog defaults`.

**Which "AgentGuard" strings change** (choice 7; each changed string is its own §12 row): the command tree (D308),
the report's default title (D309), its file-name prefix (D310), its failure line (D311) and the doctor's
management-credential line (D312) change. These keep "AgentGuard" because they name the service or its API: the
report's product line `Prisma AIRS AI Supply Chain — AgentGuard`, the request failure line
`AgentGuard request failed…` (§20.3), the size-bound line (D320) and the SDK's `airs.agentguard.*` debug operation
names (G67). TypeScript's `Invalid AgentGuard query. …` text is not used: every check has its own text (D314).

### 20.3 Common rules

**Clients and planes** (SK§1.2). Every command that sends requests builds
`clients::SupplychainClients::build(config, session, secrets, debug)` from the selected tenant only:
- `supplychainDataEndpoint` (else `scm::constants::AGENT_GUARD_DATA_ENDPOINT`,
  `https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/aiag/data`), `supplychainMgmtEndpoint` (else `AGENT_GUARD_MGMT_ENDPOINT`,
  `…/aiag/mgmt`) and `mgmtTokenEndpoint` (else the §5 default), each admitted by §5 (the D48 message names the key,
  never the value; a trailing `/` of a base is ignored, both SDKs);
- the §3.5 management credential check before any client is built, with the §3.5 messages (D316); this is the
  management OAuth plane and never sends scanner credentials;
- `oauth_parts` (the lease-recording provider, one transport, the direct one when any of the three endpoints is
  loopback http, one `OriginPolicy` admitting both bases and the issuer), `Limits` with `max_response_bytes` = 32 MiB
  and the validation bounds at the SDK's maxima (G66), then `scm::airs::agentguard::AgentGuardClient::new(client, data, mgmt)` (OAuth required, `x-tsg-id:
  <mgmtTsgId>` forced on every request: TS parity, SC§2.1). A construction failure is
  `AISEC_SDK_ERROR:The supplychain client could not be configured` (exit 1).
- Planes (SC§2.1): **data** — `scans list`, `scans vulnerabilities`, `stats` and the report's Scans and Statistics
  sources; **management** — `rules list` and the report's Rules source.
- Every read command awaits the token before its first request, under the command's options (`authenticate`, as
  `ModelSecurityClients`); a token failure is a failure of the command (the request failure line below, with the
  token answer's status). `report` builds the client without a token request (§20.9). One token per invocation (TS).

No environment variable is read (§2.6): `PANW_AGENT_GUARD_*`, `PANW_MGMT_*`, `PANW_AI_SEC_TIMEOUT_MS`,
`PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG` and `PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG_BODY` change nothing (TS passes every value explicitly too, SC§2.1, but
reads the timeout and the two debug variables). The tenant keys are the 0.3 `supplychain*` names (§3.3 rows 17–18);
**no tenant wording changes** (§20.10).

**Request options** (one helper, `supplychain::options`, built just before each request is sent, as §18.20 choice 73;
every call `.with_retries(0)` and `.without_response_defaults()`; TS `numRetries: 0`, SC§2.1; choice 3):

| Calls | Options |
|---|---|
| a single page (`scans list`, `rules list` without `--all`), `scans vulnerabilities`, `stats` | `with_timeout(SINGLE_REQUEST_BUDGET)` (60 s) for the token and the read; the G63 re-read once after an `Http` 401 or 403 `Rejected`, under the same budget |
| an `--all` walk | one `with_timeout(WALK_BUDGET)` (300 s) for the token and every page; the G63 re-read per page request, under the walk's budget |
| `report` sources | §15.17: one `with_timeout(300 s)` budget per source for all its pages, the G63 re-read inside it |

So every supplychain request is sent once, plus exactly one re-read after a 401 or 403 (TS: `token, GET(401), token,
GET(…)`): a 429, a 5xx, a timeout and a transport error are never retried (TS parity; D10 does not apply).

**Validation order.** clap → `--output` (§2.4) → `--tenant`'s name format → the command's argument checks in the
order of its section (the report's `--debug` refusal first) → the debug log (§2.9) → the report's destination checks
(§20.9) → the tenant (§3.4, §3.7) → the tenant `defaultOutput` (the four reads; the report ignores it, TS) → the
credential check (§3.5) → the endpoints and the client → the token (reads) → the requests. Every usage error (exit 2)
comes before the tenant is read, makes no request and opens no debug log (D314; TS checks the query, the UUID, the
window and `--time-period` after the tenant read and `--max` after the credential check, SC§2.5).

**Argument checks** (D314, D315; exit 2; values in messages through `terminal_safe`, at most 200 characters with
`…`; in this order):
- `--limit`: decimal digits only (`^[0-9]+$`; leading zeros accepted, `007` is `7`, TS), 1 to 4,294,967,295, else
  `--limit must be a positive integer` (TS: `Pagination requires a safe nonnegative integer` at parse time for
  `abc`, `1.5`, `-1`, and `Invalid AgentGuard query. …` after the tenant for `0`).
- `--offset`: decimal digits only, 0 to 2^53 − 1, else `--offset must be a non-negative integer` (TS: the
  pagination text).
- `--max`: decimal digits only, 0 to 2^53 − 1, else `--max must be a safe nonnegative integer` (TS text; TS parses it
  with `Number()`, so `0x2`, `1e0`, `' 2 '` and `''` pass, SC§3; D315). Validated even without `--all` (TS), then
  ignored without it.
- `--start`, `--end` (`scans list`): each, when given, must match zod 3's `datetime({ offset: true })` grammar (a
  leap-year-checked `YYYY-MM-DD`, `T`, `HH:MM`, an optional `:SS` with an optional fraction of any length, then
  uppercase `Z` or `±HH:MM` / `±HHMM`; an empty value fails), else
  `--start must be an ISO-8601 timestamp with a timezone (for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z)` (`--end` alike); when
  both are given the start instant must not be after the end instant (equal passes), else
  `--start must not be after --end` (TS: the query text after the tenant). A value that matches the grammar but is
  not a valid instant (an offset `+24:00`) passes alone and is sent as typed, and fails the order check when both are
  given (TS: zod's regex passes it and `Date.parse` gives `NaN`, which the `start <= end` refine refuses; the SDK's
  `time_order` does the same). The values are sent as typed (TS). The grammar is the one checker model security's
  window (§17.3) and the gateway windows (§19.8) already share, `modelsec::datetime` (choice 43).
- `<scanUuid>` (`scans vulnerabilities`): the §7.1 shape (`pagination::is_uuid`: 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits, any case,
  the SDK and zod rule), else `Invalid scanUuid: <value> (expected a UUID)` (TS: the query text after the tenant;
  `../escape` is caught here, SC§7). A valid id is sent as typed: an uppercase id stays uppercase (TS).
- `--time-period` (`stats`): exactly `30_DAYS` (case-sensitive), else
  `--time-period must be 30_DAYS (the only period the service supports)` (TS: the query text after the tenant).
- The report's checks of §20.9.

**The request failure line** (TS `run`, `ag.ts:81-92`; choice 5). Every failure of a read after the client is built
(the token request, an HTTP error, a decode failure of any status, a timeout, a transport error, a refused
redirect, a page check or walk failure of §20.4, a walk bound) prints only TypeScript's line
`  ✗ AgentGuard request failed[ (HTTP <s>)]. Check credentials, query options and service availability. No upstream body is included.`
(stderr, red as one span, never quiet-suppressed, no error block) and exits 1, with an empty stdout. ` (HTTP <s>)` is
present only when the SDK error carries an integer status from 400 to 599 (`scm::Error::status()`: an `Http` error, a
token answer, a `Limit` with an error status), so a 2xx decode failure never shows `(HTTP 200)` and a 3xx shows none
(TS). No server text, path, query or SDK message is printed (TS parity; this is stricter than §6, so D11 does not
apply). Two Rust lines take its place in their cases: the size bound (D320)
`  ✗ AgentGuard response was larger than 32 MiB; nothing was printed. No upstream body is included.` (a `Limit` error
the SDK raised while reading an answer, failure kind `Http` and no error status: one answer over the bound; the
walk's own bounds of §20.4 are also `ErrorKind::Limit` (`pagination::incomplete_walk`) but carry no failure kind, so
they print the request failure line; `supplychain::is_oversized`) and the incomplete finding list of §20.6 (D319). Tenant, store, configuration, endpoint
(D48) and credential errors keep their §3.4, §3.5, §3.7 and §5 messages, and the construction failure its
`AISEC_SDK_ERROR` text (TS prints the generic line for all of them, SC§2.4; D316, as D212). A local SDK refusal
(`Validation`, `Limit` on a query) is the request failure line too, and nothing is sent: after planning only a query
over the SDK's 16 KiB URL bound can be refused (a `--start` that matches the grammar with a very long fraction). The
size line is only an SDK `Limit` raised while reading an answer (failure kind `Http`, no error status); the walk's
bounds and a local `Limit` carry no failure kind. The scan list's own line (D325, §20.16) takes its place for a page
the tolerant projection refuses: `  ✗ The AgentGuard answer does not match the API contract; nothing was printed. No upstream body is included.`

**Streams, quiet and formats** (D50). stdout carries data only, written once after success (§2.2), except the
incomplete finding list of §20.6 (its rows are printed before the failure line, as the session-cap rule of §18.13
step 4). There is no banner and there are no sections (TS: no `ui.header` in `ag.ts`). `pretty`, `table` and `json`
exist for the four reads; `markdown`, `csv` and `yaml` are invalid formats (exit 2, before the tenant; TS renders all
six). The tenant's `defaultOutput` is honoured by the four reads (TS resolves it for them, SC§2.2) and ignored by
`report` (TS). Status lines go to stderr, dim, quiet-suppressed; the failure lines are never suppressed. `--quiet`
never drops data (TS: the same table with an empty stderr, SC§2.3).

**The record and field tables** (TS `emit`, `ag.ts:44-80`, SC§5). `pretty` is **identical to `table`** (TS: `pretty`
is rendered as `table`): the §2.7 table (`render::table`, which is TS `formatOutput(…, 'table')`: no indent, every
header and body line starting and ending with one space, `│` and `─┼─`, display width, D53), then `"\n"`. The layout
is chosen by the document:
- **Record mode** (`scans list`, `scans vulnerabilities`, `rules list`): the rows are the document's record array
  (`scans`, `vulnerabilities`, `rules`). The columns are the union of the record keys in first-seen order (each record's
  keys in its printed JSON order, §20.5–§20.8), without `description` and `remediation`, cut to the first 9; each label
  is the key with every `_` replaced by a space. Cells are the §2.7 cell text (absent or `null` empty, strings through
  `terminal_safe`, numbers through `js_number`, booleans `true`/`false`, objects and arrays as compact JSON). The
  pagination object is never shown in a table. After the table the status line of §20.4 (D313). No rows: the table is
  the empty string, so stdout is `"\n"` (TS), and the status line says `Returned 0 records`.
- **Field mode** (`stats`, always; D318): the columns `Field` and `Value`, one row per top-level member in the printed
  JSON order (§20.7); the value is compact JSON for an object, an array and `null` (`null` prints `null`, TS
  `typeof null === 'object'`), the string itself for a string (`terminal_safe`), `js_number` for a number and
  `true`/`false` for a boolean. No status line (TS).

Tables are never coloured.

**JSON** (TS `JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)` + `"\n"`, SC§4). The documents of §20.5–§20.8, written by the 2-space JSON
writer: numbers through `js_number`, non-ASCII unescaped, every C1 control (U+0080–U+009F) written as a `\u00XX` escape
(the D212 writer option; D212 extended). Records printed whole (`rules`, `stats`, `--include-content` findings) are the
SDK models re-serialised: the known keys in schema order, then the passthrough keys sorted (G64, D35 extended;
TypeScript's zod output also puts the known keys in schema order, so only the passthrough order differs).

**Server text** (D52, D47). Every server string in a table cell goes through `terminal_safe` (TS writes ESC and LF raw,
which breaks the table, SC§5; D52 extended). Any printed server string (a cell, a JSON string value at any depth, a
member name) that contains a value of the invocation's `SecretSet` (raw, trimmed, form-encoded or base64: the tenant's
secret-named values, the Basic pair and every OAuth lease, §6) is printed as `[withheld]`, and an object member whose
name carries one is dropped with its value (D47 extended, as §19.3). Nothing a supplychain answer carries is
registered in the `SecretSet` (choice 21), so this rule withholds only the CLI's own credentials echoed by the service.

**Debug log** (D64 extended). The four reads have the debug policy `log` (§2.9): status and headers only, never a body
or a URL query, under the G67 operation names (TS records the URL with its `skip`, `limit`, `start_time`, `end_time`
and `time_period` query, bodies omitted, SC§2.7). `--include-content` changes nothing in the log: no finding content is
ever in it. `report` has the policy `refused` (D156, §20.9).

**Interruption** (D323; §2.5). Reads: `Interrupted; no data was written` (stdout empty; a signal while stdout is being
written: `the output was not completely written`, §2.5). The report's contexts are in §20.9. TS dies by the signal
with nothing printed (SC§2.6). Exit 130 / 143.

**Exit codes.** 0: success, a page or walk whose document says `truncated: true`, an empty list, a report whose health
is known (without `--strict`, or with every source complete). 1: tenant, store, configuration, endpoint and credential
errors; the request failure line (token, HTTP, decode, timeout, transport, redirect, a page check, a walk bound); the
size bound (D320); an incomplete finding list (D319); the report failure line; a report with `unknown` health or
`--strict` with an incomplete source. 2: every argument check of §20 (clap's included, D1). 130 / 143: interrupted.

### 20.4 Pages, walks and the pagination document (`scans list`, `rules list`)

TypeScript's `inventory` (`ag.ts:94-133`, SC§3) is the rule, ported onto the shared loop `walk::walk_with`
(`src/walk.rs`, §18.13) with its start offset, its per-page check (`check(skip, asked, page)`: it receives the page
size the request asked for, so the §20.4 page checks run there; choice 62) and one new `Spec` option, **`shrink_last_page`**
(default `false`, so every existing walk is unchanged; choice 11): with it, each request asks for
`min(--limit, cap − rows collected)` rows, and the short-page rule compares a page with the size it asked for. Here
`cap` is `--limit` without `--all`, and with `--all` the `--max` value (`0`: no user cap, the 1,000,000-item safety
bound of §7.2). **`--offset` is honoured with `--all`** (TS; the walk starts at it; unlike model security, §17.3;
choice 10). Captured: `rules ls --all --offset 5 --max 12` sends `skip=5&limit=10` then `skip=15&limit=2` (SC§3).

**Requests** (SC§3; the query keys in this order, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` values, `:` → `%3A`, `+` →
`%2B`, explicit zeros and `false` kept; the SDK emits exactly these bytes, SK§2):
- `scans list`: `GET <data>/v1/scans?skip=<s>&limit=<l>&isBackgroundRefresh=false[&start_time=<v>][&end_time=<v>]`;
- `rules list`: `GET <mgmt>/v1/rules?skip=<s>&limit=<l>`.

`<s>` is `--offset` plus the rows collected so far; `<l>` is the shrunk page size above.

**Without `--all`** one request is sent (TS returns after the first page whatever it holds; the walk is not entered).
**With `--all`** pages follow while the walk is not complete and fewer than `cap` rows were collected.

**Page checks** (every page, the single page included, in this order, before any of its rows is taken; any failure is
the request failure line, exit 1, nothing on stdout; SC§3's `Unstable pagination`, `Repeated identity`, `Invalid
total`, `Premature empty page`):
1. the page holds at most the requested number of rows;
2. `scans`: `pagination.total_items` equals the first page's (`rules`: not compared, G62);
3. every row's `uuid` is non-empty and was not seen earlier in this command;
4. `scans`: with rows collected, `--offset + rows collected` is at most the first page's `total_items`;
5. with `--all`, an empty page that does not complete the walk (`scans`: `skip < total_items`) fails.

**Completion.** `scans`: complete when `--offset + rows collected ≥ total_items`; `rules`: complete when the last page
held fewer rows than it asked for (an empty page included). A rules catalog of exactly `--limit` rows therefore looks
truncated without `--all` (TS parity, choice 13: no probe page).

**Bounds** (D317). The walk has the §7.2 bounds (100,000 pages, 512 MiB of rows, the 1,000,000-item ceiling behind
`--max 0`) and fails at one of them with the request failure line, no partial data (TS: 1,000 pages, then the same line).

**The pagination document** (TS keys and order, SC§3):
`{"total_items": <n|null>, "returned": <rows>, "skip": <--offset>, "next_offset": <n|null>, "truncated": <bool>}`:
- `total_items`: `scans` the first page's `total_items`; `rules` the rows returned when the walk is complete **and**
  `--offset` is 0, else `null` (G62);
- `next_offset`: `null` when complete, else `--offset + rows`; `truncated`: not complete.

Captured outcomes that the tests pin (SC§3): `scans list --limit 2` over 3 scans `{3, 2, 0, 2, true}`; `--offset 2`
`{3, 1, 2, null, false}`; `--offset 5` past a total of 2 `{2, 0, 5, null, false}`, exit 0; an empty first page with
`total_items: 5` without `--all` `{5, 0, 0, 0, true}`, exit 0 (choice 12); `--all --max 2 --limit 1` over 3
`{3, 2, 0, 2, true}`; `rules list` with a full first page of 10 `{null, 10, 0, 10, true}`; `rules list --all` over 25
rules sends `skip=0,10,20` and over 20 rules `skip=0,10,20` (the third page empty and complete).

**Status line** (D313; pretty and table only, after the table, stderr, dim, quiet-suppressed):
- complete: `  Returned <n> records; see JSON for pagination metadata.`;
- truncated: `  Returned <n> records; more are available (next --offset <next_offset>); see JSON for pagination metadata.`

(TS: `  Returned <n> records; see JSON/YAML for pagination metadata.` in both cases.) `scans vulnerabilities` prints the
complete form (its pagination is the server's, §20.6).

### 20.5 `scans list|ls`

Checks (§20.3): `--limit`, `--offset`, `--max`, `--start`, `--end`, the window order. Requests and walk: §20.4, the
query built as TS's `{skip, limit, start_time, end_time, isBackgroundRefresh: false}` (SC§6), `start_time`/`end_time`
only when given. The bounds filter on the server's `created_at`; the CLI does not filter rows (TS).

**The projection** (TS `ag.ts:164-174`; exactly these keys in this order): `uuid`, `artifact_type`, `status`,
`eval_outcome` (`null` kept), `created_at`, `vulnerability_count` (`summary.vulnerability_count`, `null` when
`summary` is `null`; never `0`), `attack_chain_count` (likewise), `is_batch`, `parent_uuid` (`null` kept). Built from
the tolerant scan of G71 (`supplychain::scans`, §20.16): every member but `uuid` may be `null` (or absent) and prints as
`null`; for a page the SDK's schema accepts it is the projection of the typed `AgentGuardScan` byte for byte. The scan
is never serialised whole. Never printed in any format, never logged and
never in a summary (TS parity, `it.spec:44-57`): `name`, `git_url`, `fingerprint`, `device_metadata`,
`error_message`, `eval_summary`, `eval_details`, `scanner_version`, `child_scan_uuids`, `batch_summary`, `tsg_id`,
`updated_at`, `duration_seconds` and every passthrough key (§20.11).

- json: `{"pagination": <§20.4 document>, "scans": [<projections>]}`.
- pretty and table: record mode; the columns `uuid │ artifact type │ status │ eval outcome │ created at │ vulnerability
  count │ attack chain count │ is batch │ parent uuid` (the TS capture of SC§5), `null` cells empty; the §20.4 status
  line.

### 20.6 `scans vulnerabilities <scanUuid> [--include-content]`

Check: the scan UUID (§20.3). Request: `GET <data>/v1/scans/<scanUuid as typed>/vulnerabilities`, no query, one
request (G61; SC§7). The answer is `{pagination{total_items, …passthrough}, vulnerabilities[]}`.

**Without `--include-content`** (the default): each finding is projected to exactly `uuid`, `scan_uuid`,
`vulnerability_type`, `attack_chain_count` (TS). Its `title`, `description`, `file_path`, `node_id`, `node_type`,
`node_name`, `remediation_description`, `original_code`, `suggested_code`, `type_description`, `attack_chain_uuids`,
`tsg_id`, timestamps and passthrough keys are not printed (§20.11).

**With `--include-content`**: each finding whole, as the SDK model re-serialised (known keys in schema order, then the
passthrough keys sorted, D35): its title, description, file path, original and suggested code, remediation text and
passthrough included (TS prints the parsed record whole). The content goes to stdout only, through the §20.3 rules
(the `SecretSet` rule; `terminal_safe` in tables; C1 escaped in JSON), and nowhere else: never on stderr, in an error,
the debug log, a status line or a live summary. After the output the status line (D321; stderr, dim,
quiet-suppressed)
`  Finding content included: source code, file paths and finding text can contain secrets from the scanned artifacts; keep this output private.`
Nothing inside the content is withheld by shape or name (choice 19): a `SECRET_EXPOSURE` finding shows the code that
holds the exposed value, which is what the flag exists for.

- json: `{"pagination": <the server's pagination: total_items, then its passthrough keys sorted>, "vulnerabilities": [...], "content_included": <bool>}`
  (TS keys and order; SC§4's capture).
- pretty and table: record mode. Without the flag the columns are `uuid │ scan uuid │ vulnerability type │ attack chain
  count`; with it the first 9 non-filtered keys, for a schema-valid finding `uuid │ tsg id │ created at │ updated at │
  scan uuid │ title │ vulnerability type │ file path │ node id` (`description` filtered; the rest are in JSON only,
  TS); the complete form of the §20.4 status line.

**Incomplete answers** (G61, D319; choice 16). When `pagination.total_items` is larger than the number of findings
returned, the rows are printed as above (stdout, every format), then the status lines, then
`  ✗ The service returned <r> of <t> findings for scan <scanUuid>; the list is incomplete (the API offers no paging)`
(stderr, red, never suppressed), exit 1. The line follows only rows that were written (`Output::commit_data`, the
final write's §2.5 mapping): a closed reader counts as written (EPIPE, as at the final write), while a signal before
the write (nothing is written; `Interrupted; the output was not completely written`, 130/143) and any other write
failure (`AISEC_SDK_ERROR:Output could not be written to stdout`, exit 1) are reported in its place (choice 78). A
`total_items` smaller than the rows is printed as it is (nothing is hidden; choice 17). TS prints the short list
silently, exit 0 (SC§7).

### 20.7 `stats`

Check: `--time-period` (§20.3). Request: `GET <data>/v1/stats/scans?time_period=30_DAYS` (the variant always sent,
G70; TS). The answer is `{unique_skills_scanned{count, percent_change|null}, total_vulnerabilities_found{…},
top_vulnerability{vulnerability_type, finding_count}|null, …passthrough}`.
- json: the stats model re-serialised (the three known members in schema order, nested members likewise, then the
  passthrough keys sorted, D35); `null` kept.
- pretty and table: **always field mode** (D318): `Field │ Value` rows `unique_skills_scanned`
  (`{"count":4,"percent_change":12.5}`), `total_vulnerabilities_found` (`{"count":7,"percent_change":null}`),
  `top_vulnerability` (`{"vulnerability_type":"SECRET_EXPOSURE","finding_count":3}` or `null`), then one row per
  passthrough key, an array as compact JSON (TS switches to record mode when any member is an array, and the three
  statistics disappear, SC§5); no status line.

### 20.8 `rules list|ls`

Checks: `--limit`, `--offset`, `--max` (§20.3). Requests and walk: §20.4, with no total (G62). The catalog is defaults,
not effective tenant policy (help, TS).
- json: `{"pagination": <§20.4 document>, "rules": [<each rule whole: uuid, name, vulnerability_types, default_state, description, remediation, then the passthrough keys sorted>]}`
  (TS prints the rule whole; catalog text, not tenant data; choice 22).
- pretty and table: record mode; the columns `uuid │ name │ vulnerability types │ default state` (`description` and
  `remediation` filtered, TS), then the passthrough keys in first-seen order of the printed records (sorted within a
  record, D35: the column order differs from TS only when the service adds keys), at most 9 columns;
  `vulnerability_types` as compact JSON (`["SECRET_EXPOSURE"]`); the §20.4 status line.

### 20.9 `report` (the supplychain environment report; chunk 2)

The TypeScript collector (`src/reports/agentguard.ts`, SC§9.3) and renderer (`environment-render.ts`, SC§9.4) are
ported unchanged except for the format (D155), the debug refusal (D156), the title and file name (D309, D310), the
failure line (D311), G63, the budgets, the time parsing (D322), the destination checks (D214, D226) and interruption
(D323). The report is already safe in TypeScript (aggregates only, fixed vocabularies, no-clobber, 0600, CSP).

**Argument checks** (exit 2, in this order, before the tenant and any request; SC§9.1): 1. `--debug` (policy
`refused`): `Disable --debug for environment reports to avoid persisting sensitive traffic content` (D156; TS names
`PANW_AI_SEC_DEBUG` too); 2. `--output` given (any of `pretty`, `table`, `json`; the others already failed §2.4):
`The environment report is written as HTML; omit --output` (D155; TS `Report output must be html or markdown`);
3. `--max-pages`: decimal digits (leading zeros accepted, `007` is 7, as `--limit`), 1 to 100, else
`--max-pages must be between 1 and 100` (TS text; TS prints
`Pagination requires a safe nonnegative integer` for a non-number, at parse time, before the debug refusal; D314);
4. `--title` blank under JavaScript `trim()` or longer than 240 UTF-16 units: `--title must contain 1–240 characters`
(TS); 5. `--output-file` given and blank under `trim()`: `--output-file cannot be empty` (TS).

**Destination** (§15.17, §19.15): `--output-file -` is stdout. Otherwise `--output-file`, else
`airs-supplychain-report-<UTC ISO time with ':' → '-'>-<first 8 hex of a v4 UUID>.html` in the working directory
(TS `airs-agentguard-report-…`, D310), made absolute (TS `resolve`). Before the tenant
(`report_command::check_destination`): a last component that is not a file name (D226), anything at the path
(`lstat`, a dangling symlink included; TS) and a parent that is not an existing directory (D214; TS collects first and
fails at the write, SC§9.2) are the failure line (exit 1, no request).

**Collection** (TS order and rules, SC§9.3). The client (`SupplychainClients::build`, no upfront token: a token failure
is a failure of each source, so a token 401 makes three token requests and three `unavailable` sources, TS); no
`Collecting …` status line (TS prints none; choice 31). `end` = the time collection starts, `start` = `end` − 30 × 24 h,
both `report::iso` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`); `collectionStartedAt` = `end`, `generatedAt` = the time collection
ends. The three sources, one after the other, each under its own §20.3 budget:

| # | Source / method / window | Requests |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Scans`, `listScans()`, `<start> to <end>` | `GET <data>/v1/scans?skip=<rows so far>&limit=10&isBackgroundRefresh=false&start_time=<start>&end_time=<end>` |
| 2 | `Statistics`, `getScanStats()`, `Server rolling 30_DAYS` | `GET <data>/v1/stats/scans?time_period=30_DAYS` |
| 3 | `Rules`, `listRules()`, `Current catalog` | `GET <mgmt>/v1/rules?skip=<rows so far>&limit=10` |

The collector is TS's verbatim over the typed answers (`src/report/supplychain.rs`; choice 32):
- **The page loop** (TS `pages`, `rep.ts:78-119`, not `walk_with`): page size 10, at most `--max-pages` pages, `pages`
  counted after each successful read; a page fails when `total_items` is not a safe non-negative integer or it holds
  more than 10 rows; `Scans` also when `total_items` differs from the first page's or the rows would exceed it; any
  page when a `uuid` is empty or repeated; `Scans` ends when the rows reach `total_items`, `Rules` at a page of fewer
  than 10 rows; an empty page that does not end the walk fails; after `--max-pages` pages the note
  `Reached the <n>-page budget.` and a failure. A failure with rows collected makes the source `partial` with the note
  `Inventory incomplete: pagination changed, repeated, stopped early, failed or reached its budget.` and keeps the
  rows; with none the source fails.
- **The source wrapper** (`rep.ts:46-77`): a source starts `unavailable` with 0 pages and 0 records; a finished read is
  `complete` unless marked `partial`; a failed one is `partial` with records, else `unavailable`, plus the note
  `Request or validation failed; no upstream error body included.` (no `HTTP <code>` note, TS; unlike red team);
  every source that is not complete adds the finding `review` · `<name> incomplete` · the notes joined by a space ·
  `Check service access or increase the page budget, then regenerate.` · `<name>`.
- **Scans**: the rows whose `created_at` is a usable time within `[start, end]` inclusive in milliseconds are kept;
  when any row is excluded the source is `partial` with the note
  `Rows with missing or out-of-window creation timestamps were excluded.` A usable time (D322; choice 30) is a zoned
  ISO-8601 date-time read by `report::parse_iso` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm[:ss[.fff…]]`, `T` or `t`, then `Z`, `z` or
  `±hh:mm`) or a date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` read as UTC midnight (the gateway rule, §19.15; ECMAScript reads it as UTC
  too); a zone-less date-time and every other form are unusable (TS `Date.parse` reads them in the host's zone or
  loosely). The leaf rows are those kept with `is_batch` false and an empty `child_scan_uuids`; each is counted under
  `"<label(artifact_type, SKILL|AGENT)> / <label(eval_outcome, BLOCKED|ALLOWED|PENDING|ERROR)>"`, where `label` gives
  `UNKNOWN` for `null` and `OTHER` for any value outside the list (case-sensitive: `skill` is `OTHER`). The table
  `Scan outcomes` (note `Collected <records> rows; excluded <kept − leaf> parent/batch rows. <Partial inventory only.|Complete inventory for requested window.>`,
  headers `Artifact / outcome`, `Scan rows`, rows sorted by TS `localeCompare`, which over this closed ASCII vocabulary
  is byte order) is added only when the read returned rows or completed; the findings `attention` · `Blocked scans
  require review` · `<n> collected non-parent scan rows have BLOCKED evaluations.` · `Inspect the affected scans and
  findings before approving the artifacts.` · `Scans` (any leaf `BLOCKED`) and `review` · `Scans without a completed
  decision` · `<n> collected non-parent rows are pending, failed or have an unfamiliar status.` · `Review scan status;
  absence of a completed decision is not a passing evaluation.` · `Scans` (leaves whose `status` is not `COMPLETED` or
  whose outcome is neither `ALLOWED` nor `BLOCKED`).
- **Statistics**: the table `Skill statistics` (note `Server aggregates; percentage changes may be unavailable.`,
  headers `Metric`, `Count`, `Change (%)`, rows `Unique skills scanned` and `Vulnerabilities found` with the count
  and `percent_change` (both `Cell::Number` through `js_number`; both SDKs validate `count` as a non-negative safe
  integer, so a non-integral or negative count fails the Statistics source on both CLIs, while `percent_change` is
  the server's JavaScript number, `-3` or `1e-7` as in TS (choice 49); `null` → `Cell::Null`, rendered `Unknown`)); when
  `total_vulnerabilities_found.count > 0` the finding `attention` · `Skill vulnerabilities reported` · `<n> findings
  reported in the server statistics window.` · `Review vulnerability details and remediate before use; findings are not
  a count of distinct vulnerable skills.` · `Statistics`; records 1, pages 1; `top_vulnerability` unused.
- **Rules**: the table `Rule catalog defaults` (note `These are not effective tenant policy settings.`, headers
  `Default state`, `Rules`, rows `label(default_state, BLOCKING|ALLOWING)` counts, sorted).
- **Health**: `unknown` when every source is `unavailable`; else `attention` when any finding is `attention`; else
  `review` when any finding exists; else `no-findings`. The findings in TS order: the Scans findings, the Scans
  incomplete finding, the Statistics finding or, when the Statistics read failed, the Statistics incomplete finding,
  the Rules incomplete finding (not sorted).

Only aggregates are kept: no scan name, id, URL, fingerprint, device metadata, rule text, finding text or server
string reaches the document (labels are allow-listed; TS `ut.spec:11-28`, `:86-99`). The reader hands the collector
only `ScanRow` (`uuid`, `created_at`, `artifact_type`, `status`, `eval_outcome`, `is_batch`, the count of
`child_scan_uuids`), `RuleRow` (`uuid`, `default_state`) and `Stats` (the two metrics) built from the typed SDK answers
and, for the scans, G71's tolerant read (`commands/supplychain_report.rs`, `scan_row`, `rule_row`, `stats_of`; choices
50, 71), so the exclusion holds by type; a `pagination.total_items` that is not a non-negative safe integer fails its
page, a scan page the tolerant read refuses fails its page (the generic note) and a statistic the SDK cannot read
fails the source. A `ScanRow` member is `None` for a `null` (G71): a `None` creation time is a missing one (excluded,
the timestamp note), a `None` status is not `COMPLETED` (unsettled), a `None` artifact type or outcome is `UNKNOWN`,
and batch membership is read from either signal (choice 84): `is_batch` `true` or at least one child is a parent
(excluded) whatever the other holds, `false` with no child is a leaf, and only a kept row neither signal decides (a
`None` where the other does not show a parent) is left out of the outcome counts and the two findings (it could be a
parent counted beside its children) with the note
`Rows with unknown batch membership were excluded from outcome counts.` and the source `partial`; the table note's
`excluded <n> parent/batch rows` counts the decided parents only.

**Tokens** (measured in chunk 2). The client fetches the token on the first request of each source and keeps it: one
token request per run when the issuer answers (TS, `writes_html_with_the_typescript_reads`); an issuer 401 fails each
source on its own token request, so three token requests and no API request (SC§9.3's capture,
`a_token_failure_fails_every_source`; the G63 re-read follows only an API answer's 401 or 403).

**Model and rendering.** `{schema 1, product "Prisma AIRS AI Supply Chain — AgentGuard" (TS; it names the service),
title, collectionStartedAt, generatedAt, window, health, sources, findings, tables}`, rendered by
`html::render(report, &html::SUPPLYCHAIN)`: `html::Profile { product: "Prisma AIRS AI Supply Chain — AgentGuard",
window_label: "30-day scan inventory; rolling 30_DAYS statistics; current rule catalog", footer_label: "Experimental
browser APIs", limitations: &report::supplychain::LIMITATIONS }` with TS's five limitations (`rep.ts:37-41`, SC§9.4)
verbatim. The document is TypeScript's byte for byte (times normalised; with the same `--title` on both sides): the
shared CSP (the red team hashes, SC§9.4), `&#<code>;` escaping, `Unknown` for `null` cells, numbers through
`render::js_number` (`12.5`, `-3`, `1e-7`), the `Evidence and completeness` table with the source windows, one
trailing `\n`. `--title` is written as given (escaped; control characters kept: the document is data, TS parity; the
default title D309). The Markdown renderer is not ported (D155). `report::Source::window` becomes an owned string
(the Scans window holds the run's times); the red team, runtime and gateway documents stay byte-identical (their
parity and unit tests unchanged).

**Publishing and exit** (§15.17, `report_command::publish` and `conclude`). stdout delivery writes the document as the
stdout data (a closed pipe or write error is the failure line, exit 1; TS `it.spec:152-166`); a file goes through
`files::publish_new` (exclusive temp, fsync, link, 0600, never overwriting), then
`  Report → <abs path, \p{Cc}\p{Cf} → _> (mode 0600)`; then, when any source is not complete,
`  <n> source(s) incomplete; review the evidence section.` (both status lines TS, quiet-suppressed). Exit 1 when the
health is `unknown` (the document is still written) or `--strict` and a source is incomplete; otherwise 0. Any error
after the checks (the destination checks, a tenant, store, configuration or credential error, the client, a write)
prints only `  ✗ Supply chain report failed. Check credentials and a writable, new output path. Existing files are never overwritten.`
(D311; stderr, red as one span, never suppressed, no path, OS error or server text), exit 1 (`report_command::conclude_with`
with the report's line; the red team, runtime and gateway reports keep `conclude` and their own line). The tenant,
store, configuration, endpoint and credential errors are this line too (TS; D316 is the reads' row). Interrupt contexts (D323):
`no report was written` (no file, no temporary), `the report was saved in <path>` once it was published.
