### 20.11 Sensitive data per command

| Command | Printed (stdout only) | Never printed |
|---|---|---|
| `scans list` | the 9-key projection: ids, artifact type, status, outcome, creation time, counts, batch flag, parent id (`null` where the service sent `null`, G71) | scan `name`, `git_url` (which can hold `https://user:token@…`), `fingerprint`, `device_metadata`, `error_message`, `eval_summary`, `eval_details`, `scanner_version`, `child_scan_uuids`, `batch_summary`, `tsg_id`, `updated_at`, `duration_seconds`, passthrough keys: in no format, error, log or summary (TS) |
| `scans vulnerabilities` | the 4-key projection and `content_included: false` | finding titles, descriptions, paths, nodes, code, remediation text, type descriptions, passthrough keys |
| `scans vulnerabilities --include-content` | each finding whole (JSON), its first 9 columns (tables), `content_included: true`; the D321 notice on stderr | the content anywhere but stdout: never on stderr, in an error, the debug log or a live summary |
| `stats` | the server aggregates and their passthrough keys | — |
| `rules list` | the rule catalog records (descriptions and remediation in JSON only) | — |
| `report` | aggregates, counts, allow-listed labels, the title and window | scan names, ids, URLs, fingerprints, device metadata, rule text, finding text, server text (TS) |
| every command | the fixed failure lines (with an HTTP status at most) | server text, bodies, queries; bodies and queries in the debug log (D64); the invocation's credentials (`[withheld]`, D47) |

`git_url` is never parsed for printing, so the gateway's URL rule (D251) has nothing to apply to; its parts are not
registered in the `SecretSet` either (choice 21). Fixture markers make this testable (§20.13). G71's tolerant read keeps
less than the typed model did: only the nine projected members and the child count (choice 67), so `name`, `git_url`,
`fingerprint`, `device_metadata`, error text and evaluation details are not even held in memory after the page is read.

`Route::Supplychain(Sc)` in `crates/airs-test-harness` (`src/server/supplychain.rs` with the dataset
`SupplychainData`, its knobs and `seed_supplychain`/`supplychain(edit)`/`sc_requests`; `src/fixtures_supplychain.rs` with

check covers them (already in its key list). Every route checks the `mock-token-<tsg>` bearer **and**
`x-tsg-id: <tsg>`, records the raw query, and answers only `GET`.

|---|---|

**The report's scans** (chunk 2). The report filters on the run's own clock, so its tests seed
`fixtures::supplychain::recent_scans()`: the 12 scans above with their members and order unchanged and their creation

inside) and 112 (`garbage`). `recent_zoned_scans()` leaves out 110 for the scenarios that compare bytes with
TypeScript, which reads a zone-less time in the host's zone. The seeded dataset gives the report `AGENT / ALLOWED`,
`AGENT / BLOCKED`, `OTHER / ALLOWED`, `OTHER / OTHER`, `SKILL / ALLOWED`, `SKILL / BLOCKED`, `SKILL / ERROR`,

**Real shapes** (the 0.10 lesson, choice 40): every answer uses the shapes of SC§4 and SK§4.2, with the service's key
order (the documented field order, **never sorted**: `uuid, tsg_id, created_at, updated_at, name, git_url,
artifact_type, status, error_message, summary, eval_outcome, eval_summary, eval_details, duration_seconds, fingerprint,

(`summary`, `eval_summary`, `eval_details.rule_outcomes[]`, `device_metadata` maps, `top_vulnerability`), `null` in
every nullable member, realistic content (multi-line code, paths with directories, rule texts with punctuation) and

the pagination object, so D35 and the projections are exercised on what the service sends. A fixture the CLI's own
models would re-serialise identically is not a fixture of the service.

The existing per-route plans give the knobs: 401 once (the G63 re-read), 403 twice, 403 with `x-opa-decision: false`,
429, 500, 503 with `Retry-After`, 302 to another loopback port, a hang (timeouts, interrupts), malformed JSON, a 2xx
failing the schema (a statistics answer without one of its metrics; a scan page is G71's tolerant read, so a scan
without a `uuid` or with a member of another type stands for its refusal), and for the walks an empty page while the
total says more, a repeated `uuid`, an empty `uuid`, a total that changes between pages, more rows than `limit`, and
rows beyond the total.

**G71's rows** (`fixtures::supplychain::null_scans`, ids 113–115, `NULL_SCANS`; §20.16): the same real shape and member
order with the `null`s the service sends: 113 is a complete `SKILL`/`BLOCKED` scan with `"fingerprint": null` and nothing
else changed (the observed row); 114 has every member but `uuid` `null` (`tsg_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `name`,
`git_url`, `artifact_type`, `status`, `error_message`, `summary`, `eval_outcome`, `eval_summary`, `eval_details`,
`duration_seconds`, `fingerprint`, `scanner_version`, `device_metadata`, `parent_uuid`, `is_batch`, `child_scan_uuids`,
`batch_summary`); 115 is `AGENT`/`ALLOWED` with `name`, `fingerprint` and `device_metadata` `null`, a summary whose
`vulnerability_count` is `null` and a `null` passthrough member. `recent_null_scans()` moves 113 and 115 an hour before
the run (114's creation time stays `null`). The seeded dataset is unchanged, so every existing parity scenario still
compares the pages both SDKs accept.

**Deep rows** (`fixtures::supplychain::deep_scans(depth)`, §20.16 choice 77): the seeded scans with the first scan's
`eval_details` in the service's shape (`rule_outcomes`, `skill_override_applied`, `unknown_findings`) whose rule outcome
carries an `evidence` chain of `{"context": …}` objects ending in a marked string, so that the deepest value of the page
sits at `depth` (`json_depth`, the root at 0, the SDK's preflight count). Depth 64 is accepted by the SDK's scan-list
schema and prints as the seeded rows do; 65 is the typed call's `Limit` and the request line.

**Markers.** `PRIVATE-` never appears on stdout without `--include-content`, nor ever on stderr, in the debug log, the
report or a live summary (the runner's leak check enforces it on every airs-cli-rs `supplychain` run: the marker is a
forbidden form everywhere, or on stderr and in the debug log only when the arguments carry `--include-content`,
`is_supplychain_command`); `FAKE-SECRET-<tsg>` and the tokens never appear anywhere. **Over-withholding** (the 0.10
lesson): the same suites assert that ordinary data prints unchanged in every format: a rule description that says
"secret token", a finding path `src/password_reset.py`, a finding whose code holds `api_key = os.environ["KEY"]`,
timestamps, ids and counts are never `[withheld]`; only a planted copy of the tenant's own
`mgmtClientSecret` (and a token) inside a finding or a rule is.

### 20.16 G71: scan pages with `null` members (the first live run)

The first live run (2026-10-20) agreed with TypeScript on `stats`, `rules list` and the report's other sources, but
`scans list` failed on both CLIs with a 2xx and the request failure line: the service sends `"fingerprint": null`
(at least) where both SDKs require a string (G71). The scan list is therefore read by the CLI, not by the SDK's typed
`list_scans`; every other read stays typed (only `AgentGuardScanList` contains `AgentGuardScan`; choice 75).

**The read** (`supplychain::scans::send`; choice 64). `RawRequest::read("/v1/scans")` with TypeScript's query pairs in
the SDK's order and value forms (`skip`, `limit` as JavaScript numbers, `isBackgroundRefresh=false`, then `start_time`
and `end_time` when given; the SDK's 16 KiB query bound is the engine's own: its preflight refuses a longer query as a
`Limit` with no failure kind before the request is sent, so the request line and nothing sent, as before; choice 82),
sent with `send_optional_json::<serde_json::Value>` on `AgentGuardClient::data_client()`: the client the typed call
uses, so the OAuth bearer and `x-tsg-id`, the origin policy (no redirect followed, G65) and the 32 MiB bound (D320) are
the same (`tests/supplychain_reads.rs::g71::the_raw_scan_read_keeps_the_typed_calls_rules` pins the 302, the size line
and the G63 re-read on this path). An empty 2xx body is the SDK's `Decode` (the request line), not `{}` (choice 83).
The raw read's decoder alone allows depth 128, so the validation bounds (G66) are checked by the CLI on the decoded
answer (`supplychain::scans::within_bounds`, choice 77, against `SupplychainClients::validation`, the bounds the client
was built with, computed once per command; choice 87): the SDK's preflight, iterative, the root at depth 0, no value deeper than 64, at most 1,000,000 values and
32 MiB of keys and strings; an answer past them is an `scm::Error` of kind `Limit` without a status or failure kind,
so the request failure line, as the typed call prints it (`scans vulnerabilities`, a typed `Limit` at status 200).
The work bound (16,000,000) counts the typed schema walk's steps, which this read does not take: the projection reads a
fixed number of members per scan, so its work is bounded by the value count. The options
are the command's (`supplychain::options`: the budget, `with_retries(0)`); the G63 re-read is the caller's
(`clients::reread` for `scans list`, `SourceBudget::read_typed` for the report). The SDK names a raw read
`custom.read` (`RawRequest::named` is crate-private), so the send runs inside `debug::named("airs.agentguard.list_scans",
…)`, a task-local scope under which the debug transport logs a `custom.read` attempt with that name; the token request
and every other operation keep their names, and the record is still status and headers only (G67 holds; choice 70).
The task-local reaches the transport only because scm-sdk 0.2.2 awaits `Transport::send` inside the caller's future
(no spawned task, channel or worker): a pin constraint, written at `debug::named` and pinned by
`tests/supplychain_reads.rs::g71::no_scan_page_is_logged_as_a_raw_read` (choice 88).

**The tolerant projection** (`supplychain::scans::project`; choices 65–68). The answer must be an object whose
`pagination` is an object with `total_items` a non-negative safe integer and whose `scans` is an array of objects (the
SDK's rules). Each scan's `uuid` must be a string (the SDK's rule; empty and repeated ids are still the page checks of
§20.4 and the report's page loop). Every other member the CLI reads accepts `null`, and an absent member reads as
`null`: `artifact_type`, `status`, `eval_outcome`, `created_at`, `parent_uuid` (a string or `null`), `summary` (an
object or `null`; its `vulnerability_count` and `attack_chain_count` each a non-negative safe integer or `null`),
`is_batch` (a boolean or `null`) and `child_scan_uuids` (an array, only counted, or `null`). Any other type of a read
member, a scan without a string `uuid`, or a page without its total refuses the whole page: nothing is printed and the
command prints the contract line (D325), never the rows it could read (no row is dropped). The members the CLI never
prints (`name`, `git_url`, `fingerprint`, `device_metadata`, `error_message`, `eval_summary`, `eval_details`,
`scanner_version`, `batch_summary`, `tsg_id`, `updated_at`, `duration_seconds`, the passthrough members) are neither
validated nor kept.

**Output** (D324). The projection of §20.5 from the tolerant scan: a `null` member is `null` in JSON (the nine keys and
their order unchanged) and an empty cell in pretty and table (the §2.7 cell rule), the counts `null` when `summary` or
the count is `null`. For every page the SDK's schema accepts the output is byte-identical to the typed-model projection (scm-sdk 0.2.2 `AgentGuardScan`)
(`scans_tests::accepted_answers_project_as_the_typed_model_did` compares the two over the seeded, recent and numeric
edge pages; every existing parity test is unchanged). The report reads the same tolerant scans (§20.9, choice 71).
TypeScript refuses such a page with its generic line (`  ✗ AgentGuard request failed. …`, exit 1) and its report's
Scans source is `unavailable`.

**Failures** (D325; choice 69). A page the projection refuses prints
`  ✗ The AgentGuard answer does not match the API contract; nothing was printed. No upstream body is included.`
(stderr, red, never quiet-suppressed, exit 1, stdout empty, no server text), on a single page and on any page of an
`--all` walk (`supplychain::Failure::Contract` through `inventory`; the walk stops at that page; choice 76). An answer
that is not JSON, or that exceeds the SDK decoder's bounds, is still the SDK's `Decode` and prints TypeScript's request
line (as choice 59), and so does an empty 2xx body (choice 83), a typed read's 2xx failing its schema (`stats`, `rules list`, `scans
vulnerabilities`) and an answer past the G66 bounds (the `Limit` above; on any page of a walk too; in the report the
page fails with the generic note). In the report a refused page fails its page like any other failure (the generic note, §20.9).

**Live tier** (§10; choices 72, 85, 86). TypeScript prints the same status-less request line for a timeout, a network
error, a body that is not JSON and a credential error, so the line alone is no evidence. A scan read (the json and
table checks of `scans list`) passes with the note
`airs-cli-rs reads rows the shared contract refuses (G71); TypeScript refuses the answer` only when airs-cli-rs exits 0
with at least one row (the json projection or the table) and TypeScript fails with exactly that line, with nothing on
stdout, on the first read and again on the re-read; a TypeScript refusal on the first read only lets the re-read decide
as any other answer, and one on the re-read only fails with
`TypeScript refused the answer on the re-read only; G71 needs the refusal on both reads`; anything else stays a
mismatch. The vulnerabilities checks then read the first scan airs-cli-rs listed, on both CLIs (choice 73). The report
pair may differ in its Scans source alone (`reports_agree_g71`: TypeScript's source `unavailable` with the failed note,
the other sources equal, and the table titles equal as a multiset once one `Scan outcomes` is taken from the Rust side)
only when the json and the table checks both passed as G71 in the same flow and no TypeScript scan run exited 0. The
content run, the report re-read and the leak checks are unchanged.

### 20.17 Choices decided

Every decision was delegated; each takes the safest option that keeps the command useful (the rejected alternative in
each item).
1. Enable scm-sdk's `agentguard` feature at the `=0.2.2` pin; the lock file does not change (verified in chunk 1). The
   0.2.2 sources, models and the 107 reachable schema nodes equal 0.1.1's, so the research holds. Rejected: a newer SDK
   (none is needed).
2. Every call passes `without_response_defaults()` through `supplychain::options`, though no response default is
   reachable. Rejected: omitting it (a future default would print a value the server did not send).
3. Retries: one attempt plus the G63 re-read for every request (TS `numRetries: 0`). Rejected: the SDK read retries of
   D10 (a §12 row with no safety gain; extra load on an experimental API; the TS specs pin the request counts).
4. Reads await the token first, and a token failure is the request failure line with its status (TS bytes); the report
   keeps TS's lazy per-source token. Rejected: the §6 `AISEC_OAUTH_ERROR` text for reads (a second message family for
   the same failure; D212's precedent keeps the TS line).
5. API, token, decode, timeout, transport, redirect and walk failures print TS's fixed line with at most the status.
   Rejected: the §6 messages (they print allowlisted server problem text; TS's line prints none).
6. Tenant, store, configuration, endpoint and credential errors keep their own messages (D316). Rejected: TS's generic
   line (it hides a missing credential behind "request failed").
7. Rename per string: the tree (D308), the default title (D309), the file prefix (D310), the report failure line
   (D311), the doctor line (D312); kept, because they name the service or its API: the product line, the request
   failure line, the size line and the `airs.agentguard.*` operation names. Rejected: renaming every "AgentGuard"
   (the service is still called AgentGuard, and the product line is the report's evidence of its source) and renaming
   none (MILESTONES covers titles and doctor wording).
8. Every argument check before the tenant with a flag-specific text (D314); `--max` and `--max-pages` keep TS's own
   flag texts (`--max-pages must be between 1 and 100` also for a non-number). Rejected: TS's shared texts (they do not
   name the flag) and red team's `--max-pages must be an integer from 1 to 100` (another command's TS text).
9. `--max` decimal digits only; `--limit` at most 4,294,967,295 (D315). Rejected: `Number()` coercion (`0x2`, `''`)
   and an unbounded `--limit` (the walk's page size is a `u32`).
10. `--offset` is honoured with `--all` (TS parity). Rejected: model security's refusal (TS documents the offset in the
    pagination document's `skip`).
11. The walk is TS `inventory` on `walk_with` with the new `Spec::shrink_last_page` (TS's last-page size on the wire),
    a single page is one request, and the bounds are §7.2's (D317). Rejected: a separate supplychain loop (a second copy
    of the shared rules) and TS's 1,000-page bound (`--max 0` would not mean "no cap").
12. A single page that is empty while `total_items` says more is printed with `truncated: true` and exit 0 (TS); with
    `--all` it fails. Rejected: failing the single page (TS prints it, and D313's line says more are available).
13. The rules document keeps `total_items: null` and a catalog of exactly `--limit` rules looks truncated (TS).
    Rejected: probing one more page (a request TS never sends; the document already says `truncated`).
14. The record-table status line says JSON only and names `--offset` when the listing is truncated (D313). Rejected:
    the TS text verbatim (it names the dropped YAML and reads the same for a page and a whole inventory).
15. `stats` is always the field table (D318). Rejected: TS's array switch (a server addition hides the statistics).
16. An incomplete finding list prints its rows and fails with exit 1 and a named line (D319). Rejected: a warning with
    exit 0 (the gateway's D248; an automated gate on findings would pass a truncated list) and exit 1 with an empty
    stdout (a large scan's findings could never be read, since the API cannot page).
17. A `total_items` below the rows is printed as received. Rejected: failing it (nothing is hidden by a low total).
18. The response bound is 32 MiB with its own line (D320). Rejected: the 8 MiB default (a large unpaged finding list
    could never be read) and no bound (TS; unbounded memory).
19. `--include-content` prints the findings as TS does, on stdout only, with the D321 notice; inside the content only
    the `SecretSet` rule and `terminal_safe` (tables) apply. Rejected: withholding credential-shaped text in the content
    (it would hide the evidence a `SECRET_EXPOSURE` finding exists to show, and shape rules are unreliable on code),
    refusing the flag when stdout is a terminal (the flag is already the explicit opt-in) and no notice (TS).
20. The default finding projection is TS's four keys. Rejected: adding `title` or `file_path` (they can carry secrets
    from the scanned code).
21. The scan projection is TS's nine keys; nothing a supplychain answer carries is registered in the `SecretSet`.
    Rejected: registering `git_url`'s userinfo and query (no printed field can carry them, and a short password would
    withhold timestamps and ids: over-withholding).
22. Rule descriptions, remediation and passthrough keys print in JSON (TS; catalog text). Rejected: dropping them
    (they are the catalog's content and carry no tenant data).
23. The vulnerabilities `pagination` prints with its passthrough keys (TS; D35). Rejected: `total_items` only (it would
    drop server paging hints G61 may need).
24. A scan UUID is sent as typed, uppercase kept (TS). Rejected: lowercasing (another path than TS sends).
25. Control characters: `terminal_safe` in tables (D52), C1 escaped in JSON (D212), the report title kept and escaped
    (TS; red team and gateway choice 49). Rejected: stripping them from the document (the HTML escaping already makes
    them inert, and the title is the user's text).
26. The debug log records status and headers only, under the SDK's `airs.agentguard.*` names (D64, G67); no content is
    ever in it. Rejected: renaming the operation names in the log (they are the SDK's).
27. The report is HTML only, refuses `--debug`, ignores `defaultOutput` (D155, D156, TS). Rejected: Markdown (dropped).
28. The report's destination is checked before the tenant: the last component, `lstat`, the parent (D226, D214).
    Rejected: TS's late parent failure (three sources read for a file that cannot be written).
29. The report's budget is 300 s per source with `with_retries(0)` and the G63 re-read (the red team model). Rejected:
    TS's 60 s per attempt and no total, and one shared budget (one slow source would fail the rest).
30. Report times: zoned ISO date-times and date-only as UTC (D322; the gateway rule). Rejected: `Date.parse`'s host
    zone and loose forms (results would depend on the host), and refusing date-only (deterministic in TS too).
31. No `Collecting …` status line (TS). Rejected: red team's line (not TS's text for this report).
32. The page loop, notes, findings, health and their order are TS's verbatim, without an `HTTP <code>` note.
    Rejected: red team's HTTP note (a TS difference with no safety gain).
33. A token failure in the report makes three `unavailable` sources, writes the document and exits 1 (TS). Rejected:
    failing the whole report before writing (TS writes the diagnostic document).
34. The renderer gains `html::SUPPLYCHAIN`; `report::Source::window` becomes owned; the other reports stay
    byte-identical. Rejected: a supplychain copy of the template (the bytes are the shared template's).
35. No supplychain doctor check (TS has none, MILESTONES lists none); only the credential line changes (D312).
    Rejected: a probe (no TypeScript counterpart to agree with).
36. No tenant wording changes (the keys and the import rename shipped in 0.3). Rejected: new key aliases.
37. Interruption prints the §2.5 contexts (D323). Rejected: TS's silent exit.
38. Help texts are TS's with the program name; the report description drops "/Markdown" and `--output` reads as
    refused. Rejected: new help texts.
39. The live flow is reads only, one page each, `--include-content` Rust only and in memory; a tenant without AI
    Supply Chain access records `supplychain unavailable` and passes (the 0.8 model-security precedent). Rejected:
    `--all` walks live (outside the one-page rule) and running TypeScript with `--include-content` (it prints scanned
    code into a captured stream).
40. Fixtures use the real shapes, unsorted key orders, nested objects, nulls, realistic content and over-withholding
    checks (§20.13). Rejected: the simplified sorted fixtures that hid three defects in 0.10.
41. Two chunks (§20.1): the clients and every read first, then the report, the doctor wording and the live tier.
    Rejected: one chunk (the report and the live tier depend on the clients and fixtures of the reads).
42. `--time-period` is the exact, case-sensitive `30_DAYS` (TS zod literal). Rejected: case-folding (`30_days` fails in
    TS).
43. The window grammar is the zod `datetime({offset: true})` checker model security and the gateway already share
    (`modelsec::datetime`); an empty value fails; equal bounds pass; a matching value that is not an instant passes
    alone and fails the order check with the other bound (TS). Rejected: a supplychain copy of the grammar.
44. pretty is the table and an empty list prints `"\n"` (TS bytes). Rejected: the management-list empty phrase (not
    TS's output for these commands).
45. `defaultOutput` is honoured by the four reads (TS). Rejected: ignoring it (TS resolves it there).
46. A `<scanUuid>` that starts with `-` is read as an option, so it is a parse error (exit 2, D1; commander also reads it
    as an option). Rejected: accepting hyphen values for the positional (the value would fail the UUID check anyway,
    with a message that quotes what may be a mistyped flag).
47. Record-table labels and field-table member names are server text: they go through `terminal_safe` like the cells
    (D52), and a member name that carries a `SecretSet` value is dropped with its value (D47). Rejected: printing the
    names raw (TS; a passthrough key could carry control characters).
48. An incomplete finding list (D319) prints its rows, then the status lines (D313 complete form, D321 with the flag),
    then the D319 line last; `--quiet` drops only the status lines. Rejected: the failure line before the status lines
    (the last line on stderr is the one an operator and a script read).
49. (chunk 2) The statistics' counts are `Cell::Number` like their `percent_change`, and the evidence text of the
    vulnerability finding uses `js_number`. Both SDKs validate `count` as a non-negative safe integer (TS `SDK:9403`,
    the Rust schema's `int` and `min 0` checks), so a non-integral or negative count fails the Statistics source on both
    CLIs and only `percent_change` reaches the report as the server's JavaScript number (`-3`, `1e-7`), as in TS; the
    report parity's `numbers` scenario renders and compares that table, and `a non-integral count` pins the refusal on
    both. Rejected: `Cell::Count` (a `u64` cell for a value the model holds as a number; no output would differ).
50. (chunk 2) The report's reader maps the typed SDK answers into aggregate-only rows (`ScanRow`, `RuleRow`, `Stats`)
    before the collector sees them; the collector cannot reach a name, URL, fingerprint, device metadata or text.
    Rejected: the ordered JSON documents of the red team and gateway collectors (the exclusion would rest on the
    collector reading the right members only).
51. (chunk 2) The live tier's scanned-content markers are a plan list of their own, `LivePlan::content_markers`, checked
    like `extra_secrets` on every stream and in the summary, except on the stdout of the one run whose
    `RunPlace::content_stdout` is set (the Rust `--include-content` run); its stderr and debug log stay checked.
    Rejected: `extra_secrets` (it would stop the content run itself) and no marker check on that run (a marker on its
    stderr would pass).
52. (chunk 2) A live check that disagrees is re-run once on both CLIs and the second comparison decides (noted
    `(after one re-read)`); `live_supplychain_reads_reread_once_when_the_data_rolls` pins both outcomes. Rejected: no
    re-read (the service's scans and statistics roll between two runs) and a re-read until agreement (unbounded runs).
53. (chunk 2) A Rust gate failure that is not 401, 403 or 404 is a mismatch and stops the flow (`the gate failed`).
    Rejected: running the other checks (every later read would fail the same way and multiply the noise).
54. (chunk 2) The report's tenant, store, configuration, endpoint and credential failures print the report's line
    (D311, TS), unlike the reads (D316). Rejected: the §3 messages here (the report keeps one failure line in every
    TS-shared report, §15.17, §19.15).
55. (review) The stdout of the Rust `--include-content` live run is checked for the plan's secret forms without the
    JWT-shape heuristic, and the flow checks the shape on that document with its finding rows emptied
    (`live::supplychain::outside_findings`; a stdout that is not the document is checked whole): a finding that exposes
    a bearer token is the content this flag prints. Its stderr, its debug log and every other run keep the full check.
    Rejected: the full check on that stdout (any JWT-exposing finding aborts the tier as a false leak) and no shape
    check on it at all (the CLI's own token outside the rows would pass).
56. (review) A live check that differed and whose re-read both CLIs answer 401, 403 or 404 fails
    (`differed, then unavailable: … on re-read (first: <masked note>)`), and the flow goes on with the first Rust run.
    Rejected: the `unavailable` row of the re-read (it drops the difference, and the empty listing then skipped the
    finding and content checks with the run passing).
57. (review) The Rust content run refused with 401, 403 or 404 after the plain read of the same scan answered is a
    failing row (`content run refused after the plain read succeeded: HTTP <s>`); it is `unavailable` only when the
    plain read was. Rejected: `unavailable` in both cases (the D321 policy check would silently not run).
58. (review) D318 is tolerated in its shape only: the Rust field rows equal the json pair's statistics document member
    by member (an array row parsed back to its array) and the TS table is the record table of one of those arrays (row
    count, header labels as a set). Rejected: any table difference once the json has an array member (a passthrough
    array hid a differing count) and a cell-exact model of the TS record table (TS's cell formatting is not this
    check's subject; the counts and labels show the shape).
59. (review) The supplychain client sets the SDK's maximum validation bounds (1,000,000 values, 16,000,000 work) beside
    the 32 MiB byte bound (G66); a denser answer than the SDK decoder's fixed 1,000,000-value cap prints the request
    failure line. Rejected: the bounds the SDK scales from 32 MiB (400,000 values refuse an ordinary 16 MB finding list
    that TS prints) and the D320 size line for that decode failure (the SDK reports it as `Decode`, indistinguishable
    from a malformed answer, and the line would claim a size the answer does not have).
60. (review) The Rust content run's findings that are not the plain read's (the data rolls) run the Rust plain read and
    the content run once more, and the second pair decides (choice 52's one re-read; noted `(after one re-read)`); the
    TypeScript plain read does not run again (the content check is Rust-only and its row already decided).
    `live_supplychain_reads_reread_the_content_run_once_when_the_findings_roll` pins both outcomes. Rejected: no re-read
    (a scan whose findings change between the two reads fails the tier) and re-running the content run alone (a
    rolled list would never match the stale uuids).
61. (review) A report pair that differs runs once more on both CLIs and the second pair decides (choice 52); a Rust
    file holding a `SecretSet` value or a listed scan uuid fails at once with its own note.
    `live_supplychain_reads_reread_the_report_once_when_the_data_rolls` pins both outcomes. Rejected: no re-read (the
    scans and statistics roll between the two runs) and re-reading a leak (a defect, not rolling data: a clean second
    file would hide it).
62. (review) `walk::walk_with`'s per-page check is `check(skip, asked, page)`: it receives the page size the request
    asked for, so the supplychain page checks run in the hook with plain mutable state, and every other caller ignores
    the size (behaviour unchanged). Rejected: running the checks inside the fetch closure (the only place the size was
    known), which needed `Cell`/`RefCell` to share the state between the closure and the listing.
63. (review) One `member` and one `count` helper (`supplychain::{member, count}`) serve the reads, the projections and
    the report reader; one `pagination::MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (with `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER_F64`) serves the supplychain flags,
    the report's counts and `walk::total_of`; `supplychain::failure` takes the `scm::Error` and decides the size line
    with `is_oversized` itself. Behaviour unchanged. Rejected: the per-module copies and the `ReadFailure` wrapper (a
    derived flag that a hand-built value could contradict).
64. (G71) The scan list is read by the CLI: the SDK's raw read on its AgentGuard data client, decoded by a CLI-side
    tolerant projection (§20.16), until an SDK release fixes the contract. Rejected: keeping parity and failing (the
    command, the uuid for `scans vulnerabilities` and the report's Scans source are unusable on real tenants), patching
    or vendoring the SDK (a fork of a pinned dependency for one schema) and waiting for the SDK fix (0.11 would ship a
    command that cannot list).
65. (G71) Every member the CLI reads but `uuid` accepts `null`, and an absent member reads as `null`; a `null` prints as
    each layout prints `null` today. Rejected: skipping the rows that hold a `null` (it hides data: a listing would
    look complete while scans are missing), printing a placeholder such as `unknown` (not what the service sent; JSON
    consumers would read a string) and requiring each member's presence (an absent member is the same unknown value).
66. (G71) A scan without a string `uuid` refuses the page (the contract line); an empty or repeated `uuid` stays the
    §20.4 page check. Rejected: dropping that row (silent loss) and inventing an id (it would be given to
    `scans vulnerabilities`).
67. (G71) The members the CLI never prints are neither validated nor kept. Rejected: validating every documented member
    (a type drift in a member nobody prints would refuse the list again) and keeping the raw scan (the name, git URL,
    fingerprint and device metadata would sit in memory for no output).
68. (G71) The page, its `pagination.total_items` (a non-negative safe integer) and its `scans` array keep the SDK's
    rules. Rejected: tolerating a `null` total (the §20.4 checks and the completion rule need it; a walk could not be
    shown complete).
69. (G71) The contract line (D325) is printed only for a page the tolerant projection refuses; a body that is not JSON
    or exceeds the decoder's bounds, and a typed read's 2xx failing its schema, keep TypeScript's request line.
    Rejected: one contract line for every 2xx `Decode` (the SDK reports its 1,000,000-value cap as `Decode` too, so the
    line would claim a contract mismatch an answer may not have, choice 59) and keeping TypeScript's line for the
    projection's refusals (it sends the operator to check credentials for an answer that arrived).
70. (G71) The raw read is logged as `airs.agentguard.list_scans` through `debug::named`, a task-local scope the debug
    transport reads only for a `custom.read` attempt. Rejected: logging `custom.read` (the G26 precedent, but the
    command's record would change name for an internal workaround) and naming by URL in the transport (a second,
    path-based routing table).
71. (G71) The report reads the tolerant scans: a `null` creation time is missing (excluded with the timestamp note), a
    `null` status is unsettled, `null` labels are `UNKNOWN`, and a row of unknown batch membership (neither signal
    decides, choice 84) is left out of the outcome counts with its own note and the source `partial`. Rejected: reading a `null` `is_batch` as `false`
    (JavaScript's falsy reading; a parent could be counted beside its children) and leaving such rows out silently.
72. (G71) The live tier passes a scan read only when TypeScript fails with exactly its status-less request line and
    airs-cli-rs exits 0 with the projection (json) or a table, both with rows and on both reads (choice 85), and
    tolerates the report's Scans source only after both listing checks passed as G71. Rejected: tolerating any TypeScript failure (a real defect on either side would pass) and a
    Rust-only scan check (the json comparison would never run again once the SDK is fixed).
73. (G71) The vulnerabilities checks read the first scan airs-cli-rs listed and still run on both CLIs. Rejected: a
    Rust-only comparison (TypeScript reads a scan's findings by uuid without listing, so the comparison holds).
74. (G71) The fixtures carry the `null`s in the service's shape (`null_scans`, member order unchanged) beside the
    seeded dataset, which stays as it was. Rejected: removing members (an absent member is not what the service sends)
    and changing the seeded dataset (every parity scenario would compare a TypeScript failure).
75. (G71) Only the scan list leaves the typed SDK call; `stats`, `rules list` and `scans vulnerabilities` stay typed.
    Rejected: raw reads everywhere (their contracts hold live, and the SDK's validation is the check there).
76. (G71) A refusal travels as `supplychain::Failure::Contract` (the other variant is the SDK error): `inventory`'s read
    returns `Result<ListPage, Failure>`; inside the walk a refusal stops `walk_with` through its `scm::Error` channel and
    a flag local to `inventory`, set only where the read returned `Contract`, turns that stop back into `Contract`;
    `read_failure` prints the line. Rejected: an `scm::Error` built by the CLI to stand for the refusal (a `Decode`
    without a status: an SDK error of that shape would print the contract line, choice 63's derived-flag concern) and
    an error type parameter on `walk_with` (every walk of §7.2 would change for one caller).
77. (review, G66) The raw scan read checks the SDK's validation preflight on the decoded answer
    (`scans::within_bounds` with `clients::supplychain_validation_limits`: depth 64, 1,000,000 values, 32 MiB of keys
    and strings) and refuses an answer past them as a `Limit` (the request failure line, the typed call's line);
    `scans_tests::the_validation_bounds_are_the_typed_calls` pins that the SDK's scan-list schema at the same bounds
    draws the same line (depth 64 accepted, 65 a `Limit`), and the loopback tests pin depth 64 printing every row as
    the seeded data does. Rejected: documenting the decoder's bounds (depth 128) for the raw read (a page the typed
    call refused would print, and every other supplychain read keeps 64) and the contract line for it (the answer may
    match the contract; the typed reads print the request line for the same bound).
78. (review) A command that prints its rows and then a failure line (D319 here; the partial listing of
    `runtime dashboard`, §18.12, through the same helper) commits through `Output::commit_data`, the final write's
    §2.5 mapping: written rows or a closed reader (EPIPE) are `Ok` and the line follows; a pending signal writes nothing
    and returns `Interrupted` with `the output was not completely written` (130/143); another write failure returns
    the stdout failure (exit 1). `finish` uses the same helper. Pinned by
    `output::tests::commit_data_reports_what_the_write_did` and the closed-reader case of
    `tests/supplychain_reads.rs::an_incomplete_finding_list_fails_closed`. Rejected: discarding the commit result
    (a cut-off list was reported only as incomplete, with the signal's own context lost) and a supplychain-only match
    (a third copy of the §2.5 mapping beside `finish` and `report_command`).
79. (review) Every "non-negative safe integer" check of the supplychain code calls `walk::total_of` directly (the
    scan page's `total_items`, the summary counts, the report's page totals, D319's `total_items`); the scan
    projection's summary reader is `scans::summary_count`, so `supplychain::count` (choice 63) is the only helper of
    that name. Behaviour unchanged. Rejected: the three thin wrappers (two `safe_count`s with different signatures and
    a `total`), which hid the shared rule.
80. (review) The document pass of D47 (`withhold`: every string and member name against the `SecretSet`) lives in
    `secrets.rs` and the D212 JSON writer (`json_text`, `escape_c1`) in `json.rs`; runtime, gateway and supplychain
    import them from there, and `supplychain::views` keeps no pass-through. Behaviour unchanged (the runtime unit tests
    moved with the functions). Rejected: importing them from `runtime::views` (a change made for runtime output would
    silently change gateway and supplychain output) and a copy per feature.
81. (review) The supplychain list options take explicit help positions (`cli::sc_order`: `--all, --end, --limit,
    --max, --offset, --start`), because the flattened paging struct otherwise listed its four flags before `scans
    list`'s window; `help_texts_match_typescript` (reads and report) now compares the leaf options' order with
    TypeScript's, the global options aside. Rejected: declaring the window inside the shared paging struct (`rules
    list` would gain `--start` and `--end`) and sorting the global options in as well (it would change the help of
    every command of every milestone). `gateway telemetry`'s leaves list their flattened filters before the window
    too; §19.2 makes no order promise, so 0.10's help is left as it is.
82. (post-gate review) The raw scan read leaves the 16 KiB query bound to the SDK engine: its preflight
    (`config::resolve`, before authentication and dispatch) refuses a longer query as a `Limit` with no status and no
    failure kind, the error `ScanQuery::pairs` raised itself, so the request line and no GET, on a single page and in a
    walk (`tests/supplychain_reads.rs::failures::failures_print_the_typescript_line_only`). Rejected: keeping the local
    copy as a pre-send guard (a second copy of the SDK's rule, which would drift silently from the engine's, and the
    engine also checks the whole URL, which the copy did not).
83. (post-gate review) An empty 2xx body of the scan list is the SDK's `Decode` (the request line), as a body that is
    not JSON: the read is `send_optional_json`, and its `None` becomes `Decode`. TypeScript prints the same line
    (`tests/parity_supplychain_reads.rs::parity::failures_match_typescript`). Rejected: `send_json`'s `{}` for an empty
    body (the projection then refused a page that never arrived with the contract line, D325, against choice 69: no
    answer arrived to mismatch the contract).
84. (post-gate review) The report reads batch membership from either signal: `is_batch` `true` or a non-empty
    `child_scan_uuids` is a parent whatever the other holds (`null` included), `false` with no child is a leaf, and
    only a row neither decides is of unknown membership (the note, `partial`; `report::supplychain::batch_membership`,
    `supplychain_tests::either_batch_signal_decides_a_parent`). Rejected: requiring both members known (a parent the
    service flags plainly was reported as unknown and the source `partial`) and JavaScript's falsy reading of `null`
    (a parent could be counted beside its children).
85. (post-gate review) The live tier needs evidence for G71: airs-cli-rs exits 0 with at least one row, and TypeScript
    refuses with its status-less line on the first read and on the re-read of the same check; the report's G71
    tolerance needs the json and the table checks both so and no TypeScript scan run that exited 0
    (`live::supplychain::Reads::scan_compared`). TypeScript prints that line for a timeout, a network error, a body
    that is not JSON and a credential error too, and an empty listing has no row the contract could refuse.
    `live_supplychain_reads_need_rust_rows_for_g71` and `live_supplychain_reads_need_the_refusal_twice_for_g71` pin
    both. Rejected: one refusal on one check (a transient TypeScript failure passed as G71 and loosened the report
    comparison) and comparing the report's Scans source Rust-only (the comparison would never run again once the SDK is
    fixed).
86. (post-gate review) The report's G71 tolerance compares the table titles as a multiset with one `Scan outcomes`
    taken from the Rust side (`live::supplychain::ReportShape::tables`). Rejected: counting one more table section on
    the Rust side (a Rust report that dropped a table and added two passed).
87. (post-gate review) The supplychain validation bounds are computed once per command, when the client is built,
    and kept on `SupplychainClients::validation`; the raw scan read checks every page against that value (the bounds
    the typed calls validate with). Behaviour unchanged. Rejected: computing `supplychain_validation_limits()` per page
    (repeated work, and a second value that could differ from the client's).
88. (post-gate review) `debug::named` documents its pin constraint: the task-local name reaches the transport only
    because scm-sdk 0.2.2 awaits `Transport::send` in the caller's future;
    `tests/supplychain_reads.rs::g71::no_scan_page_is_logged_as_a_raw_read` fails when any scan page (a single page,
    the G63 re-read, every page of a walk) is logged as `custom.read`. Rejected: the unit test of the scope alone
    (`debug::tests::named_raw_reads_take_the_scoped_operation` cannot see the SDK moving the attempt to another task).
89. (post-gate review) Red team and runtime use `pagination::MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (choice 63's one constant); the
    gateway keeps its `i64` bound (signed paging arithmetic). Behaviour unchanged. Rejected: the private `u64` copies.
90. (0.11 CI fix) `tests/supplychain_report.rs::interrupt::a_signal_after_the_report_is_saved_names_it` holds the run
    with the runner knob `RunOptions::fill_stderr` (harness only, no CLI change): the child starts on a stderr pipe the
    runner has already filled (its filler is left out of the capture), so its first stderr write blocks until
    `Running::release_stderr`. The report writes nothing to stderr before its `Report →` line, which follows the
    publish and the interruption context, so the run is held right after the file is saved, however little it writes
    there; the test asserts the whole stderr, those lines included. Rejected: `RunOptions::stall_stderr` alone (it
    holds a run only once its writes exceed the pipe buffer; the report's last lines are far shorter, so the run could
    exit before the signal, and the Linux CI job and an Alpine host failed with `the CLI did not record SIGINT`), a
    sleep or a retry (timing, not a hold), a debug-build pause hook in the CLI (a second production test hook where the
    harness alone suffices, choice 129), and moving the assertion to a unit test of `report_command::publish` (the
    executable path, signal thread and exit code would go untested).

## 21. 1.0 Rename and distribution

1.0 changes the name the program is invoked under and how it is distributed. The product, the crate (`airs-cli` on
crates.io) and the repository keep the name airs-cli; only the executable changes, to `airs`. `airs-cli-rs` stays
through 1.x as a compatibility name. No command, flag, exit code, stream, request or data byte changes; the only
observable change is the program name in the texts of §21.4. This section is binding for both chunks and overrides
any earlier section that quotes the program name. The settled scope (MILESTONES "1.0") is not re-opened here: the
name is `airs`, the compatibility name is `airs-cli-rs`, there is no `airs-cli` alias (it would collide with the
TypeScript CLI's npm `bin`), and directories, store formats, environment variables and tenant keys do not change.
**8.0 amends this section** (§21.15–§21.17): the Rust CLI replaces the TypeScript CLI in `cdot/prisma-airs-cli` and
on npm, so `airs-cli` becomes a third name of the same program (D330), doctor gains the `Executable` check (D331),
and npm becomes a distribution channel; where §21.2–§21.14 say there is no `airs-cli` name, they describe 1.x.

"airs-cli-rs" remains the name of this Rust implementation and its repository in prose (this document, TESTING,
COMPATIBILITY, the harness), where it tells the Rust CLI from the TypeScript `airs-cli`. Every command line, example,
executable path and output text says `airs` (§21.4, enforced by §21.6).

No SDK work in the rename and distribution chunks: they do not touch `scm-sdk`. The 1.0 release also moves the pin
to `=0.2.3` (the same features, §15.24, with its own rows D327–D329), which opens no SDK gap either (G72 is
unused). The rename adds one §12 row, D326 (the executable name); the program-name texts are folded into D73, and D26, D41, D90,
D160, D227, D229 and D308 are updated in place (D151, D175 and D215 note that their format names are kept).

### 21.1 Build chunks

1. **Chunk 1, the rename** (code, help, messages, tests, docs): the two `[[bin]]` targets and `default-run`
   (§21.2); clap's fixed `name` and `bin_name`; `store::PROGRAM = "airs"` and every text of §21.4; the uv download
   user agent; every test on `CARGO_BIN_EXE_airs`, the harness normaliser and the compatibility tests (§21.6,
   §21.13); the live tier's binary (§21.11); the CI musl job's binary paths and artifact names; the docs pass of
   §21.12 (README usage sections, DESIGN, TESTING, COMPATIBILITY, MIGRATION, AGENTS). No distribution files.
2. **Chunk 2, distribution**: `scripts/release.sh` (the tarball layout with the compatibility link, `--bin airs`
   builds, the new packaging checks, the release name), the new `scripts/package-release.sh`, the Homebrew template
   `packaging/homebrew/airs-cli.rb.in` and `scripts/homebrew-formula.sh` with their offline tests and fixtures
   (§21.7–§21.9), `docs/RELEASING.md`, the README `Install` and `Upgrading to 1.0` sections (§21.10), the MILESTONES
   definition of done for 1.0, TESTING's prerequisites, CI's `jq` step (choice 51). Chunk 2 changes no Rust source
   under `src/`.

Neither chunk bumps the version: the orchestrator sets `version = "1.0.0"` in `Cargo.toml` at release. Neither chunk
creates a remote repository, pushes, publishes or contacts a service (the tap repository, the crates.io publish and
the tap commit are the orchestrator's, §21.8).

### 21.2 The executable and the compatibility name

`Cargo.toml` declares two binaries and runs `airs` by default:

```toml
default-run = "airs"

[[bin]]
name = "airs"
path = "src/main.rs"

# The TypeScript CLI's name (DESIGN §21.2, 8.0): the same program, so 7.x scripts keep working.
[[bin]]
name = "airs-cli"
path = "src/bin/airs-cli.rs"

# The 1.x compatibility name (DESIGN §21.2): the same program under its 0.x name.
[[bin]]
name = "airs-cli-rs"
path = "src/bin/airs-cli-rs.rs"
```

`src/bin/airs-cli-rs.rs` (and, from 8.0, `src/bin/airs-cli.rs`) is exactly one doc comment line and
`include!("../main.rs");`, so every binary is built from the same `main` and calls the same `airs_cli_rs::run`; they
cannot differ. The library target keeps the name
`airs_cli_rs` (choice 13). `[package] description` drops "(executable airs-cli-rs until 1.0)" and reads
`Native Rust CLI for Prisma AIRS (the airs command), built on the scm-sdk crate`.

**The name never depends on how the binary was started.** The root command is
`#[command(name = PROGRAM, bin_name = PROGRAM, version, …)]` with `store::PROGRAM = "airs"`. With `bin_name` set,
clap never derives it from `argv[0]`, so `airs`, `airs-cli-rs`, a symlink with any other name and a path such as
`./target/debug/airs-cli-rs` all print `Usage: airs …`, the same help, the same D91 usage line and the same messages.
Nothing else reads `argv[0]`. For every invocation the compatibility name (and from 8.0 `airs-cli`) prints the same
bytes on stdout and stderr and exits with the same code as `airs` (D326, D330). No deprecation notice is printed in 1.x (choice 5); the compatibility
name is dropped no earlier than 2.0, announced in that release's notes.

How each install path provides the names (the `airs-cli` column from 8.0):

| Install path | `airs` | `airs-cli` (8.0) | `airs-cli-rs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cargo install --locked airs-cli` (and `cargo install --path .`) | the `airs` binary | a `[[bin]]`: another copy of the same program | a `[[bin]]`: another copy (about 22 MB each); a 0.x install's `airs-cli-rs` is replaced by it on upgrade |
| `cargo build --release` | `target/release/airs` | `target/release/airs-cli` (a copy) | `target/release/airs-cli-rs` (a copy) |
| release tarballs (§21.7) | the signed `airs` | a relative symlink `airs-cli -> airs` | a relative symlink `airs-cli-rs -> airs` |
| Homebrew `cdot65/prisma-airs-cli/airs-cli` (§21.8) | `cargo install --bin airs` | `bin.install_symlink "airs" => "airs-cli"` | `bin.install_symlink "airs" => "airs-cli-rs"` |
| npm `@cdot65/prisma-airs-cli` (§21.16) | the `bin` `airs`, the launcher | the `bin` `airs-cli`, the same launcher | none |

In 1.x there was no `airs-cli` name on any path. Another `airs` (or, from 8.0, `airs-cli` or `airs-cli-rs`) earlier
on `PATH` (for example one installed by an unrelated npm package, or the TypeScript CLI's `airs-cli`) wins by `PATH`
order; README says how to check (§21.10), and from 8.0 `airs doctor` reports it (§21.15).

### 21.6 Tests

- **The binary.** Every `Cli::rust(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_airs-cli-rs"))` becomes `Cli::rust(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_airs"))`,
  in `tests/*.rs`, `tests/live.rs`, the harness docs and examples; `Path::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_…"))` likewise.
  `CARGO_BIN_EXE_airs-cli-rs` is used only by the compatibility tests below.
- **Assertions keep their meaning.** Expected texts change from `airs-cli-rs` to `airs` exactly where §21.4 changes
  the output; no assertion is loosened (an `assert!(contains("Usage: airs-cli-rs …"))` becomes `contains("Usage: airs
  …")`, never a check that drops the program name). The `dNN_` tests whose names carry the old name are renamed:
  `d73_hints_name_airs_cli_rs` → `d73_hints_name_airs`, `d73_success_lines_name_airs_cli_rs` →
  `d73_success_lines_name_airs`, `d73_the_dlp_mapping_hint_names_airs_cli_rs` → `d73_the_dlp_mapping_hint_names_airs`,
  with COMPATIBILITY updated in the same change.
- **The normaliser.** `compare::normalise_program` maps the Rust program token to `airs-cli` in context only: an
  `airs` preceded by the start of the text, whitespace, `'`, `` ` ``, `"` or `(`, and followed by one space and a
  token (a maximal run of `[A-Za-z0-9-]`) that is one of `tenant`, `doctor`, `runtime`, `redteam`, `model-security`,
  `gateway`, `supplychain`, `help`, `--tenant`, `--output`, `--debug`, `--quiet` (the harness's public
  `compare::PROGRAM_NEXT`, the one copy of the list, choice 67). Every ad hoc
  `replace("airs-cli-rs ", "airs-cli ")` in `tests/parity_*.rs` and `live/runtime.rs` and the `$ airs-cli-rs`
  replacement in `parity_redteam_reads.rs` call it instead. Its unit test pins `'airs tenant import'` →
  `'airs-cli tenant import'`, `$ airs runtime scan` → `$ airs-cli runtime scan`, `Use airs runtime sessions` →
  `Use airs-cli runtime sessions`, and leaves `repairs tenant`, `chairs runtime`, `airs.management.profiles.list`,
  `airs-cli tenant`, `AIRS runtime` and `airs-gateway-report-` unchanged. Parity tests therefore compare the same
  bytes as in 0.11, modulo D73 and D326.
- **Harness labels stay.** `Cli::label` (`airs-cli-rs` / `airs-cli`), the runner's refusal texts and the live
  summaries' `(airs-cli-rs/TypeScript)` name the implementation, not the executable, and are unchanged (choice 15).
- **Source scan** (`tests/program_name.rs::the_source_names_only_the_kept_format_names`): every occurrence of
  `airs-cli-rs` in `src/**/*.rs` is immediately followed by `.bulk-scan`, `.redteam-targets`, `.dlp-resources` or
  `.runtime-profiles`. (Unit-test argv vectors use `"airs"`; the `TestDir` prefix becomes `airs-<tag>-…`.)
- **Docs scan** (`tests/program_name.rs::current_docs_invoke_airs`): in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`
  (outside §21: from its `## 21. ` heading line to the next `## ` heading line, the one rule of
  `tests/common/mod.rs::design_section_21` that `tests/docs_consistency.rs` also uses, choice 63), `docs/TESTING.md`, `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` and (from chunk 2, which rewrites
  the release flow it describes, choice 36) `docs/RELEASING.md`, no
  `airs-cli-rs` is preceded by `$ ` or `Usage: ` or followed by one space and a token from the normaliser's list
  (`PROGRAM_NEXT` itself, imported from the harness) or `--version`, `-V`, `--help`, `-h`, unless it is preceded by `/` (a path such as `./airs-cli-rs` that deliberately runs
  the compatibility name, choice 40). Release notes, `docs/research/`, `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` and `docs/MILESTONES.md`

- **Help walk** (`tests/program_name.rs::every_help_text_names_airs`): `airs <path> --help` for every command, found

  `airs-cli-rs` anywhere; the compatibility binary prints the same root and leaf help (choice 37). The command words
  of `PROGRAM_NEXT` must be exactly the root help's commands and `help`, so a new top-level command cannot be left

- **The compatibility binary** (`tests/program_name.rs::the_compatibility_binary_is_the_main_binary`):
  `src/bin/airs-cli-rs.rs` (and from 8.0 `src/bin/airs-cli.rs`) is byte-for-byte the expected shim, and
  `Cargo.toml` declares exactly the `[[bin]]` targets of §21.2 (three from 8.0) with `default-run = "airs"`.

### 21.7 Release tarballs, signing and notarisation (chunk 2)

`scripts/release.sh` keeps every step, check, ordering, dry-run behaviour and recovery path of RELEASING §3; only
these change:

- `BIN="airs"`, `COMPAT_BIN="airs-cli-rs"` (release.sh); `PKG="airs-cli"` is package-release.sh's alone, which
  holds the one tarball naming rule; release.sh reads the asset names back from the `SHA256SUMS` it wrote (each line
  `<sha256>  <name>`, a `*.tar.gz` name, one per packaged target, else `release: …` and exit 1; choice 58). The builds are `cargo build --release --locked --target
  aarch64-apple-darwin --bin airs` and `cargo zigbuild --release --locked --target <musl> --bin airs`, so the
  compatibility binary is never built for a release and can never be packaged.
- The binary checks (`file`, the macOS `--version`) apply to `target/<target>/release/airs`.
- Signing: `codesign --force --options runtime --timestamp --sign <identity>` on `airs` only; the verification adds
  `Identifier=airs` to the Authority, Timestamp and runtime checks. The identifier is the file name (it was
  `airs-cli-rs`; choice 19). The symlink is not a Mach-O and is not signed; Gatekeeper evaluates the binary it
  resolves to.
- Notarisation: `ditto -c -k --keepParent target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/airs` and the same notarytool flow.
- Packaging moves to `scripts/package-release.sh [--run-check <target>] [--verify-signature <target>] <version> <dist>
  <target>=<binary>…`, which release.sh calls with `--run-check aarch64-apple-darwin`, in a real run also
  `--verify-signature aarch64-apple-darwin`, and the three targets (the dry run calls it too, as it packages today). For each target it stages `airs` (0755, copied from `<binary>`), from 8.0 `airs-cli` and
  `airs-cli-rs` (relative symlinks to `airs`, made with `ln -s airs`), `README.md`, `LICENSE` and, from 8.0,
  `NOTICE` (0644; Apache-2.0 §4(d) carries the NOTICE with every distribution), and writes
  `<dist>/airs-cli-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar --no-mac-metadata --uid 0 --gid 0 --uname
  root --gname root -czf … airs airs-cli airs-cli-rs README.md LICENSE NOTICE` (bsdtar stores the links as links). Then
  `SHA256SUMS` (`shasum -a 256` of the three tarballs, nothing else). It refuses an empty positional argument
  first (`package-release: the <dist> argument is empty`, likewise `the <version> argument` and `a <target>=<binary>
  argument`; exit 2 with the usage, before any `mkdir` or `rm`, choice 59), then a `<dist>` that exists and is not
  empty, a missing or non-executable `<binary>`, and any tar other than bsdtar (exit 1, `package-release: …`), and a
  version that is not the release pattern, a `<target>=<binary>` that is malformed or repeated, a `--run-check` or
  `--verify-signature` without a target (`package-release: --run-check needs a target`; a value that starts with `-`
  is missing, so `--run-check --verify-signature …` names the missing target, choice 65), a `--run-check` or
  `--verify-signature` target that is not packaged and an unknown option (exit 2, with the usage), all before it
  writes anything. A failure after the first write removes every file the run wrote, and the `<dist>` if the run
  created it (choice 43). release.sh's Tools step also requires bsdtar (choice 49).
- **New packaging checks** (they only add to the existing ones): each tarball lists exactly `airs`, `airs-cli`
  (8.0), `airs-cli-rs`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` (8.0) in that order; extracted into
  `<dist>/.verify/<target>/`, `airs` is a regular 0755 file, `airs-cli` and `airs-cli-rs` symlinks whose target is
  exactly `airs`, the text files 0644, every entry owned by `root:root` in the listing; the extracted `airs` is
  byte-equal to its `<binary>` and the text files to the repository's (choice 44); for the `--run-check` target,
  `./airs --version`, `./airs-cli --version` and `./airs-cli-rs --version`, run inside the extracted directory, all
  print the version (choice 54). A real run then runs `codesign --verify --strict` on the
  extracted macOS `airs` (the signature survived packaging): package-release.sh does it for the
  `--verify-signature` target before `.verify` is removed (choice 42); a dry run prints that it would. `.verify` is
  removed afterwards, and `SHA256SUMS` must list exactly the tarballs and pass `shasum -a 256 -c`.
- The Forgejo release name and the tag message become `airs-cli <version>`; the default body starts
  `airs-cli <version>.`. The asset count stays four (three tarballs and `SHA256SUMS`).
- The last line of a real run names the next steps: `next: cargo publish -p airs-cli, then
  scripts/homebrew-formula.sh <version> (docs/RELEASING.md §6)`; for a pre-release, `next: cargo publish -p airs-cli
  (a pre-release gets no Homebrew formula; docs/RELEASING.md §2)` (choice 50). release.sh never renders, commits or
  pushes the formula (the crate is not published yet when it runs).

### 21.8 The Homebrew formula and the tap (chunk 2)

The Forgejo repository and its release assets need a login, so the formula builds from the public crates.io crate.
The template is `packaging/homebrew/airs-cli.rb.in`; rendered for 1.0.0 (with the fixture checksum of the tests) it is:

```ruby
# airs-cli 1.0.0, rendered by scripts/homebrew-formula.sh from packaging/homebrew/airs-cli.rb.in.
class AirsCli < Formula
  desc "Native Rust CLI for Prisma AIRS"
  homepage "https://crates.io/crates/airs-cli"
  url "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/airs-cli/1.0.0/download"
  sha256 "<the .crate file's SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex>"
  license "Apache-2.0"

  depends_on "rust" => :build

  def install
    system "cargo", "install", "--bin", "airs", *std_cargo_args
    # The TypeScript CLI's name (from 8.0) and the 1.x compatibility name.
    bin.install_symlink "airs" => "airs-cli"
    bin.install_symlink "airs" => "airs-cli-rs"
  end

  test do
    assert_equal version.to_s, shell_output("#{bin}/airs --version").strip
    assert_equal version.to_s, shell_output("#{bin}/airs-cli --version").strip
    assert_equal version.to_s, shell_output("#{bin}/airs-cli-rs --version").strip
    ENV["AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR"] = (testpath/"store").to_s
    assert_equal "[]", shell_output("#{bin}/airs tenant list --output json").strip
  end
end
```

The template holds `@VERSION@` (two places: the comment and `url`) and `@SHA256@` (one place) and nothing else
variable. There is no `version` line: Homebrew scans the version from the URL path (`Version.detect` of
`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/airs-cli/1.0.0/download` is `1.0.0`, checked against Homebrew 7.0.9), and
`brew audit --strict` reports an explicit `version` equal to the scanned one as redundant (choice 41). The `test do`
block sends no request: an absent store is an empty store (§3.2), so `tenant list` prints `[]` and exits 0 (checked
against the 0.11 binary with an absent `AIRS_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`, which it does not create).

**The tap** is a separate public GitHub repository, `cdot65/homebrew-prisma-airs-cli`, holding `Formula/airs-cli.rb`
(and a README). It replaced the Forgejo `cdot/homebrew-tap`, which needed ssh access to tap. The orchestrator commits
each rendered formula. Users run:

```sh
brew tap cdot65/prisma-airs-cli
brew trust cdot65/prisma-airs-cli
brew install airs-cli
brew upgrade airs-cli        # later releases
```

Tapping needs no login (`brew trust` is Homebrew's one-time consent for a third-party tap); the build downloads only
the public crate and its public dependencies. The formula's `cargo install` builds from source (no bottles: there is nowhere public to host them).

### 21.9 `scripts/homebrew-formula.sh` (chunk 2)

```
scripts/homebrew-formula.sh <version> [--checksum <sha256> | --metadata-file <path>] [--output <path> | --output -]
```

- `<version>` matches `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`; a pre-release suffix is refused
  (`homebrew-formula: <v> is a pre-release; the tap carries stable releases only`, exit 2, choice 26), as is a
  leading `v`, a second version, an unknown option (`--checksum=<v>` included), a missing option value (a value
  that starts with `-` is missing, except `--output -`), an option given twice, or both `--checksum` and
  `--metadata-file` (exit 2, a `homebrew-formula: …` line and the usage on stderr; choice 47).
- **Checksum source**, in order: `--checksum <sha256>` (64 lowercase hex, else exit 2); `--metadata-file <path>` (a
  saved crates.io version answer, read with `jq`); otherwise crates.io: `curl -q -sS --fail --proto '=https'
  --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 --max-time 30 -A 'airs-cli-homebrew-formula
  (+https://git.cdot.io/cdot/prisma-airs-cli)' https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/airs-cli/<version>` (the repository named `cdot/prisma-airs-cli-rs` until 8.0). The answer
  must have `.version.crate == "airs-cli"`, `.version.num == <version>`, `.version.yanked == false` and a
  `.version.checksum` of 64 lowercase hex; any other answer is `homebrew-formula: crates.io has no usable airs-cli
  <version> (<which check failed>)`, exit 1, where the check is the first of `no version object`, `the crate is not
  airs-cli`, `the version is not <version>`, `the version is yanked`, `no yanked flag` (missing or not a boolean,
  choice 48), `no checksum`, `the checksum is not 64 lowercase hex` and `the answer is not JSON`. The answer is read
  with `jq -s` and must be exactly one JSON document: none (an empty file) or more than one is `the answer is not
  JSON`. The checksum test is anchored with `\A…\z` (jq's `$` also matches before a final newline). Whatever the
  source, the checksum is checked against `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` once more just before rendering
  (`homebrew-formula: the checksum '<c>' is not 64 lowercase hex`, exit 1; choice 60). A metadata file
  that cannot be read is `homebrew-formula: cannot read <path>`; a failed request, the answer or the `.crate`
  download, is `homebrew-formula: cannot fetch <url> (curl exit <n>)` (choice 61); a download that does not hash to the checksum is `homebrew-formula: the downloaded
  airs-cli-<version>.crate has sha256 <got>, crates.io says <checksum>` (all exit 1). Only from crates.io, the script also downloads
  `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/airs-cli/<version>/download` (the same curl flags, `--location`, `--max-filesize
  67108864`) into a private temporary file and requires its `shasum -a 256` to equal the checksum (choice 25). No
  credential is sent or read; the user agent names the tool and the repository, never a person (choice 27). `-q`
  (`--disable`) is the first argument of both requests, the only place curl honours it, so curl reads no `.curlrc`
  (`$CURL_HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `$HOME`): the maintainer's curl config (a `user`, `header`, `netrc`, `proxy-user`
  or `insecure` line) never reaches crates.io or weakens TLS for the answer and the `.crate` (choice 55). The
  `https_proxy` environment variable still applies, as for any download on that machine.
- **Output**: the rendered template. The default path is `<repo>/target/homebrew/Formula/airs-cli.rb` (its
  directories created); `--output <path>` writes elsewhere and requires the parent directory to exist; `--output -`
  writes to stdout. A file is written to a temporary name in the same directory and renamed over the target (mode
  0644), so an existing formula is replaced whole or not at all; an `--output` that is a directory is refused. Messages
  go to stderr; the last is `homebrew-formula: wrote <path> (airs-cli <version>, sha256 <checksum>)` (`wrote standard
  output (…)` for `--output -`). On any failure nothing is written and the temporary file is removed.
- `jq` is needed for `--metadata-file` and crates.io (the release Mac has it, RELEASING §1); `--checksum` needs only
  `sed`. The script is portable bash for Linux and macOS (`sha256sum` when `shasum` is absent).
- **Offline tests** (`tests/homebrew_formula.rs`; every run in a temporary directory under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`
  with a cleared environment, `HOME` inside it, and a `PATH` whose first entry holds a stub `curl` that records a
  marker and exits 97): `--checksum` renders exactly `tests/fixtures/homebrew/airs-cli-1.0.0.rb`;
  `--metadata-file tests/fixtures/homebrew/crates-io-airs-cli-1.0.0.json` (a synthetic answer with the same fixture
  checksum) renders the same bytes; every refusal above exits with its code and writes nothing; an existing output
  file is replaced; the stub `curl` is never run. One more test replaces the stub with one that serves local files
  (choice 46): the crates.io path sends two requests with the flags above and no credential, renders the served
  checksum, and refuses a mismatched download, a failed download and a failed answer request. No test uses the default output path, so a
  formula the maintainer rendered there is never replaced by a fixture (choice 45). The tests need `jq` on `PATH`
  and fail, naming it, when it is missing (no skip; choice 28).

### 21.10 Upgrade notes for 0.x users (README `Upgrading to 1.0`, release notes)

1. **The command is `airs`.** `airs-cli-rs` keeps working through 1.x and prints the same output; switch scripts to
   `airs` at your pace. The TypeScript `airs-cli` is not affected.
2. **Nothing to migrate.** Tenants (`~/.config/airs-cli/`), debug logs, bulk-scan jobs, backups and the fetched uv
   stay where they are, in the same formats: a 0.x bulk-scan job resumes under 1.0, and 0.x backups restore.
3. **Texts name `airs`.** Hints, remedies, usage lines and help examples say `airs` where 0.x said `airs-cli-rs`;
   scripts that match stderr text change accordingly. Data, exit codes and streams are unchanged.
4. **cargo:** `cargo install --locked airs-cli` installs `airs` and `airs-cli-rs` (two copies of one program).
5. **Tarballs:** the archives are now `airs-cli-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` with `airs` and the link. Install `airs`
   and replace a 0.x copy of `airs-cli-rs` with the link (`ln -sf airs ~/.local/bin/airs-cli-rs`); otherwise the old
   0.x binary keeps answering to `airs-cli-rs`.
6. **Homebrew** is new (§21.8). Remove a hand-installed `airs` or `airs-cli-rs` from Homebrew's `bin` first, or
   `brew link` refuses to overwrite it.
7. **Another `airs` on `PATH`** (an unrelated npm package, for example) wins by `PATH` order: check with
   `type -a airs` and `airs --version` (it prints `1.x.y`).
8. **scm-sdk 0.2.3** (§15.24): targets with a Vertex AI or `client_session` config are newly read (D329) and backed
   up, unless the service masks a Vertex AI `project_id`, `location` or `engine_id` (a failed row naming them,
   §15.24 choice 13); `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N` and `REALTIME` targets, which 0.11 read but could not back up or send,
   are now backed up and sent (D328, D329); a target's `audio_curl` is `[REDACTED]` like `curl` (D327); the four
   0.86.0 fields (`audio_request_json`, `audio_curl`, `basic_username`, `basic_password`) print after the declared
   fields, no longer sorted among the unknown keys (D35); requests carry `PAN-AIRS/0.2.3-rust-sdk`. No other output
   changes.

### 21.11 The live tier

`tests/live.rs` runs `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_airs")`; the private store under `target/live/` is filled with
`airs tenant import --from <isolated registry> --name <tenant> --output json` (§10). It never runs the compatibility
binary. The session guard, budgets, isolation, ledger, fingerprint check and summary texts are unchanged (the
summary labels name the implementation, §21.6). The 1.0 release's bounded live run (the user's) is the base
comparison with the renamed binary; the loopback self-tests cover the rest.

### 21.14 Choices decided

1. **`cargo install` gets the compatibility name from a second thin `[[bin]]`** (`src/bin/airs-cli-rs.rs` =
   `include!("../main.rs")`): one source, so the two cannot drift; it also replaces a 0.x `airs-cli-rs` on upgrade.
   Rejected: documenting a manual symlink (cargo removes a binary the new version of a package no longer installs,
   so `cargo install airs-cli` would delete the 0.x `airs-cli-rs` until the user acts); two `[[bin]]` on the same
   `src/main.rs` (cargo warns on every build); a wrapper that execs `airs` (a `PATH` lookup that can find another
   `airs`).
2. **Tarballs and Homebrew use a relative symlink.** Rejected: a second copy (twice the size, a second signature and
   notarisation) and a hard link (tar hard-link entries extract poorly when files are moved one by one).
3. **Release builds use `--bin airs`.** Rejected: building both and packaging one (an unsigned compatibility binary
   left beside the signed one in `target/`).
4. **clap's `bin_name` is fixed to `airs`.** Rejected: clap's default (`argv[0]`): the two names would print
   different usage lines, breaking D326's byte equality and D91's fixed usage line.
5. **No deprecation notice under `airs-cli-rs` in 1.x.** Rejected: a stderr notice (changes stderr bytes for scripts
   within 1.x and makes behaviour depend on `argv[0]`). The removal, not before 2.0, is announced in release notes.
6. **No `airs-cli` alias** (settled for 1.x; it would shadow or be shadowed by the TypeScript CLI). Superseded in
   8.0, which retires the TypeScript CLI: `airs-cli` is a name of the Rust CLI (D330, §21.15–§21.17).
7. **The four file format names keep `airs-cli-rs.*`.** Rejected: `airs.*` with a reader accepting both (0.11 could
   not read 1.0 files, so a downgrade loses resumable jobs and backups; one more reader branch).
8. **Directories, environment variables, store format and tenant keys are unchanged** (settled).
9. **`store::PROGRAM` stays where it is**, now `"airs"`, and clap uses it. Rejected: moving it to `lib.rs` (about 50
   uses change with no behaviour gain).
10. **Rust-only texts that named the implementation say `airs`**, and "written by a newer airs-cli-rs; upgrade
    airs-cli-rs" becomes "written by a newer version of airs; upgrade airs". Rejected: keeping `airs-cli-rs` in
    Rust-only texts (two names for one program in its own output); "a newer airs" (reads like a typo).
11. **The uv download's user agent is `airs/<version>`.** Rejected: `airs-cli/<version>` (indistinguishable from the
    TypeScript CLI in a server log) and keeping `airs-cli-rs/<version>`.
12. **The SDK user agent on API requests is unchanged** (it names the SDK, not the CLI).
13. **The library keeps the name `airs_cli_rs`.** Rejected: `airs_cli` (every test's `use` changes; the library is
    not a public API and its name is never printed).
14. **"airs-cli-rs" stays the implementation's name in prose; invocations and quoted texts say `airs`**, enforced by
    the docs scan; history (release notes, research, BENCHMARKS, MILESTONES notes) is left as written. Rejected:
    rewriting every prose mention (thousands of lines, history rewritten, the Rust/TypeScript contrast lost).
15. **Harness labels and live summaries keep `airs-cli-rs`.** Rejected: `airs` (the `airs`/`airs-cli` pair is easy to
    misread in a comparison, and the live summary texts of §10 would change for no behaviour).
16. **The normaliser rewrites `airs` only before a command word.** Rejected: a plain `replace("airs ", …)` (it
    rewrites `repairs tenant`, `chairs runtime`).
17. **Tarballs are `airs-cli-<version>-<target>.tar.gz`, flat as before.** Rejected: a top-level directory (every
    install recipe and verification step changes for no gain).
18. **Packaging gains checks** (listing, link target, modes, ownership, both names' `--version`, the extracted
    signature); none is removed.
19. **The codesign identifier is the default (the file name, now `airs`) and is checked.** Rejected: an explicit
    reverse-DNS identifier (nothing reads it; one more flag on the signing step).
20. **Packaging moves to `scripts/package-release.sh`** so it can be tested offline. Rejected: leaving it inline
    (testable only by a full release).
21. **The formula builds from the crates.io crate** with the API download URL (and no explicit `version`, choice 41).
    Rejected:
    Forgejo release assets (they need a login), the `static.crates.io` `.crate` URL (a CDN detail), bottles (no
    public host).
22. **The formula installs `--bin airs` and links the compatibility name.** Rejected: installing both binaries (two
    22 MB copies in the Cellar).
23. **The formula test checks both names' `--version` and an empty-store `tenant list`.** Rejected: `--version` only
    (proves nothing about dispatch) and any command that sends a request.
24. **The formula script writes under `target/` by default, elsewhere only with `--output`, atomically.** Rejected:
    writing into a tap checkout by default (a path outside the repository).
25. **From crates.io the script also hashes the downloaded `.crate`.** Rejected: trusting the API field alone.
26. **Pre-release versions are refused by the formula script.** Rejected: rendering them (`brew upgrade` would move
    tap users onto a pre-release).
27. **crates.io requests carry a user agent naming the tool and repository, no e-mail address.**
28. **`jq` parses crates.io answers; its tests fail, not skip, without it.** Rejected: parsing JSON with `sed`, and
    a silent skip.
29. **The tap is a separate public GitHub repository, `cdot65/homebrew-prisma-airs-cli` (first the Forgejo
    `cdot/homebrew-tap`, which needed ssh access to tap), maintained by the orchestrator.** Rejected: a formula in
    this repository (`brew tap` expects a `homebrew-` repository; the source is private) and rendering or pushing
    from release.sh (the crate is published after release.sh, and pushing is the orchestrator's).
30. **release.sh's order and safety checks are unchanged**; it ends by naming the next steps.
31. **`CLAUDE.md` is left to the maintainer.**
32. **One new §12 row (D326); the other program-name texts extend D73**, and the rows that quote a hint (D90, D160,
    D227, D229, D308) are updated in place. Rejected: a row per family (duplicates of D73).
33. **CI's musl job smoke-tests both names** and uploads `airs-cli-<target>` artifacts holding `airs`.
34. **`--version` stays bare** under both names (D26).
35. **The formula's `homepage` is the crates.io page** (public); the Forgejo URL needs a login.
36. **(chunk 1) The docs scan leaves `docs/RELEASING.md` to chunk 2.** RELEASING §3–§5 describe release.sh, which
    chunk 1 does not change (it still packages `airs-cli-rs`, which chunk 1 still builds); chunk 2 rewrites both and
    adds RELEASING to the scan. Rejected: editing RELEASING's commands in chunk 1 (the document would describe a
    tarball release.sh does not yet build).
